Title: Accident, The
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
The story unfolds at Winthorp Castle, a grand estate known for being filled with priceless treasures. Dr. Carlton and Dawson stand outside the castle, with Dawson explaining that the most famous treasure lies within "The Locked Room." Dawson finds it fascinating.

Years earlier, Lord Winthorp’s grandfather saved the life of a Maharajah. In gratitude, the Maharajah's people spent nineteen years creating an extraordinary gift—a carpet called the "Carpet of Snow." It is priceless, woven from the hairs of white tigers, and the first person ever to walk on it was Queen Victoria. The caretaker has the carpet meticulously brushed twice daily and cleaned every three days.

One day, a box mistakenly delivered to the kitchen is sent straight to the caretaker’s room by the new boy on orders. The boy notices a key in the door and decides to sneak in for a nap on the soft rug, thinking no one will disturb him.

Later, Dr. Carlton is introduced to Lord Winthorp. Dawson explains about the Maharajah's gift, and Lord Winthorp recounts the story of his grandfather and the priceless carpet.

Lord Winthorp orders Jenkins to open the door to his guests for a once-in-a-lifetime event. As the door opens to reveal the "Carpet of Snow," the new boy accidentally knocks over a bottle, spilling a liquid that stains the beautiful carpet.

Furious, Lord Winthorp exclaims that his prized carpet is ruined. He feels sick and demands to be taken to bed. Despite efforts to remove the stain over several hours, nothing works. In his anger, he orders the carpet to be removed and burned, declaring he will not tolerate anything with a stain in his castle.

At his bedside, Dr. Carlton tells Lord Winthorp that in one respect, he is like God in Heaven. Confused, Lord Winthorp asks what he means. Dr. Carlton explains that no soul with a stain on it will be allowed into heaven. Lord Winthorp is shocked and questions this, claiming everyone says he is a good man.

Dr. Carlton asks Lord Winthorp if he has ever told a lie, to which Lord Winthorp admits everyone has. He quotes scripture that says all have sinned and come short of the glory of God, and that all liars will face judgment in hell.

Terrified, Lord Winthorp wonders how his soul can be cleaned if the stain on the "Carpet of Snow" couldn't be removed. He asks if becoming religious and doing good works would help. Dr. Carlton explains that it will not. Baptism as a baby also doesn't help.

He teaches that when Adam and Eve sinned, their souls became stained, passing down sin to everyone who has ever lived, separating humanity from God. The wage of sin is death.

To have sins forgiven, innocent blood must be shed. In Old Testament times, animals were sacrificed to cover sins temporarily, but this could not remove sin’s stain. Two thousand years ago, God sent His Son, Jesus Christ, to shed His precious blood once and for all to deal with sin.

Lord Winthorp wonders about the special nature of Jesus' blood. Dr. Carlton explains that Jesus' blood was pure and sinless because Mary, a virgin, was overshadowed by the Holy Spirit, and the blood in Jesus' veins was God's blood, not human.

Therefore, when Jesus shed His blood on the cross, it was for the sins of all humanity. The greatest day in history for Lord Winthorp was when Jesus shed His blood to wash away sins, giving everlasting life to those who believe.

Dr. Carlton asks Lord Winthorp if he would like the stain of sin removed from his soul and assurance of eternal life. Lord Winthorp eagerly agrees and wonders what to do. Dr. Carlton advises him to talk to God in his own words, repent of his sins, and ask Jesus to save him.

Five minutes later, Lord Winthorp joyfully declares that the blood of Jesus Christ has washed away his sins, and he feels so clean—the stain is gone.

The story ends with a message to the reader: the stain of sin can be removed from your soul right now, but there is only one way—believe that Jesus Christ shed His precious blood and died on the cross for you, and trust Him alone for your salvation.

Title: Adopted
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Carter
Responses:
A girl cheerfully announced to her friend Sharon that she was adopted. Sharon reacted with surprise and concern, but the girl reassured her, saying Sharon didn’t understand the whole story.

She explained that she had been growing inside her mother, but some people told her mom she was just a blob of stuff and urged her to get rid of her. However, some caring people eventually showed her mom that she was a real person after all, leading her mom to make a big decision. She wanted to give the baby a chance but decided to place her with a family who would love her. And that’s how she was adopted.

When asked if it made her feel bad that her mother gave her away, she said not at all. Her mother loved her very much but knew she couldn't take care of her, so she made the loving choice to let her be adopted.

But then she shared that she was adopted twice, this time by God. Her friend was curious how that worked, so the girl began to explain. God is perfect and holy and always does the right thing, but people don’t always do the right thing and sometimes even do bad things called sins, which make God sad.

All humans sin, which means we are called sinners. Because of sin, we can't enter heaven. But God has a Son named Jesus Christ who volunteered to do what He could to get us to heaven.

Jesus came to earth and was born as a baby, just like all of us. He grew up and lived a perfect life without ever sinning. Jesus then told us that our sins could be forgiven if we did one thing: believe that Jesus died for us.

Jesus died on the cross, taking the penalty for our sins which is death. But He was innocent and did not deserve it. Because He did not sin, He could shed His blood for us and die in our place. After His death, they buried Him, but three days later, He rose from the dead—alive!

Because Jesus is God, all we need to do is believe that He died for us, was raised again, and ask Him to forgive our sins.

When asked what happens next, the girl explained that God forgives all our sins and gives us the Holy Ghost, who guides and comforts us until we go to be with God when we die. This makes us adopted children by God, the Father Himself.

The friend was excited and wanted to be adopted too. The girl showed her how to pray a simple prayer to accept Jesus, asking Him to forgive her sins and save her. After praying, the friend was overjoyed and eager to tell her friends.

Finally, the girl reminded everyone that if they want to be adopted by God, they just need to believe in Jesus and ask for forgiveness, pointing to a prayer guide to help them.

And so, the story of being adopted twice—once by a loving family and once by God—was shared with joy and hope.

Title: All God's Creatures?
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
Here is the written story based on the comic strip:

One day, a woman asked, “Where’s Sam? He’s supposed to walk my dog!” Her father, an irritable old man, was upset and said, “It’s more important that he walks my dog!” The woman replied, “Don’t complain, Daddy. He’s at Sunday school. It’s important to him.” The old man grumbled, “Sunday school’s a waste of time!”

The woman pleaded, “Daddy, please stop. You do this every week. Please, I’ve got a headache.” The man snapped, “Are you telling me to be quiet? That’s rude! Shame on you!” Then he ordered, “Put me under my tree!” The woman urged, “Now take me outside, so I can get some peace of mind.” Her father reluctantly said, “Right after I put this in the oven…” The woman scolded, “NO! Show your father some respect! Take me outside, NOW!”

The old man accused Sam of complaining like his mother did, feeling sorry for himself. Meanwhile, at Sunday school, the teacher said, “Sam, your scripture verse is Mark 16:15, ‘And he said unto them, Go ye into all the world, and preach the gospel to every creature.’” The teacher praised him, “Very good!”

Later, Sam told his mom, “Hi, Mom! I knew all my verses and got a new Bible!” His mom replied, “Good job, Sam! Your room is a mess. Could you clean it for me?” Sam cheerfully agreed, “Okay, Mom! I love you!”

While tidying up, his mom said, “Looking good, Sam! Ugh! But why are your toys such ugly creatures?” Sam was startled, “Did she say creatures?” He decided, “Now I know what I’ve gotta do!” He put away the last toy and called, “Come on, Goldie!” Brett puffed and scraped trying to keep up. “Hang on. I’m putting all of you on the bench. I’m gonna obey Mark 16:15!”

Sam gathered his toys and declared, “Mom called you creatures, so I’m gonna preach to you guys! Don’t be scared, Mr. Frog.” Meanwhile, his grandpa fell asleep outside. Sam prayed, “Lord, please keep Daddy asleep so I can get dinner ready.”

Sam prayed aloud, “Heavenly Father, please help me remember my verses. Make me wise to win souls. Thank You, God. Amen.” He quoted Proverbs 11:30: “...he that winneth souls is wise.” Then he warned his toys, “Listen to me! These are not my words. They’re God’s holy words! Here goes...”

Sam spoke to the toys about scriptures. “As it is written, ‘There is none righteous, no not one;’” (Romans 3:10) meaning everyone is in trouble with God—even you, sir!” His grandpa snorted, “ZZZ—What in blazes? Who says I’m a sinner? Hmph! Nothing wrong with m—ZZZZ... Lots are worse than I am...ZZZ.”

Sam continued, “‘For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God;’” (Romans 3:23) “Not one of us is good enough to go to heaven!” He went on, “‘Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned:’” (Romans 5:12) “Adam’s disobedience messed it up for all of us!”

“The good news is: Number four. ‘But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.’” (Romans 5:8) Sam explained that Jesus paid the penalty for our sins and did something special for us. Then, “Number five: ‘For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.’” (Romans 6:23) Grandpa was shocked, asking, “Am I going crazy? I keep hearing Bible verses! Sam, is that you?”

Sam beckoned, “Did you hear that? God’s gift is eternal life through Jesus! Sam—come here!” Sam was busy with his toys and replied, “Hold on, Grandpa. I’ve got three more!” Then he said, “Number six is my favorite! ‘For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved.’” (Romans 10:13)

Grandpa yelled, “SAM! STOP IT! I’m ordering you—NO MORE!” Sam apologized, “Sorry, Grandpa, ‘...We ought to obey God rather than men.’” (Acts 5:29) And added, “I have to tell you—you are on your way to hell!” Grandpa thought, “I know he’s right! If I died tonight, I’d drop straight to hell! I’m scared to death! What do I do?”

Sam taught, “Number seven, Jesus said, ‘Behold, I stand at the door, and knock...’ (Revelation 3:20) ‘...if any man hear my voice, and open the door, I will come in to him, and will sup with him, and he with me.’” (Revelation 3:20) Sam assured, “’Any man’ is you, Grandpa! He wants to live inside your heart!” Grandpa replied, “I’m too wicked, Sam!”

“No one’s too wicked, Grandpa. Listen to this! ‘That if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved.’” (Romans 10:9-10) Sam explained, "With the heart man believeth unto righteousness; and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation.” Grandpa exclaimed, “I DID IT! I remembered them all! Okay guys, now who wants to get saved?”

Sam asked, “Anybody?” Grandpa responded, “I do, Sam.” Grandpa wiped tears and admitted, “I’m going to hell. I know it.” Then he asked, “How can I get saved?”

Sam said, “God has a love gift for you. God’s gift will forgive every sin you’ve ever done.” Grandpa asked, “Every single sin?” Sam said yes. Grandpa said, “Sam, that’s what I want. Tell me more about that gift.” Sam explained, “God doesn’t want you cast into the lake of fire. So this is what He did to save your soul.” (Revelation 20:15)

Sam told how God sent His only begotten Son, Jesus, down from heaven to be born as one of us. “He was in the world, and the world was made by him, and the world knew him not.” (John 1:10) But we can’t get to God the Father in heaven on our own. A sinner’s only father is the Devil. (John 8:44) Jesus said, “I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.” (John 14:6)

Sam explained Jesus came to pay for our sins, saying, “I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep.” (John 10:11) Only the blood of God’s holy Son Jesus could wash away our sins. (Revelation 1:5) Nothing else! God’s greatest gift was His Son offering Himself to pay for our sins. “So Christ was once offered to bear the sins of many...” It cost Him His life. (Hebrews 9:28, 5:3, 7:27)

Sam said, “All the sins of the world were piled on the Lord Jesus Christ.” “For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.” (John 3:16) Jesus shed His blood, died, and was buried. Three days later, He rose from the dead. He paid the price! Now sinners could be saved! (Isaiah 53:6, Titus 2:14, 1 John 2:2)

Sam told Grandpa, “Just admit you’re a sinner. Believe that Jesus died and was raised for you. Ask Him to forgive you, and He will!” Grandpa answered, “Yes! Lord Jesus, I’m such a sinner! I believe You died for me. Please save me and come into my heart. Amen.” Sam said, “Thank you!” and exclaimed, “Praise God!”

Later, Sam’s family wondered, “What was all that yelling?” Grandpa answered, “Just me! All Sam’s preaching about God’s free gift got through my thick skull! Hallelujah!” Mom asked, “What about you? Will you take the free gift?” The story ended with a worksheet asking questions about faith and salvation based on Romans 10:9-10.

The end.

Title: Allah Had No Son
Subject: Islam
Author: Carter
Responses:
A father and his son stood watching a group of people praying at a mosque. The son asked, "What are they doing, daddy?" The father replied, "They're praying to their moon god, son." The son questioned, "Moon god?" Suddenly, a man dressed in traditional garb overheard and confronted them. "You!... Wait!" the son stammered, surprised. The man said he heard the father’s comment and called him an infidel. The father explained he wasn’t speaking to the man, but the man insisted that the holy Qur'an says he could kill the father for such a statement.

The man accused the father of being an ignorant fool to speak against his religion and warned him to tremble, claiming many don’t realize what’s happening in America. He boasted that Islam is the second largest and fastest-growing religion in America, and Muslims should be feared. He predicted a Muslim flag would fly over the White House soon and that Christianity would end in America. He reminded them that Britain, the first target, was being brought to her knees by Islam.

The father asked the man if he was a Christian, to which the man said yes. The father responded by calling the man an infidel and said the Bible is corrupt because the Qur'an condemns it. The man denied Christianity, asserting that Jesus, a Jew, was never crucified, claiming someone else died on the cross. He also said Jesus could not be God’s Son because the Qur'an explicitly rejects that idea.

The father countered with historical facts, saying the Sabeans of Arabia worshipped the moon god who married the sun goddess and bore three goddesses, names later becoming idols across the world called the “Daughters of Allah.” The crescent moon symbol is everywhere in Islam and used to mark Ramadan. The man admitted Muhammad knew about this and chose the moon god, Allah, as the one god for his own religion. He declared himself Allah’s prophet.

The father produced a photo of an idol found in the 1950s at Hazor in Palestine, showing Allah on a throne with a crescent moon, proving Allah was pre-Islamic. He explained that on Judgment Day, all Muslims would be trembling, having been betrayed. The father then explained the true God is in heaven, who died for all Muslims and wants them to know the truth – God as the Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost, the one true God.

The father spoke of Jesus Christ, the only begotten Son of God who created the universe, and how every Muslim is alive by His life, though many don’t know Him. Jesus would judge everyone on the last day, and even Muhammad would bow down and say, "Jesus Christ is Lord!" The man gasped and said if this were true, he had no hope. The father told him because of sin, heaven’s gates are closed, but God provided a way for all, including Muslims, to be forgiven.

He shared that God sent Jesus Christ to die for sins because God loves lost people and wants them to live with Him in heaven. The father spoke of Mary's conception by the Holy Ghost and Jesus' sinless birth, adding that Mary later had other children with her husband Joseph. Jesus’ public ministry included Him saying, "I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father but by me."

At the crucifixion, Jesus shed His blood to wash away sins, offering eternal life to all who believe. Jesus fulfilled over 30 prophecies at His death. He died, was buried, and rose again three days later, now sitting at God's right hand and coming again in glory. Later, Jesus appeared to John and declared He holds the keys of hell and death. The man asked how he could be saved from hell.

The father told him to recognize that Satan deceived him, to admit he was a sinner in need of a Savior, to repent, and to ask Jesus into his heart. The man prayed, accepting Jesus as his Savior, declaring that Allah is a false god and Muhammad was not a prophet. He was changed, free, and loved by God. The father assured him God would hear and answer his prayers, and Jesus would never leave or forsake him.

The new believer said he must tell his people about the moon god and the glorious Christ who saves sinners and is coming soon. The father agreed that although it may cost him his life, it will be worth it to be with the loving Father in heaven for eternity.

Title: Almost Time
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
One day, a man named Billy told his father about seeing Jeremiah Gentry in town. Billy's father was surprised, thinking Jeremiah had died because he was very sick. Billy explained that Jeremiah had pulled through despite being very ill. However, Billy's father remarked that it was unfortunate. Billy added that Jeremiah was back on his street corner, loudly preaching again, though he couldn’t even hold up his sign. Billy confessed that he hated Jeremiah since the day he beat him up for preaching so persistently.

Billy's father asked if it was a real fight, and Billy told him Jeremiah wouldn't stop preaching, so he hit him on the head with a shovel, breaking his jaw. Billy was tired of Jeremiah warning about Jesus coming back to judge everyone, insisting there was no Judgment Day.

Billy explained that Jeremiah had made his mother afraid by warning about Jesus' return, and she ended up dying. Because of this, the Bible was forbidden in their house. That night, Billy couldn’t stop thinking about Jesus judging him and decided he needed to talk to Jeremiah secretly, so his father wouldn't find out.

The following day, Billy's father, Henry, left for a week to deal with a family property dispute. During this time, Billy visited Jeremiah, who said he had prayed for this moment for nineteen years and was happy to see Billy. Jeremiah asked Billy what he needed to know, and Billy asked about the meaning of the "second coming." Jeremiah explained it meant Jesus returning to take over the world and fix things.

Billy was shocked; he had never heard of Jesus before and asked what had happened between Jeremiah and his family. He explained that his father had forbidden the Bible and that Henry was trying to take Billy and his sister to hell with him. Jeremiah said that when people do bad things, it is sin, and the punishment for sin is death.

Jeremiah taught Billy that God’s Son, Jesus Christ, came to take the punishment for humanity’s sins by dying for them, so people wouldn’t have to face God’s judgment. Jeremiah quoted John 3:16 to explain God’s love and Jesus’ sacrifice. He explained that Jesus lived a perfect life, died on the cross, and rose again after three days.

Jeremiah told Billy that over 500 people saw Jesus alive after His resurrection, and after forty days, Jesus ascended to heaven, promising to return as King.

Jeremiah shared that Billy’s mother believed in Jesus, asked for forgiveness, became a new person, and was born again. Billy was instructed to tell his sister Sarah that their mother was in heaven waiting for them to be saved too. They prayed together, and Jesus came into Billy’s heart.

When Billy returned home and shared the news with Sarah, she was shocked and saddened by what their father was doing. They bonded over their shared faith and were confronted by Henry, who was angry that they wanted to join Jeremiah’s church. The tense situation escalated for three days until two women fainted during the church service, showing how serious the conflict had become.

Six months later, Billy had read the whole Bible and had many questions about the Second Coming of Jesus. Jeremiah explained that the Jewish people would one day return to the land God gave them after scattering all over the world. This land, which looked like a desert in the 1800s, would be filled again with Jewish people.

Billy asked about the prophecy of two witnesses being killed, and Jeremiah read from Revelation, explaining how news and gifts could be sent worldwide even then, which amazed Billy.

When Billy asked about "Armageddon," Jeremiah explained it was a great battle where Jesus would destroy the armies gathered against Israel. Jesus would rule from Jerusalem for a thousand years before the final judgment and the eternity that follows.

The story concluded with Jeremiah reminding Billy that many prophecies had already come true: Israel becoming a nation, the rise of global communication, and the increasing hatred against Jewish people. The stage was set for Jesus' return, and Jeremiah urged Billy to accept Jesus as Savior to avoid God's coming wrath.

Jeremiah explained how to pray the prayer of faith to receive eternal life, quoting Romans 10:9, and invited Billy to make the decision for Jesus, giving him a form to mark his commitment.

Thus, Billy’s journey took him from confusion and fear to faith and hope, showing how the promises of the Bible came alive in his life and pointing toward the future fulfillment of God's prophecies.

Title: And It Was Good!
Subject: Creation
Author: Chick
Responses:
In the beginning, God created everything. He looked upon all He made and saw that it was good. Yet, something was missing. God wanted to create a helper who was just right for Adam. So, He decided to make a helper to meet Adam's needs.

God formed every beast of the field and every bird of the air and brought them before Adam to see what he would call them. Adam named each living creature. However, none of the animals proved to be just the right helper for him.

When the hen came by, she had her rooster as a mate, which was not suitable for Adam. Similarly, when the mare came by, although she could help Adam carry heavy loads, she had her stallion and was not the right match. Then the apes came along, resembling Adam slightly, but she was still just an ape and not right for him. It seemed hopeless as all the female animals had their male partners. According to Genesis 2:20, no suitable helper was found for Adam.

Understanding the object lesson, God put Adam into a deep sleep, took one of his ribs, and made a woman from it, bringing her to Adam. Adam was overjoyed and named her Eve. God brought Eve instead of someone exactly the same as Adam. Adam needed a helper who was "just right" for him.

Adam said, "This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh; she shall be called Woman because she was taken out of Man." Thus, to be "one flesh," a man needed a woman as his wife, and this was good. Anything else was not good.

Life was easy in the Garden of Eden with abundant food and just one rule: "Thou shalt not eat from this tree." However, the serpent tempted Eve to doubt God by suggesting, "If you eat it, you'll be like gods! Go ahead..." Eve saw the fruit and thought it looked good, questioning God's rule.

One day, Adam and Eve disobeyed God by eating the forbidden fruit. Eve encouraged Adam to try it, saying it was delicious and that no one would know. But God saw everything and punished them by kicking them out of the Garden of Eden. Life became challenging, needing hard work and separation from God's presence.

Since that day, everyone has been born separated from God. Everyone sins by disobeying God, and this is called sin. God's punishment for sin is death, as stated in Genesis and Romans.

The worst sin is unbelief—refusing to trust God. When people don't trust God, they are stuck in their sins and separated from Him, heading toward death and hell. But God didn't want this for us.

God loved humanity and made a way for reconciliation. He sent His only Son to become a man and live a perfect life. God's Son did the unthinkable by paying the price for sin. He was beaten and whipped, then forced to die on a cross, which was God's plan.

Jesus, God's Son, shed His blood on the cross to take the punishment for our sins. He died, was buried, and rose again three days later. Through His sacrifice, He provided a way back to God.

If you believe Jesus died for you and ask Him to forgive your sins, He will do so. He will give you peace and joy in life. As it says in 2 Corinthians, anyone in Christ becomes a new creature, with old things passing away and all things becoming new.

When you die, you will stand before God's Son to be judged. He will say, "Well done," and welcome you into Heaven.

Title: Angels?
Subject: Rock Music
Author: Chick
Responses:
The story begins with a rock band called the Green Angels, who are frustrated after performing a gig. They expected to make $500, but the pastor who booked them paid only $200. The band members feel cheated and lament their lack of money, struggling even to pay rent. They decide to go eat after feeling hungry, questioning why the preacher stopped them because of their Christian rock music. They believed they were incorporating Jesus into their music just like other church rock groups, but they realize they were pushed away because the preacher was old-fashioned.

One night, a man named Siffer approaches the band, praising their music and suggesting they could hit the charts if they relaxed and flowed better. He offers them $500 apiece to play for him and invites them to his place. At his place, Siffer shows them a grand view of the city and offers himself as their agent, promising to make them rich and famous if they follow his way. Although suspicious, the band agrees because of the tempting offer.

Siffer explains that he plays things low key but actually controls the global music system through a sinister organization called "Killer Rock." He has manipulated music history by promoting powerful rock and roll influences that encourage destructive behavior, including murder, drugs, free sex, and suicide. His music has infiltrated churches, and he boasts about turning millions into "rock-a-holics," essentially zombies controlled by his heavy metal influence.

Siffer dismisses the band's Christian faith, saying he has infiltrated churches too and asks if they would die for their beliefs. When they express their commitment, he warns them that they must sign a contract with their own blood to have his full support. Reluctantly, they sign, making them his servants - "lock, stock, and souls." 

Lew, the leader of this arrangement, tells them they will serve him, and he reveals his grand plan. His organization has brought about revolutions, changed music history, and dominated the world through his influence. The band begins to gain fame and success under his direction, playing huge concerts and attracting attention.

Two years later, tensions rise within the band as members fall ill and die from AIDS, and rumors circulate over their destructive lifestyle. They encounter angry mobs and police after concerts. Tragedy strikes during a show when one member collapses and can't breathe. A week later, the band is in ruins; Bobby has died of AIDS, Jim has overdosed, and Don has succumbed to vampirism. Amidst the chaos, another member finds a Bible verse about confessing sins and cleansing from unrighteousness and prays for salvation.

Tom, one of the band members, defies Lew and Satan, submitting himself to God and resisting the evil influence. He is empowered by faith and banishes Satan with the Word of God.

Tom then shares his experience, warning others that even "Christian" rock music can be a powerful demonic force controlled by Satan. He emphasizes that to resist this influence, one must die to their flesh, destroy anything related to rock music, and fully commit to faith in God.

The story concludes with an audience listening intently to Tom's testimony, suggesting hope for freedom from the destructive power of rock music through faith.

Title: Apes, Lies and Ms. Henn
Subject: Evolution
Author: Carter
Responses:
In a classroom filled with eager children, the principal announced some exciting news: their previous teacher, Mrs. Tucker, had twins and a new teacher, Ms. Henn, would be joining them. The children warmly greeted Ms. Henn, who spoke confidently about the great friendships they would build and the many new friends they would meet—on the condition that the students followed her instructions carefully.

Ms. Henn began her lessons by explaining how great humans were and how evolution had taken millions of years to transform apes into humans. The students marveled at the concept of living in outer space someday. She showed the class an "Evolution of Man" chart, asserting that scientists had proven evolution was true.

One curious student, Timmy, raised his hand to question if humans really came from monkeys. Ms. Henn confirmed this was scientifically proven, but Susy Barnes boldly declared that Timmy's statement was a lie, angering Ms. Henn. When Ms. Henn asked for Susy's name, she identified herself as Susy Barnes. Ms. Henn challenged her and demanded that Susy come with her, accusing her of lying and embarrassing her in front of the class. Susy insisted she was calling God a liar, which further infuriated Ms. Henn, who warned Susy to keep quiet or face consequences.

Despite the tension, Ms. Henn tried to smooth things over by calling it a misunderstanding, but the room was tense. She then lectured the children on the "overwhelming" scientific evidence of evolution, including dinosaurs ruling the earth millions of years ago and the theory that birds evolved from dinosaurs.

Susy questioned the accuracy of this, explaining that, according to the Bible, God created the earth in only six days, not millions of years. She asked how Susy knew this, and Susy said it was because God was there and told them in the Bible. She further explained that God made the first dinosaur and the first man on the same day about 6,000 years ago.

Timmy was intrigued and asked if this was really in the Bible. Susy assured him that it contained lots of information, including where people go after they die and the concept of heaven and hell. She explained sin as disobedience to God, which prevents people from going to heaven.

Susy expressed concern that if people believed in evolution, they wouldn’t listen to God. Timmy asked her what to do to go to heaven, and Susy told him about Jesus. She said Jesus left heaven for people and fought the devil for their souls. The angels in heaven witnessed everything, and Jesus grew up to show everyone the only way to heaven.

Susy recited a famous Bible verse, John 14:6, declaring Jesus as the only way to the Father. She described how Jesus was arrested, tortured, and killed because of lies but rose from the dead and went back to heaven. She explained that because of sin, most people end up in hell, but those who believe in Jesus can be saved.

Timmy wanted to believe, so Susy told him to pray and ask Jesus to forgive him and save his soul. Timmy prayed, and Susy reassured him that now the devil wouldn’t get him.

Later, Susy shared her thoughts with Timmy, mentioning how Ms. Henn, their teacher, didn’t believe in Jesus and was blinded by her belief in evolution. She emphasized the importance of loving and praying for people like Ms. Henn.

The story concluded with a reminder that those who believe in evolution over Jesus risk ending up in hell, quoting Acts 16:31, urging everyone to "Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ and thou shalt be saved."

Title: Are Roman Catholics Christians?
Subject: Catholicism
Author: Chick
Responses:
This story explores Helen’s journey as a devout Roman Catholic, highlighting the contrast between her church’s practices and the teachings of the Bible.

Helen’s spiritual life begins with the Sacrament of Baptism, which the Roman Catholic Church regards as one of seven channels of grace leading to salvation. Baptism, as the church teaches, cleanses original sin and initiates membership into the Catholic Church. Helen undergoes baptism with water after a priest performs a ritual to protect her from evil spirits, and at this moment, she is considered “born again” into the church, subject to its laws. According to the Bible, baptism is a demonstration of faith in Christ’s death, burial, and resurrection.

As a Catholic, Helen holds dual citizenship—one to her country and one to the Vatican, which is itself a government with its own laws, money, and ambassadors. The Vatican’s pope acts both as a political and religious leader, to whom Helen owes first loyalty.

Next, Helen participates in the Sacrament of Penance, where she must confess her sins to a priest, who offers forgiveness through absolution and prescribes penance. Unlike biblical teaching that instructs believers to repent directly to God, Catholicism substitutes repentance with this ritual of penance, a practice said to have originated from ancient Babylonian religious customs and not found in the Bible. The confessional booth is described as a man-made invention for control and manipulation.

The story also questions the origin of the priesthood, noting that the Bible speaks only of pastors and deacons, never priests or popes. Catholic clergy roles, prayers, statues, and rituals, it says, were created to impress followers rather than follow scripture.

One of Helen’s key moments is her first Holy Communion, where she takes a wafer—called the host—believed by Catholics to become the actual body and blood of Christ through consecration in the Mass. The wafer, shaped like the sun, traces back to Egyptian sun worship where wafers symbolized the sun god Osiris. Catholics bow down and worship the wafer, which the story says is idolatry and misinformation, exposing the doctrine of transubstantiation as false and pagan in origin.

The Catholic Church’s Council of Trent is also highlighted, showing that in 1563 the church declared its Eucharist as truly the body and blood of Christ and anathematized those who disagreed. The story argues this council’s rulings contradict Scripture and that such doctrines have led to deception and spiritual peril for Catholics.

Helen believes she has received Jesus through communion, but the story contrasts Catholic symbolic beliefs with the Bible’s teaching that the Lord’s Supper is a remembrance, not a literal transformation.

Further, the story recounts the biblical sacrifices for sins before Christ’s atoning death on the cross, stressing that Christ’s sacrifice was once and for all, ending the need for continuous sacrifices like the mass. It claims the Catholic mass tries to perpetuate an ongoing sacrifice, which is an abomination in God’s eyes.

Helen partakes in the Sacrament of Confirmation, where the bishop lightly slaps her cheek, signifying the receiving of the Holy Spirit. According to the story, Helen is not truly saved because she does not have assurance of salvation based on biblical faith but depends on sacraments and church authority. It notes the Catholic Church’s definition of itself as a militant church, engaged in spiritual warfare and control.

The story challenges the Catholic doctrine of papal infallibility, listing troubling statements made by popes throughout history and warning that the Bible regards such claims as signs of a man exalting himself to godlike status.

Helen eventually receives the Sacrament of Matrimony within the church, but unlike baptism and communion, this sacrament applies only to Catholic clergy who carry out sacred duties. At her death, Helen receives the Sacrament of the Anointing of the Sick (formerly Extreme Unction), yet despite all six sacraments, her soul, according to the story, is destined for purgatory—a place not named in the Bible—created by the Catholic Church as a source of revenue through Masses and prayers.

The story draws parallels between the veneration of Mary in Catholicism and ancient pagan goddess worship, accusing the church of elevating Mary to a false, divine status to mislead followers. This veneration is described as a betrayal of Christ’s redemptive work.

The final message emphasizes that the Bible alone is the final authority in faith, and any teaching contrary to it should be rejected. It warns Catholics that their religious system deceives many, despite sincere intentions to serve God, and urges them to come out from it to receive true salvation.

Jesus is portrayed as calling out the false church as "the great whore" and "the Mother of Abominations," expressing His desire for everyone to repent and come to Him for salvation. The story closes with a plea for readers to heed this warning and trust in the Word of God alone for eternal life.

Title: Assignment, The
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
In a heavenly council, it was announced that Charles Bishop was destined to die on November 22 at 3:10 a.m. from a massive coronary. The angels had only two and a half weeks to reach him before his departure and wanted to know if there was anyone who might be able to get to him in time.

Two potential candidates were discussed. The first was Tim B. Dobbs, Bishop’s assistant, but he was considered very weak in faith and unreliable. The second was Cathy Hillman, a 16-year-old who was very close to Bishop’s daughter and known to be faithful. The angels decided that Cathy could be used for this mission and emphasized that every precaution must be taken to ensure its success.

Meanwhile, evil forces became aware of Bishop’s impending death and vowed to prevent any interference. They identified that only two people could possibly get through to Bishop: Tim Dobbs and Cathy Hillman. They planned to work on Tim’s wife, Ethel, to destroy his testimony and prevent salvation. Ethel was a threat because of her knowledge of the word and her potential to reach Bishop through Tim. The adversaries planned to distract her with a handsome young man during the two and a half weeks.

Back on earth, Tim was scolded for never talking to Bishop about eternal life. Tim was determined to reach Bishop and planned to start by giving him a small tract. Ethel, however, feared that Tim might jeopardize their home and livelihood by preaching to Bishop, so she warned Tim to keep quiet. Tim was conflicted but determined.

Tim’s attempt to pray over lunch failed when Bishop misunderstood and walked away, and Tim felt it was a lost opportunity. Meanwhile, Cathy Hillman met Buz Adams, a handsome young man assigned by the adversaries to charm her and keep her away from Bishop.

Buz accidentally spilled something and caused a scene at school, earning Cathy sympathy and perhaps complicating the evil plan. The angels and allies prepared for the day before Bishop’s death, the final chance to reach him.

The adversaries devised a plan to call Bishop and set an appointment for 3 p.m. the next day. The plan seemed easy and foolproof.

On the day, Buz’s father suggested visiting Sandy Bishop, Charles Bishop’s daughter. Cathy saw this as a chance to reach Sandy. After a tire blowout delayed Buz, Cathy went to talk to Bishop, who was at home.

Cathy carried a Bible, and Bishop asked what she wanted to share about Sandy. Cathy began to read scripture about sin, salvation, and God’s love, impressing Bishop with the message of eternal life through Jesus Christ.

Although interrupted by a phone call from Buz’s father, Cathy persevered. She referenced Revelation, urging Bishop to open his heart to salvation. Slowly, Bishop seemed to be listening.

Ethel was worried, but Cathy encouraged Bishop to receive Jesus as his personal Savior. Bishop admitted fears about losing friends if he accepted Christ but was encouraged to make the decision.

As the fatal time approached, Bishop hesitated, thinking he had plenty of time. At 3:10 a.m. on November 22, Bishop suffered his massive coronary, but the angels declared they had gotten him—that he was saved from eternal damnation.

Though Bishop physically died, the story ended on a hopeful note: though he was lost for eternity according to one view, anyone else now had the opportunity to choose salvation and not be lost themselves. The mission to reach him, filled with struggles and divine intervention, was a testament to faith, perseverance, and ultimate victory over evil forces.

Title: Attack, The
Subject: For Christians
Author: Chick
Responses:
The story begins with a man drinking a potion that will cause his stomach to cramp in about three hours and ultimately lead to his death by morning. A doctor is called, and although he tries his best, the man dies the next day. The deceased man had been one of the Puritans who translated the Bible for the king, and his family is at risk of persecution for aiding the spread of God's word in English.

The narrative explains that the first attack on the word of God dates back to the Garden of Eden when Satan planted doubt in God's command to Adam and Eve, leading to rebellion, sin, and death. Satan has continuously sought to distort God's words by adding to, taking away from, or changing scripture.

One major attack involved the "Apocrypha," a collection of Jewish semi-historical moral stories written after Malachi and before the time of Jesus. These stories, idolized by some as scripture, were falsely incorporated into the Bible by the Catholic Church during the Council of Trent, leading to erroneous doctrines like purgatory and prayers for the dead.

Despite Satan's attempts to include the Apocrypha into the Old Testament, Jewish rabbis rejected it as counterfeit scripture. The birth of Jesus and the inspiration of the New Testament writers by the Holy Spirit made Satan powerless to destroy God's word directly.

However, Satan continued his attacks by persecuting believers and attempting to mutilate Old and New Testament manuscripts through intellectuals in Alexandria, Egypt. This led to corrupted manuscripts known as the "Alexandrian manuscripts," which do not truly represent God's words. Translators who rely on these manuscripts are used to cast doubt on the biblical text.

The Catholic Church, particularly under early church father Jerome, used these corrupted manuscripts to produce the "Latin Vulgate," a version that aligned with the Roman Catholic system and furthered Satan's aim to corrupt God's word. The Vatican proceeded to forbid certain biblical texts and officially included the Apocrypha in its canon during the Council of Trent, condemning those who rejected it as heretics.

Satan's war intensified with the Inquisition, marked by violent persecution, torture, and massacres aimed at destroying the "Textus Receptus," the preserved true text of God's word. The Catholic Church falsely claimed that salvation could only come through it, opposing the true message of salvation through faith in Jesus Christ.

God stirred men like Martin Luther to rise against the Vatican’s corruption, sparking the Protestant Reformation. Luther translated the Textus Receptus into German, making the word of God accessible. Similarly, William Tyndale translated it into English but was executed by the Pope's orders for his efforts.

The pope, claiming sole divine authority, persecuted opponents and sent Jesuits to infiltrate England, spreading Catholic influence and resistance to English Bible translations. Jesuits infiltrated key positions to undermine and destroy Protestant efforts, secretly plotting to alter the Bible.

Jesuits aimed to replace the authentic biblical text with readings from the Vatican’s corrupt manuscripts. They failed to insert the Apocrypha into the Old Testament but succeeded temporarily in placing it between the Old and New Testaments, deceiving many Protestants to accept it as scripture.

After the King James Bible was printed without the Apocrypha, Jesuits plotted to eliminate translators opposed to them and spread propaganda to sway English royalty. Puritans caught wind of these Jesuit schemes and were placed on high alert.

Eventually, missionaries exposed the Jesuit conspiracy by distributing Bibles without the Apocrypha. Preachers boldly taught using the pure word of God in English, affirming the King James Bible as God's true word.

In response, the Vatican initiated a campaign for a "new and better" Bible translation, led by Westcott and Hort, who produced a version based on corrupt Alexandrian manuscripts. This revision sought to discredit the King James Bible and impose Roman Catholic theological influences covertly.

Jesuits infiltrated Protestant seminaries to teach and ridicule the King James Bible, leading many young believers to doubt. The Vatican invested heavily in producing numerous Bible translations rooted in corrupted manuscripts, undermining the original truth.

The story ends by challenging readers to consider how much of God's word is in their Bible, listing many verses missing from modern versions but present in the King James Bible. It emphasizes that only the King James Bible can be trusted as the true word of God and urges readers to reject modern corruptions and hold firmly to the promise that Jesus made: "Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away."

The reader is reminded that despising God's word will lead to destruction and encouraged to accept and cherish the King James Version as the authentic Bible.

Title: Awful Truth, The
Subject: Catholicism
Author: Chick
Responses:
Once upon a time, two characters pondered their day's plans. One exclaimed that they were going to take over the world. However, the other responded that someone had already beaten them to it. The one who proposed world domination explained that their rival was mean, nasty, a big fat liar, and had tried to take over heaven but was kicked out, according to John 8:44. This rival now ran the show down on earth with his corrupt friends.

This rival was a shape changer who could appear as an angel of light or a dragon, being the second most powerful being in the universe and smarter than all humans, making resistance futile (referencing 2 Corinthians 11:14 and Revelation 12:9). He was destined for hell but aimed to drag others down with him because of hatred rooted deep back to the beginning.

God created Adam in His own image, breathed life into him, and made him the ruler of the earth. Adam and God were friends. God then gave Adam a wife, Eve, and instructed them to obey Him. However, God’s enemy deceived Eve with lies, leading her and Adam to disobey God by eating the forbidden fruit when He was not watching (Genesis 2:21-22; 3). This rebellion caused God to throw Adam and Eve out of paradise, firing Adam as ruler over all living beings.

The devil, also known as Satan, stole Adam’s place and claimed the world’s systems for himself. Humanity’s population grew but so did their wickedness, increasing God’s displeasure. In response, God sent a worldwide flood to destroy the wicked, sparing only Noah’s family. Despite this reset, humanity’s depravity resurfaced.

God then found a friend named Abraham and promised him the land of Canaan for his descendants. Abraham’s people, the Jews, were chosen, but Satan hated them more than others.

The most powerful being in the universe was Jesus Christ, described as the image of the invisible God, through whom all things were created (Colossians 1:15-16). Jesus warned that judgment belongs to the Son, and every person in history would be judged by Him.

Humans refused God’s way to heaven and created strange religions with idols, but nothing helped them, leading them toward hell. God had planned a way to save the lost, but some refused because it seemed too simple—just faith in Jesus Christ.

Jesus came to earth in human form and allowed Himself to be executed for humanity’s sins. After dying a terrible death, He rose from the dead. People had the choice to believe or not. Those who accepted Him became His children and enemies of Satan.

When Jesus completed His mission, He returned to heaven. Believers became His true church tasked with spreading His message. However, Satan was furious and persecuted them, which only made the church grow stronger.

By 100 AD, the church had the holy scriptures to guide them, but Satan devised a plan for his own powerful "holy" church, preaching a false gospel from a corrupted Bible. The ruthless Roman rulers were replaced by religious leaders posing as divine, calling their religion the true Catholic faith but excluding salvation outside it.

These leaders created odd rituals, new laws, and invented titles like popes, nuns, and masses not found in the Bible. Instead of truth, they set up believers for hell, manipulating the faithful with lies about purgatory and false veneration.

The Council of Trent condemned anyone claiming salvation by Christ alone, while the Bible says those who believe in Jesus are not condemned (John 3:18).

Roman Catholicism, called "The great whore" in Revelation, had three deadly daughters: Islam, Communism, and Nazism—all seeking world control and causing countless soul losses.

Satan tempted Jesus with worldly power, but Jesus refused. The popes, however, willingly submitted to Satan and received their dominion, becoming pious gangsters who falsely claim to represent God.

The Vatican, the mother church, amassed wealth and power through deceit and lies, claiming authority of ancient emperors and speaking for God while hiding a darker truth.

Many popes died terrible deaths, some through poison, others by betrayal and violence. Some engaged in terrible sins, including incest and corruption. Monks condemned the rampant corruption, leading to wars and the Reformation sparked by Martin Luther’s exposed truths.

The Catholic Church launched the bloody Inquisition with millions of victims and created the Jesuits to enforce their control. Jesuits were behind revolutions, wars, and even assassinations, including that of President Lincoln. Allegations even tie them to JFK’s death for defying Catholic dogma.

The Vatican aims for world domination through politics disguised as religion. Jesus warned to come out of her, God's people, to avoid sharing her sins and plagues.

Jesus shed His blood to wash away sins and now invites everyone to believe in Him and be saved, as stated in Acts 16:31 and Romans 6:23.

The story ends urging people to accept Jesus Christ, the Savior, and trust in Him alone for eternal life, not any pope or church leader.

Title: Baby Talk
Subject: Abortion
Author: Chick
Responses:
A man excitedly tells his companion that his folks are coming over for a surprise visit. They are riding in a car, and the companion tells him to stop hitting her. When they arrive, the man introduces his latest wife, Thelma, and their pets to his mother, who is visibly shocked and gasps when she recognizes her son, Billy Bob. He explains that they are moving in because he lost his job. The family decides to take Ashley's room for the newcomers, and Ashley is told she will have to sleep with the dog, Fang.

After dinner, the man asks Thelma to help with the dishes, but she refuses, saying she doesn't do dishes. Ashley is then told she must do them because she's going out with Eric, who is called a bum by Thelma. Eric's mother asks if Ashley's teachers gave her more free condoms, to which Ashley proudly answers yes.

Two months later, Ashley is sick and vomiting. At school the next day, she reveals to a friend that she is pregnant and is unsure what to do. The friend advises her to talk to Ms. Smith from the sex education class, who is described as really cool.

At the sex education class, Ms. Smith reminds the students to pick up condoms. Ashley asks to talk to her privately, asking how she got pregnant when they used condoms every time. Ms. Smith explains that condoms can break and reassures Ashley it's not a big problem, just some pregnancy tissue. She promises to call the clinic and take care of everything, assuring Ashley that they won't tell her parents and that she doesn't have to live under their old-fashioned values.

That night, Ashley tells Eric she is leaving him and blames him for ruining her life. She begs for him not to leave, but he is resolute. Later, Ashley prays for help.

The following afternoon, Uncle Mike reads the newspaper and asks Eric if he has a date with Ashley. Eric responds no, saying it's over because she got pregnant. Uncle Mike tells Eric that he is sick of the lying propaganda kids believe and tells Eric it’s time he heard the truth. He takes Eric to see a doctor.

At the doctor's office, Uncle Mike asks if what they've been told — that the pregnancy is only tissue — is true. The doctor confirms it's a living baby, shown by ultrasound. He warns Eric that an abortion would be a grave mistake because the baby has its own fingerprints, can urinate, make a fist, and feel pain. The doctor quotes a biblical passage highlighting that God was watching over the baby before birth. He adds that if Eric does not take responsibility, it will lead to the baby's death and that Eric's desertion could force Ashley into abortion, which he calls murder. He tells Eric that God will hold him responsible.

Later that night, Uncle Mike tells Eric that the doctor was right but didn’t reveal the nightmare to come. He reads a passage about murderers and liars suffering the second death, but assures Eric that God doesn’t want him to go there and offers a gift that will save him.

Eric is scared but asks what this gift is. Uncle Mike explains it is the gift of eternal life. He quotes Jesus saying He gives eternal life so believers shall never perish. Eric learns that Jesus, God the Son, left heaven to die as a supreme sacrifice for humanity’s sins, rose again after three days, and now the Holy Spirit guides those who accept Him.

Eric prays sincerely, repenting and asking Jesus to save him. Uncle Mike tells him he is now born again and on the path to heaven.

However, Eric realizes he must act. He wants to live right and cannot let their baby die. He insists on telling Ashley the truth.

When he calls, he learns that Thelma took Ashley to the clinic for an abortion an hour ago. Eric prays earnestly for Jesus to stop it. Meanwhile, Ashley, scared and hesitant, fears the abortion.

Forty-five minutes later, Eric arrives at the clinic, demanding Thelma to let go of Ashley. Thelma asks what he’s doing, and Eric pleads with Ashley to forgive him. He tells her he loves her, wants to marry her, and doesn't want them to kill their baby. Ashley, moved, says she prayed for this moment and thanks God.

One year later, Ashley holds their child, Nathan, and tells Eric their life wouldn’t be the same without him. She declares that next to Jesus, Eric is the most precious gift she’s ever received.

The story ends with a message to the reader, offering God’s forgiveness for abortion, highlighting the value of unborn life, and inviting the reader to accept Jesus as their Savior.

Title: Back From The Dead?
Subject: Hell
Author: Carter
Responses:
A paramedic ambulance raced through the street with sirens blaring, speeding to save a critically ill patient. Inside the hospital emergency room, doctors and nurses rushed to the bedside, calling a "Code Blue." The medical team frantically tried to stabilize the patient, but the nurse reported, "I don't get a pulse! There's no pulse, doctor!" The doctor yelled, "We're losing him! Get out the paddles!" A resuscitation attempt was made with chest compressions.

After the intense effort, the doctor announced grimly, "Terminated! He's gone... It's over... We lost him." The patient was declared clinically dead. The doctors discussed contacting the patient's relatives, but none were reached. They moved the body to the morgue.

Barney, a doctor, joked with Cathy, a morgue nurse, commenting on how the place gave her the creeps. Cathy began filling out paperwork, but suddenly, after about 15 minutes, the dead man stirred and revealed his wide, terrified eyes. He suddenly screamed in horror, causing Cathy to scream in fright as well.

Doctors were shocked to learn the man was alive. Cathy explained urgently that the patient claimed to have been to hell and was terrified. The man begged for help, unable to stand the memory or experience he had endured.

The medical staff sought a preacher because the man was yelling for one, scared out of his mind. The preacher, who had been nearby, was brought in. The man recounted his terrifying experience, saying that if he were to die again, he would surely go back to that awful place. The preacher listened carefully as the man described an unimaginable horror.

He spoke of a dark room filled with hideous, smelly, laughing demons who tormented him. Then a massive door opened to an ocean of fire with flames everywhere. Painful screams filled the air. The man was panic-stricken and terrified beyond description.

The preacher explained the Bible's description of hell as a lake of fire burning with brimstone, a place of outer darkness with weeping and gnashing of teeth. The man expressed shock that the Bible was true and wondered why churches did not warn people about hell. The preacher said many preachers don’t believe in hell or avoid preaching about it to not offend their congregations.

They discussed how Jesus knew about hell and warned of it, and that it's reserved for those who die in sin, including murderers, sorcerers, and all kinds of sinners. The man was horrified but also listening intently. He questioned if there was any hope for salvation.

The preacher explained that salvation could not be earned by good works or religious rituals. There was only one way to heaven: through Jesus Christ, who said, "I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father but by me." He emphasized that no religion or good deeds could save one from hell, only Jesus.

The man learned that God's love meant forgiveness and new life through Jesus' sacrifice. The preacher shared Bible verses promising cleansing from sins and eternal life for believers.

The story ended on a hopeful note: the man who experienced hell as clinically dead prayed, accepted Jesus as his Lord, and transformed his life. His name was now written in the Book of Life, and by God's grace, he was going to heaven.

The message was clear — God’s love offers a free gift of salvation, so no one has to face the horrors of hell. The comic urges readers to accept Jesus Christ and be saved.

Title: Bad Bob!
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Carter
Responses:
The story begins with a little boy named Bobby, described lovingly by his mother as her "little angel." Despite her affection, Bobby is a challenging child with a mind of his own, often causing trouble and chaos. His grandmother remarks that "yet man is born into trouble, as the sparks fly upward," quoting from Job 5:7.

Bobby’s antics soon frustrate his family; he floods the house with a hose, which leads his father to take him outside, expressing mixed feelings about his mischievous son. A visit to a child guidance counselor follows, where Bobby’s mother asks if she should spank him. The counselor discourages physical punishment, fearing it might ruin Bobby’s personality and creativity, quoting Proverbs 22:15.

Years pass, and Bobby grows into a rough, angry young man who terrorizes those around him. One night, Bobby returns to a bar with his cousin, causing trouble that results in their arrest for drug possession. Bobby is hostile and uncooperative, angry at the others for trusting a narc. At the jail, a Christian visitor tries to share the message of God’s love and salvation with Bobby and his cousin, but Bobby reacts with hatred, rejecting God and claiming he hates Him and refuses to be told what to do.

The visitor calmly explains that everyone deserves punishment but God, in mercy, sent His Son to pay the penalty for sin. He tells Bobby and his cousin that they have rejected the gift of eternal life and will face damnation as a result.

That same night, a fire breaks out in the jail, and while Bobby's cousin screams in terror inside the burning building, the visitor manages to open the cell and rescue him, though the cousin is horrified by the flames and the screams he witnessed. The visitor warns Bobby that though he has been given another chance by God, his cousin is doomed to eternal punishment.

The visitor encourages Bobby to repent, explaining that God desires everyone to turn from their sins and believe in Jesus Christ for salvation. Bobby expresses confusion about what repentance means. The visitor clarifies that repentance means acknowledging one’s sin, admitting the need for salvation, and trusting Jesus as Lord and Savior to avoid eternal damnation.

Bobby is eager to begin this new spiritual journey immediately. The visitor encourages him, saying God is always ready to forgive and leaves Bobby to settle his own relationship with God.

In a heartfelt moment, Bobby prays for forgiveness, renounces his rebellious ways, and accepts Jesus. This transforms him into a new person, one who will not suffer eternal punishment but will go to heaven.

Later, others notice the change in Bobby. Former acquaintances are surprised to hear that he prays and has turned his life around. They comment that they must find a new dealer because Bobby is no longer the same troublemaker.

The story ends with the message that, while it is an abomination for foolish people to depart from doing good, true repentance brings transformation and a new life in God’s grace.

Title: Beast, The
Subject: End Time Prophecy
Author: Chick
Responses:
The story tells of the coming of the Lord Jesus Christ, drawing parallels between the times of Noah and the present day, warning of the same kind of judgment and tribulation.

Long ago, during the days of Noah, God was grieved by mankind's wickedness. The earth was filled with evil, so much so that God decided to destroy every living thing on the earth. Only Noah and his family, who were righteous, were spared. Despite clear signs, the rebellious people of the time refused to believe in God's impending judgment until it was too late.

Fast forward to today, life is filled with conflict, hatred, and immorality. People engage in hatred, infidelity, and violence. Society is corrupt, with evil flourishing and people dismissing warnings about judgment. Some mock the gospel and claim power through Satan, turning toward a united world government that rejects God.

Few are prepared for Jesus's unexpected return, which will come "like a thief in the night." Most are spiritually blind or apathetic. Religions will unite under a world ruler called "The Beast," who will demand total loyalty and establish a global control system with the aid of technology, requiring people to bear a mark to buy or sell.

Those who reject the Lord will be persecuted, and many believers will become martyrs. Satan's influence saturates the world, bringing about violence, occultism, and despair. Plagues, disasters, and divine wrath pour over the earth as punishment for mankind's sins. World leaders will rebel against God’s kingdom but ultimately fail.

A final great battle, known as Armageddon, will occur near Israel, where Jesus Christ, the true King and Judge riding a white horse, will return with power and righteousness. He will defeat the Beast and its followers, casting them into eternal punishment. After this victory, Jesus will establish peace on earth, ushering in a millennium of harmony.

Finally, after 1,000 years, all will stand before God for judgment. Those whose names are found in the Book of Life will inherit eternal life, while those not found will be cast into the lake of fire. Though God’s judgment is stern, His love remains, offering salvation to those who trust and receive Him as their personal Savior.

The story closes with an invitation to accept Jesus Christ, promising eternal joy and reigning with Him forever. It emphasizes the importance of faith and readiness for the coming of the Lord.

Title: Bed Time
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
A family is gathered for dinner, with the mother saying goodbye as she leaves, telling the children they will take good care of her. The kids express their excitement for dinner as the mother calls them to eat, and they all sit down happily.

As they begin to pray before dinner, one of the girls named Emily gasps and asks if someone died. The father explains that they pray to thank God for the food, not because someone died, which confuses Emily since the food was bought at the store. Another child remarks on how unusual this praying is, saying they never pray at their own house. 

Later that evening, two children marvel at the stars in the night sky. They wonder where the stars came from. One says Jesus placed the stars and knows each of their names, quoting Psalm 147:4, while the other recalls their teacher saying the stars came from a big explosion. The first child corrects her, saying the stars came from God, referencing John 1:3.

At bedtime, the mother calls everyone upstairs, even though the children plead to stay up a little longer. Hannah, one of the girls, tells her sister Emily she loves secrets before heading to bed. Emily expresses her fear of the dark, asking if they can leave a light on, and Hannah offers to ask their mom, knowing she’s kind. 

The mother announces it’s prayer time. Emily questions why they have more prayers, but Hannah says she loves it. They kneel down and the mother leads them in a classic bedtime prayer asking for their souls to be kept safe through the night.

After saying "Amen," Emily is startled and asks Hannah what that was all about, admitting she’s scared. Emily asks who Jesus is, what a soul is, and why Hannah prayed in the way she did. Hannah carefully explains that Jesus made everything and loves them, and that their soul is the most important part of them because it lives forever. She describes the soul as still being Emily even without the body, which will turn to dust after death. 

Emily wonders if her soul will be able to talk, to which Hannah replies yes, saying it can think, feel, and has a tongue and eyes. Hannah then tells Emily that when she prayed, she asked the Lord to take her soul because after death, two groups will try to take it — Jesus and His angels on one side, and devils on the other. Emily is scared at the thought of devils grabbing her soul.

Hannah explains that Jesus knows everyone sins and that’s why sinful souls are not allowed in heaven. However, Jesus loves them so much that He did something special to take away their sins so they can be with Him forever. She says Jesus paid for their sins with His own blood when He died on the cross, citing scripture.

Emily learns that three days later, Jesus rose from the dead and went back to heaven. Hannah tells her that Jesus is preparing a mansion for her there but she has to do something to get there: believe Jesus died for her sins, ask Him for forgiveness, and invite Him to live in her heart.

The next night, Emily prays a heartfelt prayer confessing that she’s sorry for her sins and asks Jesus to come into her heart so the devils won’t get her soul. Hannah and Emily celebrate their new sisterhood in Jesus and excitement to go to heaven together. Hannah agrees to teach Emily the bedtime prayer.

The following night, Emily invites her mom to hear a surprise. The mother listens as Emily recites the bedtime prayer perfectly. The mother begins to sob as Emily asks why she’s crying. The mother admits she stopped praying after Emily’s grandmother died, though she used to pray every night when she was a little girl. Emily encourages her, saying Jesus forgave her sins the night before and she just needs to ask for forgiveness too.

Emily’s mom admits she drifted away from God but Emily assures her that Jesus still loves her and will forgive her if she prays and asks. In the end, the family prays together every night, with the comic concluding on a note encouraging readers to accept Jesus and remember God’s promise to save their souls.

Title: Best Friend
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
Two girls were talking in a yard filled with flowers and trees. One girl excitedly told the other, "I've got a NEW best friend." The second girl, looking a little sad, responded, "But what about ME?" 

The first girl looked surprised and said, "I thought I was your best friend." The other girl explained, "This friend is different. Let me tell you about Him." She went on to describe how her new friend loves her and will take care of her forever, even after she dies. She said, "And He's building me a BEAUTIFUL mansion to live in up in heaven." 

Her friend was amazed. "He can make a MANSION?" she asked. The girl replied, "Sure! He made everything, even you and me!" When asked what his name was, she answered, "It's JESUS!"

The second girl was curious and asked, "Can I tell you more about Him?" "Sure!" said the first girl. She began explaining that God made the earth and the first two people, Adam and Eve, placing them in a beautiful garden. However, God made them leave the garden because they disobeyed Him. God said their sin would bring death, so they had to die. Their sin was passed down to their children, and eventually, everyone dies because of it.

The second girl realized she had done many wrong things too and said, "I had done lots of wrong things, and God saw ALL OF THEM! And I got SCARED." The first girl told her that God will never allow sin into heaven, so the second girl thought she'd never go there until she heard what God said in His Holy Book — the Bible.

The first girl shared John 3:16 from the Bible: "For God so loved the world that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish but have everlasting life." Her friend was confused and said, "I don't understand." So the first girl offered to show it in pictures.

She explained that "the world" means everybody — God loves all of us. Jesus came from heaven and was born as a baby. Because Jesus is God, He never sinned, so He didn’t have to die. But He allowed people to hurt Him and put Him to death on the cross. He shed His blood to wash away our sins—this was God's gift to us.

Then, three days later, Jesus rose from the dead. The girl said, "I believed in Him and got saved." She told her friend a prayer she said: "Lord, I'm a sinner. I'm sorry for what I did. Please come into my heart and save me."

She explained that people who don’t have Jesus in their heart go to hell after they die, but if you ask Jesus to save you, He will start building you a home in heaven and become your best friend right now.

The second girl said, "I WANT Jesus in my heart." The first girl asked, "Will you pray now?" The second girl joyfully replied, "Oh my, YES!" They prayed together, thanking Jesus for dying for sins and asking Him to come into their hearts.

After praying, the second girl said, "I feel so good! My sins are GONE. Now Jesus is MY best friend, too!" She then asked, "Can I ask you a question?" The first girl responded, "Sure!"

Later, the two girls walked happily through the yard. The second girl whispered, "When we get to heaven, could I live next door to YOU?" The first girl smiled warmly and said, "Oh, I’d LOVE THAT!" They hugged, happy to share their friendship both on earth and for eternity.

Title: Bewitched?
Subject: Drugs/Alcohol
Author: Chick
Responses:
The story unfolds in a dark, ominous chamber where a hooded figure announces that the preparations are ready to begin. The master, sitting at the head of a long table surrounded by similarly robed figures, commands that everyone must wait quietly until his favorite TV program ends, after which he will demand reports from all present.

As the old television show concludes, the master gleefully laughs, appreciating the innocence and disarming nature of the re-runs, yet recognizing their effectiveness. When asked why such shows are important, the master explains that the program laid the groundwork for widespread occult and vampire programming seen by millions today.

The master then instructs each figure around the table to report on their areas of influence. One reports that the sale of Ouija boards has exceeded expectations, fueled by hallucinogenic drugs and fortune-telling. Another boasts a win in the drug division, with no opposition to their operations. A report on astrology shows booming sales of astrology books, with the market overwhelmed and hunger for more.

Further updates reveal that their prophetess may soon push for astrology to be taught in schools, and various social issues like anarchy, pornography, and homosexuality are on the rise. The master receives news that their long-term goal of forming a One World Government is nearly complete, with their people firmly placed in pivotal roles. Although some Bible-believing churches remain resistant, the majority have joined their ecumenical movement, edging closer to establishing a “superchurch.”

When asked about any remaining trouble areas, a serious problem is identified: a praying grandmother whose prayers for a girl named Ashley are proving to be out of control. Ashley’s case is examined closely: she’s a 16-year-old girl with a troubled history—her parents divorced when she was seven, her mother died a year ago and is believed to be in hell, she has been on drugs since 14, ran away from home at 15, and her father is an alcoholic executive.

At 14, Ashley pretended to accept Christ during a pregnancy scare that wasn’t real; afterward, she turned to drugs and left home. The adversaries plan to use Ashley as an example, aiming to break the grandmother’s influence since the grandmother’s prayers threaten their control. Ashley has overdosed on LSD and speed numerous times, and her mental state deteriorates with flashbacks and damage to her brain and arteries.

Ashley, struggling with her addiction and loss, is introduced to Madam Tossel, a psychic medium who claims to contact the dead. During a seance, the medium conjures Ashley’s deceased mother, convincing her that communication with the dead is genuine. This deceives Ashley and undermines her grandmother’s prayers.

Despite the grandmother’s persistent prayers, the forces aligned against Ashley remain confident and discuss their strategy to prevent Ashley from accessing the protective influence of her grandmother. The grandmother’s prayers are seen as a major threat.

Ashley eventually reveals to her grandmother the false message she received during the seance. The grandmother, relying on Scripture, explains that the spirit impersonating Ashley’s mother is a deceiver and warns about dealing with familiar spirits.

One night, Ashley experiences severe LSD flashbacks, suffering a massive heart attack. She is hospitalized in critical condition, and her family prays fervently for her recovery. The grandmother leads a passionate prayer, asking the Lord to heal Ashley and bring her back to salvation.

By 9:30 PM, Ashley regains consciousness and reconnects with her grandmother. They discuss faith, with Ashley learning about Jesus’s sacrifice and the gift of salvation. With a renewed spirit, Ashley accepts Jesus as her Savior, joyously declaring that she is saved.

However, at 2 A.M., a phone call shatters the hope: the doctor informs that Ashley passed away just ten minutes ago. The dark master and his followers lament their loss, vowing retribution for losing control over her mind and soul. Yet, the grandmother rejoices, thanking the Lord that Ashley’s name is recorded in the Book of Life, securing her eternal salvation.

The story closes with a biblical warning, emphasizing the spiritual battle between light and darkness, and the eternal consequences of souls not found in the Book of Life.

Title: Big Daddy?
Subject: Evolution
Author: Chick
Responses:
A university professor stood in front of his classroom, asking, "How many of you believe in evolution?" His students enthusiastically responded, "We do, Sir!" When he asked if anyone disagreed, one student stood up and said, "I do, Sir!" The professor became furious, shouting that the student could get out of his class and might be allowed back only after apologizing for his rudeness and ignorance.

Calming down briefly, the professor then threatened to systematically tear apart the student's beliefs in front of the entire class. The student remained seated, and others labeled the professor as crazy. The professor challenged the student to explain why he thought evolution was untrue. The student replied, "Because the Bible says that each kind..." The professor angrily interrupted, branding him a fanatic and warning that mentioning the Bible in school was unscientific and could get him jailed. Insisting that only scientific terms were acceptable, the professor demanded the student understand this rule.

The professor then launched into a detailed defense of evolution, citing overwhelming evidence accepted by all schools everywhere, proven by DNA, science, and Carbon-14 dating. He listed six basic concepts of evolution, from cosmic evolution to micro-evolution, explaining that only micro-evolution — change within a kind — was truly observable science. When the student pointed this out, the professor admitted he disliked the student's attitude but shifted the topic to prehistoric man.

Displaying a Neanderthal skullcap, the professor explained that modern dating methods showed man to be older than Darwin could have imagined. He presented Lucy, the oldest known human ancestor, at 2.9 million years old, but the student countered that Lucy was really just a chimpanzee, not a missing link. The professor told him to sit down.

The professor then shared fossil evidence pieced together to demonstrate man's evolution from ape-like ancestors, with various hominid examples such as Heidelberg Man, Nebraska Man, Peking Man, and Cro-Magnon Man, ending with a "modern man" who supposedly descended from a monkey. The student questioned the logic and data behind fossil dating, challenging the professor on circular reasoning.
