When the professor cited petrified trees and other geological claims, the student questioned the accuracy of such dating methods. The professor then showed drawings of embryos with "gill slits," claiming it proved evolution, but the student refuted these drawings as discredited.

The debate grew more intense as the professor explained vestigial organs, claiming the human tailbone proved evolution from animals with tails. The student corrected him, saying these organs aren’t vestigial but have important functions. When whales' vestigial pelvises were cited, the student pointed out that whales cannot reproduce without these bones, questioning the narrative of evolution.

The professor tried to explain atomic bonding with gluons, but the student called gluons a fictional theory, demanding real evidence. The professor faltered, unable to answer when asked about positive charges in protons repelling each other.

Finally, the student quoted from the Bible, stating that Christ, the Creator, holds all things together and that everything was made by Him. The professor asked if he was saying Christ was the Creator, which the student confirmed using scripture. The student announced he was quitting because he couldn’t teach evolution any longer.

Outside the university building, the professor told the student to leave and only be allowed back after apologizing for rudeness and ignorance. The student walked away, reflecting on the truth.

Back in the classroom, students discussed spiritual matters, agreeing that while evolution was false, salvation through Jesus Christ was real. They understood that though man’s system had been feeding them lies about evolution, they each had a soul and could repent and turn to God for eternal life.

The story concluded with a reminder of the biblical promise from John 3:16 about eternal life through belief in the Son of God.

Title: Big Deal, The
Subject: Bible Stories
Author: Chick
Responses:
Ronnie is bailed out of jail early by his sister Janet, who warns him that this is the last time she’ll help him. Ronnie insists he was innocent and that it was a misunderstanding, despite Janet calling him a "lousy con man." She explains that she sweet talked the guards into letting Ronnie out a day early because she has a meeting with Bob Williams, who might have a deal that Ronnie would be interested in. Ronnie agrees to follow Janet.

At the meeting, Janet introduces her brother Ronnie to Bob Williams, who is pleased to meet him. Janet has already told Bob all about Ronnie’s shady past, which Ronnie isn’t happy about. Bob tells Ronnie about someone just like him who made a deal, became rich and famous, and ended up with other people’s possessions. Intrigued, Ronnie asks for more details.

Bob begins telling Ronnie about twin brothers born to a man named Isaac, referencing the biblical story from Genesis 25:21-24. The first born, Esau, was a mighty and strong man but not very bright, while his brother Jacob was gentle, a good cook, and a schemer – much like Ronnie. Jacob’s main goal was to get Esau’s birthright, which was the right of inheritance to control the family’s wealth.

One day, Esau returned from hunting feeling starved. Jacob took advantage of Esau’s hunger by offering a deal: Esau could eat everything on the table, but in exchange, he had to give Jacob his birthright. Esau, desperate and hungry, swore to the deal. Jacob thus gained his brother's key position in the family.

Isaac was old and blind, so he called Esau to his tent and asked him to kill a deer and make his favorite supper in exchange for his blessing – a blessing meant to prophesize Esau's future greatness. But their mother overheard and wanted Jacob to get the blessing instead. She devised a plan for Jacob to fake the dinner and dress like Esau, even covering his hands and neck with goat skin since Esau was hairy.

When Jacob delivered the dinner, Isaac was suspicious but ended up giving Jacob the blessing. As soon as it was over, Esau walked in angry and demanded his blessing. Isaac was confused and explained that he already gave it to Jacob. Their mother assured Jacob to leave, telling him to go to her brother Laban until the situation calmed down.

As Jacob left, his father told him to marry one of Laban’s daughters so the family blessing would be with him. On the journey, God appeared to Jacob in a dream promising to bless him and bring him back safely. Jacob agreed to worship God if God protected him.

Jacob arrived at Laban’s and fell in love with Laban’s younger daughter, Rachel. He agreed to work seven years to marry her. When the wedding came, Laban tricked Jacob into marrying Rachel’s older sister Leah instead. To marry Rachel, Jacob had to work another seven years. Jacob now had two wives and faced many years of hard labor.

Jacob’s family grew to eleven sons and one daughter. God blessed him with flocks that became larger than Laban’s, causing jealousy. Eventually, God told Jacob to go back home. They took everything they owned, and God helped them escape from Laban’s anger.

Meanwhile, Esau had become a powerful man, and Jacob was afraid of him. On the way home, Jacob sent gifts ahead to Esau to ease tensions. When they met, Esau embraced Jacob, and the hatred was gone. Jacob’s wife Rachel later had one more son, giving him twelve sons who became the tribes of Israel.

Bob offers Ronnie a better deal — riches, a mansion, and ruling nations. Ronnie asks what the catch is, but Bob explains this deal is from God, promising eternal life, mansions, and crowns in heaven. He explains that all people deserve hell, but God made a deal by sending His Son Jesus to die for sins and rise again.

To accept this deal, Ronnie must repent by turning to God, believing Jesus died for him, and inviting Jesus into his heart. Ronnie is encouraged that after doing this, he will receive all of God’s promises. Feeling the weight of the moment, Ronnie prays with Janet and Bob, surrendering his life to Jesus and asking for forgiveness and change.

Ronnie feels clean, forgiven, and eager to stay on this new path. He realizes this is the greatest deal he has ever made and is now on the way to heaven.

The story is a comparison of Ronnie's life of trickery to the biblical story of Jacob, demonstrating that with God's deal through Jesus, forgiveness and a better life are possible.

Title: Big Spender, The
Subject: Bible Stories
Author: Carter
Responses:
Here is the story from the comic strip rewritten in prose form:

Howard Madison was a man who won a huge amount of money—$250,000—in a game, which amazed the onlookers. On his way to claim his prize, he was offered payment in cash or draft by a man behind bars; Howard confidently chose cold cash despite warnings of risk. Driving home, he angrily confronted someone who had cut him off in traffic.

Later, Howard and an accomplice fled a crime scene with the stolen $250,000, not caring if anyone was hurt or dead. Howard almost died from the incident but survived, much to the relief of those around him. However, three months later, Howard was destitute and unable to qualify for food stamps, expressing despair about his situation. His friend Charlie seemed to have abandoned him.

Howard returned to find Charlie, but his friend rejected him, not wanting the trouble in his house. Howard was harshly told to go to a skid row mission and never come back. Feeling rejected and lost, Howard sought a place in a mission but was met with hostility and had to endure a sermon he found difficult to sit through.

Inside the mission, Howard listened to a preacher reading Luke 15:11-32, the story of the prodigal son—a young man who squandered his inheritance. The story resonated deeply with Howard, reminding him of his own foolish spending and downfall.

The preacher explained that the prodigal son asked for his inheritance early, which was wrong, yet his father gave it to him out of love. The son wasted his fortune on extravagant living until he became broke during a severe famine. He then took a job feeding pigs—a humiliating role for a Jew, as pigs were abominable according to Jewish law.

Howard identified with the prodigal son’s misery and hopelessness. The son came to his senses and decided to return to his father, willing to ask for forgiveness and be treated as a hired servant rather than a son. Meanwhile, the father prayed desperately for his son's safe return.

Despite his fears of rejection, the son’s father welcomed him back with open arms, running to embrace and kiss him. He ordered his servants to dress him in the best robe and prepare a feast to celebrate. The son admitted his sins, and the father declared his son lost but now found and alive again.

The preacher concluded that God loves every sinner much more than any earthly father and sent His Son, Jesus Christ, to die for humanity’s sins. This love came at a terrible price—Jesus’ blood on the cross—so that anyone could receive forgiveness and eternal life.

The preacher encouraged listeners hungry for something real to come to God with sincere repentance and trust in Jesus Christ. Howard, moved by the message, prayed for salvation and accepted Jesus as his Savior. He called his dad to share that he was saved and on the path to a changed life.

Howard’s father forgave him completely, despite all the hurt. They reconciled with love, understanding that God’s mercy and forgiveness extend to all who repent sincerely. Howard expressed his remorse, and his father assured him of God's forgiveness, quoting Scripture about forgiving others as God forgives us.

The story ends with hope and restoration, urging people to return to God, who eagerly waits to welcome every lost child home.

Title: Birds and the Bees
Subject: Homosexuality
Author: Carter
Responses:
One day in school, the teacher announced a big surprise to her class. The children were excited as she explained that two dentists had come to visit them. These dentists were highly respected in their community. She introduced the two men, Larry and Charles, but quickly made an unusual mistake by saying that Charles was her wife. The children were surprised, and one of them even questioned this slip of the tongue.

The teacher explained to the children that the dentists represented an ordinary, loving family. She said that God had blessed them because they loved each other. She added that next month, Larry and Charles were going to adopt a baby.

Then, the teacher asked if the children had any questions. One boy named Frankie raised his hand and asked if the men were "Queers." The teacher quickly scolded him for using that word, calling it forbidden at the school and shaming him. But Frankie argued back, saying his dad told him that being gay was wrong. The teacher shouted that Frankie's father was wrong and that people like him were dangerous. She then ordered Frankie to apologize to Larry and Charles or face the principal’s office.

The teacher went on to say that many famous people were gay, but some people were evil and intolerant. She implied that "the gays" were changing how children think by sharing their message.

Later, some of the children discussed the visit. Susy said her grandpa told her not to say anything about it outside school. They talked about the Bible and what it said about homosexuality. One child asked if God really blessed the gay lifestyle since the teacher said so. Susy explained that the Bible actually says God hates homosexuality and warns people to stay away from it. She added that long ago, the Bible was taught in schools, but now they weren't allowed to have Bibles or talk about Jesus.

The children learned about “The Book of Life,” a book that God uses to decide who will go to heaven. Susy said that if someone's name is not in this book, they will be cast into a lake of fire. She told them that God sent His Son, Jesus, to die on the cross to wash away sins so people could have their names written in the Book of Life.

Susy asked if the children wanted to pray to be saved. They all agreed, and all three kids prayed and were saved.

Then Susy explained the story of the old cities that were under the control of Satan, focusing on Sodom, the worst city. The people there were wicked, hated God, and worshipped Satan. God planned to destroy the cities but rescued a man named Lot, who loved God, and his family. Angels blinded the wicked people of Sodom and rescued Lot’s family before God destroyed the cities with fire and brimstone.

Susy said the people in Sodom were like today's gay community. She explained why the teacher had to bring them into class because of new laws and warned her friends to stay away from anyone who tries to make them gay.

She reminded them about the coming judgment day when Jesus would return to defeat the devil. On that day, the Book of Life would be opened to see whose names were written there.

Susy reassured her friends that they would go to heaven because they had made the right choice. She felt sad for kids who were tricked into thinking being gay was okay because their names would not be in the Book of Life.

She told them not to be upset if others laughed at them for following Jesus, because they would be on the winning side when Jesus Christ returned to rule the world.

The story ended with a reminder from the Bible verse, Revelation 20:15: whoever’s name is not found in the Book of Life would be cast into the lake of fire. The children understood the importance of their faith and making the right choices.

Title: Boo!
Subject: Halloween
Author: Chick
Responses:
Sure! Here's the comic strip transformed into a written story:

---

Charlie rented an entire rustic camp for only fifty dollars—a bargain he couldn't resist. The place, called Camp Basil Bub, was holding a grand reopening. His friend expressed surprise at the deal, but Charlie explained the camp was meant for their class Halloween party. Everyone from Salem High was expected to attend.

His friend was puzzled why Charlie got the place so cheap. Charlie revealed the grim reason: the previous Halloween had ended in tragedy, with thirteen people murdered there. This revelation shocked his friend, who gasped in disbelief.

When questioned if the killer was caught, Charlie said the suspect had been riddled with bullets, but his body was never found. Therefore, he must be dead. Charlie reassured him there was nothing to worry about and eagerly anticipated the gang arriving by dark, excited to surprise them.

Charlie joked about the notorious attendee Carrie, who planned to sacrifice a cat to Satan at midnight—something his friend found gross. Charlie laughed it off, but his friend was uneasy.

As midnight approached, a figure with a pumpkin head solemnly prepared to sacrifice a cat to Satan, declaring the ritual was on Satan’s birthday. Suddenly, the figure reviled the cat and demanded Carrie instead, wielding a chainsaw.

Chaos erupted as this pumpkin-headed killer began slaughtering the campers. Screams echoed through the night. The local police chief was informed about the massacre at Camp Basil Bub. If it was the same culprit, they’d need an army to stop him.

Forty minutes later, the killer confronted the chief, mocking him before a gunfight ensued. When the chief demanded to know what the monster was, the killer revealed his devilish nature and told them to run—he was the devil himself!

Despite their efforts, the killer vanished into thin air. The chief realized fifteen people had already died and urged that he must be stopped. Another man noted the killer must be heading to the village, offering a prayer for the villagers' safety.

Outside the village church, the killer was spotted praying. Observers noted his arrival, preparing for the confrontation. A man boldly shouted, "The Lord rebuke you, Satan!" citing scripture to resist evil. The killer shouted back in rage and fled, cursing his own birthday.

The next morning, Joey asked the pastor if Halloween was really Satan’s birthday. The pastor explained that Satan was actually Lucifer, a beautiful being created in heaven to guard God's throne. However, Lucifer rebelled against God and was cast out of heaven, becoming Satan.

Around a third of the angels rebelled with him and were turned into demons. The pastor said it was Jesus Christ, the Creator, who expelled them from heaven.

Joey expressed disgust for the name Satan, and the pastor explained that Satan is alive, actively working to destroy mankind. He and his demons know their time is short, but Satan wants everyone to join him in hell.

Unfortunately, most will. Satan is a master deceiver, and Halloween is just one of his tricks. Kids love Halloween because it’s fun and scary, but they don't understand its dark origins.

To satanists and witches, Halloween is the most solemn ceremony of the year. As the world approaches the Second Coming of Jesus, satanism and human sacrifice are expected to increase.

Halloween began in the British Isles with the Druids—who practiced dark rituals and human sacrifice. On October 31st, known as Samhain, Druids would go door to door capturing victims for sacrifice. In exchange, they left behind jack-o-lanterns to protect homes from death demons.

Satan loves Halloween because it glamorizes darkness and lures children into his camp. Witchcraft is also spreading rapidly among teens today.

Satan’s sacrifices mock God’s perfect sacrifice through Jesus. The pastor explained that Jesus died on the cross for humanity’s sins, and Halloween opens the door to satanism.

Satan hates the message of Jesus and blocks it from people’s minds—that's his trick.

The comic ended with a message to readers: sin prevents anyone from reaching heaven. But through God’s love, He provided a way. Jesus Christ died in our place to save us.

The Bible says, "For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish but have everlasting life."

Those who believe in Jesus and invite Him in will be saved and will reign with Jesus forever. That decision is the smart choice.

However, if you reject Jesus and follow Satan, you will end up in the "laughing place" with him.

---

That’s the story based on the comic strip!

Title: Born Wild!
Subject: Respect
Author: Chick
Responses:
Once upon a time, there was a boy named Dexter who had a troubled relationship with his mother, Connie. One day, Connie demanded Dexter turn off his program and finish his homework. Dexter snapped back at her, telling her to shut up and expressing his disgust. Connie, furious, reminded him that she was his mother and insisted he stop disrespecting her by calling her "Connie."

Dexter retorted that when he earned her respect, he might start calling her "Mama." The argument escalated with insults and threats, Connie warning Dexter she would slap him, and he dared her to try. In a moment of anger, Connie threatened to report Dexter for child abuse if he touched her. The tension was broken by the ringing phone, to which Connie responded nervously, realizing it wasn't Jerry, her little brother.

Suddenly, a loud thud startled an elderly man and his dog in another room. The man asked if someone had fallen. The woman there explained that someone had died and fainted. They decided to pick up the fainted woman to find out who had died.

The news spread quickly: Jerry, the woman's baby brother, was dead. Everyone spoke of Jerry as a beloved, saint-like person. They revealed that when the godfather found out who was skimming money, he blamed Jerry the Rat. Now, the godfather wanted the actual culprit to "look like a hit-and-run," threatening anyone who objected.

On Saturday night, just before the tragedy, Jerry was seen counting money he had gathered. At 11:42 PM, Jerry was killed in a hit-and-run accident with no witnesses. The only person who mourned was his sister, Connie.

Family tensions flared as Jerry's relatives argued over funeral arrangements. Some refused to pay for the funeral but wanted the body cremated to save money. Everyone hated Jerry for being cheap, and the funeral was planned for the coming Tuesday, expecting everyone to attend.

Connie's younger brother Dexter was curious but scared about the funeral. He wondered where Jerry was now—he was told Jerry was in heaven, but Dexter questioned what about hell. The family pastor, Reverend Andrews, claimed hell was a fairy tale. Dexter imagined the worst, worried Jerry might come back as a walking dead to get them.

One night, Dexter claimed he saw Uncle Jerry floating into his room and calling his name. Determined never to attend the "creepy funeral," Dexter opposed going with his family. His mother agreed, saying Grandpa should stay behind because nobody wanted Dexter around.

Grandma informed the family that Grandpa had been released from the hospital, but they worried about Dexter being exposed to him. They told Dexter to stay away and watch TV instead. When Dexter's family arrived late for the funeral, Dexter was frustrated and told them he would never trust Connie again because they lied about watching TV.

At the funeral, Dexter refused to greet Grandpa, calling him crazy. But Grandpa smiled and talked kindly to Dexter, explaining that liars won’t enter heaven. Grandpa shared a lesson about honoring parents, quoting scripture that emphasized respect and the consequences of sin.

Grandpa explained that Uncle Jerry hated his own family and that Jerry's soul went to hell because of his sins, despite the family pastor's claim there was no hell. Grandpa warned that Jerry's soul was in a burning hell, according to what the Bible said.

Grandpa told Dexter he had warned Jerry about Jesus when Jerry was sixteen. Jerry rejected God's gift and told Grandpa to "go to hell." But Grandpa had accepted Jesus when he was six, and that saved him.

Grandpa then told Dexter about Jesus, the Son of God, who came to earth and shed His blood to wash away sins. Jesus was crucified and rose three days later, offering salvation to all who believe.

Dexter prayed to accept Jesus, and Jesus came into his heart. He felt different and wanted to live rightly and make Jesus happy. A week later, Dexter apologized to his parents for his behavior, and they noticed a positive change.

However, life remained chaotic. Connie, overwhelmed and drunk, confessed she hated Dexter because he prayed for her soul and cleaned his room. One night, Connie tripped and broke her neck. Though alive, doctors were unable to help her as she slipped into a coma.

Dexter begged Connie to ask Jesus to save her soul. Connie squeezed Dexter’s hand three times, showing she accepted Jesus just before she died. Her soul was taken into heaven.

Dexter encouraged others to believe in Jesus, emphasizing that Jesus loves everyone and offers salvation from hell. He reflected on how both he and Grandpa were saved when they were very young.

The story ended with a heartfelt invitation for readers to believe in Jesus, accept salvation, and remember the date for when God saved their souls. Dexter’s journey from a troubled boy to a child of God was a testament to faith, forgiveness, and hope.

Title: Brat, The
Subject: Bible Stories
Author: Carter
Responses:
Once there was a man named Sammy who was pressured to come up with a sum of money within 30 days. Determined, Sammy declared that he would get the money somehow. With a plan in mind, he thought about visiting his wealthy cousin Joseph and figuring out a way to steal his money.

Once Sammy had bribed someone named Brat with the money, he hoped to be free from debt and live like a king. Sammy persuaded his cousin Joey to visit him, telling him about the women in Damascus who would be crazy about Joey’s charm. Joey's father worked Joey hard, but Sammy told him Joey was rich and encouraged him to demand his inheritance.

Joey eventually told his father he was retiring and requested everything that belonged to him, wanting to leave home. His father warned him that he was making a bad mistake.

Days later, Joey pleaded with his father to stay, but his father coldly dismissed him, calling him a miserable brat. Joey saddled his horse to leave, with his father bidding him farewell and hoping God would watch over him.

Joey was excited to be free at last and set off with confidence, asking what could possibly go wrong.

To Sammy’s surprise, Joey arrived at his place, and Sammy expressed pride in what Joey had done. Sammy insisted that Joey deserved better than the house he was in, promising they would find a new place soon.

Joey showed Sammy his new home, an expensive place Sammy said was necessary to impress the rich and famous. Joey assured Sammy he had paid off dangerous threats, freeing Sammy from trouble. Sammy was happy and looked forward to taking advantage of wealthy people.

However, Joey soon found himself surrounded by people asking for expensive gifts and favors, claiming they loved him. Despite this, Joey found relief in their company.

Joey planned to get Nada a chariot for their engagement, confident that her approval would come. He thought his brother would be broke soon and was glad the new house was in his name.

One month later, Sam was in trouble as the money was gone. Sammy told Joseph off, saying he wasn’t going to support him anymore. At home, Nada refused to feed Joseph, calling him a filthy beggar and threatening to run him over with the new chariot.

Outside, hungry beggars roamed due to a famine, and Joseph said he would do anything for food. He finally found work feeding pigs, commanding the pigs to be clean and fat, grateful for the job. Despite this, Joseph’s father’s servants were full, and Joseph was starving.

After a month of this, Joseph realized his mistake and wondered what he was doing living in such misery. He decided to go back home and ask his father to hire him as a servant.

Joseph was frightened and worried whether his father would accept him back. Every morning, his father hoped for Joseph’s return. One joyful morning, the father saw Joseph coming from afar, tears streaming down his face.

Joseph confessed his sins and begged to be hired as a servant, saying he was no longer worthy to be called a son. His father, however, ran to him, crying out joyfully, and welcomed him back with open arms, showing how much he truly loved Joseph.

The father ordered a celebration for his son’s return, preparing the fatted calf. He told others to rejoice because his son who was lost had been found.

The story ends with a message reminding readers that, like the father loved his son, God loves everyone even more. It encourages those who have turned away from God to return to Him, just as Joseph returned to his father.

The message stresses the importance of accepting Jesus Christ as Savior to receive forgiveness and eternal life, quoting Bible passages and warnings about the consequences of turning away from God.

In the end, the story reassures that God is ready to forgive those who seek Him and invites readers to come back to Him before it is too late.

Title: Bull, The
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
Blue Baker, the new warden at Blakefield Prison, faces immediate disdain from Commissioner Henderson. Henderson openly admits to disliking Blue and never wanting him in charge, but his real hatred stems from Blue's belief in prison reform. He even hopes Blue screws up so badly that he might get fired. Blue, however, responds with a sly remark about Henderson’s knack for making prisoners feel at home, indicating both tension and the harsh environment within Blakefield.

Two weeks later, things go from bad to worse. The governor has had to call out the National Guard as eighteen guards are held hostage and at least 43 inmates are dead. The prison is in chaos as inmates are burning everything they can find. The crisis began when a guard placed a notorious prisoner known as “The Bull” in solitary confinement, and all hell broke loose inside.

The governor, aware that “The Bull” is the center of the problem, struggles to decide how to handle him. Henderson suggests sending “The Bull” to Blakefield as a test for the new warden. Meanwhile, Blue Baker experiences a mysterious and worsening pain in his side. He's advised to call an ambulance but is assured that the prison will be managed in his absence.

Once in charge, "The Bull" terrorizes the prison. When anyone opposes him or refuses his commands, he violently enforces his rule, making it clear that this prison is now his domain. He demands absolute control, declares hatred for everyone, and delights in the suffering of men under his iron fist. Anyone who laughs or disrespects him faces deadly consequences.

Despite being sentenced to five years of hard labor at Blakefield, a prisoner pleads to avoid the place, knowing its hellish reputation. News reveals “The Bull” has ordered the murder of three prisoners whose girlfriends refused to smuggle heroin, underscoring his ruthless grip on the prison population.

Henderson reprimands Blue Baker sharply, emphasizing that he's running Blakefield, not “The Bull.” He commands Blue to throw “The Bull” in solitary confinement immediately, fearing the chaos that might ensue otherwise. However, it’s clearly no simple task—those who put “The Bull” in the hole reportedly do not survive. Henderson ominously warns Blue that he and his family are targets if he fails.

Ironically, even “The Bull” has moments of reflection. He quietly reads a book titled “Somebody Loves Me,” showing a brief, softer side. But his reign of terror resumes swiftly when the prison chaplain returns and confronts “The Bull” about his lack of faith and understanding of Jesus. The chaplain insists Jesus is the true authority, the "biggest shot caller," not “The Bull,” and warns him about the consequences of his sin.

Tension builds as Blue Baker receives a warning from Henderson about potential riots if he doesn't control "The Bull." Blue is caught between defying “The Bull” and risking his career or giving in to his brutal authority.

When the governor is informed that “The Bull” is out of solitary and rallying the inmates, he gleefully expects a spectacle. Inside the prison, “The Bull” declares he's back in charge—no more killing or raping, because he just learned God hates sodomy. He announces this as the beginning of major changes at Blakefield.

Six months later, Blue Baker addresses the inmates firmly but with a message of faith and hope, quoting scripture and promising them a better future. While Blakefield starts to transform, the governor’s frustration grows, especially when a government official reveals that someone has been spying on prison conditions, complicating Blue’s efforts.

Meanwhile, new prisoners arriving at Blakefield hear about the notorious “Bull” and his powerful grip over the facility. Blue continues his mission to bring order, faith, and reform to the prison despite the many threats and challenges.

In a conversation with the chaplain, Blue learns more about judgment and salvation, reinforcing his resolve to lead Blakefield away from darkness. The story concludes with Blue receiving a “Warden of the Year” award and openly crediting “The Bull” for helping bring about positive change—although Henderson remains bitter and shouting obscenities.

The tale ends with a challenge to the reader: to think about where they will spend eternity, in heaven or in the lake of fire, urging reflection on faith, redemption, and the power of transformation even in the darkest places.

Title: Bully, The
Subject: Drugs/Alcohol
Author: Chick
Responses:
Once upon a time, three men were drinking together at a bar, laughing and enjoying themselves. One man noted that they were getting drunk, which seemed perfectly fine to one of them. The conversation took a dark turn when a man named Harry bragged that his daughter was at church that night. Another man, Andy, expressed disbelief, saying Harry couldn’t possibly mean that. Harry admitted that he told his daughter he would beat her if she attended church.

Andy asked Harry how he knew about this, and Harry explained that his wife took their daughter to church. Andy warned Harry about the danger of his violent attitude, but Harry was unapologetic, declaring that if his daughter ever embraced religion, he would kill her and her entire family.

Feeling the situation was too dangerous, Andy decided not to return to the bar. When the bartender suggested calling the police due to Harry’s disappearance, Andy said it wouldn’t help. Harry was clearly unstable and potentially violent.

Meanwhile, Ashley, Harry’s daughter, had just attended church with the pastor Megan. When asked why she didn’t pray with Megan, Ashley confessed she was afraid. Returning home, Ashley was confronted by Harry, who had found out about the church outing. Harry violently commanded Ashley to get inside, calling her a liar and threatening her with a weapon.

Harry continued his threats, warning Megan that if she ever contacted Ashley again, he would burn her house down with her inside. Megan urged Ashley to drive away quickly to escape Harry’s wrath.

One week later, Harry ranted at Ashley, telling her how he beat her mother every time she went to church and how he enjoyed destroying her mother’s Bibles after she died. Harry demanded Ashley promise never to read the Bible, pray, or seek salvation, threatening to throw her out if she didn’t comply. Ashley agreed, swearing never to believe in Jesus as long as she lived.

Two years passed, and Harry was frequently drunk, boasting to his friends that he preferred Ashley ruined by alcohol rather than religion like her mother. His friends asked about Ashley’s sobriety. Harry shrugged, saying she was usually passed out and that he liked it that way.

Then one day, Harry was seized with chest pain and collapsed. At the hospital, the doctors declared he was very lucky to be alive. When the doctors mentioned that Harry claimed to have seen hell, they dismissed his story as nonsense and delusions.

Released from the hospital, Harry was ready to leave, but the nurse asked if someone should be called for him. Before he could leave, he encountered the local pastor, who remembered Harry as a cruel bully from years ago. The pastor warned that Harry was there demanding to see him, and they prepared for trouble.

Harry approached the pastor urgently, insisting that he was going to hell and that he knew it because he had seen it. The pastor told Harry that he needed to be born again to be saved, which Harry initially rejected, calling the pastor nuts and questioning why.

The pastor explained that everyone is a sinner and needs salvation through Jesus Christ’s sacrifice. Though Harry found it hard to believe, the pastor continued, sharing Bible verses and urging Harry to accept Jesus.

Standing in front of a church, Harry listened and finally admitted that he wanted to go to heaven. The pastor told him that Jesus died for his sins and rose three days later, and if Harry believed this, he would be saved.

Harry was overwhelmed, realizing he had no idea how much God loved him. The pastor encouraged him to ask for forgiveness and receive Jesus as his Savior. Harry accepted and felt different, having been born again and saved.

Excited, Harry called his daughter Ashley to share the good news, but he learned she was in jail after being arrested for drunk driving. At the jail, Harry confronted Ashley, who was bitter and hateful, blaming him for making her turn against God.

Ashley confessed she was dying from cirrhosis of the liver and did not have long to live. Despite this, she still mocked and rejected God, lighting a bottle in the process.

Harry reflected on his past ways and his daughter's situation, praying desperately for her soul. Suddenly, nine days later, strange screaming noises were heard, and as Ashley lay dying in her bed, Harry urged her to trust Jesus and be saved.

Ashley finally admitted her faith in Jesus, and instantly, the fire and screaming ceased. She experienced beautiful music and saw her mother welcoming her into heaven. Jesus was there with open arms, and Ashley felt peace as she left the world.

The story ends with a reminder of the choice between heaven or hell and an invitation to choose salvation through Jesus Christ.

Title: Burn Baby Burn
Subject: Bible Stories
Author: Carter & 3rd
Responses:
King Nebuchadnezzar was deeply engaged in a secret project, promising it would be magnificent but not revealing any details. His curiosity was met with a warning not to inquire further or risk disappearing.

He attentively oversaw the construction of this grand work on the plains of Dura. After two weeks, he decreed that letters be sent to all provinces, summoning everyone to witness his masterpiece, threatening death to anyone who refused to comply.

People from all nations came in response to the royal summons. They watched in anticipation as the cover was removed, revealing a formidable 90-foot statue made entirely of pure gold. Nebuchadnezzar commanded all to bow down and worship the idol, issuing a death sentence for those who would not obey.

The king's loyal officials complied without hesitation, showing their allegiance by bowing to the idol. However, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, three government officials and friends of Daniel, faced a critical test. They consulted the Word of God, knowing that the first commandment forbade the worship of any other gods or graven images, and they resolved to obey God rather than the king.

As the music played, everyone fell down and worshiped the idol, except for Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, who refused. The king was infuriated by their defiance and ordered them to be brought before him. He gave them one more chance to bow, warning that refusal would lead to being thrown into a blazing furnace. The three men stood firm, declaring their faith in God to deliver them but stating that even if He did not, they would never worship the golden image.

Furious, Nebuchadnezzar ordered the furnace heated seven times hotter than usual and commanded the men to be cast into the fire. As the men were thrown in, the extreme heat also consumed the soldiers who cast them. To everyone's astonishment, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego were unharmed, and a fourth figure appeared with them in the fire, described as having a form like the Son of God.

The king called them out of the furnace, amazed that not even their hair was singed. He praised their God, declaring that He was superior to all other gods. Nebuchadnezzar then issued a new law forbidding anyone from speaking against their God and promoted the three men for their unwavering faith.

It was later revealed that the fourth man in the furnace was the Lord Jesus Christ, who had left heaven centuries later to save mankind by dying for their sins. This biblical story serves as a warning that history will repeat itself, with a coming world leader who will enforce worship of his image, and those who refuse will face death. The story concludes with a call for readiness, emphasizing that those who receive Jesus will escape this future nightmare, highlighting the ongoing spiritual battle between faithfulness and compromise.

Title: Busted!
Subject: Ten Commandments
Author: Chick
Responses:
Here is the written story based on the comic strip:

Tony is arrested and told by the police that anything he says can be used against him, and he has the right to an attorney. Tony protests that he’s broke, but a lawyer will be appointed to him anyway. Tony meets his lawyer, Douglas Rogers, who has been assigned to defend him. Douglas reveals that the prosecutor is Douglas Rogers himself and that they have a lot of work ahead.

Douglas is confident as a prosecutor, hoping to win the case and eventually become governor. When questioned about the accused’s innocence, Douglas dismisses it, expressing that he wants to find everything possible to bring him down. Behind the scenes, someone tells Doug that the evidence is piling up against the accused and that they intend to use the law to crush him.

Doug insists he isn’t on trial, but another man tells him he will be because he’s broken God’s laws. Doug protests, claiming he’s a respected community leader. He is warned he will have to answer to God for his crimes. Doug is told his God is not the God of the Bible. The man challenges Doug by saying the Ten Commandments have condemned him, proving he is a sinner.

Doug demands an apology for the accusation, but the man says he can prove Doug is lost by those very commandments. Doug agrees to become governor and will do anything to get there, including lying, cheating, and stealing. The man points out that Doug has admitted breaking five of the Ten Commandments in just ten minutes, and this is only what Doug has admitted so far.

The man explains that when Doug dies in his sins, he will appear before God without an attorney. Since Doug has broken God’s law, he is guilty and will be sentenced to the Lake of Fire forever. Doug protests that if he’s guilty, then everyone must be guilty, but the man explains that the whole world is guilty before God and headed for hell.

God made a way to clear people of all charges and erase the evidence. An innocent man took the punishment for Doug’s sins—Jesus Christ, the only one who never sinned. Jesus was falsely accused, beaten, and crucified, yet He didn’t break any commandments. Jesus is God Almighty, the Creator and Judge, and He died for Doug’s crimes.

Jesus shed His blood for human sins, was buried, and rose from the dead three days later. No one else died for sins—only Jesus is the way. Jesus said He is the way, the truth, and the life, and no one comes to the Father except through Him.

Doug admits guilt by the Ten Commandments. Charlie reveals he was once like Doug but was fortunate to have his evidence erased through Jesus. Charlie tells Doug he believed that Jesus died for his sins, made Him his Savior and Lord, and gave his life to Him. He challenges Doug to make his decision.

Doug admits he likes sinning and doesn’t want to give it up, fearing his career and social life will suffer if he becomes a Christian. Charlie warns Doug that death could come tonight, and Doug says he’ll take the chance and promises to become a Christian if he becomes governor. Death, personified by the Grim Reaper, reminds Doug it’s almost time.

Gloria is asked if she wants a ride to court. She declines, having more work to do. Suddenly, a man with a gun demands the keys to Doug’s car, threatening his life. Despite Doug’s protest, the man forces him into the car. The man shoots Doug multiple times and speeds off.

Gloria is devastated and realizes Doug has gone to hell. Charlie tells her Doug is lost. Gloria admits she’s broken God’s commandments and wants Jesus but doesn’t know what to do. Charlie suggests going to Jesus in prayer to ask for forgiveness. As Gloria prays, she becomes a child of God.

The story concludes with a reminder not to look down on the Ten Commandments, which could condemn people on the day of judgment. It warns that liars will be punished in the lake of fire but encourages belief in Jesus for salvation.

Title: But Everyone Does It
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Daniels
Responses:
Ryan's mom reminded him to have fun at the park and to stick with his friends the whole time. Ryan assured her he would, and after a quick goodbye, he rode off with his friends, saying, "Okay, Mom! Bye! We'll be back before dark!"

As they rode their bikes, one of the kids suggested cutting through Mr. Henderson’s field to find some fun jumps. Ryan hesitated, pointing out the "Keep Out, No Trespassing" sign. But the others urged him not to be chicken, saying everyone does it. Ryan was unsure, worried about what his mom would say, but the others promised they wouldn’t tell her. Reluctantly, Ryan agreed to go with them, remembering his mom told him to stick together.

Together, they took the risky shortcut through the field. Ryan sighed but decided he couldn’t be alone, so he came along. The group cheered.

Meanwhile, at home, a man named Gunther scratched at the door. His owner asked what was wrong, and when Gunther growled at the open door, the owner questioned where he was going. Gunther dashed off as one of the kids in the park exclaimed, "Whee! Look at me!" while riding a bike.

Ryan, flying on his bike over jumps, heard Gunther growling and chasing. He called for his friends to wait for him, but Gunther was right behind. Suddenly, Ryan crashed. Gunther barked fiercely as Ryan fell. His owner shouted for Gunther to stop.

Later, the man praised Gunther and asked if Ryan was okay. Ryan had a few scrapes but was fine. The man explained the "No Trespassing" sign was for their protection, showing Ryan a wooden board with nails that could have hurt his tires or him.

Ryan apologized, explaining he only trespassed because the others called him a chicken. The man taught Ryan that if someone asks him to do something bad, he shouldn’t do it. Ryan pointed out that his mom said to stick together, so he wondered if he had to follow the group always.

The man said not if the group is doing something bad. To explain, he shared a true story about a rich man named Joseph. Joseph’s powerful friends wanted him to kill an innocent man they disliked, Jesus, but Joseph refused to join their evil plans.

That night, Jesus was arrested and falsely accused by those men. The man told Ryan that Jesus was God’s Son, sent to Earth on a great mission. An angel told Jesus’s mother that He would save people from their sins. When Ryan asked what sins were, the man gave examples like lying to parents, cheating, and stealing.

Even though Jesus was condemned to death, Joseph chose to do the right thing by asking for Jesus’s body and placing it in his own tomb. Jesus only stayed there three days because God raised Him from the dead.

If people believe in Jesus and ask His forgiveness, they can live forever with Him. The man explained that people could follow the crowd to hell or trust Jesus, be forgiven, and join Him in heaven.

Ryan and his friends decided to believe in Jesus. They prayed for forgiveness and thanked Him.

Ryan said he would tell his mom about Jesus and about cutting through Mr. Henderson’s field. He knew God wanted him to do what’s right.

The story concluded with an invitation to believe in the Lord Jesus Christ and follow Him.

Title: Camel's In The Tent
Subject: Islam
Author: Chick
Responses:
On a cold, wintry night, a camel approached a tent and politely asked the sheik if it could put its nose inside to warm up. The sheik agreed, and the camel nestled its nose in the warmth of the tent. Feeling more comfortable, the camel then asked if it could warm its neck as well. The sheik responded that it was fine. Encouraged, the camel asked if it might pull in its forelegs, since there was plenty of space within the tent. Again, the sheik consented and made more room by his bed. Growing bolder, the camel inquired if it could come all the way inside, to which the sheik grunted and rolled over, granting more space. The camel squeezed in with all its might, eventually pushing the sheik out of the tent by morning. The frightened sheik ran away, chased and scared off by the camel.

This story is used as a metaphor for how some people view the spread of Islam. The camel represents the religion moving in gradually, while the sheik symbolizes those who find themselves pushed out.

Our camel lives in the Middle East, like in Egypt and Arabia, where people worship "Allah." These people have a very large religion, Islam, which might be the largest in the world, with about 1.5 billion followers who pray five times a day. Many people fear Islam because of what some believe their religion instructs them to do.

The religion of Islam started in ancient times among Arab tribes, who gathered peacefully at the Ka'aba in Mecca, Saudi Arabia. The Ka'aba housed 360 idols of various gods, including five idols belonging to Muhammad's Quraysh tribe. Ancient Arabs believed that "Allah," the moon god, married three powerful goddesses: Allat, Al-Uzza, and Manat. 

Muhammad became the spokesperson for this new religion after a powerful force grabbed him in a cave, causing seizures and commanding him to "Recite!" He initially believed this force was a devil, but his wife and cousin interpreted these visions as messages from Allah. These revelations were later written into the Quran.

Muhammad cleared the Ka'aba of idols to establish one god, Allah, but he kept the name of the moon god while discarding the idol itself. His religion gained power, and his armies fought relentlessly, often brutally, in the name of Allah and Muhammad.

Today, some claim that those practicing Islam use a pattern to gain power over countries: infiltrate by moving in, populate by growing large families and recruiting others, legislate by making laws aligned with Sharia, decimate by taking over cities slowly, and eliminate those who do not submit. This expansion worries some people, especially in places like England and America.

Even though some try to be tolerant, Islam continues to spread, sometimes causing fear in leaders and citizens alike. Muhammad’s teachings have been controversial, including his views on other religions, Jesus Christ, and his harsh treatment of enemies. 

This story also contrasts Muhammad’s teachings with Christian beliefs. According to Christianity, Jesus is the Son of God and the savior of mankind, who died on the cross for the sins of humanity and rose from the dead. In contrast, Islam rejects this view, seeing Muhammad as the final prophet and Allah as the only god.

The comic concludes with a warning about future conflicts involving Russia, Israel, and Muslim countries, forecasting a great battle and Jesus Christ’s eventual return to rule the world justly for a thousand years. It urges readers to consider their choices between heaven and hell and to seek salvation through Jesus Christ.

The ultimate message is that Jesus Christ can be your personal savior in the face of spiritual conflict, and the choice between following Him or following other paths is yours to make.

Title: Cathy
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
One day, Joey asked Mrs. Smith if he could see Cathy. Mrs. Smith told him Cathy was in the backyard and warned Joey not to stay too long because Cathy was very weak. Joey promised he would be quick.

Joey found Cathy lying outside. Cathy told Joey that all her hair was gone because of the medicine. Joey asked her if she was going to die. Cathy said yes, and after she died, she would “fly away” too.

Joey asked if Cathy was afraid. She said no because she was going to heaven, where Jesus was waiting for her. She explained that Jesus loves her. Joey then asked if Jesus loved him too. Cathy assured him that Jesus loves everyone and wants all of them to be with Him in heaven forever. Joey said he didn’t know Jesus, and Cathy offered to introduce him to Jesus, describing Him as wonderful.

She said Jesus is the most important person and her best friend. Jesus sent her to Joey's house that day to tell him about what He did. Jesus is the most powerful and richest person in the universe and wants to be friends forever.

Cathy explained that Jesus created everything—stars, sun, moon, earth, trees, flowers, and all animals—and made humans to be His friends.

Joey asked if Jesus was God, and Cathy confirmed He is, and that He loves Joey very much. She also told him that people became sinful and naughty, turning against God, which shut the door to heaven. But Jesus made a way.

Cathy stressed it was very important for Joey to understand. The bad news is that people who sin end up in hell when they die. But the good news is that Jesus did something so they could be with Him forever.

Joey learned there are three parts to God: God the Father, God the Son (Jesus), and God the Holy Ghost—a true God who rules the universe. Jesus was sent to Earth to make humans fit for heaven.

A young Jewish virgin named Mary, loved by God, was chosen by the Holy Ghost to give birth to Jesus, God’s Son on Earth.

Joey learned that no one is good enough for heaven because everyone sins. Jesus was the only one who lived a perfect life, teaching love and forgiveness, and came to wash away sins because sin isn’t allowed in heaven.

Jesus said He came from heaven and was the Son of God. Some people laughed, but religious leaders wanted to kill Him for claiming He was the only way to heaven.

Jesus washed away sins with His sinless blood. When He was arrested, hurt, and hung on a cross, He died to get people into heaven. He was buried and rose again three days later, returning to heaven.

Joey was amazed Jesus did all that for everyone, including him. Cathy told him what he must do: Pray and tell Jesus he is a sinner, ask for forgiveness, and believe that Jesus died and rose again to save him.

Joey prayed and something wonderful happened—his heart became God’s home, and Jesus became his friend. Cathy explained that Joey was saved and wasn’t going to hell.

Mrs. Smith came to call Joey home, reminding him Cathy needed her medicine. Joey thanked Mrs. Smith for the time with Cathy and promised to pray for her.

Later, Mrs. Smith told Joey Cathy had pneumonia and wanted him to know she had a present for him. Cathy passed away but left Joey her Bible. Mrs. Smith asked Joey to tell other children what Cathy had told him—about Jesus’s love and going to heaven.

Joey promised he would share this message with others, so they too could be friends with Jesus and go to heaven.

Title: Cats
Subject: Bible Stories
Author: Carter
Responses:
The river had been dammed and diverted, making the riverbed only ankle deep. Upon receiving this news, the commander ordered the captain to move the forces quickly to attack, instructing, "No lights; no talking." In the dead of night, the attacking forces advanced toward the heavily fortified city of Babylon.

Inside the great city, however, it was a time of celebration. Belshazzar, the arrogant son of King Nebuchadnezzar, was hosting a grand feast for a thousand of his lords, enjoying drink and sumptuous food. He drunkenly toasted to Ishtar, his favorite golden goddess. The lazy guards did not even notice the riverbed’s dropping water level beneath the city walls.

King Belshazzar drank from golden cups that had been stolen from the temple of God in Jerusalem, making toasts to false gods. This caused God Almighty to send him a warning. Suddenly, eerie fingers appeared, writing on the wall, terrifying everyone. The message told the king to see Daniel.

None of the wise men could interpret the writing, leaving the king a miserable wreck who shook uncontrollably. The queen suggested calling Daniel. The king feared Daniel, knowing God was with him, so he tried to flatter him, but Daniel was unimpressed.

Daniel was promised gifts and the promise of becoming third ruler if he could read the writing. But Daniel declined the gifts and read the message anyway, fully aware that by the next day, there would be no kingdom. He reminded the king how everyone had feared his father, Nebuchadnezzar, who had gone mad for seven years until he repented.

Addressing Belshazzar, Daniel said that he knew all this and that the king had lifted himself up against the Lord by praising false gods that could neither see nor hear. This was the meaning of the writing on the wall, which foretold the king’s shock: God declared that Belshazzar’s kingdom was finished and deemed him a zero. The kingdom would be divided between the Medes and Persians.

The stunned king proclaimed Daniel as third ruler, but two armies were already sneaking beneath the city walls. Mighty Babylon fell to the Medes and Persians, fulfilling God's prophecy in Jeremiah 50. Belshazzar’s drunken captains were slaughtered, and Belshazzar himself was killed. The army began killing those in power, but Daniel was spared because he was a man of God.

King Darius appointed 120 princes over the kingdom, with three presidents over them, Daniel being first. Daniel was a blessing to everyone and prospered under the Spirit of God. However, jealous princes envied him as he was only a Jewish slave who rose to power and was not of royal blood. They wanted him dead.

These princes investigated Daniel, hunting for dirt such as corruption, witchcraft, or any fault to hang him on. After much scrutiny, they found nothing but discovered he prayed three times daily to God. They crafted a new law forbidding prayer to anyone but the king for thirty days, knowing that if Daniel prayed, he would face punishment.

The law was signed, becoming unchangeable, and disobedience meant death by lions’ den. Daniel knew the danger but chose to pray anyway, pledging allegiance to God above all else. His enemies reported this, and the furious king was tricked into condemning his best friend.

Daniel was thrown into the lions’ den, facing starvation and instant death. The worried king called out, "Your God will deliver you," though he was filled with doubt. King Darius spent a sleepless night and prayed for Daniel’s safety. At dawn, he came to the den and exclaimed, "There’s not a scratch on him!" God’s angel had shut the lions’ mouths, protecting Daniel.

King Darius learned his lesson and ordered Daniel’s enemies and their families thrown into the lions’ den, where they were torn apart before hitting the bottom. The story ends with a stark warning about those who reject Jesus Christ, foretelling judgment and eternal punishment as described in the Bible.

God wants no sinners to perish, which is why Jesus Christ suffered and died for their salvation. By sincerely praying to Jesus and accepting Him as Savior, believers can be saved from hell. When facing judgment, the Lord Jesus will welcome the faithful, saying, "Well done, thou good and faithful servant... enter thou into the joy of thy Lord!"

Title: Caught
Subject: Bible Stories
Author: Chick
Responses:
A man named Roger decided to get a room at Motel Delight, telling his partner he would get them a room. His partner was nervous, saying they had never done this before and didn’t feel right about it. Roger reassured her, saying no one would see them there.

Inside the motel room, Roger and his partner drank and expressed love for each other. Roger promised that God was his witness to his love. Three hours later, at a restaurant, a man greeted Roger with surprising questions about a woman named Linda. Roger claimed to love the situation, but the man revealed that Linda was actually Roger’s wife and that Roger had three great children.

The next day, Roger was confronted by the man who explained that Linda had written him a letter, calling Roger a snake and accusing him of ruining their lives and possibly spreading AIDS. Roger was upset, denying that Linda’s accusations were true and blaming another woman named Jessica. The man hoped Jessica would get pregnant as a form of punishment.

The following week, Henry called Bob for prayer, saying Roger had shown up asking for prayer. Bob agreed to see Roger and later told Roger he would do what he could to help. During their conversation, Roger shared that he had tried to comfort a lady in their church, which made his wife jealous, causing her to accuse him of doing something terrible and take their children away.

Bob confronted Roger about his actions, emphasizing that God hates adultery and that Roger’s sin was severe. Roger defended himself, saying everyone is doing it and that he came for Christian love and comfort, not to be preached at. Bob insisted that Roger examine the biblical story of King David to understand the gravity of his sin.

The story transitioned to David as a boy, describing his love for God and his courage as a fierce warrior, including a famous battle with a giant Philistine named Goliath, whom David killed with a stone. David became king, loved and respected for being God’s man, but the devil hated him and watched for his every move.

One year later, David was in Jerusalem when he saw a beautiful woman bathing, later identified as Bathsheba, the wife of Uriah. Despite knowing she was married, David committed adultery with her. God was watching, but David did not realize all were observing his sin. David’s actions broke three of God’s commandments.

Bathsheba became pregnant, revealing David’s sin. Uriah, Bathsheba’s husband and one of David’s mighty men, was unaware of the affair. David summoned Uriah from battle, tried to get him to sleep with his wife, but when Uriah refused, David sent him back with orders that led to his death in battle.

David then married Bathsheba, and their baby was born, but God was displeased. God sent the prophet Nathan to confront David with a story about a poor man’s pet lamb, which David condemned harshly. Nathan revealed the story was about David’s sin, telling him he was the man who committed those atrocities.

David repented, and God forgave his sin, but his family life was ruined, and the baby died. The story of David’s adultery was recorded throughout history.

Returning to the present, Bob asked Roger if he truly understood the gospel. Roger initially said the church stuff was for preachers and seemed uninterested, but Bob stressed that knowing the gospel was important to avoid hell. Roger reluctantly asked Bob to tell him more.

Roger then angrily declared he was done with guilt and sick of being condemned, telling Bible teachers to go to hell. Bob calmly explained that Jesus saved them and that they couldn’t be condemned once saved.

Eight weeks later, Roger dropped dead. The comic referenced scriptures stating judgment after death and punishment for adultery according to both Old and New Testaments.

The comic concluded with a warning from Jesus to Roger about eternal punishment for those not found in the Book of Life, but also hope for forgiveness through repentance and accepting Jesus as personal Savior, whose blood washes away sins. The final message asked if Roger believed this truth.

Title: Chaplain, The
Subject: Military
Author: Chick
Responses:
In the midst of a fierce battle, soldiers were caught in a deadly firefight. Shouting commands, one soldier urged his comrades to fire their weapons with cries of "Death to all infidels!" The enemy was cutting them to pieces, and desperation set in as the soldiers called for help over the radio. One soldier taunted another, asking, "Where’s your God now, Preacher boy?"

Amidst the chaos, one soldier, Benny, prayed fervently, asking the Lord for help in Jesus’ name, but the situation only worsened. A sudden, blinding sandstorm enveloped them, forcing a retreat amidst choking coughs and blinding sand. Forty minutes later, as the storm eased, one soldier remarked that it was luck, not God, that had saved them. However, the cost was severe—Max, a fellow soldier, had been fatally wounded.

As they prepared for another flight, there was uncertainty about which body bag contained Max. Benny and the preacher discussed whether Max was in heaven. The preacher explained that since Max died in his sins, Jesus would reject him. Benny questioned this, asking why Jesus was considered such a big deal in heaven.

The preacher asked Benny about what he knew regarding Jesus. Benny hesitated, describing Jesus as a Jew who was killed on a cross because he wrote the Bible. The preacher corrected him, explaining Jesus' significance, revealing that Jesus is God Almighty, creator of the universe, knowing everything anyone has ever done. Benny was scared by this revelation.

The preacher told Benny about Judgment Day, where everyone's life would be shown, including secrets people wanted hidden. They discussed the concept of sin and hell, and Benny asked if that meant he was damned. The preacher assured him there was a way out and begged Benny to seek help.

Benny expressed hatred towards Tex Wilson for the wrongs done to him and admitted he would kill Wilson given a chance. The preacher asked Benny if he would die for Wilson. Benny said yes. The preacher explained that Jesus died for everyone’s sins, including Texans. Benny was puzzled why Jesus would do this.

Benny confided in the preacher that his own mother didn’t love him, but Jesus loved him even in his rotten state, because He’s God. The preacher told Benny about Jesus’ humble birth in a stable and the opposition Jesus faced for speaking the truth. They discussed how Jesus was arrested, framed, beaten, and crucified, all while allowing it to happen.

The preacher read John 3:16 to Benny, explaining that Jesus willingly died to save the world, but three days later, Jesus rose from the dead, finishing His mission and glorifying His body. He said anyone who believes in Jesus will be saved and resurrected with a new body. Benny asked what happens if he doesn’t believe.

The preacher warned Benny he would die in sin like Max and be damned to the lake of fire if he didn’t choose Jesus now. Suddenly, orders came to break up and move out. Benny was taken away.

They were soon flying to the front lines, where an explosion killed Benny when their vehicle hit a landmine. As he died, Benny asked the preacher why he did all this for him. The preacher said he couldn’t let Benny die unready, emphasizing the great love that Jesus had for him.

Days later, a new chaplain named Captain Davis arrived to help with spiritual needs. Benny shared how his best friend, Preacher, died trying to save him, and how Preacher always talked about Jesus. Davis asked about Preacher’s credentials but dismissed those alone as not making a true preacher.

Davis said many ways to heaven existed, welcoming everyone to follow their own faiths, warning that Benny’s friend was just a wannabe preacher. Benny refused to accept this and prayed for salvation. The next day, Benny joyfully told the chaplain he was saved, though Davis scoffed at him, calling him a religious terrorist and a threat.

Benny invited Davis to ride with the soldiers, but Davis refused, saying he didn’t associate with Bible believers. Davis, frustrated, revealed he was a theologian with many years of study and publications but felt disrespected. The vehicle hit a landmine, killing all inside.

In the afterlife, Benny was welcomed into heaven because he believed Jesus died for him. The chaplain, however, was condemned for being ashamed of his faith and acting piously to impress others, facing eternal punishment.

Finally, a choice was presented to the reader: to humble themselves like Benny and accept Jesus, or to stubbornly reject God and face condemnation. The story ended with a scripture urging belief in Jesus for salvation.

Title: Charlie's Ants
Subject: Basic Gospel
Tag(s): ['Little Children', 'Most Popular Titles', 'Older Children and Adults']
Author: Chick
Responses:
Charlie and Sarah were outside talking about Charlie's ants. Sarah asked Charlie how his ants were doing, and Charlie replied that they were busy as ever. Charlie confessed that he loved watching the ants and considered them his little friends.

Suddenly, Sarah warned him that the land where the ants lived would be flooded and become a lake next month. Charlie was horrified, realizing that his ants were in big trouble. He wanted to warn them and told them they had to move to higher ground. He was desperate to save them and expressed his frustration, fearing they would all die.

Sarah then suggested that Charlie use his ants to demonstrate something important because the ants couldn't understand him. She explained that the only way to warn them properly would be to become an ant himself. Charlie was reluctant, unwilling to give up everything he had to live like an ant. Sarah pointed out that warning them would be useless if they didn’t believe him and that they might even get mad and kill him.

Charlie admitted he didn’t love his ants that much, but Sarah corrected him, saying she knew someone who loved even more than that—God. She explained that God loves everyone because He created everything, including Charlie’s ants.

Sarah then shared the story of how people began their trouble by disobeying God, starting with Adam and Eve, whose sin was passed down to all people. Because of sin, everyone deserved to go to hell. However, God loved humanity so much that He sent His Son, Jesus, from heaven to earth.

Jesus was born as a man in a stable, lived among people, and taught them to love God and one another. Though many people rejected and hated Jesus for telling them the truth, His main purpose was to pay a terrible price by dying to remove the sins of everyone.

Charlie learned that Jesus was willing to die in the place of humanity, shedding His blood to wash away sins. Jesus died, was buried, and rose from the dead three days later. This was God’s greatest act of love, offering everlasting life to anyone who believes in Him.

Sarah explained Jesus then returned to heaven to prepare a place for those who believe, where they could live forever. Charlie asked if he was saved, and Sarah said only those who receive Jesus by faith are saved. Charlie expressed his desire to go to heaven, and Sarah guided him to pray and ask Jesus to forgive his sins and come into his heart as his Savior.

After praying, Charlie and Sarah both felt great joy. Sarah told Charlie that Jesus was now his best friend and would always be with him to help. Charlie was eager to tell everybody about Jesus.

Finally, Charlie asked others if they were saved, encouraging anyone who wasn’t to ask Jesus to be their Savior immediately, highlighting the promise of everlasting life for those who believe.

Title: Choice, The
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
The story begins with a man named George facing many choices throughout life. Some of these choices turn out well, and some do not. However, there is one choice that is more important than all the others—George must make the right decision before he dies.

George anticipates that he'll be told to choose between God and the devil, but he is told this is incorrect. Most people end up in hell because they think like him. George doesn't like hearing this and demands to be told what he needs to know.

He is warned that he has a terrible enemy, Satan, who hates him and wants him in hell forever. Satan was originally created as Lucifer to cover God's throne but became proud and rebelled against God, leading to his expulsion from heaven. Because Adam and Eve sinned after being tempted by Satan, sin entered the world and passed down to all humans, making everyone spiritually dead and destined for damnation in hell.

Satan knows there is only one way to escape hell, and he actively works to keep people from learning it. He uses religion, education, peer pressure, busyness, and sports to blind and distract people from the truth.

The message then shifts to God, who knew people were spiritually dead, so He sent His Son, Jesus Christ, to earth. Jesus lived a sinless life for 33 years, then sacrificed Himself on the cross to pay for humanity's sins. Three days later, Jesus rose from the dead, defeating death and Satan.

George is told that the only way to escape hell is through faith in Jesus Christ. Although it sounds too easy, this is the simple truth. Those who believe in Jesus and trust Him as Savior become children of God and will go to heaven after death. George learns that he does not have to choose the devil, because if he rejects Jesus, he already belongs to Satan and is condemned.

George expresses fear and concern for his friends and family, wondering how so many could be doomed. He asks about religious people who don't believe this message. George is told that Jesus said no one comes to the Father except through Him and that Jesus is the only one who can rescue from eternal damnation.

George wants to know how he can be sure this is true. The answer is that it is all recorded in the Word of God, the Bible, which is inspired and profitable for teaching and correction.

Realizing the gravity of the situation, George declares he wants to be saved immediately. He asks what he must do, and he is instructed to sincerely repent, turn to God, and believe in Jesus Christ as his Savior.

George prays for forgiveness of all his sins and asks Jesus to come into his heart, trusting Jesus as his Savior. He makes Jesus his personal choice.

Finally, the reader is invited to make their own choice—if they accept Jesus Christ, all their sins will be forgiven, and they will receive the gift of eternal life. If they do nothing, they remain condemned and one moment away from hell. The story ends with a call to choose Christ right now.

Title: Cleo
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
The Owens family was preparing for a trip, packing their car when the mother suggested, "Before we start our trip, we'd better all go back in the house to see if we forgot anything." Meanwhile, their dog Cleo, who had been sleeping peacefully in the car, suddenly became alert when a butterfly flew in. Cleo barked excitedly at the butterfly and chased it.

As the butterfly led Cleo out of the driveway and into the bushes, the Owens family drove off, unaware that Cleo had gotten lost. Three hours later, the family was on the road. Timmy asked, "We should be at the hospital tonight. Is Grandma gonna die?" His father remained serious as they continued.

Suddenly, an animal control officer appeared, holding a net, and shouted, "Hold it, mutt!" He caught Cleo in his net, much to her surprise and fear. Cleo found herself trapped in a cage along with other dogs. Timmy was devastated, shouting, "CLEO! CLEO!" from the back of the car.

The Owens family discussed their desperate situation. Timmy begged his dad, "We've gotta go back, Dad!" But his dad replied, "We can't, Tim... not for 3 days!" Timmy prayed, "Oh, dear God, please protect Cleo! And please don't let her get killed."

Timmy's mother encouraged him to eat, but Timmy was too upset, responding, "I CAN'T, Mom! I feel sick!" Then Timmy suddenly realized, "Oh, no! I forgot to put Cleo's collar on! Now they can't trace her."

At the animal control center, Cleo gave affectionate kisses to the officer despite being trapped. The officer said, "Here's your new home for 4 days." In a phone call, Timmy's dad asked a neighbor if they had seen Cleo. The neighbor said no but mentioned seeing a dog catcher yesterday.

At the hospital, the doctor delivered good news: "Your mother is going to make it." Timmy and his family gave thanks, hoping the same grace would protect Cleo.

Back at the animal control, the officer informed the family, "We've gotta get rid of 4 dogs today." Timmy's parents anxiously drove to the pound. Timmy asked how long it would take, "About 30 minutes, Timmy," his dad replied.

Once at the pound, they spotted Cleo trembling in a cage. Timmy cried out, "Dad, I hear CLEO barking! She's in HERE!" But the officer said, "Sorry, little girl."

The officer warned, "Unless I have a receipt in 10 minutes, I must put her to sleep," though payment could be made at the office. Timmy and his family hurriedly paid the fee and rescued Cleo. Timmy exclaimed, "Thank you, Lord!"

Driving home, Timmy's dad reflected, "Timmy, we learned a great lesson about the grace of God today." When asked how, he explained, "When Cleo was in that cage, she had no hope and was scheduled to die. Under the law, time had run out, but we asked for mercy to save Cleo's life."

He continued, "That man showed us grace by waiting 10 minutes until we paid to set her free. We redeemed Cleo by paying the bill."

Timmy's dad shared a personal story, "Years ago I was in deep trouble, like Cleo. I, too, had no hope! Sin had me in a cage. Satan controlled my life and if I had died, I'd have gone to hell." He cited, "For the wages of sin is death... (Romans 6:23)."

"But God, in His great love, gave me grace. He extended my life long enough for me to hear the good news."

Then Timmy's dad described learning that "God left heaven and became a man to suffer and die in my place. Jesus Christ paid the price to redeem me." He quoted, "For when we were yet without strength, in due time Christ died for the ungodly." (Romans 5:6).

Timmy's dad said he was overwhelmed by the love of God. Jesus shed His precious blood to wash away his sins, and when he received Him, he got redeemed, citing scripture.

Timmy looked determined and said, "Dad, I want to get redeemed, too." His dad encouraged him to pray, "Lord Jesus, I believe you died on the cross for me. I accept you as my personal Savior. Please come into my heart and save me so I can go to heaven. Amen."

Timmy prayed, and the family rejoiced, "Wow! I'm saved!" Timmy hugged Cleo and said, "Hey, Cleo. We both got redeemed on the same day!" And with that, the Owens family continued their journey, filled with hope and gratitude.

Title: Contract!, The
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Carter
Responses:
Once upon a time, a loud, roaring noise startled a young boy who hurried to wake his father, asking about the strange sound. The father, groggy and confused, realized the noise was hail falling fiercely outside. As he looked out, the harsh hailstorm had ravaged their crops, leaving their livelihood in ruin. The father lamented the lost crops, feeling cursed by the cruel weather.

The next morning, the father and son surveyed the damage. The fields were destroyed, and the father knew they were facing financial ruin. He considered going to the bank to borrow money, but he warned his son they were in serious trouble.

That afternoon, the father went to the bank, hoping to secure a loan. The banker, Mr. Boggs, sneered at him, reminding him that he already had a loan he couldn’t repay. Boggs warned, with a cruel smile, that the bank would soon own the farm and that he had orders to evict them if the debt wasn’t settled.

Filled with anger and frustration, the father vowed to fix this injustice, cursing Boggs for his heartlessness. But Boggs coldly retorted that many people are mistreated, and he didn’t get paid for being loved. He told the father to take his worthless son and leave, never to return.

Back at the farm, the desperate father cried out that he would sell his soul to keep the farm. This plea reached the ears of a man named B. Fox, who found the idea music to his ears.

One day, Fox knocked on the door of John Freeman (the father) and introduced himself. John doubted Fox’s offer, saying he was as poor as a church mouse. But Fox insisted John was sitting on a fortune. He explained that he had obtained a map showing treasure buried on John’s property. Fox proposed they split any treasure they found equally if John signed a contract.

John quickly agreed, but Fox warned there was a minor catch—after John died, Fox would claim his soul. John laughed off the idea but signed the contract anyway, unaware it was a pact sealed with his blood.

Fox led John to the land where the treasure was supposedly buried. John dug and soon hit an old metal box. Overjoyed, he shouted that they were rich. But Fox reminded him of his promise to fix things with Boggs.

John had a plan, and the two partners went to the bank. However, when Boggs heard about the treasure, he warned John never to return. Upon being confronted by John, Boggs was fired by the banker, ending his cruel reign.

Two weeks later, John visited his cousin Bob Goode and told him about the contract with Fox. Bob warned John that signing away his soul was a terrible mistake. John, however, insisted his soul was priceless and refused to be swayed.
