Bob explained that he was a God-fearing man who believed in doing good and following the commandments. He warned John that the "B" in B. Fox stood for Beelzebub, a satanic name, and that John would never escape the contract.

Ten years later, John was dying in his mansion. The doctor told him he only had a few weeks left to live. John lamented his foolish decision to sign the contract with the devil.

A pastor visited John, explaining that while the devil had limited power, Jesus Christ had unlimited power and wanted to save him. The pastor told John that if he turned to Jesus and accepted him into his heart, he could be freed from the contract and saved.

John eagerly accepted, asking Jesus to save him and take him to heaven.

One week later, John went to visit Bob Goode to share the wonderful news. Bob was surprised by John's condition and his newfound faith.

However, one hour later at John's funeral, Bob preached about salvation, but John's brother rejected the message. He believed his good deeds would earn him heaven, rejecting Bob's warnings.

Suddenly, a violent storm began. Lightning struck, causing a crash, and someone was thrown from a horse-drawn wagon, badly hurt. The injured person awoke in a terrifying place filled with suffering souls.

A man identified himself as B. Fox, claiming this place would be Bob Goode's eternal home. Fox gloated that he controlled everyone here except those who accepted Jesus Christ.

Bob protested, saying John was in heaven, having escaped Fox’s grasp. Fox warned him that the contract didn't matter—he had captured almost everyone else.

Thus, the tragic tale closed on a warning—a man who sold his soul for earthly riches but found eternal loss, while only faith and acceptance of salvation could truly set a person free.

Title: Crazy Wolf
Subject: Occult
Author: Chick
Responses:
In a small town, gossip spread about a woman named Old Mary, who was rumored to have gone crazy and turned away from the traditional gods of the community. People called her a traitor and warned each other against speaking with her. One man explained that he only interacted with her when necessary because she had tried to tell a little girl named Sarah about her "White God." He even took his own child away, warning her never to listen to Old Mary again.

Some villagers expressed frustration about living near Old Mary and wished they could silence her. One suggested putting curses on her. They mentioned that a medicine man had tried three times to help, but each attempt failed because something blocked his power. They asked for advice on whom to turn to for help.

Another man mentioned hearing about a powerful witch named Crazy Wolf, whose curses never failed. Only his cousin, Henry, knew where Crazy Wolf lived. They decided to have Henry contact Crazy Wolf to see if he would help them.

A week later, Henry returned having stolen hair, nail clippings, and a picture of Old Mary to bring to Crazy Wolf. Henry said he would return in six days to report if Crazy Wolf would carry out their plan to harm Old Mary by the next full moon. They eagerly awaited the outcome, confident their witchcraft would overpower Old Mary's God.

Margaret, curious, asked Henry if Crazy Wolf was a Skin Walker who had killed his brother. Henry refused to answer further, warning her she was playing with fire. On his way, Henry passed by snakes, marking his path to Crazy Wolf.

At Crazy Wolf's hideout, he was seen killing a trespasser with corpse powder, made from ground-up finger and toe tips and ear lobes of the dead. Crazy Wolf told Henry that the spirits had revealed Old Mary had turned against their god and must die. He handed Henry money and a picture of Old Mary, commanding him to leave immediately after. The full moon was crucial for their plan.

Three days later, Henry assured Margaret that Crazy Wolf had agreed and said Old Mary would be no more by the full moon. Margaret felt reassured despite hearing about how terrifying and evil Crazy Wolf was, resolving to hide when he came.

Meanwhile, Old Mary faced hostility from the villagers, who cursed her, threatened her, and declared that Crazy Wolf was coming for her at the full moon. In a heated argument, Old Mary told them their god had white skin and argued Jesus was a Jew, not white, but the villagers insisted their sun god was stronger.

Mary reached out to her pastor for prayer and help. She told him about Crazy Wolf and that he was a powerful witch and a Skin Walker. The pastor acknowledged the danger, reminding Mary that she was not alone and that he had alerted their church for help.

As the full moon rose, Crazy Wolf invoked dark powers and summoned spirits. Falling into a trance, his evil spirit began to rise and transform. Meanwhile, Mary prayed fervently to Jesus for protection, asking for a miracle and for angels to guard her. She entrusted herself fully to God’s will.

Suddenly, there was loud banging, and Crazy Wolf shouted that he would kill Mary and rip out her heart. Everyone heard his voice and trembled. But then, God answered Mary’s prayers. An angel appeared and fought the "Skin Walker," eventually pulling the evil spirit back into Crazy Wolf’s body.

Crazy Wolf was now facing the "king of terrors," a powerful being who had come to punish him for his evil deeds. Satan stripped Crazy Wolf of his magic powers, leaving him a shattered mess. Mary prayed for Crazy Wolf’s soul, asking that he be saved and go to heaven, even though others questioned mercy for such a monster.

Three weeks later, a surprising visitor knocked on Mary’s door. It was Crazy Wolf, asking to come in. Mary welcomed him, offering food. He confessed that he was afraid because of what he had seen of Mary’s Jesus protecting her. He asked if Jesus was the source of such power.

Mary explained Jesus created everything, would judge him after death, and was the only one who could save him. Though reluctant, Crazy Wolf was curious and asked to be taught more. Mary shared how Jesus died for every sin people have committed and rose from the dead, making it possible to escape hell.

She explained how easy it was to accept God’s gift. Quoting Scripture, she told how confessing and believing in Jesus could save his soul. Crazy Wolf agreed to repent and believe, trusting Jesus with all his heart.

Mary later told her pastor that Crazy Wolf was at her door ready to be saved. The pastor welcomed him warmly.

However, Margaret remained hostile. She warned that Crazy Wolf had stolen money from her and urged others to kill him. When Crazy Wolf returned to confront Margaret, she shot and killed him, ending the terror he had caused.

Though Crazy Wolf’s physical life ended, his soul was saved by Jesus. In heaven, God welcomed Billie Wolf, his new name, praising him for believing. This contrasted Margaret, who had rejected Jesus and descended into hell.

The villagers learned that only Jesus saves. Trusting religion, idols, or other gods was futile compared to faith in Jesus Christ. The story closed with the Scripture urging belief in Jesus for salvation and eternal life.

Thus, the tale told of hatred, fear, spiritual warfare, repentance, and the power of Jesus to transform even the darkest hearts.

Title: Creator or Liar?
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth. He made man from the dust of the earth and established fellowship with him. Man was then given a choice to obey God's commandments or to disobey. However, man chose evil and disobeyed God's direct instructions. This broke the fellowship with God, as God cannot have fellowship with sinners, resulting in man being lost.

As man multiplied and covered the earth, violence became widespread. Due to man's wickedness, God decided to destroy the earth's inhabitants with a flood, sparing only one righteous man, Noah, and his family, who were saved in the ark.

Despite this, mankind multiplied again and continued to choose evil, refusing to serve God. God selected the Israelites as His chosen nation and gave them laws to live by. God loved them and sent prophets to teach them obedience to His laws, but they rebelled and killed the prophets.

God instructed His people to offer sacrifices, using a lamb to atone for their sins. Despite this, they continually failed and turned away from the Lord. 

To redeem humanity, God the Son left heaven to take human form. Jesus Himself would become the sacrifice, the Lamb of Atonement for mankind's sins. Jesus was born in Bethlehem to a virgin named Mary. By the power of the Holy Spirit, she conceived Jesus, who was the Savior. 

Jesus grew up without sin, teaching love for God and neighbors, and healed the sick. Though challenged and crucified as a threat to authority, no fault or sin was found in Him. He was the only perfect life ever lived.

Because He was without sin, Jesus was not subject to death but voluntarily took mankind’s penalty—death and separation from God—upon Himself. Through His righteousness, believers are restored to fellowship with God when they accept Christ as their master.

Jesus fulfilled over 30 prophecies by allowing Himself to be crucified. However, Satan was defeated when Jesus rose from the dead three days later. Jesus then returned to heaven, instructing His followers to share this story with the world.

In the future, all who reject Jesus as Savior will die in their sins and be judged guilty by Jesus Himself. The Bible states the lost will be cast into the lake of fire, prepared for the devil, his angels, and all who serve Satan instead of God.

But those who believe Jesus died for their sins, repent, and receive Him will enter into the joy of the Lord and go to heaven. For God so loved the world that He gave His only Son so that whoever believes in Him will not perish but have everlasting life.

Today, many claim Jesus was a liar or deny His divinity, but you must decide whether to accept or reject Jesus. If He was a liar, then forget Him. But if Jesus is who He claims to be, your decision will determine where you spend eternity.

What will you do with Jesus Christ, the Creator of the universe? Will you reject Him or accept Him? Of all decisions, this will be the most important, for when you meet Him face to face, He will be your Savior or your Judge.

Title: Crisis, The
Subject: Jehovahs Witness
Author: Chick
Responses:
A little girl who had been hit by a car was rushed into the emergency room, bleeding severely. Hospital staff quickly announced, "We've got a bleeder!" The nurse on the phone explained the situation: the girl was bleeding to death, and her family were Jehovah's Witnesses who would absolutely refuse a blood transfusion. The doctor expressed frustration but knew he had no time to argue and had to get back to the child immediately.

In the waiting room, Doug and Donna sat anxiously. Donna worried out loud, and Doug reassured her that he was sure their decision was right. A hospital employee asked about what had happened, and Doug explained they had been out witnessing when the girl was struck by a car. The employee asked if they were Christians, and Doug confirmed they were Jehovah's Witnesses.

A nurse informed a doctor that Chaplain Barnes was talking to Doug and Donna, trying to convince them. The doctor muttered that if the chaplain couldn’t persuade them soon, the hospital would have a “little corpse” on their hands.

Inside the waiting room, Chaplain Barnes began discussing their beliefs with Doug and Donna. Barnes expressed disagreement with their faith, especially concerning the deity of Christ, which Jehovah’s Witnesses did not accept. Doug confirmed his belief in Christ’s deity. Barnes asked to review some Bible verses, including Isaiah 43:11, questioning the translations used by the Jehovah’s Witnesses, specifically the New World Translation.

The conversation grew tense as Barnes recited scripture showing Jesus is God Almighty, contrasting it with the Witnesses’ teachings. Doug countered with verses from Acts 4:12 and other Scriptures to explain their beliefs, causing Barnes to point out contradictions. The two debated the nature of God, the Trinity, and Jesus' identity.

Meanwhile, hospital security was alerted to keep the conversation between the chaplain and the family uninterrupted. Barnes presented more evidence from Watchtower headquarters, revealing printouts about Donna’s prior trouble with the elders for reading anti-Witness materials and her repentance afterward.

He challenged Doug on the Watchtower Society’s links to Jesuit sources and corrupt Roman Catholic manuscripts, questioning their opposition to Catholicism. Doug and Donna became uneasy, realizing that the Watchtower might be more connected to the Vatican than they thought.

Barnes pressed further, pointing out failed prophecies such as the Watchtower’s prediction of the return of biblical figures in 1925, which never materialized. He also highlighted multiple date changes for the Battle of Armageddon, used by the Society to cover their mistakes. Doug expressed surprise and admitted he hadn’t realized this before. Barnes insisted that if the Watchtower was wrong about prophecies, perhaps it was also wrong about blood transfusions.

The chapel conversation grew heated, but Doug remained skeptical. Barnes explained the biblical references to blood bans focused on eating animal blood, not medical transfusions. He quoted Mark 7:15, emphasizing that spiritual defilement comes from within a person, not from external sources like medical treatments.

Barnes shared his own past, revealing that he was once a devoted Jehovah’s Witness who had tried to gain salvation by selling Watchtower literature door-to-door. He recounted working undercover following suspect members and realizing the leadership’s corruption and false teachings. Meanwhile, Doug and Donna listened, unsure but attentive.

Barnes argued that the Watchtower Society had led them to believe in a false gospel and warned that salvation could not be earned through works like selling literature. He read from the Bible about salvation by grace through faith and urged them to trust the Bible over the Watchtower’s words.

Desperate, Doug finally called for the doctor to proceed with the transfusion. Donna cried out for the doctor, pleading, “Please!” The doctor agreed without hesitation, relieved. The nurse smiled, saying the girl would survive thanks to the transfusion.

Doug stood firm, declaring he was no longer uncertain. He accepted Jesus as Jehovah and his Savior, feeling freed from the restrictions of Watchtower teachings.

The story closed noting that for more information on Jehovah’s Witnesses, readers could consult the book “Answers to My Jehovah’s Witness Friends” by Thomas Heinze.

Title: Dark Dungeons
Subject: Occult
Author: Carter
Responses:
A group of friends was playing a game of Dungeons & Dragons. One player, the Dungeon Master, declared that the thief Black Leaf had not found a poison trap and was therefore dead. Marcie, the player of Black Leaf, panicked and protested that she was going to die in the game. The Dungeon Master insisted, telling Marcie that she was dead and did not exist anymore in the game. Marcie begged for help, begging not to quit the game.

Debbie, another player, was told by her Dungeon Master that her cleric character had been raised to the 8th level and that it was time to learn how to truly cast spells. Debbie was encouraged that she had the personality for it.

Through intense occult training, Debbie was prepared to enter a witches' coven. She was to become a priestess of the craft and join the Temple of Diana. Debbie explained to Ms. Frost that last night she had cast her first spell, describing it as real power. Ms. Frost told her that there was much more to come.

When asked, Debbie revealed she had cast a mind bondage spell on her father, who had been trying to stop her from playing D&D. The result was that her father bought her $200 worth of new D&D figures and manuals, much to her delight.

Later that week, Debbie was informed Marcie was on the phone and very upset. Debbie was busy, so Ms. Frost took the call for her. It turned out Marcie had shut herself in her room for weeks, distraught over her character's death in the game, feeling as if a part of her had died.

Marcie’s distress escalated, leading to a tragic moment where Debbie screamed that Marcie didn’t have to do something irreversible. A note was found from Marcie stating that it was her fault Black Leaf had died and she couldn’t face life alone.

Debbie was wracked with guilt, unable to stop thinking about Marcie and questioning how it had come to this. Ms. Frost insisted Debbie prioritize her spiritual growth through the game rather than Marcie’s life, dismissing Marcie as a loser.

Debbie questioned the faith’s teachings, troubled that Marcie’s spirit had been too weak and worried about the harm done. Ms. Frost warned Debbie to let her character Elfstar take over and that Debbie was losing control. Debbie resisted, wanting to be herself rather than her game persona.

Debbie confided in Mike that she felt lost and everything was falling apart. Mike, knowing the spiritual battle Debbie faced, urged her to turn to Jesus. He invited her to a meeting where a speaker who left witchcraft would talk about overcoming this darkness.

At the meeting, the speaker cautioned those involved in the occult that they were trapped in bondage, with their power only leading to destruction. He explained the freedom Jesus provides and urged repentance, instructing people to burn their occult materials.

The speaker called for anyone wanting Jesus as their savior to come forward. Debbie cried out for help, and at the altar, she repented, asking Jesus to be her savior and commanding the occult spirits to leave her in Jesus' name.

That night, Debbie burned all her occult materials, thanking the Lord for setting her free. The message ended with an invitation to believe in Jesus and remember the moment when God saved their soul.

Title: Death Cookie, The
Subject: Catholicism
Author: Chick
Responses:
Here is the comic strip turned into a written story:

---

A man pondered how he could gain control over many people without having an army. Another figure told him it was simple: make the people believe that their immortal souls are in his hands. If he could convince a person that he had the power to send them to Hell, that person would do anything to save their soul.

The man was skeptical and said nobody would believe such a thing. But the other assured him to try it, promising it would work, and offered to guide him step-by-step. The man hesitated, doubting how people could believe he had such power, but finally agreed to trust this guide.

He was taught that because man is naturally religious, he must appear very holy. It was not enough to pray a lot; he needed to be mysterious and different, speaking in ways that no one understood, and surround himself with rituals like burning many candles.

The guide emphasized that it was crucial for the people to believe that only he and his "Holy Helpers" knew God, which would grant him great power and riches. To draw the people in, they had to see him as their spiritual leader — their Papa — and they must become like his children, loving him if they wished to live.

Next, they needed a god that people could see, touch, and pray to. The guide presented a simple object: a cookie. The man was shocked and considered it insane, thinking no one would believe that. But the guide explained that this had been done before in ancient Egypt, where the sun was worshipped as "The Great God Osiris," through round wafers on altars made of unleavened bread.

Egyptian priests would pray over the wafers, claiming they miraculously turned into the flesh of Osiris. This moment, called "transubstantiation," made the people eat their god, even though it tasted just like ordinary bread — and they dared not question the priests.

Inspired, the two devised a plan to have their cookie become a "death cookie" for anyone who opposed their holy work. They believed that the people would die for this god, love it, and worship it, truly believing it was almighty God.

The scheme began with the Papa and his Holy Helpers dressing in religious costumes and dazzling the people with ceremonies, declaring themselves as the spiritual parents of the people’s souls. Using the "transubstantiation" ritual, the cookie appeared unchanged but was claimed to be their God. The people, out of fear and reverence, bowed down and served this strange new idol. The Papa had gained absolute control.

They then renamed their religious system "Mama Church," teaching that only through this church could people reach heaven. They threatened the people that if they didn’t obey and continued to eat the "Jesus cookie," they would lose their immortal souls. The people grew fearful of the church and its magic, knowing the cookie-god meant life or death.

A problem soon arose when people began reading the sacred writings and realized they’d been tricked. Fearful, the Holy Papa called his religious advisor, the only trusted one, to devise a plan. They told the people that the scriptures were dangerous, and only the Holy Helpers could understand them. Anyone reading the scriptures would go crazy.

To further confuse and control the people, the advisor added many versions of Jesus to "Mama Church" — the baby Jesus at Christmas, Jesus on the cross, angry Jesus in heaven, and more. The Holy Papa himself became a type of Jesus. The children were kept in darkness about God’s first commandment forbidding other gods.

"Mama Church" became so rich and powerful that even kings feared her. One day, a child found the sacred scriptures, and chaos was about to erupt when they read Jesus’ true words about salvation through belief in Him alone. But the Holy Workers passed laws to stop the spread of this truth, threatening death to anyone who said the cookie-god wasn’t really Jesus or who didn’t eat it.

The Holy Papa became furious as the children started leaving. To maintain control, a brutal Inquisition began. Tortures and deaths threatened millions as the church sought to destroy anyone opposing their control. The struggle was a battle for survival of "Mother Church."

The Catholic Church inflicted horrific torture from 1200 to 1808, with 68 million victims under Satan’s influence, using magic and witchcraft through control of the wafer god.

The church passed cruel laws at the Council of Trent stating that denying the real body and blood in the wafer made someone a heretic, punishable by death. Kings and presidents feared these laws, which remain firmly in place.

Another law decreed that the cookie must be worshiped as God himself, and anyone denying this was condemned as a heretic. The cookie was carried in religious parades and adored as God Almighty, making it a powerful weapon of control.

The creation of the wafer god was the greatest religious con job in history. One billion people live in fear of losing salvation if the priest refuses them the wafer god. This idol keeps people in bondage, making it very hard to break free.

The Lord Jesus hates this wafer god because it is an idol, and behind every idol is a demon. The Vatican is marked for judgment and destruction by the Lord for blasphemy against Jesus.

Jesus orders believers to leave this occult system before it is destroyed. "Come out of her, my people," warns Revelation.

---

This summarizes the story presented in the comic strip, covering the deception, control, rituals, and dangers associated with the wafer god.

Title: Deceived, The
Subject: Islam
Author: Carter
Responses:
Yusuf was deeply troubled, feeling sick after reading something that devastated him. His friend Adil asked what was wrong, and Yusuf shared that they had been betrayed. Yusuf explained that a passage he read stated, "God said, Let us make man in our image..." and then created Adam. Adil was confused and questioned if it could be Allah speaking, but Yusuf insisted it wasn't. He warned that if this was true, they were all lost.

Yusuf recounted the story of Adam and Eve's sin, after which the earth was destroyed by a flood, sparing only Noah, his family, and the animals on the ark. From the ruins of Babylon, where Nimrod ruled with his mother Semiramis, a new evil religion emerged, controlled by Satan. Semiramis was worshiped as the "Queen of Heaven," and behind each idol was a demon controlling those who bowed down.

God’s hatred for idols was shown when He gave Moses the Ten Commandments, which forbade making or worshiping graven images or any likeness of anything. Yusuf and Adil reflected on how idols caused destruction because demons controlled those who worshiped them. They then discussed Jesus Christ, who shed His blood to wash away sins and free people from demonic control. Jesus died, was buried, rose from the dead, and ascended to heaven. His followers spread the word that He was the Son of God and Creator of the universe, though many of Ishmael’s children did not believe.

Satan sought to destroy true Christianity by moving his religion from Babylon to Rome. Many followers of Jesus were martyred or forced underground, while Roman Catholicism was born, ruling from the Vatican with the "Queen of Heaven" as a central idol. The popes wanted to rule Jerusalem but needed an army to kill the Jews and destroy true Christianity.

At that time, Arab tribes were divided, each worshiping its own idols but honoring the "House of God," the Kaaba in Mecca, which was believed to be built by Abraham and his son Ishmael. The Kaaba housed 360 idols, each controlled by powerful demons causing problems for the people.

Yusuf read that Vatican spies searched for a leader for a new religion and found a youth named Muhammad from the Quraysh tribe of Mecca. Khadijah, a beautiful Roman Catholic woman who lived in a convent, was tasked with marrying Muhammad as part of a trap set by the conspirators. If their plan worked, soon the Arab world would be serving the pope.

Around 610 A.D., Muhammad claimed to have had a vision, declaring himself the messenger of Allah, and thus Islam was born. When Muhammad declared, "There is no god but Allah, and Muhammad is his Prophet," Islam spread rapidly. Yusuf questioned where the name Allah came from, since Abraham, Moses, and Jesus never used that name for God.

Two popes secretly financed Muhammad’s military in exchange for Jerusalem. In 630 A.D., Muhammad invaded Mecca and cleared the Kaaba of idols. However, one of the idols belonged to Muhammad's own tribe and was called "Allah." Yusuf was horrified that Muhammad blasphemed God by calling his idol "The Almighty." Adil exclaimed that Islam was a false hope and that they were lost in their sins.

They discussed how Father Abraham never called upon "Allah," but rather Jehovah, and that the Bible speaks of the Father (Jehovah), the Word (Jesus Christ), and the Holy Ghost, stating they are one. Yusuf explained how Jesus was the Word made flesh, who came to save the lost, and that this was the path to salvation.

Jesus shed His blood to wash away sins, rose from the dead, and offers eternal life to those who believe. While Muhammad remained in his grave, Jesus loves and never forsakes His followers. Yusuf and Adil both prayed, accepting Jesus and feeling freed from sin. They realized they had been deceived by dark religious forces—the "Queen of Heaven" and "Allah"—used to keep them in bondage.

Yusuf acknowledged they must tell their people the truth, even if it puts them in danger. In the end, everyone must choose between Jesus Christ and the deceivers. Those who choose Jesus will reign with Him in heaven, while those who choose the idolatrous "Queen of Heaven" or "Allah" face eternal damnation.

Title: Demon's Nightmare, A
Subject: Hell
Author: Chick
Responses:
Once upon a time, two devils were on a city rooftop, tasked with watching humans below. They alerted each other of an enemy sighted and prepared for action. The devils observed a man walking, and one devil worried, "Here comes nothing but trouble! What could he be up to now?"

The man walked into a house where three people sat. He asked to sit down, and they agreed, telling an old goat to keep moving. The man asked if they had ever heard the story about when God was murdered by man. Shocked and scared by the implications, the people responded with concern, warning that it was a dangerous topic that might set them up for a kill. They needed to break up the fact from the tactic.

The story began, tracing back to creation when the Lord Jesus created the heavens and the earth. One said, "Man oh man—look at that! What a doll!" while another mockingly dismissed the tactic. The man explained that God is holy and will not allow sin in His presence. The Bible said all have sinned and come short of God's glory, and by nature, man hates God. He asked if mankind is lost and headed to hell, to which the others confirmed.

The man continued, explaining God’s love and how He provided an escape through His only begotten Son, Jesus. The devil overheard and shouted, "I hate those words! Now we're going to lose another good man!" The man said that Jesus became flesh to be a sacrifice and shed His precious blood to wash away sins. One devil lamented that they never knew Jesus would rise from the dead, or they would have stopped the crucifixion. Another devil angrily told him to shut up and drop the subject.

The man insisted on surrendering life to Jesus to become a new person and spend eternity living with Him. The devils were frustrated but acknowledged this meant war. The man was advised to read the Bible continuously, keep faith, and remember the community of believers. The woman felt changed, and the devils feared reporting the loss.

Dark forces ordered their minions to keep the kid away from the Bible at all costs, warning of extreme danger. The devils planned to crucify the kid if necessary but worried what the family and friends would say about the new Christian.

The family reacted with shock and scorn, worried this new faith would ruin their social reputation and name, calling him a fanatic. The youth’s mother urged him to hide the change so as not to upset friends or cause embarrassment. Despite warnings, the young man faced temptations and partying attempts from old friends, who mocked his faith and pressured him to join in. He refused, enduring laughter and insults.

The kid heard about Jesus’s crucifixion and resurrection again from a preacher and pledged to take the faith seriously. The devils despaired but knew the battle was only beginning.

The family continued to resist faith. The young man began attending a church led by a modern pastor promoting love and the second coming of Christ. The devils sneered but acknowledged its influence.

The boy’s brother spotted the change and threatened trouble with their old friends. Despite social pressure, the boy held firm, making new Christian friends and attending prayer meetings. The devils attempted to discourage him by calling prayer meetings useless, but the young man persisted.

One evening, the devils reported failure after the boy attended a prayer meeting, striking a key blow against them. The enemy forces vowed to dig deeper to stop the spreading gospel of Christ.

In the end, the devils pleaded with readers to reject the message and burn the book, warning that accepting Christ meant eternal separation from them. The story closed urging everyone to choose wisely, for faith in Jesus leads to everlasting life, while rejection leads elsewhere.

Thus, the comic narrated a classic battle of good versus evil, faith versus temptation, and the power of belief to change a person's life despite opposition.

Title: Devil's Night, The
Subject: Halloween
Author: Carter
Responses:
One day, a mother and her young daughter spotted a figure of Dracula at a Halloween display. The little girl found it scary and expressed her dislike, but her mother assured her that they would buy a spooky costume soon. The girl declared her love for Halloween, calling it her favorite holiday.

At school, their teacher, Ms. Henn, announced that they would draw Halloween pictures that day and come to school dressed in costumes the next day. The children shared their costume plans: some would be witches, werewolves, or wanted to draw spiders. Ms. Henn chuckled and told an older man, Mr. Harvey, that it seemed all her students loved Halloween except for one little girl named Susy, who had a stone in her shoe.

Susy’s grandpa emphasized that everyone must obey Ms. Henn, as she was an authority, and insisted that all the kids wear costumes. The next day, Ms. Henn was thrilled to see all the kids in costumes and announced a prize for the winner. However, when Susy came out dressed not in a typical Halloween costume but in a historical-style outfit claiming it was a costume, Ms. Henn was displeased. Susy’s classmates hated her for not conforming.

Later, another student noted how angry Ms. Henn was at Susy. Susy explained that she hated Halloween because it was too spooky. Her mom loved it, although Susy didn't, especially since her mom watched vampire shows that upset her.

Susy confessed she was afraid of ghosts, monsters, and spiders. When asked why Halloween was like that, Susy explained that it belonged to the devil and was his night—one that witches loved.

Susy then shared what her grandpa told her about Halloween’s origins in old England, where people didn’t know God and lived in fear. Pagan priests, who were in control, were evil and involved in occult practices, serving Satan. They taught that Saman, the Lord of Death, called back souls, frightening people.

These priests lit huge fires, wore masks, and danced to drive away evil spirits. They would demand offerings from households, and if the families had no food, they threatened to take a child for sacrifice. When trick-or-treating started, it was a method to take a child for ritual sacrifice, leaving pumpkins with faces as warnings so their victims would be alone.

Susy assured that although such things don't seem to continue, real sacrifices still happened, and every year animals like cats and dogs were found dead as Halloween sacrifices. Many kids disappeared before Halloween, thought to be taken by satanic priests.

Susy went on, explaining there are still people today serving Satan, just as badly as before, which is why kids must be careful during Halloween. Teens often involve themselves in witchcraft, serving the devil. Although God hates witchcraft, witches don’t care and will end up in hell.

Susy thanked her grandpa for teaching her about Jesus, which would keep her from hell with those who serve the devil.

Buffy, curious, asked who Jesus was. Susy explained Jesus is very real and currently in heaven, preparing to rule the world. Jesus created everything, including the universe, heaven, angels, and people. Buffy concluded Jesus must be God, which Susy confirmed, but warned that the devil has a role too.

Susy recounted how one fallen angel tried to rule heaven, turning angels against God. Those angels were cast out and sent to Earth, where their leader became Satan, the devil.

God created Adam and Eve perfect, putting them on Earth, but Satan tricked them into disobeying God, causing sin and separation from heaven. Now all people are sinners, which keeps them from entering heaven.

Jesus came to save people from sin by teaching love and forgiveness. The devil opposed Him, and Jesus was arrested, beaten, and nailed to a cross to take the punishment for sins. Jesus died, but God’s blood saved humanity. Three days later, Jesus rose from the dead, defeating the devil and opening heaven’s doors.

When Buffy asked how to get into heaven, Susy said to believe in Jesus, pray, ask Him to forgive sins, invite Him into the heart, and accept Him as Lord and Savior.

Buffy was no longer afraid, feeling wonderful and wanting to reach other kids for Jesus, especially on Halloween night. Susy explained their plan: since the devil and witches love Halloween due to witchcraft, she and her grandpa fill plastic bags with candy and include comics that tell kids how to get to heaven, battling for the souls of children.

They went out trick-or-treating, giving out the comics and candy. The story closed by asking who the reader would follow: the old devil, destined for hell, or Jesus, who loves them and offers salvation. It ended with a biblical quote inviting belief in Jesus for salvation.

Title: Dirty Diamond, The
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Carter
Responses:
Charlie’s mailman was worried because he hadn’t seen Mr. Petersen for two days. He knocked on Charlie’s door asking if he was inside, but got no response. Charlie wondered if Mr. Petersen was okay. Soon, a lady who lived nearby told the mailman that Mr. Petersen always waited for his mail and that she was worried about him. They decided to check on Mr. Petersen together.

When they got to Mr. Petersen's house, they found the door unlocked. They called out for Mr. Petersen, but no one answered. The lady went to check the backyard and her son ran to get his dad. The son found Mr. Petersen lying outside and feared he might be dead. However, upon checking, it appeared Mr. Petersen was still alive. They immediately called an ambulance.

Later that night, at the hospital, the doctor explained that Mr. Petersen had two broken legs. He assured them that in about three months, Mr. Petersen should recover fully. Mr. Petersen expressed his gratitude, saying he wouldn’t have survived if he hadn’t been found.

Three months later, Mr. Petersen visited the family who helped him and thanked them warmly. He gave them a cake as a token of appreciation. Then, he revealed something special he wanted to share—a story about his great-great grandfather, Jedidiah, who was an engineer in South Africa searching for diamonds with his son, Randolph. Their work took place in old mine shafts, where, during an earthquake, Randolph became trapped under debris. Jedidiah dug desperately to save him but was too late.

Randolph’s hand held a large, uncut diamond. Jedidiah kept it uncut as a reminder of his son. Before he died, Jedidiah made a special request in his will—that the diamond should be appraised or cut. His family honored this, but by the time Mr. Petersen got it, the diamond looked dirty and worthless.

Mr. Petersen announced that he had just learned he had inoperable cancer and had no kinfolk or friends left, only the family who found him. He wished to give them the diamond. The family took it home to discuss.

However, his wife scorned the diamond, calling it glass and demanding it be returned immediately, despite her husband's feelings. The diamond was returned, and shortly after, Mr. Petersen died. Without a will, the state took possession of his property.

Six months later, government officials informed the family they found an uncut stone among Mr. Petersen's belongings and appraised it as worth just over 4 million dollars. This news was shocking and caused the woman who initially rejected it to faint. The family was deeply regretful, mourning lost fortune.

Later, a lawyer visited them, recognizing their hardship but showing them hope. He explained that God had prepared a "will" for them. This "will," unlike others, didn’t require anyone to die for its gifts. The lawyer shared how God had died in the person of Jesus to take away sins and offer forgiveness and eternal life—this spiritual gift was more valuable than any diamond.

The lawyer urged them to accept God’s gift through faith in Jesus. Though confused and skeptical at first, especially with questions about God’s death, the lawyer explained that Jesus’ sacrifice was to cleanse humanity from sin and offer a free gift.

He described that those who accept this gift and believe in Jesus are given eternal life and inherit everything God promised. Those who do not accept will face judgment. He stressed that this gift is free and available to all.

Moved by this message, they expressed a desire to receive God’s gift, and the lawyer invited them to a moment of faith and prayer.

The story closed by inviting the reader to consider this greatest gift, freely given through belief in Jesus, referencing biblical assurances of salvation and eternal life.

Title: Don't Read That Book!
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
The story begins by introducing the Holy Bible as the most controversial, most hated, and most loved book ever printed. The Bible has caused the death of countless numbers and has given eternal life to millions. Throughout history, Satan has relentlessly attacked those who love this book, using every type of imaginable attack. Now, in the 21st century, Satan employs a new clever technique to keep Christians from reading it.

This latest attack is launched through films and television. The villain in stories is often depicted as a Bible-quoting nut, usually portrayed worse than Frankenstein. Christians are warned by others not to read the Bible because it might cause them to "go nutty." This, according to the narrative, is a victory for Satan.

In some countries, Christians are imprisoned because of their love for the Bible, finding comfort only in the scriptures they memorized before imprisonment. The story poses a reflective question: how would one fare in such a predicament? It suggests that this situation might be faced by others soon.

The narrative then shifts focus to the greatest weapon Satan uses in homes—the television, humorously called "the boob tube." Statistics show the average daily viewing time is about three and a half hours. The story encourages viewers to stop wasting time on one-hour TV shows and instead dedicate that time to studying the Word of God.

To aid in Bible study, numerous courses have been created but often go unused due to indifference or laziness. A special book is provided as an assignment, promising not to self-destruct and urging the reader to keep it handy.

The story shares an example of a person who glows with the love of Jesus, highlighting that his secret is reading over twenty chapters a day while managing multiple responsibilities, including two jobs and teaching ministry. However, the reader is only asked to read five chapters a day.

A list of common excuses for not reading the Bible is presented, such as lack of time, tiredness, feeling sleepy, misunderstanding the Bible, or fear of losing marbles. The story emphatically rejects the idea of quitting once the Bible reading is underway, likening the need to reading the Bible to breathing—essential and life-sustaining.

Imagining a future conversation with Habakkuk in the afterlife, the story humorously suggests that one might feel silly for not having read the Bible. The program then sets a goal: to read five chapters daily, promising that by the end of eight months, more chapters will be covered than the entire Bible contains.

A toolkit is provided for study, including colored pencils, a notebook, and a Bible, along with a prayer to ask the Holy Spirit for guidance in understanding scripture. The method involves marking favorite or exceptional verses as one reads, with the encouragement that the Holy Spirit will reveal precious insights in familiar chapters.

The story warns against speed reading, emphasizing retention over speed to properly absorb God’s Word. It introduces a reading plan of five chapters daily, each from a specific list of books in the Bible, with repetition schedules to help reinforce learning.

Detailed lists are given for the reading plan, covering various books from Genesis to Revelation, each set to repeat after a certain number of days. The first day’s reading includes five chapters, each from a different list, and subsequent days move on to the next chapters in each category.

The reader is encouraged to use their own color code to trace previous readings so that their Bible will eventually look like a rainbow. This detailed and structured approach aims to make Bible study systematic and rewarding, leading the reader closer to a successful Christian life grounded in scripture.

Title: Doom Town
Subject: Homosexuality
Author: Carter & 3rd
Responses:
The story begins with a passionate crowd rallying against homosexuality, claiming that 12% of children will grow up to be lesbians and homosexuals. They declare that these children will not be labeled with derogatory terms and vow to save their children from what they consider a moral threat. Signs in the crowd proclaim that hate is not a family value.

Amidst the protests, there's a fierce debate about AIDS research funding and blood donations. Some claim that if research money isn't given by a certain time, gay men should donate blood, even if it means "blood terrorism." Others express fear that AIDS threatens the nation’s blood supply and call it cold-blooded murder. Religious protesters urge calm and advocate for bringing Christ's love to those they see as lost souls, though they are warned not to preach, fearing violent backlash from the hateful crowd.

A man offers his perspective, stating that the protesters are repeating the sins of Sodom and Gomorrah from the Bible, about 4,000 years late. He tries to share the Bible’s story, but is met with resistance, with some refusing to hear anything biblical or preachy.

The narrative then shifts to the biblical story of Abraham and his nephew Lot. Abraham and Lot had so many cattle that their herdsmen quarreled over pasture lands. To resolve this, Abraham generously allowed Lot to choose whichever land he wanted. Lot, driven by greed, chose the fertile plains of Jordan, where the city of Sodom was located—a decision he didn't realize would doom him.

Abraham settled in the plains of Mamre, serving the Lord, while Lot made the grave mistake of living in Sodom. The city was inhabited by wicked men who sinned greatly against God. The city’s degeneration included perverse acts, even endangering children, and Lot was deeply troubled by their lifestyle.

God and two angels appeared to Abraham, informing him that Sodom's days were numbered. Abraham pleaded with God to spare the city if as few as 50 righteous people could be found there. God agreed, but as the count lowered to 10 righteous souls, it became clear that no one truly loved God in Sodom.

That evening, Lot saw the two angels entering the city and hurried to get them off the streets to prevent the Sodomites from assaulting them. The men of Sodom surrounded Lot's house, demanding the angels be handed over to be sexually abused. Lot protested, even offering his virgin daughters instead, but the mob was unrelenting and violent.

The angels pulled Lot inside and blinded the lust-filled mob. Despite this, the mob searched furiously for Lot’s door but eventually gave up and left. The angels warned Lot to leave immediately, but he hesitated until they physically dragged him, his wife, and two daughters out of the city.

As dawn broke, Abraham witnessed from a distance as God rained fire and brimstone upon Sodom and Gomorrah, utterly destroying those who had rebelled. This was a divine act of judgment against the sin of homosexuality.

The story continues with a warning from Scripture, comparing rebellion against God to witchcraft and stating that all who rebel will be cast into the lake of fire. God's laws given to Moses explicitly condemn homosexuality.

Back in contemporary times, a man named Sean is confronted by friends who question why he speaks out so strongly against homosexuality, noting the backlash he faces. Sean explains that he cares deeply for homosexuals and wants them to understand they face a terrible judgment according to Scripture.

However, Sean also shares the good news—that God loved homosexuals and wants to save and set them free through Jesus Christ. He emphasizes that Jesus shed His blood on the cross to cleanse all sins, including homosexuality, and that anyone who trusts Christ can be forgiven and made new.

In the closing scene, Sean prays to Jesus, asking to be saved. The story encourages readers to accept Jesus as their personal Savior to escape the sin of homosexuality and find eternal salvation, ending with a biblical promise about the new life given to those who believe.

Title: Dreamer, The
Subject: Bible Stories
Author: Carter & 3rd
Responses:
Jacob had twelve sons, but Joseph was his favorite. One day, Jacob asked Joseph to go check on his brothers and the sheep as Joseph took a long journey to do this. Joseph was specially gifted by God with dreams in which he saw all his family bowing down to him. When Joseph shared these dreams with his brothers, they were furious. They declared they would never bow to him and questioned who he thought he was.

Joseph’s brothers were deadly, vicious men who hated him deeply. When they saw him coming, they plotted to kill him. However, Reuben stopped the killing and instead, they stripped Joseph of his multi-colored coat, a special coat their father had given him, and threw him into a dry, sandy pit, hoping this would end Joseph’s dreams and envy.

Later, seeing a caravan nearby, Joseph’s brothers hatched another plan. They sold Joseph for twenty pieces of silver to some traders. To convince their father that Joseph was dead, they dipped Joseph’s coat in blood and showed it to Jacob. Heartbroken and horrified, Jacob mourned Joseph's supposed death, driving everyone crazy with his despair.

Joseph didn’t complain as he was taken to Egypt; in fact, he never complained. He trusted God and believed his dreams would still come true. In Egypt, Joseph was bought by Potiphar, the captain of Pharaoh’s guards. God blessed everything Potiphar owned, so Potiphar respected and trusted Joseph, putting him in charge of his house.

However, Potiphar’s wife desired Joseph and tried repeatedly to seduce him. Joseph refused, saying it would be wicked and against God’s law. Whenever Potiphar was away, she would act innocent when servants were near but try to seduce Joseph when no one was around.

Eventually, she caught Joseph alone and tried to force herself on him. Joseph resisted, but she was furious and decided to get revenge. She called all the servants, falsely accusing Joseph of trying to rape her. Believing his wife’s lies, Potiphar was enraged and had Joseph thrown into prison.

Despite the injustice, God was still with Joseph. God touched the heart of the prison warden, who put Joseph in charge of the prison. One day, two of Pharaoh’s servants were arrested and imprisoned. Both had strange dreams, and Joseph interpreted them—one would live, and the other would be hanged. This came true, but the one who was saved forgot about Joseph for two years.

Pharaoh then had strange dreams that none of his wise men could interpret. The saved servant remembered Joseph and told Pharaoh about him. Pharaoh sent for Joseph, who explained the dreams as a warning from God: Egypt would have seven years of plenty followed by seven years of famine. Joseph advised Pharaoh to appoint someone to store food during the good years to prepare for the famine.

Pharaoh was impressed and chose Joseph to be in charge. For seven years, Joseph stored tons of corn in overflowing granaries. When the terrible famine struck, Egypt was well-prepared, and Joseph was in control.

During the famine, Joseph’s wicked brothers came to Egypt to buy food. They were afraid, but Joseph tested them, remembering their past cruelties. After severe questioning, the brothers confessed what they had done to Joseph. When Joseph secretly heard their repentance, he wept. Later, he revealed himself to them, hugged them, and forgave them.

Joseph reassured his brothers, saying that though they intended evil, God turned it to good. He sent them back to bring their families to Egypt so he could protect them. Thus, all the children of Israel dwelt safely in Egypt as long as Joseph lived.

Nearly 1,700 years later, God sent another Savior to Israel in the form of a man, Jesus Christ. Despite God’s love and purpose, evil men crucified Him. Jesus shed His blood to wash away the sins of those who believe. This act opened the door for the Gentiles to be saved.

At Christ’s Second Coming, Satan’s armies will be destroyed at the Battle of Armageddon. Jesus will rule the world from Jerusalem as King of kings. Everyone can reign with Christ forever if they make Him their Lord and Savior by confessing and believing in Him, as described in the Bible.

Title: Earthman
Subject: Bible Stories
Author: Carter & 3rd
Responses:
The world teaches that man is just a highly developed primate, and we are told this took millions of years through the process of evolution. Most people believe this idea. However, now top scientists denounce evolution as a bad joke, yet godless media and public school leaders continue to push it. Evolutionists hate one man more than any others and do not want people to know about him. There is a book that could soon be banned in public schools, so it is encouraged to read it now.

Before time began, the triune Godhead—God the Father, God the Son (Jesus), and God the Holy Spirit—formed a plan that involved humans. Your eternal destiny rests on what you do with God's plan. Lucifer, a beautiful, high-ranking angel who guarded God's throne, became proud. Because of his pride, he became jealous and wanted to be like God. Lucifer led a rebellion, and the angels who joined him were thrown out of heaven. He became known as Satan, and his fallen angels are called devils.

Satan and his followers settled on Earth, which became Satan's domain. Later, the first man appeared, and Satan was furious. This new creature, man, was so important that the entire Godhead got involved. As the Bible says, Christ formed Adam from the dust of the earth. Adam was perfect and made to live forever.

Adam's mind was pure, and he was innocent before God. Adam named all the animals that Christ had created. Adam walked with God, and God gave him rule over all living things. However, Satan hated Adam and wanted him dead.

God ordered Adam not to eat from a certain tree. If Adam ate from it, he knew he would die. This was a big test given to Adam by God to protect him, demanding total obedience. If Adam failed, all mankind would suffer.

To create a companion, God created Eve from one of Adam's ribs. She was perfect, and Adam loved her. God was their friend, and they loved the Garden of Eden and all the animals. Everything was perfect except that Satan had a plan, and his target was Eve.

One day, Satan approached Eve as a beautiful serpent. Eve didn't suspect any danger. Satan told Eve it was okay to eat from the forbidden tree, calling God a liar and saying that she would not die but would be as gods. Eve believed Satan rather than God.

Suddenly, the tree became more beautiful and its fruit more enticing. Eve ate some and gave some to Adam. When Adam ate that fruit, he lost his innocence, and Satan won control of the earth. Spiritually, Adam and Eve died.

They knew they had sinned and realized they were naked. In fear, they covered themselves with fig leaves and hid from God. God demanded an explanation. Eve blamed the serpent, saying the woman God gave to Adam made him do it. God judged all three.

God killed little animals to provide skins to cover Adam and Eve's bodies. Sin had cost them their friendship with God, and everything they had was about to be lost. God drove them out of the Garden of Eden and blocked their return. God cursed the ground, and Adam had to sweat for his bread.

Adam's sin passed on to all humanity, for "all have sinned and come short of the glory of God." Unless God intervened, everyone would die in their sins and go to hell. As a result of Adam's sin, the earth was cursed with thorns, poisonous snakes, insects, wild animals, wars, earthquakes, killer diseases, and more. Satan uses all these miseries to ruin mankind.

Eve's firstborn was Cain, who had a mind of his own. Then came his brother Abel. When they grew up, God required them to bring lambs as sacrifices. But nobody was going to tell Cain what to do. In rebellion, Cain offered vegetables, which God rejected.

Abel obeyed God, and his offering was accepted. Cain was furious. Cain, the first child born on earth, brutally murdered his kid brother Abel. Because Cain never repented, God cursed him, and he ended up a miserable old drifter. Wicked Cain died in his sins and went to hell.

Adam died when he was 930 years old, leaving humanity with two horrible problems: sin and eternal damnation.

But God had the perfect solution. God Almighty left heaven to be born as the Savior of the world. His name was Jesus Christ. John the Baptist introduced Jesus to the world by saying, "Behold the Lamb of God which taketh away the sin of the world."

Because Jesus is God Almighty, He was sinless and the perfect sacrifice for man's sins. Jesus said, "I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me." The Creator loved the world so much that He shed His precious blood on the cross to wash away sins. "For God so loved the world that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life."

Jesus was buried, and three days later He rose from the dead! His death and resurrection bought eternal life for all who trust in Him. All sin could now be forgiven. Jesus told His followers to go tell everyone this wonderful news.

To go to heaven, receive the Lord Jesus as your Savior by confessing your sins and asking Him to come into your heart and save you. Jesus said, "In my Father's house (in heaven) are many mansions: if it were not so I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you."

Title: Empty Tomb, The
Subject: Bible Stories
Tag(s): ['Basic Gospel', 'Most Popular Titles', 'Older Children and Adults']
Author: Carter & 3rd
Responses:
Inside the great Jewish temple in Jerusalem, religious leaders were perplexed by a twelve-year-old boy who astonished them with his knowledge. "Who is he? I can't even answer his questions," one said. Another called it ridiculous, wondering where the boy had come from. They marveled, "How can a 12-year old possibly know so much about Moses and the prophets?"

After celebrating Passover, the boy’s mother discovered he was missing. Panicked, she searched everywhere. Others suggested he must still be in Jerusalem, so they went back to find him. To their amazement and fear, the boy was found in the temple questioning the astonished teachers, who admitted he knew too much.

When questioned by Mary, the boy asked, "How is it that ye sought me? Wist ye not that I must be about my Father’s business?" This fulfilled the prophecy: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel (God with us)." Mary recalled the angel Gabriel’s words: "...that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

Unknown to the religious leaders, this 12-year-old was God in human form—the very One who gave Moses the law. Scripture tells us Christians that Jesus Christ created the universe. As John recorded, "He was in the world, and the world was made by him, and the world knew him not." This was the greatest life ever lived.

Jesus’ public ministry began at age 30 when John the Baptist introduced Him as "the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world." John meant that Jesus would one day be sacrificed for the sins of all humanity. This was the purpose for coming from heaven.

Jesus taught profound truths that astonished the people. He explained that committing adultery begins in the heart with lust, not just in deed. He shocked the religious community by healing the blind, deaf, and lepers, and even by raising the dead. When he called Lazarus from the tomb, He taught that He was the only way to heaven, saying, "I am the way, the truth, and the life."

He openly challenged the religious authorities, calling them “serpents” and “a generation of vipers,” knowing it would lead to His death. In the high priest’s palace, His enemies plotted against Him. Satan provided the traitor Judas Iscariot, who agreed to betray Jesus for thirty pieces of silver.

At the Last Supper, Jesus explained that His forthcoming crucifixion would be the final blood sacrifice for sins, replacing the old priesthood. He said, "This do in remembrance of me," inviting His disciples to remember His sacrifice. Yet, they did not fully understand His words.

Later, in the Garden of Gethsemane, Jesus prayed in deep sorrow, His sweat like drops of blood. He told God, “Not my will, but thine, be done,” willing to bear the sins of the world though He was sinless. Judas arrived with an armed mob and betrayed Jesus with a kiss, breaking 18 Jewish laws to hand over the Son of Man.

Religious leaders accused Jesus of blasphemy when He declared, “Hereafter shall ye see the Son of man sitting on the right hand of power, and coming in the clouds of heaven.” They demanded His death. Angels watched helplessly as Jesus faced their wrath.

Jesus was taken to the Roman governor Pontius Pilate. Pilate found no fault in Him but yielded to the bloodthirsty crowd who shouted, “Crucify Him!” Despite Pilate’s innocence plea, the people demanded Jesus’ death, saying, "His blood be on us, and on our children!"

Jesus was scourged with a whip embedded with bone and metal, tearing His flesh and muscles. He was mocked with a purple robe and crown of thorns, then forced to carry a heavy cross nearly 650 yards to the execution site, losing part of His beard to rough treatment.

His hands were tied to an overhead beam where He suffered excruciating pain as the whip tore open His back. Soldiers nailed Him to the cross, driving spikes into His wrists. Medical experts agree this caused unimaginable suffering—nerve pain, muscle convulsions, and eventual exhaustion and paralysis.

As Jesus endured this agony, He prayed, "Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do." Just before dying, Jesus shouted, "It is finished!" His death paid the penalty for all sins in full, offering salvation to anyone who would put faith in Him.

Three days after His burial, Jesus rose from the dead, defeating Satan, death, and hell. To His disciples, He said, "All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth" and commissioned them to preach the gospel to every creature worldwide.

Those who accept Jesus as Savior will live with God forever in heaven, while those who reject Him face eternal punishment in a lake of fire. The Bible urges all people: someday everyone will bow before God.

Who will you serve? Jesus Christ or Satan? The choice determines your eternal destiny. The message is clear: believe in the Lord Jesus Christ, and you shall be saved.

Title: Evil Eyes
Subject: Occult
Author: Chick
Responses:
Once, a woman approached an older man known for his amazing powers, seeking revenge. A Santeria priest had told her about the man’s abilities, and she was willing to pay any price. She explained that she wanted her relative, Carlos, to be ruined—not killed—and asked the man to turn Carlos into a vegetable to destroy his life. The man assured her that he was very good at ruining lives and would make Carlos wish he had never been born.

Meanwhile, 300 miles away, Roberto received a request from his mother to visit Carlos and his Aunt Maria, as their birthdays were approaching and Maria hadn’t been able to mail a present.

As evening fell, Carlos, who had been feeling sick, stayed out of the festival that celebrated ancient African spirits called Orishas. These spirits were believed to temporarily possess their human followers, making them very powerful. Opposite this, the woman cast a dark spell intended to destroy Carlos.

Carlos joined the dancing spirits at the festival, unaware that the timing was perfect for the spell to reach him. Suddenly, a violent force slammed into Carlos, and with a dreadful scream, he collapsed, motionless.

The next morning, Maria sent a terrified message to Father Dominic, begging him to help Carlos. When Father Dominic visited the house, he found Carlos unable to see, hear, speak, or eat. Maria described him as a zombie, and the situation seemed hopeless. Roberto disagreed, insisting that there was still a chance.

Trouble soon erupted as Maria’s nephew, furious with Father Dominic, threw him out of the house, angrily discarding crucifixes and religious icons. He accused Father Dominic of being a threat to their traditions and believers.

The crowd, fearing change and new ideas, labeled Father Dominic a dangerous heretic. They vowed to hunt him down. Meanwhile, Roberto prayed fervently, asking Jesus to remove the evil and break the spell that held Carlos captive.

In a powerful moment, Roberto called on Jesus’ mighty name to shatter the spell. Suddenly, Carlos opened his eyes and recognized Roberto, praising God for his deliverance.

Carlos revealed that something horrible—a powerful devil in the form of a zombie—had taken over his body through the spell. Roberto warned that this evil wanted to return with even more power if the empty space inside Carlos was left unfilled.

Scared and confused, Carlos asked what to do. Roberto explained that only God could fill that empty space and protect him from the devils' return. Though Carlos doubted this, Roberto reminded him that the whole world was headed for destruction unless they embraced Jesus Christ.

Roberto told Carlos the story of Jesus—the Son of God who was sent from heaven, sacrificed for human sins, and who rose from the dead. Jesus declared Himself the only way to heaven. The religious crowd at the time hated and crucified Him, but His power delivered Carlos from the zombie spirit.

Roberto invited Carlos to believe in Jesus as his Savior. Jesus would fill the empty space in Carlos’ heart, save him, and be with him forever. Carlos hesitated, worried about giving up Santería and the Catholic Church, but Roberto emphasized the high price of keeping the devils.

Later, Carlos returned to the village, much to the shock and anger of those who had tried to destroy him. They accused Roberto of casting a spell and vowed never to let him return.

On the bus, Carlos spoke with Father Dominic, confessing his past sins of witchcraft and lies. He admitted to abusing and robbing his people but asked if Jesus could forgive him.

Father Dominic assured Carlos that Jesus could forgive even the worst sins and explained why Jesus hates false churches that harm souls. He urged Carlos to follow Jesus and live.

Carlos agreed, declaring that he was done with Santería and recognized Jesus’ power to save. The story ended with a reflection on salvation, encouraging readers to believe in Jesus Christ and be saved.

Title: Execution, The
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
Once upon a time, there was a mean little boy named Sonny who was a bully. His mother loved him deeply and begged him to be good, but Sonny kept getting worse and often shouted hateful words at her.

As Sonny grew older, his love for hurting people grew too, and everyone became afraid of him. One day, he committed a terrible crime: he killed an old man for his money. A lady witnessed the crime and reported it to the police, leading to Sonny’s arrest.

Sonny went to court for his trial, where the jury found him guilty. The judge sentenced him to death, declaring, “Guilty of murder! You will hang by your neck until you are dead!” Even in jail, people feared Sonny. Despite this, his mother continued to visit him and bring him cookies. Though she expressed her love, Sonny still shouted, “I hate you … and your cookies!”

One day, the warden informed Sonny that he was to be executed next week. Filled with fear, Sonny cried, “I’m scared! I don’t want to die!” His mother visited one last time, expressing her love and willingness to do anything for him, but Sonny angrily told her to be quiet.

Sonny requested a pardon, but the governor denied it, and Sonny was told he would die the following day. That night, his mother spoke to the warden, pleading for her son’s life, but the warden explained that the law demanded death for such a crime. Later, she respectfully asked the warden a question.

The next morning, Sonny was escorted to his execution with a heavy heart, gulping in fear. Suddenly, they turned the wrong way—towards freedom. The gallows was out in the yard, but Sonny was taken instead to receive a pardon and was told he was free to go home.

Confused, Sonny protested that he was supposed to die for his crime, but the officer explained that someone else had already taken his place. When Sonny demanded to know who, he was shocked to learn it was his own mother, who had died in his place.

This story reveals that someone was executed for Sonny, someone who loves him more than anyone else ever could—his mother. It continues to explain that God the Father in heaven sees that people have a problem called sin, which keeps them out of heaven. Everyone has sinned, but God loves us and made a way to remove sin.

God sent His Son, Jesus, to earth to be executed for people’s sins. Jesus is God Almighty—the Creator of the world, stars, and everyone on earth. He was crucified, shedding His blood to wash away sins. Jesus was buried and then rose from the dead three days later. Afterward, He ascended into heaven to sit at the right hand of His Father.

To be free from sin, one must repent and believe in Jesus. If they do, God will welcome them into heaven. However, if someone rejects God’s gift, they remain guilty and face eternal consequence.

This story urges readers to receive Jesus while they still can, so they may be saved and enter heaven, escaping eternal separation from God.

Title: Fairy Tales
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
The story begins with a chaotic scene outside a courtroom, where a crowd shouts angrily, demanding the death of a boy named Harry, calling him a monster. News reporters announce that Harry's parents, Mr. and Mrs. Garner, will soon face the tragic news that their son will be executed.

Harry's parents are devastated, insisting that their son was a sweet, innocent boy who would never have done anything bad. They question why he is called "The Monster," unable to reconcile the accusations against him.

The story flashes back to Harry's childhood. Harry excitedly tells his mother that his tooth has fallen out, and she explains that the Tooth Fairy will come to leave money under his pillow. Harry eagerly places his tooth under the pillow, trusting his mother's promise that the Tooth Fairy is real.

Next, Harry's father tells him that Santa Claus is coming to town soon, and Harry eagerly waits, proud to have been very good. He marvels at meeting Santa in person, believing in the magic and promises of these childhood fantasies.

On Christmas morning, Harry thanks Santa Claus and vows to never stop believing. His parents discuss whether they should tell Harry the truth about Santa, the Tooth Fairy, and the Easter Bunny but decide not to break his little heart.

Three months later, Harry learns about the Easter Egg hunt at church and excitedly looks forward to the Easter Bunny's arrival. But soon after, everything changes when Harry is told by other children that Santa Claus isn’t real and that his parents lied to him. Angry and distraught, Harry threatens to harm them both.

Harry is arrested for a terrorist act at school that results in the death of a student. The news reports reveal that Harry is only eight years old and that the school has been shut down due to the tragedy. He is tied down for his protection in the juvenile hall and insists to his parents that Santa is real.

Eventually, his parents confess that they pretended to be Santa Claus, the Easter Bunny, and the Tooth Fairy. This revelation shatters Harry, who demands to know if God and Jesus are also just fairy tales. The story shows Harry's furious rejection of his parents’ lies and his vow never to believe them again.

Harry is moved to Juvenile Hall, where he faces court. The judge condemns him to stay locked up until age eighteen, after Harry kills a cellmate. In Juvenile Hall, Harry meets another inmate, Jamal, who talks about Jesus Christ, explaining that He is real and not a fairy tale, emphasizing Jesus’s divinity, miracles, and sacrifice for humanity.

Jamal explains the story of Jesus — His virgin birth, sinless life, betrayal, crucifixion, resurrection, and how He offers forgiveness and salvation to everyone who believes in Him. Despite Harry's initial rejection of Jesus, Jamal shares how he personally found salvation through faith in Christ.

Ten years later, Harry, now a notorious criminal, is on the FBI's Most Wanted List and is captured, sentenced to death for his crimes. The story shows a final visit from Jamal, who tells Harry he has never stopped praying for him and reminds him of Jesus’s love and forgiveness. Harry rejects Jamal and Jesus one last time.

Four hours later, Harry is executed. The story ends with the message that Jesus is not a fairy tale and that everyone will face Him on the day of judgment, urging belief in Jesus Christ for eternal life.

This narrative chronicles the loss of innocence, the destructive effects of broken trust, and a spiritual appeal centered on faith in Jesus amidst tragedy.

Title: Faithful
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Carter
Responses:
The story begins with a tense moment in a car. A mother, sitting next to her daughter April, is on the phone telling someone, "So I told her, 'Get rid of him!'" Then she abruptly stops, saying she thinks she can make it through the intersection despite the traffic. Suddenly, a car screeches to a halt, narrowly missing two girls crossing the street. April rushes to check if a girl named Iman is okay. Iman thanks April, saying she's fine and reassuring her not to rush since they're not late.

Iman expresses her gratitude for April's kindness and admits she is not used to such warmth. April explains that not everyone is like the reckless driver they just encountered. Iman explains her interest in learning about different cultures, and April invites her along to see where she worships. Iman is hesitant, asking if she will be allowed in. April assures her she will, since Iman wanted to visit.

Inside the place of worship, the pastor begins a lesson. He talks about how many people despise their own kind, referencing Jesus who was despised and rejected by his own people. April asks what religion those people belong to. The pastor explains that Jesus grew "in favour with God and man" and, at age 30, began teaching about God's kingdom through parables like the sower going forth to sow. Jesus healed the sick, cast out devils, and even raised the dead. Despite His miracles and teachings, those people soon turned against Him.

The pastor recounts how Jesus fed 5,000 men, plus women and children, using just five loaves of bread and two fishes. The crowd was so impressed they wanted to make Him king, but Jesus slipped away during the night. The following day, they found Him teaching in the synagogue. The crowd wanted more free food, but Jesus challenged them to work for food that endures eternal life. He revealed that the work God wants is for them to believe in Him.

Jesus spoke about being the "bread of life," saying, "Whoso eateth my flesh, and drinketh my blood, hath eternal life," which many found difficult to understand or accept. Many followers left Him because they refused to believe in this spiritual teaching about faith rather than physical food.

When Jesus asked the twelve disciples if they would also leave, Peter responded passionately, saying, "Lord, to whom shall we go? Thou hast the words of eternal life." Peter affirmed their belief that Jesus was the Christ, the Son of the living God. Jesus reminded them He chose them, but one among them was a devil—referring to Judas Iscariot.

Judas betrayed Jesus to the chief priests for thirty pieces of silver, selling his Master for the price of a servant. Some people unleashed their hatred on Jesus; He was beaten, whipped, and eventually condemned to die on a cross. Despite being God's Son with the power to summon angels to save Him, Jesus chose not to resist. Instead, He showed faithfulness to God by forgiving those who persecuted Him, saying, "Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do."

The story emphasizes that forgiveness is the hardest thing to do, especially toward someone who abuses us, but Jesus set an example for humanity. He took upon Himself the punishment for all sins, dying and being buried in a tomb. Three days later, Jesus rose from the dead and later ascended to heaven. He declared, "I am the resurrection and the life; whosoever believeth in me shall never die."

The pastor explains that Jesus never sinned, but the rest of humanity has all sinned and fallen short of God's glory. Even Job, regarded as the world's most perfect man, was a sinner. Thus, everyone needs the forgiveness Jesus offers. He urges people to believe in Jesus Christ and allow Him to change their lives. They are invited to come forward and give their hearts to Jesus.

The story returns to April, who prays, "Lord Jesus, I believe You died for my sins. Please forgive my sins and help me learn to forgive others." A friend expresses surprise that April is a Christian, and April confidently states that Christianity is the right path.

Later, a group of men confront Iman outside the infidels' church, accusing her of needing another lesson for associating with them. When they attempt to attack her, the cover of her coat reveals wounds, stopping them in their tracks. Despite their threats, the question is posed to Iman: Do you want Jesus to forgive you too?

Iman lies injured but asks, "Do you want Jesus to forgive you, too?" She references 1 Peter 2:21, noting that Christ also suffered for us, leaving an example to follow. A form appears, inviting readers to admit their sins, believe Jesus died for them, and ask Him to forgive and come into their hearts, with space to record the date and name as testimony.

This story intertwines personal experiences, biblical teachings, and the message of forgiveness and salvation through faith in Jesus Christ. It invites readers to reflect on their own lives and consider the path of faith and forgiveness exemplified by Jesus.

Title: Fallen
Subject: Bible Stories
Author: Chick
Responses:
Bruce Burke was a troubled young man who had always been hated by his family. One day, he was violently thrown out of the house, accused of being worthless and having taken money. The final insult was the revelation that his mother’s old purse had been found under the back seat of the car he was kicked out of, and the purse was cruelly thrown to him as a "going away present."

Bruised and rejected, Bruce was left sitting on the curb, watching the car drive away. Soon after, police officers found him wearing the woman’s purse and took him into custody. When Bruce explained the purse belonged to his mother and offered the owner's name and phone number, the police contacted Frances, Bruce's mother.

Frances was overjoyed to hear about Bruce's custody and spoke sweetly on the phone about how much she loved her son and wanted to rescue him. She assured the officer she would bail Bruce out, which she did without hesitation, despite his ungrateful attitude.

Back at home, Bruce’s hatred for his parents boiled over, even as his mother expressed appreciation that her son was safe and gave him a list of things she wanted him to buy with the money she gave him. Bruce remained defiant, blaming his mother for his troubles.
