Bruce’s uncle Henry, a godly man, contacted the family friend Bob Williams to pray for Bruce, who was deeply troubled and far from God. Frances showed concern and hope, but Bruce was continuing down a dark path. Shortly after, Bruce got into more trouble when he showed up at a bar called Frankie’s and was recognized by someone there. A group of thugs attacked him viciously, leaving him badly beaten and broken.

Bruce survived but was paralyzed from the neck down and developed pneumonia. Bob visited Bruce in the hospital and tried to talk to him, reminding him of their time together in Sunday School years ago. Bruce was initially dismissive, but Bob began to share a story about repentance and God’s love.

Bob recounted the parable of a younger son who demanded his inheritance early from his father, then wasted it on reckless living and bad company. The son ended up starving and feeding pigs, a terrible place for a Jewish boy. Only when he came to his senses and decided to return to his father, asking for forgiveness, did his life start to change.

Bob explained what true repentance meant: being genuinely sorry for past wrongs and willing to change. He described how the father in the story joyfully embraced his lost son, bringing him back to life. This was a picture of God’s love.

Bruce struggled with the message. He admitted he hated God and wondered if God hated him back. Bob assured him that God’s justice demanded punishment for sin but that God also loved him and offered hope through the gospel.

Bob shared how Jesus Christ came to earth, suffered a brutal death on the cross, and rose from the dead to save people from eternal punishment. He told Bruce this was God’s love gift and the only way to be saved.

Faced with the choice between heaven and hell, Bruce wanted to think it over. But his condition worsened, and he passed away early the next morning, his soul taken to hell for eternity.

Though Bruce’s story was tragic, Bob made it clear that God doesn’t play games. He urged others to choose salvation now, quoting scripture that promises eternal life to those who believe in Jesus.

Bruce Burke’s life was filled with hatred, rebellion, and pain, but the gospel message of love and repentance remains, offering hope to all who hear it in time.

Title: Fame
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Carter
Responses:
Douglas Ford, a renowned and award-winning TV and film star, was admitted to St. Lucy Hospital with chest pains. News spread quickly, and people worldwide offered their prayers for him. The hospital staff were thrilled to have such a celebrity, and Douglas was reported to be responding well to treatment. His hospital room was filled with flowers, and he even received a call from the President.

Cardinal Rooney had said a mass for Douglas and sent greetings, while Douglas himself was scheduling more films despite his condition. His wife and fans were eager for his autograph. Meanwhile, hospital staff discussed what to do with the many flowers sent by fans, debating between discarding them or giving them to other patients.

Douglas discussed with his friend Saul about money demands related to his work, showing pride in his earnings and fame. However, an ongoing conversation with Daisy, a hospital cleaning woman, began to challenge his views. Daisy confronted Douglas about his lifestyle, particularly his involvement in "dirty movies" and raised moral concerns, telling him he was a wicked sinner before God.

Douglas was shocked by Daisy's frankness, as no one had ever spoken to him like that before. Daisy explained that Cardinal Rooney only wanted Douglas's money, not his spiritual well-being. Douglas was confused but intrigued by these talks, especially about facing God after death. Daisy talked about heaven, hell, and the reality of judgment, stressing that hell was a real and terrible place where those who die in sin end up.

Douglas, struggling with the idea of the afterlife and judgment, was haunted by thoughts of dying twice—once physically and once spiritually. Daisy told him that he would face God's judgment and that his whole life would be replayed like a movie, where every sin and good deed would be seen and judged. She warned him that he could not avoid the consequences of his actions.

As Douglas's health improved, the staff prepared to release him from the hospital, but the idea of facing God and hell lingered in his mind. He was scared by the thought of being condemned and separated from God forever. Daisy continued to share the gospel message with him, explaining that Jesus is the only one who can save him from his sins and the punishment they deserve. Jesus had died for everyone’s sins and rose from the dead, offering eternal life to those who believe and repent.

Douglas wrestled with doubt and pride, worrying about losing fame and fortune if he accepted this truth. Daisy urged him to accept God's love and forgiveness, encouraging him to get on his knees and pray to Jesus. Despite skepticism from others, Douglas prayed sincerely, asking Jesus to save him.

One year later, Douglas died in a car accident. Upon his death, he heard Jesus welcoming him, saying, "Well done, thou good and faithful servant." Douglas entered the joy of his Lord, having found salvation through faith in Jesus Christ. The story ends with scripture affirming that God sent His Son not to condemn the world but to save it.

Title: Fat Cats
Subject: Communism
Author: Chick
Responses:
In a tumultuous country plagued by starvation, unemployment, and signs of revolution, El Supremo and his generals feast, unconcerned by the suffering beyond their palace walls. One day, they are informed of government forces attacking San Marcos, where many villagers, including Carlos' cousin, live. Carlos is raising a People's Army to overthrow the government, claiming they have something to live for. Despite warnings from Juan's wife, Maria, and pleas to talk to his father before joining, Juan is drawn to Carlos’ cause.

Juan’s father tries to dissuade him, warning that Carlos is a charmer who uses people to gain power, comparing him to historical revolutionaries like Stalin and Castro who betrayed their own followers. He believes that true justice will never come through human governments, quoting scripture that peace will only return when Jesus Christ comes back to rule the world.

Juan's father explains the Christian gospel, emphasizing Jesus Christ’s sacrifice, urging Juan to accept Christ as his personal savior rather than follow Carlos. Juan resists but promises to think about it, deciding to support Carlos, believing the revolution will bring positive change.

Juan joins Carlos’ growing People's Army, which is well-equipped thanks to connections with Father Dominic, a Jesuit priest who is a powerful socialist. Father Dominic defends his socialist beliefs by referring to Jesus as a revolutionary who fought oppressive governments and teaches that mankind is inherently good but oppressed by capitalist systems.

Juan is troubled by this, especially when he discovers that his own father-in-law, Perez, is labeled a threat by Father Dominic. Meanwhile, Carlos' forces begin attacking government troops and villages loyal to the regime, executing leaders and burning settlements. Violence escalates as Carlos' revolution progresses.

After months of fighting, Carlos and his army capture the palace, executing El Supremo and his staff. The victory is costly; many of Carlos' followers are killed or wounded. Soon after, Juan receives a heartbreaking letter from Maria, urging him to reconsider his choices for the sake of their family’s safety. Two days later, Juan learns that his family has been brutally murdered because of their faith and opposition to Carlos’ regime.

Juan’s father-in-law, Perez, and other Bible-believing Christians were tortured and killed, crimes ordered by Father Dominic. Grief and rage consume Juan, who vows vengeance against Father Dominic and Carlos. However, Carlos orders Juan’s execution to set an example, betraying his most loyal follower.

In a spiritual vision, Juan confronts the reality of his choices. He is told that if he had accepted Jesus Christ as his Savior, he would be with his family in heaven. Instead, his decision to follow Carlos condemns him to eternal torment.

The story ends where it began, five years later, with Premier Carlos dining lavishly while the northern unrest continues—starvation, unemployment, and signs of revolution once again plague the land, locked in a vicious cycle of violence and betrayal. Carlos, like El Supremo before him, feasts recklessly, showing no concern for the suffering around him.

Title: Fatal Decision
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
A man is hiking through dense woods when suddenly he yells out, "Yaaaah! Something's biting me!" He is in severe pain and exclaims, "The pain's killing me!" Those with him are shocked, noticing how terrible the bite looks. They know they must get him to a doctor immediately.

At the hospital, doctors examine him and conclude that they have nothing to treat the infection with locally—it’s so serious the man must be airlifted to the U.S. immediately. They see his leg is badly injured and fear it may be a miracle to save him.

Urgent blood work is ordered, as the patient’s condition is critical. The doctors are gravely concerned. The tests reveal two nearly identical strains of infection—Type 1, which is worse than Ebola, and Type 2, which is less contagious but lethal within a week unless treated.

Hospital staff are warned to use triple gloves and isolate the patient to prevent spreading the disease, as attending medical personnel are in great danger. Meanwhile, Dr. Bowers receives an urgent call from the Centers for Disease Control informing him about a new vaccine developed in Switzerland that could save the patient. Dr. Bowers is eager to learn more.

The patient's desperate mother pleads with Dr. Bowers, explaining that her only living relative is her son and without him, she cannot survive. She offers her life savings of $3,000 to save him. Moved, Dr. Bowers promises to do everything he can.

Dr. Bowers contacts the Swiss facility, where he is told they have one vial of the vaccine left. It is extremely expensive, costing six figures, but Dr. Bowers insists on securing it. His colleagues warn him this is insanity, but he is determined and takes a leave of absence.

The next day, hospital staff report Dr. Bowers has received multiple complaints about his behavior, threatening to fire him if he continues. The head of maintenance harbors resentment toward Dr. Bowers and vows to get even with him.

Dr. Bowers obtains the vaccine and is briefed on its administration: roughly a week before the patient's expected death, he will experience a euphoric phase when the medicine must be given to ensure survival. He receives a heartfelt "Good luck!"

The patient, now in the hospital, is asked by a nurse how he is doing. He replies he's feeling a little better, crediting Dr. Bowers. Suddenly, the maintenance man who dislikes Dr. Bowers arrives, implying something bad. The patient denies it and refuses to talk to him.

Dr. Bowers returns with the precious vaccine and is greeted by his son, who drives him to the hospital. Minutes later, Dr. Bowers is involved in a terrible car accident. John, his son, dies instantly, but Dr. Bowers is saved by an airbag and rushed to the hospital.

Back at the hospital, the patient says he feels much better and believes he is healed. Doctors remind him it is now Dr. Bowers' responsibility. The hospital staff express sorrow over John's death, but there is no time to lose.

Dr. Bowers arrives with a surprise for John, who is still alive. John is amazed to learn the vaccine has arrived just in time and that the injection will save his life. Despite feeling well, doctors insist John is in another disease stage and must take the vaccine now.

Dr. Bowers carefully administers the vaccine, explaining it is priceless because it keeps a promise he made to John's mother. But John suddenly reacts with fury, rejecting the vaccine and accusing Dr. Bowers of trying to poison him. He demands Dr. Bowers leave.

In his rage, John throws the syringe, which could have been his lifeline. Three days later, John suffers a horrible death from the untreated infection. Dr. Bowers mourns the loss of his son, devastated that his sacrifice and the vaccine were rejected.

The story shifts to a spiritual message, explaining that all people are born infected with sin, which is fatal and separates them from heaven. The Bible says God sent His only Son to offer the gift of life to a dying world. Jesus Christ's sacrifice and resurrection give eternal life to those who believe.

The story ends with a warning: like John, those who reject Jesus' gift of life will face eternal punishment, but those who accept Him will be saved. The final plea urges readers not to make a fatal decision but to embrace the promise of salvation through Jesus Christ.

Title: Fire Starter?
Subject: Bible Stories
Author: Carter
Responses:
In ancient Israel, during the reign of King Ahab, a grievous battle between faiths was unfolding. Ahab's family, influenced by Queen Jezebel, had turned to worship the god Baal, forsaking the God of their ancestors. One tragic act symbolized this betrayal when Jezebel's evil priests of Baal sought to sacrifice little Samuel, a grandson, to satisfy their dark deity. Samuel's father pleaded, horrified, that this would not happen, but Ahab, driven by loyalty to Baal, forced the sacrifice. This harrowing event was burning alive Samuel, an act forbidden by God’s laws.

Baal, known as the sun god, demanded human sacrifices during times of famine and drought. When the summer’s fierce heat withered crops, Baal's priests called for such offerings to appease him. Meanwhile, Queen Jezebel ruthlessly eliminated all prophets of the God of Israel to remove any opposition.

King Ahab was the most wicked king Israel had ever seen, prompting God to decide to teach him a severe lesson. God sent the prophet Elijah to declare that it would not rain until he said so, challenging Baal’s control over the seasons. Elijah obeyed God's instruction to hide by a brook called Cherith, where ravens fed him.

As the drought worsened and hunger spread across the land, with babies still being sacrificed to Baal, Ahab grew desperate, demanding Elijah to be found. Elijah had been sent to a widow who, despite having almost nothing, generously fed him. Elijah assured her that her food supply would not fail until the rains returned, and indeed, God faithfully provided for them throughout the famine.

Three years later, the looming showdown approached. King Ahab summoned Obadiah, a man loyal to God who had defied the king by hiding and feeding 100 of God’s prophets. However, Ahab instructed Obadiah to find water for his horses, dodging the real task of confronting Elijah. When Elijah appeared, Obadiah was stunned but obeyed Elijah’s command to inform Ahab while fearing for his life.

Ahab, unprepared, questioned Elijah about troubling Israel. Elijah boldly responded that it was Ahab who had forsaken God to follow Baal. He then ordered Ahab and all Israel to gather atop Mount Carmel, bringing with them 850 false prophets of Baal.

Facing the crowd’s accusations that Elijah was the cause of the drought, he challenged the people: If the Lord is God, follow Him, but if Baal is God, follow him. The people were afraid to answer. The challenge was clear: whichever god answered by fire to consume a sacrifice would be acknowledged as the true God.

The prophets of Baal cried out and cut themselves from morning until noon, but Baal gave no response. Jeering at them, Elijah mocked that perhaps Baal was asleep or busy. Then Elijah's turn came. He soaked his altar with water three times, dousing the sacrifice and the wood.

When Elijah prayed, the true God sent fire from heaven that consumed the sacrifice, the wood, the stones of the altar, and even the water in the trench. The stunned crowd shouted in praise, recognizing The Lord as the true God.

Baal was defeated; his priests were slain, and the people repented and turned back to God. Elijah prayed, and God sent rain to end the famine. However, the struggle between God and Satan was not over. A similar battle for souls was still being waged.

Centuries later, the same powerful Creator who had answered Elijah was born as Jesus Christ in Bethlehem, fulfilling prophecy. Jesus came to shed His blood for the sins of mankind, bridging the gap between God and humanity. Though Satan feared and resisted Him, Jesus triumphed over death by rising from the grave.

Just as people in Elijah's time chose whom to serve, so must we today choose between God and Satan. Jesus said He is the way, the truth, and the life, and whoever calls on the name of the Lord will be saved. The eternal choice is between life in heaven with Jesus or eternal separation from God in hell.

The story closes with a call to save oneself by choosing Jesus, the one true Lord. The prize is your soul, and the choice is yours to make.

Title: First Bite
Subject: Halloween
Author: Chick
Responses:
On a night nearing midnight, a wolf at a castle eagerly awaited an event. Inside, a group gathered in anticipation, asking the doctor if Vampira was pregnant. The doctor confirmed she was expecting a child, prompting joy and celebration among them as they anticipated a new beginning.

The group inquired when this great event would occur. A man, confident in his calculations, predicted it would happen during the full moon on their most sacred night, Halloween. There was surprise and silence until the man insisted there was more to share.

He explained that in room 13, he had summoned ancient forces from the dark world, which filled the room with smoke. Through the smoke, he saw the prince of darkness himself, terrifying him so much he thought he would die. The prince told him that the coming child would possess powers greater than all of them combined. He also revealed the child's name but commanded that it must not be spoken until the child was born, under penalty of death.

Despite pleas, the man revealing this secret eventually shouted out the child's name: Igor.

With that revelation, a thunderstorm crashed over the castle, and the gathering disbanded, quietly slipping away into their coffins.

Nine months later, on October 31st, celebrations resumed as Igor, the chosen one destined to unite all covens and grant them incredible power, was born. The question on everyone’s mind was when they would finally see him—and witness his first bite.

Over the years, Igor was taught the dark secrets by dragon masters, grand lodge leaders, and the mysterious "nine unknown men." He was asleep during much of this time, as everyone hoped he would succeed and feared what might happen if he failed. The great prince was summoned, commanding the search for a virgin who would serve as Igor's first victim.

Two months before the crucial night, a kind and innocent girl named Faith was chosen. She appeared unaware she was being watched. When questioned, the hunters mocked her name but accepted her as their target.

Igor was put through training, learning where to bite; the carotid artery was his target. The night for the attack finally arrived, as cars approached the mansion of their great hope.

Gathered together, the group awaited Igor's arrival, excited and hopeful. As they cast spells against Faith, the poor girl’s fate seemed sealed.

Preparations ensured Faith would be alone; her father was away at a funeral, and her mother hospitalized, though Faith insisted on handing out candy and comics to trick-or-treaters.

Faith prepared to meet the children, her aunt watching TV nearby. She prayed to the Lord, hoping to win even one soul. Notably, she carried a Bible, causing concern among the dark group, who feared it might pose a problem.

As children arrived, Faith greeted them with candy and comics, earning thanks and blessings. As the last child left and rain began, a figure lurked in the darkness.

Faith’s exhausted aunt decided to go to bed, leaving one last visitor at the door—a vampire claiming to be Igor himself.

Faith welcomed him in, offering hot chocolate. Igor declared himself real and the child of the Devil, showing his fangs, but Faith replied with faith in God.

Igor hissed angrily as Faith cited a Biblical promise that God gives power, love, and sound mind—not fear.

Faith’s faith stopped Igor from biting her. She explained that Jesus did it, and offered to get rid of the evil inside him.

Igor confessed the Devil ruled and he came to bite Faith, but Faith introduced him to Jesus, who could save and change anyone.

Meanwhile, the dark forces observed that Igor was still inside Faith's house, enjoying his first bite and confident their chosen one would lead them to victory.

Faith prayed, causing the devils to leave. Her friend was amazed, asking what else Jesus could do, and Faith explained that Jesus could forgive sins and change hearts.

Faith declared that no witch, vampire, or satanist could change, but Jesus made it possible by shedding His precious blood for forgiveness.

She recited John 3:16, explaining how Jesus died and rose again to defeat Satan.

Igor accepted Jesus, experiencing a transformation. He went to tell the others the good news.

When the coven found out, they were horrified. The prince who lied about Igor being the "promised one" confessed his deception.

Confused and upset, the dark crowd argued about trusting Satan versus trusting Jesus. The coven never recovered from this betrayal.

Faith warned children to stay away from Satan, calling him a liar and destroyer, but assured them Jesus was God and wanted to save them too.

At the end, there was a message: the choice between heaven and hell is yours, with an invitation to accept Jesus and have sins forgiven.

The story closes urging readers to check boxes confirming their decisions about salvation and belief.

Title: First Jaws, The
Subject: Bible Stories
Author: Carter
Responses:
In the early 1900s, a British sailor attempted to harpoon a gigantic shark but slipped and fell overboard. To everyone's shock, the shark ate him in one bite. Forty-eight hours later, the shark was caught and cut open, revealing the sailor alive inside. The men quickly got him to a hospital, though the shark's juices had nearly killed him.

This unusual event reminded many of the biblical story of Jonah. Around 750 B.C., in a time when the Assyrians cruelly ruled the Middle East, Jonah was a prophet of God who stood before King Jeroboam of Israel. The king was evil and the kingdom had been warned that sin would bring suffering.

Jonah hated the brutal Assyrians, especially since their capital city, Nineveh—known as "The Robber City"—was steeped in wickedness. God commanded Jonah to go to Nineveh and cry out against its wickedness, but Jonah was unwilling to warn the Ninevites because he wanted them dead. Knowing they would repent if warned, Jonah chose to run from God by heading west instead of east. He boarded a ship going to Tarshish in southern Spain, confident the Ninevites would be destroyed.

But God sent a great storm at sea, threatening to break the ship. The terrified sailors threw cargo overboard to lighten the load and called out to their gods, while Jonah slept below deck. When asked, Jonah confessed he was a Hebrew who feared the Lord and explained he was running from God. The sailors asked what to do to calm the sea, and Jonah told them to throw him overboard. Though they tried rowing harder, the storm worsened until they finally cast Jonah into the sea, and the storm ceased.

The sailors feared the Lord and made vows, while Jonah was swallowed by a great fish, where he spent three days and three nights. Inside the fish’s belly, Jonah was in terror and prayed to God. Though trapped and covered with seaweed, Jonah believed God would deliver him and bring him to His temple.

The Lord commanded the fish to vomit Jonah out onto dry land. News of Jonah’s miraculous survival spread quickly, and people were amazed he had come out of a fish. Jonah, though looking terrible, obeyed God and went to Nineveh despite his hatred for its people. He was the only evangelist who prayed that he would have no converts.

Jonah warned the people of Nineveh that in forty days, the city would be overthrown. Unexpectedly, the wicked people repented and believed in God, turning away from their evil ways. Covered in sackcloth, man and beast alike sought true repentance before God, and the entire city was transformed.

Because the Ninevites repented, God spared the city. Jonah was furious; he wanted them dead. God allowed a gourd to grow up and shade Jonah, which brought him relief, but when a worm killed the gourd, the heat made Jonah faint. God used this incident to teach Jonah a great lesson: he cared more about a gourd than the 120,000 little children and the cattle of Nineveh.

The story then connected to Jesus, the one who created Jonah and the great fish, born about 700 years later. Jesus warned people of coming judgment and preached repentance. He spoke more about hell than anyone else in the Bible, warning that those who die in sin face a horrible fate. Jesus likened His death and resurrection to Jonah’s time in the fish — just as Jonah spent three days and nights in the belly of the fish, Jesus would spend three days and nights in the heart of the earth.

Jesus was the perfect and final sacrifice, shedding His precious blood to wash away sins and offering salvation. After His resurrection, He gave His disciples the command to preach the gospel to every creature.

The people of Nineveh were spared because they repented, and the Bible says anyone can escape God’s judgment by believing in Jesus Christ and being saved. The story ends with a warning to heed God's call and avoid the eternal punishment that awaits those who reject Him.

Title: Flight 144
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
The story begins onboard an airplane where a flight attendant notices something seriously wrong and exclaims, "Oh, no!" A passenger anxiously asks if they are in trouble. The flight attendant reassures everyone that everything is under control, but the aircraft captain soon informs them that this is Flight 144, one engine is dead, and the other is on fire.

Three hours earlier, at Zambolo airport, a crowd has gathered because some famous missionaries, the Davidsons, are flying to America to raise funds for another hospital. The missionaries express love and prayers to the crowd and board the plane. The reverend is surprised to find that the seats next to him are occupied by Ed and another person, who have just returned from 50 years in Africa. Ed shares that he was a cook on a tanker until he killed a man in a drunken brawl and found salvation in jail. He admires the Davidsons' good works, including schools and hospitals they've built, but questions how many souls they've actually saved.

The Davidsons explain that God's call is to help people lead better lives and not necessarily to preach salvation. Ed argues that the Bible says good works cannot save anyone and that only Christ's sacrifice on the cross matters for salvation. As the plane crashes into the ocean, no one survives.

Under water, the Davidsons are seen being taken to heaven by an angel, confident they will be rewarded for their good works. However, they stand before God and hear the heartbreaking words, "I never knew you: depart from me." In shock, they protest that they sacrificed everything, suffered for 50 years, and helped countless people. God responds with scripture that no one is righteous, and good works alone cannot save.

The Davidsons insist they followed God's name and did their best to help the needy, but God explains that Jesus Christ did all the work necessary for salvation when He died on the cross. Questions arise about those who did good works in other religions, but God clarifies salvation comes only through Christ.

The story shifts to God's explanation of the origin of sin, beginning with Adam and Eve, and how sacrifices were made to temporarily cover sin. God became man and shed His blood on the cross to pay once for all sins. After three days, He rose from the dead and ascended to heaven. Eternal life is now available as a gift through faith in Jesus Christ. Those who trust in Him receive eternal life, while those who rely on their deeds are lost.

The Davidsons express feeling betrayed and unfairly treated for not hearing this message earlier, but God points out that His Word was given and rejected. The story ends with a warning from scripture about the dangerous path of relying solely on one's own righteousness and an urgent call to trust Jesus Christ right now, before it is too late.

Title: Fool, The
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
Once upon a time, there was a king who ruled a kingdom filled with people and delighted in his court and all his subjects. Of all the people in his kingdom, he liked his court jester the best. Whenever the king faced too many problems, his court jester could always make him laugh.

One day, the king had a great idea. He called the court jester to his royal chamber, holding a little golden wand. The king gave the wand to the jester and said, "My friend, when you find a bigger fool than yourself, you must give him this golden wand!" So, the jester set out looking for a bigger fool.

He traveled through every village, asking questions of one and all, searching for someone more foolish than himself. Meanwhile, back at the castle, the king became very sick and was dying. The court jester was called back to the palace.

"Hello, my little friend," said the king weakly. "I am going on a long, long journey from which I shall never return," he spoke of his impending death. The jester asked, "Have you prepared for that journey, your Highness?" The king responded, "No, I haven’t!"

Then the jester said, "Then I must present this golden wand to you!" At last, the jester had found a greater fool than himself.

The story then shifts to ask the reader: Have you prepared for your coming journey? If not, you’re in trouble just like the king. The comic urges the reader to read carefully.

It shares Bible verses saying, "There is none righteous, no, not one," and "For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God." This is the bad news because sin stops our journey to heaven.

But there is good news: Jesus Christ, the Creator of the universe, came from heaven to take the form of a man. Because Jesus loves us, He died on the cross and shed His precious blood to wash away our sins. The Bible says, "For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son (Jesus), that whosoever believeth in him should not perish (in hell), but have everlasting life (in heaven)."

Jesus wants us to repent and accept Him as Lord and Savior. Only then will we be ready for the long journey. How about it? Are you ready for your journey?

The story ends with the jester asking, "Would the little court jester give you that golden wand?" And warns, "Don’t be a fool! Accept Christ and be saved… TODAY!"

Title: Four Angels?
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
Once upon a time, the Sawyer family faced a deep spiritual crossroads on a Sunday night. Henry, the youngest son, was reluctant to attend the church revival. "Aw, for cryin' out loud, Maw. Do we hafta go?" he whined. His mother sternly hushed him, determined to bring Henry and his brothers to hear the most wonderful message they would ever encounter.

As they hurried to the revival, Henry insisted he needed to sit in the back while his mother wanted them in front, saying God assigned her to protect Henry. At the revival, Henry repeatedly asked to go to the bathroom, but his mother reminded him he had just gone. Still, he had to go again and again, making his mother concerned.

Meanwhile, inside the revival, Henry and his brothers settled in while their mother kept a watchful eye outside, wondering why Henry was taking so long. When Henry finally returned, she was ready to go in, acknowledging the hardships of the moment with a verse from Hebrews 1:14.

Inside, the preacher shared sobering truths from the Bible. "God's Word says all have sinned," the preacher said, explaining that all who die in their sins will go to hell. The boys were shocked—especially Henry, who realized the message was about him.

The preacher continued, explaining God's love and the way of escape through Jesus Christ, who died for their sins. Henry's thoughts raced with fear and hope. The preacher urged everyone to come forward and accept Jesus as Lord for salvation.

Henry and his brothers took the step together, going forward to be saved. The revival ended, and Henry, now Frank, was excited about his new commitment. "I'm going to be a great preacher. Just watch!" he told his mother.

The next day, Frank’s enthusiasm was met with skepticism. "You a preacher? Your girl would leave you," a friend mocked. Frank admitted he felt foolish at first but was serious about his faith.

However, Frank’s journey showed struggles. The Word of God didn’t take root in him, and over time, he gave in to pressures and worldly desires. He stopped living by his faith sincerely.

Bobby, his brother, faced similar challenges but kept attending church to impress others. Meanwhile, their other brother Charles took a different path. Charlie studied Bible in college but changed, seeking fame and riches instead of true faith. He became a popular preacher, loved by all but never preached against sin.

Charlie's rise continued, gaining honors and acclaim as a great Christian leader. Yet he lived a double life, with multiple wives and affairs, betraying his sacred calling.

Henry, still a true believer, worked on the streets in a rough neighborhood, helping those in need. Despite his humble ministry, he loved the Lord earnestly, prayed for the lost, and served with compassion.

As tensions rose within the family, conflicts became fierce. Henry called out Charlie's sinful ways and warned he was on the path to destruction. Others defended Charlie, saying he was wonderful and respected, while Henry insisted on standing by the truth of God's Word.

Family gatherings were no longer peaceful, filled with anger and division over faith and morality. Henry believed there was hope for his brothers, but they mocked him and rejected his warnings.

Finally, the story ends at the great white throne judgment, where each brother stands before God. Only Henry is welcomed into the joy of the Lord for his true faith and repentance, while the others are rejected for their false beliefs and sins.

The Sawyers’ story is a poignant reminder of the choices between worldly success and true salvation, faithfulness to God or deception, and the eternal consequences of those choices.

Title: Frame Up
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Carter
Responses:
A man was sentenced to be executed in 15 days with no chance of reprieve. When the new chaplain, Joe Peterson, was introduced to him, the man brusquely rejected any religious comfort, declaring he didn't want to talk to any fanatic and didn't like religious phonies. However, the chaplain began telling him about the biggest frame-up in history.

He explained that nearly 2000 years ago, Jesus was making waves around Jerusalem by performing miracles, raising Lazarus from the dead, healing the deaf, blind, and drunkards, and even forgiving prostitutes. Jesus became a threat to the religious system, who tried to trap Him with tricky questions, but He always outsmarted them. The religious leaders believed Jesus was muscling in on their operation.

Annas, the high priest of the Jews, hated Jesus. Annas was a Sadducee who did not believe in life after death. He controlled a corrupt organization that sold cows and sheep for sacrifices at the temple and profited from converting Roman money into Jewish currency. Jesus once drove the money changers out of the temple, which infuriated Annas, who then ordered Jesus must die.

Because of His miracles, people saw Jesus as the Messiah who would restore Israel and free them from Roman rule. Judas Iscariot, one of Jesus’ disciples, was disillusioned when Jesus refused to be crowned King and declared His kingdom was not of this world. Judas decided to betray Jesus for 30 pieces of silver and led soldiers to arrest Him at night, violating Jewish law.

Jesus was first taken to Annas, who had Him struck in the face. Then He was brought to the Sanhedrin, the Jewish Supreme Court, unlawfully assembled. The trial was prejudiced, and Jesus was considered guilty before it even began. Two false witnesses testified against Him, and He was given no defense.

He was then taken before Caiaphas, the high priest and son-in-law of Annas, who accused Jesus of blasphemy because Jesus claimed to be the Son of God. Under pressure from the crowd, Pontius Pilate, the Roman Governor worried about his job, eventually gave Jesus over to be crucified despite acquitting Him four times.

Jesus was beaten by order of Pilate, forced to carry a heavy cross to His execution, during which time the crowd mistreated Him. One of the criminals crucified next to Him asked Jesus to remember him, and Jesus promised that he would be in paradise that day. After three days, Jesus rose from the dead and later ascended to heaven.

The chaplain explained that Jesus had to die on the cross to become a sacrifice for humanity’s sins. Through His blood, sins are washed away, and anyone who accepts Jesus as their Savior has their record wiped clean regardless of their past. Jesus has special love for convicts; many of His disciples had prison records, and most were executed.

The man in prison was moved by this and expressed a desire to accept Jesus as his Savior. The chaplain prayed with him, assuring him that his name was now written in the book of life. The story ended with a reflection on how Judas, Caiaphas, Annas, Pilate, and the Sanhedrin members will answer for their actions before Jesus on doomsday, while those not found in the book of life will face eternal punishment.

Title: Framed
Subject: Bible Stories
Author: Chick
Responses:
Joe Harris rushed through a crowded courthouse lobby, pushing past people on a rainy day. A woman in the crowd hurled a flask at him, shouting, "This will fix you, you old snitch!" The security guard at the metal detector smiled pleasantly and said, "Hey mister, have a nice day," as the scanner alarm suddenly blared and Joe was caught.

The guard said, "Gotcha!" as Joe accidentally set off the metal detector, exclaiming, "OOPS!" A policeman swiftly grabbed him and ordered, "Don't move! Drop that gun! YOU'RE UNDER ARREST!" Joe was shocked, saying, "What's this?"

Outside, Mrs. Harris frantically knocked on her son Bob’s door, her dog growling, "GRRR." She cried, "Bob... Bob! Open up! Something HORRIBLE has happened!" She burst inside, tearfully telling Bob, "My baby, Joey, has been arrested! He's in jail. He didn't do it!"

Bob asked, "Do what, Mrs. Harris?" She replied desperately, "They found a gun in his pocket. Joey's never owned a gun! How could they arrest him? He's a friend of the police!" Bob nodded thoughtfully and said, "Joey’s always helping them by turning in all the gang members in the neighborhood." He then said hurriedly, "Oops... I better go see him right away!"

Joe, from behind bars, pleaded, "Bob, I've been framed! I'm a law-and-order man. You know that... Help me!" Bob assured him, "I have, Joe. I've posted your bail."

Joe grumbled, "Nothing like this has ever happened to me. Did you ever hear of anything like it?" Bob answered, "Yes, Joe. In fact, the same thing happened to another guy named Joe."

Bob began telling Joe about the biblical Joseph. Jacob (Israel) had 12 sons, and Joseph was his favorite. The other brothers hated Joseph because he always told their father everything they did, so they got even.

Joseph’s brothers betrayed him and sold him as a slave for 20 pieces of silver. Joseph cried, "Lord, why did they do this to me?" His troubles were only beginning.

When Joseph reached Egypt, he was sold to Potiphar, the captain of Pharaoh’s guard. Potiphar soon realized Joseph was a wise servant and put him in charge of his entire household. God blessed Potiphar’s house for Joseph’s sake, and everything Joseph touched prospered.

Joseph, described as handsome and innocent, loved God and was a blessing to all. But Satan hated Joseph and used Potiphar’s wife to try to destroy him. She lusted after Joseph and kept trying to seduce him, but he always rejected her.

One day she grabbed Joseph, but he pulled away and fled, leaving his coat in her hand. She was furious and decided to frame Joseph. She cried loudly, accusing Joseph of trying to rape her. Everyone believed her, including her husband. In a rage, Potiphar put Joseph in Pharaoh’s special prison.

Bob told Joe that God was still with Joseph, giving him favor in the eyes of the prison warden, who soon put Joseph in charge of the entire prison.

Later, two men were brought to the prison - Pharaoh's baker and his butler. Both men had offended Pharaoh and were scared. They were upset about their strange dreams and didn’t understand what they meant. What happened in that prison cell was about to change world history.

Joe listened as Bob explained that Joseph had a special gift God gave him. When Joseph was a boy, he dreamt amazing dreams. His brothers hated him because of a dream Joseph had where they all bowed before him.

Joe leaned in as Bob continued, explaining that Joseph interpreted the dreams of the baker and the butler accurately. The baker was hanged, while the butler was released to serve Pharaoh again.

The butler had promised to tell Pharaoh about Joseph, but he forgot. So Joseph remained in prison, still trusting God to fulfill His promises.

Two years later, Pharaoh had troubling dreams. His magicians couldn’t interpret them, but the butler suddenly remembered Joseph and told Pharaoh about him.

Joseph told Pharaoh that it was God who reveals dreams, not himself. Pharaoh ordered Joseph brought before him immediately.

Joseph explained to Pharaoh that God’s dreams foretold a terrible famine after seven years of good harvests. Joseph urged Pharaoh to appoint someone to gather and store food during the good years in preparation.

Pharaoh said, "Joseph, you are the man for the job! You will be second to me in all the land."

Just think, Bob said, the one who was framed, rotting in prison, was lifted up in one hour to become a savior in Egypt.

When the famine hit, everything was destroyed, but Joseph had stored enough grain to feed all who came. Even Potiphar and his treacherous wife had to beg Joseph for food.

Joseph’s earlier dreams were fulfilled as his brothers bowed before him, asking for help.

Joseph brought his starving family to Egypt, and Pharaoh gave them the best land. What his brothers meant for evil, God meant for good.

Joe was amazed by the story and said, "Man, what a story!"

Bob smiled and said, "Now, let me tell you about the biggest frame-up in all history."

He explained how the Creator of the universe came as a man — Jesus. But no one recognized Him, even though He came as the Savior of the world.

Jesus warned people of God’s judgment and hell, speaking as no one before had. The religious crowd became furious, demanding His death, and so they framed Him.

The Lord Jesus was betrayed for 30 pieces of silver. Witnesses lied, Jewish laws were violated, and He was sentenced to a terrible death. But He came from heaven to die for our sins.

His precious blood was shed to wash away our sins.

"But did He really die?" Bob asked.

Joe gasped, "No! Three days later, Jesus Christ rose from the dead in power and glory."

Bob said, "The course of world history was changed forever by the greatest life ever lived."

"And you know what, Joe? It was the Lord Jesus Christ who delivered Joseph out of his troubles."

Bob asked Joe, "How about you? Will you turn yourself over to Christ and let Him deliver you from your sins and the mess you're in?"

Joe kneeled down, tears streaming. "I will! Oh, Lord Jesus, please take over my life. I’m a terrible sinner. Forgive me and save me from the hell You warned us about."

Thirty minutes later, the phone rang. Joe answered, looking shocked. "Excuse me, Joey, but this call is for you."

"It’s from the police. Oh, I’m so sorry."

Bob said, "Joe Harris? We traced the serial number on that gun to its owner."

His son had confessed to planting the gun in Joe’s pocket. All charges were dropped.

At death, all our lives will be replayed. Satan is a master at betrayal. He blinds our minds to the fact that we are all sinners in need of a Savior.

Jesus is our only hope. If we receive Him as our personal Savior and Lord, He promises to clear all charges and set us free.

Title: Free at Last
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Carter
Responses:
Once upon a time, every person was bound by sin, falling short of the glory of God. The path might have seemed right to many, but it ultimately led to death. Sin was evident from conception, passed down through generations, and brought death upon all people because everyone had sinned. Like an unclean thing, iniquities swept people away like the wind.

Some cried out in anguish, asking who could rescue them from this deathly bondage. From heaven, the LORD looked upon the children of men to see if any would seek and understand God. Knowing this, God sent His Son into the world—not to condemn but to save.

The Son of God came to offer freedom, standing between humanity and the devil. What is a man willing to give in exchange for his soul? Jesus came not to be served but to serve, giving His life as a ransom for many. God's love shone through as He gave His only begotten Son, so that whoever believes in Him would not perish but have eternal life.

Jesus mentioned that He would be in the heart of the earth for three days and nights, but then He rose again—He is risen! He declared, "I am the living one; I was dead, and behold, I am alive forevermore, holding the keys to death and hell."

If anyone confesses with their mouth and believes in their heart that Jesus was raised, they shall be saved and welcomed. No one who comes to Him will be turned away. Faithful servants who follow Him will enter into the joy of their Lord.

The Son of man came to seek and save the lost. Jesus carries the yoke that burdens humankind and calls those who are weary to find rest in Him. He reminds believers, "Do not let your heart be troubled. Believe in God, believe also in me." He breaks the chains that bind, freeing those held captive by sin. Joy fills the heavens when a sinner repents, for God rejoices over each saved soul.

Finally, the promise stands firm: whoever calls upon the name of the Lord will be saved. The battle is won, sin defeated, and salvation offered freely to all who believe.

Thus, from bondage and death to freedom and life, the story of redemption unfolds through Jesus Christ, the Savior of the world.

Title: Friend or Foe?
Subject: Judgment Day
Author: Chick
Responses:
A young man walks through the city, wary of the surveillance around him as cameras follow his every move. He’s reminded that “Big Brother” knows his name and where he lives, but there is someone else watching even more closely — his Creator, the Lord Jesus Christ, who knows everything he is thinking.

The story goes back to the beginning, when all things were made by God, and without Him nothing was made. God formed mankind and holds every breath in His hands. Every thought and action are recorded—the good, the bad, and the ugly.

But humanity quickly descended into evil, prompting God to flood the earth, sparing only one family to start anew. Despite this fresh start, people continued to rebel. Instead of judgment, God gave the Ten Commandments, which humanity hated then and continues to disregard.

God is righteous and sinless. Breaking even one command means being a sinner, destined for hell. Yet, despite mankind’s doom, God showed His great love by sending the only One who could help us—Jesus Christ.

Jesus spoke God’s words directly, teaching love, forgiveness, healing the sick, and raising the dead. He warned the world would hate His followers. People found Jesus offensive, even blocking His name in schools and forbidding prayers using His name. Yet, they use His name disrespectfully as a swear word, showing how little respect remains.

Television and films portray Jesus poorly, with professors and so-called intellectuals mocking Him, claiming He wasn’t divine, or distorting His story. Despite this, Jesus prayed for those who insulted Him, and God hears every insult.

Jesus himself said that every idle word spoken would be accounted for at judgment. People continue to mock and sneer at Him, but payday is coming. Many show no fear of God, and so appear corrupt and unclean to Him.

God sent Jesus to take the guilt of our sins, allowing Himself to be crucified and murdered because we cannot pay the price. Jesus shed His blood—the only thing that could wash away our sins—and rose from the dead three days later, changing the world forever.

Jesus declared He is the light of the world, the beginning and the end, holding all power in heaven and earth. He is the only way to the Father, making all other religions wrong.

A man falls to his knees, confessing belief in Jesus and asking for forgiveness, trusting Him as his Savior. Yet Satan is furious, torturing believers and trying to deny Jesus as the only way to heaven. Millions have been martyred for the faith and still are persecuted today.

Jesus will return at the Battle of Armageddon to rule the world from Jerusalem. Judgment will be given to Him to judge every nation for their crimes. There are two judgments, and each person will face one.

The judgment seat of Christ is only for believers, who will give an account of how they served Jesus. Many who consider themselves Christians will be shocked to lose their rewards, while humble servants of Jesus receive great honor.

Believers full of shame will answer for disobedience, and Jesus’ judgment of believers will be severe. Outside judgment waits for those who died in sin, suffering torment and awaiting the final judgment by Jesus with no one to defend them.

Hell is like jail, a holding place for those awaiting judgment. Every thought and deed will be played back, with no secrets hidden. Those not found in the book of life will be cast into everlasting fire prepared for the devil and his angels.

Jesus can be a loving friend if accepted as Savior, or a merciless enemy if rejected. The story ends with a plea to trust Jesus with all your heart now, as this may be your only chance. The choice between Heaven and Hell is yours to make.

Title: Gay Blade, The
Subject: Homosexuality
Author: Carter
Responses:
The story begins with a traditional wedding ceremony where a priest asks, "Wilt thou have this man as thy wedded spouse?" to which the response is a firm "I do!" Following the wedding, the couple drives away with a "Just Married" sign, highlighting that same-sex marriages, though controversial, are becoming more visible.

The narrative then shifts to depict the rise of a gay revolution, symbolized by the Greek letter lambda. The revolution is often seen as a joke by many, but it is serious to those involved. Emerging from what is described as a shadowy, oppressive society, individuals suffering from rejection and despair come forward, seeking acceptance. These individuals lead tragic lives filled with endless longing and remorse, challenging the perception of homosexuality.

"Gays" and lesbians have become common figures in media, appearing in TV sitcoms and talk shows. They are active in clubs, churches, and even school classrooms, advocating for equal rights and promoting homosexuality as a normal and healthy sexual outlet. They claim a 10% population representation, although studies suggest the number is under 2 percent. They are present in various professions and no longer hide their identity.

The story then references archaeological findings of ancient Canaanite ruins depicting religious worship, which reveal practices condemned by God. These findings are said to support biblical laws that forbid covenants with certain behaviors to prevent their spread. The focus turns to biblical accounts of Sodom, known for its great wickedness, where God planned to bring judgment.

Two angels are sent to Sodom to rescue Lot, Abraham’s nephew. Lot welcomes the angels into his home, preparing a feast for them. However, Sodom becomes infamously known for its "gay" men, who surround Lot’s house, demanding to engage sexually with the visitors. Lot offers his daughters instead to protect his guests, but the crowd rejects this and threatens worse violence.

The angels intervene, pulling Lot inside and striking the men with blindness, causing them to stumble in their search for the door. Lot and his family are safely removed before God rains down fire and brimstone, destroying the city. Archaeological notes beside this recount evidence supporting the biblical destruction of Sodom.

The narrative condemns homosexuality as sin and describes new laws encouraging those involved to be aggressive. It emphasizes that only Jesus Christ can overcome this "demonic power." Biblical injunctions against homosexuality are quoted, calling it an abomination and warning of judgment.

The story urges those involved in such sin to turn away and seek Christ's help to overcome it, contrasting this with the refusal some express to change. It warns of the shortened life expectancy for male homosexuals due to disease and violence, referencing Romans 1:27.

The story continues by stating all humans are guilty of sin and need salvation, which is provided through Jesus Christ’s sacrifice on the cross. Those who accept Him are transformed into new beings, but those who reject Him will face eternal judgment.

In conclusion, it offers a message of hope through surrender to Jesus, promising a new life free from sin, while warning of the consequences of rejecting God’s grace.

Title: Gladys
Subject: Occult
Author: Chick
Responses:
One evening, a woman was surprised to see her Aunt Gladys arrive at her home unexpectedly. Aunt Gladys explained that she had just arrived in town to attend the Astrology Convention, where she was the guest speaker. When asked how long she would be staying, Aunt Gladys said she would be in town for three days and would stay with her niece because hotels were too expensive.

During her stay, Aunt Gladys mentioned that she had written a book called "It's in the Stars" and was gaining fame, with critics calling her "The Amazing Gladys" and a "prophet of God," especially after recent events. Curious, her niece asked what had happened. Aunt Gladys replied that she had been offered her own talk show by a network. She then asked what was for dinner, saying she was starving.

Aunt Gladys' niece was hosting a small gathering that evening, introducing Aunt Gladys to her friends Bob and Helen. Gladys proudly declared herself fabulous, an author, and a prophet of God. When asked if she was like the prophet Isaiah, she showed interest but did not know much about Isaiah. Bob explained that Isaiah was a prophet but didn’t have a show like Gladys.

Bob and Gladys had a discussion about prophets, with Gladys emphasizing the special gifts she had, including visions, communicating with spirits, and having a guide named George. Suddenly, the figure of George appeared, a strange creature warning Gladys about others but she dismissed him.

The topic turned to the prophet Isaiah, and Bob explained that Isaiah was one of God’s greatest prophets, ministering for over 40 years and never missing a single prophecy. He shared how Isaiah’s prophecies about Jesus' birth, rejection, suffering, and mission had all come true. George was offended by this talk and tried to distract Gladys, but she brushed him off.

Bob recited several specific prophecies from Isaiah about Jesus being born of a virgin, healing the blind, being rejected, and suffering. He described how Jesus fulfilled these prophecies, including His crucifixion, which was remembered vividly by George. Bob explained the significance of Jesus’ sacrifice and resurrection, highlighting it as the fulfillment of Isaiah’s predictions.

When Bob asked Gladys what would happen if Isaiah had missed just one prophecy, she couldn’t answer. Bob then told her about Moses and how God provided a way to identify a false prophet—if their prophecies didn’t come true, they were false. Gladys was shocked and accused Bob of insulting her. She was told that those who lied or propagated false teachings were an abomination to God, referencing the Bible.

Gladys was so offended that she decided to leave and called her sponsor on the phone to be picked up. Meanwhile, in another location, Holly, a witch, was still being prayed for by her friends despite consistently rejecting their help and calling them names.

Gladys told Holly about Bob Williams, the man Holly despised for calling her a false prophet and liar. Holly admitted she had put a death curse on Bob. Suddenly, Holly's car collided with a truck in an accident, causing an explosion. Holly and Gladys, now dead, found themselves in the afterlife.

Holly saw Lucifer and claimed she would soon be his master, but then realized it was too late for her. She demanded to see Lucifer, who told her where she would spend eternity. Meanwhile, Gladys was shown to also be in the Lake of Fire.

On Judgement Day, both Gladys and Holly appeared before Jesus. Jesus reminded them that He died on the cross for their sins but they rejected Him. They were told to depart into everlasting fire prepared for the devil and his angels. The message was clear: while the Lake of Fire is real, there is only one way to escape it—by believing in Jesus Christ.

The story ends by urging readers to make the choice between heaven or hell, emphasizing that the decision is theirs to make.

Title: Global Warming
Subject: Global Warming
Author: Chick
Responses:
The story begins with a broadcast of a man warning about global warming and its consequences. He declares that the world was warned but ignored the signs, and now people will have to pay the price they caused. The question is posed: Is this the end of the world?

Next, brilliant scientists advise ordinary people about climate changes and the dangers of global warming. One scientist declares with urgency that they have just created global warming. People wonder if Mother Earth is doomed because of humanity, trusting the word of scientists but deciding to think further.

The narrative then shifts to a historical perspective, recalling the Dark Ages when the Catholic Church ruled the known world. People dared not question the Church's predictions, especially when they claimed the world would end by the year 1000. Terrified peasants brought gifts to monasteries, praying that God would forgive them, even offering their animals.

When the apocalypse did not come, the peasants were confused. But when they tried to reclaim their cow from the Church, they were told it belonged to God, not them. This created a divide between those who benefitted and those who suffered.

A prophet named Nostradamus, born in 1503, predicted a war lasting until the end of the world in 1999. His mentor criticized him for predicting the future without understanding the present. Nostradamus’s mistakes led people to doubt scientific claims, while some "scientific" predictions, such as England disappearing by 2000, were also proven wrong.

Other failed predictions included claims about the extinction of sea life, the melting of the Arctic, and rare snowfall in the future. Snowstorms in 2011 stranded thousands, further casting doubt on global warming predictions.

The story continues with examples of false alarms, such as a predicted "black blizzard" in 1996 that never occurred. Despite the failures of science and prophecy, some climate scientists and activists claim humanity is close to a climate Armageddon.

The narrative contrasts science with scripture, highlighting that science men do not believe in the Bible, and environmentalists pray to deities like Ixchel and Gaia instead of Jesus. It claims that the Earth belongs to God, not mankind, and cites passages from Isaiah, Psalms, and other scriptures to emphasize divine sovereignty over the planet.

The story introduces powerful spiritual forces, naming Jesus Christ as the most powerful force in the universe, opposed by Satan and other dark entities. It explains that when Adam and Eve sinned, domination over Earth was lost to Satan, causing wars, misery, and death.

Jesus Christ is described as having died on the cross to pay for humanity’s sins, shedding His blood and rising again. The story critiques those who deny this truth or mock the faith.

It further discusses mankind’s rejection of Jesus despite thousands of years, linking global troubles and ignored commandments to this spiritual rebellion. Prophecies from Revelation about plagues and natural disasters are referenced, asserting that man cannot cause true global warming and that future supernatural events are upcoming.

The story declares that Jesus will reign over the Earth for 1,000 years, restoring it. After that reign, all who died in sin will face judgment. It warns of eternal torment for those not found in the Book of Life and urges readers not to let this fate happen to them.

The final message is a choice: Heaven or Hell, urging belief in Jesus Christ for salvation with the biblical promise from Acts 16:31: "Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved."

This narrative blends history, prophecy, scientific skepticism, and Christian theology to address the concept of global warming within a spiritual context.

Title: God With Us
Subject: Ten Commandments
Author: Chick
Responses:
Two kids are hanging out when a man overhears them using foul language and warns them to watch their mouths. A third man confronts the kids about saying "Jesus Christ" in vain, explaining that they took the name of the Lord in vain. The kids mock him, but he insists they don't understand what it means. Curious, one kid asks him to explain.

The man starts by saying that God existed before anything else and that Jesus Christ, God the Son, created the entire universe in six days. He describes Jesus as awesome, the creator of heaven and hell, and the one who decides each person's eternal destiny.

He explains Jesus' name must be respected, quoting the Bible's commandment not to misuse it. The kids are surprised to learn Jesus was involved in Old Testament times, punishing the wicked and helping those who loved God.

The man recounts how wicked people populated the earth, and God, through Jesus, destroyed the world with a flood, saving only Noah and his family. Despite the flood, mankind remained sinful, and some cities were extremely evil, even provoking God's wrath through fire.

Because people didn’t know right from wrong, God gave laws through Moses. Some people hated these laws, but Jesus gave them regardless. The man goes through some laws, such as honoring God, respecting parents, prohibiting murder, adultery, lying, and stealing. Breaking these laws results in death, highlighting their seriousness.

The kids are uneasy, realizing how often they break these laws. Then the man explains that prophets foretold a special person would be born—a virgin birth fulfilling specific prophecies. The Holy Ghost made a miracle happen by placing God the Son inside a virgin named Mary.

He tells how shepherds and Wise Men came to worship Jesus when He was born, following a star signaling His arrival. As Jesus grew, He lived a perfect life and performed miracles, including raising the dead. Jesus came to do something special for humanity.

The man tells the kids that everyone sins and deserves hell, but God loved them so much that Jesus died on the cross to wash away their sins. After Jesus died, He rose again three days later, offering eternal life to those who believe.

The kids want this gift and are told to ask Jesus into their heart and be saved. They both pray, and the man witnesses them becoming born again, feeling clean and wanting to live like Jesus.

Finally, the man warns that if someone treats Jesus as a joke or curse word, they'll face judgment and eternal separation from God. He encourages them to believe in Jesus to be saved and live forever with God.

Title: God's Little Angel
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Carter
Responses:
One night, a mother quickly told her daughter Amy to get in the car. Amy asked where they were going, and her mother explained they were moving and told her to buckle up. Inside the car, Amy noticed many packed boxes and wondered why they were there. Then she asked about her father’s whereabouts. Her mother sadly explained that Daddy was not coming with them. As they drove away, Amy called out for her Daddy.

The next week, Amy sat with her mother and little brother at a theater. Curious, she asked why Daddy didn’t move with them. Her mother told her that Daddy hurt them and wouldn’t be coming anymore. Amy wanted to see her father but was too distracted by all the pretty lights and the excitement of the play starting.

During the play, Amy saw an angel and declared she wanted to be God’s little angel because angels always do what’s right and get to be in heaven with God. Her mother teased her, saying angels can’t grow wings, but Amy insisted she would still be an angel and do everything right. She believed if she was a perfect angel, Daddy would come back and they’d be a happy family again.

Her mother warned that may not happen but said if Amy wanted to be God’s little angel, she could try. Amy agreed and said she would be perfect. Later, her mother praised her for being a good girl and wanted to reward her with some cake. But when her mother asked if she took some cake, Amy denied it even though she clearly had. Her mother caught her and explained that no one can be an angel because everyone is a little sinner inside. She explained that’s why Jesus came to earth—because only Jesus is perfect.

Amy was stunned and asked if that meant she was stuck being bad and wouldn’t get into heaven. Her mother patiently explained that Jesus did something special—He came to earth as a baby, then a boy, then a man, and only He was perfect because He is God. Amy wanted to know what Jesus did, and her mother told her Jesus taught there is only one way to heaven—believing in Him.

Amy wanted to understand more, so her mother told her a story about a rich young ruler who asked Jesus what he must do to inherit eternal life. The rich man tried to be good, keeping all the commandments since youth. Jesus told him he lacked one thing and needed to sell all his possessions, give to the poor, and follow Him. The man went away sad because he was very rich, but Amy’s mother explained that the man’s true problem was trusting in his riches and not really keeping God’s commandments.

Jesus showed the man he was a sinner like everyone else, but the man wouldn’t admit it, so he was not going to heaven. Amy was saddened and wondered what sinners must do to be saved. Her mother told her that to be saved, sinners must admit they need a Savior.

Amy admitted she was a sinner and asked what she should do next. Her mother explained how Jesus shed His blood on the cross to pay for sins and that three days later, Jesus rose from the dead and appeared to His friends. Amy’s mother then asked if she believed what Jesus did and if she wanted forgiveness. Amy said yes and prayed, admitting she was a sinner and believing Jesus died for her sins, asking for forgiveness and salvation.

Amy said she still wanted to do good but now wanted to thank God for forgiving her. Her mother said that was the best reason to do good. Finally, they filled out a little card for Amy to remember the day she accepted Jesus as her Savior.

The story ends with a scripture reminding believers to believe in Jesus and the importance of confessing sin and faith in Him.

Title: Going Down?
Subject: Hell
Author: Chick
Responses:
A tense showdown unfolds in the Old West when Hank Dagget, seeking revenge, spots a lone Marshal. Determined to confront the man who killed his little brother Bobby, Hank calls out to the Marshal, ordering him to drop his rifle. The Marshal recognizes Hank and calmly responds, recalling the tragic event. Hank angrily swears to kill the Marshal, who stands fearless and challenges him to try. The two men engage in a shootout, with Hank firing at the Marshal, who falls to the ground. However, bystanders intervene before Hank can do any more harm, accusing him of shooting the Marshal in the back and demanding he be tied up without trial. Hank boasts that he killed the Marshal and is unafraid of death or the "Death Angel," prompting others to condemn him and insist he’ll burn in hell forever.

In modern times, Emily scolds her husband Horatio Evans for watching such violent westerns and using offensive language, urging him to turn it off. Horatio shares that the film made him think about themes of hell, which Emily finds unacceptable and believes is an outdated subject best ignored. Curious despite her reservations, Horatio decides to ask their local pastor, Reverend Brinks, about the reality of hell and eternal punishment.

Reverend Brinks assures Horatio that hell is not real, calling it a relic of the Dark Ages and emphasizing God's love. Yet, four nights later, Horatio is involved in a horrific car crash and rushed to the hospital, critically injured along with his wife Emily, who does not survive. Horatio shocks the Reverend with his account of near-death experiences where he witnessed hell’s terrors firsthand, saw demonic creatures, and heard terrifying screams. He believes Emily’s soul is now trapped in hell because of the warnings he ignored.

Hospital staff dismiss Horatio’s visions as hallucinations, but a nurse who cared for him suggests Horatio seek help from her grandfather, a retired pastor named Frank Thompson, who might understand what Horatio experienced. Every night thereafter, Horatio is haunted by nightmarish spirits of souls crying out for warning about hell, blaming him for their fate. Exhausted, Horatio hopes Frank can offer guidance.

The next day, Horatio meets Frank Thompson and shares his ordeal. Frank explains that Horatio has been given a rare glimpse of the spiritual reality most people deny. He emphasizes the urgency of warning others, as billions of souls are already in hell, and many more are on the way due to the lack of warnings. Citing scripture, Frank stresses that God holds accountable those who fail to warn the wicked, and that Jesus Himself spoke often about hell, judging souls and urging people to fear the consequences of sin.

Frank recounts the biblical story of Lazarus and the rich man, whose soul suffered in hell, trying to warn his family. He reminds Horatio that pastors have a duty to warn their congregations, even if the message is difficult. Horatio admits he’s afraid and has never truly believed in hell until now. Frank encourages him that God’s love means salvation is possible, and reveals that Jesus died on the cross to forgive sins, promising new life to those who believe.

Horatio surrenders his life to Jesus, accepting forgiveness and salvation. Frank comforts him, assuring him that his name is now in the book of life and that he will reign with Christ upon His return. Though many may reject the warning and turn away, Horatio is resolved to share the urgent message of hell’s reality, refusing to let others suffer the same fate.

Frank warns that many will ignore the truth until it’s too late, urging anyone who reads their story to take the message seriously and accept salvation while there is still time. The story closes with an invitation to respond to the gospel, offering to pray with those who want to avoid hell, receive forgiveness for their sins, and believe in Jesus Christ as their Savior.

Title: Going Home
Subject: Drugs/Alcohol
Author: Carter
Responses:
Somewhere in Africa, a sick man urgently wanted to see the doctor, pleading because he felt very ill and needed to lie down. When he arrived, he was told that the doctor wasn't there and there were no beds available. The staff said they couldn't help him.

Later, a nurse brought a man into the room, saying the child he was carrying had just died. A nurse called after a man carrying a patient, telling him to come back because they had found a bed.

Two days later, the sick man named Peter was at the doctor's home. Peter told the doctor he felt very bad. The doctor then explained that the lab results for Peter’s blood were not good. Peter asked if he had the "thinning sickness," and the doctor confirmed this.

The doctor solemnly told Peter that he had AIDS and unless God healed him, he would die soon. Peter was afraid, but the doctor said that everyone has to die someday and revealed that he too was dying of AIDS. 

Peter was later interrupted by a nurse informing the doctor, Dr. Burton, that he had a long-distance call from Atlanta. Excusing himself, Dr. Burton answered. On the phone, someone named Charlie asked how he was. Dr. Burton responded that he was rich in Christ, but Charlie told him to stop preaching and asked what was going on.

Charlie described a dire situation in Africa, saying entire villages were gone and that one in three people in his area had AIDS. Charlie asked if it was that bad. Dr. Burton replied it was worse and that the poor nation was doomed. He warned Charlie to get used to it as the U.S. could face the same fate in a few years.

Another call came from an authority telling Burton to leave the area immediately, which was an order. However, Burton expressed his love for the people in Africa and said they needed him there. He admitted he had an accident in the lab and expected to live only about six months. Despite knowing his fate, he said his patients relied on him and he was the only doctor they had.

Back at the clinic, a nurse gave Peter medicine to help with his pain, mentioning it was from Dr. Burton, who was "almost nice enough to be an African." She also said Burton loved Peter and would tell him about a wonderful gift soon, though Peter wondered what that could be.

In a tense meeting, Charlie asked for Burton's evaluation of the AIDS situation. Burton called it a "death zone" with no hope left. Charlie asked if they should involve the news media, but another man shouted "No! You idiot!"

The doctor asked Peter about his personal life. Peter revealed he was once married, but his wife and children had died. The doctor expressed sympathy for the loss, saying it must have been horrible.

When asked about his parents, Peter said they had thrown him out when he was only nine years old. The doctor said he supposed Peter’s parents loved him, but Peter replied he never saw his parents as he was an orphan. 

The doctor then told Peter about a wonderful Father who loved him more than he could describe. He said when he died, he would go live with this Father. Peter was surprised and asked what he meant.

Suddenly, the nurse interrupted to call the doctor for surgery, and Burton excused himself. Peter asked if Burton was okay in his head and how he could say he would live with this Father after dying. The nurse assured him that Burton was fine.

The next day, the doctor asked Peter if anyone had ever given him a present. Peter replied an old man had given him candy once. The doctor explained that a gift isn’t really a gift until the person accepts it, and Peter agreed.

The doctor asked if he could tell Peter about a wonderful gift from God. Peter said he was too evil to talk about God. The doctor said everyone knew sinners wouldn't be allowed in heaven. He asked if Peter would be interested if there was a way to remove his sins. Peter said who wouldn’t?

The doctor told Peter that God loved him and had already taken care of the sin problem, but he must believe what God says for it to work.

He read John 3:16, explaining that God gave His only Son, Jesus, so whoever believes in Him should not perish but have everlasting life.

The doctor explained Jesus died on the cross for their sins and rose from the dead three days later. Peter questioned how Jesus’s blood could do that and who Jesus was.

The doctor said Jesus shed His blood so Peter could go to heaven and that Jesus could be his dearest friend or his worst nightmare on Judgment Day.

He quoted Colossians 1:16-17, explaining Jesus created the universe and everything in it, visible and invisible, and that Jesus holds all things together.

The doctor said Jesus left heaven, was sacrificed in their place so they could reign with Him in glory and unspeakable riches.

Peter was then told that Jesus was in heaven building him a mansion, but it was his only if he accepted the gift. Peter said he would think about it because it sounded too good to be true.

The nurse urged Peter to consider that he could die that night, asking if he had suffered enough and why he would choose to die in sin and suffer forever in hell.

Two hours later, Peter prayed, asking Jesus to save him from hell and to be with him when he died. He asked the Lord to please save him.

Two nights later, Peter claimed to see Jesus.

When the doctor was asked how Peter was, he replied Peter "just went home," implying he had passed away and gone to be with Jesus.

Title: Going to the Dogs
Subject: Bible Stories
Author: Carter & 3rd
Responses:
There was a rotten king named Ahab who married a rotten queen named Jezebel. They had a rotten little brat named Ahab, who eventually became the king of Israel. Ahab married a foreign princess named Jezebel, who had a serious problem—she was deeply into devil worship. They were a lovely couple in a very wicked way.

Jezebel was a witch, and she had the prophets of God destroyed. She imported 450 prophets of Satan to establish Baal worship, making Baal the god of Israel. The Lord God in heaven was furious.

God had given Israel a commandment to protect them, saying, "Thou shalt have no other gods before me. Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image, nor bow down thyself to them, nor serve them: for I the Lord thy God am a jealous God" (Exodus 20:3-5). God hates idols and graven images because demons operate behind them, deceiving the worshipper.

God declared war on Baal. He sent his prophet, Elijah, to give the people bad news, telling them, "God will not let it rain until I say so." Then Elijah disappeared.

Three and a half years later, there was still no rain. Elijah returned and challenged the prophets of Baal. The people were ordered to Mt. Carmel to watch a contest between the prophets of Baal and Elijah. Within 24 hours, Jezebel’s evil system would be shattered.

Two days later, as it rained outside Ahab’s palace, Ahab was pale and nervous, saying, "It was a nightmare! Your prophets built an altar for Baal, and Elijah built one for his God. Both sides prayed for their God to send fire and burn up their sacrifice. Elijah won! His sacrifice burned, but Baal’s didn’t! Your prophets looked like fools!"

Jezebel angrily demanded, "Where ARE my prophets?" Ahab nervously answered, "Elijah had them all killed." Jezebel then ordered, "I want Elijah dead! TODAY!! Do you HEAR me?"
