But Elijah thought he was the only faithful one left in Israel. God rebuked him, revealing there were 7,000 in Israel who had not bowed to Baal or kissed him. Years later, Ahab saw his neighbor Naboth’s vineyard and wanted it. He offered Naboth a better vineyard in exchange, but Naboth refused, saying it had been in his family for generations.

Ahab was furious, thinking, "What an honor it would be for Naboth to give me his vineyard." When Naboth refused, thinking, "How dare he turn down his magnificent king?" Ahab was upset because Naboth had messed with the wrong man.

Back at the palace, Ahab was upset and said, "You won’t eat! You won’t speak! What’s wrong, Ahab?" He replied tearfully, "Naboth won’t give me his vineyard." Jezebel comforted him, promising, "Cheer up, poor baby. I’ll take care of it." Ahab asked, "You will?"

Jezebel wrote letters to Israel’s leaders, instructing them to frame and kill Naboth. She signed Ahab’s name and used his seal to make them official. At a surprise party in Naboth’s honor, two men stood up and said, "Naboth cursed God…and the king! He is worthy of death!" Naboth couldn’t believe what was happening to him.

The crowd shouted, "Kill him! Kill the blasphemer!" They murdered poor Naboth, an innocent man. The dogs licked up his blood, and God saw it all.

Jezebel told Ahab, "Naboth is dead!" Ahab was excited, "Oh? Wow!" Jezebel said, "Yes, Ahab. Go take his vineyard. It now belongs to you!" God then told Elijah to meet Ahab face to face. Elijah said, "Ah, it’s ALL mine! I see him, Lord."

Elijah declared God’s judgment, saying, "Because thou hast sold thyself to work evil in the sight of the Lord...Thus saith the Lord, In the place where dogs licked the blood of Naboth...shall dogs lick thy blood...And the dogs shall eat Jezebel by the wall of Jezreel." Everyone gulped in fear as the prophecies began to come true.

For many years, the Jews were divided into two kingdoms: Israel, ruled by Ahab, and Judah, ruled by Jehosaphat. They didn’t love each other, and since Ahab wasn’t strong enough to take land from Syria, he convinced Jehosaphat to help him.

Jehosaphat, who loved God, joined forces with Ahab’s evil regime. Jehosaphat asked Ahab to bring in his prophets of God to see if their war was God’s will. Ahab’s prophets all said yes—except one: Micaiah.

When asked how the battle would go, Ahab’s prophets said, "Go fight… the Lord will let you win!" But Jehosaphat wanted to hear Micaiah’s opinion. Micaiah said, "If you come back alive, I’m no prophet!" Ahab, expecting this, threw Micaiah in prison and went to battle anyway, a decision that was dumb and disastrous.

God protected Jehosaphat, but Ahab was struck with an arrow in his back and the battle was lost. They headed home with Ahab dying, bleeding all over his chariot. They stopped at the exact spot where poor Naboth was murdered. When Ahab’s body was removed, the dogs licked up the blood, just as Elijah said they would.

Twenty years later, God’s judgment struck Jezebel. Her servants threw her out a palace window to her death, and then the dogs ate her body. God doesn’t play games—Ahab and Jezebel both went to hell. And as God watched, He was watching all of us too.

Looking into the future, the Bible says the Lord Jesus Christ, Creator of the universe, will judge everyone who has ever lived on this planet. Every person’s entire life is recorded for the Day of Judgment. Jesus said, "Every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment" (Matthew 12:36).

Revelation 20:12 describes the dead, small and great, standing before God as the books are opened, including the book of life, which judged them according to their works. Many ask, "Why didn’t somebody warn me?"

Jesus shed His precious blood to wash away sins so anyone can escape God’s judgment. "For God so loved the world (you), that He gave His only begotten Son (Jesus), that whosoever believeth in Him should not perish (in hell), but have everlasting life (in heaven)" (John 3:16).

Jesus loves you and wants you to be saved, so you can reign with Him in heaven. If you pray and say:

"Lord Jesus, I know I’m a sinner. I repent. I trust You and ask You to be my personal Saviour,"

then, as the Bible promises, whoever calls upon the name of the Lord shall be saved.

This is the true story of Ahab and Jezebel, a warning for all who hear it.

Title: Gold Fever
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
Once, a man stood surveying the ruins of what used to be his land, commenting sadly on how the war had devastated everything, leaving nothing behind. Someone else revealed the same was true for him, and suggested that the man needed to start over. Encouraging him, he said miners were getting rich out West, and if he was smart, he would go there too.

So Billy Cobb joined the desperate crowd heading West. They were a mix of ex-soldiers, hungry farmers, thieves, and killers, all driven by greed. Billy staked a claim near Camp Broken Claw, a lawless town on Black Mountain. He worked hard, trusting no one, just trying to survive.

One day, he met Big Mike Clausen, an old acquaintance who was presumed dead but was very much alive, infamous for being tough. Mike introduced Billy to his son, Jake. Billy remembered how his father once saved Mike’s life. They bonded, but Mike acknowledged the horrors they had endured in the war, describing it as a slaughterhouse and quoting a Bible verse about the chaos of battle.

Despite the harsh conditions, miners occasionally struck it rich. Old Sam was one such man who struck gold and became quite wealthy. The ladies of the town celebrated his success wildly, but the joy was short-lived. The next morning, Old Sam was found dead, shot in the back, his gold missing.

Mike confided in Billy that Sam’s money was gone and warned him to keep quiet if he ever struck gold. That night, a lightning bolt struck an old tree near Billy’s tent, revealing the largest gold nugget ever found in Black Mountain. Billy brought Big Mike and Jake along for protection as word spread about the worth of the nugget.

Mike promised Billy safety and rest before they left the mountain, but that night, Mike and Jake plotted to steal the gold. They crept into Billy’s tent, grabbed the money, and left, laughing as they rode away through the night.

Billy was found shot in the belly and unconscious. His money was gone along with his so-called friends. The preacher was called to help, and when Billy awoke, he met the kindly preacher who warned him of his dangerous path and compared his betrayal to Judas betraying Jesus.

Billy confessed the preacher was right and that he didn’t believe in hell before. The preacher shared his story of survival and faith after he had been attacked by an Indian war party when traveling West, left for dead but saved by Jesus.

Billy was curious about salvation, and the preacher explained how Jesus’ blood could wash away sins and open the way to heaven, quoting scriptures. He told Billy about Jesus’ sacrifice on the cross and resurrection, emphasizing that Jesus was the only way to heaven.

Billy asked what he must do, and the preacher told him to simply believe in Jesus. Billy prayed with the preacher, admitted he was a sinner, and asked Jesus to save him.

Because of his faith, Billy avoided eternal damnation, unlike Big Mike and Jake, who remain trapped in hell. Billy’s family was overjoyed when he walked through the gates of heaven, reunited at last.

The story closes with a challenge for the reader to choose between Jesus Christ or Satan, to believe in Jesus for salvation, and to accept the gift of eternal life that starts right now. Billy survived and was saved by the love of Jesus Christ, a gift offered to all.

Title: Gomez is Coming
Subject: Gangs
Author: Chick
Responses:
One night, a car sped down the street, headlights cutting through the darkness. A man inside the car exclaimed, "Man... I'm so HIGH!" His companion urged him, "Get ready, Homes!" Inside, two men prepared for a confrontation, one pointing a gun and asking, "Which one?" The other replied, "It doesn't matter!"

Gunfire erupted with a series of pops, and one of the men shouted, "I'm hit!" as he fell, victims screaming. The shooter, grinning, declared, "Not bad, huh? I got three of 'em." Later, a group gathered around a television showing news reports about the incident—two victims were on life support. The group’s tension rose when one man reminded them, "But Luis Gomez died at the scene." Another yelled, "You idiot! You killed the kid brother of Carlos Gomez!" 

Talk shifted to "The Butcher," the feared gangster in jail but due to be released soon. One man warned, "Are you CRAZY? The Butcher will kill us ALL if we help you." Another threatened the injured, "We don't know you anymore, man! You're DEAD already!"

The Butcher’s gang ordered their members to find the injured man and bring him back alive as a "present for the Butcher." They identified their target as Ricky Valdez, hiding at his mother’s house. The gang confronted Ricky, shouting, "Come out, Valdez, we KNOW you’re in there!" When he refused, they crashed through the door.

They captured a man, recognized as Luis, yelling in agony. The gang leader said, "Stop! He belongs to the Butcher. Throw him in the van." They taunted Ricky with cruel words, "Tonight, we’ll serve you a taco supreme... because tomorrow, you'll never have to worry about eating again." Ricky was gagged and bound.

The next day, behind bars, other inmates remarked, "There goes The Butcher back on the streets." One felt safer with him incarcerated, but the officer warned, "You'll be back, Gomez." Gomez replied defiantly, "Don’t count on it!"

Some inmates greeted Gomez warmly, offering "We’ve got something for you." When asked what was wrong, they said Gomez hadn’t spoken but was planning revenge. They warned others, "STAY OUT 'til I’m through." Gomez, gagged and tied, hinted darkly, "Valdez... you can't DREAM what I’m about to do."

An hour later, a man declared, "It’s too quiet! I’m going in." Others threatened, "You wanna DIE, stupid?" Despite warnings, the man entered and was shocked to see Ricky praying, saying, "Thank you, Lord Jesus, for coming into my heart."

Ten minutes later, Gomez gathered everyone, saying, "Come in. I want you ALL to hear this." He shared how, the previous night in his cell, he met a chaplain—tougher than himself. The chaplain asked Gomez if he’d ever heard of the worst killing in history: when man murdered God. Gomez was skeptical, but the chaplain explained how Jesus, who was sinless, died for humanity's sins and rose from the dead.

The chaplain urged Gomez to repent and accept Jesus as his Lord and Savior. Gomez, surprised, exclaimed, "You mean God would accept me after ALL the rotten things I’ve done?" The chaplain replied, "Hey, I was worse than you... and He saved me!"

Gomez found hope and peace he’d never known. Later, a friend testified, "God changed me and took away my hatred... even for Ricky! Even though he killed my kid brother, I could forgive HIM because Christ forgave ME." Another man urged, "Man, you GOTTA get even with him for killing Luis." The forgiving friend said, "No way, man! That’s not for me to worry about."

They reflected on how killing each other served Satan’s evil purpose. The devil loved it when unsaved people died, because they go straight to hell. But now, with Jesus, there was hope and miracles in their lives.

Finally, they encouraged others still in gangs to accept Jesus, saying, "Jesus died for you guys, too, and He WANTS to save you!" One man asked, "How many of you will say yes to Jesus?" Hands raised as the crowd replied, "We ALL will!"

The message was clear: Satan may deceive, but salvation is possible. Make your decision now—before it’s too late. "Let every thing that hath breath praise the LORD. Praise ye the LORD." (Psalm 150:6)

Title: Good Ol' Boys
Subject: Masonry
Author: Chick
Responses:
Here is the written story based on the comic strip:

In a small village, a group of armed men suddenly burst into a church during a worship service. They shouted for everyone to get on the floor and proclaimed, “We have come to kill all who believe in Jesus!” Then they gave the congregation an ultimatum: if they denied Jesus, they would be allowed to live.

They ordered those who wanted to live to stand against the wall. The frightened people pleaded desperately, willing to do anything to survive. Some blamed others for the situation, and one woman cried out for her children. Although terrified, some declared, “We will never betray our Lord Jesus Christ! Never… never!” The armed men grew angry and insulted them, calling them cowards, but the believers were resolute in their faith, standing their ground even as the gunfire erupted.

Later, a man named Bob recounted the story to his friend Robbie. He explained that the “Shining Path” had killed everyone except the pastor and his wife because they refused to deny Jesus. Robbie was shocked and asked why such things were happening. Bob reminded him the Bible foretells that all who live godly in Christ Jesus will suffer persecution, and those believers were willing to die for their love of Jesus.

Bob explained that Jesus taught Christians to love their enemies and pray for those who persecute them, but also shared the story of Peter, who denied Jesus three times before the rooster crowed. Peter was terrified and wept bitterly, but he eventually repented and was forgiven by Jesus.

Robbie said he would never deny Jesus, but Bob confronted him about a Masonic ring he was wearing. Bob claimed that Masonry requires its members to deny Jesus, replacing His light with a false, satanic light, and that it is fundamentally opposed to Christianity. He warned that joining the Masons is like spitting in Jesus’ face and walking in darkness.

Bob explained the dangers of secret societies and how Masonry teaches lies and even worships Lucifer. Robbie expressed fear and confusion, so Bob shared the good news of Jesus — that God sent His Son to rescue people by shedding His blood for their sins, dying, and rising again so they could be saved.

Robbie prayed and asked Jesus to forgive his sins and become his Savior. He felt a peace and joy he had never known before, understanding that God wants believers to live holy lives. Bob then gently urged Robbie to be cautious about his church pastor, who was involved in Masonry. When Robbie admitted his pastor's affiliation, Bob told him it made a big difference because Jesus is a jealous God and does not tolerate divided loyalty.

Bob warned that secret societies are detestable in God's eyes and one must choose whom to serve. He urged Robbie to repent, renounce Masonry, and wholeheartedly follow Jesus. Robbie agreed and asked for God’s forgiveness.

Finally, Bob advised Robbie that if he ever found a pastor who was a Mason and didn't renounce it, he should leave that church. He reminded Robbie of the promise that those who truly believe in Jesus would be saved and welcomed into heaven, contrasting that with the grim fate of those who reject Him.

The story ends with Robbie making a commitment to follow Jesus fully and walking in the light of truth and salvation.

Title: Great Escape, The
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
A man waited carefully as a car approached him at night, its headlights cutting through the darkness. Suddenly, someone yelled, "LOOK OUT!" The man sprang out of the way just in time as the car screeched to a halt nearby. Breathing heavily, he said, "He missed me!" Another man rushed over exclaiming, "Hey! You could’ve been killed!" The man on the ground answered fiercely, "That’s what I wanted!"

They decided to discuss the incident over a cup of coffee. Inside the car, they began talking about the environment. One of them explained that he had been studying environmental issues in college. The other argued that it was too late for any escape—that the problem had already become overwhelming. But the first insisted there was still hope.

The man studying the environment asked if the other knew how many acres of land on Earth could actually produce food. Surprised, the other said no. The explanation followed: due to erosion, deserts, marshes, mountains, polar ice caps, swamps, jungles, and unusable soil, only 2.5 billion acres remain productive. This is enough to provide an adequate diet for only one billion people, yet the global population is already over 8 billion and expected to reach 9 billion in just fifteen years.

The harsh reality of famine was described next: 40 million people currently face emergency levels of hunger. The seas are dying due to oil spills, plastic waste, overfishing, and climate change. Plankton, which produce half the world's oxygen, have declined drastically. Experts warn about mercury poisoning in fish. Air pollution fills the lungs of nine out of ten people, and climate change threatens to melt polar ice caps and flood cities. Despite these dire circumstances, the man studying the environment insisted there’s no real escape. Yet, he was sure that every exit was being blocked.

The other man shared bleak truths about humanity: rogue viruses could end civilization, nations face bankruptcy, and global riots could spark wars. Attempts to colonize the moon or other planets are currently just dreams—they are stuck on a dying planet.

The discussion turned to spiritual matters, with one man emphasizing that without faith, the situation seems hopeless. He revealed that these crises were predicted in the Bible centuries ago, referring to it as the Great Tribulation—a seven-year period of great suffering foretold by Jesus.

Jesus had said that during this time, the world would experience unprecedented tribulation, lawlessness, and turmoil. After World War II, an Antichrist figure known as the Beast would rise to power, bringing more conflict. Yet, this war would be decisive and brief.

Biblical prophecies from Ezekiel were discussed, predicting an alliance of Russia, Islamic nations, Germany, Libya, Ethiopia, and Turkey attacking Israel—a war that has been anticipated for decades. Despite Israel’s scattering, it has uniquely returned to its homeland, fulfilling prophecy.

Convinced that there must be a way out, the man asked for the escape. The answer was that Jesus Christ would remove His true followers from the earth before everything worsens—that is the only escape.

This event is called "The Blessed Hope." True believers would suddenly disappear, shocking the world. It’s not aliens taking them, but the Lord descending with the dead rising first. Believers will be caught up together in the clouds to meet the Lord, transformed instantly.

To join this escape, one must believe in Jesus Christ, turn from sin, and accept Him as Savior. Jesus came to earth, died, and paid the price for humanity’s sins.

The man accepted this, asking for forgiveness to be ready when the trumpet sounds. He felt clean and peaceful despite the chaos around. Grateful for learning about "The Great Escape," he was encouraged to share this hope with others while there is still time.

Title: Great One, The
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
This is the story of a man who lived in a big city. He graduated from a major university with honors and was very proud of himself. He then became very rich and famous, which made him even more proud. Everyone called him "The Great One."

He got married, and he and his wife had a little girl named Ashley. From that point on, "The Great One's" life would never be the same.

Ashley went to Sunday School where she learned that God loved her deeply and that He sent His Son, Jesus Christ, to die on the cross for her sins. She read in the Bible that salvation is a free gift, the gift of eternal life through Jesus Christ. Ashley learned that the only way to receive this gift was to repent of her sins and trust Jesus Christ as her Savior.

One day, Ashley got on her knees, admitted that she was a sinner, and asked Jesus to come into her heart and save her—and He did! She knew that she had just become a child of God and that she would go to heaven when she died.

The next day, Ashley asked her father, "Daddy, do you know where you will go when you die?" He responded proudly, saying he was far too educated to believe there is a God. When Ashley told him that the Bible says he couldn't go to heaven without Jesus, he scoffed, wondering what a mere child could possibly teach him.

Ashley warned her father that his pride would be his downfall, but "The Great One" refused to listen. She begged him to trust Jesus, but he declared that religion was only for the weak. Ashley told him she loved him and pleaded with him not to think he was smarter than God.

"The Great One" was furious, but his rebellion stopped him from trusting Christ. One day, he died. When he stood before Jesus, he learned he wasn't great at all. "Depart from me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels," Jesus said. But it was too late.

"The Great One" had been a fool because he rejected Christ, and he was cast into the lake of fire, the second death.

When Ashley died, she went straight to heaven where she would live with God forever.

This story reminds us of the most important message ever written: For God so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son, that whoever believes in Him should not perish but have everlasting life. Don’t let pride and rebellion take you to hell forever. Trust Jesus Christ right now.

Title: Greatest Insult, The
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
Once upon a time, a group of conspirators gathered in secret, struggling to figure out how to overthrow their beloved king, who was deeply loved by all his people. One conspirator suggested using lies and nasty insults to turn the king's loyal subjects into a howling mob. 

The next day, a town crier announced the king's latest celebration and feast, which everyone was invited to and eagerly anticipated. However, the conspirators believed the king was too good, too loved by everyone to be overthrown easily, but another conspirator dismissed that, claiming that everyone has a weak spot and loves gossip.

At the feast, the king reminded everyone that he had given his people homes, more land, and even exempted them from taxes. The people cheered, proclaiming that no king loved them like their own. But amid the crowd, questions arose about the queen's absence.

It all began with a tiny rumor—that the queen was sick, though others doubted the maid's word. Then whispers spread that the king might be poisoning the queen, fueling fear and suspicion among the people as the lies grew.

Within two months, the rumors had escalated to tales of a torture chamber and virgins chained to a wall. The lies turned darker—claiming the king hated women and loved men, and that he was a monster. The conspirators fueled the growing hatred until it became a roaring fire.

Despite hearing these insults, the king chose to ignore them, unwilling to confront the troublemakers. Unfortunately, his failure to act only made things worse. The angry mob stormed the palace, shouting for the king’s death, and they beheaded their generous ruler. Strangely, no one remembered the kindness he once showed them.

But above all earthly kings, there was a real King—God—who created the universe and gave a planet for man to inhabit. This King planted a beautiful garden for man and gave him a wife. He gave man a simple rule—to not eat from the tree of knowledge of good and evil.

Would this happy couple obey their generous King? Sadly, no. They turned against their King and God, despite all His loving warnings. For this act of rebellion, they were kicked out of the garden. Wickedness spread everywhere, and God decided to destroy humanity.

Only one man, Noah, remained faithful to God. God told Noah to build a giant boat and warn the people of the coming judgment. But the people insulted God, calling Noah insane and claiming there was no God.

God sent a worldwide flood that wiped out everyone on earth with no mercy. Noah and his family were the only ones saved. Yet even after the flood, people’s hearts did not change.

God sent His only begotten Son to earth on a special mission. The Bible says that this Son, Jesus, was with God from the very beginning and was God Himself. God placed Jesus in the womb of a virgin, and Jesus came into the world as a human.

By age 12, Jesus was already wise beyond his years, knowing Moses’ law better than the teachers. At 30, John the Baptist announced Jesus as the Lamb of God who takes away the sins of the world.

Jesus came to earth to be sacrificed to God, fulfilling the law. He boldly challenged the corrupt religious leaders and judged the world’s sins. Jesus also warned that the world’s wickedness would lead to destruction, just like in Noah’s day.

Jesus loves the guilty and provided a way for forgiveness. Though He was cursed, tortured, and sentenced to death by those He created, he died for mankind’s sins and rose from the dead three days later.

Today, Jesus invites everyone to turn to Him in faith and be forgiven, with the promise of eternal life in heaven. But many reject this only path to heaven, choosing instead to live in contempt of God.

Because of this rejection, God’s righteous judgment without mercy awaits the unrepentant. Everyone will stand before God, guilty for insulting Him by refusing His gift of forgiveness.

This comic ends with a call to repent, to believe in Jesus’ sacrifice, and to invite Him into one’s heart. Those who do so will be saved, while those who do not face eternal separation from God.

Will you choose to follow the real King and find forgiveness and life? The choice is yours.

Title: Greatest Story Ever Told
Subject: Bible Stories
Author: Carter
Responses:
Long ago, it was foretold by the ancients that a special star would appear, signaling the birth of the King of the Jews. This momentous event inspired the leaders of the land to send an envoy to worship this promised child. One said, "I will organize a caravan immediately," feeling honored to witness the fulfillment of this prophecy.

A great caravan was assembled, preparing for the long and perilous journey ahead. The wise men followed the star, carrying precious gifts to honor the newborn king. To truly understand this story, we must go back to the beginning, before the earth was even formed.

In the vastness of outer space existed a divine power known as the Godhead, composed of three distinct personalities: the Father, the Word, and the Holy Ghost, also called the Holy Spirit. These three are one, as described in sacred scriptures. From this Godhead originated the plan for the universe.

The second person of the Godhead, known as the Word, created the universe. The Bible states, "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. All things were made by him; and without him was not anything made that was made." This Word later became flesh and dwelt among us, becoming the very Great One that the wise men sought to see.

Around 700 B.C., the prophet Isaiah spoke of a mystery to come: "Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel," meaning "God with us." Seven centuries later, Jerusalem was ruled by Rome, and the Jewish people fervently prayed for the Messiah, the Promised One.

Into this world came the angel Gabriel, who visited a virgin named Mary, betrothed to Joseph of David's lineage. Gabriel spoke to Mary: "Fear not, Mary: for thou hast found favour with God." The angel revealed that Mary would conceive by the Holy Ghost and bring forth a son named Jesus, the Son of God.

Mary, astonished, asked how this could be since she had never known a man. Gabriel assured her, "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee." Mary accepted the message, declaring, "...be it unto me according to thy word," trusting that with God, nothing is impossible.

Meanwhile, Joseph was troubled by this news until God appeared to him in a dream, explaining that the child was conceived by the Holy Ghost. Joseph was told to take Mary as his wife, for the son to be named Jesus would save his people from their sins.

When Caesar Augustus decreed that all should be taxed, Joseph and Mary journeyed 80 miles to Bethlehem to register. This taxing was under God's hand, fulfilling prophecy that the Messiah would be born there. Upon arriving, they found Bethlehem overflowing with people—there was no room at the inn. Thus, Mary and Joseph were forced to find shelter in a smelly stable.

Then the child was born—the Son of God, an incredible, eternal Spirit clothed in human flesh. Nearby, shepherds watched their flocks when suddenly, an angel of the Lord appeared, radiating glory. The angel announced, "For unto you is born this day in the city of David a Savior, which is Christ the Lord." Angels filled the sky, singing, "Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will toward men."

The shepherds hurried to Bethlehem and found the child wrapped in swaddling clothes, lying in a manger, and worshipped Him.

Months later, the wise men arrived in Jerusalem and sought King Herod, asking, "Where is he that is born King of the Jews?" Herod's advisors told him, "In Bethlehem, your Highness." Fearful of losing his throne, Herod plotted to kill the newborn king.

The wise men followed the star to the very house where Jesus stayed. They worshipped the child and presented gifts of gold, frankincense, and myrrh, declaring their devotion and desire to worship Him.

God warned Joseph to flee to Egypt with Mary and Jesus, for Herod was furious and intended to kill the child. Herod then sent soldiers to Bethlehem to kill all male infants two years and under, fulfilling a dark prophecy. After Herod died, the family returned safely to Nazareth.

At 12 years old, Jesus amazed religious leaders with His wisdom, revealing knowledge others only dreamed of. While they questioned how a child could understand the laws of Moses, little did they know they spoke to God Himself.

Each year, Jesus saw a lamb sacrificed during Passover, a symbol of innocence and purity. Like the lamb, Jesus was pure and sinless. At 33, He would become the ultimate Passover lamb, fulfilling prophecy.

At age 30, Jesus began His earthly ministry, bringing light to the world. The Bible says, "In Him was life; and the life was the light of men." His light shone brightly, piercing through the darkness.

Jesus healed the sick, raised the dead, cast out demons, and preached forgiveness and repentance. He declared, "For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved." When asked why He came, Jesus replied, "For God so loved the world that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish but have everlasting life."

Jesus also confronted corrupt religious leaders, calling them "serpents" and "vipers," warning them of the consequences of their evil deeds. Hated and falsely accused, He was tried and sentenced to death by a rigged jury.

The Lamb of God willingly sacrificed Himself for the sins of humanity. One soldier proclaimed, "Truly this was the Son of God!" The Bible explains, "But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us." Jesus was buried, but three days later, He rose from the dead, conquering death and offering eternal life to all who believe.

Today, anyone can receive eternal life by trusting in Jesus Christ. One can pray, "Lord, I know I’m a sinner. I repent and believe You died for me. Please come into my heart and save me." The promise is clear: "For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved."

Those who receive Christ will live forever with Him in heaven. This is the greatest story ever told—the story of God's love and the salvation He offers to all through Jesus Christ.

Title: Guilty?
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
Once upon a time, a judge named Judge Rawlings left his car and decided to walk to work on a beautiful day. As he greeted some ladies on his way, he noticed two boys playing baseball nearby. One of the boys, Jimmy, swung the bat and hit the ball with a loud "whack." The ball nearly struck Judge Rawlings in the face, missing him by inches.

Jimmy chased after the ball, but he ran into a dangerous situation on the street when two truck drivers began arguing loudly, even calling each other idiots over the right address. Suddenly, Jimmy found himself in the middle of the street, and one truck driver shouted for him to get out of the way.

At that moment, Judge Rawlings acted quickly and tackled Jimmy to the ground just as a truck screeched to a halt, narrowly avoiding an accident. Judge Rawlings calmed Jimmy and reassured him.

Years later, Jimmy had grown into a cocky, arrogant young man. He kept boasting to his friends about the power he believed he had because of his past connection with Judge Rawlings. He even boasted that with a judge like Rawlings on his side, he could get away even with murder.

One day, Jimmy decided to test his "power" by trespassing on private property, ignoring warning signs, and confronting a sheriff. When the sheriff recognized the name Judge Rawlings, he gave Jimmy a warning instead of charging him. Jimmy felt unstoppable and believed the judge's friendship gave him immunity from consequences.

But five years later, Jimmy's arrogance caught up with him. He committed murder and was arrested. Despite the judge being his old friend, Judge Rawlings refused to let personal feelings interfere with the law. During the trial, the jury found Jimmy guilty of first-degree murder.

Jimmy pleaded with the judge to help him, reminding him of their friendship and how he once saved Jimmy's life. Judge Rawlings explained that he had been Jimmy's friend but now had to act as a judge and follow the law. He sentenced Jimmy to death by lethal injection and expressed hope that God would have mercy on his soul.

The story then reflects on a greater Judge: God Almighty, who will not allow sin into heaven. It explains that although all people are sinners guilty before God, He sent His Son, Jesus, to die for our sins. Jesus is the ultimate judge who will judge everyone at the end of time.

Despite judgment being certain, there is hope: God sent Jesus to wash away sins and save the world. The comic encourages readers to make an important decision—to accept Jesus as Lord and Savior or face judgment apart from Him.

The story concludes by urging readers to consider where they will spend eternity and to choose salvation through Jesus to avoid eternal condemnation. It offers a prayer to invite Jesus into one’s life as Lord and Savior.

Thus, the comic conveys a message about justice, friendship, and ultimately, spiritual judgment and salvation through Jesus Christ.

Title: Gun Slinger
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
In a quiet town, an old grandmother grew visibly disturbed and told her granddaughter that something evil was coming to town. She could feel it, saying with wide eyes and shaking hands, "I can FEEL IT!"

Then, the townsfolk caught sight of a menacing figure riding into town on horseback. The people whispered in fear, "Who’s THAT?" and "Did you see his face?" One man explained through gritted teeth, "I’ve KILLED people for looking at me like that!"

A dark stranger arrived inquiring about Bart Dawson. Told Bart was in his saloon down the street, the stranger ominously said, "I KNEW you would come."

Later, a rough-looking man was asked, "Who do you want me to kill?" He replied angrily about a man who had been a curse to the town—the preacher—who had ruined his thriving business by turning the town religious, causing prostitutes to marry, men to quit drinking and gambling, leaving him almost out of business. He vowed to be at the preacher’s church Sunday, saying, "By Monday, he’ll be in a CASKET!"

About forty miles away, a man showed a wanted poster to a crowd, asking if they had seen the outlaw known as Terrible Tom. Someone confirmed Tom was headed for Bottlesville.

On Sunday morning, the ominous man arrived at the church wearing guns and intimidation. A boy questioned why he wore guns to church. The man snapped, threatening to kill the boy if he didn’t shut up. Inside, the preacher greeted the stranger warmly, saying, "Welcome, stranger. God bless you!"

During the service, the preacher pointed to scripture, declaring the devil would not reclaim the town. "The Bible says, 'Resist the devil, and he will flee…' Devil! Get out of here!" Suddenly, the intimidating man felt strange.

Outside, the sheriff showed a photo of a cold-blooded killer to his men. The marshal confirmed the man was in church. Urgently, the sheriff ordered all deputies and shotguns to surround the church.

The preacher continued preaching love and forgiveness, quoting verses about God’s love for the world and how Jesus paid for all sins on the cross. He recounted the stories of King David, who was a murderer but repented, and Apostle Paul, who killed many Christians but was saved by God and used to write much of the New Testament.

He reminded the congregation about the criminal crucified next to Jesus, who was promised paradise, saying that no matter how bad a person is, Jesus can forgive and wants to enter their heart to change them.

The once-feared outlaw, Terrible Tom, tearfully confessed he didn’t believe God would forgive a sinner like him. The preacher assured him that God will forgive if he truly repents and asked Tom to pray with him.

One hour later, Tom and his gang were confronted in a dramatic showdown, ending with Tom’s arrest. The next day, Tom expressed gratitude to the preacher for telling him about Jesus’ love for even terrible men like himself. The preacher declared, "You’re not terrible anymore, Tom. You are now a child of God!"

That night, Tom prepared to meet God, ready to embrace eternal life. However, the next morning, as the lawmen escorted him, a gunshot echoed through the air. Terrible Tom was finally gone.

Minutes later, Tom stood before a shining figure in heaven, welcomed home with love—the fulfillment of John 5:24 about everlasting life.

Meanwhile, the marshal spoke to a reverend, asserting he was the most honest, law-abiding man in the territory and questioning if he was good enough for heaven, believing no one was.

Three hours later, the reverend encountered death and suffered eternal damnation, realizing too late he had neglected salvation.

In hell, a man cried out, protesting that he was a good man who upheld the law. The dark figure condemned him, saying he never received Christ as his Savior.

The story concludes with a powerful message: going to heaven isn’t about being good or bad, but about being saved or lost. No matter how bad someone has been, Jesus still wants to save them if they will let Him in.

Title: Happy Halloween
Subject: Halloween
Author: Chick
Responses:
Three friends stood in front of an eerie haunted house, one excitedly shouted, "There it is!" Another encouraged, "Let's do it!" As they ventured inside, one warned, "My mom said not to," but was quickly teased, "Come on, chicken!"

Inside, they encountered spider webs, eliciting disgust and fear. "Yuk... spider webs!" one said, while another confessed, "I DON'T like this!" Suddenly, a giant spider appeared, sending them screaming and shouting, "Run!"

Their fright continued as they faced various spooky sights. "I was NEVER so scared!" one said, while another pointed out, "Look... it's a witch!" One of them bravely claimed, "She doesn’t scare ME." The witch greeted them, "Happy Halloween!" but then scared them again with a loud yell.

Suddenly, the floor beneath them gave way, and they fell down with a loud "Thud!" Confused and scared, they looked around and saw terrifying creatures surrounding them. A devilish figure spoke ominously, "Welcome to the Abyss... You will be spending ETERNITY with us." The boys gasped in horror.

Panic set in as they decided to run. "No way! We’re outta here!" they shouted. But outside, danger lurked as they tried to escape, and one of the boys, Timmy, was almost hit by a car. Despite their efforts, Timmy was lost, and later they mourned, "I can’t believe Timmy’s gone," and "It could have been any of us."

Timmy found himself among terrifying figures in darkness, being told, "Welcome to the Abyss, Timmy. You’ll be here for ETERNITY because you died in your sins," quoting a Bible verse.

The next day, one of the boys reflected with sorrow, telling Timmy’s mother, "If I had listened to you, mom, Timmy wouldn’t be dead." She responded sadly, "Oh, how I wish he was, Bobby." She explained how she had cried upon hearing about Timmy's death, describing him as a beloved Sunday school student. However, Timmy had refused to repent and follow Christ, preferring to impress his worldly friends and quitting Sunday school.

She shared how she had told Timmy that Jesus was the only way to heaven, but he called her a fanatic, and it broke her heart.

Bobby was shocked that Timmy's decision could send him to hell forever and that being a 'good person' wasn’t enough. She explained that this was a lie from the devil, and that all humans are sinners deserving hell, but God loves everyone and made a way for anyone to reach heaven through Jesus Christ.

She told him that God sent His Son to die in their place, paying the punishment for their sins on the cross, offering eternal life to those who believe. They discussed how those who accept Jesus go to heaven, while those who reject Him go to hell. Bobby questioned if being good could get him to heaven, but she explained that he must accept Jesus.

When Bobby asked if there was a second chance, she said, "No, once you die, it’s settled forever." She urged Bobby to turn from his sins and give his life to Jesus.

Bobby prayed, "Lord Jesus, I believe You died on the cross for me. I’m sorry for my sins and I ask You to forgive me. Please come into my heart and save me right now." Feeling safe and sure, Bobby said, "I KNOW I’ll go to heaven when I die. I’ll never forget THIS Halloween."

The story closed with a call to repentance: be truly sorry for sins and invite Jesus into your heart. It warned not to make the same mistake Timmy made, emphasizing that the choice is yours.

Title: Happy Hour
Subject: Drugs/Alcohol
Author: Chick
Responses:
Jerry was frantically trying to escape through a window when Alice confronted him, telling him that the money he was trying to take was all they had. Jerry pushed her away and told her to get out of his way. Alice was determined, insisting Jerry would spend the money over her dead body, but he forcefully told her to let go of him. Alice accused Jerry of ruining their family and demanded the money back, but he refused to give it to her as they struggled violently.

A loud crash and shouts filled the house. Jerry fell to the floor as Alice yelled for help. Their children, watching from outside, asked if Jerry was hurting their mother. As Jerry lay injured on the floor, Alice called for help. Later, at a doctor's office, Jerry was asked if he wanted the usual treatment, and he admitted he had had a bad morning.

Outside, Janice asked if her mother was going to die, but was told no one knew. She was asked if she could find her father. Janice went searching for Jerry and learned he had already visited two clubs, Diablo's Den and The Cork, during happy hour. Janice pleaded aloud for help in finding her daddy but hated the places he frequented.

When she finally found Jerry at the bar, she begged him to come home because her mother was sick, but the men at the bar told her to leave. Jerry, needing another drink, told Janice to stay out of it. Janice explained to Mrs. Jenkins, the neighbor, that Jerry was drunk all the time and wouldn't come home. Mrs. Jenkins suggested they go to the hospital to see how Alice was.

At the hospital, doctors urged them to try again, though they feared it was too late. Alice passed away, and the somber news was delivered to the children by Mrs. Jenkins. Janice tearfully said that she thought her mama had died. Mrs. Jenkins gently explained that their mother had gone to heaven and was not killed by Jerry but had a bad heart.

At Alice's funeral, Janice mourned that her daddy wasn't there when she needed him and expressed hatred towards him. Aunt Mary gave Janice twenty dollars to give to Jerry for food, but warned that Jerry would spend it on alcohol since he was an alcoholic. Janice tried to convince Jerry to buy food, and he promised he would, assuring her not to worry.

As night fell, Bobby asked Janice why Jerry wasn't home and if he was still buying food for them. Janice somberly replied that he was getting drunk. When Jerry returned, Janice accused him of lying about buying groceries. Jerry, feeling sick, told Janice to go to bed. Janice, fiercely standing up to him, crashed a bottle on the floor to "fix him." Jerry's behavior worsened, causing Janice and Bobby to fear him. They wished their daddy had died instead of their mama.

Jerry apologized to his children, begging for their forgiveness and help, admitting he couldn't control his drinking. But the children refused to forgive him, stating they hated him.

Mrs. Jenkins kindly took the children to church and agreed to drive them again at night. At church, Janice offered forgiveness to Jerry, quoting Jesus's teachings and asked if he would attend church with them. Jerry agreed, reluctantly saying he would go.

The story then shifted to a message about how many people turn to drugs or alcohol when facing hardships, but only Jesus can provide true rest and freedom from burdens. The Bible verses encouraged those struggling to come to Jesus for help. Janice witnessed her father giving his heart to Jesus, and they embraced a new beginning.

Three years later, Jerry joyfully declared to Janice that this new life was his real "happy hour," having found happiness through faith and healing.

Title: Hard Times
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Carter
Responses:
During a fierce storm on a gloomy, rainy night, a man suffering from hiccups stumbled out of a small cabin, holding a large mug. His hiccups were persistent as he ventured into the rain with the mug, attempting to catch raindrops. People hurried by under umbrellas, but the man continued alone, hoping the rain would help stop his hiccups.

As the man stood in the pouring rain, someone approached and dropped a shiny penny into his mug. Startled and annoyed, the man swore and dropped the mug, spilling the penny. Taking the mug, the person picked up a wooden stick from a table nearby and threateningly raised it. The man, frightened, began to run through the rain, chased by the person wielding the stick.

In his rush to escape, the man stumbled, and the attacker stopped beside him. The man collapsed, and the aggressive figure grabbed him, dragging him back to the cabin. The man resisted and was thrown violently inside the cabin, hitting the floor painfully. The thunder crashed loudly, illuminating the dark storm outside.

Alone again, the man, drenched and exhausted, crawled away from the cabin, leaving the mug behind. He wandered through the rain, drifting aimlessly until he collapsed to the wet ground, weak and overwhelmed. Nearby, people’s feet passed him by indifferently, and a stray cat sat on a trash can watching the scene.

The man found refuge in an empty box, curling up to sleep among the trash, surrounded by discarded bottles and debris. Near him, a sign blew in the wind reading, "SOMEBODY LOVES YOU." The man noticed the sign, but it seemed strange and confusing in his dark situation. A curious young girl approached, holding another sign and smiled, but the man didn’t understand.

Suddenly, a voice called out, "JESUS LOVES YOU!" The man held the sign closer and, despite his weariness, whispered to himself, "Jesus loves me." Tears filled his eyes as hope stirred faintly in his heart.

With renewed spirit, the man hugged the sign and imagined a comforting angelic presence enveloping him with love. The scene shifted to a bright, peaceful image of the man as an angel, symbolizing salvation and care.

Lastly, a message appeared, "AND THE LORD JESUS LOVES YOU TOO!" citing John 3:16, reminding that God's love is everlasting and anyone who believes in Him will have eternal life.

This powerful story of despair, kindness, and faith revealed that even in the darkest moments, love and hope can reach those who seem lost and forgotten.

Title: Heart Trouble
Subject: Ten Commandments
Author: Chick
Responses:
A man visited his doctor, who told him he had a bad ticker — a heart problem. The man anxiously asked if the doctor could fix it. The doctor replied that it should be fixable unless there were complications. When the man asked if he could die, the doctor told him not right away, but eventually, everyone dies.

Curious, the man asked if he was born with this heart problem. The doctor explained that everybody is born with a bad heart problem, and it wasn’t just about physical tissue, blood, and nerves. There were ugly things deep inside the heart that couldn’t be seen by human eyes, but God knew about them.

The doctor said that the Lord gives a very real picture of what’s inside the human heart. The man asked what part of the heart the doctor was talking about, and the doctor said it was the "fleshy" part—the parts that slip out from time to time and are really nasty. These things are offensive to God, and the man needed to do something about it.

The doctor then revealed that inside every heart is adultery, causing people to cheat on their spouses and destroy families and homes. The man gulped, thinking about his wife's best friend, Judy, and admitted this was why he wanted Judy every time he saw her.

Next, the doctor said murder was also hatched in the heart, asking if the man ever wanted to kill someone — like his boss or mother-in-law. This shocked the man. Then the doctor mentioned lying, and the man admitted to telling a few “little white lies.” Theft was also inside the heart, as taking things without asking was common. The doctor explained this fills prisons.

The conversation moved to blasphemy — insulting God by saying Jesus is not God — and the man asked if “Jesus” was a swear word. The doctor insisted Jesus is God Almighty and the only way to get into heaven.

The doctor continued, saying hearts also hold evil thoughts. The man got defensive, blaming "sickos" out there and saying they should be slaughtered. The doctor asked if the man expected to get into heaven with a heart like that.

The doctor told the man that God is holy and won't allow wickedness into heaven. He asked if the man knew what God says about his heart. The man wanted to know, and the doctor quoted Jeremiah: the heart is deceitful above all things and desperately wicked.

The man was horrified and asked how hearts got that way. The doctor explained that everything changed when Adam and Eve disobeyed God, especially their hearts, and this problem passed down to everyone. The man felt hopeless, believing no one could get into heaven.

The doctor offered a secret: God doesn’t want anyone to perish or go to hell, but humans can’t clean their hearts by themselves. The man said he needed a new heart.

The doctor said that he could get one, but it came at a cost — the life of the Lord Jesus. Jesus came from heaven, took on human flesh with a sinless heart, and was sacrificed to wash away sins by shedding His blood. He died and was buried, and three days later, He rose from the dead — paying the price for a new heart.

The man asked if he needed surgery to get a new heart. The doctor said no, he needed Jesus. He explained that by believing Jesus died for his sins, admitting he was a sinner, and accepting Jesus as Lord and Savior, a miracle would happen: Jesus would come into his heart and make him a new person — born again.

The man asked what would happen if he didn’t accept this. The doctor warned that at death, he would be taken to hell and die in his sins.

The man doubted and said he liked his lifestyle and would wait until he was old. The doctor asked what if his heart stopped tonight. The man was scared and realized he was a "dead duck" without Jesus.

The doctor assured him that God was dealing with him right now and warned that if he rejected God today, he might never get another chance. The man admitted he was ready but had never prayed before and asked what to do.

The doctor told him to talk to God in his own words. The man prayed, asking God to forgive him and clean his dirty heart. Suddenly, he felt different.

The man joyfully told the doctor that even if his X-rays hadn't changed, he felt clean — forgiven — because only Jesus Christ can do that.

The story ended by reminding readers that the choice between heaven and hell is theirs, and to believe in Jesus Christ and be saved.

Title: Help
Subject: Your Soul
Author: Carter
Responses:
Once upon a time, in the old days, people would often ask, "How is it with your soul?" One curious person once asked, "What's a soul? Do I even have one?" The answer was simple and certain: everyone has a soul because we're all born with one inside us.

But what does a soul look like? Many wondered if science had ever seen one. The truth was that a soul was invisible—so invisible that science ignored it as if it were a joke. However, God could see the soul clearly.

The soul is the true self, the real you. While the body will eventually die and return to dust, the soul lives on forever. Once the body is gone, where do you think the soul will go? Some might think this is about scary concepts like God, heaven, or hell, but it’s really about the matter of sin.

God gave Moses the Ten Commandments to show how He wanted people to live. However, many had never heard of these commandments. Worse, some politicians removed the Bible from schools and even got rid of the Ten Commandments because they found them offensive. They turned against God and His words, which led to the doom of many souls.

Curious to know the commandments, someone asked to hear them despite warnings that this topic was politically incorrect. The commandments were:

1. Thou shalt have no other gods before me.  
2. Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image (an idol).  
3. Thou shalt not take the name of the LORD thy God in vain.  
4. Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy.  
5. Honour thy father and thy mother.  
6. Thou shalt not kill.  
7. Thou shalt not commit adultery.  
8. Thou shalt not steal.  
9. Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbour.  
10. Thou shalt not covet.

Everyone was asked if they had ever broken any of these laws. Many admitted they had, but some believed they were still good people at heart. Nonetheless, mistakes were made.

The lesson was clear: God wouldn’t allow sin in heaven no matter what people thought. When questioned, many admitted to lying—sometimes just little white lies—or stealing, or using God's name as a swear word. Others confessed they didn't respect their parents or had lustful thoughts.

Most believed they were just normal people who would go to heaven, but when asked to see their soul, they were shocked. Their soul was full of sins like adultery, lies, hatred, thievery, cursing, and using God's name in vain. The questions arose, would God allow that mess into heaven? The answer was no. Their souls needed saving.

Some were scared and realized their souls would stink up heaven. They asked if the sins could be wiped away before they died. The answer was yes. God did not want any soul to perish and offered a way to be saved.

A special plan was made to cleanse souls. Nothing could wash away sins except a very special blood, the blood of Jesus Christ. God is three persons—Father, Son (Jesus Christ), and the Holy Ghost—who together make up the one true God.

Jesus Christ created the universe and sits on His throne in heaven. Knowing that humans could do nothing to erase sin, God the Son left heaven to be born as a baby. He came on a mission to be a human sacrifice and die for the sins of the world.

Before His death, Jesus healed the blind, deaf, lepers, and even raised the dead to prove He was God. After saying, "I am the way, the truth, and the life," He was crucified, beaten, and cursed. His holy blood was shed to wash away the filth clinging to souls.

Jesus died but rose again three days later, completing His mission. Believing in this, praying for forgiveness, and inviting Jesus into the heart saves a person’s soul. Then, God’s blood cleanses away sins forever, and the soul becomes as white as snow, ready for heaven.

The body becomes a temple of God, filled with Jesus’ presence. Though millions worldwide perish in sin every day, Jesus commands His followers to spread the gospel to warn people.

Those with souls covered in sin can pray: "Lord Jesus, I'm a sinner, but I believe You died for me. Please forgive my sins, come into my heart, and save me." By believing and accepting Jesus, a soul is saved from hell and given eternal life.

The choice of heaven or hell is yours alone. To choose Jesus is to choose life and forgiveness. So, will you decide to save your soul today?

Title: Here Comes The Judge
Subject: Judgment Day
Author: Chick
Responses:
In a certain city, there lived a highly respected judge named Shelton Barnstead. His reputation was spotless, and he was even being considered for the state supreme court. Shelton was honorable and wealthy; his late wife had left him a mansion and a fortune. He generously gave to charity and was loved by all.

However, Shelton had a dark side unknown to most. One evening, his home was troubled by chaos. His wife and children, returning home, were met with a horrifying scene. The children watched helplessly as Lance Clawson, Kyle Keefer’s best friend, brutally attacked their father with a knife. Amidst the struggle, Mrs. Keefer had tried to intervene to save Shelton, but in a tragic turn, Shelton was killed.

Lance Clawson confessed to the murder over the phone, but Shelton’s wife and children had caught him by surprise. Mrs. Keefer revealed that her husband was a private investigator gathering evidence, though she never saw the evidence herself because her husband said it was too dangerous.

Despite this, everything went terribly wrong. Police planted false evidence at Mrs. Keefer’s house and framed her for possession of illegal drugs. She was arrested, separated from her children, and faced horrendous injustice. At the same time, Shelton’s children accused Lance of murder, but the official story blamed Kyle Keefer’s wife for the crime.

Two weeks later, in the criminal court presided over by the honorable Shelton Barnstead, shocking corrupt practices were revealed. The judge sentenced the accused to only 40 years instead of death, inciting outrage from those seeking justice.

Later, Lance died mysteriously in his cell, and Mrs. Keefer was confined to a mental hospital, undergoing shock treatments. In the shadows, the true villain—Shelton himself—was pulling strings and hiding the truth. After a reporter named Maxine West got him drunk and he revealed information, the governor gave orders to silence her at all costs.

A terrible explosion at a popular café severely injured Judge Shelton Barnstead but did not kill him. Two weeks later, his loyal house servant Conrad visited him in the hospital and asked Shelton to listen to the truth he had kept hidden for 23 years.

Conrad spoke about Jesus Christ, the Lord and final Judge who would stand over Shelton after death. Despite Shelton’s lifelong disdain and unbelief, Conrad explained that Jesus had come 2,000 years ago to save sinners by dying in their place and rising again. He warned Shelton that unless he repented and accepted Jesus as Savior, his fate would be sealed in judgment.

Conrad urged Shelton to understand that God’s judgment awaits everyone after death and that terrible times were coming on earth, including the rise of an antichrist and global calamities. Jesus would return someday to defeat evil and establish peace, offering hope to those who trust Him.

Shelton was told he must choose—either accept Jesus and be forgiven or reject Him and face eternal consequences. Conrad assured him that his soul was no longer on the servant's hands; now the judgment was Shelton's to face.

As the doctor prepared to inject Shelton with a fatal dose, Shelton’s spirit was carried away. His muffled screams remained unheard.

The story ends with a warning: just as Judge Shelton’s stubbornness and pride cost him his soul, everyone must decide whether Jesus Christ will be their dearest friend or deadliest enemy. The choice determines where one’s soul will spend eternity. Don’t make the same mistake Shelton Barnstead did. Believe in Jesus Christ and be saved.

Title: Here He Comes!
Subject: End Time Prophecy
Author: Chick
Responses:
In a dramatic and urgent conversation inside a car, Helen tells Damien that there is something really important he should know. As Damien starts to ask what it is, he is abruptly distracted by a sudden, terrifying event. Helen screams that someone has disappeared, followed by a frantic search for Bob, who is also missing. The chaos escalates as the car spins out of control on the road with screeching tires. Outside, a "lost dog" poster with a reward for a dog named Fang is noticed amid the commotion, and the chaos worsens as there is shouting and uncontrolled panic.

Damien then wakes up in distress, realizing it was all a terrible nightmare. His friend checks on him, relieved to find him okay after hearing his cries for help. Damien explains that in his nightmare, he and Helen had disappeared in "the rapture," but he was left behind, which shook him deeply. The narrator then explains the biblical context of the rapture, quoting scriptures that describe Christ's return and the hope it offers.

The story transitions to a theological explanation: When Damien accepted Jesus as his Savior, he was saved from God's wrath, which is actually meant for an unbelieving world. God’s vengeance will not be against believers, but against others, as referenced in Romans. Jesus came from heaven, shedding His blood to wash away sins, then rose after three days, supported by scripture John 3:16.

Jesus will rapture His church before a seven-year Tribulation begins, though after the rapture, those left behind who remain faithful will face severe persecution. The biblical Tribulation period is described as the last days, featuring the rise of the Antichrist. Damien asks if this is true, and his friend confirms it, showing some disbelief.

Jesus, when asked about the end of the world, predicted terrible trouble and suffering unlike anything previously experienced. The comic then depicts biblical prophecies: four horsemen representing wars, famine, and death arrive as the Tribulation starts.

Next, the narrative reveals that prophecies in Ezekiel indicate Russia, Germany, and a Muslim world attack Israel, only to be miraculously defeated by God in a devastating World War III. This culminates in the destruction of the Muslim Dome of the Rock mosque, allowing Jews to rebuild their holy temple in Jerusalem.

The pope and Jesuit general closely watch these events from Rome, eager to take control. A deceitful seven-year peace treaty with Israel is signed, bringing false security to Israel. That same period sees the emergence of a great evil entity, the Great Whore, who controls every nation during the Tribulation.

All world faiths unify into one massive world religion, with the pope declared as its spiritual leader. Then Satan enters the Beast, the political leader, giving him tremendous power. The Beast desecrates the rebuilt temple by placing an image of himself in the Holy of Holies and demanding worship, betraying the people’s trust.

The False Prophet enforces worship of the Beast by mandating everyone to receive a mark, without which they cannot buy or sell. Those who refuse, like in Damien’s dream, are executed mercilessly. These faithful ones suffer beheading for their witness to Jesus.

As God's patience ends, His wrath descends upon the earth. A series of plagues follow: a third of the earth is set on fire, the sun scorches many, waters become undrinkable, and famine, death, and wild beasts run rampant. Despite these horrors, most continue to refuse to repent.

The Beast faces an uprising when ten leaders rebel and destroy the Vatican by fire, yet God allows the Beast to escape to Jerusalem. The Beast commands armies from around the world, especially from the East, preparing for war against Israel.

In a climactic moment foretold by John, Jesus returns as the Jewish Messiah riding a white horse and waging righteous war. His eyes blaze with fire, and He is accompanied by heavenly armies. Jesus attacks at Armageddon, defeating the Beast, the False Prophet, and all their forces, casting them into eternal fire.

Israel is saved by their Messiah, who will then reign over the entire world from Jerusalem for a thousand years, rebuilding the damaged world into a place of incredible beauty. Subsequently, the devil is judged and cast into the lake of fire, where he will be tormented forever.

Following the judgment of the devil, those who died without accepting Jesus face judgment at the great white throne. Only those whose names are found in the Book of Life will be saved; others face eternal punishment.

Damien is told this is precisely what is going to happen, emphasizing the urgent need to preach the gospel. Bob is reminded that billions face eternal damnation and must be warned. The comic ends with a solemn warning that rejecting Jesus and missing the rapture means likely receiving the mark of the Beast and eternal torment. It is no joke—this may be the reader's last chance, with a final call to believe in Jesus Christ for salvation.

Title: Here, Kitty Kitty!
Subject: Halloween
Author: Chick
Responses:
Three friends gather to prepare for an important event, checking if they have everything needed. One has candles, another has brought chalk, and the third proudly carries a book of spells. They believe they are all set, but a fourth child interrupts, declaring they forgot the most important part: a black cat and a knife. The girl protests, saying the cat is her beloved pet, Fluffy, but the other insists they need it for their spell. Torn between her love for Fluffy and wanting the spell to work, the girl is pressured to agree. The cat is kept in a cage until Halloween night.

At school, the girl, Betsy, is caught crying by a classmate. Later, her teacher Miss Johnson asks Betsy to stay after class. Miss Johnson gently inquires why Betsy is upset. Through their conversation, Betsy reveals that her brother and some boys plan to kill her cat because they intend to cast a spell on Halloween night. Surprised, Miss Johnson asks why they would do such a thing. Betsy explains their belief in the spell.

Miss Johnson then asks who they're going to cast a spell on, and Betsy points at her teacher. Miss Johnson responds that spells don’t work on her. Curious, Betsy asks why not. Miss Johnson explains that Jesus protects her because He loves her—she is God's Son, who made the universe. She tells Betsy that everyone does wrong things called sins, and God won’t allow sin into heaven.

Betsy wonders if God would let her in just as she is, but Miss Johnson explains that everyone needs to be made clean first. Betsy imagines soap and water, but Miss Johnson says God has a much better way. She tells how God loved Betsy and everyone so much that He sent His Son, Jesus, to become human and teach love and forgiveness—even to Betsy’s mean brother.

Miss Johnson explains that God must punish sins, but Jesus took the punishment upon Himself. She shares that Jesus died for their sins, was buried, but three days later, a miracle happened—Jesus rose from the dead. He shed His blood to wash away sins so people could go to heaven.

Miss Johnson asks if Betsy wants to go to heaven, and Betsy eagerly says yes. Miss Johnson explains that Jesus is the only way to heaven and asks if Betsy wants to pray to accept Him. Betsy prays, asking Jesus to forgive her sins and take her to heaven.

Feeling clean and forgiven, Betsy tells Miss Johnson she’s going to heaven. Later, Miss Johnson asks where they plan to cast the spell, and Betsy says in her backyard when the moon is up. When asked why, Betsy says they want better grades.

On Halloween night, Betsy finds Fluffy’s cage empty and the cat missing. She confronts her brother, who reveals he took Fluffy because he thought she’d back out. Betsy begs him to save Fluffy, but he shows no mercy. The boys get ready to carry out their plan, but suddenly Miss Johnson arrives, shining a flashlight and demanding they stop.

Miss Johnson takes Fluffy and scolds Betsy for doing spells and tells her she doesn’t need spells to get good grades. The boys apologize, and Betsy and Miss Johnson realize that both Betsy and Fluffy were saved that Halloween.

Title: Hi There!
Subject: Hell
Author: Carter
Responses:
Charlie Conners was a man who often clashed with his coworkers about religion, steadfastly refusing to believe in heaven or hell. Whenever one of them teased him about going to hell, Charlie bluntly told them to go to hell themselves. He said he didn’t want to go to heaven; instead, he wanted to be where all his buddies were. His friends tried to explain that churches only used the idea of hell as a scare tactic, with one mentioning that his sister’s group said hell was just a grave. Another joked that the old man upstairs (God) wouldn’t put anyone in hell because he was dead.

Charlie believed in a naturalistic origin of life, saying humans came from monkeys and even from the ocean, which he called our mother. He stressed that when you’re dead, you’re truly dead. Heaven and hell, he said, were just concepts on earth, and he was going through "hell" with his wife, complaining about small irritations like a peanut butter sandwich she made even though she knew he hated peanut butter.

Charlie dismissed the preachers as phonies who only yelled for money and thought the Bible was written by old Jews. He scoffed at the idea of sin and found the notion of a single way to heaven absurd, especially since there were so many religions—Buddhists, Muslims, and many others who never heard of Jesus. He considered the Bible contradictory and refused to waste his time on it.

One day, as he argued with his friends, a grim figure in a cloak interrupted, saying they had an appointment with Charlie. Suddenly, a strong wind knocked Charlie down, and he fell hard to the ground. His friends panicked, calling for an ambulance and questioning if he was alive. But Charlie was clearly in trouble, gasping and crying for help, burning mysteriously.

Eventually, Charlie died, and his friends were left wondering what to tell his wife about what happened. At his funeral, people mourned and expressed disbelief at his sudden death. One of his friends tried to find comfort by saying that Charlie’s troubles were over now, but another challenged this, prompting a closer look.

In the afterlife, Charlie found himself in a place that was definitely not heaven. Confused and terrified, he asked why he was there, only to be told it was hell and that he had died in his sins. Shocked, Charlie gasped at the news. He asked if he could return to warn his buddies about this dreadful place, but he was told that even if he went back to the living, no one would believe him because they trusted their own versions of God's word, the Bible, but would reject his warning.

Desperate and anguished, Charlie wondered if he would be alone forever, recalling something his grandmother said about the lost being cast into the lake of fire. He demanded to know when that would happen.

An angel explained that after Jesus returned and ruled on Earth for a thousand years, all who died in their sins, including Charlie and others, would be judged. Charlie was dismissive at first, saying he didn’t care about sin. The angel explained that by accepting Jesus as Savior and believing in his sacrifice, a person’s sins would be washed away.

Charlie scoffed at the idea, citing the many religions and the Bible’s empty tomb, questioning if Jesus was really the way. The angel told him there was no one righteous who sought after God except through Jesus.

A millennium later, the time came for Charlie’s judgment. God, identified as Jesus Christ, confronted Charlie. Jesus said that he loved Charlie so much that he left heaven, endured suffering, death, and was resurrected for Charlie’s sake. Charlie was reminded that on April 7, 1992, he had been told Jesus was the only way to heaven, but he had laughed it off.

Jesus expressed sadness that Charlie chose his friends’ ways over God. Now, Charlie was without excuse. God had to judge him, and Charlie was condemned to everlasting fire, separated from God.

In agony, Charlie admitted he was guilty and a fool for wasting his life trying to please friends who didn’t care. He was now to face the consequences of his rejection.

The story closes with a warning to readers that many will end up like Charlie Conners because they fear what others might say. It reminds readers that friends can be unreliable, but Jesus will never leave or forsake them. This was possibly the reader’s last chance to accept Jesus as their Savior.

The comic includes scripture references reinforcing the Christian message of salvation through Jesus Christ and the reality of judgment.

Title: Hit!, The
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
Once, Tony Stiletto, a notorious mobster, approached a house with a bottle of alcohol in one hand and a weapon in the other, declaring, "Here’s a present from Tony Stiletto." That night, his wife, Rose, woke her husband up, alarmed by a strange sound. Before long, a massive explosion shattered the house — it was a bomb.

The police arrived on the scene, and one officer confirmed it was definitely a bomb. They found the tragic remains of Rose’s husband and their two children. The captain expressed his condolences to Rose, informing her that her entire family was gone. Filled with grief and fury, Rose swore she would get revenge, vowing, "I know the devil who’s responsible for this. I swear upon the souls of my children... I WILL get revenge!"

Fast forward fifteen years. In a special news report, Tony Stiletto was shot down but survived and was now in critical condition at St. Mary’s hospital. His four bodyguards died at the scene. The police chief ordered 24-hour protection for Tony, allowing only his priest, doctor, and nurses into his room.

Two days later, in his hospital bed, Tony gasped when Rose appeared. She declared, "I’m Rose Lucci. You killed my husband and my two precious boys." She accused him of destroying her life and said she had mourned for her family every day for fifteen years. Now, she intended to take her chance at revenge.

With a syringe in hand, Rose prepared to end Tony's life. But Tony pleaded, "NO! Stop! Please!... Don’t kill me!!" Just then, a policeman entered and said, "I would, but I can’t! Despite all the evil things you’ve done to me... God has ordered me to love and forgive you."

Tony was surprised. The officer began to share how God changed his life. He had once hated his life, walking the streets in the rain, but a little lady led him to a room full of singing people. They told him all sins could be forgiven, and he was amazed.

They taught him that Jesus died for his sins on the cross, asking God to forgive even those who crucified Him. Those words transformed the officer’s life, and he fell to his knees, inviting Christ to save him.

Tony, weak and broken, said he didn't want to die and asked the officer to pray for him. Rose joined the prayer, laying her hands on Tony’s chest and asking for healing.

Two days later, doctors proclaimed it miraculous—there was no damage to Tony's lungs. A nurse asked if they should send the priest in, but Tony refused, insisting on seeing Rose instead.

Tony asked Rose how to receive what she had. She explained it was simple. "You can know right now that you are going to heaven," she said, quoting scripture. She emphasized that faith in Christ alone, not good works or churches, is the only way to heaven.

Later, Tony prayed, confessing, "Lord Jesus, I’ve been so evil... but now I trust You as my Saviour. Thank you for saving me from going to hell." Rose smiled and guided Tony on what God wanted him to do next, starting with cleaning up the mess he had made.

Six weeks later, Tony surprised everyone. He met with his old mob associates and told them he intended to pay them back generously for their past services. Declaring himself done with his old life, Tony announced an offer they couldn’t refuse: accept Jesus Christ and go to heaven, or reject Him and suffer eternal damnation.

The mobsters were shocked. One angrily exclaimed, "Did you hear what he did for his prostitutes?" Tony had sent them all to college.

At the police commissioner’s office, Tony read a passage from the Bible, John 3:16, about God’s love and eternal life through belief in Jesus.

Tony shared a powerful message: Jesus loves you so much He laid down His life for you and wants you to reign with Him in Heaven, offering riches and power beyond imagination. God desires that no one end up in hell but invites everyone to accept Jesus as their Savior today. "It’s an offer you can’t refuse!" he declared.

And thus, a story of vengeance turned into redemption, showing the power of forgiveness, faith, and transformation.

Title: Holocaust
Subject: Israel
Author: Carter
Responses:
In the bustling setting of a public meeting in the USA, a heated confrontation erupts as members of the Jewish Defense League vocally oppose a group displaying signs with swastikas and Nazi symbols. The crowd angrily shouts at them to leave, expressing their disdain for the Nazi presence. Among the spectators are Bob and Ruth, who notice an elderly man named Mr. Weiss becoming visibly distressed by the scene.

Concerned, Bob and Ruth urge Mr. Weiss to leave, explaining that he was once imprisoned in Nazi concentration camps and suggesting they go home. Mr. Weiss resists, compelled to remain as the taunts and insults escalate, including the Nazi followers calling the crowd "filthy Christian swine." Bob and Ruth worry that Mr. Weiss is endangering himself, but he insists on staying to bear witness.

Once home, Mr. Weiss solemnly recounts the horrors he experienced in the Holocaust, where his family was murdered in gas chambers and cremated. He laments the ongoing denial of these atrocities. Bob encourages him to speak out, acknowledging that the truth about World War II has long been suppressed. Mr. Weiss reveals that he was forced to wear the yellow star and lived through the camps, wearing the signs of persecution.

Curious, Bob asks why Mr. Weiss has never shared these stories before. Mr. Weiss responds that the Nazis brought back a terrifying form of persecution, something like a new Inquisition, but rooted in modern times in the United States. Ruth is shocked and asks if an Inquisition could really exist today.
