Mr. Weiss explains that the Vatican orchestrated this, updating old methods using the Gestapo under Nazi uniforms during the war, and continuing secret activities now under different guises.

Bob listens as Mr. Weiss details how Hitler, though often seen as an enemy of the Jews, was never excommunicated by the Catholic Church for his crimes and was even considered a hero by the Vatican. Historical evidence shows that the Church gave Hitler the authority to carry out actions under the guise of purging heretics, including Jews and others.

The conversation shifts to the Council of Trent, convened in 1545 by Pope Paul III, to establish strict Catholic laws aimed at opposing Protestantism. These laws defined who was considered a heretic, and historically, this resulted in the slaughter of many labeled as such. Even in modern times, Pope John XXIII acknowledged and accepted the decrees of the Council.

Bob and Ruth are surprised to learn that Catholic influence is strong in the United States today, with millions of Catholics and significant control over media, politics, and immigration policy. This influence is seen as part of a larger plan to convert America to Catholicism and suppress Protestant and non-Catholic opposition.

Despite reassurances that the Vatican had reformed after Vatican II, Mr. Weiss insists that the same oppressive system remains, merely repackaged under new names. He points to the political power of the Vatican and its behind-the-scenes control, which many Americans are unaware of due to media manipulation and political pressure.

As their discussion deepens, Bob wonders about how to resist this influence. Mr. Weiss points to history, faith, and the unwavering truth of Christianity outside the Catholic system. He explains how true Christians reject the false teachings and harmful actions of the Roman Catholic institution, which he describes as the "Whore of Revelation," destined for destruction according to biblical prophecy.

Moved by these revelations, Bob expresses doubts about his faith and shares his experiences. Mr. Weiss reassures him, explaining that true salvation comes from repentance and belief in Jesus Christ, not from rituals or institutions. Over the course of their conversation, Bob comes to realize that Jesus is the Messiah, the Son of the living God, and gains peace through this truth.

Ten minutes later, Bob joyfully proclaims his new faith, ready to share the truth with others. Mr. Weiss recognizes that if this message spreads widely, it could undermine the spiritual hold of the Inquisition, potentially stopping this cycle of oppression.

The story ends on a hopeful note, emphasizing the power of faith and truth to overcome historical and ongoing persecution by religious and political institutions cloaked under layers of authority and secrecy.

Title: Holy Joe
Subject: Military
Author: Chick
Responses:
The story begins in a military barracks, where one soldier is telling another to knock it off and turn out the lights. Suddenly, a man exclaims, "Whaaa the—I'm seeing things!! Get the Sarge—quick!" The sergeant arrives and wonders what is going on. Another soldier reveals they're dealing with a man known as "Holy Joe."

The soldiers describe Holy Joe as a religious fanatic unlike any they've seen before. They mention how they know how to "crack" him, and one moment later, they mockingly douse him with a shower of blessings, which involves tossing boots at him.

The next morning, the sergeant is informed that Holy Joe has shined the shoes they threw at him. Frustrated, the sergeant insists to put Holy Joe in the "K.P." (kitchen patrol) for one week, saying he's begging for trouble.

Four days later in the mess hall, the sergeant complains about Holy Joe’s strange behavior as the harder he works, the crazier he seems. Some soldiers discuss taking Holy Joe to the head shrinker (a mental health professional) and note that nothing has stopped his preaching so far. One soldier mentions how he sounds like his mother, who is also a Christian.

Later, Holy Joe spends time with the head shrinker and shares his testimony about finding peace of mind and forgiveness through Christ. The mental health professional, however, stops him, asserting that it’s his job to analyze, not Holy Joe’s.

The sergeant debates whether to put Holy Joe in the "booby hatch" (a psychiatric ward), but a higher officer says Holy Joe is harmless and experiencing a religious neurosis. The sergeant sarcastically wonders what if Holy Joe’s message is true, burping while drinking beer.

During maneuvers, a soldier named Henderson is shocked to learn his life is being recorded for judgment. The sergeant explains that on Judgment Day, every thought and word will be accounted for. Henderson is disturbed by the message and expresses doubt about God and religion.

Months later, the soldiers completed their maneuvers. Some express concern that Holy Joe hasn't changed at all. Henderson vents that he doesn’t need Christ or Holy Joe’s preaching anymore. Holy Joe replies with words from the Bible, asserting he is the way, the truth, and the life.

The situation escalates as a soldier warns Henderson to stop his religious fervor, or he'll be dead. The sergeant calls for a volunteer for a dangerous mission, and Holy Joe steps up. Despite Henderson's protests, the sergeant sends Holy Joe out, claiming he's just giving him a shove in the right direction. Holy Joe prays for the sergeant.

The following day, a soldier reports that Holy Joe has been shot. Observing Holy Joe’s peaceful expression, some soldiers are unsettled, but others want to leave the warzone immediately. Henderson, caught in combat, cries out to God for salvation, inspired by Holy Joe’s faith.

Sergeant is told they are surrounded and urges everyone to run. The scene shows soldiers running, some falling. A few lie dead in the jungle.

Suddenly, the dead soldiers, including Holy Joe and Henderson, arise, awakening from death. An angel tells them it’s time for their judgment. Henderson defends his life, saying he lived well and never hurt anyone, but the angel clarifies judgment comes after death.

Henderson stands before his creator, and his entire life is replayed like a movie. He recalls rejecting Holy Joe’s message and now understands he is lost without hope.

A question arises if Henderson’s name appears in the Book of Life. The answer is no, and it’s explained that those not found in the book are cast into the Lake of Fire.

Henderson pleads with God, acknowledging he is a sinner and asking to be saved like Holy Joe was. He begs, "Oh God, save me for Christ’s sake!" The angel commands Henderson to enter the joy of the Lord, quoting scripture about those who have not seen or heard but are prepared to love Him.

Through faith, Henderson puts his name in the Book of Life and is shown God’s grace.

The story ends with a reminder from scripture about salvation being by grace through faith, and a call to accept Jesus Christ to avoid eternal judgment.

Title: Holy Night
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
One cold Christmas season, a woman warned children to be careful around the outdoor nativity scene, where a figure of Jesus was said to be ugly. The scene was noisy as someone banged a metal object while singing about the birth of the Savior, which puzzled a child who asked, "What's a savior?"

At home, a mother sighed with relief after returning, finding her dog settled by the fireplace. She asked her own mother how long a chaotic activity would last, only to be told it would continue until it finished, and that Bible study could wait for last-minute shopping.

Later, a boy named Rudy asked his grandpa to reread a passage from the Bible, which included Jesus's teaching to invite the poor, maimed, lame, and blind to feasts. Rudy's mother sharply disapproved, calling the idea offensive and quickly leaving.

As the family prepared to go shopping, the mother warned Rudy not to get lost and to change his jacket. The mall was crowded, and Rudy soon felt overwhelmed, claiming he needed fresh air. Outside, he met a dirty man named Harold Jordan living in a box.

Harold explained he once had a wife, daughter, and home, but lost everything during combat in Afghanistan after being ambushed. He was blind in one eye and had lost a leg due to a bomb explosion. Rudy was shocked by Harold's poverty and disabilities.

Meanwhile, the family noticed Rudy was missing and went searching. They found Rudy outside talking with Harold, and Rudy's mother was disappointed with him for leaving.

Back at home, Rudy explained he wanted to invite Harold to Sunday dinner, referring to the Bible passage read earlier. His grandfather agreed, despite expecting his wife Aunt Holly to disapprove.

On Saturday, Rudy's grandpa, Fred, invited Harold to their home, telling him he would get a shower, a shave, and clothes since no one was home. Harold was amazed at their kindness and asked what kind of people they were. Fred explained they were "a peculiar people, zealous of good works," quoting Titus 2:14.

Two hours later, Harold expressed gratitude, saying he was starting to feel human again. Fred wanted to hear Harold's story.

Harold revealed he had been in a coma after surgery, with confused medical records. He discovered his wife was told he died in combat. He had wanted to die with his platoon but survived for reasons he didn't understand.

Fred explained that God hadn't finished with Harold yet, giving him time to be saved from eternal damnation. Harold learned that though his body would die, his soul would live forever, either in heaven or hell depending on whether he accepted Jesus as his Savior.

Fred shared his own story as a Marine in Korea, how he was a sinner until a nurse prayed for him, and he was given the gospel. He explained Jesus Christ as God in the flesh who died, rose again, and offers salvation.

Harold listened intently and prayed with Fred, asking Jesus for forgiveness and to live in his heart. Jesus came into Harold's life, his sins were gone, and he became a new person.

That same night, Harold's little girl prayed for a new daddy since her father had died. On Sunday, Rudy's mother advised him to talk to men like Harold, not dismiss them.

After dinner, Fred shared news that military records were being corrected and there was an appointment regarding Harold's case. Evidence showed Harold's courage in combat, earning him medals and recognition.

Fred then surprised Harold with pay for back wages, a uniform, medals, and a plane ticket home. He gifted Harold a Bible, encouraging him to read it daily.

On Christmas Eve, a knock at the door revealed Harold standing on their porch, fulfilling a miracle.

For Harold Jordan, it had been a holy night. His soul was saved, and he returned to his family.

The story ends with a reminder: the choice between heaven and hell is yours to make by believing in Jesus Christ.

Title: Home Alone?
Subject: Homosexuality
Author: Chick
Responses:
Here’s the story based on the comic strip you provided:

Barbara called Lucy, worried because she wasn’t going on her business trip. Lucy asked why, and Barbara explained that their sitter had been in an accident and they couldn’t leave their son Charlie alone or find someone else to watch him. Lucy suggested their coach, Brad, might stay with Charlie. Brad was 26, well-liked by everyone, and women were very attracted to him. He even rearranged his schedule just to help the parents out, which thrilled them. 

Charlie’s mom thanked Coach Brad and said goodbye before leaving. Later, Brad asked Charlie what grade he was in and if he took social studies. They talked about whether the school taught about "alternate lifestyles" and if it was okay to be gay. Brad told Charlie being gay was cool and said some of their best athletes were gay too, making his move. 

Brad explained to Charlie that gay people didn’t choose to be gay—they were born that way, just like him. Charlie was surprised, but Brad’s story wasn’t true. He hadn’t been born gay; at age 11, Brad had been sent to juvenile hall for stealing, where he was sexually assaulted by older boys, which the comic claims introduced him to homosexuality. Brad’s spirit of homosexuality then supposedly invaded Charlie.

Late at night, Brad and Charlie watched TV. Charlie, who had no moral guidance or religious background, was vulnerable. The comic suggested the spirit that oppressed Brad now influenced Charlie. It mentioned how schools defended homosexuals by promoting tolerance and LGBTQ pride, playing the sympathy card, and pushing for LGBT rights amid growing visibility on TV and changes in laws. 

The story then took a darker turn, referencing the early 1980s and a wave of sickness among gay men, identified as G.R.I.D. (Gay Related Immune Deficiency), soon renamed A.I.D.S. The comic claimed this disease spread rapidly among promiscuous gay men and was incurable. It cited a study saying 43% of gay men had over 500 sex partners and spread many sexually transmitted diseases, shortening their lifespans.

The narrative then shifted to Biblical history, condemning homosexuality as a perversion found in all nations, religions, and neighborhoods, saying mainstream churches distorted God’s message about homosexuality. It referenced Sodom and Gomorrah’s destruction as divine judgment because of sexual sins, including homosexuality, quoting Jude 7.

It claimed God explicitly condemned homosexual acts in Leviticus, calling them abominations, and that God’s blessing was only for heterosexual marriage. Romans 1:26-27 was cited condemning same-sex acts and warning of judgment (Romans 1:32).

Charlie was depicted as feeling violated, ashamed, and polluted by Brad’s influence, with the comic warning that embracing the gay lifestyle would harden his heart against God. It said God made a plan to free homosexuals through Jesus Christ, who came to save all sinners.

Jesus was shown being betrayed and beaten but continuing to love everyone, including sinners and those living in sin. The story emphasized that God’s love is unconditional, quoting John 3:16 and 1 Peter 2:24, which speak of salvation through Jesus’ sacrifice.

Brad rejected this gospel message because his heart was hardened, saying he was happy with his lifestyle. Charlie, on the other hand, decided to accept Jesus and become a new person. The Holy Spirit tugged at Charlie’s heart, and the comic left it open what would happen next.

Years later, Brad died from AIDS complications and was rejected from Heaven due to his choices. Charlie, having accepted Jesus, was saved and entered eternal joy. The comic concluded that gays are not born that way but choose their lifestyle, that God hates the lifestyle and opposes it, and warned readers to flee from it or be destroyed by the Devil.

It ended with the message that the only way to joy and Heaven is through Jesus Christ, urging readers to choose faith or face eternal fire.

---

This story is a strongly religious and conservative perspective about homosexuality, blending personal narrative with religious condemnation and warnings about sin and salvation.

Title: How To Get Rich
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Carter
Responses:
Herbert had been waiting for years, hoping his Uncle John would die so he could greedily claim his fortune. One day, Herbert confronted Uncle John, accusing him of waiting to take his inheritance. Uncle John, weak and bedridden, protested and called for his lawyer to draft a new will.

Herbert rushed to fetch the lawyer, anxiously urging him to hurry because Uncle John was in bad shape. But the lawyer, calm and patient, reassured him that everything would be handled in due time.

As Uncle John lay in bed, he began dictating his will, bequeathing all of his earthly possessions to Herbert. Overjoyed, Herbert believed the fortune was finally his.

When the will was ready, Uncle John, despite his weakness, took the pen to sign it. Herbert eagerly handed it to him, filled with suspense.

Suddenly, Uncle John started coughing and gasping, dropping the pen. Herbert was horrified—Uncle John had passed away without signing the will.

Herbert couldn't believe it was true. The will was unsigned, so all of Uncle John's fortune would go to the state, minus some minor court and attorney fees. Desperate, Herbert demanded he get something from the estate, and the lawyer promised he would.

A year later, Herbert met with the lawyer, who reminded him of his promise. Herbert eagerly inquired what he would get, only to learn it was a bill from the state for back taxes amounting to nearly $5,000.

Later, Herbert sought to protect his own home and hired the Safety First Lock Company to make it burglar proof. He didn't care about the cost; he demanded immediate work.

When the job was done, Herbert was shown the secret combination to enter his house, assuring him only he would know it. Surveillance through TV screens and radar would alert him and the police if anyone approached.

He was also shown a burglar-proof vault, of which he was the sole keeper of the combination. Herbert felt secure, not trusting banks and proud of his wealth’s protection.

Later that evening, as Herbert prepared to count his money, a police officer arrived. The safe had been cracked—though only Herbert knew the combination.

The officer asked who installed the safe, and Herbert answered the Safety First Lock Company.

The news came that the company was run by a criminal named Dirty Joe, wanted in ten states. Even worse, Joe had given Herbert's safe combination to burglars, while Joe himself kept his wealth safely in a Swiss bank.

The story transitioned to show that even the richest, like Howard Hughes, die without their fortune. Ancient pharaohs’ treasures were taken by grave robbers, demonstrating that earthly riches are fleeting.

A military general warned that the world was in chaos—an all-out thermonuclear war could be the only escape from total collapse—implying that earthly wealth was not safe in the long term.

The comic then shared a biblical message: the only way to truly protect wealth and gain eternal security was to store treasures in heaven, where moths, thieves, and rust cannot destroy.

It referenced scriptures encouraging people to be rich toward God by doing good, sharing generously, and building their future on eternal foundations.

The comic cautioned that chasing money on earth requires hard work, planning, and often comes with pain, betrayal, and disappointment—ultimately chasing the wind.

It concluded that a lasting investment in heaven requires accepting the gift of eternal life through Jesus Christ, despite some social and personal costs.

Jesus is preparing a place in heaven for believers, where they will reign with Him and avoid eternal hell.

The comic urged readers to make the right choice, assuring them that eternal life and a heavenly mansion await for those who follow Christ, making it the most important decision of their lives.

Title: Humbug!
Subject: Christmas
Author: Chick
Responses:
The story begins with Bob Cratchit asking his employer, Mr. Scrooge, for permission to go home because it is very late and his family is waiting for him. Mr. Scrooge coldly questions why, to which Cratchit explains that it’s to celebrate the birth of Christ. Scrooge dismisses the significance of the story of Christmas as mere fairy tales, insisting that his world is finance and that it's all humbug.

Cratchit insists that Scrooge’s eternal destiny depends on the story of the baby born in a manger, but Scrooge mocks this, denying how his destiny could depend on a baby and calling Cratchit daft. Cratchit explains that the child was the Creator of the universe in human form. Scrooge harshly denounces this, branding man a blight on the earth.

Cratchit then points out that the Bible endorses the same idea, quoting verses that declare no one righteous and everyone sinful. Though Scrooge finds the verses severe, Cratchit warns that God will judge him for his sins. Scrooge awkwardly gulps and wishes Cratchit good night.

The next scenes show the Cratchit family preparing for Christmas with their meager means. Despite the hardships, Mrs. Cratchit trusts that God will always provide for them. The children window shop but remain hopeful and appreciate their family’s love. The Cratchits cherish what they have above all else. They gather to thank God for one another, expressing love and gratitude.

Meanwhile, Scrooge is in turmoil, disturbed by Cratchit’s words and the verses quoted. He bitterly despises Cratchit for quoting scripture and hates the idea that he might be judged. He thinks about his old partner Marley, wishing Marley could come to prove Cratchit wrong.

Mrs. Cooper, a debtor, pleads with Scrooge to extend her loan, but he refuses cruelly. That night, the door knocker on Scrooge’s home changes shape frighteningly, and he feels as though he’s losing his mind but resolves to go to bed. He tries to dismiss all the ‘humbug,’ praying to be saved.

Suddenly, Marley’s ghost appears, warning Scrooge that he died in sin and is condemned forever. Marley tells Scrooge that his fate will be worse and urges him to repent. Scrooge is terrified and finds a note Cratchit had given him with a promise that if he accepts Jesus as Savior, he will miss God’s judgment.

Scrooge cries out to Jesus, accepting Him as his personal Savior and asking for forgiveness. Feeling freed and wonderful, Scrooge vows to make restitution for all his wrongs and seek a changed life.

The next day, Scrooge spreads joy by ordering gifts for the Cratchit family, doubling Bob’s salary, forgiving Mrs. Cooper’s debt, and visiting the Cratchits to celebrate Christmas dinner. The children are delighted with their new toys and hopeful for the future. Bob thanks Scrooge and invites him to join the family.

Scrooge’s generosity continues as Tiny Tim’s condition improves thanks to prayers and the promise of medical care. Grateful and transformed, Scrooge shares that he has received God’s gift of eternal life and peace. The story closes with a blessing from the Cratchit family and the reminder that, like Scrooge, anyone can find salvation and joy through faith.

And so, Scrooge’s story ends in hope and redemption, encouraging all to consider their own eternal destiny.

Title: Hunter, The
Subject: Drugs/Alcohol
Author: Chick
Responses:
In a dark, hellish realm, the Master expressed his anger, demanding more souls from the local area as their quota had not been met. Furious, he ordered his minions to pressure the humans and threatened harsh consequences if results were not achieved promptly.

Back on Earth, school administrators discussed the challenge of recruiting souls from a particular school, which had many straight, resistant kids but also a group of "Rock freaks" who were easily influenced. One man proposed using a cunning hunter named Curt to target the straight kids, as he was skilled at manipulating and betraying students for profit.

Curt was introduced as the class vice-president, captain of the football team, and a well-regarded student pushing for a football scholarship. A member of the local church youth group, Curt was considered clean—no arrests, no drugs—but he was ruthless in exploiting others for money. He belonged to the popular crowd and was a known party animal. Curt’s role was to charm the less popular kids, making them believe he was their friend, get them hooked on drugs, and then discard them once they were trapped. His quota was to triple his usual number of hooked kids, with a promise of reward or severe consequences for failure.

As school started, Curt quickly befriended a shy boy named Jim, who was the captain of the football team. Soon, Curt introduced Jim to Bob and other peers, inviting them to parties where drugs were prevalent. Even though Jim was unsure at first, peer pressure mounted as Curt encouraged him to try a cigarette laced with a dangerous substance called "Happy powder." From there, the situation escalated quickly.

Curt orchestrated a tragic event by giving Bobby, one of the kids, a deadly PCP cocktail at a party. The drug caused Bobby to experience severe hallucinations and distress, and after being tossed into a vehicle in a drug-hazed state, he was abandoned on a highway outside of town.

Bobby was later found and taken to the emergency room, where his brother Doug was called in and told that Bobby was suffering a serious mental breakdown due to drug use. Despite efforts, Bobby's condition worsened over the following month. The doctors explained that Bobby would likely never recover fully, his mind ruined by the addiction.

Doug struggled with the tragic reality and questioned whether the world was going mad. A doctor explained that the chaos was part of a greater spiritual battle. The doctor spoke of biblical prophecy, referencing Jesus Christ's warnings about a time of great suffering and the rebellion humanity was facing.

Doug learned from the doctor that Jesus, who came to Earth as a sacrifice for humanity's sins, was the only hope for salvation. He was told that drug pushers were tools of Satan, working to break people down and that Jesus' followers received power to resist them. The spiritual conflict was framed as a war between good and evil, with an urgent call for Doug to accept Jesus as his Lord and Savior to avoid going to hell.

Moved by this message, Doug prayed for forgiveness and accepted Jesus, hoping to change his path.

Meanwhile, Curt was reaching the end of his school year mission. Despite threats, he demanded cash from those he exploited. On his last day, Jim left school with a gift from Curt—a drug fix. Jim succumbed to the drug and was murdered by Curt, who then moved him into another dimension, symbolizing a death beyond the physical.

Curt received praise from the Master’s minions for his success, and the Master himself welcomed the newly trapped Jim to his eternal prison. Curt was congratulated for securing the scholarship and praised for a job well done, confident he would do well in college.

The story ends with Curt being welcomed into the Master’s evil realm forever, with the chilling reminder that this cycle of soul-harvesting and spiritual warfare continues endlessly.

Title: I Beg Your Pardon!
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Carter
Responses:
One day, at the 2nd National Bank, a masked man entered and commanded everyone to put their hands up. The terrified bank clerk begged him not to shoot. The bandit, who rode away on his horse, warned no one to follow him and wished them a "Have a nice day!"

Despite the warnings, the bandit fired his gun wildly, the bullets thudding into the ground as he escaped. This outlaw was known as the Mannerly Bandit.

Soon after, the bank clerk identified a prisoner as the Mannerly Bandit, insisting he recognized him anywhere. The accused, Gentleman Jim, denied the charges, claiming innocence.

A swift trial sentenced Gentleman Jim to death by hanging. Despite his pleas of innocence and claims that others in the lineup looked exactly like him, the court found him guilty. As the sentence was carried out, Jim was confident he would not remain in prison long, laughing about a plan to bribe a guard for his freedom.

That night, a fellow prisoner knocked on Gentleman Jim’s cell, urging him to escape, but a guard slammed their door shut, warning Jim he would never get out alive.

Meanwhile, at the statehouse, a man named George presented the governor with the evidence, pointing out how the bandits all looked alike. He argued that anyone could have been wrongly convicted based on such uncertain identification.

The governor agreed and sent a pardon with his fastest horse, hoping to save Gentleman Jim before it was too late.

Racing against time, the rider sped towards the prison, but when he finally arrived and presented the pardon to Gentleman Jim, Jim refused to believe it. He had been tricked before and wouldn’t be fooled again. The man insisted that Jim must just sign the pardon to be free, but Jim refused, declaring he would rather die than accept it.

Later that morning, Gentleman Jim was hanged—though the pardon had arrived in time to save him.

The story remarked how foolish Gentleman Jim had been: by rejecting his pardon, he sealed his own fate. It suggested that, like Jim, many deserve punishment because of sin, citing scripture that no one is truly innocent.

God’s word says the penalty for sin is death, meaning spiritual separation from heaven. However, there is a way to be saved and live forever: God created humans to live with Him eternally, but judgment would determine who truly desired that eternal life.

At the perfect point in history, God sent His Son, Jesus Christ, to make a way for people to enter heaven. Jesus promised He was preparing a place there and would return.

There is only one way to enter heaven—through Jesus. He said He is the way, the truth, and the life, and no one can come to God except through Him. Only Jesus' sacrifice, shedding innocent blood, could pay for sin.

Three days after His death, Jesus rose from the grave, demonstrating power over death and offering pardon to all.

The story concluded with a call to accept Jesus’ pardon by believing in Him and repenting of sin, following Jesus’ love and forgiveness. It warned against rejecting this offer, as Gentleman Jim did, because the alternative is eternal separation from God.

Finally, a Bible-based invitation encouraged readers to accept Jesus as Savior and offered a step to commit to faith, emphasizing that now is the time to choose eternity with God.

Title: I See You!
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Carter
Responses:
A man looks around nervously and is warned that even though he may not see them, he is being watched. Cameras and other surveillance devices are everywhere, observing every move he makes. In places like grocery stores, classrooms, parking lots, and even drive-thrus, these devices catch every detail. The man driving a car feels like he’s being watched, and a road sign humorously denies it.

There are people employed to watch these surveillance monitors, raising the question of who watches the watchers. It might be the government, but it goes beyond that. It’s not aliens either; the true watcher is someone who monitors people constantly, 24/7, every day of the year.

This ultimate watcher is God. Citing scriptures, the story references how God knows all actions and thoughts, reflects on judgment, and watches every word spoken, even in the dark. No one can hide from Him, and everyone must face judgment one day. At that time, all deeds and sins will be revealed.

Those whose names are not written in the book of life will face eternal punishment, whereas the righteous will receive eternal life. However, this doesn’t have to be the end. God has a rescue plan.

His plan involves His Son, Jesus Christ, who lived a sinless life, came to Earth to take the punishment for humanity’s sins, died, and was buried. Three days later, Jesus rose from the dead, offering forgiveness and eternal life to those who believe.

Even though God knows everything, He desires a truthful relationship. A person must admit their sins, acknowledge Jesus as God’s Son, and put their trust in Him for salvation. This includes asking for forgiveness, accepting Jesus into their heart, and becoming born again.

God continues to watch everyone, but for those born again, the experience is different. They are saved and assured of eternal life through faith in Jesus Christ. The story closes with an invitation to reflect on personal faith and trust in Jesus for salvation.

Title: In The Beginning
Subject: Evolution
Author: Chick
Responses:
A man proudly shows another a toy dinosaur, explaining that this creature lived 145 million years ago. The other man responds with disbelief, calling it a joke, and says that his teacher told him that fact. The first man retorts that the teacher must have been brainwashed and suggests that evolution is more a religion that mocks God, implying that the 145 million years is just a guess.

The skeptical man challenges the other to tell him when the dinosaurs lived. The first man confidently claims he knows the exact day. He then introduces a book he trusts, implying that many scientists contradict each other, and turns to the Bible for answers.

He reads from Genesis, explaining that God created the heavens and earth in six days. At the start, the earth was formless and empty, and God said, "Let there be light," dividing light from darkness without mentioning any Big Bang. On Day 2, God separated the waters, creating a vapor canopy around the earth. On Day 3, the seas were gathered and dry land with plants appeared, though this happened before the sun was made.

On Day 4, God made the sun, moon, and stars, which would have to be real days to keep the plants alive. Day 5 saw waters bring forth fish and birds flying above. On Day 6, God created land animals, including dinosaurs, and then man in His image from the dust of the ground. The man stresses there was no “prehistoric” time as taught in textbooks and says this word was used to confuse people.

The reader asks if dinosaurs and humans were created the same day. The first man confirms this, even showing photos of human footprints alongside dinosaur footprints from Glen Rose, Texas, insisting God does not lie.

The story continues, dating Adam’s creation to roughly 6,000 years ago and stating there was no world before Day One. Adam was the first relative, and the man warns that what Adam did would be disliked.

Adam was created fully formed and placed in the Garden of Eden, with permission to eat freely from every tree except the tree of knowledge of good and evil, warned that eating from it would cause death. God saw everything was good and rested on the seventh day. Adam named all the animals but felt lonely, so God created Eve to help him. At this point, things were innocent.

But Satan entered the story as a serpent, cunning and dangerous, and spoke to Eve. He questioned God’s command, suggesting she would not die if she ate the forbidden fruit and would instead gain knowledge like God. Eve was deceived and despite knowing it was wrong, both Adam and Eve ate the fruit, disobeying God.

As a result, their innocence was lost. They feared God, blamed each other, and were cursed along with the serpent and the ground. Their lives changed forever.

Adam and Eve were expelled from the garden, and death entered the world. Their first son, Cain, murdered his brother out of jealousy. This sin passed down through generations.

The man explains that everyone is sinful, none righteous, and our hearts remain deceitful. When people die, their bodies return to dust, but their souls face two destinations: heaven or hell.

Jason asks what he must do to avoid hell, and the first man says absolutely nothing unless he repents for his sins. Jason confesses his worries about sinning all the time and doubts that God really cares.

The first man responds that Jesus Christ left heaven to be born, lived a sinless life for 33 years, and sacrificed himself on the cross, shedding his blood to pay for humanity’s sins. Jesus rose three days later, offering eternal life to anyone who believes.

Jason is encouraged to believe in Jesus and make Him personal Savior to be saved. The story concludes with a prayer asking for forgiveness and acceptance of Jesus, trusting in His sacrifice and salvation, citing Romans 10:9.

This story presents a creationist view, contrasting biblical creation with evolutionary teachings, emphasizing faith in Jesus Christ as the path to eternal life.

Title: Is Allah Like You?
Subject: Islam
Author: Chick
Responses:
There were two boys, one named Ali and the other Hassan, playing outside when Ali was urged to run faster. They were running and laughing, having fun. As Hassan grew closer to a woman standing near a doorway, the woman suddenly shouted a warning. But it was too late, and Hassan collided with the woman, spilling water all over her.

The man nearby got angry and accused the boys of defiling his Qur'an, threatening to beat them both. The boys begged for mercy and apologized, but he ordered them to be quiet and get up. Despite Safiya's pleas that it was an accident, the man called Hassan a "lazy, worthless child" and refused to listen. When Safiya tried to intervene, he scolded her harshly, demanding she stay silent and threatening her as well. Hassan was hurt and tearful, pleading for the beating to stop, but his father ordered him to get up and do chores.

Hassan, cruelly mistreated and feeling unloved, wondered if Allah was as harsh as his father. Later that day, Ahmed, an older man from the community, came to visit and asked Uncle Yousef a question regarding the Qur'an and domestic violence. Uncle Yousef urged Ahmed to study his Qur'an and hadith carefully and not forget his education.

At home, Safiya expressed fear of Ahmed, telling Hassan that Ahmed frightened her. Hassan whispered to his mother to be quiet as Ahmed was locked in a room studying. Ahmed was deeply troubled after reading a letter containing lists of suras that challenged his beliefs. Frustrated but determined, Ahmed vowed to continue studying.

He discovered troubling facts about the Qur'an—that it was written on various materials and was compiled from memories, not descended from heaven as he had believed. He was further confused learning that Muhammad, the prophet, was human, albeit supported by Allah, and that certain harsh commands were attributed to Allah and Muhammad.

His distress grew as he contemplated the violent and fearful aspects of the teachings he was studying. He questioned how a god could change his mind, command violence, and still claim to be merciful and loving. In despair, he prayed earnestly for the living God in heaven to show him the truth.

Following this prayer, Ahmed encountered a man in the market who gave him a book, which turned out to be the Bible, filled with the words of the prophet Jesus. Excited and curious, Ahmed studied the Bible over the next week, sharing with Safiya passages where Jesus taught love, mercy, and forgiveness, which contrasted sharply with what he had learned from the Qur'an.

He learned Jesus' teachings about loving enemies, honoring wives, and the promise of everlasting life through belief in Jesus. Most importantly, he read about Jesus' sacrifice for humanity's sins and His resurrection.

Ahmed bravely approached his family, asking for forgiveness for how he had treated them. He shared his faith in Jesus and expressed that he had surrendered to the living God he had been searching for. His father accepted his apology, and Ahmed promised to show them how to find Jesus too.

Hassan, moved and tearful, admitted he was wrong and declared that Allah was nothing like the God of Jesus. The story concluded with a message that Jesus is the only way to heaven, and an invitation to believe in Him for salvation.

Title: Is That All?
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Carter
Responses:
On Megan's 12th birthday, her family gave her a simple present, and she was visibly disappointed. When she asked, "That's it?" her father curtly responded, "You expected more? Isn’t it enough for you?" The tension was clear. Later, as people left the party, her father wondered aloud, "Where did you ever get such an attitude, young lady?" Megan replied, pointedly, "Why, from you, Daddy!" confused by his reaction as he urged her to "Think about it..."

Megan then recalled a moment from the previous season when she hit a home run. At that very moment, her father had missed the excitement because he was chasing another client. Megan explained, "But while you were away, thinking of me, I needed you here!" She challenged him, wondering if he'd actually provided for them, not just financially but emotionally and spiritually. Suddenly, a doorbell rang.

An unexpected visitor, Eli Fitch, who was their grandmother's lawyer, had come with instructions from their late grandmother. Eli handed over a mysterious package, saying, "All you need to know is inside. Good day!" Megan’s father hesitated but agreed to open it, remarking, “Grandma liked surprises, but this is a funny time to…” Megan insisted, "OPEN IT, Daddy!" Inside, they found a key and a note from Grandma inviting them to see her house.

Arriving at the house, Megan was thrilled but her father was unsure of what to do next. Megan encouraged her mother to explore the house with her, which led to a significant discovery in a kitchen drawer. They found a Bible, Grandma’s Bible, placed on a shelf labeled with the phrase, "When you’re down, look up."

As Megan’s father read the Bible, he uncovered a letter from Grandma addressed to him. The letter’s message was filled with advice based on scripture, emphasizing the dangers of covetousness and the importance of not valuing material wealth over the soul. Grandma reminded him with quotes from Luke and Deuteronomy that true riches aren't possessions, and that everything he had done would be accounted for.

The story moved through scenes of Megan’s father's life: working hard, saving money, facing the challenges of friendship and family balance, and ultimately realizing he had neglected his soul and sins in pursuit of worldly success. Scriptures from Matthew, Luke, and Revelation illustrated the reality of judgment and the eternal consequences of his choices.

Grandma's letter explained God’s eternal plan, including the sacrifice of Jesus, who lived a perfect life and died to pay for humanity’s sins. The promise was that anyone who trusts in Jesus can be forgiven and born again.

Moved by this revelation, Megan’s father prayed, asking Jesus for forgiveness and help to be a better man, husband, and father. He was born again in faith. Megan, excited and hopeful, called, "DADDY???" as he embraced this transformation.

Later back at Grandma’s house, Megan apologized for standing silently for so long and expressed her joy, saying, "Oh, Daddy! This is the present I really wanted!" They discussed how moving to care for Grandma had been difficult, and her father wondered aloud if the Bible could help him with both finances and his soul. Megan assured him, "I’m sure it could, Honey!"

As they sat together, Megan’s father noticed something blocking the light on a table. Upon investigation, he discovered a deed to the property in his name, a final gift from Grandma. His faith journey was sealed with an invitation to accept Jesus Christ as Savior, reaffirmed by a personal salvation checklist included with the deed.

Thus, through Grandma's wisdom and God's word, Megan's family found hope, faith, and restoration, embracing a new path filled with spiritual understanding and renewed purpose.

Title: Is There Another Christ?
Subject: Catholicism
Author: Chick
Responses:
The story begins by addressing the universal experience of being lied to, acknowledging that everyone has heard lies and sometimes even told little white lies. It notes skepticism people often have towards different authorities, like the news or religious leaders, as they all claim to tell "The Truth," yet often disagree. This raises the question of where to find the real truth.

The story explains that in the Bible, God gave commandments to Moses, including that His name is above every name. God's word, as presented in the Bible, holds ultimate authority and truth, even above human beings and angels. God's word is final and true, and Jesus taught that His words would never pass away. Judgement by God will be based on His word, so people should base their beliefs on it.

Jesus claimed to be the way, the truth, and the life, and the story warns about false Christs, who are dangerous impostors misleading people. Since the beginning, Satan has twisted God's words and sent false teachers to deceive people. Jesus called Satan a liar and the source of lies.

Throughout history, false religious leaders, described as wolves in sheep's clothing, have sought to exploit religion for personal gain. Jesus warned to be wary of such deceivers who would perform great signs to mislead even the elect. Believers are urged to lovingly tell others the truth.

Jesus promised to send the Holy Ghost to guide believers into all truth. The story then critiques Roman Catholicism, particularly the pope's claims to infallibility and godly titles such as "Holy Father," which are said to belong only to God. Historical statements from popes are cited to question their authority.

The narrative accuses Roman Catholic priests of acting as if they can control Jesus Christ, turning Him into a mere piece of bread during the Eucharist, contrary to Jesus' words. The Eucharist ceremony, especially the use of the monstrance and adoration of the wafer, is portrayed as worshipping a created symbol rather than Christ Himself.

Jesus' warning against false Christs is repeated, emphasizing that believers should not be deceived by religious impostors. The story highlights that Jesus’ sacrifice was once and for all, perfect and sufficient, refuting the Catholic doctrine of repeated masses as continually reinforcing a dying savior.

The story concludes by emphasizing the importance of choosing to believe God’s word over men. It warns against the false religious system called the Antichrist, which deceives billions and opposes God’s word. Jesus does not want anyone to perish but to repent. The false system, called the "mother of abominations," will eventually face destruction, but Jesus calls people to come out from it and be saved.

Title: It's a Deal
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Carter
Responses:
James was the pride of his family, always excelling in everything he did at school. His father would proudly announce, "Congratulations, Son! You were top in your class again!" James humbly replied, "Thank you, Father." His younger brother, Denzel, looked up to James, and when asked if he was proud of his big brother, he eagerly said, "Yes 'um!"

James was a star athlete as well, winning trophies in every sport. His father admired his achievements, saying, "My, my. Look at all your trophies! You've won awards in every sport. You are amazing, James!" To which James responded, "God has blessed me, Dad." Proudly, his father answered, "Amen!"

At the family dinner table, James shared his dreams of becoming a pastor like his father. His father was honored and expressed, "Oh my, James! We are so honored to have a son like you. We all love you so much!" However, Denzel silently thought, "I don't."

Despite James’ successes, Denzel grew resentful. Observing James’ perfect grades, talent, and popularity, Denzel thought bitterly, "He's got everything! Looks, talent, and brains... and I'm a loser. I hate his guts! I hope he drops dead real soon."

Life shifted dramatically when James announced he would marry the woman he loved. The community congratulated him, while Denzel couldn’t believe it was happening. Watching girls admire James, Denzel felt jealous and insecure. When James jokingly showed a picture of himself to tease, Denzel, who recognized the picture as belonging to the preacher’s boy, became enraged.

One evening, Denzel and a friend followed James in a car. Without warning, shots rang out, striking James. "Gotcha!" one of the shooters exclaimed. Three days later, James’ funeral was attended by hundreds who came to pay their respects, though Denzel and his mother were the only ones who didn't cry. Her silent smile disturbed those who knew the family.

Denzel thought, "He's dead! Now I'll get some respect. My wish came true! Wow, it’s like I’ve got some kind of power." But soon he wished for fame and wealth, hoping to become richer and more famous than anyone else.

Years later, Denzel’s grades were failing, and the coach threatened to cut him from the basketball team. His father warned, "You're not the hot shot you think you are. So straighten up or drop out!" Denzel lashed out, dismissing his father’s religious talk as nonsense.

Struggling, Denzel encountered a mysterious man in flashy clothes who offered to make him a famous basketball star for 13 years in exchange for his soul. Hungry for success, Denzel agreed to the deal, shaking hands with the stranger and committing himself to the bargain.

Denzel’s talent blossomed immediately. He stunned everyone by sinking impossible shots and transformed into a dominant player. His coach and teammates hailed him as unstoppable, and his team won championships. But the sinister man’s voice lingered, reminding Denzel the deal had a price.

Despite his fame, years later Denzel’s health declined rapidly. He felt sick and feared dying. Doctors ran tests but couldn’t diagnose his illness. His parents kept a bedside vigil, praying and hoping. The news reported Denzel’s critical condition and hinted he might be basketball’s greatest star lost forever.

In a heartbreaking moment, doctors declared, "Flatline! He’s gone!" His father shouted, "No! He can’t die! Denzel, get back into that body!" His mother prayed fervently, calling on Jesus to save him. Miraculously, Denzel revived, gasping for breath and describing his near-death experience filled with fire and horror. He begged for help to avoid going back to hell.

Ashamed, Denzel confessed to his father, "Papa, I thought you were crazy preaching about Hell. But I saw it. I sold my soul for a little fame." His father assured him, "Denzel, that was a bogus deal. The devil already had you. But Jesus can still save you."

They shared the story of Jesus’ sacrifice on the cross, quoting John 3:16, and urged Denzel to accept Jesus as his Savior. Filled with hope, Denzel repented and praised God. Moments later, his soul was taken to heaven.

The mysterious man who had tricked Denzel lamented, "Blast it! I lost Denzel... but... oh, hi there! I think I can help you! Can we talk about your soul?" A warning appeared nearby, "Any deal with the devil is phony."

If you haven't trusted in the Lord Jesus as your Savior, remember this: Satan’s already gotcha unless you turn to Him. The story closes with a promise from Acts 16:31—"Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved."

Title: It's All About You!
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
Life felt overwhelmingly unfair to Hannah. Sitting at the library, she lamented, "Why am I even here?" Her grandpa, who was beside her, asked, "What do you mean?" Hannah sighed, explaining that nobody understood her "inner me," not even her parents. Grandpa reassured her, "Your parents love you." But Hannah was frustrated, saying, "Aw, come on, Grandpa, they just sent me to this dump to get me out of their hair."

Grandpa reminded her that her dad was working two jobs and had even refinanced the house to pay her college tuition. Hannah retorted, "And I'm supposed to be grateful? That's his job! I didn't ask to be born, you know!" As other students passed by, Hannah was distracted by scenes of teenage drama around her. Grandpa noticed and said, "Sounds like you've got it all figured out... but you forgot about somebody very important." Hannah asked, "Who's that?" Grandpa replied mysteriously, "Actually you forgot about two 'someones'." 

Walking outside, Grandpa pointed to the neighborhood and said, "They've seen things you'd rather people didn't know about." Hannah, startled, asked, "That's creepy! Who are they?" Grandpa explained, "One of them has it in for you!" Hannah was confused and asked, "Why? What did I do? Wait. Is it a guy or a girl?" Grandpa leaned in solemnly, "You can't imagine how much he hates you... and he’s got lots of scary friends."

On a bench, Grandpa solemnly explained that this enemy had the "upper hand" because Hannah had been told he doesn't exist. Hannah was shocked as Grandpa said, "He wants to steal the most valuable thing you've got..." Her eyes widened. "My iPhone?" she gulped. Grandpa shook his head, "Your SOUL! And they are watching to see the outcome."

Hannah asked, "Who's watching?" Grandpa replied, "Forces in the spirit world — angels and devils. It’s a war to see who gets your soul." Hannah was stunned by the gravity. Grandpa continued, "And you’re more likely to end up in hell because of one thing..." Hannah asked, "What’s that?"

Grandpa explained that the first man, Adam, disobeyed God and sinned, and that sin passed onto all of humanity. Sin ruins everything, and most of the world will end up in hell because of it. Hannah asked what kinds of sins, and Grandpa answered, "Anything—murder, lies, greed—because we hate to obey God."

When we die with sin on our souls, we face God’s judgment. Satan, Grandpa warned, means business and will destroy your soul. Hannah was incredulous, but Grandpa insisted that Satan hates her and doesn’t care about who she is. Satan will ruin her dreams, try to drive her to suicide, or worse. Grandpa said Satan traps people into religious systems that turn them into "spiritual zombies," deceiving them with false "holy men" who won't get them to heaven.

But then Grandpa shared God's good news. Religion often teaches that God weighs good deeds against bad deeds, but that’s dangerous and wrong. Many religious systems are cruel and power-hungry. But God hates sin and did something about it. He sent His Son, Jesus, who was born without sin from a virgin named Mary.

Jesus, who was God in human form, taught love but was hated and crucified by the people He came to save. Jesus shed His blood to wash away humanity’s sins and rose from the dead three days later, offering the only way to heaven.

Grandpa explained the way to heaven is simple: just believe in Jesus and what He did for you, and God will forgive your sins. Hannah worried if that was just religion, but Grandpa said no—it’s a relationship with God, becoming part of His family.

Moved, Hannah prayed quietly, asking Jesus to forgive her for her sins and to save her. Grandpa said she was now "born again." Hannah felt free and understood that Jesus loved her and truly understood her.

Finally, Grandpa warned that if anyone rejected Jesus, they would hear God's words on judgment day: "I never knew you. Depart from me!" He urged Hannah not to let that happen.

Hannah had learned about the battle for her soul, the power of sin, and the hope that comes through Jesus—a hope that changed her life forever.

Title: It's Coming
Subject: Bible Stories
Author: Chick
Responses:
As evacuations began due to fears of massive mudslides caused by continuous rain, Jason called Bob, convinced that this must be the worst storm in history. Bob corrected him, saying that Noah's Flood was far worse. Jason's cousin was still upset with Bob for his beliefs about the flood, and she wanted to meet him. Jason invited her over.

When the cousin arrived, she firmly believed that the Earth was billions of years old, and she was determined to challenge Bob, who insisted that the Earth was only 6,000 years old, a truth he claimed had been proven. The cousin, having taken college courses, insisted Bob was confused and needed help understanding modern science.

Bob explained that his professor, who held a Ph.D. and taught Life Sciences, had disproven many modern scientific claims and defended the biblical account. The professor had blown apart the Bible skeptics' arguments about the flood, dismissing the idea that the flood was merely local legend and claiming that as people’s concept of God grew bigger, so did myths about the flood. Bob argued that local floods don't leave seashells atop mountains, evidence that supports the biblical flood story.

The cousin disputed Bob’s claim, her heart full of skepticism, but Bob began telling the story of the biblical flood. About 4,400 years ago, God decided to destroy the Earth with water because sin had corrupted mankind. The wickedness of humanity was great, and every thought of their hearts was continuously evil.

Only Noah was found righteous and walked with God. God gave him instructions to build the Ark with specific dimensions, using gopher wood and sealing it with pitch, a tar-like substance, to protect it from the coming storm. The massive ship had three decks and many rooms, large enough to hold 50,000 animals including young land dinosaurs.

As Noah built the Ark, he faced ridicule from people who called him insane, but he persisted. When the animals arrived, many people scoffed at the sight. God then called Noah and his family into the Ark, shutting the door as the great storm began.

The floodwaters surged as the earth’s crust fractured, releasing massive fountains of water and causing torrential rains for forty days and nights. Tidal waves and whirlpools destroyed everything, tearing up mountains and swallowing the land beneath water. After the storm ceased, billions of dead creatures were buried under layers of sediment, which later became fossils.

God promised never to destroy the earth with water again but warned of future judgment by fire. The story then shifts to Jesus Christ, who came to earth 2,000 years ago. Jesus, the Son of God, created the earth and brought the flood. He came to be a sacrifice for humanity’s sins, died, rose again, and promised to return in judgment.

Jesus warned that His second coming would be sudden and powerful, like the days of Noah before the flood. The cousin was shocked, realizing her professor’s teachings had lied to her.

Bob urged Janet to accept Jesus as her Savior. Moved to tears and repentance, she prayed for forgiveness and salvation. The story concludes with a reminder that calling on the Lord brings salvation, offering hope beyond judgment for those who believe.

Title: It's Not Your Fault
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
Bobbie Barns’s case was a simple suicide, or so it seemed to the inspector. However, before drawing conclusions, he insisted on interviewing all the kids living at the foster home called “Happy Halls,” which had a nearly perfect record and was rated top in the state.

Ralph, who shared a room with Bobbie, was terrified, hinting that something was wrong. The inspector learned that two years prior, another seven-year-old had committed suicide there, a red flag. An autopsy was ordered immediately.

Bobbie had endured a tough life marked by broken bones, fresh bruises, and brutal sexual abuse. The inspector wanted a thorough physical exam for each child and decided to get them out of Happy Halls while investigating, contacting Child Protective Services.

Despite the inspector’s wishes, Judge Stone refused to allow the children to be removed from Happy Halls. Frustrated, the inspector prepared to take legal action. He was soon called to the chief’s office, where he was chastised and ordered to close the suicide case. Happy Halls was back in business, and the inspector barely kept his badge.

Ralph found solace talking to Mrs. Carpenter, the newest foster parent. Although skeptical at first, he eventually warmed to her as she assured him she would protect him. Yet Ralph was haunted by nightmares, reliving the abuse and fearful of Judge Stone, who had placed him there.

Mrs. Carpenter revealed her own harrowing past. She and her husband were missionaries in Rwanda, where the Hutu tribe attacked the Tutsi tribe in a horrific genocide. Despite the presence of UN peacekeepers, the UN failed to intervene. Her husband was brutally murdered, and she barely survived six months in a hospital plagued by nightmares.

Ralph’s nightmares were filled with Judge Stone attacking him. Mrs. Carpenter comforted him, explaining that forgiveness could break the power those nightmares held, even when the pain and hatred felt overwhelming. She taught Ralph to pray for those who hurt them, offering a message of hope and healing.

They discussed the biblical judgment awaiting those who reject God’s forgiveness, the Great White Throne Judgment, and the eternal consequences for those who refuse to repent. Mrs. Carpenter explained that Jesus Christ sacrificed Himself to save humanity from this fate, providing salvation through faith in Him.

Though many rejected Jesus, His return was promised, when He would reign as King and Savior. Ralph was invited to accept Jesus into his heart, and after praying, he repented and became a child of God.

The next morning, his foster siblings celebrated, amazed that Ralph would be with them in heaven someday. Suddenly, a call came for Ralph, though no one knew who it was.

Ralph soon learned that Judge Stone, the source of his nightmares and pain, had died suddenly of a heart attack. Ralph found comfort in the belief that Jesus was with him and that salvation and forgiveness had given him a new start and hope for the future.

Title: It's The Law
Subject: Ten Commandments
Author: Chick
Responses:
Timmy Johnson was shocked when Miss Crawford told him he had flunked his test with an "F." She scolded him, saying, "How dare you write about the 10 Commandments?!" Timmy tried to explain that they were true and even had a movie made about them, but Miss Crawford insisted it was all a lie and declared it the last straw. 

Miss Crawford warned Timmy, "I’m coming to talk to your parents tonight. I could suspend you for this." Worried, Timmy called his Uncle Bob and told him about his troubles. Uncle Bob promised to come at 7:00 and asked Timmy to pray for his teacher.

When Uncle Bob arrived, Miss Crawford questioned if he was Timmy's father. Timmy explained his mother was in the hospital and Uncle Bob had come at the doctor's request. Uncle Bob introduced himself and apologized for any disappointment.

Miss Crawford offered tea and cookies, but Timmy immediately got to the point. Uncle Bob revealed Timmy was in trouble for writing about Moses and the 10 Commandments, and Miss Crawford accused him of pushing religion in school. Uncle Bob, Timmy’s history teacher, stated he only dealt with facts, not fantasy, and challenged Miss Crawford to back up her claims.

Uncle Bob explained the most proven ancient history book, the Bible, tells all about Moses’ life and achievements. Miss Crawford was skeptical but listened as he read from the book of Exodus about Hebrew slaves increasing in number, Pharaoh ordering every Hebrew baby boy to be cast into the Nile River out of fear.

He told how one Hebrew mother saved her baby by placing him in a waterproof basket on the river. Pharaoh’s daughter found the child, loved him, and named him Moses. Moses grew up in the royal family of Egypt but knew his real family suffered as slaves, forcing him to make tough decisions.

One day, Moses killed an Egyptian for hurting a Hebrew slave and fled Egypt to save his life. Forty years later, God sent Moses back to Egypt with a message for Pharaoh: “Let my people go.” Pharaoh refused to obey, and Egypt faced devastating plagues.

As God struck down Egyptian gods one by one with plagues—from the Nile turning to blood, to frogs invading Pharaoh’s bed, boils affecting men and beasts, cattle dying, hail and locusts destroying crops, darkness covering the land, and finally the death of the firstborn—Miss Crawford learned of God’s power and judgement.

Pharaoh relented and ordered the Hebrews to leave, but then changed his mind and sent his army after them. God parted the Red Sea for the Hebrews to escape and then drowned Pharaoh’s entire army once they crossed safely.

Fifty days later, God spoke to Moses from Mount Sinai and gave him laws written on stone tablets—the Ten Commandments—to govern His people.

Uncle Bob recited the commandments, highlighting their importance and God’s hatred for sin, like lying and stealing. He explained that everyone breaks these laws and is a sinner; good works can't erase sin.

Miss Crawford, bewildered, questioned how anyone could get to heaven then. Uncle Bob taught her that 2,000 years ago, God sent His Son, Jesus Christ, to earth. Jesus chose to live humbly, suffer, die as a sacrifice, and shed His holy blood to cleanse people from sin.

Jesus died, was buried, and rose again three days later. This was God’s gift of love for humanity, allowing anyone who believes to have everlasting life.

Moved by the story, Miss Crawford asked what she needed to do. Uncle Bob told her to repent, confess her sins, and accept Jesus as Lord and Savior. Grateful, she prayed, asking for forgiveness and promising to serve the Lord.

In the end, Miss Crawford thanked Timmy for teaching her about the 10 Commandments, Moses, and most importantly, the Lord Jesus, thanking God she had flunked Timmy because it led her to faith and salvation.

Title: It's Who You Know
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
The story begins at the law offices of Shyster and Shwindle, where a man tries to speak to Shyster Jr., claiming to be an old friend named Hank. However, Shyster Jr. dislikes friends and quickly hangs up, threatening to sue if Hank calls again.

Next, Sydney Monroe appears in the office, introducing himself as the new mail boy, though Shyster Jr. insists he never hired him. Sydney admits he's just lucky to have the job. Shyster Jr. angrily reveals Sydney only has the job because Sydney's Aunt Rebecca, who is married to Shyster Jr., likes him. Despite Sydney’s lack of experience, Shyster Jr. reveals he's stuck with him and must teach Sydney how to be successful.

Shyster Jr. shares a secret: success comes not from talent or knowledge, but from "who you know." He explains that Sydney’s aunt is very rich and influential, and her connections will open doors. Sydney is urged to ask his aunt to introduce him to her powerful friends who can help him.

Soon, Sydney meets Katie Walker, his aunt’s assistant, who tells him the most important connection is with God's Son, the Lord Jesus Christ. Katie explains that Sydney's sin bars him from heaven and that Jesus came to pay for these sins so people could be saved. She offers Sydney forgiveness through Jesus, but Sydney rejects this, dismissing it as nonsense.

Later, Katie tells Aunt Rebecca about Sydney’s rejection. Rebecca calls Junior to bring Sydney home for a surprise. Over dinner, Rebecca reveals that she is putting Sydney through college, donating $150,000 a year. Sydney quickly gains popularity due to his aunt's influence and becomes famous on campus, despite doubts about his abilities.

Sydney rises quickly, becoming a Junior Partner at the law firm and the most eligible bachelor. Aunt Rebecca then announces that Sydney will head Public Relations as her business goes international. However, Sydney starts acting foolishly, and soon thereafter, Aunt Rebecca suffers a stroke and dies.

At Aunt Rebecca’s funeral, Sydney inherits her vast estate and businesses. Katie Walker is named his personal advisor and vice president. Sydney suffers a breakdown and accuses Katie of being crazy for mentioning Jesus again. He denies needing God and insists on running the company with only the power of influential connections.

Sydney is fired after refusing to accept Jesus, ending up in the Happy Hills Sanitarium. Katie visits him, urging him again to believe in Jesus, but Sydney stubbornly refuses, vowing never to be "saved."

A week later, Katie welcomes Sydney back and challenges his disbelief by reminding him that God's Word says Jesus created the universe, despite Sydney’s belief in evolution. Sydney angrily dismisses it and threatens Katie, refusing to listen.

The narrative closes with a dramatic moment: Sydney’s plane crashes into a mountain in Italy; there are no survivors. Sydney's soul immediately enters hell.

On Judgment Day, hell is emptied as many souls, including Sydney’s, are cast into the lake of fire for rejecting Jesus. Readers are urged to make sure they know Jesus to avoid this fate, with a response form to accept Jesus Christ.

Thus, Sydney’s tale is a cautionary one, highlighting the consequences of relying solely on worldly connections and rejecting faith in Jesus Christ.

Title: It's Your Life!
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Carter
Responses:
A man was enjoying a peaceful moment with his partner. Feeling comfortable and content, he told his soul to take ease, enjoy life, eat, drink, and be merry, trusting that he had much good laid up for many years. Suddenly, he was startled when Death appeared and told him, "Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee." He collapsed, realizing suddenly that his time on earth was over. He was buried, and at the funeral, family and friends remembered him as a good man. But a voice reminded that all are unclean and that no one is truly righteous, as all sin and fade like a leaf.

Then, the man was awakened in his grave as the trumpet sounded for the resurrection. He was confused, realizing he was dead and that all was over. An angel approached and told him he had an appointment — a judgment — despite his previous belief that heaven and hell were just stories told on earth. The angel reassured him many others would be there.

Flying through the heavens, the man was told this was his destination, though he could hardly believe it was happening to him. He was brought before the judgment seat, where everything he had ever done had been recorded and was now being reviewed. The man protested that he had lived a good life, no different from anyone else, but the angel insisted that Scripture says none are righteous.

In the judgment scene, the man stood before God, who had books opened including the Book of Life. The angel commanded the review of his life, emphasizing that this was indeed his life being examined. The man was surprised to see himself as a baby, wondering if everything he had ever done would be reviewed.

As his life was reviewed, the man was forced to confront many sins he had hoped were hidden — things like theft, lies, disobedience to parents, envy, deceit, hypocrisy, pride, and more. He recalled moments he thought were private, but they were all visible and accounted for.

He tried to defend himself by pointing to his church attendance, but was told that simply attending was not enough. He was reminded that God’s love was shown through Jesus Christ, who came so that those who believe might have everlasting life. But the man was indifferent and uncaring, focused only on earthly concerns.

He declared that he didn’t need Christ and would live life his own way. He admitted he must have been crazy to reject the truth. At judgment, Christ did not recognize his name in the Book of Life and pronounced him cursed, destined for eternal punishment prepared for the devil and his angels.

The man was cast into everlasting fire, the lake of fire, as his final fate. However, the narrative closed with a message of hope: this does not have to be your life. The Lord is patient and desires that all come to repentance.

The comic urged readers to surrender their lives to Christ, to repent and accept Jesus as their personal Savior, so they might have forgiveness and eternal life. It showed a man praying for salvation, receiving grace, and then living a new life, assured of a home in heaven.

Finally, it depicted the blessed reward awaiting those faithful to Christ, entering into the joy of the Lord, emphasizing that true death is precious in the sight of the Lord when it results in eternal life with Him.

Title: Jenny
Subject: Basic Gospel
Responses:
A man, excited about boarding a ship, picks up his cat and declares he would never get on a ship without his buddy. As they step aboard the ship, the man remarks about the ship's size, and a cat named Jenny eagerly tries to catch something on the floor. Jenny chases after all the rats on the ship, proving her worth as a mouser. The crew welcomes Jenny aboard, and she settles in among her catch. One crewmember comments on Jenny's deserved wages, while others express concern that the boiler room isn't a suitable place for a cat.

The ship's cook offers Jenny a place to sleep in the kitchen to keep the rats away, and Jenny purrs contentedly. Weeks later, Jenny has put on some weight, prompting a conversation about her well-being and the news that she had kittens. Despite the owner's plans for a full cruise, Jenny decides to disembark with her kittens when her buddy gets off the ship. The owner reluctantly agrees and follows Jenny off.

As the ship, named the Titanic, is about to embark, the captain expresses hope and confidence, given that the ship is reputed to be unsinkable. Many passengers are aboard, unaware that their final journey is imminent. Captain Smith accepts the risks posed by fire and icebergs, believing the ship is invincible. However, tragedy strikes when a seemingly minor scrape with ice leads to the sinking of the Titanic, marking a historic disaster.

Meanwhile, people in everyday life are oblivious to impending dangers, confidently claiming good health and longevity. The story shifts to a spiritual message, explaining that one day, every person will stand alone before God to be judged. Ignoring this appointment won't prevent it from happening, as stated in Hebrews 9:27. The only way to avoid eternal disaster is through Jesus Christ.

Jesus, God's Son, came to earth, proclaiming Himself as the way, the truth, and the life, with no one coming to the Father except through Him (John 14:6). He foresaw humanity's destruction from sin and the coming judgment (Ezekiel 18:20; Acts 17:31). Jesus made the ultimate sacrifice by shedding His blood to pay for all sins on a cross. Despite His death and burial, He rose again after three days and ascended to heaven (1 Corinthians 15:4; Acts 1:9). Believing in Jesus grants forgiveness of sins and eternal life in a paradise beyond imagination (Ephesians 1:7; 1 Corinthians 2:9).

The story concludes by addressing those who doubt this message, encouraging them to reconsider, as everyone will face judgment (Ecclesiastes 12:14). It offers a checklist to reflect on one's faith and encourages the reader to make a decision about salvation through Jesus Christ.

Title: Just One More
Subject: Drugs/Alcohol
Author: Chick
Responses:
Here is the written story based on the comic strip:

Byron, a man known for his lies, once begged a woman for money, claiming he was very hungry and needed it for food. She gave him five dollars. Later, Byron sought shelter in a bar, asking if he could stay the night. The bartender refused and called Byron selfish.

That night, a police officer reported a body found in an alley at 1st and Garfield. An investigation revealed it was an old man who looked like he had been run over. The man was wearing a wedding ring. The next day, a detective informed a woman named Ruth Witherspoon that her husband, Byron Witherspoon III, had died.

Ruth recalled how much she loved Byron, a great husband and father, though he was troubled by his drinking while trying to entertain clients. Their family lost everything because of his alcoholism, and it eventually cost Byron his life.

Ruth's brother spoke bitterly about how alcohol had caused such suffering in families worldwide. He condemned liquor as a malevolent force, quoting Proverbs about the danger it poses to the soul.

Despite the harm it caused, people refused to give up alcohol because they loved it, and governments and distilleries profited from it. Even the media glamorized it. No one had successfully stopped it.

In 1865 England, a man named William Booth worked in the East End, a godless slum filled with crime, drunkenness, and death. He preached the gospel amidst hostile crowds of drunks who relied on alcohol for survival. Though they mocked and pelted him, Booth persevered, determined to save their souls.

As converts increased, Booth and his "Salvation Army" sang hymns in bars and preached against alcohol. He led this fight against the "demon" drink. Another warrior in the fight was Carry Nation, a fearless woman nearly six feet tall, who carried a hatchet and smashed saloons.

After losing her husband to alcoholism, Carry joined the Woman’s Christian Temperance Union to ban liquor. She believed God wanted her to destroy saloons. Starting with stones, she escalated to using a hatchet to break bottles and fixtures.

Between 1900 and 1910, Carry was arrested 30 times but paid her fines herself. Although hated by the press, bartenders, and drunkards, she remained a determined crusader against alcohol.

Around the same time, evangelist Billy Sunday preached against liquor trafficking, calling it "the most damnable, corrupt institution." He shared the story of a poor, crippled boy who lost his mother to his drunken father’s violence. The boy supported his siblings by selling newspapers and shining shoes.

When the boy’s father was sentenced to hang, the preacher prayed with him and promised to fight the liquor industry until death. The boy’s tragic story illustrated how alcohol creates orphans.

The detective then shared his personal story of growing up with a father who fed him whiskey as a child and became a chronic alcoholic himself. Both his parents died from alcoholism, leaving him miserable and unwanted.

A stranger once spoke to him about Jesus, explaining that Jesus died for sinners and drunkards to save them from hell. Through faith in Jesus, the detective found salvation and freedom from alcohol’s grip.

He explained that believing in Jesus and receiving Him as Savior can cleanse one from sin and save the soul. Jesus Christ rose from the dead and lives, offering hope and salvation.

The detective encouraged everyone to give their lives to Jesus, who loves them and wants to save them from sin and hell. He explained how to be saved: by believing Jesus died for their sins, rose again, and receiving Him as personal Savior.

Ruth and her son gave their hearts to Jesus, securing their future with God. The detective invited anyone struggling with alcohol or sin to do the same before it’s too late.

Finally, a simple salvation prayer was provided, prompting readers to admit their sin, believe in Jesus’s sacrifice, and commit to following Him, along with space to record the date and name.

This story tells how alcohol ruined a family, how brave men and women fought against it, and how faith in Jesus Christ brings hope, healing, and salvation from the destructive power of alcohol.

Title: Just Sign Here
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Carter
Responses:
Bill was introduced to a man he was encouraged to call Jim, who told Bill that his wife loved Bill’s house and that there was an opportunity to buy it. Jim, who was in a position of authority, offered Bill a deal to buy the house with an arranged down payment, emphasizing trust between them. Bill happily agreed, feeling honored and trusting Jim.

Jim hinted there was even more benefit for Bill if he helped him out. Bill was grateful for Jim’s offer and trusted him, accepting the proposal with a sense of fraternity and loyalty.

Come Monday, Bill, fully committed, asked where to sign. Jim revealed that Bill’s new task was to act as a “Quality Control Inspector” (QCI) for a rocket contract. Bill was to sign off on paperwork approving parts without necessarily checking them fully. Though initially hesitant, Bill agreed to trust Jim and signed the documents.

Six months later, Bill and his family happily settled into their dream house. They watched the launch of a rocket from their home—a rocket Bill’s signatures had helped authorize. The rocket was meant to supply food and equipment to a space station, and its launch was declared perfect.

However, the rocket exploded in midair moments later, shocking Bill’s family and friends. A few days after the incident, two men arrived to arrest Bill, accusing him of falsifying government documents related to the failed rocket parts, which had not been properly tested.
