Despite proclaiming his innocence and claiming to be a good and honest person, Bill was confronted with the harsh reality of his actions. The arresting officer pointed out that Bill had lied and that the “Big Guy,” a reference to God, knew everything about him, even his thoughts.

Bill tried to laugh off the situation, but was seriously challenged when the officer showed him a Bible and recited verses about God’s judgment. Bill was reminded that the heart is deceitful and wicked, and honesty before God mattered beyond mere appearances or intentions.

Bill was offered a chance to make a deal, but his attempts to justify himself were contrasted with the Biblical message that just one mistake can cause great harm. The story shifted to biblical examples of individuals who disobeyed God just once and faced serious consequences. Moses, Joshua, and Adam each made singular mistakes with long-lasting impacts, showing the seriousness of sin.

In contrast, the story introduced Jesus Christ, who lived a sinless life and came to bring people to God. Though Jesus was treated unjustly, betrayed, and sentenced to die on a cross, His sacrifice was presented as the means to save people from separation from God.

Back in the present, Bill’s boss confessed and offered Bill a way out if he would write and sign a statement. Bill accepted, feeling relieved. However, Bill’s former “brother” Jim betrayed him by ratting him out to the authorities, and Bill was chased by a truck as he tried to run away.

Although Bill narrowly avoided a deadly crash, he was left in darkness, confused, and uncertain. The story ended with an angel urging Bill to believe in Jesus Christ for salvation and forgiveness. Despite Bill’s rejection of Jesus, the reader was invited to accept salvation, admit their sins, and ask Jesus for forgiveness, with a form to record this decision.

The overarching message was to trust Jesus and seek forgiveness before it’s too late, emphasizing that even one wrong choice can have serious consequences but that redemption is possible through faith.

Title: Keep The Secret
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
A baby boy was born, and the happy mother named him Joe, with Joseph being a name she found nice. She lovingly told Joe that he belonged to her, but an evil creature claimed, “She’s wrong! He's mine!” This creature wondered what Joe knew that they didn’t, what big secret he held.

The evil being swore revenge, planning to take everyone down with it if it could not have Joe. It plotted to deceive everyone into thinking God did not exist and there was no judgment, promising to get revenge. Its minions revealed they knew all of Joe’s weaknesses and had programmed his life in secret to carry out their plan.

The evil forces infiltrated Joe’s school, demanding the Bible be removed from the classroom, despite protests from a student who insisted they were God’s words. Thanks to a teacher who declared “There is no God!”, Joe never read the Bible.

At the university, Joe’s science professor misled students with lies about evolution and the universe’s origins, contradicting the Bible’s teachings that God created the heavens and the earth. Joe trusted evolution over God, becoming a “jobless party animal,” much to the dismay of his sorrowful mother.

Joe was eventually imprisoned for three years as part of the dark forces’ plan. When released, he suffered a brain tumor and only believed in drinking and drugs. Meanwhile, Joe’s mother was devastated, believing her world was ruined and headed for hell.

The comic explained that Satan controls the world's system and hates everyone born in his kingdom. When people believe Satan's lies, they live under his control. The story urged that Jesus is the Son of God, who shed His blood to wash away sins. Jesus rose from the dead three days later, offering eternal life to those who believe in Him.

Charlene, Joe’s mother, was born again after praying and believing in Jesus. She felt free and alive, saved from Satan’s kingdom to God’s kingdom. She received the promise of a mansion in heaven, her name recorded in the book of life, symbolizing God saving her.

Though Satan was furious and plotted to use Joe to attack Charlene, Charlene read the Bible and found strength through God’s word. One day, Charlene shared the good news with Joe, telling him she was saved. Joe initially refused, rejecting Jesus.

The story showed Joe’s continued resistance to God, proclaiming he did not want to hear about Jesus and needing his pain meds. Tragically, Joe died, his soul fully awake and faced with truth, prompting the question: was Mama right?

The comic ended with a stark choice between Jesus Christ and Satan. It invited readers to choose Jesus by believing in Him, accepting Him into their hearts, and receiving God’s gift of eternal life, warning that rejecting this gift meant losing out on salvation.

The story portrayed a spiritual battle over Joe’s soul, highlighting themes of faith, redemption, and the power of belief in Jesus Christ.

Title: Kidnapped!
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Carter
Responses:
The story begins with a police officer named Carter being informed about yet another incident involving a young girl. The girl is nine years old and was taken on her way home from school. Carter learns that the case involves a ring from Saudi Arabia, likely connected to the trafficking of children. His heart goes out to the poor little kids, and he hopes to bring the perpetrators to justice.

On a Sunday morning, a young girl named Holly introduces her friend Donna to Mrs. Comfort, who wants to teach Donna about Jesus. Holly shares that she believes she is saved and going to heaven and wishes the same for Donna. Donna listens as Holly explains how the Ten Commandments scared her, especially since she lies often and fears not being worthy of heaven. Holly confirms that everything said is recorded and that no liar shall enter heaven.

Mrs. Comfort tells Donna that only Jesus can save her by wiping away every lie and sin. Donna is amazed and curious about how Jesus can do that. Mrs. Comfort explains that Jesus, being God Almighty, shed His blood and died but rose from the dead and is now in heaven, coming back soon. Donna is encouraged to ask Jesus for forgiveness and to accept Him as her Savior, which she does, crying and asking for Jesus to save her. She is now on her way to heaven, her record wiped clean.

Meanwhile, police officers respond to a domestic disturbance call. Carter takes the case and prays for help, uncertain about what he will face. At the scene, children inside the house call for help, revealing a violent conflict upstairs. Carter crashes through the door to stop the abuser hurting his mother.

After the event, Donna thanks Mrs. Comfort, saying it was the best day ever because she is now saved. Holly offers her a ride home, but Donna prefers to walk. Elsewhere, a man with sinister intent watches a young girl who is seemingly alone, thinking he will use a "missing kitty" trick to lure her. He plans to take her away on a long trip.

In the house, the domestic violence incident escalates until the police stop the abuser. The distressed woman pleads for help, and the officer warns them about the consequences and urges them to go back to church and change their ways. The couple admits they drifted from God and replaced Him with television. They repent and ask for forgiveness.

The man tries to lure the young girl by asking about a missing cat and claims there are kittens in his car trunk. When the girl shows interest, he traps her in the trunk, lying about the kittens. The officer arrives and, after the children pound on the trunk and plead for help, orders him to open it. He rescues the girl, who prays and thanks God for answering her prayers.

As the story closes, the officer reflects on the power of faith in God, while the man who tried to kidnap the girl is caught, facing justice. The comic ends with a note that God sees all and listens to prayers, highlighting a moral about faith, forgiveness, and the fight against evil.

Title: Killer Storm
Subject: Bible Stories
Author: Carter & 3rd
Responses:
During World War I, a Russian pilot named Sergi flew over Mt. Ararat at about 14,000 feet. From the air, he spotted what he thought was a submarine. Eager to confirm his sighting, Sergi hurried back to base, where the captain demanded to see what he had found immediately. Sergi revealed what he saw—an enormous structure that appeared to be Noah's Ark. The captain exclaimed that this could be the most important discovery of the age.

News of the discovery reached Czar Nicholas of Russia, lighting up the palace with excitement. He ordered a scientific and military expedition to search for the ark. At the base camp near Mt. Ararat, the mission to find Noah's Ark began. A newcomer asked what Noah was, and another explained the biblical story.

According to Genesis 5-9, a man named Enoch had a son, Methuselah. God decided to destroy the earth in the year Methuselah died because mankind was totally corrupted, and violence was everywhere. God was fed up. God only trusted one man—Noah, who was just and perfect in his generation and walked with God. God decided to save Noah and his family from the coming disaster and instructed Noah to build an ark.

The ark was to be 300 cubits long, 50 cubits wide, and 30 cubits high, with three decks. A cubit, about 18 inches from elbow to fingertip, meant the ark was roughly 450 feet long, about the size of a World War II escort aircraft carrier. The ark weighed about 34,000 tons, making it the biggest wooden ship ever built.

Building the ark took many years. People from far and wide came to watch and laugh at Noah. It was difficult for Noah since it had never rained before; God had watered the earth with a mist. Despite the ridicule, Noah warned people for years to turn from their wicked ways, but no one listened. Exhausted and disregarded, Noah persisted in his faith.

God was so longsuffering that He let Methuselah live to 969 years old. At his death, no one imagined what was about to happen. Noah then gathered two of every kind of animal, both male and female, into the ark. God also told Noah how much food to bring. The animals entered, and people watched, unaware of the impending disaster.

Then, God ordered Noah and his family into the ark. The people mocked them as rain started just seven days later. Suddenly, dark clouds gathered, thunder roared, and flashes of lightning illuminated the sky. Fear gripped the people as the rain began to fall heavily. Noah had been right all along.

After years of warning, God's judgment finally struck. The fountains of the great deep broke up, and the windows of heaven opened, causing rain to pour for forty days and forty nights. Every living being on land that had the breath of life died. Only Noah and those with him in the ark survived.

When the flood ended, the ark settled on Mt. Ararat, and all inside were safe. God made a rainbow as a promise never to destroy the earth again by water. The Russian soldiers scaled Mt. Ararat in two columns. One was stopped by a swamp filled with deadly snakes and insects, forcing them to turn back. The others reached the ark and stood in awe, recognizing it as Noah’s ark and confirming the Bible story was true. The ark measured about 500 feet long, with the entire back end encased in ice.

Inside, the ark contained rooms with cages from floor to ceiling, coated with a dark brown substance like varnish—pitch—just as the Bible had described. Documents proving the ark's existence were handed to a Russian soldier to deliver to the Czar. Unfortunately, upon reaching Moscow, he was captured by the Communists. Rumor says he was shot, and the documents fell into the hands of Trotsky, the Communist leader, after which all the documents disappeared.

The story ties to Jesus Christ, the Creator who sent the flood, who came to earth as a baby. Thirty-three years later, Jesus warned of a judgment worse than the flood, saying that billions would die from famine, plague, and war, and one-third of the earth would burn up.

To be spared such judgment, one must believe that Jesus shed His blood for sins and rose from the dead. Accepting Him as Savior makes Him your personal ark of safety. His promise is "The Blessed Hope," when the Lord Jesus will return, and the dead in Christ will rise first.

Then those alive will be caught up with them in the clouds to meet the Lord, and they will be with Him forever. Just as the ark saved Noah and spared him from judgment, Jesus will save and spare those who trust in Him.

So, just as Noah escaped judgment by trusting God's command, you can be saved by placing your faith in Jesus Christ.

Title: Kitty In The Window
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
Mark stood at his window, staring in disbelief as snowflakes swirled outside. “It can’t be snowing! We were promised sunshine!” he exclaimed, frustration tightening his voice. “I hate that lying weatherman. It’s all his fault!” Nearby, his mother watched him cautiously and instructed, “Mark, cover your mouth when you cough.” Mark obliged with a grumble, “Ok, Mom!” Meanwhile, his sister Claire urged, “Please see a doctor.” Mark waved her off, “Shut up, Claire! I’m fine.” His coughing persisted nonetheless.

Mark’s mother questioned him sternly, “You’re not going out tract passing in that blizzard, are you?” Mark responded nonchalantly, “It’s Saturday, Mom. It’s what I do.” His mother smiled wryly, “Is little Sister trying to be a missionary like our Grandpa and Grandma?” Mark sneered, “Well, this isn’t the African Congo, Claire! But I suppose God told you to do it, right?” Claire earnestly replied, “Yes! He says ‘Go ye into all the world, and preach the gospel to every creature.’” (Mark 16:15)

Mark snapped at Claire, “You embarrass me! I wouldn’t be caught dead passing out a gospel tract. They can all go to hell for all I care! Besides, giving out religion is the pastor’s job, not yours.” Claire quietly said, “I do my religious act when Mom begs me to go to church. I even throw a dollar in the plate to pay for the show.” Mark scoffed, “So, I’m a phony, just like everybody else.” Mom added softly, “God sees that, Mark.”

Mark harshly ordered Claire to stop praying for him, “Just shut up, Claire! I don’t want to hear it anymore. Go! Freeze to death. I’m going back to bed. You’re making me sick.” Meanwhile, Claire bundled up and went outside, determined to pass out tracts despite the blizzard.

Claire approached an elderly woman on her porch. “May I give you a gospel tract, sir?” Claire asked politely. The woman smiled, “Well, thank you, young lady!” Nearby, two women gossiped, “Happy 83rd birthday, Lizzy. You look like an old hag.” Lizzy replied sadly, “What happened to those good looks? The years made them fly away.”

Inside, Lizzy confided sorrowfully, “When Walter died, I lost everything. I’m all alone. No friends. I hurt everywhere. After that devil stole my social security check, I’m broke. I wish I was dead!” She set out a rope and ladder, intent on ending her life. “Here’s the rope. And there’s the ladder,” she murmured. “This is my last tract, Lord. Shall I ring this doorbell?” A voice in her heart answered, “YES.”

She rang the doorbell, but no one answered. “If I don’t answer, they’ll go away,” she muttered, but more ringing followed. “Now they’re knocking!” she gasped. “Stop it! You’re ruining everything!” she raged at the unseen visitors. Peering in the window, she spotted a kitty and smiled, “I guess nobody’s home. But there’s a kitty in the window. Hi, kitty! For you, I’ll try one more time.”

Finally, a young woman answered. Exhausted, Claire said, “Whew! My arm is tired. Sorry, Lord, I did my best.” “Hello! What do you want?” Lizzy asked. Claire gently shared, “I want to give you a little present.” Lizzy frowned, “Why?” Claire smiled, “It’s about how much God loves you, and what Jesus did for you to save your soul from going to hell!”

Lizzy took the tract hesitantly, “From hell? I’ll read it! It’s a love story. Hi, I’m Claire Wilson. My phone number’s on the back. Call me, OK? Bye, and may God bless you.” That very moment, Mark grew pale and nauseous. “What’s wrong, Mark? You’re really pale.” Mom urged, “Better go back to bed.” “I’m really sick, Mom. I think I’m going to throw up.”

Lizzy read the tract aloud, “Jesus is God? No one ever told me this stuff. Oh oh... I’m in trouble.” Reaching for the phone, she called Claire. “Claire, why is there a hell?” she inquired. Claire explained, “That’s God’s judgment of sin. Man could never do enough to pay for his sins. He’s too rotten. So God prepared a love gift for them, to pay the price for their crimes. Jesus is God’s love gift, Lizzy. He paid the price for your sins by shedding His blood, God’s blood, on the cross.” (Acts 20:28, John 3:16) Three days later He walked from the grave, granting eternal life to those who believe.

Lizzy prayed with Claire, asking Jesus into her heart and accepting Him as Savior. Meanwhile, Mark was terrified. “Nurse, get them away from me!” he cried out in fear. “Who?” they asked, puzzled. “Don’t you see them?” Mark screamed.

Doctors noted Mark’s vitals were normal but he was screaming horrible things: “They’re coming for me! I’m beginning to burn! I’m in hell!” Then, suddenly, he stopped. All grew silent. Mark’s soul had instantly been cast into hell to face God’s wrath.

In hell, a demon sneered, “You’re in the pit of the damned. You wouldn’t let Jesus pay for your sins. Now, you get to pay! You, Mark Wilson, are a fool. A damned fool! Set him on fire!” The future awaited Mark as the lake of fire, the second death. (Revelation 20:14)

Back on earth, Lizzy reflected, “Nobody ever told me about Jesus. I thought I’d just die and it was over. I didn’t know about being judged after death. I should read that little book again.” She realized that everyone she knew who died without Jesus was in hell. She cried out to Claire.

Lizzy asked Claire questions, seeking understanding. Claire explained that God’s wrath was kindled because man rejected God’s love gift. For refusing His gift, they would pay for their sins in hell forever. (2 Thessalonians 2:12)

Claire encouraged, “If you believe Jesus died for your sins and receive Him as Savior, your sins are washed away forever. You become a child of God, never to go to hell.” (Acts 16:31)

Mark recovered in the hospital. “I’m too mean to die.” “Mark, you scared us,” Claire said gently. Mark admitted, “I pretended to get saved to make Mom happy. To me, it’s all baloney.”

Lizzy held up the gospel tract Claire gave her. “If Claire hadn’t come and given me this little tract, I’d be in hell screaming right now!” she said.

The story ends with a call to faith, inviting readers to accept Jesus as Savior and avoid eternal damnation.

Title: Kura's Ants
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Carter
Responses:
Kura loved watching his ants. They were always busy and active, and he considered them his little friends. He enjoyed observing their every move, fascinated by their tiny lives.

One day, a boy told Kura and Sarah that the land where the ants lived would soon be flooded and turned into a lake. Kura was horrified. "Oh no! My ants!" he cried. Feeling a sense of urgency, he decided he had to warn the ants about the impending danger. Kura tried desperately to communicate with them, shouting and gesturing, urging them to move to higher ground. He pleaded, "I'm trying to save you! How can I make you see... you're all gonna die!" But, of course, the ants couldn't understand him.

Sarah approached Kura with a thoughtful look and asked if she could use his ants to teach him something important. She explained that the only way Kura could truly warn the ants was if he became an ant himself. She challenged him, asking if he would be willing to give up everything — his human life, grow six legs, live under the dirt — all for the ants. Kura grimaced, admitting he didn't love the ants that much and didn't think anyone ever loved that much.

Sarah then suggested a scenario: what if Kura tried to warn the ants but they didn’t believe him? They’d likely be mad at him for speaking of doom and might even kill him. She asked if he’d be willing to give his life for those ants. Kura firmly said no.

Sarah smiled and said Kura was wrong. She knew somebody with far more love than that — God. God loves everyone in the world because He created them, including Kura and his ants. She explained that God made everything but a long time ago, humankind was in trouble — even worse trouble than the ants. It started when Adam and Eve disobeyed God. Their sin was passed down to everyone, and as a result, all deserve to go to hell because "for the wages of sin is death."

Yet, God loved people and didn’t want them to go to hell. Kura asked how God could save them from such a fate. Sarah explained that God the Father sent God the Son, Jesus, from heaven to earth to be born as a man. Jesus lived among people, warning them about hell, and taught them to love God and each other. But most people rejected His message because it was hard to hear and accept.

Sarah told Kura that the main reason Jesus came was to pay a terrible price to take away the sins of humans. Though arrested and hurt badly, Jesus freely gave His life for everyone. He died, was buried, and three days later rose from the dead. This greatest act of love offered salvation to all who believe.

Kura was amazed. "God did ALL THAT for us?" he asked. Sarah affirmed it and told him that Jesus then returned to heaven to prepare beautiful homes for those saved, where they will live forever.

Eager to know if he was saved, Kura asked Sarah if he was. She said no — only those who received Jesus by faith are saved. Kura wanted to go to heaven along with Sarah and the boy.

Sarah then told Kura he must believe that Jesus died on the cross for him and ask Jesus to forgive his sins and come into his heart as his personal Savior. They all prayed together, and afterward, Kura felt great. Sarah told him that Jesus was now his best friend who would always be with him to help him.

Filled with joy, Kura promised to tell everybody about Jesus. Together with Sarah and the boy, they went out sharing this greatest love story — that Jesus can save anyone who believes in Him.

Finally, Kura asked if the reader was saved. If not, he urged them to ask Jesus to be their Savior right now, promising eternal life through faith in Him.

Title: Last Generation, The
Subject: End Time Prophecy
Author: Carter
Responses:
In the near future, the world is shaken by a dramatic announcement from the World Court headquarters in Rome. Supreme Justice Mahoney addresses the global audience with a grim declaration: anyone who claims that Jesus Christ is the only way to the Father in Heaven will face severe consequences. Those holding this belief will be sent to mental treatment camps or face execution. Additionally, all who oppose this law are declared enemies of the state.

In a family home, a father speaks to his daughter, Connie, reassuring her that, regardless of the challenges ahead, they will soon be moving to their mansions in heaven. He reminds them that they have everything to gain and nothing to lose, citing Philippians 1:21 about living for Christ and the gain in dying with Him. They discuss the signs of their times—persecution, diseases, earthquakes, and wars—which might indicate they are the last generation. The father reads from Romans 8:18, encouraging hope despite suffering, and expresses his joy and readiness to meet Jesus face to face.

However, the darker the world grows, the brighter their hope becomes. Yet, on the street, a boy named Bobby faces cruelty from others who mock him for his parents’ faith and marriage. Bobby shares that his teacher called certain animals great for a Halloween sacrifice, revealing an occult influence at school. He is warned about a "Mother Goddess" and learns that those opposing these beliefs could be reported and persecuted. His peers betray one another, encouraged by authorities offering rewards for turning in those labeled as "sickos" or heretics.

As Bobby’s father tries to comfort him with the truth of Jesus Christ as the Creator and Savior who shed His blood for sins, Bobby reacts with hatred and rebellion. His family is torn apart: his parents plan to send Connie and her brother Paul to safety, while Bobby faces being taken to a mental camp. The camp is cruel and torturous; microchips are implanted to increase pain for those who hold to their Christian faith. The story follows the siblings as they escape and struggle to survive.

Soon, the fateful moment arrives—the Rapture—when all believers are taken up to heaven. As chaos ensues on earth, those left behind face terrifying tribulations under a one-world dictator and plagues. The story concludes with a call to faith, emphasizing the importance of believing in Jesus for forgiveness of sins to be ready for this "Blessed Hope." It warns against rejecting Christ like Bobby and urges readers to trust in Jesus and pray for salvation, ending with Jesus’ own words about being the only way to the Father.

Title: Last Judge, The
Subject: Bible Stories
Author: Chick
Responses:
Bob was working on an electronic device when Kelly walked in and told him that he had finally got it working. Bob replied modestly, calling it a piece of cake. Just then, Uncle George arrived, and Kelly introduced Bob to him. Uncle George asked Bob if he was a "computer man," and Bob replied he wasn't doing too badly.

Uncle George, with an eye patch, shared that he used to be a judge, a tough and honest one, until he had an accident. Bob and Kelly were sorry about the accident, and Uncle George invited them to join him for coffee. Kelly spoke highly of Uncle George, saying he was an honest judge respected by lawyers and feared by criminals. Bob said he only knew one judge like that.

Bob began to share a story from history. He said that over 1,000 years before Christ, Israel was judged by a man named Eli, who was also a high priest. Eli had two rotten sons who were completely out of control and polluted everything they touched, but Eli did nothing to stop them. One day, Eli saw a woman praying and crying. She told God that if He would allow her to have a son, she would give that son to the Lord. She named the boy Samuel, and Eli had no idea what God was going to do with him.

God stopped talking to Eli because of his sons but began talking to the child Samuel instead. When Samuel was young, God warned him that because of his sons' sins, He would judge Eli and his children forever. Samuel grew, and the Lord was with him; none of his words fell to the ground. Samuel became the judge of Israel.

During a long war, Israel was losing. Their most holy treasure, the Ark of the Covenant, was taken into battle with them, but Eli’s two sons—whom God hated—carried the ark. The Philistines defeated Israel, slaughtered 30,000 Israelites, and captured the Ark. Upon hearing this tragic news, Eli fell backward, broke his neck, and died.

The children of Israel became tired of having a judge and demanded a king like everyone else. God warned Samuel that a king would take their sons, daughters, servants, and property, leading to hardship. But the people wanted a king regardless. Their first king was Saul. At first, Saul was shy and listened to God, but after two years, he became arrogant and took upon himself to do things he shouldn’t, like making a burnt offering to God without waiting for Samuel.

Saul’s fatal mistake was disobeying God's command to destroy everything in the city of Amalek. Saul and his 210,000 soldiers wiped out the Amalekites but spared some possessions and livestock. Samuel confronted Saul, telling him that he had rejected God’s word, and because of this, God had rejected him as king. God then chose David to be the future king, and the spirit of the Lord left Saul and came upon David.

Saul faced many problems alone, including a giant Philistine warrior named Goliath, who terrified Saul’s soldiers. But young David rose to fight Goliath and defeated him with God’s help. Although David loved Saul, the king grew to hate him.

Samuel ruled Israel righteously for 40 years, never accepting bribes or letting people influence his decisions because he knew one day he would face the greatest Judge of all. Samuel died, and all Israel mourned him.

Bob then explained that one day this greatest Judge would sit on His throne and judge the whole world. Everyone, rich or poor, powerful or weak, will stand before Him. The Bible says that everything people have done will be made known, even their most secret thoughts.

Then comes the most important question: Is your name written in the book of life? If not, what happens?

The Judge will say, "Depart from me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels." This Judge is Jesus Christ—resurrected and very much alive.

Bob confessed that he hadn’t been perfect, and Uncle George said that meant he was in trouble because all have sinned and fall short of God’s glory. Bob asked if there was any way to escape this sentence. The answer was yes: Jesus Christ, who was executed for sins and rose again, offers salvation to those who believe.

Jesus is in heaven now, defending us against the Devil. He can be either our Savior or the toughest Judge we will ever face.

Bob realized that if he didn't give his life to Jesus, he was a guilty sinner facing eternal punishment. Uncle George told him to confess his sins in prayer, ask Jesus to forgive him, come into his heart, and be saved. Bob agreed.

That evening, Bob thanked Jesus, grateful that instead of being condemned forever, he was saved. Uncle George said the experience of one day standing before God is a sobering reminder not to wait.

The story ended with a strong call: Don't let this happen to you. Receive the Lord Jesus as your Savior today.

Title: Last Rites
Subject: Catholicism
Author: Chick
Responses:
John and Hazel were driving in heavy rain when Hazel angrily accused John of missing a turn, calling him an idiot. John shouted back for Hazel to shut up. Hazel retaliated by telling John not to tell her to be quiet and accused Henry of emotional abuse. The tension escalated, with Hazel calling John a male chauvinist pig and saying marrying him was the biggest mistake of her life. In response, John told Hazel to zip it because he needed to think. As their argument continued, John suddenly shouted a warning to Hazel to look out.

In an instant, the car screeched, and Hazel was thrown out with a thud. Emergency responders arrived and rushed John to the hospital. Despite their efforts, John’s condition was critical. Forty minutes later, a priest asked if John had made a good confession, to which the nurse responded yes, implying John would die soon. The priest reassured those gathered that John had received Last Rites and had been forgiven for all his sins. The community mourned John Sullivan, a devoted parishioner who had even met the pope, calling his passing a terrible loss.

John then faced the Lord but quickly realized his assumption that he was ready for heaven was a mistake. He found himself in purgatory after a stay, but when his name was not found in the Book of Life, John was confronted with the terrifying words of condemnation telling him to depart into everlasting fire.

John pleaded with the Lord, insisting he had spent his life doing good works. The Lord explained that salvation is by grace through faith and not by works. John tried to justify praying to the Virgin Mary, like the pope, but the Lord called this idolatry, which barred entry to heaven.

When John mentioned attending Mass twice a week and being an altar boy, the Lord challenged him to find scriptural support for Mass, which John could not. The Lord stated the Mass was a lie and that Jesus’ sacrifice on the cross was finished—there was no ongoing sacrifice.

John argued his baptism cleaned his original sin, but the Lord clarified the truth, saying John misunderstood his catechism. He had placed faith in teachings rather than God’s Word. John falsely believed confessing sins to Father Damien had granted forgiveness. The Lord declared no man can forgive sins, only He can.

Realizing he had been deceived like millions of other Catholics, John expressed horror and questioned why God had not warned him. The Lord told John that a servant had warned him with a tract explaining the truth, but John dismissed it as hate literature and trusted his priests instead.

The tract John rejected quoted Scripture, assuring believers that they may know they have eternal life through faith in Jesus Christ. It explained that salvation is only through Jesus and that the Roman Catholic Church wanted to keep people serving the church rather than trusting Christ.

John admitted he was upset by the tract because he loved the Catholic Church. The Lord told him her false teachings were the reason for his damnation and warned him sharply to come out of her people. John desperately asked if he could still receive Jesus and be saved. The Lord said it was too late for him, only those still living could be saved.

Back at the funeral, the priest proclaimed John was now enjoying the rewards of serving the one true church and urged others to join him. The story ended admonishing readers not to end up like John but to put their trust in Christ alone for salvation, praying for forgiveness and accepting eternal life as a personal gift.

Title: Last Surprise, The
Subject: Hell
Author: Chick
Responses:
The story begins with a woman presenting a check for $35,000 to a pastor. It came from Frances Goodman, who requests a phone call. Frances's donation is intended to recarpet the entire church, which the pastor appreciates as generous.

Later, Frances visits the pastor and insists he change the carpet color to one her late husband Earl had preferred. Saying Earl always knew best, she exerts influence over the pastor. They reminisce about their long history with the church and how things have changed since Earl’s time, marking the new pastor's tenure with tension.

Frances tells the pastor she was insulted by the youth pastor who asked if she was "saved." She demands the new youth pastor be fired, despite the fact his wife was recently diagnosed with cancer. The pastor agrees to handle it.

The next day, the new youth pastor, Glen, defends his work with the youth group, who have now turned away from drugs and are seeking God. But the pastor sides with Frances and shuts down the issue. Glen leaves the church.

Later, church members mourn Glen's departure, shocked and saddened by what happened. The pastor himself questions how it unfolded, pointing to Frances's controlling influence through her money.

Then the pastor becomes very ill and passes away suddenly. Frances visits the hospital demanding answers and slams the hospital staff. Three days later, Frances arrives at the hospital insisting on visiting her brother, the late pastor, who is in intensive care. The hospital staff limit her visitation.

Two months later, Frances demands to help choose the new pastor’s sermon topics and retracts her donation, saying the old carpet is fine. She criticizes the new pastor, Glenn Benson, calling him offensive and unacceptable.

Pastor Benson starts preaching about hell, something the congregation is unaccustomed to hearing. He recounts how, as a missionary, he encountered people who worshipped devils and sacrificed babies to Satan. He preached the truth and won many to Christ despite the spiritual battles. 

Benson explains that after death, souls go to heaven or hell. He describes the horrors of hell—eternal torment, fire, and darkness—and the importance of accepting Jesus to avoid this fate. His sermon shocks Frances and others. She finds the topic dangerous and offensive.

Despite warnings in the Bible, most pastors avoid preaching on hell, fearing they will lose their congregations. Pastor Benson’s bold message causes upset in the church, especially from Frances, who resents his directness.

Soon after, Frances, driving in anger, runs a red light and crashes her car. She is taken to the hospital by ambulance, where staff comment on the strange smell of rotting eggs around her, a metaphor for spiritual decay.

The story ends with the choice laid out plainly: heaven or hell. The message emphasizes that believing in Jesus saves souls from hell, leaving each person to choose their eternal path.

Title: Let's Fly Away!
Subject: Rapture
Author: Chick
Responses:
At 8:00 AM, people at a factory noticed important executives arriving. Workers speculated it might be for a big meeting. Suddenly, Greg was called into the office by a superior, and he worried he might be in trouble.

Inside, the chief broke bad news to Greg—he was being fired. Greg was shocked and pleaded, pointing to his 17 years at the company and questions about his retirement money. The chief explained the company was closing down completely, and everyone was getting pink slips.

Outside, workers were told they had just 30 minutes to pack up and leave. Greg worried about what to tell his wife and how they would manage financially. When Greg reached home by 9:30 AM, his wife Delores was surprised to see him back so early. Greg predicted a rough day ahead and advised her to get another bottle.

Delores expressed her fears about losing their house, car, and even their daughter Julie’s braces. Greg insisted it wasn’t his fault, blaming the factory shutdowns caused by new regulations. He warned that the whole country was in trouble. Delores tried to calm him down by comparing their situation to their neighbor Herb’s, who had lost his job, was facing foreclosure, and had become depressed.

Suddenly, a gunshot rang out. Greg confirmed to Delores that it was a gunshot, and soon they learned that Herb had shot himself. Neighbors discussed Herb's troubles, his family leaving, and how the community had failed to help him. Some ostracized Herb even after his death.

Four months later, Julie noticed new neighbors moving in, including a little girl named Karen. While Delores didn’t want Julie to befriend these newcomers, Julie introduced herself to Karen and they quickly became friends.

However, Greg struggled, visiting the Employment Development Department, lamenting how they couldn’t survive without a job. Unemployment had soared to 23%, and the family faced hunger and hardship. Julie’s behavior became difficult, but Karen’s mother was kind and offered help.

One day, Julie heard Karen singing a hymn about flying away after death and thanking Jesus. Julie wondered who Jesus was, noting that she only heard the name when her parents fought. Karen’s mother patiently explained that Jesus is God’s holy Son, who saves people from their sins.

Julie learned that everyone has sinned, meaning they do bad things that separate them from God, and only Jesus could fix that. Despite her doubts, Karen’s mother explained how God knew Julie was in danger because of sin, and only those without sin—Jesus—could save her.

Karen’s mother detailed how Jesus came to Earth as a baby, lived perfectly, and paid the price for everyone’s sins through His death. Jesus was tortured and crucified but rose from the dead three days later, offering eternal life to those who believe in Him.

After hearing this, Julie prayed and accepted Jesus into her heart. She felt joy and wanted to share what she had learned with Karen. Karen shared a wonderful hope with Julie—that Jesus would return one day to take believers to heaven. This gave Julie comfort and a reason to sing.

However, back home, Greg reacted badly to Julie mentioning Jesus. He forbade her from seeing Karen again, accusing the religious influence of making her crazy and threatening to get a doctor for her. That night, Julie sang and prayed, unafraid despite her father’s anger.

She continued to joyfully sing about flying away to be with Jesus. Greg was startled when Julie suddenly disappeared from her bed "in the twinkling of an eye," symbolizing the hope of believers being taken to heaven.

The story illustrates a family’s struggle during economic hardship and how faith in Jesus brought hope and salvation to a young girl amidst turmoil and disbelief at home.

Title: Letter, The
Subject: For Christians
Author: Carter
Responses:
Mildred encountered a man who approached her, offering a small book to read because he was concerned about her soul. She refused sharply, finding his method offensive and resented what she saw as an imposition. She declared herself a Christian and criticized the man for cheapening the gospel and being fanatical. She was adamant that she lived rightly and scorned attempts to "cram" religion down people's throats. 

Later, Mildred fell asleep and had a strange, vivid dream. It started in the realms of the damned, where souls punished for their sins dwelled. In this dream, a tortured soul had written a letter and requested that it be delivered to someone still living. Two messengers were dispatched to carry this letter through the terrifying caverns of the lost, passing through nightmarish sights and horrific sounds, places warned of in the Bible. 

The messengers journeyed past countless souls who had rejected God's gift of eternal life and were doomed to eternal darkness, weeping and suffering. Eventually, the messengers reached the entrance to the living world—the final destination of this dreadful letter. One messenger stayed at the gate while the other proceeded to deliver the letter.

In her dream, Mildred envisioned a phone call from a grateful church pastor thanking her for her generous donation. Then, she was abruptly awakened by the presence of the messenger from the damned, who announced himself and presented the letter meant for her. The letter frightened Mildred, who initially believed she had been dreaming poorly or that the letter was a product of her imagination. 

Yet, as she read, the letter revealed a somber truth. It was from a friend named Frances, who stood in judgment and blamed Mildred for never sharing her faith. Frances lamented that despite knowing the Lord, Mildred had never told her the gospel story or about Jesus' salvation. The letter accused Mildred of failing to guide her friend toward eternal life, resulting in Frances' condemnation and eternal separation from God.

Frances' words stung as she described how they lived together, shared life, and yet Mildred never told her about her "second birth," the salvation in Jesus. Frances felt betrayed and abandoned in her final judgment because of this silence. The letter described the darkness and torment Frances now faced.

Mildred was shaken awake by the nightmare and felt deeply disturbed. She prayed fervently, vowing that she would not let her friend Frances suffer such a fate. Even if it cost their friendship, Mildred promised to tell Frances about Jesus—His birth, death, resurrection, and the gift of eternal life.

She resolved to call Frances soon and share the gospel, hoping that her friend would accept Jesus as her Savior and Lord, and that they would both meet again in heaven.

Monday night came, and Mildred called Frances. She was met with tragic news: Frances had died instantly in a car accident days earlier, while John, another friend, survived. Mildred was overwhelmed with grief and regret, having missed the opportunity to share the message that could have saved Frances. The dream and the tragic reality combined to deliver a powerful warning to her—and to all who heard her story—about the urgency of sharing one’s faith before it is too late.

Title: Li'l Susy
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Carter
Responses:
Susy was sitting quietly when Cathy approached her and asked if she was waiting for her mom. Susy replied sadly that she didn’t have a mom. Cathy, curious, asked if Susy’s mom had left home, to which Susy explained that her mom had died when she was born. Cathy, feeling sympathy, asked if her parents were divorced like hers, but Susy said no, her mom loved her very much.

Cathy then asked about Susy's dad, and Susy revealed that her dad had died of a heart attack last year. When Cathy inquired who was taking care of her, Susy said it was her grandpa. Cathy said she still had her daddy, but Susy sadly shared she didn’t have a daddy either because he had run away to marry another lady. Although Cathy asked if he talked to Susy, Susy tearfully explained that he hated them and didn’t want anything to do with them. Susy’s mom and she cried a lot because of that.

Susy explained that when her daddy died, she cried until her grandpa taught her how to get a new father. Cathy was shocked and wanted to know more. Susy told her that she was very happy with this new father who loved her and watched over her. Cathy wished she could have that too, and Susy said she would show her how because this new father was also her grandpa’s father.

Susy clarified that this new father lived in heaven and loved them very much, but there was only one way to meet him. Cathy was eager to hear more, so Susy began to tell her a story about God.

Susy explained that God did something special for Cathy. God sent His Son from heaven to be born as a baby through a virgin mother. The baby, named Jesus, grew up without ever doing anything wrong or sinning because He was God.

Cathy didn’t understand what sin was, so Susy explained it as the naughty things people do, like being mean and not believing or obeying God. Susy mentioned that her dad sinned when he left them and married another lady. Cathy admitted she lied a lot, so Susy told her that God knows everything, including their sins, and the Bible says no liar will enter heaven.

Saddened, Cathy asked how she could get rid of her sins. Susy responded that only Jesus could fix that. She then told Cathy about how Jesus came to earth, was arrested, beaten, and nailed to a cross because He told people He was God’s Son. Jesus shed His blood to wash away their sins, and even though He died on the cross, He came back to life three days later. This resurrection defeated the devil.

Jesus said He was the way, the truth, and the life, and no one can reach God except through Him. When Cathy asked what that meant, Susy explained that if you ask Jesus to save you, become sorry for your sins, and believe in Him, you become God's child.

Cathy eagerly asked what she needed to do, and Susy led her in a prayer to ask Jesus for forgiveness and to come into her life. After praying, Cathy felt wonderful and clean, and Susy told her that Jesus had come into her heart and she was now part of God's family.

Susy reassured Cathy that her Father in heaven would never leave her, and Jesus had given her everlasting life. Cathy was no longer going to hell because her sins were gone; she was on her way to heaven with Susy. Together, they realized they now had the same Daddy in heaven and were sisters. They expressed their love for each other, feeling happy and blessed.

The story ends by quoting John 3:16, underscoring God's love for everyone and the promise of eternal life for those who believe in Jesus.

Title: Limited Time Offer
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Carter
Responses:
A woman, while driving, spots a sale and excitedly demands her driver to stop the car. They rush to a store that’s closing down, filled with signs reading “Seal the Deal”, “Final Days”, and “It's Now or Never!” The woman, eager, claims that they might have something she wants, while the man reminds her that his wallet hasn't recovered from the last "I want."

They argue playfully, with the woman pointing out that he's saving her money, while the man suggests that saving him more will leave him broke. Inside the store, the woman admires some dolls saying the grandkids would love them, while two men discuss how the woman is easily tricked by sales tactics like price jacking and "limited time offers."

One man introduces a serious topic, telling the other that one day Jesus will return to "judge the world in righteousness" and offers a limited time to get ready. He invites the skeptical man, Joe, to listen. Joe eventually joins the conversation, where the man explains that religious fire isn't meant for him, but God had better plans from the beginning, using Adam and Eve as an example.

The story describes how God gave Adam and Eve everything but prohibited them from eating the fruit from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, warning that eating it would bring death that day. But the Devil, in the form of a serpent, tried to deceive them by saying they would be like gods if they ate the fruit. Eve, then Adam, disobeyed, and it cost them greatly. They broke the only command from God, and consequences followed.

God killed two animals and made coats of skins to clothe them, symbolizing substitutionary punishment. Sin entered the world, paradise was lost, and things took a downward turn.

The man continues, explaining God had a plan for salvation because no animal or human could pay the price for sins. Jesus came to earth and lived a perfect life without sin. He died on a cross, taking humanity's curse upon Himself, paying for all sin, showing the ultimate act of love.

The couple wrestles with these ideas, with the man dismissing religion as old-fashioned. The other man warns that everyone will face judgment, and the offer to be saved won't last forever. The skeptic argues about being judged by the balance of good and bad deeds and concludes he would go to hell. However, the man explains that those not found in the book of life will face the lake of fire, and no one escapes God's judgment.

Jesus tasted death for everyone, so no one needs to be punished if they receive His gift through faith. Trusting Jesus, not trying to save oneself by deeds, is the key. The skeptic learns that anyone who admits they are a sinner and trusts Jesus can be forgiven.

The invitation is urgent, as the offer is limited. The skeptic is ready, surprised by how simple it is, but must go. As he leaves, the woman hurries away with her cart full of purchases.

Suddenly, a runaway shopping cart careens into the road just as a truck speeds by and crashes, narrowly avoiding the woman. Shocked, she realizes she could have been hurt or worse without Jesus.

She turns back to find the man she was talking to, wanting to accept Jesus and be forgiven. The scene ends with a silhouette handing out a salvation card with steps to pray and believe, encouraging the reader to admit sin, believe Jesus died for it, and accept Him as Savior.

Title: Little Bride, The
Subject: Islam
Author: Carter
Responses:
Once upon a time, Ms. Henn, a teacher, reminded her students that Monday was a holiday and to complete their homework. She said she would see them again on Tuesday. As the children left, two of the girls, Becky and Tashana, ran excitedly to Susy to share some news. They told her about their new neighbor, a boy named Amir, and his sister. The two new neighbors were talking to them about God, and Amir even wanted them to become Muslims.

Later that evening, Susy asked her Grandpa what it meant to be a Muslim. Grandpa, who wore an eye patch, was concerned. He explained that Becky and Tashana were thinking about becoming Muslims and asked if Susy had told her friends about Jesus. When Susy mentioned the new kids in the neighborhood, Grandpa warned her that her friends were in danger. He explained that Islam was a dangerous religion starting to spread into their neighborhood.

Grandpa described that in Islam, the main holy book is the Qur’an, and the god they worship is called Allah. He also mentioned the prophet Mohammed, who set up the religion. He spoke about the Hadith, a collection of writings about Mohammed that contained strange teachings. Grandpa insisted that the god of Islam was not the God of the Bible and told Susy she must learn these things to protect her friends.

The next day, Susy was warned by Mrs. Davidson that Becky and Tashana were in the backyard talking to Amir and his sister. Susy approached them and learned that Amir was teaching Becky and Tashana how to say the words to become Muslims. When they began reciting a phrase, Susy stopped them and asked many questions.

Amir responded, confirming that the Qur’an was their most holy book and Mohammed was a prophet who never lied. Amir was surprised that Susy knew about the Hadith as well. When Susy asked if a prophet could lie, he said Mohammed never did. The conversation was interrupted when Amir’s sister, Safiya, told them they were being called away to leave for the airport.

Susy, Becky, and Tashana then talked about Mohammed. Becky said Amir called Mohammed a man of God who never lied. Susy challenged this, sharing that Mohammed said Allah once turned some Jews into rats and pigs and monkeys, which made Becky uncomfortable. They also learned Mohammed had many wives, owned slaves, and married a girl who was just nine years old, which shocked them all.

Susy pointed out that the god of Islam was not the God of the Bible, but both Becky and Tashana were confused because Amir told them Allah is God and Mohammed is his prophet. They then learned that the crescent moon on their mosques and flags represented the moon god, Allah, who was once worshiped in Arabia and was married to the sun goddess.

Susy explained that the story of Jesus was different. When Jesus died, he was buried and rose from the dead after three days, and many people saw Him alive. Becky was amazed. Susy told them that Jesus created the universe in six days, including animals and the first man, Adam. She explained the Christian belief that because Adam and Eve sinned, sin entered the world, and that Jesus came to save humanity.

Susy described how Jesus was born to a virgin named Mary, shed his blood to wash away sins, allowed Himself to be crucified, died, and rose again three days later to give believers the hope of heaven. She encouraged them to believe and accept Jesus to be saved.

Moved by the conversation, Becky and Tashana decided to ask Jesus for forgiveness and to be their Savior and Lord, joyfully proclaiming they were saved and would never sin again. Susy expressed her relief and prayed for the Muslims who, she believed, had been misled by false teachings.

The story ended on a hopeful note, acknowledging the importance of faith, understanding, and making choices about one’s beliefs carefully.

Title: Little Ghost, The
Subject: Halloween
Author: Chick
Responses:
A girl named Joey tries to scare her friends by dressing as a ghost and saying "Boo!" But her friend is unimpressed and tells Joey that her ghost costume isn't scary. Joey insists, "I'm a ghost," but her friend still isn't scared. Then a boy arrives dressed as the devil, claiming he's scarier. But Joey and the ghost both refuse to be frightened by him. Joey explains that she isn't afraid of the devil because Jesus loves her, and the devil is afraid of Jesus.

Curious, the ghost asks, "Who's Jesus?" Joey happily explains that Jesus is God who loves all children, no matter their color. She sings a little song about children being precious in His sight. Joey tells them Jesus loves the children of the world, but the devil hates them.

She continues, saying Jesus came from heaven to save everyone from the devil. Another friend asks what Jesus did, and Joey explains He came down to die for all the bad things people do — which God calls "sin." She quotes John 3:16 to emphasize that God loves the world so much He gave His only Son so people can have everlasting life.

Joey says Jesus allowed mean people to hurt Him and put Him on a cross. The devil laughed because he thought Jesus would be defeated. The children wonder why Jesus did that, and Joey explains that the only thing to wash away sins was Jesus' blood.

She tells them Jesus is God, and the devil was happy to see Him die. But three days later, Jesus rose from the grave, beating death and the devil. The devil became furious because now children could be free from him.

Joey says Jesus asked children to love Him for what He did and believe He died for their sins. This faith would allow them to go to heaven. She admits the devil didn't want her to tell this story because if children gave their hearts to Jesus, it would make the devil angry.

Joey tells them Jesus will love and protect them forever. She asks if they want to follow Jesus or the devil. The children choose Jesus. Joey invites them to pray with her, to make the devil mad and make Jesus glad.

Together they bow their heads and pray, asking Jesus to forgive them, come into their hearts, thanking Him for dying for their sins, and giving themselves to Him.

Joey then smiles and says, "God did all that for us. Isn't that a wonderful story? Give your heart to Jesus so He can save you and take you to heaven, too."

Title: Little Princess, The
Subject: Halloween
Author: Chick
Responses:
Heidi Spencer was gravely ill, and her father gently told his son he needed to talk to his wife alone. The doctor informed Mrs. Spencer that Heidi was dying quickly and might have only a couple of weeks left.

That night, Heidi asked her parents if she was going to die soon. They sorrowfully confirmed she was. Despite her weakening state, Heidi expressed that there was one thing she really wanted to do before she died. She asked her parents if she could go trick-or-treating on Halloween, and they told her that if she had the strength, she could go. Lying in her hospital bed, Heidi also asked her father what would happen to her after she died. He honestly admitted he did not know, and she said she didn’t think anybody did.

On Halloween night, Heidi dressed as a princess while her brother Josh dressed as a cowboy. Josh expected her choice, commenting he should have guessed the princess costume. When it was time to leave, Josh called Heidi to hurry, and she said she was coming. Half an hour later, they went door-to-door, with neighbors calling Heidi a beautiful little princess. However, Josh became concerned and insisted they go home, though Heidi pleaded to visit just one more house—specifically the new neighbors, the Smiths.

Trick-or-treating at the Smiths’ house, Heidi received candy and a special treat along with a small book. The neighbors prayed for her and said the little girl was in trouble, urging themselves to pray for her right then.

Later that evening, Heidi thanked God for saving her but worried about her parents and Josh. She told her parents urgently that she must see the Smiths immediately, explaining they gave her a book and she knew they would come to help. Her father promised to do anything for her.

George Spencer from across the street introduced himself to the Smiths, explaining that their daughter was dying and she had read their book, wanting to see them right away. Heidi proudly announced she had done it—prayed the prayer in the book and asked Jesus to be her Savior. Now, she had peace in her heart and was no longer afraid to die. Her parents expressed their happiness for her, and Heidi thanked the Smiths for caring, saying if they hadn’t given her the book, she might have ended up in hell. But now, knowing Jesus, everything was perfect except for one thing—her parents and brother didn’t know about any of it. She pleaded with her parents to share what she had learned with Josh and them.

Heidi’s father urged his family to listen to the Smiths, who explained that this meeting was no accident but a divine appointment. They shared God’s love and the most important message Heidi’s family would ever hear.

The Smiths asked Mr. Spencer if the thought of their daughter dying broke his heart. Of course it did. They explained God’s heart was even more broken because He sent His Son to die on earth. They said all people are sinners and deserve hell. The only way to get into heaven is through someone sinless dying in their place and paying the penalty for sin—the Son of God, Jesus Christ.

They shared scripture from the Bible and told Heidi’s parents about Jesus’ sacrifice on the cross, His prayer for forgiveness for those who crucified Him, and His resurrection three days later. The Spencer parents realized Jesus died for all of them.

The Smiths then asked if the Spencers wanted to pray and trust Christ that very moment. They all agreed and did so together. Shortly after, the Smiths told Heidi the good news that they had prayed with her parents and brother, and Heidi joyfully thanked God.

That night, Heidi peacefully passed away, welcomed to heaven by Jesus. She was promised a heavenly home where her whole family would eventually join her. 

Josh later visited Heidi’s grave, acknowledging his little sister was in heaven because she trusted Jesus. He was asked, “What about you?” reminding everyone that life is uncertain and it’s important to trust in Jesus before it’s too late.

Title: Little Sneak, The
Subject: Basic Gospel
Tag(s): ['Black Tract Series', 'Little Children', 'Older Children and Adults']
Author: Carter
Responses:
Once upon a time, a man was hard at work breaking rocks with a pickaxe. After his laborious work, a well-dressed man approached and gave him a handful of money. The man with the pickaxe walked away happily, returning home to his family where he gave the money to his wife.

Later, the wife took the money and hid it carefully inside a drawer. However, their child secretly saw where the money was kept and then took some of it for himself.

The child gleefully counted the stolen money and stored it back in the drawer when a stern couple scolded him and pointed to the money, warning him not to steal. The child was frightened by the adults and a representation of his conscience or evil spirit appeared behind him, but he yelled, "No!"

The man and woman, possibly the child's parents, were sad and powerless as the child was then handed over to a stern man in a hat, who pointed away, sending them away visibly upset. The family found themselves displaced, living under a bridge while a religious figure preached about judgment and salvation, mentioning Jesus Christ and his sacrifice on the cross.

The family prayed sincerely, filled with hope and faith, but the child was still troubled by thoughts of money and theft. Eventually, the man and woman returned to the place where the money was hidden and found it gone, only to sigh in despair. They confronted the child, and it was clear he was guilty and ashamed.

A man, perhaps a community leader, stepped in and handed the family a key, possibly to a new home. Another man gave the child a book titled "Proverbs" and shared the teachings of Jesus with them, encouraging them to believe in Him.

The family prayed humbly, and the evil spirit was seen retreating as the child joyfully left, singing and following the path of righteousness. Suddenly, a violent scene depicted the child suffering harm, symbolizing the struggle with sin and evil, but then he was seen being lifted by an angelic figure toward heaven.

Eventually, the child and the angel rose above the clouds, flying toward a heavenly realm where Jesus awaited with open arms. The family reunited with Jesus and rejoiced together, surrounded by divine light.

The story concludes with the message: "Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved." (Acts 16:31)

Title: Long Trip, The
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
Little John was born, weighing 7 pounds and measuring 20 inches long. His life had just begun. Life, at times, was a long journey from the cradle to the grave. As a baby, John was wobbly but showed his first steps, beginning to explore his world.

At one year old, John had developed a mind of his own, though he faced the typical challenges of childhood and still had 69 more years to live. By the time he was 15, John found himself on the great highway of life, moving in the same direction as everyone else around him.

At 20 years old, John acted as if he had all the answers, confidently navigating his path with 50 years ahead of him. By 40, John was married with two children, but life had turned into a rat race on that same great highway. When John reached 50, he no longer had all the answers and had only 20 years left. He questioned where he was headed and was shocked to learn he didn’t really know.

People urged John to seek some good news, but the rush of life kept moving him forward. When John pointed out to a woman that she was on the wrong path that led to destruction, he offered her good news: a narrow path to heaven. John explained that Jesus is the way on that narrow path. In His great love, Jesus, God the Son, left heaven, became a man, shed His blood for mankind’s sins, died on the cross, and rose again three days later. He is now in heaven and will return.

John asked if everyone on the highway was doomed, and was told that the gift of God is eternal life in heaven through Jesus Christ. The question became whether John and others would receive God's gift. Many said yes.

John was encouraged to follow this narrow road to heaven, but he hesitated. His wife went ahead, choosing the narrow path. John’s friends told him he still had plenty of time, since he was only 62 and had eight years left. John found comfort in this thinking.

Six months later, John experienced his death, falling into a chaotic abyss. He confronted a devil who admitted lying to him about his lifespan. The devil admitted tricking John and claimed him forever.

The story concludes with a reminder: the whole world is on the great highway of life, but there is still time to take the narrow road to heaven. It warns others not to make John's mistake and to receive Jesus today.

Title: Look Out!
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
Once upon a time, there was a great danger lurking—a devil who prowled like a roaring lion, seeking someone to devour. The only escape from this fate was one path, and if you didn’t take it, your chance of escape was zero.

This terrible enemy had many names: Satan, Lucifer, Baphomet, the god of this world. Many people were destined for hell, though they didn't believe it. When they realized too late, they cried out in despair, "Why didn’t somebody warn me?" The hope lay in following the guidance of a little book, the Bible, so God would not have to put them in hell.

Satan’s power was deceptive; he already had many trapped in his web without them even realizing it. People had three great weaknesses from birth: the lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life. These vulnerabilities became the Devil’s tools used against everyone throughout their lives.

Satan worked even through the educational system to spread lies, teaching children that the universe was created by a big bang, not by God. Children trust their teachers, and these false teachings have been used to destroy generations. Satan controlled many aspects of the world—politics, wars, governments, religions, news media, and entertainment—all corrupted and filled with lies.

But God was not some distant figure; He was the Holy God who created the universe and made the rules. These laws were absolute and unforgiving. The Bible warns, "The soul that sinneth, it shall die," a fate first realized by Adam and Eve when they disobeyed God and paid the price for their sin. Afterward, they awaited the Day of Judgment in hell.

Generations after Adam grew worse, mocked God's warnings, and loved doing evil. God finally decided to intervene. He saved Noah and his family from a great flood that destroyed the wicked world around them. God’s righteous anger has been made clear through the Bible accounts of His judgment—like when He struck Egypt with plagues, wiped out entire armies, and destroyed the cities of Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim with fire and brimstone.

Still, God did not wish for anyone to perish but for all to repent and come to Him. That meant He wanted everyone to live with Him in heaven, not be cast into hell’s fire with Satan.

So God, the Creator of the universe, sent His Son, Jesus Christ, to save mankind. Jesus left heaven, taking on a human form, even as a young boy impressing religious scholars with His wisdom. Throughout His life, Jesus showed great mercy, healed the sick, and performed miracles, though many called His power "Devil power." Soon, those same people would want to kill Him.

Jesus revealed Himself as the only way to peace with God, saying, "I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father but by me." There was no other path. When the time came, Jesus was sentenced to death by Satan’s influence. His crucifixion was the worst day for Satan but only momentary.

After three days, Jesus rose from the dead, defeating death and hell. God accepted Jesus’ sacrifice as full payment for the sins of all who believe. This victory shattered Satan’s plans.

The gospel, the true message of Jesus and salvation, spread rapidly, bringing hope, peace, and joy to a frightened world. Jesus promised forgiveness, welcomed all into God’s family, and came to live within believers through the Holy Spirit.

But Satan countered by creating counterfeit churches and religions to distort the gospel message. His world system, with a false leader known as "The Holy Father," works to deceive people into damnation. Many who claim to be saved are actually lost, trapped by Satan’s lies.

Souls continue to fall into hell because of these false teachings. But for those who have just read this true gospel message, now is the critical moment to make a choice.

The choice is clear: eternal life through Jesus Christ or eternal damnation with Satan. Your future is in your hands — do not become Satan’s dinner.

Will you believe Jesus died for your sins? Will you ask Him to come into your heart? This decision will determine your eternity.

Choose Jesus Christ and be saved.

Title: Loser, The
Subject: Bible Stories
Author: Chick
Responses:
Once, a boy named Tommy was being bullied by a group of older kids who claimed that the area was their turf. They mocked him for being scared and told him to go home to his mother. Tommy felt threatened and tried to avoid confrontation, but the bullies continued to chase him, yelling that they wanted to fight and calling him a coward. Tommy was terrified, convinced that they were trying to kill him.

Concerned adults noticed Tommy's distress, and one man, Mr. Williams, addressed the situation by inviting Tommy to sit and talk. Tommy admitted that he had gotten into trouble simply because he was trying to make friends. Mr. Williams asked if Tommy’s dad knew about the harassment, to which Tommy replied sadly that his father wouldn't care because he thought Tommy was a loser.

Then, a woman came to the door and invited Tommy inside for some hot chocolate. She asked if Tommy had ever heard about the bravest loser in the Bible. Curious, Tommy asked who that was.

The man began to tell Tommy the story of Gideon from the Bible. He explained how God’s people had suffered as slaves in Egypt for 400 years and were called the children of Israel. God sent Moses to help them escape, but they were ungrateful and complained. Because of their disbelief, God kept them wandering in the desert for 40 years, gave them commandments, but eventually, due to their continued disobedience, God allowed them to face struggles.

The Israelites fell into sin, worshipping false gods and doing evil things, even worse than those they lived among. They married those evil people, and in return, their enemy, the Midianites, destroyed their food and livestock. The Israelites were powerless and fearful, even forgetting God.

God decided to change things by using a man named Gideon, who was scared of everything, especially the Midianites. When Gideon was hiding, an angel appeared and told him, “The Lord is with thee, thou mighty man of valour.” This shocked Gideon, but the angel gave him a mission: to save Israel from the Midianites.

Gideon was unsure and questioned why these troubles had come upon them if God was with them. The angel explained and showed signs to assure Gideon that God supported him. Gideon obeyed God's command to destroy the altar of Baal and a sacred grove, doing so quietly at night with a few servants.

The townspeople were furious, demanding justice and trying to protect Baal, but Gideon's act challenged their false god. The Spirit of God came upon Gideon, filling him with courage. God then had Gideon call for an army, but because the people were boasting, God reduced his army from 32,000 men to just 300, showing that victory would come from God's power alone.

Gideon sneaked into the enemy camp and overheard their fears, realizing God had given him a brilliant plan. At night, Gideon and his men blew trumpets and broke their pots to reveal torches, creating confusion and fear among the enemy. The Midianites turned on each other in their panic, and God delivered the Israelites from their foes.

Tommy was amazed by the story and asked if he could have God with him, like Gideon did. Mr. Williams explained that Gideon was once a scared loser, just like Tommy, but God’s power changed him.

Then, Mr. Williams told Tommy about Jesus, who came to Earth, died on the cross to save everyone from sin, and rose again. He said Jesus wants to be Tommy’s best friend and protect him.

Tommy decided he wanted Jesus in his life and prayed to accept Him as his Savior, asking for strength to face the bullies. The next day, the bullies noticed that Tommy seemed different. When they asked if they could be friends, Tommy confidently said yes, explaining that he now had a powerful friend to protect him. He even shared the story of Gideon with them.

Tommy had found courage and hope through faith, and Psalm 27:1 became his guide: “The Lord is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? The Lord is the strength of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?”

Title: Love Story, A
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
This story begins with a simple yet profound question: Who gave you life? According to the Bible, Jesus is the one who gave you life. It says in John 1:3, "All things were made by him (Jesus); and without him was not any thing made that was made."

Next, consider who created the world you live on. The Bible again tells us that Jesus did. Colossians 1:16 states, "For by him (Jesus) were all things created that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions or principalities, or powers; all things were created by him and for him."

You might wonder who knows everything you've ever said or thought in your heart. The Bible says Jesus does. Psalms 139:4 tells us, "For there is not a word in my tongue, but lo, O Lord, thou knowest it altogether."

Who understands you, especially when you feel lonely or scared? Jesus truly understands. Hebrews 4:13 says, "Neither is there any creature that is not manifest (exposed) in his sight: but all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him (Jesus) with whom we have to do."

Who knows all about your sins—such as murder, envy, cheating, swearing, lust, lying, and selfishness? Jesus does. Matthew 9:4 declares, "And Jesus knowing their thoughts said, Wherefore think ye evil in your hearts?"

Who desires for you to be next to Him in heaven? The Bible says Jesus wants that. According to 1 Thessalonians 4:16-17, "For the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout... and the dead in Christ shall rise first: then we which are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air and so shall we ever be with the Lord."

Who wants to keep you from going to hell? Jesus does! 2 Peter 3:9 states, "The Lord (Jesus) is... not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance," meaning to be truly sorry for your sins and willing to turn from them.

Who loved you so much that He would leave His throne in heaven just for you? Jesus did. John 3:16 says, "For God (the Father) so loved the world (that's you), that He gave His only begotten Son (God the Son, that's Jesus), that whosoever believeth (trusts) in Him should not perish but have everlasting life (in Heaven)."

Who loved you so much that He shed His precious blood to wash away your sins and die for you? Jesus! Colossians 1:14 tells us, "In whom we have redemption... through His blood, even the forgiveness of sins."

Who loved you so much that He rose from the dead and went back to heaven? Jesus did. Acts 1:9 reads, "And when He (Jesus) had spoken those things, He was taken up (into Heaven); and a cloud received Him out of their sight."

Who loves you enough to build a gorgeous mansion in heaven for you to live in? Jesus! John 14:2-3 shares His words: "In my Father's house (in Heaven) are many mansions... I go to prepare a place for you... I will come again, and receive you unto myself; that where I am, there ye may be also."

Who wants you to tell Him how very sorry you are for your sins and that you'll turn away from them? Jesus does. Luke 5:32 says, "I came not to call the *righteous, but sinners to repentance." Romans 3:10 reminds us, "As it is written, there is none righteous, no not one."

Who wants to come into your heart if you ask Him to? Jesus! Romans 10:9 says, "That if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised Him from the dead, thou shalt be saved."

If you have done that, then He loves you so much that He wants to share His riches, power, and glory with you. 1 John 3:2 promises, "Beloved, now are we the sons of God... but we know that when He (Jesus) shall appear, we shall be like Him."

Who loves you so much that He would put angels at your side to protect you? Jesus! Hebrews 1:14 tells us, "Are they not all ministering spirits (angels), sent forth to minister (care) for them who shall be heirs of salvation?"

Who wants you to be with Him when He returns to this earth as King of Kings and Lord of Lords? Jesus! Revelation 19:11,14,16 describes, "And I saw heaven opened, and behold a white horse; and he that sat upon him was called Faithful and True (Jesus)... And the armies which were in heaven followed him upon white horses… and on his vesture and on his thigh a name written, KING OF KINGS, and LORD OF LORDS."

Who loves you so much that He wants you to rule at His side throughout eternity? Jesus! Revelation 5:10 says, "And hast made us unto our God kings and priests: and we shall reign (rule) on the earth."

Isn't that a beautiful love story? Who could ever love you like that? Only God Almighty!

And that is who Jesus really is! Revelation 1:8 declares, "I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the ending, saith the Lord (Jesus), which is, and which was, and which is to come, the Almighty."

Title: Love That Money!
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
Here is the story from the comic strip written out:

A woman tells her mother she’ll be right out and to be careful not to fall again. The elderly mother promises to try not to. The mother steps outside, but then falls. When a man roughly tells her to move, she asks for help. The man refuses to get involved and tells her to crawl over the wall so he can get through. She tries and later thanks the man, saying she’ll be praying for him. He replies to pray for herself, calling her a "little old creep." The mother prays silently, asking the Lord to help the man who is in deep trouble, while her dog listens.

Later, the daughter asks if the mother is hurt; she is fine but had a bump. The daughter heard the mother praying and wonders where "Molech" is.
