At work, a man named Joe Bronson is questioned for being away from his assignment. He says he was resting in his car while "Big Joe" went into the store. The boss demands that Joe not leave Big Joe’s side because Big Joe is their "treasure."

Two men discuss Joe Bronson, with one remarking Joe reminds him of Aunt Louise, whom the other man hates. They agree to focus and carry out a plan to destroy someone named Wilson. Later, Joe comes in to wish the boss a happy birthday with a gift. The boss is touched and invites Joe inside. An older woman asks to close the door, feeling something important must be shared.

Joe begins to say he doesn’t want to be unkind but has heard that someone put down who he thought was a friend. He encourages Joe to speak freely. The boss reveals he took the bait and got Wilson fired, taking his job, stating this is just the beginning because they are family and will take care of Joe. On Monday, Joe tells Tyler he was fired but Tyler reassures him Joe is a good friend, saying the boss had to cut back. Joe feels betrayed when the boss chooses someone he doesn’t know, laughing at Joe’s ignorance.

Six months later, people worry about Joe Bronson taking his place, but they hear he is being moved to top management in New York. A creature named Molech says Joe will become a star in politics and have incredible wealth, instructing others to keep an eye on him because he is invaluable.

Five years later, Joe refuses to talk to Aunt Louise, stating his hatred for her. Someone tells Joe the Aunt Louise just called to say she loves him, but he refuses. Meanwhile, the mother prays, asking the Lord to remember the cruel man who fell a few years ago and to do whatever it takes to save him. The scripture reminds viewers that God’s eyes are on the righteous.

One week later, a family hears the stock market just crashed. They are ruined, and all their money is gone. Joe wakes up, and they discuss what to do, with his family feeling hopeless. They consider moving in with Papa but don’t want to sleep in the park. Joe will sleep on the floor until they find a bed. Joe thinks about how he is now nothing, with no hope or friends. His wife hates him, and his father-in-law calls him a bum.

Molech tells Joe to shut up and listen, warning that if Joe gives up on Joe Bronson, Molech will destroy him. Molech says Joe needs money and should be allowed to win the lottery. Someone says the idea has been overdone and calls for a better plan, telling Molech not to let Joe down. Another character declares they know what to do and has an idea.

A man holding a "Will Work For Food" sign laments that death won’t change anything because the soul lives on and one will still be miserable. The other says he wishes he were dead. Molech is shocked and says he will stop this immediately.

Someone tells Molech to stay out of it because now it’s their turn to leave Joe alone. They plan to take a walk with the "little monster." Joe asks what it means that his soul lives on; the other man explains that the soul is who you are, and after death, the soul will either be with Jesus or the Devil. Joe questions what Jesus has to do with his soul.

The man explains that Jesus did something special for Joe. Jesus, the Son of God, left heaven, became a man, and shed His blood on the cross to wash away people’s sins. Three days later, Jesus rose from the dead to take souls to heaven.

Joe is told he must believe Jesus did this for him and ask Him to forgive his sins and come into his heart to become his Savior. Joe asks what happens if he doesn’t accept. He is warned that when his heart stops, it’s over, and if he rejects Jesus, he will be condemned to hell forever.

Joe considers whether he should follow Jesus’ teaching but is advised against believing what a fanatic said, as someone calls the wind strong and tries to stop him. Afterward, Joe is called about a lawyer on the phone who says somebody has died. Joe doesn’t know who and is told to ask the lawyer.

The lawyer tells Joe that Aunt Louise is dead and he is named in her will, leaving him a fortune – over two million dollars. Joe rejoices, claiming he never needed Jesus because Aunt Louise saved him, and he loves money.

At 2:47 a.m., a storm with 100 mph winds causes a crash outside Joe’s house. Joe cries out, but he is dead. A voice says that his soul has been required that night. Another scripture reminds readers of the emptiness of gaining the world but losing one’s soul.

Later, Molech congratulates others that Joe’s soul is in hell, cursing Aunt Louise; the plan was a close one. Another remarks that most people love money more than Jesus. Molech insists they are after Joe’s soul and will get it if it’s the last thing they ever do. The advice for saving one’s soul is to believe on Jesus Christ and be saved.

The story ends here.

Title: Love The Jewish People
Subject: Israel
Author: Chick
Responses:
At one time, Egypt was the envy of the world. No nation could rival her in wealth, military power, agriculture, or science. Architecturally, Egypt stood unmatched and was the most powerful nation on earth. However, Egypt made a fatal mistake by using slaves to build her empire who belonged to someone else. Their rightful owner observed the mistreatment of His people for 400 years and was determined to stop it.

These slaves were the Children of Israel, belonging to God. Within weeks, God sent 10 plagues that overturned Egypt, each destroying one of Egypt's false gods. When God struck down every Egyptian firstborn, the Pharaoh relented and allowed God's people to leave. As the Pharaoh’s mighty army died in the Red Sea, God's people left Egypt, taking its wealth with them, resulting in Egypt’s destruction.

Today, Egyptian tour guides can only boast about Egypt's glorious past. Egypt has become a backward nation, full of memories and dependent on external aid. Despite this, Egypt remains an enemy of Israel.

When mighty Rome ruled the world, Jews suffered under harsh oppression, yet the Roman empire eventually crumbled. Throughout history, empires like Babylon, Persia, Greece, and others attempted to capture Jerusalem. Their glory faded into ruins as the Jews suffered, and every empire eventually collapsed.

In 1933, Catholic Germany, serving the Vatican, launched a 20th-century inquisition, murdering six million Jews. Though Hitler sought to destroy the Jews, God destroyed Hitler and his ambitions. Israel’s deadliest enemy today is the Vatican, and it is said they will be destroyed before the Messiah’s second coming.

Father Abraham had two sons: Ishmael, the father of the Arabs, and Isaac, whose son was Jacob (Israel), the father of the twelve tribes of Israel. God promised both Abraham and Jacob that He would bless those who blessed them and curse those who cursed them.

This curse is still seen today in certain African nations, such as Niger, Chad, Ethiopia, Nigeria, Senegal, Mali, and Upper Volta. These countries share two traits: all broke diplomatic ties with Israel, and all suffered terrible famine and drought caused by the expanding Sahara desert.

England is another example. God once blessed England through Queen Victoria, a God-fearing ruler, leading Great Britain to power until 1918. However, forgetting God’s promise to Israel, Britain was cursed and has since declined as a major power. At the start of World War I, Britain ruled vast territories, but by the war’s end, her empire shrank to a few isolated islands and small colonies.

During World War I, the British navy ran short of gunpowder. Sir Winston Churchill sought help from Jewish chemist Chaim Weizmann, who produced 30,000 tons of synthetic acetone for gunpowder manufacture and became a national hero. When asked what he wanted in return, Weizmann asked for a national home for his people. His wish was granted.

The Balfour Declaration in 1917 promised the Jews a homeland in Israel. After World War I, Great Britain took control of Palestine but favored the Arabs by dividing the land and limiting Jewish immigration, causing tensions.

In 1938, as Hitler’s persecution escalated, Jews begged Britain for entry into Palestine but were turned away, many ending up in Nazi camps. In 1948, when Israel declared independence, Britain ignored God’s promise, opposing Israel, supporting Arabs, disarming Jews, and backing Arab military units, bringing Britain into deep trouble.

Russia, too, has been an enemy of Israel and is currently in turmoil. Biblical prophecy states Russia will be destroyed when she moves against Israel, triggering World War III, a catastrophic war killing one-quarter of the world’s population. Remarkably, Israel will survive this war.

God blessed the United States for supporting Israel, but now America has shifted, arming Israel’s enemies and experiencing rising anti-Semitism. Heavily indebted, America is becoming a puppet to the U.N. and the world court, jeopardizing itself, especially due to interests around oil.

In the end times, Israel plays a vital role in Bible prophecy. Satan’s man, known as the Beast, will rise from Rome as a world leader. His goal will be to annihilate Israel, ordering armies worldwide to converge on Israel for destruction in the Battle of Armageddon.

When all seems lost, Israel’s Messiah will come from the heavens to save Israel. He will destroy invading armies, take control of all governments, and judge all nations opposing Israel.

Prophecies describe this Messiah in detail: His pre-existence, birth from the seed of Abraham, from the tribe of Judah, His birth in Bethlehem, virgin birth, Him being declared the Son of God, a prophet rejected by His own people, His entry into Jerusalem riding a donkey, betrayal for silver, accusations, silence to accusations, suffering without cause, sacrificial death, crucifixion with criminals, pierced hands and feet, offering vinegar and gall, soldiers gambling for His coat, no bones broken, burial with the rich, resurrection, ascension to God’s right hand, and coming glory. The only one to fulfill all these is Jesus (Yeshua the Messiah).

Jesus came to earth, shedding His precious blood to remove the sins of the world, rose from the dead, and was witnessed by over 500 people. Despite being rejected by many of His own, He offers everlasting life to all who believe in Him.

This story traces the intertwined destinies of Egypt, empires, nations, and Israel, highlighting biblical prophecy and the ultimate salvation through the Messiah.

Title: Mad Machine, The
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
Once upon a time in modern society, people were facing immense pressures that had never been experienced before. The question on everyone's mind was whether things would get better, but cynicism prevailed, with many doubting any improvement was possible.

Individuals were overwhelmed by stress, anxiety, and fear. One man, especially distraught, declared he was going to see his psychiatrist due to everything collapsing around him, but his wife reminded him that the doctor had an appointment with another patient. This highlighted how widespread the feelings of fear and uncertainty had become.

People relied on experts to guide them, but even the experts seemed conflicted. One said the only way to stop inflation was to cut taxes, whereas another insisted that increasing taxes was the solution. This contradiction only amplified public confusion.

In search of something reliable, people clung to what they trusted most. A man praised his doctor for years of care, only to learn he might have made mistakes. Another man endorsed blackstrap molasses as a remedy, and a third claimed gold and silver coins were the only true security—until he was robbed. The real answers seemed elusive.

Alongside economic and social turmoil, new marriage problems were surfacing, leading to rising divorce rates. Some were relieved to say they didn’t face these issues, while others revealed spouses running off—sometimes with partners of unexpected genders—causing more chaos in family life.

Even the financial world was unstable, with international banking experts admitting confusion and turmoil. Von Koffenheimer, a once-reliable figure, found himself lost and overwhelmed, symbolizing the fragile global economy and looming depression.

Alcoholism was on the rise, now affecting children as young as nine to twelve. Families sought help at places like Sobersides Sanitarium, where supposedly guaranteed cures awaited patients, though the problem was widespread and entrenched.

Meanwhile, the arms race raged on. World leaders expressed a desperate yearning for peace, but others insisted on war to achieve it, fueling fears of global conflict.

Crime rates soared, with punishments harsh but justice seeming ineffective. Those convicted promised revenge on witnesses, and parolees requiring protection illustrated the ongoing social instability.

Science was seen as a potential savior for issues like pollution, population growth, and energy shortages. But when asked how long solutions might take, professors estimated decades or even centuries—time few felt they had.

The cumulative effect was overwhelming. Many could not cope with the relentless pressures of life, leading to breakdowns and despair. A mother on the brink of collapse, facing eviction, domestic violence, and mounting stress, cried out for help but found none.

Mental health care was a grim reality. At places like Happy Halls Asylum, shock treatments were common, and medications were used to calm patients. Group therapy sessions were harsh, filled with anger, prejudice, and pain rather than healing. Insurance issues and resource shortages made treatment even harder, pushing many to the brink.

Dr. Hyde, the asylum’s administrator, eventually met a tragic end, leaving unanswered questions about the true effectiveness of the mental health system.

Amidst this chaos, people sought answers. One woman with severe hardships encountered a man who shared his faith in Jesus Christ. Though initially skeptical, she was introduced to the promises of peace and hope found in the Bible. She learned about Jesus’s life, miracles, and the sacrificial love that offered salvation.

The story revealed how God’s love was extended to all, offering forgiveness and eternal life through Jesus. It explained how Jesus became human without sin, died to atone for humanity’s sins, and promised to be the only way to heaven.

The woman was assured that guilt and fear could be removed, replaced by lasting peace and confidence in God’s care. The story ended with the hope that, through faith in Jesus, people could find real relief from the pressures and tragedies overwhelming their lives.

Thus, in a world full of confusion, fear, and instability, the message was clear: true hope and peace come not from human solutions, but from trusting in God’s promises through Jesus Christ.

Title: Mama's Girls
Subject: Catholicism
Author: Chick
Responses:
Here is the comic strip transformed into a written story:

The two greatest forces in the universe clashed at the cross of Jesus Christ. A war was underway for the souls of men. When Jesus arose from the dead, the rulers of darkness in this world were in shock. They asked, "How could we have known?" The Bible says, "...for had they known it, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory" (1 Corinthians 2:8).

Before Jesus came, people were like sheep—lost in darkness, confused, and scared. Some tried to find a way to heaven but could not. Satan waited in the shadows, ready to grab souls the instant they died. To solve this problem, God the Father sent His Son, Jesus, from heaven to save souls. Jesus made an easy way for people to get into heaven by becoming a human sacrifice.

Jesus said, "I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me" (John 14:6) and, "My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me: And I give unto them eternal life..." (John 10:27-28). Jesus was a prophet who could not lie. He was arrested and asked, "Art thou the Christ, the Son of the Blessed?" to which He replied, "I am." For this blasphemy, He was condemned to death.

They beat Jesus almost to death and hung Him on the cross. Jesus said, "It is finished." The Creator of the universe died on the cross, shedding His holy blood to wash away sins and save souls. God’s love made this gift as easy as possible —just believe and be saved (John 3:16; John 3:15-18).

However, the world says only believe? That's too easy! It takes work, sacrifice, and suffering to go to heaven. But Jesus said, "...he that believeth not is condemned already..." Those who trust in good works over faith will not be saved (Ephesians 2:8-9).

Satan, called "the god of this world," took his title after Adam’s fall. He is a created being and can only go so far. He noticed Jesus' church growing after Jesus was taken up to heaven. Satan knew he needed a church of his own. He planned to destroy the mighty, unbeatable Roman empire from within. Rome was full of evil—corruption, craziness, betrayal, and unnatural sins.

Rome fell into ruins, no longer the leader of nations. From its ashes, Satan intended to build a deadly "phony church" that would spread darkness through the dark ages. By 430 AD, Satan had called Mary "The Mother of God" and created Roman Catholicism, replacing the fallen Roman Empire’s Caesars with Popes and the Roman Senate with Cardinals.

Satan’s religious machine replaced the government to destroy more souls. This monstrous church had many daughters. One was Islam. The Vatican’s political power and wealth scared kings, presidents, dictators, media, intelligence agencies, and others.

The Whore’s first daughter, Islam, wanted Jerusalem for herself but was blocked by Jews and Christians. So, Rome needed a strong force in the Middle East. They sought an Arab messiah to create an army to capture Jerusalem for the Pope. A woman named Khadija, an Arab widow who gave wealth to the church, was chosen to find this man.

She found Muhammad, who would create a new religion for Ishmael's children. Khadija married Muhammad, and the church gave birth to Islam. Muhammad had visions in a cave, which Catholic advisors helped "interpret" into Islam’s Qur'an. Muhammad chose Allah, his tribe’s moon god, as his god, selecting the crescent moon as its symbol. Those opposing Muhammad died.

After Muhammad’s death, his armies took Jerusalem, double-crossing the Pope. Rome’s first daughter had turned on her mother, as Islam fought Roman Catholics. The Whore's religious daughters all want to rule the world and are destined for doom because works can’t save souls (Ephesians 2:8-9).

Pope Innocent III ordered the Orthodox Church of Constantinople to submit; they refused and were slaughtered. The survivors turned to the Czar of Russia for help, triggering a revolution. The famous "Sealed Train" carried Lenin and the Pope’s gold to fund the Russian Revolution, which led to millions of deaths including the Czar and his family.

The revolutionaries took both the Czar’s and Pope’s gold. The Pope's own Communists betrayed him. The Communist Revolution ended with Stalin becoming dictator, killing over 20 million souls. Meanwhile, Nazi Germany was born to use Catholics to destroy Communism and make the world Catholic. Nazi Germany started WWII by invading Russia but lost, leaving Europe in ruins. Rome denied involvement, but the devil boasted how Pius XII "poured tons of souls into hell."

Another daughter, Masonry, seeks to unify the world through Baal worship, with leaders swearing oaths on the Quran. Masonry brings spiritual death to churches. The ancient force behind Baal worship and Masonry pushes for "unity" for the coming antichrist. Masonic leaders secretly belong to Rome—if involved, get out!

Satan is attacking by blinding minds with confusion. People are misled by TV, false religions, holy books, evolution, environmentalism—anything but Jesus. Satan hates that people might find out who Jesus really is.

Jesus Christ is the Creator of the universe and will judge all lives. He will cast unbelievers, including Satan, into the lake of fire. Those who believe and receive Jesus as Savior will be served by angels, live forever in a mansion with Jesus. Those who reject Him will face judgment and be cast into fire.

The choice is yours—choose Jesus Christ or Satan. Believe in Jesus and be saved. If you have not accepted Jesus, now is the time.

---

If you want, I can help with the decision part included in the comic.

Title: Man in Black
Subject: Catholicism
Author: Chick
Responses:
On a rainy night, a drunken man named Damien staggers across a street after abruptly stopping his car with a screech. Another man, Bob, notices this and wonders what Damien is doing so close to the edge of a bridge. Damien appears ready to jump and Bob pleads with him, saying, "Wait, mister... don’t jump! Let's talk about it." But Damien is angry and bitter, cursing his life and the deceptive game he's been living. He declares his hatred for his religion, and Bob responds firmly, "So does Jesus!"

Surprised, Damien demands to know who Bob is and why he is so disrespectful. Bob reveals that he is a priest, and Damien retorts that Bob is standing about 100 feet from hell. The confrontation escalates as Damien challenges Bob's faith, questioning if Bob thinks he is lost. Bob confirms this with conviction.

Damien admits he's too mad to jump but not willing to listen, while Bob insists on talking. Bob introduces himself as Father Damien, and Bob reveals his own name. Damien accuses Jesus of hating the Church because, he says, the Bible calls it "The Great Whore." Bob shows Damien biblical passages to prove the history of this great Whore. 

Bob explains how the apostle John, while imprisoned on the island of Patmos around 90-100 AD, wrote about this vision of the Whore’s power and her destruction. He recounts how Satan created the Whore after Noah's flood in ancient Babylon, represented by Nimrod and his wife, Semiramis, who was worshipped as the "Queen of Heaven." This occult religion had priests and confessionals to control people.

As time passed, empires rose and fell, but the worship of Semiramis continued under different names like Isis in Egypt, Shing-Moo in China, Diana in Ephesus, and others, even reaching Rome where Semiramis was called Venus and worshipped by Caesars treated as gods in a world of darkness.

It was during this era that God sent Jesus, the Light of the World, to shatter the darkness of this pagan power. Jesus was crucified, buried, and rose on the third day. His message of love and forgiveness was so powerful that it shook Satan’s kingdom. The early Christians, fearless and loving, fed the poor and clothed widows, spreading Jesus's teachings even in the face of brutal persecution and slaughter, especially in Rome.

Satan then devised a plan to counter this movement by creating a false Christian church, a counterfeit Bible, and a counterfeit God. Constantine, the last great emperor of Rome, claimed to be a Christian but also worshipped the sun god. He ordered his troops to become "Christians," allowing pagans to infiltrate and corrupt the true church. Genuine Christians fled to the mountains with the Word of God, while the phonies stayed in Rome.

In Alexandria, Egypt, by 350 AD, Satan’s counterfeit church, Bible, and god were firmly established. This was the birth of Catholicism, with Constantine considered its first pope. Within 25 years, the Whore controlled the world: civilization collapsed, vandals plundered and destroyed Europe, and monks built cathedrals teaching idol worship and superstition.

Popes became the new Caesars, claiming to be Christ on earth, ruling even kings and the masses who bowed to them. Satan had created his own anti-Christ who blasphemed God's Word. The real Peter was not the first pope, contrary to popular belief.

Jesus, the King of Kings, was reduced to an idol—the baby Jesus, the wafer turned to Jesus, priests as little Jesuses, and the pope as "Jesus on earth.” The masses were told the real Jesus was angry in heaven because of their sins, urging them to obey Mary, Satan's masterpiece for controlling religious slaves dressed as the new Queen of Heaven.

This counterfeit church was exposed in the Book of Revelation, which calls it "Mystery, Babylon the Great, the Mother of Harlots and Abominations of the Earth." Vatican City controls the world's wealth and power, creating wars and shaking leaders in their boots, opposing Jesus directly.

The Inquisition (1200-1808) showed the church's brutal hatred, torturing and killing millions. Secret files within the Vatican revealed even darker practices: intermarriage, pedophilia, incest, and occult murders swept under the rug. 

Bob shares a warning from Jesus to "Come out of her, my people," for her sins have reached heaven and God has remembered her iniquities.

Damien, overwhelmed and lost, asks Bob how to reach the real Jesus. Bob answers that Jesus commands repentance, believing that He died and shed His blood to wash away sins. Those who receive Jesus as their only Savior will be saved. Damien prays to Jesus, asking for forgiveness and salvation.

Thankful and saved, Damien worries for his lost relatives trapped by the Whore. Bob promises to pray for them and reminds Damien that neither the great Whore nor the pope cares for their souls—it is religious show business. But Jesus loves everyone and is the only way to heaven.

The story ends urging belief in the Lord Jesus Christ for salvation, highlighting the stark contrast between the true church of Christ and the counterfeit created by Satan.

Title: Man of the Match
Subject: Sports
Author: Carter
Responses:
In the heat of a World Cup overtime, sports commentator announces that Eddie Jackson has the ball. Eddie performs an acrobatic move and takes a shot at the goal. The crowd erupts as he scores the golden goal, ending the game and earning the title of man of the match.

The next day, Eddie is at a press conference where it's announced that he has signed a $20 million contract and a $5 million shoe deal. Riding the wave of his success, Eddie proudly shows his friend Leon his new contract, boasting about the mansions, cars, fame, and power he now has, claiming he can have anything he wants.

Leon, however, confronts Eddie and tells him he has nothing. He points out that someday Eddie will die and none of his wealth will matter. Leon reminds Eddie of a profound truth: "For what shall it profit a man if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul?"

Furious, Eddie insults Leon and orders him to be quiet and get back to work, while internally suffering knee pain and considering seeing a doctor.

That night, Eddie attends a lavish party, loved and admired by those around him. He thinks about showing Leon how much respect he receives and decides to go find him. But when he arrives near Leon's home, he gasps in surprise.

Inside Leon's home, a man prays fervently that Jesus will show Eddie that he is lost and needs to be saved. When Eddie finds out about the prayer, he angrily forbids Leon from praying for him again.

Two weeks later, Eddie visits the doctor to check his knee problem. The doctor delivers the grim news: Eddie has terminal cancer, which has spread throughout his body, and only has a few weeks left to live.

Desperate and scared, Eddie asks Leon if he can talk with him in his study. There, Eddie reveals his fear and the diagnosis. He asks Leon if he is going to hell. Leon tells Eddie the truth but encourages that it is not too late. He recounts a story from 23 years ago when a real friend helped him realize he was a sinner on the path to hell but also shared the good news that God loved him so much He sent His Son, Jesus Christ, to die for his sins.

Leon explains how he admitted his sin, received God's gift of eternal life by trusting Christ, and how his life has never been the same since. He encourages Eddie to trust Christ now, warning that there's no guarantee of tomorrow.

Moved, Eddie confesses that he had placed all his trust in money and ability and asks Jesus to come into his heart and be his Savior. He feels a huge weight lifted from his shoulders and is no longer afraid to die.

A few weeks later, Eddie passes away. In heaven, his spirit is welcomed warmly. On Earth, friends and family gather at Eddie's mansion for the reading of his will. A letter from Eddie reveals his journey and newfound faith, sharing how he was rich on the outside but lost until Leon showed him salvation in Jesus Christ.

Eddie's will leaves his $18 million estate to Leon, whom he trusts to use it wisely, and he urges everyone to receive Christ as their personal Savior for eternal life.

Eddie's parting truth is that fame and money cannot buy eternal life, peace, or joy, and nothing is more important than a relationship with Jesus Christ. He hopes his friends will trust Christ and live fulfilling lives, looking forward to heaven someday.

Title: Mary's Kids
Subject: Catholicism
Author: Chick
Responses:
Samuel came with his wife Janet and their little girl Megan to visit his mother. Samuel wanted to reconcile, apologizing for their past terrible fight. Although his mother found the situation very awkward, she decided to let them in. Megan greeted her grandmother warmly.

The grandmother immediately took offense at a doll Megan wanted to play with, exclaiming "HOLY MOTHER OF GOD!" and insisting it wasn't a doll. She sharply demanded Megan give it to her and scolded her for asking to play with it. Samuel and Janet watched as the grandmother spoke sternly about what happens when a non-Catholic woman marries in the family, blaming Janet for Megan's lack of understanding. She lovingly told Megan the doll was special and that she loved it.

The grandmother asked to spend time with Megan alone, and Samuel and Janet agreed to be quiet so she could speak with their daughter. She showed Megan a little book that used to belong to Samuel, explaining it was a classic of the Catholic Church called The Glories of Mary by Saint Alphonsus Liguori. She taught Megan that Mary was queen of the whole world, and Megan found that idea pretty.

Then the grandmother explained troubling things about Mary also being queen of hell, that many devils tremble at her name, and that all must obey Mary even as God is obeyed. Megan was concerned and asked if her daddy ever prayed to Mary, and was told no. She was sad to hear that those who do not serve Mary will not be saved. The grandmother further explained that Mary is considered the ladder to heaven and the joy of both the just and sinners.

Janet then revealed that she was a former faithful Catholic but had left the church. At 16, she was raped by a priest and was abused further when her mother refused to believe her. Samuel shared he too had been abused by a priest named Father John as an altar boy. The grandmother refused to believe it, calling Father John a saint.

Samuel insisted it was true and explained that the church taught priests were superior to even Mary. Janet suggested they read what the Holy Scriptures say about Mary. The story shifted to recounting biblical accounts: the angel Gabriel appearing to Mary and announcing she would conceive Jesus by the Holy Ghost; her visit to cousin Elisabeth; her fiancé Joseph being assured in a dream that the conception was holy; and that Mary was a virgin when Jesus was born.

However, the Scriptures also revealed that Mary offered two doves as a sin offering and later bore other children, thus conflicting with Catholic teaching about her perpetual virginity and special status. Jesus treated Mary just like everyone else, calling those who do God's will his brothers and sisters. A woman had once tried to force Jesus to exalt Mary and proclaim her blessed, but he refused.

Mary grew old and died like everyone else and was with her Savior in heaven, but her body was in the grave. Mary also had to do what everyone must: admit sin, believe in Jesus' sacrifice, and accept him as Savior. And she was saved.

The story then described how Jesus rising from the dead gave Satan a mighty blow. Satan then devised a plan and used a fallen angel called "the queen of heaven" to deceive people into worshipping a false virgin goddess named "Mary." Satan made the world believe this false Mary ruled heaven and was part of the divine Trinity, deceiving even believers.

Samuel confronted his mother about this lie, declaring Mary really was not an eternal virgin, had children with Joseph, was a sinner who needed a Savior—just like him. The grandmother angrily shouted that Samuel's family was damned to hell because of his words and hurled curses at him.

Megan, playing on the floor, called the doll "Oh! Queen Mary!" and was told by the grandmother that she was just a doll.

Janet admitted to her mother that she felt lied to and betrayed because she had worshipped Mary all her life, and so had her mother. Samuel asked what God would do to him, and was told that if he did what the real Mary did, God would not condemn him. Both Janet and the grandmother prayed to accept Jesus as their Savior with forgiveness for their sins.

The story ended prompting readers to accept Jesus into their hearts and save their souls, emphasizing that salvation comes through Christ alone.

Title: Mean Momma
Subject: Anger
Author: Chick
Responses:
The story begins with the solemn funeral of Ansley Parker, held at a gloomy cemetery under a pouring rain. The priest conducts the burial ceremony, solemnly reciting the phrases, "Earth to earth, ashes to ashes, dust to dust." As the ceremony ends, the only person present silently laments the tragic fact that no one else attended the funeral, considering it the saddest one they've ever conducted.

In a nearby home, a woman reading the newspaper exclaims in surprise, noticing that no one attended old Grandpa Parker’s funeral. She wonders aloud if he had a daughter, and another woman confirms that he did—a woman named Petunia. However, she immediately remarks that Petunia was an awful person who was universally hated in their class.

Becky suddenly shudders with a horrible thought: if Petunia is still around, might she inherit Grandpa Parker’s house? The very idea sickens her. She recounts that in school she was terrified of Petunia, who had beaten her up multiple times and knocked out several of her teeth. Petunia was so malicious that when the school library caught fire, she cheered, and everyone suspected she started the fire.

Trying to comfort Becky, her friend insists that no one knows where Petunia is and that the house will probably go to the state. But two weeks later, Petunia shows up at the house with a shotgun, threatening to blow off the head of a frightened man. She announces that she will inherit her father's house.

Nearby, Petunia proudly introduces her sons—Charlie, Austin, and Billy Bob—to the neighbors, asserting her dominance and ownership of the town. The neighbors bring a cake, trying to welcome Petunia to the neighborhood and hoping to meet her husband, but she coldly informs them that he is dead and that they should stay away.

Soon after, complaints to the sheriff pour in. Petunia and her sons are terrorizing the town, breaking windows, fighting kids, and generally causing mayhem. The sheriff reports multiple emergencies and stresses how Petunia’s family is driving the town insane.

At a town meeting, worried citizens recount various troubles, from robberies to an eight-year-old caught trying to steal a car. They plead with the mayor for a solution, and someone suggests that Pastor Sam Jones might be able to help.

Though some dismiss the idea as foolish, the mayor asks Pastor Jones to confront Petunia. The pastor agrees to try, emphasizing that he will need lots of prayer.

When Pastor Jones knocks on Petunia’s door, she mocks him, calling him a coward from their high school days. But Pastor Jones reveals he is now a preacher. Their conversation turns to how he came to faith and what Jesus did for him, sharing the pivotal Bible verse John 3:16 about God's love and salvation.

Petunia listens as Pastor Jones explains that Jesus left heaven, died to wash away sin, and rose three days later. He speaks about fearing God and the consequences of wickedness, warning about the "day of evil," or doomsday, when the unsaved will face judgment.

Petunia scoffs at the idea but eventually confesses to Pastor Jones that she has cursed him and is afraid of God. The pastor explains that God wants to save her and invites her to accept Jesus.

Despite her tough exterior, Petunia shows signs of change after weeks pass. But in a tragic moment, her son Charlie dies in a car crash driven by a reckless child. Petunia is heartbroken and curses God for allowing it, while Austin, another son, is left alone and grieving.

Months later, Petunia faces more challenges as a tornado threatens the town with Billy Bob home sick. The destruction brings Petunia to a breaking point, losing everything and confessing her fear and guilt to Pastor Jones. She asks if God will ever forgive her for cursing Him.

Pastor Jones reassures Petunia that God absolutely wants to save her and invites her to follow Jesus. Petunia accepts Christ as her Savior and praises Him for removing her fear.

The story closes showing Petunia’s new faith, her acceptance into Christ, and an invitation to the readers to consider salvation through Jesus, affirming that true power comes from faith, not fear.

Thus, the tale unfolds from tragedy and bitterness to redemption and hope through faith in God.

Title: Men of Peace?
Subject: Islam
Author: Chick
Responses:
A story begins with a man hurriedly leaving a room, forgetting his money and suitcase. Suddenly, an explosion blasts through the city, destroying part of London. A man on the phone declares, "Your wicked city is feeling the wrath of Allah! This is only the beginning!" Alarmed, others react with shock and concern as they learn from the news that an extremist group called "Muhammad's Faithful" has claimed responsibility for the massacre, leading world leaders to denounce the act. London is on edge, and the recent attack in Paris exacerbates fears worldwide.

Jenny rushes to show her grandfather the terrible news on TV. They discuss how the whole free world is reeling, trying to understand why this is happening. Jenny asks about the so-called holy war and why people can commit such atrocities, harming even children. Her grandfather explains that the war is in the name of God, but Jenny questions which God he means. He clarifies it's Muhammad and God.

Jenny vehemently defends Muhammad, explaining what she learned in college about his greatness. Another person intervenes, admonishing Jenny for putting down an entire religion. They debate tolerance and judgment, with the elder explaining that the extremists are not truly bad Muslims but followers of Muhammad who intend to carry out Allah's will.

The explanation turns historical, revealing that four idols, including the moon god called "Allah" by the Arabs, were worshipped by the Bedouins at the Ka'bah in Mecca. Muhammad eventually took control and proclaimed Allah the only true God, declaring himself his prophet. Jenny wonders how Muhammad became a prophet. The story recounts his visions and dreams, his encounters with a spirit named Gabriel who gave him revelations causing physical distress.

Muhammad married Khadija, who supported him, but after her death, he was vulnerable and fled to Medina. There he led raids, robbing caravans and capturing women for ransom, showing no mercy. His actions included terror, murder, plunder, and rape, which were justified by harsh verses in the Qur'an. Jenny is horrified to learn that Muhammad killed a man after finding out the location of his money and took Safiya as a wife, accumulating at least 23 wives.

The story reveals that Muhammad died in 632 AD and that his soul is condemned for eternity. Jenny’s grandfather reflects on the similarities between Jenny and Muhammad—they both rejected Jesus. While Jenny is skeptical and has heard the Christian message many times, her grandfather explains that many Muslims are unaware that their teachings include Jesus worshiping Allah, which is insulting to true God.

To truly understand God, the grandfather encourages Jenny to look at Jesus, who was sinless, healed the sick, raised the dead, and preached forgiveness and love, unlike Allah as depicted by Muhammad. Jesus demonstrated the way to heaven and even prayed for forgiveness for his enemies on the cross.

Jenny argues that she is not a terrorist, but her grandfather insists she is lost unless she repents and trusts Jesus as her Savior. He explains that salvation is not about being good or bad but about being saved through faith in Jesus, who died for all sins, even Muhammad's.

Jenny fears hell, so her grandfather urges her to accept Jesus, who saved her. The story ends with a message that going to heaven is not based on good or bad deeds but being saved by Jesus, who wants to save everyone immediately. The invitation is given to let Jesus into one’s life for eternal salvation.

Title: Miss Universe
Subject: Bible Stories
Author: Carter
Responses:
Around 520 B.C., the king of the Medes and Persians, King Ahasuerus, threw a grand party that lasted over six months. He invited everyone important from all 120 of his provinces, stretching from India to Ethiopia. During the festivities, the king showed off all the riches of his glorious kingdom. When he was drunk, he decided to flaunt his beautiful queen, Vashti, ordering her to be brought before everyone. However, Queen Vashti refused to come, causing the king to lose face before his people.

The news of her refusal spread quickly, sparking revolts among wives everywhere. The king convened an emergency meeting, where all the men agreed that Queen Vashti had to go. A law was issued requiring all wives to honor their husbands.

To find a new queen, a beauty contest was suggested to select the world’s most beautiful virgin for the king. Every mother dreamed of her daughter becoming the new queen, though some daughters expressed doubts because they were not virgins, prompting harsh reactions from their mothers.

Meanwhile, God was setting the stage to block one of Satan’s most vicious attacks against the children of Israel. Over 100 years earlier, Jerusalem had been attacked, and most of its population was taken to Babylon as slaves. Eventually, Babylon fell to the Medes and Persians, and many Jewish people lived in exile under King Ahasuerus.

Mordecai, a Jew, lived in the palace and had a beautiful foster daughter named Esther. He instructed her never to reveal that she was Jewish. Along with other virgins, Esther was prepared to meet the king through a year-long purification process. She won the hearts of those she worked with and was eventually sent to see the king. The king loved Esther above all other women and made her queen instead of Vashti, not knowing she was a Jewess.

One day, Mordecai overheard a plot to assassinate King Ahasuerus. He informed Esther, leading to the conspirators' execution. Despite saving the king’s life, Mordecai received no thanks.

Around this time, the king promoted Haman, a dangerous Jew-hater, commanding everyone to bow to him. Everyone did, except Mordecai. Haman was enraged and sought to destroy all Jews. Learning Mordecai was Jewish, Haman’s hatred intensified, and he cast lots to choose the day for their slaughter. Haman convinced the king to issue a decree condemning these people to be destroyed, and the king granted his signet ring to make the law official.

The chosen day for the massacre was the 13th of the month Adar, and the Jews were terrified. Mordecai sent Esther a message, urging her to go before the king to save her people, though she risked death if the king did not extend his scepter to her. Esther asked all Jews to pray and fast for three days.

At the same time, Mordecai refused to bow to Haman, prompting Haman to build a 75-foot gallows intending to have Mordecai hanged. Haman planned to ask the king’s permission for this.

One day, the king couldn’t sleep and reviewed the records. He asked if Mordecai had been rewarded for saving him, but was told no. Just then, Haman arrived to speak about hanging Mordecai. The king asked how to honor a man he wished to reward. Haman foolishly assumed he was the man and suggested dressing him in royal robes, crowning him, and parading him through the city on the king's horse. To Haman’s humiliation, the king ordered this honor given to Mordecai.

At the banquet Esther invited the king and Haman to, the king asked what her petition was. Esther requested the lives of her people be spared. Haman fell across Esther’s bed, begging for his life, just as the king returned. The king, furious, went outside to cool off. He then ordered Haman to be hanged on his own gallows and issued a new law allowing Jews to defend themselves.

The Jews rejoiced and feasted, celebrating their deliverance. Today, Jews worldwide commemorate this story with the Feast of Purim.

For centuries, Jews awaited the promised Messiah to save them. The prophet Isaiah described him as a child born to be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, and Prince of Peace. Isaiah also said to watch for the sign of a virgin conceiving and bearing a son named Immanuel, meaning "God with us."

The Messiah had to suffer, shedding His precious blood to wash away sins. Jesus did this, as described in John 3:16. He rose from the dead and now sits at the right hand of God, creator of the universe and judge of all at His second coming.

At the end of days, Jesus will defeat the Russian and Arab armies on the mountains of Israel. When hope seems lost, the heavens will open, and Jesus Christ will return as Israel’s Messiah. Like Haman, another enemy of the Jews known as “The Beast” will rise to power but will be destroyed. Jesus will destroy Satan’s armies at Armageddon, rule the governments of the world from Jerusalem, and ultimately cast Satan into the lake of fire.

Jesus promised, “In my Father’s house are many mansions... I go to prepare a place for you.” The choice remains: trust Jesus Christ or Satan. The decision is yours.

Title: Missing Day, The
Subject: Thanksgiving
Author: Chick
Responses:
A family was preparing for dinner when a relative named Uncle Mortimer was on his way to visit. At the dinner table, there was a mix of complaints and casual chatter, including frustrations about the cooking and concerns about missing a football game. The arrival of Uncle Mortimer sparked curiosity, though some family members expressed disdain for him. Despite this, the family welcomed him, and he was about to share the story of Thanksgiving.

Uncle Mortimer began by explaining the origins of Thanksgiving, which couldn’t be mentioned in their school. He started telling the story from England and talked about the Pilgrims, a group of Christians who wanted to worship God freely. They traveled to Holland to catch a boat to America, boarding a tiny ship called the Mayflower. They endured a grueling 65-day journey on the cramped ship, living on rotten food.

Upon arrival at Plymouth Rock, the Pilgrims were dirty, cramped, sick, and exhausted. They faced a harsh, unfamiliar environment with no houses or restaurants, just rocks, trees, and wild animals. As winter approached, they built shelters to keep warm, but many were starving and sick. By winter’s end, half of the Pilgrims had died, and the survivors were in dire condition.

Just as they were losing hope, someone watched them from behind the trees. A kind Indian came forward with his friend Squanto, who spoke perfect English. They taught the Pilgrims how to fish and plant crops, leading to an incredible harvest. The Pilgrims invited the Indians to join the first Thanksgiving dinner, praising God for their survival and honoring Him for bringing them to America.

Uncle Mortimer emphasized that this was a time of deep trouble for the Pilgrims, much like the struggles they faced today. He lamented that Thanksgiving had become a joke in modern times, offending God. He read from Psalms, warning that nations forgetting God would face judgment.

The family debated and argued about faith and the existence of God. Uncle Mortimer explained that Jesus was the one who keeps hearts beating, came to Earth to save people from hell, and suffered for humanity’s sins. He told how Jesus was crucified, died, and was buried, but rose again, conquering death and the grave.

Jesus opened the door to heaven for those who trust Him as their Savior, and Uncle Mortimer encouraged the family to pray and accept Jesus. Some were ashamed, some insulted him, and others rejected the message, but the kid at the table accepted and thanked Jesus.

Despite being saved, the kid faced hostility from the others, who were blinded by disbelief and mockery. Uncle Mortimer explained that without fear of God, people perish, and the preaching of the cross seemed foolish to some. The unbelievers mocked the saved kid, declaring he had been ruined, but the kid was the only one who chose salvation.

The story ended with the kid in a joyful state, thankful for Jesus and urging others to follow his example. The comic strip quoted Acts 16:31, encouraging belief in Jesus Christ for salvation.

Title: Monster, The
Subject: Bible Stories
Author: Chick
Responses:
A.J. was a man who believed he was the greatest. He felt wonderful, thought business was fantastic, and saw himself getting richer every day. His employees admired him, calling him a genius. But behind the scenes, A.J. was a harsh and demanding boss. He berated his secretary for not making a decent cup of coffee and threatened to replace her, calling her a "dumb broad." 

Despite his rudeness, one of his employees, Dudley, managed to close a $5 million deal with Japan. Instead of praise, A.J. flew into a rage that Dudley flew first class and fired him on the spot. A.J.’s anger and harsh words continued to alienate people, including Shirley Shepherd, who worked close to him. She described A.J. as a monster and had even stopped praying for him because of how awful he was. 

However, she was encouraged not to stop praying, as this was a battle for A.J.'s soul. She and some others prayed with scripture passages, asking God to intervene in his life. They prayed against Satan and spiritual wickedness influencing A.J.

A week later, things turned worse for A.J. The deal Dudley set up backfired, and the other company was suing them. Then came personal disasters — his son was arrested for selling drugs, his daughter was pregnant and heartbroken, and his wife’s lawyer served him divorce papers. His wife was suing him, and the children were siding with her. A.J. felt betrayed and cried out for help from Shirley.

Bob, one of A.J.'s contacts, saw how bad things had become and invited him to meet with Shirley and some others for help. A.J. was desperate for guidance after everything in his life had fallen apart.

Shirley shared a story from the Bible, found in Daniel chapter 4, about King Nebuchadnezzar — a powerful but ruthless and proud ruler. Nebuchadnezzar had a dream that troubled him deeply. In the dream, there was a great tree providing shelter to all animals, but a holy being from heaven came and cut down the tree, leaving only the stump. A voice said the king would be humbled, live like an ox, and experience judgment.

Daniel, the prophet, explained that this dream meant the king’s pride would cause his downfall unless he humbled himself and acknowledged God’s authority. Nebuchadnezzar did humble himself for one year, but then pride took control again. God then caused the king to lose his sanity and live like an animal for seven years. After this time, the king repented, recognized God's control, and his kingdom was restored.

Shirley told A.J. that his situation was similar. His pride made him like Nebuchadnezzar — arrogant and out of control, which led to his downfall and broken relationships. Shirley warned that God hates how he treated his family and employees and that he was on the path to destruction.

She explained that the only way to salvation was through Jesus Christ, who came as a human sacrifice to save people from their sins. Jesus' love was shown by His death, burial, and resurrection, offering eternal life to those who believe in Him.

A.J. realized his need for Jesus. He prayed from his heart, asking for forgiveness and inviting Jesus to take over his life. He promised to give God the glory. That day, A.J. was saved, and God took control of his life.

After this spiritual breakthrough, good things started to happen. The Japanese contract was secured again, Dudley was re-hired with a raise, and even A.J.'s family began to support him. People noticed a new A.J., one who was humble and changed because Jesus was now his partner.

This story showed how pride and arrogance can lead to destruction, but humility and faith in God bring restoration and blessing.

Title: Moving On Up!
Subject: Evolution
Author: Chick
Responses:
Once upon a time, a curious boy named Tyler asked his mother where they came from. His mother excitedly explained that in the beginning, everything came from goo. Tyler was fascinated and wanted to know where the goo had come from, but his mother said that only science knows that, and science knows everything.

His mother stressed the importance of always believing what scientists say because they are the ones who guide us, whereas others only claim to know. Tyler asked if they had looked like tiny dots when they lived in the goo, and his mother explained that initially, they were tiny, wiggling dots in the goo. Then, over time, the goo turned into water, and they became pollywogs that learned to swim. Eventually, they turned into fishes.

As evolution progressed, the fishes began to grow legs, moved onto land, and eventually evolved into monkeys. They lost their tails and began a long journey into what his mother called humanism. Millions of years later, humans became what they are today. Tyler was amazed and asked who told his mother all this.

His mother replied that their teacher had taught them this in school, so it must be true. Science calls this evolution, and through natural selection, the smartest and best of the species survived. Tyler, feeling superior because of his blonde hair and blue eyes, claimed he was part of the master race, looking down on those who didn't fit in his view.

Tyler's mother told him that since there is no God, evolution does away with morals, and that meant anything goes. Tyler declared himself a god, deciding right and wrong for himself. He believed nobody could tell him anything, and everything was relative.

Then, Tyler’s friend Cathy told Tyler she had been saved and was going to heaven. Tyler was skeptical and said there was no heaven according to science. She started explaining about Jesus and how He saved her. Tyler was confused, but Cathy told him everyone is a sinner and needs salvation.

A devilish figure told Tyler he was a god, not a sinner, questioning why Cathy didn’t realize that. Cathy explained that Jesus came to earth to save everyone because of sin, which started with Adam and Eve, the first people created by God who disobeyed Him. Sin had been passed down, but God sent Jesus to wash away their sins through His blood.

Jesus taught love and forgiveness and died for humanity's sins. Three days later, He rose from the dead, and Cathy shared her faith with Tyler, inviting him to accept Jesus as his Savior. Tyler was shocked and angry, rejecting her beliefs and calling her crazy. He boasted that since he was a god, he couldn’t go to hell.

Cathy warned him that rejecting Jesus meant going to hell, but Tyler laughed, saying he was a god and above all that. Tyler’s father praised evolution for making Tyler who he was and was proud of the schools teaching it.

One day, Tyler suddenly died. Cathy reminded him that she told him Jesus died for him, but he had rejected that gift. Now, Tyler faced the worst mistake ever – being separated from God forever, joining billions who believed they evolved from monkeys.

The story ends with a powerful call to wake up and accept Jesus before it’s too late.

Title: Murph
Subject: Catholicism
Author: Chick
Responses:
A robbery erupts at the Central Bank, causing panic among the employees. Mildred, an employee, accidentally sets off an alarm while clutching her slippers in shock. The robber demands everyone get on the floor and threatens to kill them if any alarm sounds.

Meanwhile, at the police station, an officer is informed about the robbery. As one officer requests a large sprinkled donut from Mildred, Murph exclaims how this always causes problems. Upon hearing the robbery report, Murph and his partner Joe rush to the scene. Joe warns Murph to stop using the Lord's name in vain, but Murph tells him to be quiet.

Backup is announced on the way, and Murph volunteers to enter the bank first. A violent gunfight ensues. Two hours later, Officer Donovan wakes up in the hospital with only flesh wounds, but he learns that Murph has been hit severely in the spleen and kidney and is not expected to live.

Thirty minutes later, Donovan questions why Murph risked his life for him. Murph expresses readiness to die and insists that Donovan isn't ready. Murph shares his hope of eternal life based on Biblical scriptures, quoting from 1 John 5:13 and John 3:36 about belief in Jesus and eternal life.

Donovan questions purgatory, but Murph insists it doesn't exist and says it was invented by the Catholic Church. They discuss that a God who truly loves would not want anyone living in ignorance of their eternal destiny. Murph asserts that God's word assures certainty about going to heaven.

Murph contemplates his Catholic faith and considers talking to his priest about his newfound beliefs. He warns that he must settle matters quickly as he is not going to make it. The priest tells him that his claim to know for sure he will go to heaven when he dies is a mortal sin called presumption, warning him against that.

The priest emphasizes the need for more than just the Bible, saying church tradition and the magisterium are essential. He insists that no one, not even popes, can know where they will go after death and states that purgatory is a church doctrine. He claims the Catholic Church is infallible on these matters.

Later, Joe returns to Murph and shares his own doubts about religion. He explains how he was once a Catholic but found no peace until a friend showed him salvation is a free gift, not dependent on church work. Joe says his spiritual eyes opened, realizing salvation comes through Christ, not a church.

Joe explains how Catholicism is deceptive, keeping people in bondage by relying on good works to earn heaven. Murph acknowledges Joe’s genuine hope from God's word, contrasting with the priest’s reliance on tradition. Joe urges Murph to choose between Christ or dead religion, warning that time is running out.

Murph decides to trust only in Christ’s sacrifice on the cross. Joe encourages prayer, and they pray together for Murph’s forgiveness, especially for trusting the Catholic Church over God. Murph expresses assurance and readiness to die, confident he is saved.

At 1:30 am, angels welcome Murph’s spirit into heaven. A message is directed to Catholic readers, challenging them to choose between sinful traditions and the word of God. It reminds that Catholicism requires earning heaven through good works, while God's word offers salvation as a free gift available immediately.

The story highlights the contrast between church tradition and Biblical teachings on salvation, urging belief in Jesus Christ alone for eternal life.

Title: Nervous Witch, The
Subject: Occult
Author: Chick
Responses:
A woman calls home while driving, telling her family she will be back in an hour with two big surprises. Her daughter, who is sitting inside and on the phone, says she hates surprises and worries about what they might be. The woman reveals she’s bringing along Uncle Bob, which causes the daughter to protest, saying she doesn’t want him in their house. The mother tells her daughter to show some respect.

Inside, the daughter explains that she is nervous about Uncle Bob because he reminds her of Jesus. The other daughter expresses disbelief, saying she’s never seen Uncle Bob do anything wrong and thinks of him as a good man. One of the girls then says Uncle Bob is an enemy and declares that she will cast a powerful love spell on him. Holly, presumably another daughter, warns her not to try that because they don’t know what they’re up against and asks what they should do.

The girls decide to go to their room and summon spirits for help with the situation. They agree to act quickly since they only have an hour. One suggests the other light the candles while she gets the robes, reminding her to think of Samantha. They chant “Witches rule!” proclaiming God is dead, churches are powerless, and that the old “Bible boy” won’t stand a chance against their black magic.

As they perform their ritual, it gets late, and nothing seems to be working. One of the girls voices concern and decides they should try again. Suddenly there’s a doorbell sound, which alarmed them — it’s their mother coming home. They rush to lock the door.

Their parents come in and call for Samantha to come say hello to Uncle Bob, but she’s hesitant. The mother instructs Samantha to get a rug to cover a pentagram drawn on the floor. The father encourages Samantha to stay calm and reminds her they are stronger than Uncle Bob. Then Uncle Bob introduces himself to Holly and Samantha. Holly warns Uncle Bob that she hates surprises, but their mother reassures her to stop it and everyone braces for the second surprise.

Suddenly, Holly declares she has been saved and received Jesus Christ as her Savior, and that her sins are gone. The mother is overjoyed, but the other girls gasp in horror, thinking this was impossible. Holly exclaims she never wants to sin again. She calls her mother to share the good news, while the others think of her as a "muggle" — a person who can’t do magic.

Holly explains that inside her she feels a spirit crying to be freed, and she calls to the Lord for help. Uncle Bob reassures her that it is her spirit guide reacting, and Holly is shocked he knew. Uncle Bob asks the witch girls if they want to hear a Bible story before leaving. They respond angrily, saying they do not believe in the Bible, fear nothing, and challenge him to tell it.

Uncle Bob recounts the story of when God gave Moses the Ten Commandments and outlawed witchcraft, which was punishable by death. He tells how King Saul, Israel’s first king, initially was humble but later grew rebellious and ignored God, who only spoke to the prophet Samuel. Saul asked his servants to find a woman with a familiar spirit to summon Samuel.

Saul disguised himself and visited the witch of Endor at night. When she summoned the spirit, it was Samuel, not one of her usual familiar spirits. Saul was confronted with a prophecy of defeat and death for himself and his sons. Later, Saul died in battle, and the witch died and went to hell.

Uncle Bob tells the girls that God hates both the wicked and workers of iniquity, meaning witches. He explains that anyone today who rejects Jesus Christ will end up in the lake of fire. Holly angrily rejects this and curses Uncle Bob, vowing to destroy him if necessary.

Uncle Bob prays for Holly to take back her curse and commands the spirit to come out of her in Jesus’ name. Holly screams as the spirit leaves her body.

Holly kneels and prays, asking Jesus for forgiveness and salvation, recognizing her sins. Later, Uncle Bob and the parents reflect on how Holly and Samantha got involved in witchcraft through Harry Potter books and other occult items like curses, magic spells, potions, ouija boards, and crystal balls. Samantha pledges to destroy all the occult junk in her room.

The story ends with the girls feeling empowered by their new Spirit within, the Holy Ghost, who grieves the evil around them. Uncle Bob gives advice to the girls: Samantha should read a King James Bible every day because Satan hasn’t messed with that version. They are urged to pray for other kids drawn to witchcraft, who are in trouble.

The comic closes with a warning that the children of darkness hate Jesus and will face judgment one day, leaving one’s only hope in believing in Jesus Christ to be saved.

Title: No Fear?
Subject: Suicide
Author: Chick
Responses:
Lance, feeling overwhelmed, declared to his friend that he was going to take his life on Friday night. His friend cheered him on, promising that if Lance went through with it, he would do the same at Lance’s funeral. Dolly, Lance's sister, was on the phone, and when asked if she was afraid, she confidently replied that her middle name was "No Fear." 

Lance was told not to tell anyone about his decision, except to confide in his sister. The conversation turned grim as his friends affirmed that suicide was the only solution, agreeing with a dark camaraderie. Dolly, however, wondered aloud about what happens after death, admitting she didn't know but insisted it had to be better than their current pain. Lance and his companions agreed with her as Lance professed his love for Dolly before making their fatal decision.

On Friday night, Lance prepared to jump, encouraged by his friends. After jumping, his friends celebrated, but Lance suddenly found himself in hell. Demons greeted him, explaining the eternal nature of his punishment – endless torment in a fiery abyss as described in biblical scriptures.

Lance was terrified, realizing the horror ahead. He questioned whether he was in hell for committing suicide, but the devil explained that hell was the fate for those who rejected Jesus Christ. Lance cried out in agony, with no escape from the eternal flames and torment.

Meanwhile, back at Lance’s funeral, Dolly confused and frantic, reached out to the preacher for urgent help, explaining that Lance had planned to kill himself during the funeral. They rushed to Dolly’s house, where she was about to do the same. The preacher and others arrived just in time, saving her from following through.

Dolly was shocked to learn she had been seconds away from hell herself. She expressed confusion because she and Lance believed suicide would solve all of their problems, but the preacher explained this was a lie from the devil. He shared important truths about hell, describing it as a place of devouring fire, weeping, eternal torment, and separation from God, citing various Bible verses.

Dolly realized that everyone who dies without trusting in Christ is destined for hell, including Lance. She was horrified, having almost been lost too. She mentioned how she had been lied to, believing hell was a party with friends, but now understood the grave reality.

The preacher explained that everyone deserves hell because all are sinners, and sin keeps people from heaven, but there is only one way to be saved: through Jesus Christ. He quoted John 14:6 and other scriptures, emphasizing God’s desire for all to repent and be saved.

Dolly learned about God's special gift—eternal life through Jesus Christ. The preacher described Jesus’ sinless life, sacrificial death, and resurrection as the payment for humanity’s sins. Dolly grasped the concept of grace and salvation through faith.

Moved by this, Dolly and others decided to accept Jesus that moment. They prayed for forgiveness and salvation, with Dolly expressing deep gratitude for being saved from hell. She joyfully reflected on how nearly going to hell was the darkest day of her life, but that day also marked her receiving eternal life.

The story ends with a hopeful message about salvation, mercy, and the forgiveness God offers to those who accept Jesus Christ as their Savior.

Title: No Justice?
Subject: Judgment Day
Author: Chick
Responses:
The story begins with a dramatic scene where witnesses identify a large man with a gun as the killer. An officer calls for backup, but the man loudly declares that no one offends the Prophet and lives. The officers attempt to stop him, warning they will fire, but the man resists, beating all the officers badly.

At the trial, the judge questions if it is true that no one read Mr. Ali his Miranda rights. The answer is yes, no one did. The judge explains that this means Mr. Ali’s civil rights were violated, so the law must be followed. Consequently, the judge apologizes to Mr. Ali and sets him free, prompting Mr. Ali to praise Allah.

The victim’s mother protests, demanding justice for her murdered son. She is ordered out of the courtroom by the bailiff for her disorderly conduct. Quietly, she laments how her husband died of cancer and now her son is gone, questioning where God’s love is.

The next day, the grieving mother, Mrs. Dempsey, receives a call from Charlie Dexter and his wife Jasmine, the wife of Eric, a man who played with her son Jimmy as a child. They want to visit and help. Mrs. Dempsey agrees.

During their visit, Jasmine shares that her husband Eric died stepping on a landmine in Afghanistan six months ago. Mrs. Dempsey is grateful for their visit. Charlie and Jasmine explain how they knew both Jimmy and Eric are with Jesus. Mrs. Dempsey is confused and wonders what they mean.

They clarify that her idea of "Bible God" as cruel was mistaken—Jesus is not the cruel God who judged the world but a loving and merciful one who came to save people from hell with the greatest act of love—His sinless blood wiped away humanity’s sins.

Charlie explains how Jesus raised the dead, healed the sick, and warned people of God’s judgment on sinners. Jesus let Himself be arrested and crucified, shedding His blood as a sacrifice for sinners. But through His resurrection, He saved souls and returned to heaven.

Mrs. Dempsey learns that to be saved, one must ask Jesus to forgive and come into their heart. When this is done, Jesus never leaves or forsakes the believer. Mrs. Dempsey trusts Jesus and is saved.

They discuss that many reject Jesus and will face judgment and the lake of fire. Jesus will return as a righteous judge, not gently, to bring true justice and peace, defeating evil at Armageddon.

Charlie explains that Jesus sent the Holy Ghost to guide believers, helping them understand the Bible and grow spiritually. The Holy Ghost also sanctifies believers and lets them know when they have done wrong.

They talk about God as a Trinity: God the Father, Jesus the Son who created everything, and the Holy Ghost who comforts and guides. Though no one has seen God the Father, many have seen Jesus, the Son of God, the exact image of the Father.

Mrs. Dempsey is invited to receive Jesus as her personal Savior—to believe He died for her sins and come into her heart. Those who do receive Jesus gain the Holy Ghost as their Comforter and enjoy eternal blessings. Those who reject Jesus lose forever and face eternal separation from God.

The story closes by emphasizing the critical choice everyone must make: to accept Jesus as Savior or be lost. It ends with a call to acknowledge one’s sin, believe in Jesus’ sacrifice, and commit to Him, recording the date as a marker of a new life.

Thus, from a tragedy and injustice springs the hope and offer of salvation through faith in Jesus Christ.

Title: No Way In?
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Daniels
Responses:
Once upon a time, atop a hill, there stood a magnificent castle filled with untold riches. The villagers nearby longed to gain access to these treasures, but they wondered how to get inside.

Determined, they attempted to climb the walls with ropes and grappling hooks, but these efforts failed as the ropes were cut. They then crafted enormous catapults, hoping to launch themselves over the walls, but this too was unsuccessful.

Some believed meditation might grant entry, professing that deep enlightenment would open the gates, and their followers paid dearly to hear about the elite life inside. Yet, these so-called sages were frauds, surviving only because others supported them, starved otherwise.

Despite their varied efforts—scheming, planning, and attacking—the great and the small, the rich and the poor, the wise and the foolish all failed to breach the castle walls.

One day, a little child approached the castle quietly and noticed a small door. She knocked gently, and the door opened. She stepped inside unnoticed while the others were too preoccupied with their futile plots to break in by force.

Eventually, people realized that their strength and wisdom could not grant entry; only by acknowledging the door and knocking were they welcomed inside. However, many dismissed this easy way, suspecting a trick or refusing to believe such a simple solution could exist.

The door had been there all along, offering a straightforward path into the castle—yet many preferred to forge their own difficult way. This door symbolizes the humble entrance to God's kingdom described in the Bible, where Jesus said, "I am the door: by me if any man enter in, he shall be saved" (John 10:9).

Like the castle's villagers, people tend to seek their path to happiness and heaven through selfish means, but God's way is the true right way because God is wholly good. Solomon, the wisest man, admitted no one is without sin, and the Bible reiterates that all have sinned and fall short of God's glory.

God desires a perfect relationship with us in His heaven, but as sinners driven by our own ways, we cannot enter on our own merits. There is a divine "book of life" that records who may enter heaven; if one's name is not written there, the penalty for sins must be paid.

What if someone else could pay that penalty? But this substitute would need to be perfect.

That substitute is Jesus, God's Son from heaven. Though divine, Jesus humbled Himself, becoming a servant, living as a man, willingly dying on the cross for our sins, and rising again after three days.

By conquering sin, death, and hell, Jesus opened the way into heaven. The Bible declares that every knee shall bow and every tongue confess He is Lord.

The only way to heaven is by admitting we are sinners, believing in Jesus' saving sacrifice, and accepting Him as Lord. Jesus taught that to enter God's kingdom, we must be "converted, and become as little children."

Having the simple faith of a child means acknowledging our need for help and trusting Jesus. When we knock on His door with that faith, He promises to open it and welcome us in.

He said, "Him that cometh to me I will in no wise cast out" (John 6:37).

The invitation stands: admit you are a sinner, believe Jesus died for you, ask Him to forgive you, and enter into a life with Him—forever welcomed inside the eternal kingdom.

Title: Now or Never
Subject: Basic Gospel
Tag(s): ['Black Tract Series', 'Most Recent', 'Older Children and Adults']
Author: Cater
Responses:
The story begins by stating that throughout life, everyone makes choices. Some choices are right, and some are mistakes. However, there is one choice more important than all others. It is vital to make the right decision before you die.

George anticipates that the difficult choice will be between God and the devil, but he is told he is wrong. Most people will end up in hell because they think the wrong way. The importance of hearing the truth is emphasized.

George learns that he has a terrible enemy—the devil—who hates him and desires to have him in hell forever. At the same time, he has a powerful friend, God, who loves him and wants him to be with Him in heaven.

Satan was originally created as Lucifer, whose job was to cover God’s throne. But Lucifer became proud, rebelled against God, and was kicked out of heaven, becoming Satan. When Adam and Eve were created, they were tempted by Satan and they sinned, causing sin to be passed down to all people. Because of sin, everyone is born spiritually dead and destined for damnation in hell.

Satan knows there is only one way to escape hell's flames and works hard to prevent people from discovering it. He uses religion to keep billions in bondage and employs education, peer pressure, and distractions like sports to keep people from accepting this truth.

God knew people were spiritually dead, so He sent His Son, Jesus Christ, to earth. Jesus was born a virgin, lived a sinless life for 33 years, and sacrificed His life on the cross to pay for humanity's sins. Three days later, Jesus rose from the dead, defeating death and Satan.

The only way to escape hell is through faith in Jesus Christ. Though it sounds too easy to George, he learns that Jesus promised everlasting life to those who believe in Him. Those who trust Jesus as their Savior are born into God’s family and receive eternal life.

It’s like George initially thought—there is a choice between God and the devil. But you do not have to choose the devil; if you don’t choose Jesus, you are already condemned and headed for hell. This truth is terrifying for George, and he worries about his family and loved ones.

He questions what about the billions of religious people who don’t believe this, thinking God wouldn’t send all of them to hell. He is told that Jesus said no one comes to the Father except through Him, and He is the only Savior who can rescue from eternal damnation.

George is assured that this is all recorded in the Word of God, the Bible, which is inspired and profitable for teaching righteousness.

Relieved to have learned the truth, George decides he wants to be saved. He asks what to do and is told to sincerely repent, turn to God, and believe in Jesus Christ as Savior.

George prays, asking Jesus to forgive all his sins and makes Jesus his choice, trusting Him as his Savior.

Finally, the story urges the reader to make their own choice. If they choose Jesus Christ, their sins will be forgiven and they will receive God’s free gift of eternal life. But if they do nothing, they remain condemned and headed for hell.

The story ends with a call to choose Christ right now.

Title: One More Step
Subject: Basic Gospel
Responses:
Once upon a time, there was a curious squirrel who spotted a large acorn resting on a patch of grass. The squirrel excitedly approached it, thinking it had found a treasure. However, as the squirrel picked up the acorn, it suddenly snapped shut, trapping the animal inside. The squirrel was shocked and scared, realizing it had been caught in a trap.

The shadowy figure behind the bars cackled, "I caught you! You walked into my trap! Now you're mine!" A mischievous boy grinned as he taunted the trapped squirrel, proclaiming that the squirrel's mistake was taking that last step, because that was its doom. Proudly, the boy declared he was smarter and would never fall into such a trap. The squirrel, frightened, vowed it would never get caught like the boy.

As Logan grew older, he confidently boasted that he'd never repeat such a mistake. But temptation crept into his life. One day, Logan decided "just one sip" of alcohol wouldn't hurt, but then he had to stop himself from taking more. Later, he celebrated being completely sober at a party, but when a girl offered him a cigarette, he tried "just one toke."

Unfortunately, Logan couldn't resist. He was busted—caught by friends who laughed, saying he couldn't stop himself. Again, a girl named Sofia intervened, warning Logan about the danger he was in, urging him to stop.
