Logan was dismissive, claiming he wasn’t doing anything dangerous and justified his choices by saying he only did it once and was still safe.

Sofia became serious, telling Logan that everything he did was dangerous. One time might be the last time, and then he'd be dead and in hell. Logan tried to calm her down, saying she was extreme, but she insisted God wouldn't allow sin in heaven, and it was a one-way ticket to doom. She pressed that Logan didn't understand God at all.

When Logan challenged her to explain, Sofia spoke about God making everything—even humans—so they could be with Him forever. But the cost of sin was death. God had people sacrifice spotless animals to cover their sins, but there weren’t enough animals to cover all the world’s sins. Someone had to be punished for all the sin, but no one on earth was perfect enough to pay that price.

That’s why God sent His Son from heaven to live as a perfect man—the spotless sacrifice for humanity’s sins. Jesus died, was buried, and three days later rose from the grave, offering forgiveness for sins.

Sofia urged Logan to admit he was a sinner and take one more step: believe in Jesus Christ who shed His blood for him. Logan hesitated, angrily refusing to take that step.

Later, Logan was offered drugs with the promise of trying “just one” thing once. He accepted, saying he’d try anything once, only to find himself trapped in a dark place. The same devilish figure from before appeared, furious that Logan still hadn’t taken that one more step and accepted Jesus. The figure declared, “You’re mine!”

The story ended with a call to action, asking if the reader would admit they're a sinner, believe in Jesus, and receive forgiveness, so they would not fall into that same trap.

Title: One Way!
Subject: Basic Gospel
Tag(s): ['Little Children', 'Most Popular Titles', 'Older Children and Adults']
Author: Chick
Responses:
Once upon a time in a beautiful garden, a glowing figure approached a man and a woman, the first human beings. The figure warned them, "No!" as the woman reached for a fruit from a tree. This tree was forbidden and marked with the word "Sin." Despite the warning, the woman ate the fruit, and the man followed. Their once pure and glowing bodies became covered in marks and shame.

The glowing figure then began to build a great wall, separating the couple and all their descendants from Himself. The people, now marked by sin, faced separation and darkness. They walked through a vast space filled with heat and sorrow, approaching a massive fortress.

Signs along the way invited them with messages like "Love Gift Ahead," "Free Gift Ahead," and "God's Love Gift Inside." Eventually, they entered a passage marked "Welcome," with pictures of a mother and child, a journey, and the crucifixion of Jesus on the walls. A sign pointed the way forward: "One Way."

As they moved along, these images told the story of God's free love gift — Jesus, who died on the cross. Some people, touched by this love, knelt before the cross, hearts opened. They transformed, shedding their burdens and walking joyfully.

However, not everyone chose the path of love. One boy ignored the guidance and wandered in the darkness, eventually becoming consumed by it. Despite the invitation and warnings, he turned away, rejoining the crowd in despair.

Meanwhile, those who embraced the gift found stairs leading upwards. Two joyous children climbed toward light and freedom, welcomed by the glowing figure and Jesus, surrounded by countless others in eternal joy.

The story concludes with a powerful message: “For God so loved the world, that He gave His only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in Him should not perish, but have everlasting life.” — John 3:16.

Title: Only Hope, The
Subject: End Time Prophecy
Author: Carter
Responses:
The story begins with a portrayal of the wickedness of humanity as seen through a biblical lens. Despite being gods in their own eyes, people revel in sinful and evil acts such as drug use, incest, murder, and torture. Chaos and immorality reign as men fight over women, disregarding the sanctity of marriage.

God, seeing the corruption on earth, repents creating mankind and decides to destroy them. Meanwhile, Satan's influence grows as people worship him for his power and evil deeds. The earth becomes completely corrupt with all flesh succumbing to sin. 

However, God finds favor with a man named Noah, instructing him to build an ark out of gopher wood to save himself, his family, and pairs of animals from a forthcoming flood destined to destroy all living creatures on earth. People mock Noah and doubt the coming flood, but he faithfully obeys God’s commands.

The flood lasts for 40 days and 40 nights, covering the earth in water and killing every living thing not in the ark. Once the flood passes, Noah and those with him in the ark remain alive, repopulating the earth.

The story then shifts to future prophecy. God destroys the world once more, but this time with fire. Jesus himself foretold the end times, comparing it to the days of Noah when people were oblivious to the impending doom until it was too late. 

Jesus promises a "Blessed Hope," when he will return with great power and glory, gathering his faithful followers. However, no one knows the exact time of this event except God the Father. The Bible proclaims Jesus as the Creator and Judge of the world, warning of great tribulations before his return.

The narrative details the rise of an evil system called "Mystery Babylon," representing the antichrist's kingdom, which persecutes believers and gains control of the world. The last Pope is said to be the antichrist, working to unite the nations under his influence.

God’s wrath will be poured out with plagues, disasters, and wars leading to the Battle of Armageddon where evil forces, including Russia and Islamic armies, attack Israel. Despite overwhelming odds, God intervenes to save Jerusalem and judge the wicked.

Following the battle, Christ returns on a white horse, defeating Satan and his armies. The antichrist and false prophet are cast into the lake of fire, and Christ reigns for a thousand years in peace. All people stand before God’s great white throne for final judgment, with those not found in the Book of Life condemned to eternal damnation.

The story ends with a warning: moral conditions today mirror those of Noah’s time, and only by trusting Jesus Christ—the Lord and Savior—can people hope to be saved from the coming judgment and receive eternal life. The final hope for the world lies in Jesus Christ’s return.

Title: Only Way, The
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Carter
Responses:
In a beautiful garden, a man and a woman are holding hands with a glowing, faceless figure in a flowing robe, under a tree with ripe fruit. Nearby, a serpent watches them, smiling slyly. The glowing figure warns, "No!" as it points toward a tree laden with forbidden fruit, cautioning them not to eat from it. However, the man and woman gaze longingly at the fruit.

The woman reaches and plucks the fruit from the tree, despite the warning, and both she and the man become ashamed, covering themselves with leaves as a skull and crossbones symbol labeled "SIN" appears on the tree.

Feeling the effects of their disobedience, the man and woman hide and shiver in sorrow and shame. The glowing figure then builds a large wall between itself and the couple, separating them further. The couple, now brimming with guilt, try to cleanse themselves in water, but the dirt of sin remains, clinging to their bodies.

Soon, they have children, who are also stained with the mark of sin. The family and many others are seen walking away from the glowing figure, separated by the high wall. On the other side of the wall, signs read "LOVE GIFT AHEAD," "FREE GIFT AHEAD," and "GOD'S LOVE GIFT INSIDE," but many choose to stay on the wrong side, where flames and darkness threaten them.

Some people begin to approach the door in the wall that leads to God's love gift. When they enter, they see images depicting the story of Jesus — His birth, His suffering, His crucifixion on the cross, and His resurrection, all under a sign that says "ONE WAY." The children gaze at the cross, labeled "GOD'S FREE LOVE GIFT." 

Among a few skeptical people, three children look at the cross with hearts above their heads and kneel, accepting the gift with joy. Streams of love rain down from the cross onto them, making them happy and free. They dance and celebrate, pointing to and inviting others to join them. Meanwhile, a man who refuses the love gift glares angrily and is left alone in the dark.

People turn away from the gift, wandering the path of sin, but one man changes his mind, follows the signs, and enters through the door labeled "GOD'S LOVE GIFT INSIDE." He joins the children upstairs, smiling and ascending steps together. 

The final scene shows the faceless glowing figure welcoming the children with open arms as joyful music and a dove fill the air. The story ends with the verse from John 3:16: 

“For God so loved the world, that He gave His only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in Him should not perish, but have everlasting life.”

Title: Oops!
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Carter
Responses:
A crowd gathered in alarm when a man named Bobby was found overdosing on speed. Friends and onlookers expressed shock and sorrow, remembering how Bobby had mentioned he was going to do it but wasn’t believed. Despite attempts to save him, Bobby died, leading to grim reflections about his fate.

An older man posed a serious question: where would Bobby spend eternity? Some in the crowd questioned the idea of judgment and eternal loss, calling one man a fanatic for suggesting Bobby was eternally lost if he hadn't accepted Jesus Christ as his Savior. This led to a discussion where the older man cited biblical scripture, explaining that all have sinned and are separated from God, emphasizing the need for salvation through Jesus Christ.

A skeptical man challenged these claims, calling the Bible contradictory and dismissing the religious talk. In response, another person defended the Bible as God’s inspired word, insisting that understanding is key. The skeptic eventually grew impatient and left, but one curious individual decided to listen more.

The conversation continued, clarifying that Jesus Christ came to earth, died for humanity's sins, rose again, and offers salvation to those who trust in Him. The skeptic angrily rejected this, accusing the believers of fear-mongering and outdated beliefs. Yet, a card was handed over, urging acceptance of Christ to gain eternal life or face eternal loss.

Tensions escalated as the skeptic and others argued vehemently, but one person stood firm in his faith. Later, the skeptic tried to justify a life without sin, but the believer persisted, emphasizing the need for Jesus beyond just good deeds or teachings.

On a drive, the skeptic was distracted by an oncoming train. An urging voice told him he could make it across the tracks, but he hesitated too long and was tragically struck by the train.

The skeptic then found himself in a place of torment, not a temporary purgatory but a place awaiting final judgment by God. Despite wanting Jesus as his Savior now, he was told it was too late since he had died in his sins.

A former friend confronted him, accusing him of being wrong about the choices and beliefs he once espoused. The skeptic screamed in despair, and a devilish figure revealed that his true fate was sealed because he had never accepted Jesus as his personal Savior.

The story ends with a powerful warning about the consequences of rejecting the gospel message and not accepting salvation through Jesus Christ.

Title: Outcast, The
Subject: Bible Stories
Author: Chick
Responses:
One evening, there was a sudden knock at Janet's door. When she asked who it was, a distressed voice called out, "It's Shirley Shepherd. I need help!" Janet, alarmed by the desperation in Shirley’s voice, opened the door to find her in a terrible state. "Shirley... Oh, Shirley! What happened?" Janet asked, horrified. Shirley pleaded, "Help me!"

Without hesitation, Janet guided Shirley inside and said, "I’m calling an ambulance. Oh, Shirley, I’m so sorry." Shirley, shaking her head, begged Janet not to call for help, "No, no... Janet! I’m not worth it. Please don’t!" As Janet tried to comfort her, she asked, "Shirley, who did this to you?" Shirley looked at her battered face and replied, "My pimp!"

Soon, Bob and Helen arrived with medicine, clothes, and extra food. Helen suggested, "Maybe I can talk to her." Bob then said, "I’ll leave you ladies alone for a while so you can talk." Janet expressed her gratitude, "Thanks, Bob." Helen added, "Let’s help this poor girl get to bed."

Two hours later, Shirley shared her painful story. She explained how after her father abandoned them, her mother remarried Hank, who couldn't work. "So Mom got a job and then it started," she said, tears streaming down her bruised face. She recalled turning seven when the abuse began. "I tried to tell you in high school, but I was ashamed. Do you know why I dropped out?"

Shirley explained that she finally stood up to Hank and exposed him, but he beat her and threw her out of the house. "That’s when I hit the streets and died inside," she said. She spiraled into drugs and did tricks to pay for her habit, losing all hope and giving up on God. "God couldn’t want to have anything to do with a person like me... I’m absolutely filthy!" she sobbed. "Last night I told my pimp it was over... and he beat me worse than Hank did."

Helen comforted her, saying, "I know of a prostitute that God loved. Wanna hear about it?" Shirley nodded, hesitant but curious.

Helen began the story of a prostitute from the city of Jericho. After Moses died, Joshua was told to bring the Israelites into the Promised Land. God sent two of Joshua’s men to spy on Jericho. A prostitute named Rahab took the spies into her home to hide them from the king’s men. Rahab convinced the spies to leave her city, promising to protect them in return. Believing in the God of the Israelites, she made a pact with the spies to save her family if Jericho was destroyed.

God commanded Joshua’s army to silently march around Jericho for seven days. On the seventh day, they shouted, blew their trumpets, and the walls crumbled. The troops conquered the city but spared Rahab and her family, honoring her because she trusted God.

Rahab became part of Israel and was greatly honored. A man named Salmon fell deeply in love with her. Rahab even became the great-grandmother of King David — and an ancestor of Jesus Christ Himself.

Shirley was amazed by the story. "Bob, Helen just told me the wonderful story of Rahab... God even loves prostitutes!" Helen nodded, "He sure does, and let me tell you about Jesus."

Shirley asked, "Was Jesus Christ a man of God?" Bob explained, "He was God. Jesus loved us so much, He left heaven to become a man.” He said Jesus treated women like Shirley with dignity and respect.

He reminded her of when a woman caught in adultery was about to be stoned. Jesus said, "He that is without sin among you, let him cast the first stone." The stone-throwers dropped their stones and walked away. Jesus told the woman, "Neither do I condemn thee: go and sin no more."

Another time, Jesus told religious leaders, "Verily I say unto you, the publicans (tax collectors) and the harlots (prostitutes) go into the kingdom of God before YOU."

Religious leaders hated Jesus and secretly plotted to kill Him. They crucified Him, and Jesus shed His precious blood to wash away all sins, including those of prostitutes, pimps, sinners, and murderers — everybody.

But that wasn’t the end. Three days later, Jesus rose from the dead. "Jesus loves you, Shirley," Bob said. "He wants you to spend all eternity in heaven with Him."

He asked Shirley, "Wouldn't you like your sins completely forgiven?" Shirley’s eyes filled with hope. "You mean there’s a chance I can get to heaven?" Bob reassured her: "Absolutely. If you give your life to Him, He will never leave nor forsake you."

Bob told Shirley she needed to pray and confess her sins to Jesus, receive Him as Savior. Shirley knelt down and prayed, "Oh, Jesus, I love you. Please forgive me of my sins. Please come into my heart and be my Lord and Savior."

Suddenly, Shirley cried out with joy, "WOW! I can't believe it! He did! I’m clean! Oh Jesus, thank you! Thank you!"

She hugged Janet and said, "Oh, Janet! Thank you for calling Bob and Helen! I feel like I’ve got a new family! I’m not an outcast anymore. I never want to sin again."

The story ends with a message for those who have been abused and feel no one cares to come to Jesus, who is always waiting with open arms, ready to forgive and welcome anyone who turns to Him in repentance.

Title: Outsider, The
Subject: Bible Stories
Author: Carter & 3rd
Responses:
Around 1320 B.C., during a famine that covered Israel, the land was dry and desperate. Elimelech and his family found their well had dried up and were forced to leave Bethlehem to find food and water in Moab, despite it being a nation hostile to their God. Elimelech’s wife, Naomi, was bitter about leaving their homeland to live in such an idolatrous place.

Elimelech’s two sons disobeyed God by marrying Moabite women, Orpah and Ruth. But after some years, a disaster struck and both of Naomi's sons died, leaving Naomi widowed and Ruth and Orpah as widows as well. Life in Moab had been harsh and full of loss.

When the famine ended, Naomi decided to return home. She encouraged Orpah and Ruth to return to their families. Orpah left, but Ruth refused to abandon Naomi. Ruth pledged to stay with Naomi, saying, “Where thou goest, I will go... thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God.”

Back in Bethlehem, Naomi and her Moabite daughter-in-law Ruth faced hardship and exclusion, being on the lowest rung of Jewish society. Naomi had a wealthy relative named Boaz, a man who loved the Lord and owned many fields. During the barley harvest, Ruth asked Naomi if she could glean kernels from the fields to survive. Naomi agreed, and Ruth went to Boaz’s field.

Boaz noticed Ruth’s kindness and diligence. He protected her and assured her safety if she worked in his fields. Touched by her humility, Boaz spoke kind words and promised that the Lord would reward her for her loyalty and goodness.

Naomi instructed Ruth to follow an old custom of the near kin by going to lie at Boaz’s feet on the threshing floor at midnight, urging him to take up his role as a kinsman redeemer. When Boaz awoke, Ruth introduced herself and asked him to fulfill this duty. Boaz was moved and blessed Ruth, acknowledging her virtuous character.

However, Boaz revealed there was a closer relative with a prior claim. He said he would settle the matter with that man. Ruth prayed for God to give her Boaz instead. Boaz confronted the other kinsman, who agreed to relinquish his rights after Boaz paid the price but refused to marry Ruth. Boaz then completed the deal.

Ruth and Boaz married, saving Naomi and Ruth from poverty and continuing the family line. They were blessed with a son, Obed, who became the grandfather of King David. Through David's lineage came the Savior of the world, Jesus Christ.

Boaz, a kinsman redeemer, had to be related, wealthy, and willing. He redeemed Ruth, a Gentile widow and outsider, fulfilling her only hope. Like Ruth, all people are outsiders because of sin and need a redeemer who can pay the price for them.

Jesus Christ, Creator of the universe, is that redeemer. The Bible says in John 3:16 that God loved the world so much He gave His only Son, so whoever believes in Him will have eternal life. Jesus suffered and shed His blood to wash away our sins and rose victoriously from the dead.

Jesus can be your redeemer if you let Him. Accept Him as your Savior and Lord, and you will reign with Him in heaven forever.

Title: Papa
Subject: Catholicism
Author: Chick
Responses:
A breaking news broadcast announces the death of the Holy Father, the Pope, who passed away at 3:10 in the morning. The world is stunned, mourning the loss of this highly revered religious figure. Presidents, kings, and dictators from across the globe are expected to come to the Vatican to pay their final respects.

Curious about why the Pope is called "His Holiness," a man named Jimmy asks, and he's told it’s because the Pope is the world's most holy man, loved by over a billion Christians, as he is considered God's representative on earth. Jimmy wonders if he can read about the Pope in the Bible, but is cautioned that only the Catechism, the official book of Catholic teachings, reveals the glory of the Pope. The Bible alone might confuse him.

Jimmy is surprised by this and admits he's not Catholic. An older man explains he once looked into the Pope’s eyes and found it like looking at the face of God, but now the Pope is dead. Jimmy thinks it might be a good idea to talk to a priest, but his Uncle Frank warns him to stay away from Father Flannigan.

Later, Uncle Frank reveals the Pope has been arrested over something involving altar boys. He explains that if the Pope is the holiest man, why isn't everyone Catholic? Jimmy is left puzzled.

The story shifts to a conversation with Mr. Powell on a farm. A reporter asks about the Pope's death, but Mr. Powell mistakes "Pope" for "Caesar," explaining they are essentially the same. He reveals that the papacy is just a continuation of the Caesars' power, dressed in different costumes, maintaining control over the world from Rome.

When the Caesars ruled, absolute power corrupted them, and they saw themselves as gods but were actually puppets of Satan. Jesus Christ left heaven during Caesar Augustus's reign to be born on earth, taking on the form of flesh. He is God, and His purpose was to fix the sin problem — the reason sin cannot enter heaven is that God won't allow it.

Jesus shed His blood to wash away sins so believers could enter heaven. He died and was resurrected on the third day, paying the full price for sin. This act ruined Satan's control, causing many to leave Satan and find salvation in Christ. Enraged, Satan commanded his Caesars to slaughter Christians.

Years later, when Rome was in ruins and the Caesars gone, an obelisk—symbolizing Satan—stood on Vaticanus hill, the place of Satan’s bloody sacrifices. Satan created his own form of Christianity there. His “new” religion brought back the Caesars' power under new titles, such as the Pope, and a magnificent Roman temple was built: the Vatican.

Today, Rome still holds power over the world beneath the surface. Catholicism controls its members from birth to death, wielding immense influence and power, but the question remains whether Jesus approves of this.

The story then follows a boy named Anthony, born into a Catholic family. He is baptized into the Roman system because, without baptism, he would go to limbo. This marks the beginning of his journey as a faithful Catholic, hoping for heaven.

Anthony learns to fear and love his priest, Father O’Tool, deemed a “divine man” equal to Jesus, and the Holy Ghost is seen as more powerful than the Virgin Mary. Father O'Tool performs mass, during which he pronounces the words of consecration, believed to transform bread into the really incarnate body of Jesus — a wafer god to be adored.

Anthony then takes his first communion, believing the wafer contains the "body, soul, and divinity" of Christ, and later goes through confirmation, said to bind him to the Church. He must also regularly confess to Father O’Tool to rid himself of sins, and before dying, he must receive last rites—anointing of the sick.

Despite his devout faith, Anthony is burdened with many rituals: prayers, servings, and offerings to the Mother Church and saints, while Jesus remains in the background. Religious life for him is full of obligations, yet he wonders what lies ahead.

After all these religious practices, Uncle Frank explains to Jimmy that the one thing Satan loves most is Purgatory, a religious scam wherein souls must pay off sins by suffering after death before entering heaven. Even good Catholics must be “burned off” in purgatory, paying priests for masses to release them. This is likened to religious kidnapping and a money tree for the Church.

Jimmy is stunned that people might be trapped in purgatory forever. Uncle Frank clarifies that Anthony isn’t in purgatory but hell, the greatest deception Satan ever invented.

He goes on to explain that precious Catholics do their works all their lives yet end in hell. But Jesus said eternal life comes from believing on Him. That’s the simple path to salvation.

Catholicism cares more about money than souls, but Jesus paid for all sins once and for all. After Jesus rose from the dead and returned to heaven, He warned the faithful to come out of the corrupt system of the Vatican. He doesn’t want anyone to be ruined by it.

In the end, Jimmy asks if Jesus will save him, and the answer is yes, if he receives Jesus. He is urged not to believe lies like purgatory but to trust in the Lord Jesus Christ and be saved. The story closes with the reminder that salvation depends on whom you trust — this corrupt system or God.

Title: Party Girl
Subject: Drugs/Alcohol
Author: Chick
Responses:
The festival was set to begin in two weeks, and at Satan's headquarters, the devil ordered a full report from all divisions. His minion proudly informed him that the city was loaded with drugs and alcohol, the music was arranged with the hottest groups in the world, and the warehouses were stocked with low-grade condoms, ready to be distributed by hundreds of volunteers. Satan was confident that the souls of all the partygoers would belong to him and was determined not to lose a single one.

Meanwhile, 3,000 miles away, Rita Jones was awakened at 4 a.m. by a divine message. She understood she had to warn her granddaughter Jill, who was staying at the Hotel Orleans to attend the festival.

Rita prayed earnestly, knowing Satan wanted Jill dead. Back at Satan's headquarters, a messenger brought bad news—Rita Jones was on her way to stop the festival. Satan was furious, referring to Rita as an old thorn in his side for twenty years and swore to kill Jill that very night for revenge.

At the festival, Rita asked for directions to the Hotel Orleans, two blocks away. Inside Club Paradise, Jill was partying and having the time of her life, celebrating with friends.

At the bar, Satan and one of his minions gloated, confident that Jill would soon be in hell. Satan's minion reminded him he was always in control, and Satan triumphantly declared, "Bye, bye Jill. I won again."

Crowds at the festival were asked about Jill, and some reported seeing her enter the hotel. Jill raised a toast with her friends, saying, "To long life!" and vowed to drink to that.

Suddenly, a man pulled Jill aside, urging her to come with him immediately because it was a matter of life and death. Jill gasped, pleading for him not to leave. The man was determined not to let her drink go to waste.

Four minutes later, a commotion ensued outside the hotel. Someone called for an ambulance, but it was too late—Jill was dead.

At the hotel, Jill’s friend Debbie was horrified and embarrassed, explaining that her crazy grandma said God told her to come and save Jill’s life.

The truth soon came out: the drink Jill had consumed was poisoned. Her friends struggled to comprehend what was happening.

Jill’s grandmother explained that Jill had an unseen enemy—Satan—who had been planning her destruction for years. Satan had used drugs, alcohol, and immoral behavior to keep her away from the Savior.

Jill asked, “But Grandma, how could God ever forgive all the rotten things I’ve done?”

Her grandmother comforted her, saying that no matter what Jill had done, God still loved her and wanted to forgive and change her life forever. However, there was only one way to get her sins forgiven, through Jesus Christ.

The grandmother recited scriptures explaining God's love, how Jesus Christ was sent to shed His blood to pay the penalty for sins and how He defeated Satan through His death and resurrection. This victory made a way for people trapped in sin to be set free.

Jill began to see the mess she had made of her life and how much she needed Jesus. Her grandmother assured her that God’s Word gives exact instructions on what to do next: repent, turn to God, receive Jesus Christ by faith, and receive God's gift of love.

Jill prayed earnestly, asking the Lord Jesus to forgive her sins and come into her heart as her Savior. She felt free for the first time in her life and experienced joy in her heart.

Back at the festival, Satan was furious that his plan was foiled. He urged people to keep partying and not believe any of the warnings. But Rita Jones urged everyone to stop believing Satan's lies and to trust Christ right away.

Thus, Jill’s life was saved through the power of Jesus Christ, overcoming Satan’s plan and finding new life in faith.

Title: Passover Plot, The
Subject: Bible Stories
Author: Chick
Responses:
For over 400 years, the children of Israel were slaves to the Egyptians, crying out to God for deliverance. Around the year 1446 B.C., God raised up a man named Moses to be Israel’s savior. Both Moses and his brother Aaron were sent to Egypt with a message: God would harden Pharaoh’s heart and send plagues upon Egypt, and Moses was to ask Pharaoh to free God’s people from slavery so they could serve the Lord.

Pharaoh’s response was defiant. He asked, “Who is the Lord that I should obey His voice to let Israel go? I do not know the Lord, nor will I let Israel go!” God then commanded Moses and Aaron to perform signs, and the first plague struck Egypt: the waters of Egypt turned to blood, causing fish to die and the river to stank, making the water undrinkable.

Next, God sent frogs to cover Egypt. The frogs even invaded Pharaoh’s bed. Pharaoh promised to let Israel go if God took away the frogs. When the frogs died and were piled in heaps, Pharaoh still refused to free Israel. 

The third plague turned the dust of Egypt into lice, causing great discomfort among the people. Pharaoh’s magicians could replicate some plagues but failed to bring forth lice, which they recognized as the “finger of God.” Yet Pharaoh’s heart remained hardened.

The fourth plague brought swarms of flies that covered Egypt, but not the land where the Israelites lived. Following this, a grievous disease struck the horses, sheep, camels, and oxen of Egypt, killing all the cattle, but none of the livestock belonging to the children of Israel.

Boils broke out on all Egyptians during the sixth plague. In the seventh, hail mingled with fire destroyed the crops. Locusts then attacked Egypt, devouring anything the hail missed. For three days and three nights, a darkness so thick could be felt covered the land, yet Pharaoh still refused to let Israel go.

God instructed the Israelites to borrow silver and gold from their Egyptian neighbors, granting them favor. Every Jewish household was told to take a lamb without blemish, kill it, and apply its blood to the doorposts with hyssop. This would be their Passover Lamb. God declared that when He saw the blood, He would pass over that house and spare them from the impending final judgment.

That night, a great cry went through Egypt for no home was left without a death. Pharaoh finally relented and freed the Israelites after 400 years of bondage. God commanded them to hold an annual feast to remember the Passover, symbolizing deliverance from death.

Fourteen centuries later, during a time when Israel was under Roman rule, many Egyptians sought another savior but missed the one God had promised. Prophecies foretold a virgin would conceive a son named Immanuel (meaning God with us). Jesus, known as the Lamb of God, was introduced by John the Baptist and would become the ultimate Passover Lamb, sacrificed to take away the sins of the world.

During a Passover feast in Jerusalem, Jesus was crucified as His prophecies were fulfilled. Jesus’ body was placed in a tomb, where religious leaders, fearing His resurrection, had it guarded by Roman soldiers. Three days later, an angel rolled away the stone, the guards turned to "dead men" in fear, and Jesus rose. Women who came to His tomb were told He had risen, and the news spread rapidly.

To discredit the resurrection, religious leaders bribed soldiers to say Jesus’ disciples stole His body. However, a respected Pharisee named Gamaliel advised the leaders that if the resurrection was not from God, it would fail, but if it was, it could not be overthrown.

Those who had prepared by applying the lamb’s blood were spared from judgment, and God’s protection passed over them. Those who accept Jesus as Lord and Savior, the true Passover Lamb, are protected from spiritual judgment. Rejecting Him leaves one vulnerable to eternal separation.

Thus, the story of the Passover from Egypt to the sacrifice of Jesus reveals God’s plan for salvation and deliverance, fulfilled through prophecy and fulfilled again for all who believe.

Title: Payback
Subject: Bible Stories
Author: Chick
Responses:
Alan worked as a nurse for Mr. John Wilson Banks, a rich old man who lived in an enormous house. Kelli, the nurse, reminded Mr. Banks to take his medicine and promised she’d be back in the morning. Mr. Banks appreciated Kelli, calling her his favorite nurse. Alan, driving away, marveled at the size of Mr. Banks’s house and confided to Kelli that he hated the old man. Alan believed they deserved a house just like that but thought it was impossible to get something so grand.

Kelli, however, was optimistic. She told Alan that nothing was impossible and that her client trusted her, which could be their doorway to riches. Three months later, Alan called Kelli, wanting to visit Uncle John, but Kelli apologized, explaining that Mr. Banks had taken a sleeping pill and was sound asleep. When Alan asked if Uncle John had any relatives, Kelli said no, only salesmen called him.

Mr. Banks appreciated Kelli's care, saying she was the only one who really cared about him. Kelli encouraged him not to let his family upset him since they were busy with their own lives, but assured him she would always be there for him. Two weeks later, Kelli came to Mr. Banks with papers for him to sign. Despite feeling sick, Mr. Banks agreed because he trusted Kelli. She affectionately called him “luv.”

Four days later, Mr. Banks said he felt like he was dying and asked about his medicine. Kelli told him to stop complaining and trust her, assuring him he was getting better every day. That evening, Kelli called the family, tearfully informing them that Mr. Banks had passed away despite their efforts.

Three weeks later, at the reading of Mr. Banks’s will, it was revealed he had left all his worldly possessions to Kelli James, his nurse. The family was shocked, saying they were his children. The lawyer confirmed the will was legal and incontestable.

Seven years later, Bonnie noticed Kelli was sick. Kelli admitted she had cancer and was dying. Bonnie told her about how God had healed her big sister’s cancer. Mr. Williams and the deacons had prayed for Bonnie, and she believed Jesus had healed her. Bonnie invited Kelli to church and asked if she could pray for her too.

At church on Sunday, as the pastor began teaching about the prophet Elijah from 1 Kings 21 and 22, Kelli felt glad she had come. The story was about a greedy king named Ahab who desired a vineyard owned by a man named Naboth. Naboth refused to sell or give the vineyard to the king, saying it was his inheritance.

Ahab, furious, begged for the vineyard, but Naboth stood firm, causing great sorrow in the king’s spirit. Jezebel, Ahab’s wicked wife, promised to get the vineyard for the king. That night, Jezebel forged letters with the king’s signet ring to accuse Naboth falsely. Naboth was eventually sentenced to death by stoning, destroyed by a mob that Jezebel had orchestrated.

God took note of this evil deed, and Ahab joyfully took possession of the vineyard, unaware that Elijah, the prophet of God, was plotting judgment. Elijah confronted Ahab, pronouncing God’s curse on him and Jezebel for their wicked deeds. Elijah warned that dogs would lick Naboth’s blood and later lick the blood of Jezebel.

In Ahab’s last battle, he was fatally wounded by an arrow guided by God. His chariot was washed in Jezreel, where Naboth had died, fulfilling Elijah’s prophecy. Jezebel was later killed by dogs as punishment.

Kelli reflected how God doesn’t play games, and she realized she had done something like Jezebel by cheating Mr. Banks’s family out of their inheritance. Overwhelmed, she feared she was also going to hell. But she learned about God’s love and forgiveness through Jesus Christ, who died for everyone’s sins to save them.

Kelli confessed to Pastor Malcolm that she was responsible for Mr. Banks’s death and was dying of cancer. She asked if God had really forgiven her for her sins. The pastor assured her she was forgiven and asked what she planned to do next.

A week later, Kelli signed the necessary papers with a lawyer, then passed away at 2:14 a.m. She went home to glory, surrounded by angels. Meanwhile, Mr. Banks’s family fought and cursed her memory, unwilling to forgive despite her tripling their inheritance for them.

The story ended with a reminder that no matter what one has done, everyone must repent and believe in the Lord Jesus Christ to be saved and forgiven.

Title: Peace Maker, The
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Carter
Responses:
One day, a police officer named Carter was told by his partner about an eyewitness at a crime scene who might have important information. Carter went to speak with the eyewitness, an anxious woman who explained that she had just been coming up the stairs when the shooting started. She was so scared that she hid behind a door until the violence ceased.

Carter questioned her further, asking if she had been there to buy drugs, to which she nervously responded that this would have been her first time, but she was late and missed it. Carter continued challenging her, asking where she would be if she had arrived early and been killed. After some hesitation, she answered, "heaven," but Carter told her to try again.

He explained that the four men now dead were in hell. When the woman asked if they were in hell because of drugs, Carter replied that nobody has to do drugs to go to hell; anyone who sins goes there, as the Bible says, "All have sinned, and come short of the glory of God" (Romans 3:23). The woman worried about her grandma, who prayed, went to church, and loved Jesus, questioning if she would also go to hell. Carter assured her that her grandma would not because she had done something to avoid that fate.

Curious, the woman asked what her grandma did. Carter explained that her grandma had discovered there was only one way to get into heaven, believed it, and grabbed onto it. Most people ignore or mock this, but those who believe are saved and avoid hell. The woman was eager to know what her grandma found out.

Carter told her that her grandma believed Jesus is God Almighty and died for her. He explained that only Jesus' blood can wash away sins (Ephesians 1:7). The woman wanted to know if she could be saved if she believed the same, and Carter responded with a confident "Absolutely!" She eagerly agreed to do it.

Suddenly, they were interrupted with a call that Clancy, another officer, was in trouble. Carter and the woman hurried to the scene, which was turning chaotic, with a hostile crowd growing larger. Carter saw Clancy's car and was determined to get through despite threats from the crowd, but when he reached Clancy, the other officer was badly injured.

The attackers warned Carter that he was next, but Carter prayed for help, relying on God's promise that all things work together for good (Romans 8:28). His partner urged him to hold on and called for backup before the situation escalated.

Meanwhile, the woman’s grandma confronted one of the assailants named Junior, demanding he hand over his knife. Junior was confused but reluctant to obey until Grandma reminded him that Carter was no ordinary cop. She told Junior about Carter's past—a life of crime, his hatred for cops, and how he was brought back from the brink by faith in Jesus.

In the past, Carter was feared because of his wickedness, even trying to outdo others in crime. He hated society, especially the police. One day, he was shot multiple times and was dying in the hospital, headed for hell. An old preacher prayed for him, fasted, and shared with him about Jesus—the God who died for sins.

Carter learned that Jesus was crucified to pay for humanity's sins, and that his blood alone could wash away the guilt (Acts 20:28). He accepted Jesus as his Savior and was forgiven. He begged God to help him turn his life around.

Now, Carter loves everyone and works to bring peace. He asked how many of them had the courage to believe in Jesus. Inviting them to pray with him on their knees, he led them all in a prayer to accept Jesus.

Watching this transformation, others were amazed at the power of God working in Carter’s life. They were now all brothers in Christ, feeling clean and renewed.

Back at the police station, Carter’s partner said he was thinking about getting a new partner, but after seeing Carter’s new life, he changed his mind—vowing it was safer to work with Carter than anyone else.

Junior, now confronted by Grandma and the police, began to see Carter not just as a cop but as God's man, someone who had changed completely because of his faith. Grandma's testimony helped open the eyes of many that day.

And so, in the midst of trouble and violence, faith, repentance, and forgiveness brought new life, hope, and peace to those involved.

Title: Pilgrimage, The
Subject: Islam
Author: Chick
Responses:
The story begins at an airport where Flight 727 is due to arrive at Gate 18 in an hour. Abdul Ali's wife expresses that this was her husband's tenth pilgrimage to Mecca, a journey he undertook with the blessing of paying all expenses for five young men, changing their lives forever. Abdul Ali himself shares his awe at seeing the Kaabah, describing it as magnificent. However, shortly after takeoff, Flight 727 declares an emergency with only one landing gear down and locked.

Air traffic control instructs the plane to dump fuel and prepare for an emergency landing, with rescue units ready on the runway. Passengers brace themselves as the plane is about to make the emergency landing, and Abdul Ali confesses his fear of dying. He encourages his fellow passengers to be courageous, expressing hope that if Allah wills, they might reach paradise soon. Despite these hopes, the plane crashes, and 246 lives are lost.

Abdul Ali finds himself alive amidst the wreckage and is told by an angel that everyone else is dead. Confused and fearful, he asks if he is dead and is taken to see if his name is in the Book of Life. Despite having performed the Hajj and being a pious Muslim, Abdul Ali's name is not recorded. He is told by God that he is cursed to everlasting fire because he rejected Jesus Christ. Abdul Ali is confused and asks about Allah and Muhammad, but Jesus Christ reveals Himself as the Lord to whom all judgment is given, explaining that Muhammad rejected Jesus and is not in Heaven. Jesus further explains that Allah is a satanic counterfeit and one of many false gods.

Abdul Ali protests, saying nobody told him this before, as he was merely following his family's religion. Jesus explains that He sent a servant to Abdul during medical school, but Abdul rejected him. The story flashes back 20 years earlier when a man named Paul tries to convey to Abdul that Islam won't get him to Heaven. Paul explains that many religions were created by the devil to trap people in doing good works to earn eternal life, but salvation is only through faith in Jesus Christ, not by works.

Abdul defends his faith, mentioning his prayers, giving to the poor, and pilgrimages, but Paul insists that salvation is a free gift. He explains sin, originating from Adam and Eve, as the main problem, which religion cannot solve. Jesus' life, sinless death, and resurrection are described as the means to pay for mankind's sins.

Paul shares Bible verses and talks of Jesus rising from the dead, witnessed by over 500 people. He tells Abdul that those who trust Jesus have their sins forgiven and names written in the Book of Life, urging Abdul to forsake his religion and accept Jesus, despite the risk of being disowned by his family.

Back in heaven, Abdul is told by Jesus that because he rejected Him, he must pay for his sins. Abdul insists he was sincere, but Jesus says sincerity alone is not enough. The comic ends with a direct message to the reader, urging them to trust Jesus to secure their eternal destiny, reminding that Abdul Ali was given the truth but rejected it.

Title: Plagues
Subject: Bible Stories
Author: Carter & 3rd
Responses:
Long ago, every Hebrew boy born in Egypt was condemned by Pharaoh to be cast into the river to die. Pharaoh's decree was absolute, and no one dared to disobey.

God had sent the children of Israel to Egypt to save them from starvation. In gratitude, they praised God for His preservation. However, a new Pharaoh arose who hated the Israelites and enslaved them. Four hundred years later, the population of Israel had grown to three million, which filled Pharaoh with fear. To stop this growth, he commanded that every newborn Hebrew boy be killed.

During these harsh times, a special baby was born to a Hebrew mother. To save him, she placed him in a waterproof basket and set it afloat on the Nile River. Pharaoh's daughter discovered the baby, loved him, and raised him as her own son, naming him Moses.

As Moses grew older, he became angered by the way the Egyptians treated the Jewish people. One day, in a moment of rage, he killed an Egyptian for hurting a slave. Realizing he was in danger, Moses fled for his life. Pharaoh never imagined that God would later send Moses back to Egypt to bring about its destruction.

Forty years later, Moses returned to Pharaoh with God's message: "Thus saith the Lord... Let my people go." Pharaoh questioned, "Who is the Lord, that I should obey His voice?" Pharaoh scoffed when Moses warned of the plagues that would hit Egypt. Each plague was designed to wipe out one of Egypt’s many false gods.

The first plague struck when Moses plunged his rod into the Nile, turning all the water into blood. Fish died, the river stank, and the Egyptians were terrified.

Next, God covered the land with frogs, which the Egyptians worshipped. Frogs were everywhere, even in Pharaoh’s bed. Pharaoh promised to release Israel if Moses removed the frogs, but he broke his word.

Then lice appeared, turning dust into swarms of insects. Pharaoh’s magicians could mimic this trick but could not remove the lice. Pharaoh remained stubborn.

Flies infested the land, tormenting the Egyptians, but notably spared the Israelites.

The fifth plague struck the sacred cattle and other animals of Egypt, wiping out horses, sheep, camels, and oxen. Yet, Israel’s herds were unharmed. The Egyptians grew to hate Moses.

Boils broke out on Egyptians, but the goddess Serapis could not help. Then hail mixed with fire fell from heaven, destroying crops and causing even the sky god Nut to turn away.

Locusts ravaged Egypt next, finishing the destruction the hail had not. Pharaoh’s sun god Horus was discredited, but Pharaoh still refused to release Israel.

God instructed the Israelites to borrow jewels, silver, and gold from the Egyptians, who gave away their wealth in fear.

The last plague was the most devastating. God warned He would kill all the firstborn in Egypt, both humans and animals, striking judgment against all Egyptian gods. God told the Israelites how to protect themselves by sacrificing an unblemished lamb—the Passover lamb—and placing its blood on their doorposts. This act would cause death to "pass over" their homes.

That night, a great cry rang out: not one Egyptian household was spared.

Pharaoh finally relented and freed the Israelites as God had promised. The Jews still celebrate Passover to remember this mighty deliverance that followed 400 years of bondage.

As the Israelites marched toward the Red Sea, Pharaoh changed his mind and sent his army after them. God stood between them as a fiery pillar, protecting His people by holding back the Egyptian army.

When Pharaoh’s forces closed in, God released the walls of water, drowning Pharaoh’s army and ending Egypt’s power forever. Egypt was ruined for rebelling against God’s Word.

This story raises the question: Will God "pass over" you on the terrible day of Judgment? The only protection is the blood of Jesus Christ, who came to earth to die for your sins.

Jesus shed His precious blood to wash away sin, offering everlasting life to everyone who believes in Him, as stated in John 3:16. He was buried, rose from the dead, and ascended into heaven. He promises to return in glory.

If you confess your sins and ask Jesus to save you, you will be covered with His protective blood. On Judgment Day, God will see Jesus' blood and say, "Well done, thou good and faithful servant... enter thou into the joy of thy Lord."

This is the enduring story of salvation, from the plagues of Egypt to the ultimate sacrifice of Jesus Christ.

Title: Poor Little Lamb
Subject: Bible Stories
Author: Chick
Responses:
Once upon a time in ancient Egypt, a young boy told his father that Moses had said they should get a lamb and put its blood on their doorposts. The father angrily responded, blaming Moses for the troubles Egypt was facing, declaring that Egypt was almost ruined.

The boy questioned what had happened to Egypt, once known as the glory of the world. The father explained that Egypt was almost ruined because Pharaoh, the king, used Jewish slaves to build beautiful cities and showed them no mercy. The Egyptians treated the Jews terribly, even drowning their baby boys in the Nile to stop their population growth. For 400 years, the Israelites suffered as slaves, but God heard their cries and sent Moses to free them.

Moses was scared to face Pharaoh, the most powerful man on earth, but God was with him. Moses spoke to Pharaoh, demanding that he let God's people go, but Pharaoh refused, unwilling to obey God's voice. His refusal came with a heavy cost.

God sent ten plagues upon Egypt to punish Pharaoh and his people. The Nile turned to blood, frogs swarmed everywhere—even leaping into Pharaoh’s bed—lice and flies infested the land, livestock died, boils covered the Egyptians, and thunder, fire, hail, and locusts destroyed their crops. Throughout these plagues, the cattle of Israel remained safe, which made Pharaoh furious.

Despite days of darkness, Pharaoh still refused to release the Israelites. Moses warned the people that the firstborn of every Egyptian family would die, but those who followed God’s command had a way to be spared—by putting the blood of a lamb on their doorposts.

The boy told his father that they needed to follow Moses’ instructions and protect themselves with the lamb’s blood. The father, initially stubborn and dismissive, finally agreed but was skeptical. They put lamb’s blood on their door, hoping it would make a difference.

At midnight, all the firstborn of Egypt died, from Pharaoh’s palace to the dungeons and even the livestock, except in homes protected by the lamb’s blood. Egypt was in ruins, losing their cattle, crops, and jewels, and four million slaves were freed. The Israelites, led by Moses, journeyed to the Promised Land—a journey that took forty years.

Every spring, the Israelites commemorated this event with the Passover, inspecting and sacrificing a lamb as a new pet before eating it. This event symbolized the innocent lamb’s blood that covered their sins.

Years later, God's Son, Jesus, came to earth as the ultimate Passover Lamb, to take away the sin of the world. John the Baptist announced Him as the Lamb of God. Jesus healed the sick and raised the dead, but many religious leaders rejected Him, calling Him a liar and lunatic. Jesus taught that no one could come to God except through Him, a message hated by many.

Jesus was crucified, sacrificing His life, fulfilling the ultimate Passover Lamb's role. When He died, the temple curtain was torn, symbolizing direct access to God. Jesus rose from the dead three days later, conquering death and offering salvation.

The world found this gospel offensive, but Jesus will return one day to judge all, rewarding those who believe in Him with eternal life while the unbelievers face eternal punishment.

The story ends with a solemn question: Will He pass over you? Will you accept the blood of the Lamb to be saved from sin and judgment?

This tale serves as a reminder of God’s mercy, justice, and the only way to salvation through Jesus Christ, the Lamb of God.

Title: Poor Little Witch, The
Subject: Occult
Author: Chick
Responses:
Mandy was struggling on her volleyball team, often dropping the ball, which caused frustration among her teammates. One day after practice, one teammate angrily asked, “Mandy dropped the ball again! Can't you do anything right?” Mandy apologized, feeling ashamed while sitting on the floor. The tension didn't end on the court; Mandy’s mother was equally harsh. When Mandy tried to speak to her, her mother told her not to talk and emphasized her burden as the sole family supporter since Mandy's father left.

Feeling isolated, Mandy wished she could be like the other girls. One night, overwhelmed by emotion, she expressed her desperation, hoping to "be someone." A voice of encouragement told her she could be, and she would see that happen.

The next day at school, Mandy’s teacher, Mrs. White, asked her to stay after class. Mandy wondered what she had done wrong but soon heard kind words. Mrs. White told Mandy she was sweet, talented, and should have many friends. Mandy was surprised and hopeful.

Later, Mrs. White invited Mandy to a slumber party at her house. Mandy was eager and asked her mother for permission. Her mother agreed, but backstage, Mrs. White warned Mandy to be cautious as a new girl was joining the group.

At the party, some of the girls introduced Mandy to "neat things" and showed her tricks. Mandy was amazed and curious, wanting to learn more.

Two weeks later, a girl asked Mandy if she'd like to see the other girls purposely drop the ball in P.E. Mandy expressed her frustration with how the other girls treated her and asked if there was a way to fix it. She was given instructions to light a candle, stare into the light, and ask Bruth for help. Mandy was confused at first but finally tried it.

The next morning, before school, Mandy spoke to Bruth, asking for help to make Cathy drop the ball. Suddenly, Cathy stumbled in P.E., surprising everyone. Mandy was thrilled with the success.

Meanwhile, across town at the new church, Mr. and Mrs. White were warmly welcomed by the pastor. They were given gifts, and the pastor was treated like a king. After the pastor left, Mrs. White discussed their plans. They intended to use the same manipulative tactics on the new pastor as previous ones and wanted to get him to join a secret lodge.

Mrs. White later talked to Mandy about attending a special meeting to increase her powers. Mandy was excited but nervous. Mrs. White warned her not to enter a certain “evil” place called Gospel Hall and warned about the dangers of associating with Mrs. Grayson.

Despite warnings, Mandy was curious and went to Gospel Hall one night, where a secretive and dark ceremony was taking place, involving a sacrificed child and worship to Satan. Mandy was forced to drink the child’s blood and was told it would increase her powers. Terrified and sick, she complied.

Afterward, Mrs. White warned Mandy not to go to the police because the High Priest of the dark group was also the chief of police, leaving no way out. Mandy was scared and cried, searching for a solution.

She sought help at the big Christian church, hoping someone could help her against the Whites. She was told the pastor there was dead, but maybe he could still help somehow.

At church, some women told the pastor about a witch visiting their congregation and demanded she be removed. The pastor agreed to get rid of her.

Later that night, the church congregation quoted scriptures about not tolerating witches, stirring fear and urgency. Mandy, desperate, knocked on the door of Mrs. Grayson’s house. She confessed she was trapped in Satanism with no hope left.

Mrs. Grayson revealed she knew the dark cult and vowed to help Mandy escape. She invited Mandy to church with her, promising safety from the cult.

After the church service, Mrs. Grayson explained that the people Mandy was involved with were dangerous but true servants of God could set her free. They prayed together and Mandy repented for her sins, inviting Jesus Christ to be her Savior, rejecting Satan.

Mrs. Grayson helped Mandy rebuke the demons through prayer in Jesus' name. Mandy felt peace and protection for the first time in her life, with her faith growing stronger.

Mandy thanked Mrs. Grayson for leading her to Jesus and was assured that God would protect her from Satan.

In the end, it was reminded that when Mandy dies, God will say, “Well done thou good and faithful servant,” welcoming her to the joy of the Lord.

The story ends with a choice: Who will you serve? Jesus Christ or Satan? The invitation is to trust in Jesus for salvation and eternal joy.

Title: Poor Revolutionist, The
Subject: Communism
Author: Chick
Responses:
In a private cell meeting, Paul angrily confronted Jimmy, calling him a "stupid idiot" for crashing their gathering and preaching to them. Despite Jimmy being his kid brother, Paul threatened to give him an unforgettable beating. As others restrained Jimmy, Paul punched him. From the sidelines, some cheered Paul on, remarking on the irony of him attacking his own brother, as a woman nearby sang a revolutionary song.

Another man then voiced his frustration with Christianity, criticizing Jimmy’s faith for influencing their group. He argued that their religion was fake, pointing out that Harry, who had "born again" changed, had also joined their revolutionary cause. Jimmy replied passionately that Harry was a phony Christian who never truly repented, and thus God never dwelled in him.

Paul angrily declared that Christianity was outdated and insulted Jimmy. He expressed that their revolution aimed to create a new world government with no place for religion, refusing to ever see Jimmy again. Jimmy passionately asked Paul if he understood that Jesus died for his sins, to which Paul called him a fanatic and ordered him removed.

As Jimmy was thrown out, another man reviled him, labeling him a "God freak." Paul and this man then plotted to deal with Jimmy and his kind, denouncing religion as the "opium of the masses."

The group prepared for their impending revolution, reviewing assignments and assuring readiness for the overthrow of the free market system. They promised rewards of power and honor in their envisioned socialist world.

At 11:25 PM, the code word "Bedlam" was broadcast, signaling the start of the revolution. Violent revolutionary forces launched attacks with cries of "Death to all pigs and their families!" Police were ambushed and killed responding to false alarms, while fires raged and homes burned. Other units seized control of essential water and power infrastructure.

Looting and murders spread throughout the chaos as civilians were rounded up into detention camps. The death toll rose sharply as many civilians managed to bring concealed weapons for resistance, engaging in firefights with the revolutionaries. Jimmy was shot and fell wounded, and Paul mourned his death but refused to back down.

Meanwhile, Jimmy, in his weakness, shared scripture from John 3:16, proclaiming Jesus’ love and promise of eternal life. His wound was dismissed as not serious by onlookers.

Months later, after widespread gun confiscation, resistance dwindled. Political leaders capitulated to the revolutionaries’ demands, and the nation fell into collapse. Paul claimed victory—"The land is ours"—but lamented the high cost of their success and the devastation of their country. Foreign troops arrived, further complicating matters.

Executions began under the new regime, targeting capitalists and property owners. Jimmy was captured and brought before Paul by the gallows. Before his execution, Jimmy urged Paul to accept Jesus as his Savior for salvation. Paul called him crazy, but Jimmy blessed him and said goodbye.

After Jimmy was hanged, Paul was summoned by Comrade Gregory, who claimed important news awaited. However, Paul was betrayed—labeled a traitor and a threat to the new system. Despite his protests, Paul was sentenced to immediate death.

Behind barbed wire fences, former comrades lamented their betrayal, calling themselves "useful idiots." Paul was taken for judgment and executed with a gunshot. He faced divine judgment, and it was determined his name was not written in the book of life, condemning him to eternal punishment.

The story ends with scripture emphasizing the finality of judgment and God's warning against deception and wickedness.

Title: Present, The
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Carter
Responses:
Once upon a time, there was a king who lived in a grand palace high above the clouds. He dearly loved his only son and also loved everyone who loved his son.

Years later, the king told his son that he was building apartments in the castle as a present for all his friends. He instructed his son to go down among the people and invite them to the castle. The king promised that he would greatly bless all who responded.

However, when the prince went to visit the people, things were not as he expected. The people questioned, "Who are you? Why are you here?" When he said his father had sent him and that his father was the king with a wonderful present for them, they accused him of lying and claimed it was a trick. They rejected the prince’s message and plotted to kill him. Despite the prince’s pleas, they attacked, and they killed him.

When the king heard the news, he was outraged. He realized that his beloved son had been murdered, and the people had rejected his present. In anger, the king’s army attacked the town, and because of the crime, no one survived.

The story then transitions to a true account from the Bible. It explains that God the Father, God the Son, and God the Holy Spirit are united in Heaven. God the Father has many mansions in Heaven, and He desires for people on Earth to live there with Him.

However, there is a problem: all people have sinned and cannot live in Heaven because God cannot allow sin there. So, God sent His Son, Jesus, on a special mission to die for the sins of mankind. Jesus was born on Earth as a man and came to tell people about the wonderful present God has for them—eternal life in Heaven if they accept Jesus.

Like the prince, when Jesus visited the people, something was wrong. Many people rejected Him, questioned His identity, and called Him a liar. Despite this, Jesus declared, "I am the way, the truth, and the life." He promised that those who believe in Him will have everlasting life.

Jesus explained that He was going to prepare a place in Heaven for those who receive Him. Yet, He was also rejected and crucified by many people. But this was part of God's plan—Jesus shed His blood and died to wash away humanity’s sins. Three days later, He rose from the dead.

The story concludes with a message about the consequences of accepting or rejecting this present from God. Those who reject Jesus and His gift will be judged and face eternal separation from God. Those who accept Jesus by faith will hear words of welcome and enter into joy with God forever.

To receive God's gift of eternal life, a person must simply pray from their heart, repenting and asking Jesus to be their Savior. This is the most wonderful present in the universe, available right now to anyone who chooses to accept it.

Title: Promise, The
Subject: Israel
Author: Chick
Responses:
The story begins with a violent scene where a bus is marked with the slogan "DEATH TO ALL JEWS!" Suddenly, a man, defending his faith, declares that this violence is for Allah and his prophet, Muhammed, but others protest. An explosion follows, signifying the destruction caused by hatred in the Middle East.

People discuss the origins of this hatred, with one man explaining that it all started with one man named Abraham, who was born about 400 years after Noah’s flood. Abraham was wealthy, married, but had no children. Unlike others, Abraham was a friend of God who listened and obeyed His words. God commanded Abraham to leave his country and promised to make him a great nation. However, Abraham was troubled because, despite his riches and power, he had no son.

Worried that his riches would pass to a servant after his death, Abraham’s wife devised a plan that would later cause strife lasting 4000 years. She gave her Egyptian servant, Hagar, to Abraham so they could have a son. While pregnant, Hagar viewed Sarah, Abraham's wife, with contempt, and Sarah treated Hagar so badly that she ran away. The angel of the Lord found Hagar, told her to return, and foretold the future of her son, Ishmael—that he would be a wild man, with his hand against every man.

Thirteen years later, God appeared to Abraham again and told him Sarah would bear a child, Isaac, though it would be a miracle as she was 90 years old. Sarah was furious when her son saw Ishmael mocking Isaac, and she pressured Abraham to send Hagar and Ishmael away. God instructed Abraham to listen to Sarah, as His promise was through Isaac, not Ishmael. Ishmael and his mother became angry and were cast out from God’s chosen people. Ishmael grew up to be a powerful leader who hated Isaac’s descendants, the nation of Israel—a hatred that continues in the Middle East.

Despite these troubles, Abraham was overjoyed to have Isaac, symbolizing laughter. His life became centered on the promise God made to him. God then tested Abraham by asking him to sacrifice his only son, Isaac, as a burnt offering. Abraham was devastated and struggled with the command but trusted God's promises. He prepared for the journey, confident that God could raise Isaac if necessary.

During the journey, Isaac reminded his father about the missing lamb for the offering. Abraham responded that God would provide. At the designated place, Abraham built an altar and arranged the wood. Though it was unthinkable, he bound Isaac and prepared to sacrifice him. However, an angel stopped him at the last moment, acknowledging Abraham's faith.

Abraham then saw a ram caught in the thicket and offered it instead of his son. God kept His promise. Through Abraham, God had shown what He would do 2000 years later by sending His only begotten Son, Jesus Christ, as a sacrifice for humanity’s sins. Jesus died, was buried, and rose again three days later.

One man asked if Jesus was only a man, but he was told no—Jesus is God Almighty, and only His blood could wash away sins. They learned two more promises about Jesus: If they believed Jesus died for their sins and made Him their Savior, they would be saved—promise number one. The second promise was a warning: If they reject Jesus as their Savior, they would be cast into the Lake of Fire.

Some expressed fear of rejecting God’s love gift, and others wondered what to do. They were urged to ask God to forgive their sins and accept Jesus as their personal Savior, confess Him with their mouth, and believe in their heart that God raised Him from the dead. This confession would lead to salvation.

Thus, the story of Abraham’s faith and God’s promises culminates in the hope offered through Jesus Christ, a message of salvation amid a history of conflict.

Title: Ransom
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
Constance and her husband Poopsie were at home when Poopsie noticed Constance's sister, Bonnie, driving up their driveway. He was puzzled and asked why she was coming there. Constance explained that Bonnie was there to pay off her loan, including all the interest.

Soon, Poopsie spotted Bonnie, and the couple decided to grab her. They were shown a picture identifying her as Connie Van Clive's wife, Constance. A group of masked men then forcefully kidnapped Bonnie, putting her into a van, but the van wouldn’t start immediately. After several attempts and some barking dogs around, they finally got it going.

Half an hour later, Constance, Poopsie, and some others were anxiously wondering where Bonnie was, especially upon finding oil spilled on the driveway, which Bonnie angrily pointed out. They then called Conrad Van Clive immediately, informing him that they had his wife and demanding two million dollars cash or else. Conrad was skeptical, saying Constance was taking a bubble bath and insisted they must have the twin sister instead.

Constance's husband was informed about the kidnapping and ransom demand but seemed more concerned about missing his tennis match. Nevertheless, Constance was determined to make Bonnie pay the ransom. She received a call but refused to pay a dime, calling it her money.

Later, Constance called to report that she and Conrad wouldn't get involved as they were leaving for Europe. This led to a police capture effort. The kidnappers were then told they had been turned down, meaning no ransom would be paid.

In a surprising turn, Bonnie announced her ransom had been paid and that she was set free. The kidnappers were shocked while Bonnie explained to them a spiritual truth—that the troubles started with Adam and Eve’s original sin, introducing sin into the world. Sin, she explained, keeps people out of heaven, and only someone without sin could pay the ransom for mankind.

She elaborated that God sent Jesus Christ to pay the price of that ransom, as Jesus lived a sinless life and died on the cross to pay for humanity's sins.

Bonnie explained that those who have never accepted this ransom belong to Satan and control their lives, destined for eternal punishment after death. However, those who accept Jesus as their Saviour have their ransom paid and go to heaven.

Quoting John 3:16, the story illustrated how God loves the world and gave His only Son so believers would have everlasting life. Bonnie then prayed with the kidnappers, who accepted Jesus and were set free from sin.

Suddenly, police raided the place where they were praying. Despite the intrusion, Bonnie stopped the police from pressing charges against her new brothers in faith.

One of the officers was told by Bonnie that Jesus wants to ransom him too. The comic concluded with a message about Jesus paying the ultimate ransom to free everyone from Satan's control, encouraging readers to accept Jesus and be freed from sin.

Title: Real Heat
Subject: Bible Stories
Author: Chick
Responses:
A terrible crash occurred as a truck collided with a car. Someone shouted, "Get your fire extinguisher!" but an explosion followed with a shout of pain. A man caught in the flames cried out, "AAAH! I'm burning!" while a firefighter tried to help with an extinguisher. In an ambulance, paramedics discussed the situation somberly — the victim might survive, but the driver was definitely gone.

Two months later, Rick had a visitor named Bob Williams. Bob wanted to talk about the accident. Rick explained that he couldn't stop thinking about fire. His best friend had burned to death beside him, a truly horrible way to die. Bob said he loved history and had plenty of time, so Rick began to tell the story of Thomas Hawkes, a man who stood against a powerful religious force.

Thomas Hawkes was a gracious man who believed in God's word. When the new queen of England, known as "Bloody Mary," sought to force everyone to follow Catholicism, Hawkes refused to have his baby baptized by a Catholic priest. He declared that he would not have his child baptized by a priest of Rome, despite being told to change his religion or be burned at the stake. Hawkes stood firm, saying "I cannot change!"

In prison, Hawkes told his friends he could not deny Christ or His Gospel and asked God to help him bear the pain of being burned alive. If God gave him strength, he promised to give a sign. When the flames grew fierce and his body shrank, Hawkes suddenly clapped his hands three times, showing God was with him in the flames. The angry crowd had no idea what they were witnessing.

Bob explained to Rick that the Catholic Church's Inquisition was an engine of cruelty, producing millions of victims over centuries, mostly by burning people alive. Rick asked why such history wasn't in their school books. Bob said those in power wouldn't want it printed.

However, not all fiery executions went as planned. About 2,500 years ago, another man’s fiery execution backfired. This story, found in Daniel, chapter 3, involved King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon, the most powerful man alive at the time. Israel had sinned and become slaves to the king. The proud king built a golden idol over 100 feet tall and commanded everyone to worship it, threatening death by burning for those who refused.

At the dedication of the golden statue, everyone bowed except three brave Israelite leaders — Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. They refused to worship the idol, defying the king’s orders. Nebuchadnezzar threatened to throw them into the fiery furnace, but they answered they trusted God to save them, and even if He did not, they wouldn’t worship the golden image.

Enraged, the king ordered the furnace heated seven times hotter and had the soldiers throw the three men inside. The fire was so intense the soldiers themselves were killed. Yet, the king was amazed to see four men walking unharmed in the fire. The fourth looked like "the Son of God." When they were called out of the furnace, not even the smell of fire was on them. King Nebuchadnezzar panicked, repented, and praised God.

Rick asked who the fourth man was, and Bob confirmed it was Jesus Christ. Rick thought this couldn't be right since it happened long before Jesus lived. Bob explained the scripture that Jesus, known as "the Word," was with God from the beginning, and through Him, all things were made, including heaven and hell.

Jesus came down from heaven, became a man, and was crucified to save souls. His precious blood washed away sins, and He rose from the dead three days later. If one believes and receives Jesus as their Savior, they will go to heaven, but without Him, they will die in their sins and face eternal punishment, described as the lake of fire on doomsday.

Rick admitted he was terrified of God. Bob explained that the only way to be saved was to ask Jesus to forgive sins, invite Him to be Lord and Savior, and believe in Him. Rick, facing death, prayed earnestly for Jesus to save him, declaring he believed and did not want to sin anymore. He said that he had "enough fire."

And thus, Rick found salvation just in time, saved through faith in Jesus Christ.

Title: Reverend Wonderful
Subject: For Christians
Author: Carter
Responses:
The story begins with a crowd enthusiastically praising a man named Dr. Westhall, admiring his sermon as magnificent and appropriate enough for speaking at the presidential prayer breakfast. People comment on his sense of humor, his dedication, and how wonderful he is.

A reporter asks Dr. Westhall if he has time to talk, and he replies that he is always ready. The reporter inquires about his personal audience with the pope, to which Westhall responds that he was honored to be in the pope's presence and speaks about working together to unify all Christians. He affirms his dedication to serving humanity through the gospel. Westhall then prepares for a trip to London, receiving assistance to organize his schedule, a limo for early pickup, and a reminder about his dinner speech.

The next day, 30 miles away, a man prays earnestly, asking the Lord to lead him to someone who needs God that night and prays for boldness to share Jesus's love. That evening, the man drives a pickup truck, convinced that this is the path the Lord wants him to take, guided by Psalm 37:23.

At a formal event, the man is introduced, emphasizing how honored they are to have Dr. Westhall, praised as the most loved man in America and one of today's great men of God. Dr. Westhall gives a message about social justice, advocating unity among Protestants, Jews, Muslims, and Catholics, and stresses the importance of working together for a new age to glorify God. The audience is deeply moved, acknowledging the power of his message.

Later, Dr. Westhall is asked for notes for his speech, but no one has them, and they must return to his office. Deciding to follow his instincts, Westhall walks down a sidewalk, believing this is where the Lord wants him to be. He enters an apartment building, noticing the elevator is not working, and goes up stairs to meet a man.

After three minutes, concern grows among those waiting outside, and they decide to check on Westhall. The man inside thinks Westhall is joking when approached but soon realizes the seriousness when Westhall speaks about the man's soul and salvation. The man says he doesn't know if he'd go to heaven, claiming he's someone important, but Westhall tells him the truth about accepting Jesus as Savior.

Westhall tries to share a tract about salvation, while people outside explain to Westhall’s associates who he really is. Don, one of Westhall's companions, assesses the situation with frustration and humiliation at being questioned about salvation.

Despite complications, Westhall remains committed to his message. Don is advised to discuss with the governor about laws to protect the streets. On a flight to London, Westhall is asked for his autograph, which he gladly gives.

Suddenly, the story takes a tragic turn as the plane crashes after a warning about air traffic. It is noted that men die once, followed by judgment. At Westhall’s funeral, he is praised as a great man of God, with his soul committed to God faithfully.

On the Day of Judgment, a woman named May Lou Richards is accepted into heaven because she repented and believed in Jesus, even though she was once a prostitute and drug addict. Then Westhall himself faces divine judgment. He is shocked to learn his name is not in the book of life, despite his fame and works. God tells him he preached a false gospel of salvation through works, not faith, citing Ephesians 2:8-9.

God explains that Jesus shed His blood for humanity because of love, but Westhall never truly received Him as Savior. God declares that Westhall must be cast into eternal fire for rejecting His servant and the true gospel, as per Matthew 25:41.

Westhall realizes that he was a fool who was ashamed of the gospel, seeking power and fame instead of true salvation, and now is lost forever.

A closing message addresses the reader directly: not to let hypocrisy lead them to hell, stressing personal responsibility for one's soul and the importance of trusting Jesus as Savior. It encourages readers to receive Jesus Christ into their hearts for salvation, promising that God will welcome them into the joy of His kingdom as faithful servants.
