As Hurricane Rita struck Galveston, breaking news came that the National Severe Storm Laboratory was tracking numerous tornadoes forming across Arkansas, compounding the disaster with two simultaneous catastrophes. The blaring sirens prompted a frantic rush to the storm cellar, even as family members feared for elderly relatives left behind.

Inside a farmhouse, amidst the roaring storm, a family knelt in prayer, beseeching God to protect their home and their lives. They felt deeply that these events were a divine warning. The discussion turned to the belief that today's disasters were consequences of political actions concerning Israel. One insisted that by interfering with Israel, divine wrath had been invoked, explaining the heavens’ fury as a warning from God.

Skeptics challenged this view, doubting the connection and questioning the theological explanations. Yet others warned of the seriousness of ignoring divine authority, recalling scripture predicting judgment upon those who oppose Israel. The conversation revealed a belief that God had chosen Israel as His special people and land, a sacred covenant dating back to biblical times when God led Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and provided for Israel during their enslavement and desert wanderings.

The story recounted how God delivered the Israelites from Egypt, gave them commandments to follow, and promised to protect and bless them. Though they faced giants in the Promised Land, God’s power ensured their victory when they obeyed. Still, when Israel disobeyed God’s laws, they suffered defeat and exile, becoming the scattered "Wandering Jew" people, despised but still tied to their holy land.

Historical tragedies were linked to divine responses to Israel's situation—World War II’s Holocaust, political betrayals, and modern conflicts all interpreted as part of a divine pattern. The narrative criticized world powers for opposing Israel, asserting that God's land and covenant must be respected or suffer consequences.

The account shifted to more recent history, describing how U.S. political actions regarding Israel and its land division preceded natural disasters like Hurricane Katrina—seen as further evidence of divine judgment. It presented a timeline of escalating catastrophes, correlating political decisions about Israel with increasing turmoil worldwide.

Jerusalem was identified as a critical focal point, a city contested by many but chosen by God. Warnings from scripture predicted severe consequences for nations opposing Jerusalem. Ultimately, the story pointed to a divine promise extending beyond Israel—it involved personal salvation through faith in Jesus Christ.

The characters discussed how accepting Jesus’ sacrifice for sin offers forgiveness and eternal life, contrasting this hope with the dire consequences awaiting those who reject salvation. The story ended with an urging: individuals must choose either heaven or hell by confessing Jesus as their personal Savior.

It promised that Jesus would return as King during the final battle of Armageddon, saving Israel and establishing His rule from Jerusalem over the land God promised. The final message was clear—this choice is urgent and personal, offering eternal life or separation from God, with a call to accept Jesus before it’s too late.

Title: Somebody Goofed
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
A group of people gathered around a man lying on the ground. A police officer shouted, "Stand back please!" as someone gasped, recognizing the man as Bobby. One bystander said, "Oh no! Bobby told me he was gonna do it—I didn't believe him." Another asked, "What happened?" The officer replied, "He overdosed on speed!" A woman questioned, "Is he gonna die?" as others realized with dismay that it was indeed Bobby.

The crowd expressed their sadness and shock. One person sobbed, "That's Bobby. He's dead! How awful!" Others remarked how it gave them the creeps. The officer assured a kid, "He's better off now—no more problems!" One woman said, "He told me he had nothing to live for!" And a bystander whispered, "I just can't believe it!"

Then a man raised an important question, "Where will he spend eternity?" A young girl asked, "What do you mean by that?" while another man interrupted, labeling the topic as fanaticism inappropriate for the moment.

The man explained seriously, "That young man will stand before his Creator to be judged. If he didn't know Jesus Christ as his Lord and personal Savior, he is eternally lost!" Some laughed and jeered, mocking the idea of judgment.

A woman said, "Hey, I've never heard anything like this before. Do you mean I'm lost?" The man replied, "All have sinned and come short of the glory of God. He will not allow sin in His presence, being a righteous God."

Another man argued, "Now wait a minute! God is a God of love. He wouldn't put His creatures in a hell! There's the fatherhood of God and brotherhood of man—remember?" The first man responded, "But what you're saying isn't in the Bible!"

"Actually, it's true He is a God of love," the first man continued. "The Bible says 'For God so loved the world, that He gave His only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in Him should not perish, but have everlasting life!'" The other man dismissed the Bible as filled with contradictions and written only by men.

"The Bible is God's inspired Word," the first man insisted. "Those claiming contradictions simply do not understand it!" The skeptic decided to walk away, saying, "Well, I'm not going to waste my time arguing about it. Let's go!" But a bystander wanted to listen more before leaving.

The first man then explained how if he were going to hell, he could miss it and go to heaven. He explained Christ created the universe, was born of a virgin, loves everyone, shed His blood for sins, rose from the dead, and would be a defender if trusted as Lord and Savior.

The skeptic angrily rejected this, calling it "outdated fear" and "nuts" and claimed the first man was a menace to society. The first man calmly said, "Son, if you accept Christ, you have everything to gain and nothing to lose. Reject Him, and you have nothing to gain and everything to lose! Please read this carefully!" and handed him a card saying "You must be born again."

Suddenly, the skeptic was struck and yelled. The first man shouted, "Let's go—I've had it!" The bystander told him, "Hey cool it! You don’t have to work him over—he didn’t do anything to you!"

A man warned the bystander not to read the "propaganda," saying it would make him mentally sick. The first man assured him, "Look, let me straighten you out—I’ve got all the answers!" The skeptic admitted he sounded a little off. The first man said he was mad and irrational.

One man suggested following the Ten Commandments, believing in the Golden Rule, and that Jesus was only a great teacher, nothing more. The bystander said, "OK, I’ll listen to you from now on!"

The first man said, "There is no sin. You are your own salvation! Heaven and hell are here on earth." Suddenly, the bystander saw a train approaching and told the others. The skeptic hesitated, but the first man urged, "Go ahead! You can make it!" The skeptic refused but was struck by the train.

The bystander and the first man found themselves in a dark place. The first man explained, "This is where the lost go temporarily. This is not purgatory as many believe. There is no such place! You'll be here until you stand before the great white throne and be judged by God on doomsday!"

The bystander asked, "But can’t Jesus be my Savior now?" A shadowy figure said sharply, "Of course not! You died in your sins! It’s too late! You had your chance! Now He must be your judge!"

The bystander accused the first man of being wrong and having goofed. The first man admitted, "No, little buddy—I wasn’t wrong!"

A devilish figure revealed, "You were wrong! You didn’t accept the Lord Jesus Christ as your personal Savior!" The story ended there, dramatically highlighting the spiritual fate awaiting the skeptic.

Title: Somebody Loves Me
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
On a dark and stormy night, lightning flashed across the sky above a lonely shack in the country. Inside, a man pointed angrily at a small child, whose speech bubbled with a hiccup, signifying nervousness or fear. The child left the house, clutching a tin cup and walking out into the pouring rain.

As the child wandered through the storm, people with umbrellas hurried by, trying to avoid the downpour. The child raised the cup, hoping for some help, and a large figure approached and dropped a coin into the cup. Yet, the man seemed displeased, discarding the cup and revealing a one-cent coin in his hand. Then, he angrily picked it up, trembling with rage.

The man grabbed a baseball bat that lay on a nearby table and confronted the child, who raised their hands in defense. The man, hiccupping with anger, swung the bat, chasing the child away. The child's small figure was seen running through the rain, eventually collapsing on the ground outside the shack, exhausted and soaked. As the child crawled away, they encountered several hostile dogs and other threats but managed to find a wooden box near a trash bin, crawling inside to seek shelter.

The child fell asleep in the box, with a piece of paper lying nearby that read, "SOME BODY LOVES YOU." The paper fluttered in the wind, the message becoming their only comfort. When the child awoke, they read the note again, puzzled but hopeful. Soon, a smiling girl appeared nearby, holding another paper and pointing encouragingly towards the child.

The paper was revealed to say "JESUS LOVES YOU!" This gave the child the strength to seek help. As the child embraced the message, imagining it as a warm, comforting light, a man, an angel, or a guardian came to the box, reaching in kindly.

The final scene shows the child and the angelic figure rising towards the heavens, stars shining around them. The story closes with a message from the Gospel of John 3:16: "For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life."

Thus, amidst the darkness and hardship, the child finds hope and love through faith, symbolized by the message of Jesus' love and salvation.

Title: Something in Common?
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
The story begins by explaining how all people share many common experiences. Everyone has to eat, sleep, and live somewhere. Everyone gets sick, eventually grows old, and ultimately dies. All humans came from the same ancestors, traced back to Adam and Eve, who had many children. A great flood washed away all people except Noah, his wife, their three sons, and their wives, meaning that all humans today come from this group. Humans come in a variety of colors but share similar emotions, such as laughing, crying, getting angry, and sometimes acting in ways they shouldn’t.

The story then addresses why people do bad things. It says everyone is a sinner, tracing this condition back to Adam, who disobeyed God by eating forbidden fruit, which cost him his life. His sin was passed down to all his descendants. Because of sin, sinners will not go to heaven. Instead, all sinners are destined for hell, which is described as a terribly undesirable place.

However, since humans can't remove their sins themselves, someone else must intervene. God sent His Son from heaven, to be born as a baby through Mary, a young virgin chosen for this miracle. God, through the Holy Spirit, helped conceive Jesus, who was born without sin and was God incarnate. Jesus lived a sinless, perfect life, teaching people how to live according to God's will by loving enemies and forgiving others. He healed the sick and raised people from the dead, but his main mission was to remove human sin.

When the time was right, Jesus challenged the religious authorities and was put to death as a sacrifice, fulfilling prophecy. His perfect life qualified Him to die in place of sinners. By shedding His blood, Jesus offered a way to wash away sins because of His love for humanity. Though His followers were initially shocked by His death, three days later, Jesus rose from the dead—an event never before witnessed. Before ascending to heaven, He promised to prepare a place for believers in His Father's house.

Not everyone believed in Jesus, and many rejected Him, choosing instead their own ways, thinking they were too good for hell. The story warns that many people will go to hell, often sharing attitudes like hatred for God, disbelief in Jesus as the only way, and indulgence in sinful behaviors. The story encourages those who don't want to go to hell to confess their sins and believe in Jesus as their savior, suggesting a prayer to ask God for forgiveness and acceptance of Jesus.

If a person does this, they now share something with those going to heaven, joining a path that leads there. While some may think this is too easy or hard to accept, it is the only way to heaven. The story emphasizes this as the most important decision in life. It presents the choice clearly: accept Jesus as Lord and Savior or reject Him.

For those who reject Jesus, the story warns that after death, they will be in a horrible place and will remember this choice with regret forever. However, the story closes by stating that ultimately, everyone will bow to Jesus, according to scripture, and invites the reader to try again and choose the path to heaven rather than hell.

Title: Sorry
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
The story begins at a state prison, where a black car arrives and the commissioner is informed to notify the warden. The commissioner, Commissioner Wilson, meets with Warden Billy, and this meeting carries an uneasy tone as the warden senses bad news.

The Governor has mandated the prison to accommodate 800 new convicts next month. Despite the prison being already overcrowded, the Governor insists on making space by any means necessary and warns the warden not to upset him. The warden is instructed to empty pod #4, which contains the most dangerous felons, to house the new prisoners and to release the inmates currently there to satisfy the Governor and address the overcrowding.

Commissioner Wilson bids farewell to the warden, confident that he will handle the task, and shortly after, the warden calls for an emergency meeting with the guards. The guards are informed that pod #4 holds their most dangerous criminals, the "worst of the worst," but they must release them by month's end due to financial constraints and pressure from the Governor.

Inside pod #4, the prisoners react wildly to the news of their impending release, vowing revenge and to reclaim the streets. Meanwhile, outside, the community remains unaware of the danger they now face.

Warden Turner contacts Sheriff Phelps, warning him that Frank Morgan, one of the prisoners in pod #4, is being released that Friday, and urges him to warn Morgan’s family. Sheriff Phelps confirms the release, despite the risks, because the Governor authorized it, citing budget issues.

In the sheriff’s office, officers discuss the release of Frank Morgan. Morgan, a violent criminal who has caused great harm, is met with concern and even resignations from officers who feel unprotected without the release being halted. Morgan’s wife, Ruth, shares with her daughter the terror of living with him, including an incident where he harmed their neighbor’s dog, showing how much danger the family is in.

On the morning of the release, Frank Morgan prepares to leave prison. He’s instructed to be ready for the bus departure at 2:30. Morgan waits for instructions and is assigned to bus 14. The buses then leave the prison, dispersing these dangerous criminals widely.

Sheriff Phelps reflects bitterly on threats Morgan made when arrested, wishing he had killed him then. As the pickup unfolds, townspeople remain uninformed about the dangers ahead. At home, George Phelps forgets to put out the trash for the early arrival of the buses, leading to tension in the household.

That night, Frank Morgan confronts Sheriff Phelps, demanding if he's ready to go to hell. The sheriff pleads for mercy, but Morgan reveals he isn’t there to kill him, but to apologize. Morgan asks for forgiveness, explaining that the Bible teaches that if you don’t forgive others, you won’t be forgiven. Surprised but moved, Sheriff Phelps forgives Morgan wholeheartedly, feeling grateful.

The next day, a figure with flowers and balloons surprises Ruth and Debbie Morgan at their door—it’s Frank. Despite initial fear, the family embraces him and begins to heal. Frank fixes a meal for his family, and they pray together, thanking God for their blessings, though some remain uneasy.

Frank buys a puppy for the family’s neighbor, seeking forgiveness and to be a better neighbor. Weeks later at church, Frank recounts how he found faith while in solitary confinement, reading gospel tracts secretly passed to him. He learned about Jesus Christ’s sacrifice and salvation.

At church, the minister explains that because all have sinned, everyone needs Jesus. He invites anyone who wants salvation to raise their hand, and many do. The message emphasizes that life’s final judgment will be by Jesus Christ: those who believe in Him will be saved, others will face eternal punishment. The story ends with a call to make a choice between following Jesus or Satan.

Thus, the story shows a journey from fear, danger, and despair to hope, forgiveness, and redemption through faith.

Title: Soul Sisters
Subject: Basic Gospel
Tag(s): ['Black Tract Series', 'Little Children', 'Older Children and Adults']
Author: Carter
Responses:
Two friends were talking one day when one of them excitedly said, "I’ve got a new best friend." The other friend looked sad and asked, "But what about me?" The first friend explained, "This friend is different. Let me tell you about Him. He loves me and is going to take care of me forever... even after I die! He promised to help me whenever I’m in trouble, and He’s building me a beautiful mansion to live in up in heaven."

The friend was surprised and asked, "He can make a mansion?" The first friend replied, "Sure! He made everything, even you and me!" Curious, the other friend asked, "What’s His name?" The answer came back simply, "It’s Jesus!"

Then the first friend asked, "Can I tell you more about Him?" When the other agreed, the story began: "God made the earth, and the first two people, Adam and Eve, put them in a beautiful garden. But God made them leave the garden because they did something naughty—they disobeyed God. They had lots of kids, and they were naughty too! God called these naughty things 'sin.'"

"I had done lots of wrong things, and God saw all of them! I got scared because I learned that God will never allow sin into heaven. So I thought I’d never go there." But then the friend learned what God said in His Holy Book.

The other friend asked, "What Holy Book?" The answer was clear: "The Bible, silly!"

From the Bible, the first friend read, "'For God so loved the world...' The world means everybody! God loves all of us! '...that He gave His only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in Him should not perish, but have everlasting life.'"

"But I don’t understand," said the other friend. The first friend smiled, "Then let me show it to you in pictures."

The story continued with pictures: God so loved the world—meaning everyone—that He gave His only Son, Jesus. Jesus came from heaven and was born as a baby. Because Jesus is God, He never sinned, so He didn’t have to die. Yet people hurt Him and put Him to death on the cross. He shed His blood to wash away our sins. That was God’s present to us.

Three days later, Jesus rose from the dead. So the friend believed in Him and got saved, praying, "Lord, I’m a sinner. I’m sorry for what I did. Please come into my heart and save me."

The Bible says those who don’t believe in Jesus perish in hell after they die. But those who believe have everlasting life in heaven. If you ask Jesus to save you, He will begin building you a home in heaven and become your best friend right now!

The friend said, "I want Jesus in my heart." "Will you pray now?" the other asked. "Oh my, yes!"

Together, they prayed: "Lord Jesus, thank You for dying for my sins. Please come into my heart and save me."

Afterwards, the friend felt so good — "My sins are gone! Now Jesus is my best friend too!"

As they walked, one friend asked, "Can I ask you a question?" "Sure!"

"When we get to heaven, could I live next door to you?" The other replied with joy, "Oh, I’d love that!" And they hugged, happy to share their new friendship and hope of heaven.

Title: Soul Story
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Carter
Responses:
The comic strip tells the story of Leroy Brown, a man imprisoned for many years and involved in a violent and chaotic world inside the prison. The story opens with an emergency in the prison, but a wary guard suspects something is off about the riot. During the chaos, Leroy's secret as a snitch is revealed, but despite this betrayal, he impresses others with his cunning and manner, having been in prison for 20 years.

Leroy's elderly grandmother visits him in prison, telling him she is sick with cancer and urging him to turn to Jesus and accept God's love, promising him salvation and that Jesus loves him. Leroy brushes off her religious fervor but shows some affection toward her. His grandmother continues to encourage Leroy, reminding him of the consequences of sin and with hopes that he won't die spiritually lost.

Meanwhile, back in the prison, Leroy is forced into confrontations with other inmates and asserts dominance, declaring himself boss. Yet, tension rises as a rival named R.D. has a contract put out on Leroy’s life.

Leroy reconnects with friends, learns about the dangers he faces upon release, and starts to reevaluate people and relationships around him. He learns that his grandmother is gravely ill and rushes to see her. During their tender moment, she pleads with him to accept Jesus Christ before it's too late and assures him of God's great love for him.

After she passes away, Leroy contemplates her words and begins to consider a life beyond violence and crime. The story climaxes with a brutal gang fight involving grenades and gunfire, where Leroy is critically wounded. As he struggles to survive, his grandmother's words echo in his heart about forgiveness and salvation through Jesus.

Joyce, a woman who cares for Leroy, arrives and pleads with him to repent and embrace God's forgiveness, reading scripture to him. Despite his battered state, Leroy expresses remorse and hopes for salvation. As he dies, he finds peace in accepting Jesus and is comforted by Joyce.

The story ends with a message about God’s love and the promise of eternal life, emphasizing that through faith and repentance, one can find redemption and peace even after a life filled with hardship and sin.

Title: Soul Survivor
Subject: Your Soul
Author: Chick
Responses:
In the olden days, people would often ask a peculiar question: "How is it with your soul?" Many were puzzled by the idea of a soul, asking, "What’s a soul? Do I have one?" It was explained that every person has a soul because everyone is born with one inside them.

Curious minds would then wonder what a soul looks like. Science, however, dismisses the concept since the soul is invisible, ignoring it as if it were a joke. But it was said that God sees the soul and understands exactly what it looks like.

Your soul is the real you. While your body will eventually die and turn to dust, your soul will live on forever. When you die, God asks where you think your soul will go — highlighting the importance of this eternal part of ourselves.

Some were scared this had to do with God or places like heaven or hell. The conversation clarified that it’s actually about the concept of sin. God gave Moses the Ten Commandments, which laid out how He wanted people to live, but these commandments were removed from schools. People also worked hard to remove even the memory of the Ten Commandments because they deemed them offensive, turning against God and His words, thus risking their souls.

Despite the backlash, the importance of the Ten Commandments was stressed — following these laws was fundamental. When asked if anyone had ever broken God’s laws, people admitted to it: telling lies, stealing, bearing false witness, using God's name in vain, dishonoring parents, murder, adultery, and coveting.

It didn’t matter what people thought about these sins; God would not allow sin in heaven. Questions followed, with admissions of lying, stealing, disrespecting parents, and using God's name as a swear word. Even looking with lust was explained to be equivalent to committing adultery, according to Jesus.

Despite being ordinary people, the truth was clear: God would judge the soul, and sin was a serious matter. When asked to see their souls, people saw images covered with sins like lying, adultery, hatred, and lust. The question was posed: Would God allow such a soul into heaven? The answer was no, and many were scared at the thought of going to hell.

Thankfully, there is hope. God does not want anyone to perish and offers a way to be saved. A plan was made to wipe away every sin, leaving the soul spotless for heaven. This is only possible through the blood of Jesus Christ.

God is three persons in one: the Father, the Son (Jesus Christ), and the Holy Ghost. Jesus, God’s Son, created the universe and knew all things. To save humanity, He left heaven to be born as a human baby, unlike any other.

Jesus’s mission was to be a human sacrifice, dying for people’s sins. Before His death, He healed the blind, deaf, and even the dead to prove He was God. Despite this, He was crucified, beaten, and cursed. Every drop of His holy blood washed away the filth from one’s soul.

Jesus died and rose from the dead after three days, completing His mission. If someone believes and asks Jesus for forgiveness, their sins are forgiven, and their soul becomes pure and ready for heaven.

Having Jesus in your heart is like a heavy weight being lifted. Your body becomes a temple of God because Jesus lives within you. However, if sins are not forgiven, they lead to eternal suffering in hell — a fate that met the young lady who refused salvation.

Millions are still heading toward this destiny, but Jesus commands His followers to warn others and preach the gospel.

If you recognize your soul is stained with sin and want freedom, you can pray to Jesus, asking for forgiveness and inviting Him into your life. By believing in Him, you receive eternal life, avoiding the consequences of sin.

The choice between heaven and hell is yours to make. If you want to avoid hell, have your sins forgiven, and believe that Jesus died for you, you can commit your life to Him. Salvation is available through faith, and you can start by praying sincerely to Jesus right now.

Title: Spooky!
Subject: Halloween
Author: Chick
Responses:
A young boy named Sam was curious about his neighbor, Mr. Hill, who was preparing for Halloween. Sam asked his Aunt Sarah about what Mr. Hill was doing next door. Aunt Sarah explained that Mr. Hill usually transforms his home into a haunted house for Halloween, as he liked to get a little spooky this time of year. Sam asked if he could go outside to see what Mr. Hill was doing, and Aunt Sarah agreed.

Outside, Sam saw Mr. Hill digging a grave. When he asked about it, Mr. Hill confirmed it was a grave and asked if Sam was from around the area. Sam mentioned he was visiting Aunt Sarah for a week. Mr. Hill invited Sam to come visit his haunted house on Halloween and asked for help carrying a giant, hairy spider from his garage—an item meant to scare kids and find out who was brave and who was not.

Sam helped Mr. Hill with the spider and was invited to the haunted house on Halloween night. Although Aunt Sarah warned Sam not to go because Mr. Hill was very strange, Sam insisted. On Halloween night, Sam was scared to approach the haunted house, but Mr. Hill welcomed him inside. Sam met a witch who claimed it was the Devil’s birthday and warned that the Devil was going to get him.

Suddenly, Sam found himself locked inside a barrel, scared for his life. Mr. Hill reassured him, praising Sam for having the courage to come and told him to grab some candy and be cautious of a snake on the way out.

After the Halloween scare, Aunt Sarah asked Sam if he had enjoyed his time. Sam said it was awful. Aunt Sarah then explained that Halloween wasn’t really the Devil's birthday. Some witches might say that, but it’s not true.

Sam expressed fear about the witch’s words, asking if the Devil was going to get him. Aunt Sarah comforted him, explaining that if he followed what the Bible teaches, the Devil would never get him. She told Sam to believe in Jesus and put his trust in Him, and that God would forgive his sins and protect him forever because He loved him.

Aunt Sarah explained sin, saying everyone does bad things, but God made a way to save people. She shared the story of Jesus’ birth, emphasizing how God sent His Son, Jesus, to save people from sin by dying on the cross. Jesus’ sacrifice was God's great love gift, and through faith in Jesus, all sins could be forgiven.

Sam believed and asked Jesus to forgive his sins and come into his heart. Aunt Sarah assured him that Jesus had saved him from the Devil’s grasp. She also taught Sam that Jesus would never leave him and that it was their job to tell others about Jesus.

The next day, Sam went to Mr. Hill and asked him to go to church with him. Mr. Hill laughed and called Sam a coward, but Sam challenged him to come or be called a big phony. On Sunday morning, when Mr. Hill tried to back out, Sam and Aunt Sarah insisted he come along.

Though Mr. Hill was reluctant and angry, he went to church. During the service, Mr. Hill struggled but eventually was moved by the preacher's words about Jesus being the way to salvation. As the altar call was made, Mr. Hill struggled with his fears, saw visions of demons and fire, and finally called out for help. The preacher encouraged him to repent and trust Jesus.

Mr. Hill accepted Jesus, turning away from his fear and darkness. The story ends with a strong message that terrifying things like Hell are real, but through Jesus, anyone, even the biggest coward, can be saved.

The comic concludes urging readers to make a choice between Jesus Christ and Satan, reminding them that they can be saved by believing in Jesus, asking Him into their hearts, and living with His love and protection.

Title: Squatters
Subject: End Time Prophecy
Author: Chick
Responses:
In the beginning, God Almighty created the universe and set aside a special piece of land on Earth, considered very holy—known as the Holy Land—which still belongs to Him. About 400 years after Noah’s flood covered the world, God chose a very special man named Abraham. God loved Abraham and promised to give him and his descendants His holy land.

God promised Abraham that his family would be as numerous as the stars in the heavens. However, Abraham’s wife Sarah could not have a baby, and they were growing older with each passing day. Sarah had the idea that her Egyptian handmaid, Hagar, could bear a child for Abraham, but this was a bad idea. Without God's permission, Abraham made love to Hagar, and she gave birth to Ishmael.

But God’s plan was different. Sarah eventually gave birth to Isaac, who became Abraham's rightful heir. God chose Isaac to inherit the promises made to Abraham.

Isaac had two sons, Jacob and Esau. God loved Jacob and gave his family exclusive rights to the Holy Land. Esau joined his uncle Ishmael, and their descendants became the Arab nations known today.

God renamed Jacob as “Israel,” and Israel had 12 sons. Despite being a dysfunctional family, they became known as God’s chosen people. God’s promise to Israel came with warnings against cursing them. The Israelites lived in Egypt as slaves for 400 years and multiplied, which scared Pharaoh. God raised up Moses to lead them out of Egypt, but Pharaoh resisted. God declared war on Egypt, sending plagues and ultimately killing their firstborn. Israel was freed but was left stuck with over 3 million ex-slaves.

Despite the hardships, God's presence stayed with the Israelites as a cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night. Moses died, and God appointed Joshua to lead the army to take over the Holy Land. Joshua and his army fought long battles, eventually running out of steam.

When Joshua died, Israel’s people began marrying foreigners and worshipping idols, disobeying God’s warnings. God allowed them to be attacked by enemies. The people humbled themselves, and God forgave them but took vengeance on those who harmed His nation. Eventually, Israel demanded a human king rather than God’s rule. The first king was a disaster, but God appointed David who loved and served Him. David's son Solomon reigned with great wisdom but was led into idolatry by his many wives. After Solomon, the people grew worse, breaking every law God had given.

Prophets were sent to warn Israel, but the people killed them instead. God allowed foreign nations to punish His people, and Israel was invaded and destroyed by those nations who hated them. Despite this, God wanted Israel to be a light to other nations, but their hearts became hardened. For 400 years God did not speak to them—until the birth of John the Baptist.

John announced the coming Messiah, Jesus, who would sit on David’s throne and rule the earth. Jesus brought light to the Holy Land, teaching truth and exposing sin. When Jesus claimed to be God, the people became furious. He was rejected, crucified, and died as a sacrifice for the sins of the world. After three days, He rose from the dead. The chosen people rejected God’s offer of eternal life, preferring darkness to light.

Jesus returned to heaven, setting Israel aside and sending apostles to preach to the rest of the world. Satan created the Roman Catholic system, a counterfeit church with popes pretending to be Christ on earth, opposing the real Jesus. The Catholic church declared war on followers of Christ, becoming a powerful, satanic force. The Vatican claimed ownership of the Holy Land, making God a liar.

The Vatican created inquisitions and world wars, slaughtering Jews and Christians. After the Holocaust, God gave Israel a new nation in 1948. Arab nations threatened and attacked Israel, but the Jews vowed never to be destroyed again. Arabs who fled were rejected by their wealthy neighbors and forced into miserable refugee camps controlled by Arab gangsters, worsening the peace.

A more sinister force, the Vatican, seeks control of Jerusalem. All nations involved in Jerusalem's fate are enemies of God and will pay during the coming world war. When nobody expects, Jesus will return for His Bride, born-again believers. The dead will rise and join the living to meet Him forever.

World War III will erupt, causing millions to perish and Satan to protect the Vatican. The Holy Land will be invaded by Russian and Muslim armies, and though Israel survives, it will unknowingly sign a peace treaty with the Vatican.

When Solomon's temple is rebuilt in Jerusalem, and the treaty broken, the Beast from the Vatican will take control, unleashing plagues and madness over the earth. The armies will gather against Israel for the Battle of Armageddon, but Jesus will come down, destroy the invaders, and save His chosen people. He will rule the world from Jerusalem for a thousand years.

At that time, God’s chosen people will be astonished as He takes His place as their Messiah and King.

Finally, the story urges every person to make a choice: Accept Jesus as Savior and be saved, or reject Him and face eternal separation from God. The choice you make will determine your eternal destiny.

Title: Star, The
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
Douglas Ford, a renowned TV and film award-winning star, was admitted to St. Lucy Hospital with chest pains. The news spread worldwide, and people everywhere were standing by with prayers. Two days later, doctors confirmed that Douglas was responding well to treatment, and the hospital staff were thrilled to have such a celebrity at St. Lucy's. His room was filling with flowers, and he even received a call from the President.

Cardinal Rooney arranged a mass for Douglas, praising his recent movie, and instructed that a large donation be sent to the Pope. Meanwhile, hospital staff debated what to do with the numerous flowers, deciding to either discard them or give them to other patients. Douglas had two more films scheduled for release and was approached by fans seeking his autograph.

Despite his fame, Douglas was confronted by Daisy, a hospital cleaner, who challenged his lifestyle, especially his work in adult films. She told him that he would answer to God for his choices. This confrontation saddened Douglas, as no one had ever spoken to him like that before. He believed Cardinal Rooney thought he was a good man, but Daisy insisted the Cardinal only wanted his money.

Douglas's blood pressure rose due to the stress of his spiritual questioning, but the doctor allowed him to stay another night in the hospital. Daisy continued to tell him the truth about hell, warning him he'd face God one day and explaining the eternal consequences of sin. She described hell not as a fairy tale but as a real place where billions suffer, all because of their sins.

Douglas began to question his beliefs and lifestyle, realizing he might die twice: once physically and once spiritually in hell. The hospital staff prepared for his discharge, and Douglas felt like he was walking with Daisy, as though a dream had come true. On returning to filming, Douglas was confused and distressed, feeling obsessed with death and daisies.

In a late-night conversation, Daisy explained that those who die in sin are taken to hell, where their life is replayed before God, who judges them. The consequences are terrifying, and Douglas was found guilty and condemned to eternal separation from God.

However, Daisy offered hope, explaining that Jesus is the only one who can save him. She told Douglas about Jesus’s sacrifice—His death for sins and resurrection—and urged him to repent and accept Jesus as his Savior. Initially skeptical and fearful of losing his fame, Douglas was encouraged to reconsider.

To everyone's surprise, Douglas prayed and accepted Jesus into his heart. One year later, Douglas died in a car accident but was welcomed into heaven as a faithful servant. His story is a powerful testament that no matter one's past, genuine repentance and faith in Jesus bring salvation and eternal life.

Title: Still No Revival
Subject: For Christians
Author: Chick
Responses:
In 1961, a significant milestone was marked by the publication of a book titled "Why No Revival?" However, the reception of this message was far from welcoming. Many people hated it, with some even finding it offensive, including mothers who objected to its content. Despite this resistance, questions arose about whether a spiritual revival had truly occurred since then. Some believed it had, but wondered where it had gone and what was wrong with the spiritual state of the nation. 

The comic encourages a reflection on how spirituality has changed over the past 50 years. A comparison is drawn between the family altar of 1961, where families would gather to watch wholesome programming, and today's family altar, which might include shows like "Family Guy," known for its controversial and openly gay character, Stewie. Fifty years ago, such content would have been unimaginable. 

Since 1961, there has been a noticeable decline in true spiritual revival in the USA. When pastors are asked how many believe in core Christian doctrines like the virgin birth, hell, and the Second Coming of Jesus, only a few raise their hands. Scriptures warn of judgment beginning at the house of God, and lament the destruction caused by pastors who scatter their flocks.

Ecumenical efforts to unify different Christian denominations have led to some questionable alliances. For example, some pastors celebrate unity with Catholics, praising the absence of intolerance despite clear doctrinal differences. Yet, many Christian leaders are growing closer to the Pope, raising concerns given the historical atrocities of the Inquisition, when millions were tortured and killed in the name of Mary and the papacy—all under the guise of unity and false peace.

The comic recounts how Rome once tortured Bible believers during the Inquisition, showing no mercy and justifying their actions as for the "greater glory of God." That era ended with Martin Luther and the Reformation, but now Rome uses softer means of control, including love and brotherhood pretenses, under the leadership of Cardinal Ratzinger, now known as Pope Benedict XVI. Christians signed agreements to unite Evangelicals and Catholics, aiming to prevent criticism of Roman Catholicism.

This alliance is likened to playing with fire, as the Vatican represents the seat of the Antichrist per biblical prophecy. Meanwhile, another religious cult, Islam, is rising in influence. Despite the 9/11 terrorist attacks being carried out by Muslims, some leaders like President George W. Bush emphasized Islam as a peaceful faith. However, Islam worships Allah and Muhammad, adheres to ancient Arabian laws, and seeks to conquer the world for Allah, punishing opposition severely.

Muslim terrorists follow strict teachings from the Qur’an that call for terror and violence against unbelievers. Moderate Muslims reportedly fear and stay silent about these dangerous doctrines. Islam is growing rapidly worldwide, including taking over former Christian churches, with few resisting this expansion.

The comic reflects on how the Christian church has failed in spreading the gospel effectively. God revealed Himself in flesh through Jesus Christ, who lived a perfect life, healed the sick, and brought hope to many. Despite Jesus’ teachings, His death and resurrection proclaim salvation for all who believe and accept Him.

However, after 100 A.D., persecution of Christians began under political and religious authorities, especially the popes, who opposed and sought to destroy the Bible and its teachings. The 1611 King James Bible once spread worldwide revivals, but the Vatican countered with altered Catholic versions, leading to confusion and rejection of the Bible's authority.

Many today despise the King James Bible and have expelled it from churches and bookstores, undermining God's true words and potentially blocking genuine revival. Yet Jesus’ words warn of great tribulation and unprecedented events preceding the end of times, with war, famine, plagues, and Satan’s final Antichrist set to come.

Despite these dark times, God's promise offers hope. The Lord Himself will descend from heaven, and the dead in Christ will rise. Those alive will join them, meeting the Lord in the clouds. This event could happen at any moment, and believers are urged not to miss it.

The comic closes by reminding us that the great day of God’s wrath is coming, with vengeance against those who reject His gospel. It concludes with a plea to trust Jesus Christ now before it’s too late, highlighting that eternal destinies—heaven or hell—depend on the choice one makes today.

Title: Stinky
Subject: Halloween
Author: Chick
Responses:
On a dark Halloween night, a demon named Number Three was scolding a small rat he called a "rotten little maggot," insisting that the rat listen carefully. Number Three explained he was sending the rat topside during the Halloween festivities when crowds gathered to celebrate their master's birthday. Number Three needed the rat to find a truly unforgettable Halloween gift for Satan himself—something that would show how much the world loved Satan so that Number Three could become number two.

Number Three warned the rat to behave well and not to be squashed like a bug, to which the rat promised not to disappoint him. As the rat made his way through the night, surfaces reeked with a foul odor that made the rat’s fur stand on end. Despite the smell, the rat pressed on and found himself overwhelmed with excitement as he finally got to participate in Halloween on the surface. For the first time ever, the rat was going to collect candy and scare people.

Meanwhile, back below, Number Two was worried about Number Three’s task and doubted the rat's abilities, but Number One reassured him that no mistakes were made by Number Three. Above ground, the rat approached a group of children dressed in costumes. He asked if he could go with them and was welcomed warmly for having a great costume. They went trick-or-treating, the rat collecting candy eagerly and savoring the treats, along with little comic books the kids gave him.

But trouble arose when the rat pushed through groups of children to get more candy, causing some kids to get hurt and upset. The parents scolded the rat for taking all their candy selfishly. Frustrated, the rat tried to join other kids, but they avoided him and went into a protected area, warning him not to come. The rat panicked but the children inside were kind. They gave him candy and comic books and even explained stories from the Bible.

The children shared how Jesus was God Almighty, who created everything and loved everyone so much that He died on the cross for mankind’s sins. They read to the rat about how anyone who calls upon Jesus’ name will be saved. The rat was amazed and asked for help to understand this better. The children offered to bring him more books and read together about forgiveness and salvation.

Later, the rat returned to the underworld with his haul of candy and the special comic books. Number One was eager to see what Number Three had brought for Satan. When the rat presented the comic books and a Jack-o’-lantern filled with them, Number One accepted them but was soon enraged by the Christian message inside. The devil and his minions erupted in fury, cursing the rat and blaming him for their troubles.

In the ensuing chaos, Number Two punished Number Three, blaming him for the failure. The rat escaped the punishment and retreated to a dark cave, satisfied with his Halloween adventure.

The story ended with a warning from the children’s guardian to kids everywhere not to take hell lightly and to accept Jesus Christ's gift of forgiveness. By believing in Jesus, they explained, anyone’s sins could be forgiven, and they could be saved from eternal punishment. This message was the true gift the rat hoped to share, making it a Halloween to remember.

Title: Story Teller, The
Subject: Islam
Author: Carter
Responses:
The story begins with Yuseff, a storyteller who has traveled thousands of miles around the world, returning home. Upon his arrival, he is warmly welcomed by his father, and Yuseff mentions that he has seen and heard many strange things during his travels. He requests that the whole family gather to hear the story he has to tell, and the family eagerly agrees, curious and excited about the tales.

Yuseff asks everyone to swear by Allah not to interrupt or comment until he finishes his story. The family agrees solemnly, ready to listen. Yuseff begins by recounting a man he met during his travels who shared a strange story that Yuseff must pass on to his family—a story that would change their understanding forever.

He reveals that he had fought in the Spanish Civil War under Franco for the Holy Man in Rome and, years later, in 1953, he met a young Jesuit seminarian studying the Messo-Arabic Mass. Recently, Yuseff met this Jesuit again, who had left the Jesuit order and converted to Christianity. This former Jesuit shared secret information from the Vatican concerning Islam.

According to the Jesuit, Jesus was a prophet of God who preached the gospel and was crucified because the religious leaders hated him. Jesus claimed to be the way, the truth, and the life, saying no one could come to the Father except through Him. Early Christians spread this message throughout Africa and Europe, but their enemies—the so-called Early Fathers who exalted Mary unscripturally—murdered and tortured them.

Some converted to Christianity, but the Roman Catholic Church, led by Emperor Constantine, created a false religion, Roman Catholicism, to undermine Jesus’ followers. Catholics built convents and monasteries where they saw true Christian communities and sought to raise an Arab army to destroy Christians and Jews, capturing Jerusalem.

For a long time, the Vatican watched the North Africans, who were descendants of Ishmael and the Jews from Isaac—both considered children of Father Abraham. The Vatican created a new religion for these Ishmaelites by mixing Babylonian, Jewish, and Roman Catholic traditions with corrupted biblical manuscripts. The ex-Jesuit, Rivera, showed how the Vatican created Islam through the Koran.

In the fourth century, the powerful Roman Catholic teacher Augustine appeared in North Africa, reworking the gospel to suit Catholicism. Two hundred years after Augustine's death, the Vatican spread a message to the Arab world that a great leader was about to appear.

Satan, the enemy of Muslims, played a part in this plan through a wealthy widow who gave her wealth to the Roman Catholic Church and retired to a convent. The ex-Jesuit Rivera was told she had been tasked to find a young Arab man with leadership abilities to marry. This man was Muhammad, who married a woman named Kadijah.

Muhammad listened to St. Augustine’s teachings, guided by his wife’s cousin Waraqah, a faithful Roman Catholic who counseled him. Waraqah helped give prominence to the Virgin Mary in the Koran, forming a key link between Islam and the Vatican.

The Vatican secretly financed Muhammad’s military campaigns, and when he died with several wives, the Church’s influence remained strong. Muhammad's body is entombed in the Mosque of Medina, just as Catholic saints are kept in holy places for worship. However, Jesus’ tomb is empty.

After Muhammad's death, the pope supported Islamic generals by granting permission to invade North Africa, where faithful Catholic Arabs preached Muhammad as the Arab Messiah. Opposition dissolved as Islam spread by the sword.

The Muslim generals wanted the pope’s permission to invade Europe, leading to terrible wars known as "The Crusades." Wars between Muslim and Roman Catholic forces continued for centuries until peace was negotiated, allowing Muslims to occupy Turkey and Catholics to occupy Lebanon, with Arabs recognizing Roman Catholicism as the only true Christian church.

In the 20th century, the Jesuits aimed to bring Islam into their fold, choosing Fatima in Portugal for the Virgin Mary to appear, softening the hearts of over a billion Muslims and pulling them under Vatican influence.

Yuseff's story concludes with a warning about the coming battle of Armageddon. Islam is secretly armed by the Vatican to destroy Israel, but the Word of God promises that communist and Arab armies will be destroyed when Jesus returns as King of kings.

Yuseff urges his family to believe Jesus, who died to wash away sins and offers eternal life. They pray together, but a furious woman warns of doom. The family grapples with shame, doubt, and curiosity about Jesus and the Bible, but some seek the truth.

The story ends urging readers to explore the true story of how Islam came into existence and the role of the Vatican, encouraging belief and faith in Jesus as the true prophet and Savior.

Title: Sunday Special?
Subject: Drugs/Alcohol
Author: Carter
Responses:
Alice Douglas catches Jerry trying to take the last bit of their family's money hidden in a kitchen cabinet. She confronts him, warning him that spending that money will destroy their family. They struggle, and Alice insists Jerry stop causing harm.

Their children overhear the fight. A neighbor, Mrs. Jenkins, comforts the children as an ambulance arrives. Alice is rushed to the hospital, but Jerry is too drunk to accompany them.

Janice, one of the children, is sent to find Jerry. She searches bars and clubs, where he's drinking and ignores her pleas to come home because their mother is very sick. Mrs. Jenkins eventually finds him and tells Janice they need to get to the hospital.

At the hospital, doctors try to save Alice, but she passes away. When told of the news, Janice is devastated. The community holds a funeral for Alice, but Jerry is absent. Janice struggles with anger and sadness toward her father.

Aunt Mary gives Janice $20 to buy food for the family, warning that Jerry, an alcoholic, may misuse it. Jerry promises Janice he will buy groceries, but he returns drunk with no food. Janice angrily confronts him, and he lashes out at the children.

Jerry begs for forgiveness, claiming he struggles with addiction, but the children reject him. Mrs. Jenkins takes the children to church and invites Jerry to join them. Jerry hesitates but agrees.

At church, a pastor talks about finding hope through Jesus. Jerry hears the message and feels his heart lifted. He commits his life to Jesus, surprising Janice.

Three years later, Janice invites Jerry to see their Sunday special, which turns out to be their transformed family, finally healing and united with Jesus and hope for the future.

Title: Sunk!
Subject: Bible Stories
Author: Chick
Responses:
Andy Carlson was heading home when his wife Megan called out to him from the porch, reminding him he had forgotten his lunch. He thanked her and promised to be right in. Megan smiled, pleased with the surprise she’d prepared for him. Andy complimented her cooking, happy he hadn’t left without his meal.

Later, a fierce storm rolled in with thunder and lightning. Megan reassured Andy that he was safe inside, and he didn’t need to worry. Suddenly, Andy noticed something alarming. Megan asked if he had moved his truck, but he hadn’t. When Andy went outside to look, he saw his truck had sunken deeply into a massive sinkhole in the street.

Fortunately, no one was in the truck. Andy thanked his lucky stars for being alive, but a fireman nearby said it wasn’t luck — God had shown mercy. Megan pondered what the fireman said, wondering if there was a divine message behind the accident. Andy was skeptical but agreed to keep the event private and think on it.

News spread about Andy’s narrow escape, and a preacher spoke to a crowd, linking the event to a lesson from the Bible’s book of Numbers. He explained how God created a nation, gave His commandments, and set up a priesthood including Moses and Aaron, respected leaders chosen by God to guide the people.

The preacher recounted how Moses’ jealous cousin Korah led a rebellion against Moses’ authority, challenging his leadership and claiming they were all holy. God warned them through Moses to stay away, but Korah and 250 leaders defied the order and confronted Moses.

God’s glory appeared, and He declared He would consume the rebels. Moses told the people that if the rebels died naturally, then there was no divine judgment, but if the earth opened up and swallowed them, it would prove God had sent Moses. Immediately, the earth split open, swallowing Korah and the others along with their families. Fire also came from the Lord and consumed the rebels.

Many blamed Moses and Aaron, but God sent a plague as a sign that He was in control. Aaron bravely stood between the living and dead to stop the plague, demonstrating that God is a consuming, jealously protective deity.

The preacher continued, explaining that Jesus Christ, God’s Son, created the universe and gave mankind Adam and Eve. Their sin brought death and separation from God. Jesus, though powerful as the Son of God, humbled Himself to live as a human baby and shed His innocent blood to cleanse humanity from sin.

Jesus came not to judge but to save, teaching love and obedience to God. When He was crucified, Jesus bore the sins of the world, suffering an awful death so that believers could have forgiveness and eternal life. He rose from the dead three days later, offering the gift of salvation to those who trust Him.

The preacher invited listeners to pray and accept Jesus as Savior, emphasizing that without Jesus, everyone is lost to sin and eternal separation from God. Those who reject Him face judgment and eternal punishment.

Moved by the message, Andy and Megan asked how to be saved. The preacher gave them a prayer to confess their sins and accept Jesus into their hearts, urging them to choose salvation and peace with God.

The story ended with a reminder: Jesus offers new life to all who believe, washing away sins and making them "as white as snow." But the choice is theirs — to accept Jesus or face eternal consequences. Andy and Megan chose faith, embracing the promise of God's forgiveness and love.

Title: Superman?
Subject: Bible Stories
Author: Carter & 3rd
Responses:
This is a story set in Israel in 1160 B.C., during a dark period under the brutal rule of the Philistines. Joshua and another Jewish child were chased by a cart, and though Joshua ran fiercely, he was caught, and his life was brutally taken. This grim episode illustrated the harsh reality the Israelites faced under Philistine oppression.

For 40 years, the Israelites prayed to the Creator of the universe, pleading for forgiveness and deliverance from their suffering. They begged for someone to save them, and God heard their prayers. An angel appeared to the wife of Manoah, an Israelite woman, telling her she would bear a son who must never cut his hair and who would begin to deliver Israel from the Philistines.

When the baby was born, named Samson, his parents did not fully grasp the significance of what was to come. God had chosen Samson for a special purpose and imbued him with His Spirit. Although Samson faced certain challenges, God often uses unusual people to accomplish great tasks.

Despite his parents’ concerns, Samson chose to marry a Philistine woman. His father questioned why he couldn't find a Jewish bride, but Samson insisted, drawn to her. Unknown to them, God's hand was at work even in this unique circumstance, aiming to overturn Philistine control.

One day, while walking through vineyards near Timnath, a young lion roared at Samson. Without weapons, Samson was defenseless, but the Spirit of God came upon him, enabling him to kill the lion with his bare hands. Later, he discovered bees making honey inside the lion's carcass and took some honey to share with his parents.

During his wedding, Samson posed a riddle to his guests: "Out of the eater came forth meat, and out of the strong came forth sweetness." None could solve this mystery in seven days. Under pressure from the guests, Samson’s wife was terrified and pressed to get the answer from Samson. She nagged and begged for seven agonizing days until Samson finally revealed the riddle’s secret to her.

Betrayed, Samson’s enemies demanded their payoff. To repay his debt, Samson killed 30 Philistines and took their clothing. Furious upon learning his wife had been given to another man by his father-in-law, Samson decided to take revenge. He caught 300 foxes, tied their tails in pairs with lighted torches, and set the fields ablaze.

The Philistines responded cruelly by burning Samson’s wife and father-in-law to death. Enraged, Samson slaughtered Philistines responsible for their deaths and became a wanted man as the Philistine army searched for him.

The tribe of Judah, fearing the Philistines, turned Samson over to them. As he was about to be taken, the Spirit of God empowered Samson to break free from the ropes binding him. He grabbed the jawbone of a donkey and killed a thousand Philistines, displaying God’s unseen power working through him.

Samson soon fell for a beautiful Philistine woman named Delilah, who was an agent for the Philistines. They promised her riches if she could uncover the secret of Samson’s strength. Night after night, Delilah charmed and pressured Samson for his secret, teasing him and falsely accusing him until she tricked him into revealing that his strength depended on his uncut hair.

Once Samson fell asleep on her lap, a Philistine cut his hair, and Samson lost all his strength. Captured by the Philistines, he found himself powerless. Delilah was handsomely rewarded by the Philistines for her betrayal.

The Philistines blinded Samson and made him a slave, forcing him to grind wheat in prison. However, his hair began to grow back, unnoticed by his captors. The Philistines gathered in the temple of their god Dagon to sacrifice, bringing Samson to entertain them. They placed him between two main pillars that supported the temple roof.

Samson prayed to God for the strength to destroy the temple and take revenge on the Philistines. Pushing the pillars apart, he brought down the temple, killing himself and more than 3,000 Philistines. Before his death, Samson repented his sins, acknowledging the Creator of the universe, the Lord Jesus Christ, as the source of his strength.

The story transitions to Jesus Christ, who created the universe and came to earth to die for the sins of humanity. He shed His blood to wash away sin, rising from the dead, and ascending to heaven. It forewarns of the final battle between Christ and Satan’s evil system called the Battle of Armageddon, urging people to choose Christ.

Unlike Samson’s temporal victory, Jesus' ultimate rule will be eternal, reigning from Jerusalem as King of kings and Lord of lords. The story concludes with a call to accept Jesus as Savior and Master, emphasizing the choice between eternal life with Christ or damnation with Satan. The final message is a heartfelt prayer for forgiveness and salvation through faith in Jesus Christ.

Title: Superstar, The
Subject: Sports
Author: Chick
Responses:
During the World Cup overtime, Roberto Cordoba had the ball and took a powerful shot. The ball soared into the goal, securing the Golden Goal and ending the game with Roberto as the superstar.

However, shortly after his victory, it became apparent that something was wrong with Roberto. Despite his success, a doctor later revealed that he was suffering from a painful knee injury. The day after the game, Roberto's team announced that he had just signed a $20 million contract and an additional $5 million shoe deal.

In his mansion, Roberto proudly showed his friend Juan his lavish new contract, boasting about his mansions, cars, fame, power, and everything else he could want. Juan told him that despite his wealth, Roberto actually had nothing of true lasting value. He warned Roberto that someday he would die and none of his riches would matter. There was only one thing Roberto truly needed, and money could not buy it.

Enraged, Roberto yelled at Juan, saying he made more money in one year than Juan would in his entire life. He then ordered Juan to be quiet and get back to work, complaining that his knee was killing him and he needed to see a doctor.

That night at a party, Roberto enjoyed the fame and respect of others who praised him and his new home. He decided to show Juan how much respect he received. However, when Roberto went to look for Juan at his door, he gasped in surprise.

Juan was praying for Roberto, asking Jesus to show Roberto that he was lost and needed to be saved. When Roberto confronted Juan about praying for him, Juan firmly told him not to ever do that again.

Two weeks later, Roberto met with his doctor to discuss his knee. The doctor delivered harsh news: Roberto had terminal cancer that had spread throughout his body, and only had a few weeks left to live. Roberto, shaken, asked Juan to pray for him because he was scared.

Juan shared his own story of repentance and faith. He told Roberto that 23 years ago, a real friend had the courage to tell him he was a sinner on his way to hell. But that friend also shared the good news that God loved him so much He sent His Son, Jesus Christ, to die for his sins.

Juan explained how he repented and trusted Christ as his Savior, and had never been the same since. He urged Roberto to trust Christ now, because there's no guarantee of tomorrow.

Humbled, Roberto prayed and asked Jesus to come into his heart and be his Savior. He felt a huge weight lifted off his shoulders and was no longer afraid to die.

A few weeks later, the superstar passed away. In heaven, Roberto was welcomed home by the Lord. Back at the mansion, Roberto's friends gathered for the reading of his will.

Roberto had left a letter explaining that he had been a rich hotshot heading towards hell until Juan showed him the way out. He encouraged his friends to receive Christ as their Savior and live a fulfilling life, so that they could join him in heaven someday.

In the will, Roberto left his entire $18 million estate to Juan, because Juan was the only person he trusted to use it wisely.

Finally, Roberto left a personal message to readers: Fame and money cannot buy eternal life, forgiveness, peace, or joy. For those, you must have Jesus Christ. Nothing is more valuable or important than your relationship with Him.

Title: Tell Me About It!
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Carter
Responses:
Two girls, Laura and Judy, were talking. Judy said, "Don't you hate when people tell stories about you?" Laura eagerly shared that Carrie had texted her the juiciest rumor in Math class. Judy wanted to know more, so Laura hesitated but then said the rumor was about Judy herself.

Judy, desperate to know the details, begged Laura to tell her, promising it wouldn't leave their conversation. Laura agreed, saying it was about Judy being seen with another man—an older man at a diner on the edge of town. Laura mentioned there was also a hotel involved.

Judy was shocked and insisted Laura had it all wrong. Laura urged Judy to check Carrie's tweets, showing that the rumors were all over social media. Judy confessed she couldn't explain but said it wasn't what it seemed. She admitted this was her big chance to go viral, and Carrie almost beat her to it.

Judy was alarmed by the viral rumors, crying out that her boyfriend would be furious and that Carrie had ruined her life. She begged Laura to help clear things up. Laura apologized but said she didn't interfere in others' lives.

Judy broke down crying, feeling betrayed and wondering why people believed such lies about her without talking to her directly. Mr. Song, a man from a nearby soda shop, kindly noticed her distress and offered ice cream and a listening ear.

Later, Judy expressed her pain in the diner, saying that everyone thought she was cheating on her boyfriend and that no one would talk to her about what she'd been through. Mr. Song reassured her that God knew everything.

Judy admitted that many people had opinions about Jesus, but few really tried to understand what He said for Himself. Mr. Song asked Judy to share what she had heard about Jesus. She mentioned her coach's idea that everyone, even Jesus, was gender-fluid, dismissing male and female as social constructs.

Mr. Song corrected her by quoting Jesus: "But from the beginning of the creation... God made them male and female." He explained that there are only two genders, not fifty-two. Judy cited the saying "judge not," but Mr. Song pointed out that Jesus said, "Judge not according to the appearance, but judge righteous judgment."

Judy shared what her history teacher said—that Jesus came to bring peace and love. Mr. Song showed her that Jesus also said, "I came not to send peace, but a sword," explaining that trusting Jesus is a big deal that even divides families.

Judy asked why Jesus was so important, wondering if He was just a social reformer. Mr. Song answered, "Don't you know who He really is?" and suggested Judy hear for herself what Jesus said about Himself.

Jesus had said, "No man hath ascended up to heaven, but He that came down from heaven... even the Son of man which is in heaven." This meant He was in heaven and on earth at the same time. Jesus also said, "Before Abraham was, I am," using the name God calls Himself.

Judy realized Jesus called Himself God and told His purpose: "The Son of man is come to save that which was lost." Jesus also said He must suffer, be rejected, slain, and rise again on the third day.

Mr. Song explained that Jesus died and was buried, but God showed mercy. His precious blood on the cross paid for all sins. Jesus said, "It is finished." Three days later, Jesus rose from the dead and ascended to heaven. Believing in Him means He’ll forgive your sins.

Jesus promised, "I go to prepare a place for you... I will come again, and receive you unto myself." He asked, "Do you want your sins forgiven? Will you receive Jesus as your Savior?" Judy prayed, placing her complete faith in God’s Son Jesus.

The next day, Judy told Mr. Song she was happy but worried about the rumor. Mr. Song told her to bring her friend back tomorrow and leave everything to him. Suddenly, Judy’s father, Sgt. Benitez, returned home early from combat. Judy was surprised and happy to see him—he was the older man from the rumor.

Later, Laura apologized to Judy and said she forgave her. Laura told Judy there was someone else they had misunderstood all along. The story ended with a gospel invitation, encouraging belief in Jesus for salvation.

Title: Terminator?, The
Subject: Bible Stories
Author: Carter
Responses:
The story begins in the time of the Philistines and Israelites. A Philistine official proudly announces to his king that they now have an ultimate weapon. The king, who worships the god Dagon, is thrilled by this news and believes that when this weapon is revealed, all nations will tremble and their enemies will flee.

However, when shown the weapon - a strong and large young boy - the king is impressed but questions why he is considered the ultimate weapon. The official reveals that the boy, Goliath, is only 9 years old. As years pass, Goliath grows stronger and his killing abilities increase, becoming a true threat. Meanwhile, the Philistines worship Dagon, an idol, which the story notes as something God hates.

In Israel, a young shepherd named David loves the Lord deeply. At the same time, Israel is in trouble because they rejected God and demanded a human king. God initially rejects King Saul because of his arrogance and disobedience. When Saul is troubled by an evil spirit sent by God, David’s harp playing brings him peace.

The Philistines declare war on Israel, and Saul orders Israel to prepare for battle. David is sent to watch his father’s sheep. David, a brave shepherd, demonstrated his courage by killing a lion and a bear that attacked his flock.

King Saul and his army face the Philistines on the battlefield. Goliath, towering over eleven-and-a-half feet tall, challenges Israel’s army to send a man to fight him. The Israelites are terrified and feel hopeless. For forty days, Goliath issues his challenge, but Israel’s warriors all run away in fear.

David’s father sends him to deliver supplies to his brothers in Israel’s army. As David arrives at camp, he hears Goliath’s defiant challenge against the armies of Israel and questions who this uncircumcised Philistine is to challenge the living God.

David boldly tells King Saul that he will fight Goliath. Though others try to stop him, David is determined. He takes his staff, sling, and five smooth stones, saying, “In Dagon’s name, I curse you.”

Goliath threatens David, declaring he will kill him and feed his flesh to the birds. But David confidently replies that he comes not with sword, but in the name of the Lord of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel. He proclaims that today the Lord will deliver Goliath into his hands so the world will know there is a God in Israel.

David slings a stone that sinks into Goliath’s forehead, killing him instantly. David then cuts off Goliath’s head. When the Philistines see their champion dead, they flee. Dagon’s ultimate weapon is destroyed.

After King Saul’s death, David becomes king and shepherds his people. Isaiah later prophesies that Israel’s Messiah will come from David’s line. Almost 1,000 years later, Jesus Christ is born of a virgin and calls Himself the good shepherd who lays down His life for His sheep.

Jesus teaches about God’s love, stating that God sent His only Son so believers can have everlasting life. Jesus, the perfect sacrifice, dies on the cross to wash away humanity’s sins. Though He first came as the Lamb of God, He will return in glory to defeat Satan and reign from Jerusalem.

Jesus invites all to follow Him and warns that those who reject Him will face eternal punishment. The story ends by asking the reader to choose whom they will serve: Jesus Christ, for eternal life in heaven, or Satan, for eternal pain in the lake of fire. The choice is theirs.

Title: That Crazy Guy!
Subject: Drugs/Alcohol
Author: Carter
Responses:
Suzie couldn't believe it when Craig asked her out. Two weeks from that night, he told her he'd pick her up at 7:30. Excited, Suzie agreed, thrilled that someone so handsome had asked her out. She thought to herself she had never dreamed of this. She was amazed and called him beautiful in her mind.

Nervous about the date, Suzie was determined not to mess it up. She decided to seek advice from Ms. Damien, hoping the woman would be home and could help her. Ms. Damien told Suzie that if she practiced "safe sex," she could get away with anything. She gave her some pills, condoms, and reassured her that science had everything under control in this new age. Ms. Damien even told her to just "do it" if it felt good.

The night of the date, Suzie found Craig cute and real crazy, and she envied her friend Betty’s luck. But things soon went wrong. At 2 A.M., Betty called Suzie a jerk and said she never wanted to see Craig again because he was gross. Suzie wondered if she might be pregnant.

Twelve days later, Suzie joyfully declared she was not pregnant and felt great, thinking she was safe. But there were surprises she hadn't counted on. She sought out Ms. Damien again, asking for help with something she caught from Craig. Ms. Damien told her it was gonorrhea — or "the clap," as she explained it — and harshly told Suzie that if she caught it, it was her problem. Furious, Ms. Damien sprayed the chair Suzie had sat on.

Terrified, Suzie confided in her friends and said she feared her parents would kill her. They suggested she tell Ms. Damien's grandfather, who might help. Soon, a doctor confirmed Suzie was HIV positive. She was in disbelief, especially since Craig had used a condom. The doctor explained that while she had gonorrhea, she also had something far worse: AIDS, an incurable disease.

The doctor warned that "safe sex" was a lie; condoms couldn't protect against AIDS, as the virus was small enough to pass through latex gloves, and even experts didn't trust condoms fully for protection. Suzie was shocked to learn millions of young people were dying because of this misinformation.

Desperate, Suzie asked why God had done this to her. The doctor explained it wasn’t God’s fault—God had provided strict Bible rules about sex, designed to prevent diseases like hers. God’s laws forbade sex outside of marriage and demanded serious consequences for breaking them.

Suzie learned about the immune system—the body’s defense against disease—and how AIDS destroyed it, allowing deadly germs to spread and cause death. The doctor told her that death wasn't the worst part: if she didn’t turn to God as a true Christian, her soul might end up in a dark, terrible place after death.

The doctor shared that only one person really cared about her soul—Jesus. He explained Jesus died for her sins to prevent her from eternal punishment. Jesus' sacrifice was God’s gift of love, and by believing and accepting Jesus as her Savior, she could go to heaven after death.

Suzie listened closely as the doctor explained John 3:16 and encouraged her to accept Jesus "just as you are." Overwhelmed but hopeful, she prayed for Jesus to come into her heart and thanked Him for saving her.

With faith and newfound hope, Suzie looked forward to being with Jesus in heaven someday. The story closes with encouragement for teens to seek such help and faith for themselves.

Title: That's Baphomet?
Subject: Masonry
Author: Chick
Responses:
Mr. Scott was unreachable by phone due to a storm when a police officer finally arrived at his home to deliver devastating news. The officer informed Mr. Scott and his wife that their son, Tom, had been shot. The wife gasped, asking if Tom was alive. The officer confirmed that Tom was alive but in intensive care, urging them to get to the hospital quickly.

At the hospital, the wife questioned what had happened. The officer explained that it was a suicide attempt, causing the wife to react with shock and horror. In the intensive care unit, a medical professional gave a grim update, stating the bullet was removed and Tom might survive, but he had given up the will to live. The wife found this heartbreaking.

The next morning, the couple sat in the hospital, grappling with the situation. They wondered why God would allow such a tragedy and questioned why Tom would attempt suicide despite having everything. The wife asked why suicide would be an answer when they had given Tom their best with love and devotion. They identified themselves as good people, a church deacon and a lodge member.

Ed, a visitor or friend, suddenly accused the husband Alex of being a Mason, a member of a secretive fraternity. Alex confirmed this, proudly saying he was a Shriner, part of the organization. Ed expressed disbelief and accused Masonry of being witchcraft, to which Alex and his wife defended themselves, claiming Masonry helped them be better Christians, that their meetings always included hymns and talk about Jesus.

Ed argued that the Bible was always open at the lodge, their prayers were said in God’s name, and accused them of ignorance. Alex revealed he left Masonry after discovering Baphomet, presenting pictures and describing Baphomet as the ancient force behind Baal worship and Masonry — an ugly, frightening, satanic figure. Sally, Alex’s wife, was shocked and unaware, as was Ed, who explained most Masons don’t learn this until advanced degrees.

Alex showed images and explained the Eastern Star symbol was an upside-down star, a known satanic symbol. Ed referenced historical occultists like Éliphas Lévi and Albert Pike who linked Baphomet with Satan and Masonry, comparing writings that connected Masonry to dark forces. They showed Tarot cards and historical texts denouncing the forces behind Masonry.

Alex recounted his own initiation taking an oath whereby he declared he was in darkness and wanted to be brought to light — effectively denying Jesus. The story cited Biblical warnings about denying Jesus and spiritual consequences.

Ed explained Masonry as a form of modern Baal worship mixing ungodly religions, condemning its symbols like the "all-seeing eye" and obelisk, calling them pagan and detestable to God. He stressed salvation comes only through faith in Christ, not good works or Masonry’s false promises.

Despite Ed’s warnings, Tommy’s condition worsened. Sally and Alex faced the fact that Masonry had brought witchcraft into their home, shown by symbols like the red fez and crescent moon, which Ed explained were linked to ancient pagan gods and Islam, reinforcing the spiritual danger.
