Ed revealed other witchcraft symbols like the Masonic apron inscribed with pagan icons, which lied about righteousness before God. He gave a stern call to renounce Masonry, burn its objects, and repent. After doing so, Sally and Alex prayed to Jesus, renouncing Masonry as witchcraft.

Soon after, Sally noticed a profound change in Alex and their home — feeling clean and light. They received news Tommy was awake, no longer depressed or suicidal, and eager to see them. They praised God for the restoration.

The story ends with a call for readers needing information on whether Christians should join Masonry to read further materials provided by Chick Publications.

Title: Then What?
Subject: End Time Prophecy
Author: Daniels
Responses:
The world is said to be facing an end in ten years due to a looming crisis. Some influential people claim that the crisis can be resolved if they receive more money. They proclaim that eventually, people will own nothing but will be happy.

A young girl, concerned by what she saw on TV about the world ending, asks her father if it's really true. He admits that the world’s end is indeed coming but explains it won't happen immediately and that much must occur before total destruction. When asked if the world will be destroyed, he confirms it but assures her it won't happen in the sensational way people say.

He goes on to explain that two key things must transpire first. Many people will stop believing in Jesus, and then a man described as the "man of sin" or "the beast," a false Christ, will appear and seem to solve the world's problems. Before really dreadful events occur, Jesus Christ will return to gather and reward His faithful followers, much like He saved Noah in the past.

After Christ takes His followers away, most people will follow the beast, though some will resist the deception. Many will be fooled because they reject the truth and prefer unrighteousness. Those who reject Jesus will be deceived and follow the beast, while some will awaken and be saved once the tribulation begins.

During this time, evil deeds will be rampant much like in Noah’s days, but those who remain faithful to Jesus will face persecution and even death. The beast will make a deal with Israel, allowing them to rebuild their temple. However, about three and a half years into this period, the beast will proclaim himself as God and demand worship, especially from the Jewish people.

People will be forced to receive a mark to buy or sell, and refusing this mark will lead to beheading, while accepting it brings eternal punishment in the lake of fire. God will start displaying His anger by destroying a third of the earth’s trees and grass, darkening the sun, moon, and stars for a third of the time, and a star will fall to the earth.

Water will also be affected: a third of the sea will turn to blood, the sky will pollute rivers and fountains, and those with the beast’s mark will suffer painful sores and be tormented by monstrous locusts. However, there is hope—no one has to be caught in these terrible events.

God has a big plan, wanting everyone to be part of it. Though all have sinned and must pay for their wrongs, God’s justice requires payment for sin, which leads to death. But someone else can pay this price for everyone else’s sins, someone perfect and without sin.

Jesus Christ is that person. He willingly offered Himself as a sacrifice for sins. After being buried for three days and three nights, Jesus rose from the dead. Because of this, anyone who places their faith in Him can be forgiven and receive eternal life.

Jesus will take His followers to heaven, reward them, and then return with them to Earth at the end of seven years. He will land on the Mount of Olives, causing it to split and form a large valley. After this, Jesus will judge who is worthy to enter His kingdom with the help of holy angels.

The beast and false prophet will be thrown into the lake of fire. Jesus will then rule the world for a thousand years. However, at the end of this millennium, the devil will lead another attack on Jerusalem.

Finally, Jesus will destroy the universe, judge everyone, and the saved will live on a new earth with a new heaven. The story ends with an invitation for the reader to believe in Jesus, confess their sins, accept Jesus' sacrifice, and be saved before God's judgment.

The reader is then encouraged to make a decision to accept Jesus and write down their commitment, marking the beginning of their involvement in God's plan.

Title: There Go The Dinosaurs
Subject: Evolution
Author: Chick
Responses:
Once, a dinosaur sensed that it had been spotted by some humans and panicked, thinking it needed to hide. Meanwhile, a group of people, armed and eager, followed a tracker who spotted tracks of the dinosaur, declaring they had seen one and urging others to follow and prepare their weapons.

The dinosaur thought if it could reach the clouds, it would be safe, but it was very tired and had to rest. It could hear the humans getting closer and knew that a few more steps would bring safety. Safe among the clouds, the dinosaur felt invisible and secure.

The hunters thought they saw the dinosaur but were mistaken, laughing at their error. They talked excitedly about enjoying "dino-burgers," acknowledging it might take many trips to capture enough dinosaurs. An older man explained to a boy why dragons (or dinosaurs) were so hard to find now—they were a dying breed, and they might be eating the very last one.

In a classroom setting, a teacher explained that dinosaurs once ruled the world millions of years ago. The cause of their extinction was a giant comet hitting the earth, sparking debate about their demise.

However, a religious perspective was introduced, rejecting the scientific story as a tale from those who don't trust God. According to this view, God created man, animals, and plants in a single week, including dinosaurs, as described in the Bible's book of Genesis.

The story continued with the biblical account of the first humans, Adam and Eve. God forbade them from eating the fruit of one tree, but Eve was tempted by Satan and disobeyed God by eating it. This sin resulted in the downfall of mankind, including Cain killing his brother, leading everything to go downhill.

Humans then rejected God and created their own gods, filling the world with wickedness. God, being righteous, decided to punish sin but gave the people 120 years to repent. Only Noah listened and was instructed to build an ark capable of holding all kinds of animals, including dragons (the creatures later called dinosaurs). Once everyone was inside, God shut the door.

A great storm struck, causing massive floods and changes to the earth's surface. Many plants, animals, and people drowned or were buried with dinosaurs under layers of mud and rock. The dinosaurs that survived were initially fruitful and multiplied but faced a serious challenge— the air had changed. Because the flood destroyed many plants, which produce oxygen, the thinner air made it harder for these large animals to breathe. They became slower and easier to catch.

In a conversation between a grandfather and his grandson, the boy expressed a wish to have seen the earth before the flood. The grandfather explained that sin brought destruction on the earth, but the next time, judgment would come by fire as foretold in the Bible, with the heavens and earth passing away.

The story emphasizes that every person must recognize who Jesus really is: God Almighty, the Son of God, the one who will rule the world and judge all people. Ignoring Him leads to doom.

Two lessons are to be learned from the flood: first, God punishes sin; second, God provides a way out. Some try to hide this truth with stories about dinosaurs and comets, but the real story is found in the Bible.

At the proper time, God sent His Son, Jesus, to a world that did not want Him. Although Jesus' birth was foretold by prophets and angels, few people listened. Jesus performed miracles, healed, raised the dead, and preached, but religious leaders rejected Him and wanted Him dead.

Jesus declared He was the way, the truth, and the life, and that no one comes to the Father except through Him. When the authorities heard this, they arrested Him following Judas' betrayal. Jesus was accused of blasphemy, sentenced to death, and crucified to pay the price for humanity's sins.

Three days later, Jesus rose from the dead, opening the way for sinners to be forgiven and to have fellowship with God. To enter heaven, one must receive Jesus as Savior and Lord by faith.

Noah's family was the only group to believe God and escape the flood's wrath, illustrating that faith alone saves.

The real issue isn't the extinction of dinosaurs but where people will go after death: heaven or hell. Everyone must make a choice—either to accept Jesus as Savior or face judgment.

The comic ends with a call to believe in Jesus Christ to be saved, emphasizing that the choice between heaven and hell is yours.

Title: Thief, The
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
One moonlit night, a menacing figure sneaked into a house quietly, carrying a gun. He aimed at a man sleeping peacefully in bed, ready to kill him. Suddenly, the sleeping man made a noise that disturbed the intruder. 

The man woke up, stretching and yawning, confusing the would-be killer by greeting him with a cheerful "Good morning!" Despite being told that he would be killed for witnessing the crime, the man remained calm and cheerful, explaining this was even better for him. 

The intruder, increasingly agitated, attempted again to intimidate the man but was met with friendliness and a proposition to cook breakfast for possibly his last meal, requesting eggs cooked over easy. As the man cheerfully prepared breakfast, he explained that he would inherit great riches—crowns that are priceless and a mansion greater than anything on Earth, given by the richest man universe. This richest man was Jesus, his best friend, who was soon to return to rule over the world.

The intruder was skeptical, questioning if the man was afraid of death. The peaceful man said he feared God but not the intruder, claiming the killer could only end his tired old body since his soul was destined for heaven. The intruder demanded to hear where the man was going, prompting a vivid description of heaven, a place with streets of gold, angels serving, eternal youth, and the absence of hunger, sickness, or fear. The man would see Jesus, the Creator, face to face, who loved him enough to give His life. Jesus would return to rule forever.

The man explained that everything Jesus owns, he also owns because they are one. Hearing this prompted the intruder to declare his intent to kill the man immediately. However, as he prepared to fire, the man pleaded to be taken along to heaven with him. The intruder was shocked, admitting fear and confusion, and wondered if God would allow him entry considering his life of crime and prison record. The peaceful man reminded him that Jesus forgave even a thief on the cross, welcoming him to paradise.

To the intruder’s surprise, Jesus had suffered injustice, arrest, and execution but rose from the dead, granting eternal life as a gift to all who believe. Jesus' sacrifice paid for human sins, and the intruder was offered that gift too if he would admit his sins and ask for forgiveness. Slowly, the intruder opened his heart, inviting Jesus into his life.

The story concluded with the reminder that when people die, they face either heaven or hell, and that the choice to accept Jesus as Savior leads to eternal life in heaven. It ended with a call to choose eternal life wisely.

Title: Thing, The
Subject: Occult
Author: Chick
Responses:
The story begins on a dark and eerie night where a terrified woman named Maria is screaming for help as she is being attacked by an invisible force. A man witnessing her cries gasps, "Oh my God—poor Maria!" As the screams continue, Maria’s mother rushes into the room, explaining that the thing is after Maria once again. Despite locking the doors, they realize no protection can help her since the entity can pass through any locked door.

Concerned about Maria's mental health, someone asks about the police, but it’s revealed that even the doctor studied Maria thoroughly and confirmed she is not insane. He witnessed her being bitten but found no physical evidence or explanation for the occurrences. Then, attention turns to a priest, who was called to help and placed a medallion of the Blessed Virgin around Maria's neck. However, the medallion was instantly twisted out of shape. The priest tried to sprinkle holy water on her, but it was thrown back in his face, and he hasn't returned since.

The family ponders what this thing attacking Maria could be, reluctantly coming to the conclusion that it must be supernatural, likely a demon. They decide to seek help from a man knowledgeable in dealing with such spiritual afflictions, who is about 30 miles away.

The next day, they visit this man, describing him as a kind and devout Christian who knows the Bible well. He warns them that this is not a matter to take lightly and advises that Maria must want to be freed from the demon's power.

As they share Maria’s story, it is revealed that she began contacting spirits after her grandmother introduced her to fortune-telling, astrology, and Ouija boards, which led her into a deeper fascination with the occult. Her powers developed so much she could move objects without touching them and was called the "good witch" by others in her town. One night, something terrified her so much she swore off spirits, but the demon started tormenting her shortly afterward.

The man promises to come with a trusted friend, a man strong in the Lord, to help free Maria. Despite concerns and fears, they plan to meet the next day and undergo prayer and fasting for her deliverance.

At Maria's home, the man introduces his cousin John, a devout Christian, who wishes to accompany them. Maria's mother worries about John joining, fearing it may harm him if he's not right with God, but John assures her he is fine.

When the men talk to Maria, she demands to know their intentions. Suddenly, the demon possessing her shouts accusations and lies, attacking John viciously. The men command the demon to leave in Jesus' name, but the demon taunts them and insists John is crazy for believing in demons.

With firm resolve, John commands the evil spirit to reveal its name, and it replies, "Verono." John orders the demon to leave Maria and never return. The demon screams in agony as it is driven out.

Afterward, Maria is freed, and it's confirmed she has accepted Jesus Christ as her Lord and Savior. She experiences true peace and thanks God for her deliverance. The men emphasize that Maria must destroy all charms, Ouija boards, and occult items to prevent any future oppression.

Maria commits to living her life in faith, reading the Bible, and sharing her newfound joy. She learns that her body is now the dwelling place of the Holy Spirit, and the demon has left to seek another home.

In the final scene, the demon Verono prowls at night searching for a new victim, while John is found lying on the ground, exhausted but safe, having faced the terrifying ordeal with faith.

The story ends with a warning about the dangers of the occult and a strong message of hope through faith in Jesus Christ.

Title: Things to Come?
Subject: End Time Prophecy
Author: Carter
Responses:
A woman named Delores repeatedly visits a spiritual advisor who promises to reveal her future through a crystal ball. The advisor predicts peace, wealth, and good health. However, Delores calls her a liar and a fake, outraged since she is seriously ill with cancer, unemployed, and homeless. The advisor pleads, asking her to keep the money and begs for forgiveness, but Delores vows never to trust any fortune teller again.

Delores' friend Maria doubts the legitimacy of fortune tellers and mentions knowing someone who truly knows the future, unlike those who use crystals or palms. This person is Father Dowling, who warned Maria to stay away from such dangerous individuals. Despite the warning, Maria visited anyway and sensed a threatening force inside, which terrified her.

Maria explains to Delores that she might lose her career if she can’t provide answers but shares that others say this honest man’s predictions come from an ancient black book. She admits she’s glad it’s Delores, not herself, dealing with him.

Delores then visits Mr. Rogers, a man interested in the future, who immediately welcomes her. He explains he is a devout Roman Catholic who follows everything his priest instructs, attends Mass, helps the poor, and prays the Rosary, hoping his good works will earn him a place in heaven.

Mr. Rogers warns Delores that she is not protected and is about to miss the greatest opportunity of her life. God has given signs in His Book to prepare them for what’s coming. When God’s patience ends, He will command the sounding of a trumpet, signaling Jesus’ return from heaven.

At this moment, believers throughout history will rise with transformed bodies, joining Jesus in the clouds to become His bride. As they enter heaven, they will meet loved ones and face judgment where their deeds will be tested by fire. Good works that survive will be rewarded, including faithful preaching, resisting temptation, and leadership in the church.

Meanwhile, those left behind on Earth will panic. The world will declare an international emergency and likely spread lies to explain the disappearance, such as claiming aliens took the 'fanatics.’ Then, a man posing as Jesus will appear at the Vatican, gaining worship as the new pope but secretly backing a sneak attack on Israel.

No nation will be allowed to aid Israel, who stands alone under attack. Despite massive casualties, Israel survives. The Beast demands a mark to buy or sell food, causing a famine. Jesus calls the Vatican “the Great Whore” for destroying faith and burning followers.

Satan inhabits the Beast, defiles the Jewish temple, and prepares for Armageddon. Jesus, sacrificed 2000 years ago as the Lamb of God, now returns as a lion to defeat the Beast. The Beast’s armies are slaughtered; Jesus rules as Messiah and King.

After a thousand years, Jesus judges all according to their deeds. Those not saved face eternal punishment in the lake of fire, while believers receive eternal joy and mansions.

Delores is faced with a choice: reign with Christ forever or follow Satan’s popes, receive the Beast’s mark, and spend eternity in fire. Suddenly, a thunderous roar overwhelms her as reality confronts this prophecy.

Mr. Rogers vanishes in an instant, confirming the rapture’s arrival. The story closes with reminders: the rapture and World War III are coming, a one-world church will emerge with the Beast, and salvation is through faith in Jesus Christ. Will Jesus call your name? The answer lies in believing on the Lord Jesus Christ to be saved.

Title: This Was Your Life
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
Once there was a man who lived comfortably, enjoying the fruits of his labor. He drank, smoked his pipe, and lived a carefree life, thinking to himself, "Take thine ease, eat, drink, and be merry," repeating the words from the Bible in Luke 12:19. He was confident and full of pride, with no concern for what came after life.

One night, suddenly, the Grim Reaper appeared and said, "But God said unto him, Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee," from Luke 12:20. The man was shocked and terrified. In an instant, he was dead, and his pipe and drink were strewn on the ground as he fell lifelessly, realizing, "It is appointed unto men once to die, but after this the judgment," as Hebrews 9:27 says.

At his funeral, the pastor proclaimed, "He was a good man!" But a voice reminded that, as Isaiah 64:6 says, "We are all as an unclean thing, and all our righteousnesses are as filthy rags; and we all do fade as a leaf; and our iniquities, like the wind, have taken us away."

Suddenly, the dead were called forth from their graves by a voice: "Marvel not at this: for the hour is coming, in the which all that are in the graves shall hear his voice," according to John 5:28. The man rose, confused, thinking, "What's happening? Wait! I'm dead! It's all over!" The scripture told, "And shall come forth; they that have done good, unto the resurrection of life; and they that have done evil, unto the resurrection of damnation," from John 5:29.

An angel approached him, saying, "Come, you have an appointment!" The man protested, not understanding, "Judgment? But you don't understand, heaven and hell are here on earth—I’ve always said that!" The angel assured him, "Will anyone else be there?" and was answered, "Oh yes, quite a number!"

The man was taken through the cosmos, pointed to his destination, and cried, "I simply refuse to believe this is happening to me!" But the judgment proceeded. He claimed, "Now look! I've lived a real good life! I was no different than anyone else!" The angel said calmly, "Everything has been recorded!" Romans 3:10 emphasizes, "As it is written, there is none righteous, no, not one!"

The man was brought before God, who sat on a great throne, judging the dead by the books of life and deeds, as described in Revelation 20:12. The command came, "Review his life!" and the reply, "Yes, Lord!" The man saw images of his life projected: as a baby, a teenager, a young adult with sins and failures exposed. Embarrassed, he wished those stories could be hidden, but was reminded by Matthew 12:36, "That every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment." He saw his sins of pride, disobedience, lies, theft, and more—"For there is nothing covered that shall not be revealed," says Matthew 10:26.

Even moments in church and thoughts he ignored were recorded. Despite all this, he remained defiant. The scriptures told him, "For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have everlasting life," (John 3:16), and "That if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shall believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved," (Romans 10:9). Yet, he arrogantly said, "Bunk—I don't need Christ! I'll make it my way!"

Then the final judgment was proclaimed: "Open the book of life!" But the angel said quietly, "His name does not appear, Lord!" The sentence passed: "Depart from me, ye cursed into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels," as Matthew 25:41 warns. The man was cast into torment, for "whoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire," from Revelation 20:15.

The comic concludes with a warning: This can be your life! "The Lord is not slack concerning his promise," urging repentance, quoting 2 Peter 3:9. For those who truly believe, repent, and accept Christ as Savior, there is hope and new life.

The man who once mocked the idea of judgment now prays, "Lord, I know I'm a sinner—I repent of my sins and acknowledge Jesus Christ as my Lord and Savior," as the scripture from Isaiah 1:18 offers cleansing and hope.

In the end, the Lord welcomes those faithful, saying, "Well done, thou good and faithful servant—enter thou into the joy of thy Lord!" and it is closed with Psalm 116:15, "Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of his saints."

This story reminds us all to examine our lives, seek forgiveness, and choose the path to eternal life before it is too late.

Title: Throw Away Kid, The
Subject: Abandoned
Author: Chick
Responses:
A young girl was forcefully arrested by law enforcement officers. As she cried out "Oww! Stop it! You're hurting me!", the officers informed her that she was under arrest and had the right to remain silent. The girl responded harshly, calling one of the officers a "lousy pig." Meanwhile, an elderly woman watched the scene from her window and silently prayed, "Lord Jesus, please save her precious little girl next door."

The woman reflected on the situation, thinking to herself that she knew her daughter would end up in jail someday. She couldn't imagine raising her granddaughter, believing such a thing to be unreasonable. The judge sentenced the girl to 13 years in federal prison. However, the girl’s grandmother was determined not to raise the child herself. She arranged for a man named Herbert, who had a questionable liking for little girls, to raise the child, offering a monthly payment for the task.

Herbert and his associate, Josh, planned to deliver the child away from their town. They showed the grandmother a map and $650 as payment. Clueless about the child's name, the grandmother dismissed the concern, eager to be rid of her granddaughter. While the girl slept during the journey, Josh suggested selling her, referring to her as a "throwaway kid." Herbert agreed, displaying a cruel indifference to the child's fate.

On their way to Arkansas, Jan and Josh talked about possibly partying instead of continuing their drive, but the financial pressure kept them focused. Suddenly, a loud bang startled them—the car tire had blown out. They stopped, and after a brief delay, decided to abandon the girl while she was asleep in the forest.

The girl heard her captors insult her, calling her a brat, before they abandoned her and sought drugs nearby. As the girl woke up, clutching her teddy bear tightly, a ministering angel appeared to protect her. However, a hungry mama bear saw the child and approached, ready to attack. The angel intervened, causing the bear to flee with her cubs to safety.

Meanwhile, Jan and Josh, high on drugs, raced recklessly down the highway. Josh challenged Jan to push the car to over 100 mph. At 101 mph, the car's right front tire blew out, sending them crashing violently into two gas pumps. The accident was fatal; by 2:20 AM, Jan and Josh were dead. Moments later, devils came and took their souls to hell, unheard by anyone.

More than a mile away, an old dog named Cookie heard the girl’s name and went to find her. Guided by an angel, Cookie reached the girl and helped keep her warm. The angel then instructed Cookie to take the girl to his home, leading her into a new life.

The girl, who had no memory of her real name, was nicknamed "Little Brat," but Mrs. Baker, who took her in, renamed her Joy. Mrs. Baker showed her love and promised protection. Joy, now six years old, attended church with Mrs. Baker but had yet to receive Jesus into her heart.

One day, a preacher explained the difference between right and wrong, quoting the Bible about sin and judgment. The preacher proclaimed Jesus as God Almighty, explaining how Jesus lived a perfect life, died for sins, and rose from the dead. He invited anyone to pray for forgiveness and receive Jesus as Savior.

Joy prayed and accepted Jesus into her heart. This changed her life forever, giving her hope and salvation. The story ended with a message that Jesus loves every child and offers forgiveness and eternal life to anyone who believes in Him.

It closed with an invitation for readers to accept Jesus, reminding them no sin is too great to be forgiven and Christ's sacrifice is the only way to salvation.

Title: Tiny Shoes
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
Once upon a time in a humble village, a loving father told his young son Juanito, “When I get rich, I will buy this land for you.” But Juanito’s wishes were simpler. “Papa, all I want is tiny shoes to keep my little feet warm.” His father smiled warmly and reassured him, “Tiny shoes? Of course, my son. As soon as I get paid, I will buy your tiny shoes.” Juanito’s eyes sparkled. “Really, Papa?” “Yes, Juanito… you can trust your papa!”

Excited, Juanito ran to his mother and exclaimed, “Mama, Papa is going to buy me some shoes!” His mother replied kindly, “How wonderful. Your papa is a good man, Juanito.”

Later, when Juanito’s father was paid, he went to collect his money. But rather than buying shoes, a man tempted him, “Juan, do you feel lucky? Let’s get into that card game… you can double your money.” He followed the man to a saloon. “Let’s stop in at the saloon for one little drink. Come on, Juan.” Sadly, Juan lost his money and was given another drink. “You lose again, Juan. It’s too bad.” When the saloon closed, the bartender told him, “It’s time to go home, Juan. It’s closing time.” “Already?” Juan hiccupped.

That night, Juan came home drunk. His wife asked, “Oh, Juan… you’re drunk again. Where is the money for food?” Juan muttered, “It’s all gone… I don’t know what happened. I’ve got to get some sleep.” “Leave me alone,” he said.

The next day Juan’s son eagerly asked, “Papa, did you bring my tiny shoes?” But Juan, feeling sick and with a headache, told him to go away. Juanito said, “You said I could trust you, Papa. You lied! And God won’t let liars into heaven!” Juan told him angrily, “Shut up, Juanito! Get out of here.” Still, Juanito said, “I love you, Papa… and Jesus loves you too!”

His wife prayed silently, “O God, make my papa stop lying so he can go to heaven.” Juanito shivered, “My feet hurt. Please make him buy my shoes.” She prayed earnestly, “Father, whatever it takes to save my husband, please do it, in Jesus’ name.” She whispered, “Amen.”

The next payday, Juan’s friends urged him to join them at the saloon. “Be a man, Juan… Just one drink, okay?” they said. “I feel lucky tonight. Can I play?” Juan asked. “It’s good old Juan. Give Juan a drink.”

But soon, Juan had lost all his money again, and the friends told him, “Everybody’s gone, Juan. I’ve got to put you outside. Come on, you drunken bum.” The next morning, Juan lay outside feeling the cold. “Look at that man. Is he dead?” someone asked. “No, he’s drunk,” another said.

Juan’s wife confronted him, “Juan, how could you? You promised! I’ll have to get a job so we can eat.” “No! Your place is in the home. I’m a proud man. I’ll earn the money,” Juan answered stubbornly.

Later, Juan cut his foot on glass. “Papa, I cut my foot,” Juanito said. “Did you get my tiny shoes?” he added hopefully.

Juan promised before God, “I’ll be a good husband and father. I’ll bring home my salary. I won’t gamble anymore. And Juanito, I swear I’ll buy your tiny shoes.” “I promise,” he said.

Juanito’s mother said warmly, “Oh, Juan… please keep your word.” Juanito added, “We love you, Papa. I know you’ll bring me my tiny shoes.”

That evening, Juan shouted happily, “I’ll be home tonight with Juanito’s shoes and the money.” “Papa, I’m so excited. You won’t let me down, Papa… not this time.” “Be careful, Juan. It looks like a storm is coming,” warned his wife.

The storm raged as Juan hurried home from work. At the saloon, the owner called out, “Here’s your pay, Juan… You’d better hurry home. The storm is getting worse.” Juan declined, “Not tonight. I’ve got to get my son his shoes.”

The saloon owner and friends persuaded him, “Juan, Juan… It’s cold tonight. We need to get warm. The saloon is on the way.” “Just one little drink, Juan. I’ll pay for it.”

Juan’s wife prayed urgently, “O God, don’t let Juan go to the saloon tonight. Stop him.” She felt sick. Suddenly, lightning struck the saloon with a loud explosion. Lightning hit the saloon!

Juan’s wife thought, “That was the hand of God… I want those tiny shoes for my son. He will love these shoes. They are beautiful.” But the storm’s fury broke the bridge. “Oh no! The bridge is out… I can’t cross it tonight.”

At 1 a.m., Juanito called out, “Papa… Where are my tiny shoes, Papa? Hurry, Papa. I’m so cold.” His mother cried out desperately, “Juanito! Where have you gone? JUANITO!”

Juanito wandered in the storm, hearing beautiful music and asking himself, “Are you my Jesus?” His mother followed, crying, “JUANITO! Oh, my God, help me.”

The next morning, at 10 a.m., Juan came home with the tiny shoes. “Juanito! Juanito!” But it was too late. Juan’s wife held their son, crying, “No! Oh, no… my son can’t be dead. Not my Juanito! How could this happen?” She mourned, “He died of pneumonia, Juan.”

Juan wept bitterly. “I’ll never see my little son again. He’s lost forever.” A friend tried to comfort him, “Juan, he can’t come back to you, but you can go see him… in heaven.”

Juan sobbed, “O God, forgive me. I’ve gambled, lied, and was a drunkard. Please forgive my wickedness.” The friend shared, “For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.”

Juan prayed, “Lord Jesus, come into my heart and become my Savior so when I die I can be with You and little Juanito.” He whispered, “Thank You, Lord Jesus.”

And from that day on, Juan vowed to live a good life, keeping the promise to his son, and walking faithfully with God.

Title: Titanic
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Carter
Responses:
Chester and his wife were preparing to embark on a significant trip. As they said their goodbyes, Chester noticed that Aunt Sophie was not joining them. When asked why, his wife explained that Aunt Sophie had only wanted him to ensure Chester's name was in the Book of Life. Chester dismissed Aunt Sophie as crazy and wanted to proceed without mentioning her again.

Upon boarding the ship, Chester's wife was enchanted by the room they were given. Chester, however, was skeptical and lamented Aunt Sophie's ominous warning. He joked that God Himself couldn't sink the ship and tried to brush off any talk of Aunt Sophie. He then leaned into his ambition, planning to mingle with wealthy passengers to advance his position. His wife worried he was too focused on money, but Chester insisted it was all that mattered.

Later, Chester discovered that Aunt Sophie had placed a note in his suitcase urging him to accept Jesus Christ as his Savior to secure a place in the Book of Life. Angrily, Chester cursed Aunt Sophie and her message, wishing she was dead.

As the ship sailed, Chester prepared to meet Mr. Astor, a wealthy and influential man. He looked forward to the connections and wealth this opportunity might bring. However, moments later, the ship's communication officer reported an iceberg sighting. The captain was informed immediately, and officers attempted to spot the iceberg in daylight.

Despite efforts to navigate around the iceberg, it was clear they had struck it. The damage to the ship was extensive, and the crew began preparations to abandon ship, ordering passengers to don life jackets. Officers sent distress signals, and the captain ordered all women and children into the lifeboats.

The ship's musicians played as the last lifeboats were lowered, and many passengers faced the grim reality of survival at sea. Among the chaos, Chester's wife expressed her love for him and urged him to board a lifeboat. The ship's final moments were tumultuous, with the boilers exploding and the ship sinking.

In the aftermath, Chester was presumed lost at sea. His wife prayed that he had repented and was saved.

The story ends with a solemn reflection on the judgment that awaits all men, referencing Biblical scripture about facing judgment after death. Chester, having ignored Aunt Sophie's warnings and the message of salvation, now faces judgment at the Great White Throne, where Christ judges those who died in their sins.

The Book of Life was opened, but Chester's name was not found within. As a result, he was condemned to everlasting punishment, contrasting with the promise of eternal life for the righteous.

Title: Traitor, The
Subject: Hinduism
Author: Carter
Responses:
In India, 1982, a man approached the goddess Kali with a desperate prayer. He gave his firstborn son to Kali, pleading for her to answer his prayer. Two days later, an inspector was assigned to investigate a horrifying crime involving the child's death. The inspector vowed to find the murderer, but the case took a strange turn.

The high priest warned the inspector that if Kali’s servant was arrested for sacrificing the child, Kali would curse and destroy not only him but also the villagers who worshipped her. The inspector was ordered to close the case and live.

One night, the inspector was attacked by Kali herself, riding a tiger, and was thrown to his death over a cliff. Kali’s wrath was so fierce that she demanded blood sacrifices to calm her fury. Villagers were terrified and urged to offer blood to Kali or face her wrath.

At midnight, Kali flew on the back of a tiger to a small hut where the father of the sacrificed boy was found dead, his head severed and his blood missing. The village was left in shock.

Fearful villagers brought gifts to Kali’s high priest, who, with the help of astral projection, kept watch over nearby villages. His supernatural demons were so powerful that no one dared look him in the eyes, including his terrified wife.

Meanwhile, in Bombay, a wealthy family refused to pay the extortion demands of thugs associated with Kali’s cult. The father insisted his wealth and the police would protect his son and that Shiva would protect them.

The thugs, led by Garrar, took their request to Kali’s high priest, who gave them a black goat for a ritual sacrifice to Kali, promising great favor. Garrar begged Kali for power to kill the resistant rich man’s son, and, empowered by Kali’s demons, Garrar succeeded in killing the boy. The rich father was powerless against the forces of Kali.

The story then revealed that Kali’s power was stronger than any god in India, even Shiva, Ganesh, and Hanuman. When Kali appeared in her full terrifying form, she demanded blood from her high priest.

Politicians, police officials, and thugs all feared Kali and sought her blessing. One day, a brave stranger arrived, showing no fear. The high priest, wanting the stranger dead, called upon Kali’s demons to slaughter him.

The demons pursued the stranger fiercely, but Kali herself appeared, pushing her demons forward in a frenzy. However, a powerful force stopped the demons just feet from the stranger. They turned in rage and attacked the priest instead, who was brutally beaten.

Bewildered by these events, the priest approached the stranger and asked about his god. The stranger identified his god as the Lord Jesus Christ, who has only one head and two arms and carries no weapons. He explained that Jesus Christ demands no blood sacrifices and is the most powerful God on earth—the creator of all things in heaven, earth, and under the earth.

The stranger told the priest that God loves him with a greater love than he could imagine, and that Jesus made a way for people to go to heaven, the home of God and his Son, Lord Jesus. Upon accepting Jesus Christ, the Holy Spirit would bring peace and freedom from fear.

He explained that because of human sin, Satan controls the world and its false religions, creating idols like the gods of India, who are demons meant to steal souls and lead people to hell. The Word of God states that people die once, face judgment, and those who refuse repentance are cast into eternal fire.

But God wishes all to repent and offers salvation through Jesus Christ, who shed His blood for our sins and rose from the dead. Jesus said He is the way, the truth, and the life, and no one comes to the Father except through Him, whose commandments include worshiping no other gods.

The priest was in despair but forbidden by Kali to bring the followers food until the stranger was killed. He attempted twice to murder the stranger but failed, as the stranger’s power protected him.

In desperation, the priest secretly visited the stranger. He heard the stranger speak to God, and though scared, the priest asked if the stranger’s God hated him. The stranger replied that God loved him with an overwhelming love.

The story concluded with an invitation to choose whom to serve: Jesus Christ or Satan. Believing in Jesus Christ saves you from hell, and calling upon His name will save you and set you free.

The story is a dramatic account illustrating the power of faith in Jesus Christ over fearsome traditions and false gods, emphasizing God’s love, salvation, and victory over evil.

Title: Trap, The
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
The story begins at an exclusive party where only the rich and famous are invited, though an exception is made for Max, the husband’s brother, who isn’t quite part of their elite circle. In the midst of the gathering, someone notices the ambassador arriving with a mysterious companion.

Marsha is introduced to Robert, who has a remarkable gift. He channels the spirit entity named Seth, who speaks through him in a trance. Robert claims Seth is a highly evolved soul who is extremely wise but not currently in a human body. When asked why Seth would provide insights, Robert explains that Seth has knowledge about people's past lives, revealing the concept of reincarnation. Despite skepticism, Robert insists he only wants to help people and even offers a large sum of money for the spiritual insights he provides.

Max questions the necessity of a channeler and whether past lives are real. Robert explains the ongoing cycle of reincarnation aimed at resolving previous life's problems. However, Max doubts Seth’s character, suspecting the entity could be deceptive. Charlie, another guest, steps in and warns Max that Seth is a liar. He explains that Jesus never taught reincarnation, and in fact, warned against false prophets like Seth, comparing them to ravenous wolves in sheep’s clothing.

Charlie then recounts a true story told by Jesus, emphasizing the real message behind life and death. Jesus describes a rich man clothed in fine linens who feasted sumptuously every day. Nearby, a beggar named Lazarus, suffering and covered in sores, sought only the crumbs from the rich man’s table. Despite Lazarus’s misery, the rich man’s brother called him an embarrassment and did nothing to help.

Lazarus’s situation worsened, and after his death, angels carried him to Abraham’s bosom. The rich man also died and was buried, but he found himself in torment in a fiery place, separated from Lazarus by a great gulf that could not be crossed. Desperate, the rich man begged Abraham to send Lazarus to cool his tongue, but Abraham explained that in life, the rich man had received good things while Lazarus suffered; now, their roles were reversed with Lazarus comforted and the rich man tormented.

The rich man then pleaded for Lazarus to warn his five brothers so they would avoid his fate, but Abraham said they already had Moses and the prophets and would not be persuaded even if someone rose from the dead. The rich man argued that if one went to them from the dead, they would repent, but Abraham responded that this was not true.

Charlie explains to Max and Marsha that this story shows reincarnation is a lie and a trap to give false hope. The Bible states that life is fleeting and that humans die once followed by judgment. Max becomes troubled, realizing that all their lives are being recorded and judged.

Max reflects on his deeds, both good and bad, and worries about his eternal destiny. Charlie shares scriptures revealing that no one is righteous and all have sinned. Max questions if the rich man is still in torment after 2,000 years, and Charlie confirms he will be tormented for eternity, quoting Revelation about eternal torment.

Charlie offers hope, saying God made a way to escape, wanting everyone to repent. This is why Jesus came to die for sins. He explains that salvation comes by believing in Jesus, who is the only way to God. The channeler’s teachings, Charlie says, are lies and part of New Age deception.

To illustrate the final judgment, Charlie shares a vision from Revelation where the dead are judged according to their works, and an angel opens the book of life asking if Charles's name is there. It is not. Charlie urges Max to repent and turn to God, believe in Jesus’ sacrifice, and trust Him as personal Savior.

Max prays, confessing he is a sinner and placing faith in Jesus. His name is then written in the Book of Life. Charlie reminds Max of God’s promise that those faithful to Jesus will be welcomed into His eternal joy.

The story ends with hope and a call to choose the narrow path to salvation through Jesus Christ, the true way, life, and truth.

Title: Trial, The
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
Annie and Debbie were at school when a confrontation arose between them. Debbie threatened to tell her mother what Annie had said. When Debbie told her mother, Mrs. Baxter exclaimed that nobody would tell her daughter such things. Mrs. Baxter then took Debbie to a lawyer to file a lawsuit.

In court, the lawyer told the judge that the defendant, Ms. Ann Gordon, was infamous for saying hateful words that had inflamed the community. When asked if she wanted to say anything before trial, Ann replied that she had told Debbie what God said and even offered Debbie a cookie.

The lawyer announced that he would call highly respected clergymen from four major religions to testify, claiming that Ms. Gordon had brainwashed Debbie and violated Mrs. Baxter's civil and religious rights. The lawyer presented "hate literature," quoting Jesus saying, "I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me."

A heated debate ensued, with clergy from various faiths arguing theology: Bishop Danny O'Tool defended the Catholic doctrine, insisting there was no salvation outside the Church of Rome. Other religious leaders, including Islamic and Jewish representatives, expressed outrage, saying the statement insulted their religions and rejected their beliefs.

Dr. Green, a theology professor, testified that the verse should be removed from the Bible because of its exclusivity, calling Annie a fanatic who should be removed from society. Ann was then questioned about what she told Debbie, and she admitted that she told Debbie Jesus was the only way to heaven.

Mrs. Baxter testified about the emotional stress caused by the incident. Debbie was called to the stand, with the lawyer urging her to tell the court everything that happened. Debbie explained that when Annie told her to ask Jesus into her heart, she did so. She said she loved God and everybody, and that Jesus was her way to heaven because Jesus doesn't lie.

The case was dismissed, and a judgment of ten million dollars was mentioned in passing. Years later, Mrs. Baxter, Bishop O'Tool, Abdulla Ab-Du-La, Rabbi Ginsburg, and Dr. Green had all passed on. Suddenly, all five rose from their graves, as a higher court took over.

This higher court was the One who will judge every soul. He declared that Annie was right: there is only one way to heaven, and that He, Jesus Christ, is that way.

He explained that He left heaven to come to earth and die for humanity's sins, so they could come to heaven. Only by His sacrifice of shed blood could sin be washed away. He warned that rejecting this gift meant dying in sin and being cast into everlasting fire prepared for the devil and his angels.

Satan opposes the gospel and calls it "Hate Literature." The story ends with a call to believe on the Lord Jesus Christ to be saved and a form for readers to affirm their faith, emphasizing that Jesus is the only way to heaven.

Title: Trick, The
Subject: Halloween
Author: Chick
Responses:
One month before Halloween, in a small town in the USA, a dark gathering took place in an old mansion. A group of people assembled to prepare for Halloween, which they deemed a very important time to honor their most holy and glorious father, Satan. They believed this holy day was designed by Satan to receive additional sacrifices. The leader, Sister Charity, addressed the crowd, explaining that sacrifices were necessary for their cleansing and to receive Satan’s blessing.

Sister Charity detailed their plans, confessing they needed more sacrifices this year and had to prepare more children to worship Satan. The attendees would receive specific assignments from priests and priestesses, using techniques involving planting razor blades, crushed glass, pins, and injecting special poisons and drugs into treats. Satan also wanted to bring more children under his influence through special incantations and curses placed on candy.

Later in October, a sinister ritual was performed surrounded by pentagrams and various instruments of poison and harm. The participants requested Satan’s guiding demons to bless these tools for his glory. They eagerly awaited Halloween night, when children would come knocking on doors, unaware of the evil lurking in their treats.

On Halloween night, three children prepared to trick-or-treat. Their parents warned them to only visit familiar neighbors. Johnny Dexter was instructed to be home within the hour. As the children went door to door, one woman eagerly handed out candy bars, some of which were injected with poison.

Thirty minutes later, a scream pierced the quiet neighborhood. At the emergency room, Dr. Dexter informed Johnny’s parents that Johnny had died from a drug overdose, while Susie was in intensive care and Jerry was in surgery. Brenda, the woman who gave out the poisoned candy, was consoled in her grief, calling the tragedy unfathomable.

Meanwhile, Sister Charity watched the news and gloated over the success of their dark deeds. However, she was later condemned to eternal torment in hell, realizing too late the true cost of serving Satan.

Ten months after Johnny’s death, Brenda and a friend named Becky discussed recent troubling changes in Susie and Jerry’s behavior. They struggled with rebellion and disobedience. Becky revealed she was an ex-witch who now served Jesus and explained the dark origins of Halloween: an ancient Druid custom involving human sacrifices and cursing children as a form of control and devotion to Satan.

Becky described how the trick-or-treat tradition stemmed from Druids demanding sacrifices in exchange for protection from demons, a practice Satan had adopted and corrupted. Brenda initially resisted the idea, but Becky explained that Satan’s power was real, despite common disbelief.

The women discussed Satan’s true nature as a powerful enemy intent on hurting people, especially children, by influencing their minds through demonic incantations. Becky expressed concern for Susie and Jerry, who were clearly under this sinister influence.

However, she brought hope by sharing that Jesus Christ came to destroy Satan’s power, offering salvation and protection to those who accept Him. Encouraged by this truth, Becky led Brenda in prayer to accept Jesus as Lord and Savior, asking for deliverance from demonic influences on their children.

One month later, Brenda told Becky that Susie and Jerry were restored to their true selves, free from Satan’s grip and secure in their salvation. They gave thanks to God for His power to overcome darkness and bring healing to their family. The story closed with a message of hope, warning about Halloween’s dark origins while emphasizing the power of faith in Jesus to triumph over evil.

Title: True Path, The
Subject: Native Americans
Author: Chick
Responses:
In the beginning, a radiant figure appeared before a man and a woman in a beautiful garden filled with lush plants and fruit trees. This figure warned them solemnly, "No!" as they gazed at a tree abundant with appealing fruit.

Despite the warning, the woman reached out and took the fruit. As a result, the tree transformed into a sinister presence marked with a skull and crossbones, symbolizing sin. The man and woman became covered in soot, ashamed of their disobedience.

The radiant figure then built a tall wall between them and himself, separating them. The man and woman remained outside, dirty and burdened, along with a growing crowd of people from various backgrounds, all separated by the wall.

Along the wall were signs pointing the way to "God's Love Gift Inside" and "Free Gift Ahead." Some in the crowd looked hopeful, as these signs beckoned them.

Those who chose to enter saw pictures on the wall illustrating the story of salvation: a mother and child, the Nativity scene, the Magi, and a shepherd tending sheep. A sign labeled "The True Path" guided them forward.

They came to images depicting the crucifixion of Jesus Christ, his death on the cross, and his ascension into heaven. One sign read, "God's Free Love Gift." Many bowed in reverence, moved by the message of love and sacrifice.

The redeemed, now cleansed and joyful, moved on together with peace and unity. They pointed others toward the cross, sharing the message of hope.

Meanwhile, some in the crowd rejected the message, choosing to remain in darkness and isolation, turning away from the true path. One man, surrounded by darkness, walked past the signs with a defiant expression.

Those who accepted the gift climbed a stairway leading upward to light and peace, hand in hand, filled with joy.

The radiant figure reappeared, welcoming all, echoing the promise from scripture: "For God so loved the world, that He gave His only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in Him should not perish, but have everlasting life." (John 3:16)

The story emphasizes the choice each person has to accept God's love freely given through Jesus Christ or to reject it and remain separated. It portrays the transformation from sin and separation to redemption and eternal life.

Title: Trust Me
Subject: Drugs/Alcohol
Author: Chick
Responses:
A man is walking down an alley at night when he's suddenly threatened at gunpoint. Afraid, he is led into a dimly lit basement where he meets a group of intimidating-looking, tattooed criminals. They shake hands, but the man is soon pressured to take a mysterious pill by one of the gang members. After taking the pill, he feels an intense dizziness as his perception begins to swirl wildly.

The gang leader warns him that he must pay next time or there will be consequences. Three days later, the man, desperate for money, is seen stealing a television while the dog in the house sleeps. Upon returning to the gang, he is given a syringe with a sinister grin and called “a present.” Soon, the man becomes addicted, begging for more drugs, only to be told he can have more if he sells drugs for the gang.

Eventually, he is introduced to a larger dealer who convinces him to trust him with a promise of money. However, the man is immediately arrested in a sting operation, shackled, and faces a harsh prison sentence. In jail, the man is accosted and beaten by other inmates as guards watch. He cries out for help, but no aid comes. The next day, he is badly injured and receiving medical treatment.

Three months later, doctors diagnose him with AIDS. Six months later, in prison, another inmate, offering him a small card, says, “Here’s the only one you can trust!” The card reads "Jesus Loves You." A narrative box explains the role of Jesus Christ as the only way to heaven, emphasizing His sacrifice and resurrection.

The man, overwhelmed with emotion, repents and prays for forgiveness, trusting Jesus as his Savior. He begs the Lord to save him, and two days later, he is depicted being welcomed into heaven by angels, as the story concludes with a verse about entering the joy of the Lord.

Title: Trust the Science
Subject: Science
Author: Daniels
Responses:
A scientist was excited about his discovery and dreamed of becoming famous, envisioning books, magazines, and documentaries showcasing his work. While proudly holding his Carbon-14 (C-14) test results, he was interrupted by a woman who commanded him to get her coffee. When he tried to speak with another worker, she asserted her authority and warned that she would fire anyone who did not obey her.

The scientist shared his excitement and promised to bring her coffee if she listened. Reluctantly, she agreed. The scientist explained how his C-14 samples had been scientifically dated, and when he asked about the samples' age compared to what was needed, he winked, suggesting he had an underlying theory.

An older man, thrilled with the coincidence, claimed the C-14 results confirmed this exact age. He promised to prepare the paperwork and claimed that his positive C-14 test was proof that would change all history books. The woman challenged the scientist, questioning the evidence.

A large man dressed like a Viking argued about 300 Viking skeletons excavated in England during the 1980s, saying they proved his point that the skeletons were not from the "Great Heathen Army" of 865-78 AD. The older man insisted otherwise, but the Viking explained that the bones showed fewer C-14 results because Vikings ate lots of fish, and fish contain less C-14. Thus, the bones appeared older than they really were. Additionally, coins found with the Vikings dated from 865 to 871 AD, confirming the timeframe.

The scientist asked if science could reveal someone's birth date, admitting no test can reveal an exact date. He explained that reliable eyewitnesses record and sign such dates. The woman agreed, saying that good eyewitnesses help reconstruct the past, and it’s not enough to trust science alone — this is how knowledge about Jesus is possible.

She was interrupted by a man who threatened to throw her out for talking religion with a scientist. The woman urged him to continue.

The gathering, consisting of various people, encouraged her to share more. She explained that no ancient manuscript is as well-documented as the Bible. If the gospel writers had lied, thousands could dispute their story, but that never happened because many eyewitnesses knew the truth about Jesus.

She described how shepherds witnessed Jesus at His birth in Bethlehem, and this was just the beginning. In Nazareth, people watched Jesus grow up and learn the family trade. Tens of thousands witnessed His ministry over three and a half years, starting with His baptism. Many saw His public trial and watched Him die, quoting scripture and explaining He was buried in a tomb but rose three days later.

For 40 days after His resurrection, over 500 eyewitnesses saw Him. The apostles saw Him ascend into heaven, and angels promised His return. These eyewitnesses then wrote the Bible, which no scientific evidence can disprove.

She added that no lab can replicate one-time miracles. Science is useful for repeatable events, but to study past unique events, eyewitness accounts are essential. She listed events Jesus believed in that modern science calls “unscientific” — like the parting of the Red Sea, the resurrection, and other miracles.

Jesus believed in two other “unscientific” events: creation and the flood. He said God created male and female from the beginning, not genderless amoebas. She explained the flood when Noah entered the ark, the flood came, and destroyed all outside. Ocean fossils found in inland rock layers are best explained by a worldwide flood.

Scientists couldn't observe creation, but there was one witness: Jesus, the Creator. She quoted John 1:3 and Colossians 1:16, explaining that Jesus created all things and that He is also the judge of all.

Jesus, as the Judge, needs no witnesses because He knows all facts. The Bible says “The eyes of the LORD are in every place…” Our sins are recorded, and we are already condemned, but salvation is offered through faith in Jesus.

The woman concluded by saying that despite being “unscientific,” the many witnesses prove it to be true. She offered to teach about prayer.

Then Dr. Gull appeared, and the scientist tried to complain to her. The woman answered his call with a “Yes?” The scientist walked away saying “Never mind,” leaving a card asking if the reader admitted to being a sinner, believed Jesus died for their sins, and had asked Jesus to forgive them and come into their heart.

Thus, the story showed the relationship between science, eyewitness testimony, history, faith, and the importance of Jesus as both Creator and Savior.

Title: Twin Towers
Subject: Catholicism
Author: Chick
Responses:
The story begins during a fierce storm at sea. Powerful warships, heavily armed, aggressively attack the pope’s magnificent ship of state. The battle is intense, with cannon fire, incendiary bombs, books, and gospel tracts all deployed to destroy the pope’s vessel. To save his priceless ship, the pope directs his course toward the “Twin Towers.” Through the thick smoke and fire, he spots the Roman Catholic statues perched atop these towers, realizing they are his only hope for salvation.

As the conflict escalates, one enemy ship crashes into the pope’s vessel, creating a large hole in its side. In that critical moment, a miraculous breeze from the Twin Towers instantly seals the damage, keeping the pope’s ship afloat. Enemy cannons explode, and their own ships begin to sink. In the chaos, the enemy resorts to hand-to-hand combat, blaspheming fiercely. Sadly, the pope is mortally wounded and dies.

Hearing the news, Father Sebastian confirms the pope’s death but pledges to continue the dream of Saint Don Bosco. Victory cheers erupt among the enemy fleet, but the new pope quickly takes the helm, steering the ship safely between the Twin Towers. The two Roman Catholic statues on the towers—the “Blessed Virgin Mary” goddess and the wafer “Jesus” god—are said to have saved both the pope and his ship. The enemy ships panic and disappear beneath the waves.

Mrs. McGill adores the stories of saints told by Father Sebastian, expressing her love and asking for prayers for herself and her granddaughter, Mary Ann. Meanwhile, the religious leaders plan to gain control of Mrs. McGill’s vast property holdings for God. They reveal that Mary Ann is Mrs. McGill’s only living relative and heir to the fortune. Suspicious, they instruct Father Sebastian to find out everything about Mary Ann before making any moves.

One week later, Father Sebastian learns that Mary Ann and Mrs. McGill have had a terrible fight. Mary Ann, now “Bible crazy,” has accused the priest of attacking her faith and has rejected the church. This is horrifying news since leaving the church is seen as risking one’s soul. Mrs. McGill’s fear of Purgatory presents an opportunity, and church authorities plan to exploit her fear to control her fortune. They hope that by preying on her fear, they can influence Mrs. McGill and, in turn, advance Father Sebastian’s rise to bishop.

Mrs. McGill struggles with the truth after Mary Ann tells her the church only cares about her money, not her soul. Mary Ann reveals that religious politicians running the Vatican are hypocrites who created Purgatory as a place to hold souls for ransom. They convince families to buy prayers and masses to release souls, turning it into a profitable scheme. Father Sebastian tells Mrs. McGill he begged the Pope to reconsider Purgatory, and miraculously, the Pope agreed. However, when Mrs. McGill signs away her fortune to the church to escape Purgatory, she slips into eternal damnation.

The story then shifts to history, explaining how the “Roman Catholic” church rose in the 300s A.D., replacing the living Word of Jesus Christ with tradition and idols. To attract pagans, Catholicism introduced the worship of the “Virgin Mary” goddess, despite historical evidence that Mary had multiple children and was not a perpetual virgin. Over time, Mary was elevated to a goddess, proclaimed “Queen of Heaven” by Pope Pius XII.

In contrast, the Savior, Jesus Christ, was turned into an idol—the dead Jesus, baby Jesus, and wafer god in the form of the Eucharist—all false representations. Behind these idols is the devil, deceiving believers. Catholics are told they cannot enter heaven without participating in these rituals involving the wafer god. However, scripture warns against bowing to any graven images or idols.

Mary Ann grows fearful and questions where her trust lies—in the traditions run by corrupt men or in God’s holy scripture. The story highlights that only Jesus, who was sinless, could pay for sins, not Mary or any other figure. Jesus died for the sins of everyone and rose again, offering one eternal sacrifice, unlike the repeated sacrifices of the wafer god in the Mass.

In the end, Judy receives guidance to put her faith in the real Jesus Christ rather than idols. She asks Jesus to be her Savior, and she is saved. Mary Ann feels transformed, filled with the power of God, wanting to share her testimony with everyone. Jesus promises to destroy the sinful Vatican but warns those still caught in the deception to come out and avoid partaking in their sins.

The story closes with an invitation to know Jesus personally, accept His salvation, and be forgiven, contrasting the truth of the living Christ with the false traditions of Catholic idolatry and profit-driven rituals.

Title: Tycoon, The
Subject: Buddhism
Author: Carter
Responses:
At a prestigious ceremony, the Golden Buddha award was presented to Brother Yut Survarnin. This was his third consecutive win, a feat he humbly credited to the lord Buddha and the generosity of others. Survarnin had donated two million dollars to the temple and six million to an orphanage. Furthermore, his company, Survarnin Industries, was awarded the contract to construct six new temples.

Attendees at the event admired Survarnin's dedication and charity, noting that he fed thousands of monks every day. Many believed that his immense wealth was evidence of a saintly past life and predicted he would become the ruler of a nation in his next incarnation.

However, the celebration was interrupted when a man tried to deliver a message about the Lord Jesus Christ. He was promptly scolded, shouted down, and eventually removed by security at the behest of the wealthy tycoon and temple officials. They dismissed the idea of sin and Christianity, favoring their beliefs about reincarnation.

Shortly after, as Survarnin's limousine was leaving, it raced toward a bridge that had been destroyed. He tried desperately to stop but crashed into the chasm when the bridge gave way.

Survarnin found himself in a strange place, met by radiant beings who declared it was his time for judgment. Survarnin was shocked, insisting reincarnation awaited him. The beings explained that death leads to a one-time judgment, citing biblical scripture.

He was taken away by an angel who explained that they would not visit lord Buddha, but someone far more important: the Lord Jesus Christ. Survarnin questioned this, noting that Buddha was born before Jesus. The angel replied that Buddha was born in 563 B.C., while Jesus, the Creator of the Universe, has always existed.

Survarnin stood before Christ for judgment. Jesus reminded him that he had been told about His resurrection and divine authority and warned that no idolater would enter heaven. Yet Survarnin had continued to bow to Buddha.

Jesus reviewed the messages His servants had shared with Survarnin, including the events of when Survarnin was 12 years old and the man who told him the truth about Jesus but was brutally beaten. Survarnin had rejected these messages and even participated in the man's persecution.

Ten years later, Survarnin had changed his life, claiming peace through Jesus, but his family disowned him because he wouldn’t honor Buddha. Despite this, he understood the sacrifice Jesus made, leaving heaven to die on the cross for humanity's sins.

Jesus explained that Survarnin had rejected Him, bowed to an idol, and chose to please others at his own spiritual peril. Those who accepted Jesus lived forever in heaven, while those who rejected Him would spend eternity in the lake of fire.

All who rejected God's love would face eternal punishment, but those trusting Christ would live forever in joy. The story warned that reincarnation is a lie and emphasized that humans only have one life to live before facing judgment.

It clarified that Buddha, the virgin Mary, Allah, Confucius, and other false gods did not die for anyone’s sins; only Jesus shed His blood for salvation. Jesus is the only way to God the Father.

The story concluded by encouraging readers to receive Jesus as their Savior through prayer, admitting their sins, and inviting Him into their hearts. While it was too late for Survarnin, it was not too late for the reader. The final message admonished belief in Jesus as the only hope for salvation, quoting scriptures about judgment and the promise of eternal life through faith in Christ.

Title: Unforgiven?
Subject: Islam
Author: Carter
Responses:
A man named Lamont was warned harshly by other inmates upon his arrival in prison, told to stick to his own kind to survive. When he was threatened by a group of tough-looking prisoners, he quickly aligned himself with them, declaring, "I'm with you, brothers." The group's leader set a single condition: Lamont had to follow his instructions exactly to be protected.

Five years later, Lamont was released from prison, but his family had no idea what had changed inside him. When Lamont’s grandmother called to speak with him, his wife, Lily, refused, telling Lamont she wouldn’t let him talk to the woman because he had changed. Lamont’s grandmother sensed something was wrong and pressed for answers, learning that Lamont now went by the name Muhammad.

Lamont's wife explained that he had converted to Islam while in prison. Concerned, Lamont's grandmother prepared to visit, asking for guidance and strength. When Lamont's grandmother planned to come, his wife and friends, who were Muslim, advised her not to enter the house, citing the Qur'an’s harsh teaching that unbelievers are enemies, and they hoped the visit wouldn’t cause problems.

Despite the tension, the grandmother arrived, embracing Lamont warmly and expressing her deep love for him. She sought to understand what had happened, hearing from Lamont and others about his conversion. Lamont claimed he found truth in prison, while his grandmother said she had eternal life through Jesus, not religion, emphasizing her faith in Jesus’s love.

They debated about religious beliefs. Lamont insisted Islam was his true faith, accusing Christianity of being a "white man’s religion," while his grandmother challenged these ideas, pointing out misconceptions about Jesus and detailed differences between Islam and Christianity. She condemned Muhammad for actions attributed to him, including marrying a child and owning slaves, and stated that Jesus alone saves people.

She taught that Jesus’s crucifixion fulfilled prophecies and that He rose again, unlike Muhammad, whom she said denied Jesus and became an antichrist figure. Their conversation grew intense, as Lamont's grandmother proclaimed Jesus Christ as Lord and warned Lamont to turn to Jesus for forgiveness or face eternal punishment.

Lamont angrily rejected her, declaring his choice for Muhammad and hating Jesus, his Bible, and his grandmother. He shouted for her to get out of his house. His grandmother responded by declaring that Lamont had declared jihad on Jesus with his choice.

Six months later, Lamont died and faced judgment before Jesus Christ. His grandmother’s warning echoed, telling him that his sins were unforgiven. Lamont’s final cries pleaded for mercy, but the story ended with the biblical message of salvation through Jesus Christ.

The story conveyed a strong message about faith, choice, and consequences, framing Christianity as the truth and salvation, contrasting it with Islam as an opposing belief system.

Title: Uninvited
Subject: Homosexuality
Author: Chick
Responses:
One restless night, a man named Bobby found himself wide awake despite taking sleeping pills that were no longer effective. Feeling unsettled by the eerie quiet of the hospital at night, he decided to talk to the night nurse, Old Clara, curious about what she might be reading.

When Bobby asked Clara if she believed in the strange creatures often talked about, she assured him she did, with all her heart. Clara believed firmly in these spiritual entities, which Bobby was skeptical about, calling them baloney. 

Clarifying that she was on duty and had to check on other patients, Clara left, and Bobby returned to the other patients who talked openly about their fears and frustrations. They described Clara as superstitious and crazy, convinced that she was wrong to be so worried, and alarmed that she was even working there.

Despite their harsh judgments, they recognized the need for Clara, especially considering their pain and need for medication. They talked about how difficult their lives were, feeling that Clara didn’t understand their suffering and was an enemy to their reality.

When Clara returned, she greeted them warmly, but the patients accused her of being hateful, misunderstanding her intentions. Clara explained that she loved them all and was there to help, not to harm. 

She asked what had triggered their anger this time and accused them of lacking the Holy Spirit. Clara insisted that they were not children of God because of their lifestyles and said that they were marked by the devil, with their souls at stake immediately after death.

The patients reacted angrily, denying Clara's words and saying she had no right to talk to them this way. Clara responded by sharing her own harrowing story — when she was six years old, she had been raped and nearly killed. She described feeling lost and desperate until she found church, where she heard about Jesus and experienced a powerful spiritual change.

She recounted collapsing in pain and despair, being cared for and prayed over by church members, and asking Jesus for help. Clara testified that Jesus saved her, casting out the evil inside her. She warned that without Jesus, she could have ended up like some of the patients, suffering and dying.

The conversation shifted to the origins of evil. Clara explained that spirits who serve Satan have been deceiving humanity for thousands of years, beginning with the wickedness of mankind at the time of Noah. Because of humanity’s evil, God sent a great flood to wipe out wicked spirits and people, saving only Noah's family and animals.

After the flood, evil spirits continued to influence humanity, leading to cities like Sodom, infamous for sinful behavior and devilish influence. God saved Lot and his family from Sodom by angelic intervention and then destroyed the city with fire and brimstone as a warning.

Clara explained that this ongoing spiritual battle affects all people, with Satan being a powerful enemy controlling nations and influencing people to oppose Jesus. She said the heart's deceitfulness makes it easy for evil spirits to enter and affect unsaved people’s bodies and minds.

Jesus came to Earth to rescue people from Satan's control, seeking to save those who were lost. He was recognized as the Son of God and was executed for humanity’s sins. His resurrection three days later demonstrated his power, and he will return to rule the world.

Clara told the patients that believing in Jesus brings forgiveness, the Holy Spirit, and a new life. Bobby and another man, Fred, accepted Jesus and were saved, but the rest rejected the message and continued in their sins.

Bobby later expressed joy and gratitude for his deliverance, confident he would go to heaven because Jesus had freed him from the evil influences that once controlled his life.

Clara warned that the gay community, which some of the patients belonged to, was fulfilling a prophecy about the end times, with strong political and media influence spreading sinful lifestyles, similar to the city of Sodom. These changes foreshadowed coming tribulations under the antichrist.

Finally, Clara urged the patients to turn to Jesus to avoid hell and the horrors prophesied for the future. She quoted Scripture, promising salvation to those who believe in Jesus Christ, encouraging them to repent and be saved.

One patient, kneeling in prayer, did just that, asking Jesus for forgiveness and to save his soul. The story ends with the hope of redemption through faith, a warning about judgment, and a plea to choose salvation today.

Title: Unloved
Subject: Suicide
Author: Chick
Responses:
Once there was a boy named Jimmy who faced constant harsh criticism from his father. One day, his father asked if he had beaten up a kid, to which Jimmy said no because the kid was bigger. His father called him a sissy and expressed shame that Jimmy had never lost a fight, making Jimmy apologize. As Jimmy’s sister Nancy excelled in school with straight A’s and was praised by their parents, Jimmy was scolded and looked down upon for his poor report card.

Jimmy struggled in many areas — his team lost games, and his father called him disgusting, saying trying wasn’t good enough. Years later, Nancy earned a scholarship to study law and was praised again as wonderful and a source of pride. Meanwhile, Jimmy graduated high school but was berated by his father who said Jimmy would never amount to anything and was a dummy. Years passed and Nancy succeeded in law, winning major cases and earning a six-figure salary, while Jimmy got laid off from his job and was called a loser by his father.

Jimmy married a woman his family disliked, calling her trash and criticizing him for the marriage. He continued to face rejection from his parents who cast him out of their wills and said they hated him. Feeling unwanted, unloved, and disowned, Jimmy contemplated suicide, believing no one cared and that he was a complete failure. Suddenly, a man appeared to talk to him, saying God understands what he’s been through because Jesus lived as a man and experienced human struggles.

The man explained how Jesus came to save sinners — the unlovely, unwanted, and losers — by living a perfect life, healing the sick, raising the dead, and challenging religious leaders who sought to stop Him. Despite being innocent, Jesus was betrayed, arrested, tortured, and crucified, paying a terrible price out of love. On the third day, He rose from the dead and is now in heaven, promising to return.

Struck by this, Jimmy realized he was loved and accepted Jesus as his Savior by trusting Him. He felt a new sense of peace, becoming a new creation and a child of God, on a path to heaven with incredible blessings ahead. God was building a mansion for him, and angels would serve him. Jimmy learned he was a joint heir with Christ, destined to judge angels and join Jesus at a great celebration.

Jesus would return to rule the world, and Jimmy’s life was transformed from loser to winner. Four months later, Jimmy died and heard words welcoming him into eternal joy. If anyone feels unloved or rejected like Jimmy once did, they are reminded that Jesus loves them and offers a way to be with Him forever — now is their time to become a winner by believing in Jesus Christ.

Title: Unwelcome Guest, The
Subject: Masonry
Author: Chick
Responses:
Frank was driving and meeting his friend Larry when Larry asked how Frank managed to buy lumber at 40% off. Frank smiled and said it was his little secret. Larry then wondered if such discounts only applied to lumber, but Frank hinted that the discounts he got were unbelievable.

Larry was eager to get in on the secret, especially since he was Frank's brother-in-law. Frank cautioned that it took a special kind of person to be accepted. Larry asked if he was that kind of person, and Frank seemed unsure.

Frank explained how joining had changed his life dramatically. Before, he was going nowhere, but after being accepted, he had a beautiful home he never thought possible. Larry enthusiastically said he’d do anything to join them, which Frank acknowledged.
