Larry was asked if he believed in God, which he affirmed enthusiastically, saying he even was a deacon at church. Frank said Larry might be able to fit in, mentioning he knew someone who could call to get Larry in. Larry was excited.

The next morning, Larry was told he was accepted in the group, but also instructed to be patient and keep it a secret. Frank stressed the group consisted of good, moral people and urged Larry not to let them down. Larry promised he’d go along like his life depended on it.

That night, Larry took an oath during a ceremony that seemed somewhat sinister.

One year later, Larry’s wife, Lois, revealed to the pastor that their marriage was falling apart because Larry was ignoring her and more interested in the Lodge than church. The pastor confronted Larry, noticing the dark change in him and warning that Larry was trapped, spiritually overcome by an unwelcome guest.

The pastor urged Larry to remember his initiation and warned that he hardened his heart against God when he took that oath. He quoted scripture to stress this. Larry swore his oath but seemed to have been overtaken by the god of Masonry inside him.

The pastor asked Larry if he wanted help, but Larry resisted strongly. However, the pastor warned Larry that he was serving the god of Masonry, not the Lord Jesus, and was in deep trouble with an evil presence gripping him.

The pastor prayed, commanding the spirit of Masonry to depart in Jesus’ name. Larry then confessed his belief that Jesus is God incarnate, and rejected the spirit of Masonry.

Suddenly, a dark figure representing Baphomet, the god of Masonry, manifested and attacked Larry, demanding total worship. Larry called out to Jesus for help, rejecting Masonry and asking Jesus to take control of his life.

The pastor invited Larry to his house to show him something. There, he revealed the image of Baphomet, describing it as the real god behind Masonry, connected to ancient Baal worship. Larry was shocked.

The pastor explained that Masonry is a dark spiritual force blending ungodly religions, controlled by Satan. Photos showed Masonic ritual rooms and notable figures associated with Masonry, including its leadership wearing symbols of Baphomet.

The pastor recited a historical quote from Albert Pike, a high-ranking Mason, who admitted that their Masonic religion was rooted in Luciferian doctrine, equating Lucifer with their god, not Jesus.

The pastor showed a symbol worn by Aleister Crowley, a notorious Satanist, and pointed out a high Masonic leader’s hat showing the Baphomet symbol again.

He went on to say Masonry included powerful global figures—popes, presidents, and kings—who all aim to join the “Big Lodge in the sky.” Many churchgoers are Masons without realizing it, bringing evil spirits into churches.

The pastor warned Larry to go home and remove all Masonic objects to break the curse on his family, asking for God's forgiveness on bringing witchcraft into their home.

A week later, Lois joyfully reported to the pastor that Larry had returned to them and loves them again. They thanked Jesus for saving Larry from following the god of Masonry.

The pastor warned that those who deny Jesus will be condemned at the Great White Throne judgment, quoting scripture about eternal punishment prepared for the devil.

Many Masons are unaware that the "Big Lodge in the sky" is actually a place of torment located in hell.

Thus, Larry’s story serves as a warning about the spiritual dangers of Masonry, urging believers to seek Jesus and avoid the occult path disguised as fraternity.

Title: Virtual Reality?
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Carter
Responses:
A man proudly declared that he had achieved enlightenment and considered himself God, claiming to have all power. He boasted that he could have anything he wanted—gold, girls, glory—and all he had to do was claim it. With his newfound power, he created the sky, hills, and everything around him, convinced that nothing existed outside of his control.

One day, he noticed others in his world and questioned why they were there. They introduced themselves, explaining they were using virtual reality (VR) technology and invited him to try it. They encouraged him to explore VR to learn about where he came from, why he's here, and where he's going. However, he declined, preferring his own reality just the way it was, though they assured him they’d be there if he changed his mind.

Later, feeling bored and restless despite having everything, his reality was interrupted again by the VR group. Frustrated, he demanded they go away, but they persisted, urging him to try the VR goggles. Hesitant but curious, he agreed, and suddenly experienced a dramatic new reality.

Through the VR experience, he found himself marveling at a universe narrated by scripture, witnessing the story of creation where "the Lord God made the earth and the heavens." He learned of humanity’s early attempts to become gods and the resulting loss of paradise. He saw how mankind created their own gods, did wicked things, and became evil, prompting God’s judgment through a great flood. The story continued with Noah, a man building an ark at God’s command, despite others calling him a conspiracy nut.

Despite this judgment, evil persisted through Noah’s descendants, who rebelled by building one world government in Babylon. God confused their language, dividing the people into tribes, yet they continued fighting and taking lands from each other.

The VR guide revealed that the reason for all this was what no man could do: God’s own intervention. He introduced himself to the man as Jesus Christ, who explained how He saw everything and that he had come to earth for a purpose.

The man initially resisted the truth, wanting to keep his own version of reality. But at night, Jesus appeared again, telling him that he couldn’t escape the truth because Jesus penetrates all of reality. Jesus warned that the man had spent his life running and was running out of time.

The next day, the man screamed in shock when he discovered Jesus was in his bedroom, visible even without the goggles. Through Jesus, he learned that Jesus is more real than anything he imagined, being the creator of reality itself. Jesus was recognized even by evil spirits, who had to obey Him.

The man then learned about Jesus’ ultimate sacrifice on the cross where He paid in full for humanity’s sins, fulfilling God’s plan to save the world. Invited to admit his sinfulness and trust Jesus’ sacrifice, the man accepted the forgiveness offered, declaring Jesus as God.

Suddenly, the man awoke from a coma surrounded by doctors and loved ones praising God. He gratefully accepted Jesus’ reality over his own. Though surprised that he had never shared his faith before, he thanked God for a second chance at life—this time, in real life.

The story ends with a call to readers to consider their own beliefs, asking if they admit their sins, believe in Jesus’ sacrifice, and have asked Him into their hearts, encouraging them to remember this life-changing decision.

Title: Visitors, The
Subject: Mormonism
Author: Carter
Responses:
Aunt Fran visited her niece Janice, who was planning to go to Africa as a nurse. Aunt Fran was concerned and told Janice that her mother was crazy to let her go. Despite Aunt Fran's warnings, Janice defended her decision, saying it was her life and that her mother would regret opposing her choice.

Janice then shared that she had met some wonderful people during her mission and wanted Aunt Fran to meet them too. When the missionaries arrived for a baptism commitment night, Aunt Fran was introduced to them. She was curious and somewhat skeptical.

During their discussion, Aunt Fran asked many questions about Mormon beliefs. The missionaries explained their views, including ideas that God the Father was once a man, that polygamy was revealed by apostles, and that God now lived on a planet near the star Kolob with wives and spiritual children.

Aunt Fran was shocked to hear that spirit children who didn’t fight valiantly in the pre-earth life were born with black skin and that the faithful were born with white skin. She found this teaching terrible and contrary to the Bible.

The conversation continued about the Mormon belief that humans could become gods, and Aunt Fran learned about their practices such as secret temple rituals and their founder Joseph Smith’s involvement with occult practices and Freemasonry. She stated that Mormonism was a modern form of Baal worship and that their teachings deviated from true Christianity.

The discussion grew tense when Aunt Fran called the Mormon beliefs false and tried to convince the missionaries to know the real Jesus from the Bible. Feeling challenged and angry, the missionaries decided to leave abruptly. One of them, Bruce, was confused and troubled by what he heard.

After the missionaries left, Aunt Fran expressed her relief that Janice had been able to hear the truth. She urged Janice to make the right decision and accept Jesus’s sacrifice for her sins. Prompted by Aunt Fran’s visit, Janice prayed sincerely, asking Jesus for forgiveness and inviting Him into her life as her personal Savior.

The story ends with both Aunt Fran and Janice rejoicing in their shared faith and newfound peace. If anyone wants to learn more, they are directed to visit a website for further information on Mormonism.

Title: Walking Dead?, The
Subject: Your Soul
Author: Chick
Responses:
Once, a man named Danny found himself in a terrifying nightmare where he was hiding in a cemetery. He noticed strange, creepy creatures lurking around him. They seemed to fade away for a moment, and Danny hoped they were gone. He tried crawling along the graves quietly to avoid being seen and to find a way out through the gate. Just as he reached the last grave, he hoped to escape, but suddenly, a hand burst out of the ground! Danny screamed in horror as the creatures caught him and declared, "Now, you will walk with us! We're familyeee!"

Danny jolted awake from this nightmare. His aunt Emily noticed him having the distressing dream and quickly comforted him. Despite feeling scared, Danny shared that he felt like a lifeless, walking dead person inside.

A discussion followed among Danny, Aunt Emily, and Uncle John. Uncle John bluntly told Danny that spiritually, he was like a dead doorknob heading straight for hell. Aunt Emily explained that perhaps God was trying to warn Danny through his dream — that he must be born again to change his fate, referencing a verse from John 3:7.

Danny was confused and asked Uncle John to explain this "born again" concept so he could understand it better. Uncle John shared that God created Adam with a body, soul, and spirit, making him like a trinity resembling God Himself — the Son (Jesus Christ), the Father, and the Holy Ghost. God warned Adam not to eat from the tree of knowledge of good and evil, but Adam disobeyed and broke the connection with God.

Adam's sin caused his spirit to die, leaving everyone with a live body, a live soul, but a dead spirit — making humanity like spiritual zombies. Danny thought, "At least I have a good heart," but Uncle John informed him that hearts are deceitful and full of evil, as scripture described.

The discussion turned serious as Uncle John warned that Danny’s soul was the most important part of him, and it would live forever after the body dies. A soul, unlike the physical body, is alive and has a form with arms, legs, and the ability to see, think, hear, and speak.

Uncle John then told Danny a true story Jesus told about a rich man who died and went to hell, experiencing unquenchable fire. This illustrated the eternal fate awaiting souls that do not turn to God.

The conversation revealed that all humans are like zombies because their spirits are dead due to Adam’s sin. But Jesus Christ left heaven and made a way for souls to be saved from hell by giving new life to the dead spirit.

Danny wanted to know how to be born again. Uncle John explained that Jesus must be believed in — not by mere words, but by trusting in what He did, even though many rejected and crucified Him. Jesus bore the sins of all humanity, dying a torturous death, yet He rose again three days later, defeating death.

This story amazed Danny, who was encouraged to receive Jesus as his personal Savior by confessing and believing in Him. Uncle John assured Danny that when he did this, a miracle would happen: the dead spirit inside him would come alive, and he would have eternal life.

Danny prayed, asking Jesus to save him, confessing he was a sinner scared of hell but wanting to be saved. Uncle John encouraged him, promising that his name would be written in the book of life and that he would have a mansion in heaven.

The story ended with a reminder that nothing in the world is worth losing one's soul, and Danny was invited to believe in Jesus for his eternal salvation.

Title: Wall, The
Subject: Sports
Author: Chick
Responses:
In the mountains of Eastern Tennessee, JJ Randall's grandpa was a moonshiner known for his skill in outrunning the law. On one of his runs, he told JJ, "Hold on, JJ, I can lose them." Excited, JJ urged, "This is great. Go faster, Grandpa, faster!" His grandpa assured him that soon JJ would have his chance to drive fast cars too, but for now, he needed to check on his grandma.

One day, JJ's grandma talked with him about salvation. She told JJ, "God's hand is on your life, boy. Somehow He's gonna use you." JJ expressed his desire to be more than anything, and his grandma encouraged him to pray and accept Jesus into his heart, reciting a heartfelt prayer for forgiveness and salvation.

JJ aspired to be a race car driver, the best in the world, and promised his grandma he would never be ashamed of Jesus. As a boy, JJ got involved in dirt track racing, quickly becoming a sensation and earning the title of Rookie of the Year.

JJ won four gold cups and earned the nickname 'The Eliminator.' Over in Fresno, California, at just nine years old, Kit Young started racing go-carts, winning every race and determined to take down 'The Eliminator.' Kit became a sprint car champion known as 'The California Kid,' winning all the minor series his first year and moving into the major series by his second year, finishing second in points to 'The Eliminator.' Both men were determined to be the best.

Although JJ was concerned for Kit's soul, Kit seemed unstoppable on the racetrack, with his wife Kim Lee supporting him fully. The two racing stars pushed their limits, both miraculously avoiding fatal crashes time and again. However, during a race at Crescent City Speedway, the Kid lost control at 145 mph and began to skid on his side. The crowd watched in horror as the car burned.

A fellow racer prayed for God to save Kid's life and rushed to help him out of the burning car. Despite his injured leg, he was pulled to safety just before the car exploded. Kid was lucky — only suffering second-degree burns and no broken bones. Doctors said he'd be out of the hospital soon, and friends and fans prayed for his recovery.

Four days later, JJ wanted to talk to Kid about something vitally important that could affect him forever. Kid was skeptical, dismissing talk of death and the afterlife, but JJ was serious. He shared that Jesus declared He is the only way to heaven and warned about hell.

Kid listened as JJ explained that nothing can be done to earn salvation; it is only through Jesus, who came to save us from hell by dying and rising again. Kid was surprised to learn that Jesus is God and that salvation is a free gift.

The conversation caused tension with Kid's wife, who gave him an ultimatum to choose their marriage or Jesus. Kid chose Kim Lee over Jesus. Tragically, on the 14th lap of another race at 178 mph, Kid's car suffered a front tire blowout and slammed into the wall in one of the worst crashes ever. He was killed instantly.

Kid found himself before Jesus, who asked why Kid chose his marriage over salvation. Kid was told his choice led him to hell, the place prepared for the devil and his angels.

The story ends with the message that Jesus Christ is the only way to heaven, and any other way leads to hell. The reader is urged to ask Jesus to be their personal Savior today.

Title: War Games!
Subject: Jehovahs Witness
Author: Chick
Responses:
In a world where peace-loving people have been brainwashed and turned into soldiers—not for a country, but for a belief—Melissa Gordon is one such soldier. After death, one's soul is believed to live on for eternity, either in heaven or hell. Melissa, prepared for spiritual combat, stands ready with her young daughter Emily. Her military headquarters is located in Brooklyn, New York, within the imposing walls of the Watchtower organization, where families are programmed for world conquest.

Melissa's arsenal is the Watchtower magazine, a powerful weapon in this battle of faith. She has been trained intensively, attending five meetings a week to prepare herself for this spiritual war. Melissa is taught to love the Watchtower, defend it, and trust it more than the Bible itself.

One day, Melissa and Emily approach a home where Bonnie and Frank live. Bonnie warns Frank not to open the door because the visitors are Jehovah’s Witnesses. Frank recalls his military days, saying he never ran from combat and won’t start now. When Melissa introduces herself and Emily, Frank engages her, wanting answers. He asks if she has brought her literature, and they agree to sit under a tree while Bonnie brings lemonade.

Frank confesses his understanding of Melissa’s views—they see him and Bonnie as pagans to be saved from the annihilation awaiting at the battle of Armageddon. With heartfelt conviction, he asks which book he can trust to protect his soul—his Bible or the Watchtower. He urges Melissa to choose between these "weapons," wanting the one that will save his life and those around him.

Melissa trusts Jehovah’s Watchtower, believing it gives her new light, but Frank challenges her. He points out that the Watchtower magazine admits it is not inspired by God, unlike the Bible. This admission cracks Melissa’s armor, and a crack begins to form in her faith as she is confronted with the truth.

Despite the Watchtower’s control over Melissa’s life, this crack widens. Frank probes further, asking if Melissa really believes the Watchtower is the way Jesus died. Melissa confirms that Jesus died on a torture stake—on His hands, not the cross as traditionally believed. But when Frank questions where Pilate placed the sign over Jesus, the answer reveals contradictions. As more questions are asked—like how many nails were in Jesus’ hands—Melissa’s confidence falters, confirming that Jesus was crucified with nails in his hands, not just one.

Frank reads from his Bible to show Melissa what Thomas said in John 20:25 and challenges her trust in the Watchtower’s accuracy in guiding her to eternal life. A hesitant Melissa now confronts the possibility that Jehovah and Jesus could be one and the same, despite her previous belief in their difference.

Scriptures from Isaiah are discussed, emphasizing that Jehovah is the one true God. Yet, Philippians declares that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow and every tongue confess that Jesus Christ is Lord. If only God alone should be bowed to, then Jesus must be Jehovah—both the same God.

Frank reminds Melissa that prayer must be directed to Jehovah, but Stephen, when dying, prayed to Jesus at His right hand, indicating Jesus is God too. If Jesus was not God, accepting worship would be blasphemy. Yet, Stephen and Thomas worshipped Jesus, confirming His divinity.

Isaiah’s prophecy is presented, where the prophet says Jehovah is God and there is no other. The apostle Peter testifies that salvation is found only in the name of Jesus. Melissa begins to understand that Jesus is Jehovah.

Matthew 1 is read to Melissa, showing that Jesus’ birth fulfills Isaiah's prophecy—He was called "Immanuel," meaning "God with us." Jesus lived a perfect life, performing works that testified of His divinity, despite others accusing Him of blasphemy for claiming to forgive sins.

Despite evil men beating and crucifying Jesus, John 3:16 assures eternal life to those who believe in Him. Just as promised, Jesus rose from the dead three days later—only God could resurrect His own body. Melissa’s spiritual armor shatters completely.

Frank gives Melissa a Bible, urging her to check everything for herself and find the truth. He prays that God leads her into all truth. Back at home, Melissa prays, admitting her belief that Jesus is Jehovah God. She asks for forgiveness and invites Him into her heart—and He does.

Melissa is saved. Jesus promises that those who come to Him will not be cast out. The final message to the reader strongly affirms that Jesus Christ, who died for sins, is Jehovah God. It prompts the reader to decide if they will believe in Jesus, trust Him and His shed blood to save their soul, and receive Him as their Lord and Savior.

The story ends with an invitation: “Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved.”

Title: War Zone
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
At Westmont High School, frustration reached a boiling point when a teacher declared, "NOBODY gives ME homework!" In a reckless act of defiance, a student named Moose punctured her tires. When confronted, the furious teacher threatened to call the police. However, Moose, confident and intimidating, warned her that it would be her word against theirs—and she would lose.

One new transfer student, scared on her first day, was immediately warned about the school's notorious reputation. She learned that Westmont was a challenging place, filled with scary kids—especially Moose and his followers, whom she called "snakes."

One day, Moose violently pushed a fellow student aside and snatched all the gospel tracts from her. As tensions escalated, chaos seemed to engulf the school.

Later, in Principal Ward's office, the superintendent informed him of an emergency meeting called by angry parents. The principal was under immense pressure to calm the situation. The teacher, overwhelmed and emotionally wrecked, announced her resignation, unable to continue teaching in such a hostile environment.

During the emergency meeting, parents voiced their outrage. One declared Westmont a literal war zone, with rampant drugs, guns, and violence, leading to dropping grades and fearful students and teachers alike. Another parent questioned what was being done to address these dire issues. The principal, desperate, admitted they had tried every state program, but the problems only worsened. When he suggested praying for a miracle, the crowd erupted in boos.

The next morning, Moose was startled when a fellow student said, "I asked the Lord to bring you here this morning." Moose was shocked to hear about this Lord, but was invited to talk outside. The new friend shared how the gospel tracts they had read the previous night deeply affected them, making them scared and thoughtful for the first time.

Showing Moose a tract with a scripture about the fear of the Lord, the student explained the consequences of rejecting God—eternal punishment in hell. Despite Moose's hardened exterior, the message began to resonate.

Moose's new friend, Randy, shared his own struggles. He admitted to being rotten all his life but explained that God still loved them enough to send Jesus Christ to die for their sins. He recited scripture explaining God's love, sacrifice, and the gift of eternal life through believing in Jesus—emphasizing that salvation is a free gift that cannot be earned.

Randy reassured Moose that no matter what sins he had committed, Jesus had already paid for them all on the cross. Moose was surprised to learn that God would still love him despite everything. Encouraged, he asked if he could be saved right now.

Randy led Moose in a prayer, asking Jesus to forgive his sins and come into his heart, saving him. Moose felt like a brand new person afterward, filled with hope and peace.

The following week brought changes at Westmont. Randy happily reported that two of Moose's followers had accepted Christ, and the once hostile "snakes" were changing. Moose even approached the teacher whose tires he'd slashed, apologized as a Christian, and gave her money to replace them.

The teacher was stunned by the transformation and forgiveness she witnessed. She noticed how the school's atmosphere had become peaceful, and many felt the devil had left Westmont. She even found herself reading and loving her Bible.

Principal Ward received a call proclaiming that the school had been transformed: crime and drug use were down, and grades were up. Parents were thrilled, and teachers from around the district wanted to transfer to Westmont. The principal was advised not to fire the teacher who had quit.

Finally, at graduation, Moose proudly held his diploma, proclaiming he had made it. He had not only talked the talk but walked the walk with God, proving he was genuine. A friend gave him a gospel tract, reminding him that someone cared enough to share the most important message he'd ever hear: to ask Jesus Christ to save him right now for eternal life.

Moose's journey was one of transformation—from a troubled student feared by all to a redeemed young man with a new path, proving just how powerful faith and forgiveness could be.

Title: Warning, The
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
One day, a terrible crash occurred at a stop sign when a driver ignored the warning and collided with another vehicle. At the scene of the accident, bystanders including Bobby and his grandpa questioned what caused it. Grandpa explained to Bobby that ignoring warning signs is very dangerous and then offered to tell a story about his father, who nearly lost his life because he didn’t believe in warning signs.

Back home, Grandpa showed Bobby some old photographs and a piece of barbed wire that had saved his father's life by catching on his overalls. Grandpa then began narrating a story from long ago.

Once, some boys from a nearby farm excitedly told Henry about a new swimming hole they had discovered behind the old Simpson place. They invited Henry to come with them, and he agreed enthusiastically. Others asked if they could join, and although there were signs warning "No Trespassing" and "Stay Away," the boys ignored them and ventured in.

While trying to get past a barbed wire fence marked with danger signs, one boy got stuck and teased his friends, who showed no concern. When they reached the swimming hole, they argued about who would jump in first, despite the "No Swimming" warnings. One boy jumped in and started swimming, unaware that the water was filled with snakes.

Another boy also went in but quickly panicked upon seeing the snakes, calling for help. The others were terrified. Tragically, all three boys were eventually lost to the snake-infested waters.

Two weeks later at the funeral, the community mourned their terrible loss. The preacher reminded everyone that the boys had ignored the many warning signs, which led to their deaths. He then connected this story to a much older, timeless warning.

The preacher recounted the story of Adam and Eve, who lived happily in the Garden of Eden until Satan came disguised as a snake and tempted Eve to eat from the forbidden tree despite God’s explicit warning. Eve was deceived and, along with Adam, rebelled against God’s command. This original act of disobedience introduced sin to the world, bringing sickness, war, death, and eternal separation from God.

The preacher explained that ignoring God's warnings has dire consequences and quoted scripture about the fate of sinners and liars. But he also shared the good news: God became man in the person of Jesus Christ, who lived a sinless life and died on the cross to save humanity by paying for humanity’s sins.

Jesus’s death, burial, and resurrection offer eternal life to all who believe in Him. The preacher shared how Tommy’s daddy accepted Jesus as his Lord and Savior, repented of his sins, and was forgiven. Tommy’s daddy became a faithful follower of Jesus, leading a life that reflected his faith.

Moved, Bobby expressed his desire to be saved and live like his grandpa’s daddy. The grandpa taught him how to pray, confessing his sins, asking Jesus to be his Savior and Lord, and receiving the gift of eternal life.

The story ended with a heartfelt call to readers to accept Jesus, warning that sin is like deadly snakes in the heart that must be removed through repentance. Only by trusting Jesus Christ can one be saved and escape eternal separation from God.

This tale, told through the accident, the boys’ reckless adventure, and biblical teachings, underscored the importance of heeding warnings—both earthly and divine—and embraced the hope found in Jesus Christ.

Title: Wassup?
Subject: Hell
Author: Carter
Responses:
The story begins at a construction site where Charlie Conners is teased by his coworkers for always siding with the boss. When asked if he believes in going to hell, Charlie angrily retorts that he does and says he prefers hell to heaven because he wants to be with all of his buddies there. His friends try to convince him otherwise, explaining that hell is a scare tactic used by churches and that the "Old Man Upstairs" — God — wouldn’t actually condemn anyone to hell since He’s dead.

Charlie insists he doesn’t believe in heaven or hell; he thinks humans evolved from monkeys and that when people die, they’re just dead, plain and simple. He refuses to consider religion, pointing out the contradictions in the Bible and dismissing churches as corrupt and focused on money. Charlie mocks the many denominations and Bible translations, stating that no one really understands what the Bible says, so he won’t waste his time on it.

Charlie’s coworkers tell him to get back to work, and he is soon blown off a beam by a sudden gust of wind, falling to the ground in a serious accident. They rush to help him, but Charlie is unresponsive and appears to be dead. Some of his friends are unsure about what to tell his wife. One of them recalls just talking to Charlie shortly before the accident and can’t believe what happened.

Suddenly, Charlie regains consciousness but is trapped in a terrifying place that is not heaven. An angel appears and explains to Charlie that he died in his sins and is now in hell. Charlie is shocked and asks if there’s any way to warn his friends on Earth about this dreadful place, but the angel replies that they would never believe him, even if he returned from the dead, because they do not accept God’s word.

Charlie laments his fate and remembers the warning from his grandmother about being cast into the lake of fire forever. The angel tells him that Jesus will return to Earth and reign for a thousand years, after which there will be a final judgment for all who died in their sins. Charlie expresses his defiance towards sin and God’s judgment, feeling abandoned by the sacrifice Jesus made on the cross.

The angel explains that by receiving Jesus as Savior and believing He died for him, Charlie’s sins could have been washed away. Charlie argues that all religions claim different paths to heaven and that figures like Buddha, Confucius, and Muhammad are just like Jesus. The angel clarifies that Jesus is unique and alive after His resurrection, unlike those men who were simply humans whose bodies remain in their graves.

After a thousand years, Charlie stands before God’s Great White Throne for judgment but refuses to believe. God reminds him of the love shown by Jesus, who came to Earth, suffered, and died for Charlie’s sins. God points out that Charlie was told Jesus was the only way to heaven but rejected that truth and chose to listen to his friends instead.

Charlie’s life flashes back before him, exposing his refusal to accept the salvation offered. God declares that Charlie is without excuse and must now face judgment for ignoring the gift of salvation. Charlie feels deep guilt and recognizes he has wasted his life trying to please his friends who didn’t care.

God pronounces judgment, condemning Charlie to everlasting fire prepared for the devil and his angels. Charlie acknowledges he is guilty and has been a fool. The story then reminds readers that everyone must face this judgment one day.

The final message warns that most people will end up like Charlie because they fear what others think. It urges readers to accept Jesus as Savior because He will never leave or forsake them. The story ends with a biblical invitation to believe in Jesus and receive eternal life.

Title: What A Shame!
Subject: Hell
Author: Chick
Responses:
One night, at 2:12 A.M., a woman wakes her husband to ask the time. Suddenly, the phone rings and she warns him not to answer, fearing it might be bad news about someone dying. Despite the warning, he answers the phone because he believes he must.

On the other end, the caller—his mother—says she has horrible news but will only talk to him about it. She sobs as she explains that the news is about little Cathy, who once was her favorite granddaughter.

The family gathers anxiously to hear what happened. They ask if Cathy is in jail, dead, or has dishonored the family name. The mother responds that Cathy is dangerous.

She explains that Cathy called to say she has "got saved" and will not go to hell like the rest of the family. This revelation shakes the family deeply.

The grandmother recounts the story of their great-grandfather, Oliver Edwards, a preacher who despised evolution and preached hellfire and damnation. He scared everyone with his fiery sermons about how Jesus created the universe and fought evolution until his death. Using scripture, he condemned evolution as Satan’s lie aimed at damnation.

The family’s town chose science over Oliver’s beliefs, fired him, and the family name was shamed and cursed after that. Only when the family denounced him and embraced scientific evolutionism was their name restored.

Now, the same story is repeating with Cathy. She thinks she can save the family from hell just like Oliver tried to. But the family fears she’s "just like him," dangerous and crazy about religion. They reject her and plead with her not to go to hell.

Cathy is told to leave their house and never return, even though she insists it belongs to her per her parents’ will. Despite the cold reception and accusations, she remains determined to share her message.

The grandmother recounts the family history of hatred and fear toward religion, insisting evolution destroyed their family. She says Cathy is repeating the past by claiming salvation and opposing evolution once again.

Although the family mocks and rejects her, Cathy's purpose is to warn them about hell and salvation through Jesus Christ. She mentions that Oliver had a vision as a teenager of devils pulling him to hell, which prompted his preaching.

Cathy asks what hell is really like, and the grandmother describes it as a place of fire, torment, and eternal shame based on Biblical scripture. Despite God’s love, the family dismisses the fear of hell and clings to ideas that they are safe because they are kind and tolerant people.

The family argues about Pastor Edwards’ hatred of evolution, with some calling him a bigot while others say he was right in fearing for the nation’s destruction due to evolution and the removal of Jesus from public schools.

The family’s intolerance to Cathy’s message causes tension, and they threaten to move out. Cathy insists she will stay until they hear what she has to say.

She explains that God gives only one way to be saved from sin and hell, a simple plan that even a child can understand. This plan began when God sent His Son, Jesus, born of a virgin, to save sinners from hell.

Jesus lived a sinless life, warned people about hell, and declared Himself the only way to God. Despite suffering an illegal trial, torture, and crucifixion, Jesus paid the price for humanity’s sins by shedding His blood.

Three days later, Jesus rose from the dead, proving He is God and allowing people to believe and be saved. Some in the family turn to faith, praying to receive Jesus into their hearts, while others mock it as a big bang theory.

During a stormy night, grandma tragically overdoses on her pills and dies. Her soul descends into hell swiftly, accompanied by terrifying cries.

Five minutes later, Cathy’s family wakes her to announce grandma’s death. They ask if she said anything before she died, and Betsy recalls that grandma whispered two words—she said she saw hell.

The family is shocked and lament how grandma missed the chance for eternal life in heaven because she rejected the gospel and salvation through Jesus.

The story ends urging readers to make their choice between Jesus Christ and Satan, encouraging them to believe on Jesus, ask Him to save them, and to seek eternal life rather than eternal damnation.

Title: What About Me?
Subject: Bible Stories
Author: Carter
Responses:
Angie was feeling very lonely as she lay in a hospital bed. She wondered how long she had been there. When a nurse told her it had been three weeks, Angie sadly revealed that she didn’t have any family. She asked if God cared about poor people like her. A man overhearing her lament called himself Father Mike, but then admitted he only visited those who contributed generously to the offering plate. Confused and disheartened, Angie remained alone.

Next, another man leaned in and introduced himself as someone who had been visiting the next room. He apologized for overhearing and invited Angie in. His name was Mike, and he started a conversation by asking what was wrong. Angie shared that she was too poor to afford a priest. Mike explained that God sees beyond wealth, indicating that God cares about everyone.

Mike offered to tell Angie a story to help her understand. He began with the tale of Ruth, a poor woman who lived long ago. Ruth had recently been widowed and had come to live with her widowed mother-in-law, Naomi. They were in a foreign land where people like them faced hardship.

To survive, Ruth had to gather leftover grain in the fields. The fields belonged to the Israelites, who often clashed with the Moabites—the group Ruth belonged to. The Moabites were excluded from citizenship in Israel, making Ruth’s situation even tougher.

But a man named Boaz was different. He told Ruth to work only in his field where she would be safe. Overwhelmed, Ruth asked why he was being so kind to her. Boaz explained he had heard of her loyalty to Naomi.

Naomi had once lived in Israel, but a famine forced her and her family to move to Moab, where tragedy struck. Naomi’s husband Elimelech died there. Although Naomi found solace when her sons married Ruth and another woman, Orpah, misfortune continued. Both Mahlon and Chilion, Naomi’s sons, eventually died, leaving Naomi alone to return to Israel.

Orpah went back to her family, but Ruth chose to stay with Naomi. She made a bold pledge, saying she would go wherever Naomi went and adopt Naomi’s people and God as her own.

Boaz was impressed by Ruth’s decision and blessed her for trusting in God. He also made sure she was provided for during the harvest by allowing her to glean freely and directing his workers to leave extra grain for her.

However, Ruth and Naomi still faced an uncertain future. Ruth advised Naomi that she needed a husband, and since Naomi had to sell her land, Boaz—as a relative—could help.

One night, Naomi told Ruth to visit Boaz while he slept. Ruth approached him, uncovered his feet, and asked him to marry her, asserting that she was a close relative’s wife and requesting he fulfill his family duties. Boaz was taken aback but agreed to do as Ruth asked if the closest relative declined.

The next day, Boaz gathered the village elders and called upon this closest relative. When told Naomi’s land was for sale and that her redeemer should marry Ruth to preserve the land, the man agreed but balked at marrying Ruth. Boaz took the opportunity, agreeing to marry her despite the risks, because Ruth trusted in God.

This story amazed Angie, who thought about how no one had ever been that kind to her. She asked why a man like Boaz would take in a foreigner like Ruth, and Mike explained it was because of what had happened to Boaz’s mother.

Mike then told the story of Rahab, a woman who had been a prostitute living in Jericho. When Israel’s spies came to her town, she protected them, putting her family’s safety above all else. She believed in the God of the Hebrews.

Ten days later, God’s judgment brought down the walls of Jericho, but Rahab’s house was spared because she trusted God. Rahab married Salmon, and they became part of the lineage that led to King David and Jesus Christ, showing that God’s blessings extend beyond heritage.

Mike explained that everyone has sinned and deserves judgment, but God offers forgiveness through Jesus Christ, who died and rose again to save all who believe.

Moved by the story and Mike’s words, Angie decided to place her faith in Jesus. Mike prayed with her, and she felt saved.

Later, Angie remarked to Mike that he sounded like her son, whom she hadn’t seen in years. With a big smile, Mike revealed he was her son, Billy. They embraced, reunited by faith.

Angie was given a simple guide to faith, reminding her to remember the date she committed her heart to Jesus, knowing her life had changed forever.

Title: What's Worse?
Subject: Demons
Author: Chick
Responses:
The story begins with a question: which is worse, a flea or a demon? Fleas are everywhere, biting both dogs and people, making life miserable. They are pesky little creatures with many offspring that spread widely. People fight fleas with sprays, flea collars, and baths because fleas are physical beings.

However, demons are quite different from fleas. While fleas are visible and can be killed, demons are evil spirits, invisible and smart, and cannot be killed since they are like ghosts. These demons are as numerous and invasive as fleas but are far more dangerous because they seek something precious: the human soul. Their leader, known by many names such as Satan, the Devil, Lucifer, or the Prince of Darkness, desires to possess human souls.

The demons hate humans because their boss fears them, and he wants to take control of their souls. Although demons scare people, they won't easily reveal how Satan plans to take souls.

The story then traces the origin of these demons to a time long ago when one of God's most beautiful creatures in heaven, a high-ranking angel called Lucifer, had a rebellious idea. Despite being an honored cherub who could appear as a shining angel, Lucifer grew prideful, thinking he was better than God. Claiming he was worth more, he called for support to take over heaven. His angel friends joined him and declared war on God.

God and Jesus Christ fought back, expelling Lucifer and his followers from heaven. After being cast out, Lucifer became Satan, and his angel companions became demons. They turned ugly and evil after their fall.

As a consequence of Lucifer's rebellion, God created hell — a place of eternal fire prepared for Satan and his angels, a dreadful and everlasting punishment.

God then created Adam and Eve, breathing life and soul into them in a beautiful garden. They were intended to be God's friends and rulers of the world. But Satan, angry and wanting to be king, tempted Adam and Eve to disobey God, causing them to sin and breaking their friendship with Him. As a result, Satan took over as the ruler of the world.

Humans inherited this sinfulness from Adam; their hearts became filled with lies, evil thoughts, murder, adultery, and many kinds of wrongdoing. This sinful nature blocks the way to heaven, as no sin is allowed there.

Scientists and intellectuals today often deny the existence of demons. They dismiss the idea as superstition, unaware that their hearts are also sinful and that they, too, are at risk.

However, something extraordinary happened 2,000 years ago. The very one who cast out the demons from heaven came to the earth as a man to restore the broken relationship between God and humans. This man was Jesus Christ.

Jesus was born into the world, yet the world did not recognize Him. He came with the purpose of saving people from Satan's grip, giving them new hearts. The demons were terrified when Jesus arrived, as they knew who He truly was.

Ancient prophecies predicted Jesus’ coming, and He fulfilled them by healing the sick, raising the dead, and proving He was God. Despite this, many hated Jesus, especially religious leaders, because He claimed to be God. They eventually tortured and crucified Him.

Jesus bore everyone's sins on the cross, paying the price to save humanity. Three days after His death, He rose from the dead, defeating the Devil and his demons in their fight for human souls.

If someone believes in Jesus and invites Him into their heart, their soul is saved. God’s Holy Spirit cleanses and directs them, and upon death, they will soar into heaven.

But if a person rejects Jesus, their fate is terrible. Their soul is lost forever, falling into hell where there is eternal punishment.

Satan’s strategy is to lie about everything, convincing people God doesn’t exist and that they evolved from nothing. He even makes religion confusing by leading religions astray with false spirit guides.

Where Jesus is banned, Satan’s influence grows. But when a person welcomes Jesus, Satan must leave in defeat.

Ultimately, the question remains: Which is worse, a flea or a demon? The answer is a demon, because it threatens something far more valuable than the body— it seeks your soul. The story ends with an invitation to choose where you want your soul to be—heaven or hell—and to accept Jesus as your savior to ensure eternal life.

This is the tale of the battle between good and evil, flea and demon, sin and salvation, death and eternal life.

Title: What's Wrong With This?
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
In a conversation between two museum visitors, one man expresses disgust upon seeing a statue, saying, "That's disgusting!" When asked why, he explains that he believes the person depicted is worshipping a mere thing, calling it blasphemy. The woman argues that it's the individual's god and that he prays to it. The man insists that it is foolish because the statue, made by human hands, cannot see or hear—it's a dumb idol. The woman questions his sanity, but he stands firm, saying no civilized person worships such things.

The man then asks if she knows when this practice began. She admits she does not, and he explains that long before the biblical flood in Noah's time, people turned away from the true God and began bowing down to little statues, idols, and false gods, abandoning their Creator. Only Noah and his family remained faithful, and God saved them, washing away the idols but not the sin in people's hearts.

After the flood, the population grew, and people built the city of Babylon. Its queen, Semiramis, was wicked and longed to be a goddess, forming a religion centered on her and her son Nimrod. When Nimrod died, she claimed a miracle: Nimrod was reborn as the sun god, making her a goddess. These idols spread, becoming part of various cultures, with people talking to their statues and asking for help.

The woman suspects God didn't like Semiramis's claims, and the man confirms this, explaining that the religion changed over time to fit different cultures. People became trapped by their beliefs in religious leaders, though the woman calls this stupid.

Darkness spread everywhere until God intervened, giving Moses the Ten Commandments to end this madness. The second commandment specifically condemned the worship of graven images. The pair review the scripture, which forbids making or bowing down to images or statues, including paintings that can be worshipped.

Jesus Christ, the man explains, left heaven to stop this deception and paid a terrible price for it. He sacrificed Himself for humanity’s sins, shedding His blood to wash them away. He rose from the dead as the King of Glory and returned to heaven to prepare a place for all who believe in Him as Lord and Savior.

The woman asks if it's really that simple to get to heaven, and the man says yes, noting that there is no other way except through Jesus. Jesus is the only mediator between God and man, like a defense attorney protecting from judgment.

When people sin and ask forgiveness, Jesus forgives and washes their sins away. The man explains that God’s plan is simple, but religious systems distort it, insisting on good works and controlling people with impossible rules. Religion places many mediators—idols, statues, paintings, ceremonies—in front of true faith, and shows no mercy, binding followers with rituals hoping to earn salvation.

Some religious practices involve chanting, prayer beads, or ancestor worship, all aimed at distracting people so they miss God’s precious gift of eternal life through Jesus Christ. The woman admits to having made a terrible mistake by trusting such things.

The man assures her that Bible Christianity is not religion but a living relationship with Jesus Christ. She suddenly realizes she is as much in trouble with God as the idol worshipper was.

She prays earnestly, asking Jesus to save her and forgive her sins, trusting He died on the cross for her. It’s as simple as that—faith in Jesus Christ is all that is needed to be saved and go to heaven.

The story concludes with a reminder that salvation is a gift from God through faith, not by works, quoting Ephesians 2:8-9.

Title: Where Did They Go?
Subject: Rapture
Author: Chick
Responses:
A man lay on his deathbed, a doctor solemnly announced, "He's gone!" while a woman nearby sobbed deeply. In the shadows, a devilish figure gloated, proclaiming his work was done after making the man's life miserable for 40 years. When asked how he accomplished such torment, the devil explained he turned the man's family against him, split up his church, and subjected him to so much stress that he developed cancer. Confidently, he declared that the old pastor was no longer his problem.

However, his master instructed him to attend the funeral with the body, disregarding the devil's complaints about acting as a "baby sitter." At the viewing, the congregation mourned the pastor, saying their final goodbyes and speaking fondly of him. Suddenly, an unexpected visitor entered the room.

The two devils conversed, with one asking if he had to be there. The other ordered him to be useful and distract the congregation by putting them to sleep and disrupting the pastor's sermon. They must prevent the message from being heard.

The pastor's sermon began with the Word of God stating that everyone dies once before facing judgment, a scripture that offended some listeners who preferred to block it out. The pastor preached that mankind is lost in sin and Jesus died in their place, a concept some dismissed, likening Jesus to the late pastor and suggesting he be ignored.

Suddenly, one woman noticed a beautiful blonde from the church had arrived, causing panic among the devils. The preacher spoke of Jesus shedding his precious blood to wash away sins, dying and being buried, but rising again three days later—a promise of "blessed hope." Those left behind would endure terrible judgments on earth. He urged readiness, warning it could happen at any moment.

Despite the message, many in the congregation fell asleep. Meanwhile, the devils worried over the second coming of Jesus, fearing being caught off guard. They kept a close watch on Pastor Weber's grave, suspicious something significant was about to happen.

One devil expressed frustration, worried he might be stuck watching the grave for centuries, while the other dismissed the idea, noting how few people believed such things anymore. They agreed to stay alert and report anything unusual.

The devil then planned to visit Pastor Weber's church, now likely closed. Upon finding a notice for a prophecy conference on the "End Times," he was intrigued and decided to bring his master.

The conference revealed biblical prophecies about World War III, where Russia, Iran, and others would attack Israel, leading to its destruction in a swift war. The speaker noted no mention of the United States in scripture, but many speculated about its fate.

He condemned the rejection of God's Ten Commandments and Jesus' name as offensive, calling out new laws as attempts to erase the gospel. The U.N.'s actions against Israel were described as turning the nation into an enemy of God, with curses prophesied upon those who forsake Israel.

The preacher quoted Matthew 24:21, describing great tribulation and billions of souls descending into hell, while Satan gains control until Jesus returns at the battle of Armageddon. Despite this grim outlook, hope remained: Jesus would come for believers, taking them away before God's judgment.

The devils rejoiced at this news, eager to seize those left behind and drag them to hell. Three weeks later, the archangel's voice echoed, announcing Jesus' return. Suddenly, members of the congregation vanished into the air, leaving others fearful of being left behind.

The comic ends with an urgent message: trust and ask Jesus to save you, believing that Jesus Christ saves, and that all believers will be caught up to meet Him in the air. The final scene shows the devil warning readers against following this advice, enticing them instead to spend eternity with him.

Title: Where's My Letter?
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Carter
Responses:
Ned's cancer had reached stage 4, and the doctors told his family that all they could do was admit him to the hospital to make him comfortable. However, Nate, Ned’s son, insisted that he could take care of his father at home. The hospital staff then arranged hospice care for Ned.

Later, Nate expressed to his mother how much he appreciated her sitting with Grandpa, as it helped him a lot. When Nate asked his mother about Grandpa, she said that Grandpa had mostly been sleeping.

One day, Ned suddenly exclaimed in frustration, demanding his letter. His wife, confused, asked him what letter he meant, but he was determined to find it. He kept asking about his letter, becoming increasingly agitated.

Nate’s mother reminded Ned that he was retired and no longer delivered mail, but Ned insisted that he needed the letter. Soon after, Linda, a nurse, greeted the family and asked how her patient was doing.

The family discussed Ned’s strange behavior, with Nate’s mother mentioning that maybe it was the medications causing it. Nurse Linda pointed out that Ned might be talking to someone, but no one else was there. Nate’s mother found the idea of taking notes interesting, hoping to understand Ned's "language."

Together, they searched through Ned’s mail, checking every letter to find the important one he was looking for. They ruled out typical retirement awards or bonuses, but nothing seemed to be the letter Ned desperately needed.

Linda apologized to Nate’s mother, saying that it must be some other kind of letter Ned was searching for. But they were puzzled when Ned mentioned that an angel told him that Nate had the letter.

Nate and Linda couldn’t see the angel Ned described. Nate asked if his mother could see the angel, but she said Ned had never been religious.

Suddenly, Ned said he remembered something else and said the angel told him he only had three days left to live.

Seeking answers, Nate consulted Pastor Dwight and asked if Ned expected a letter from him. The pastor said yes, he was the only Christian in the family. Nate realized he might have something Ned needed to hear.

The next morning, Nate prayed earnestly for the opportunity to talk with Grandpa. When Nate approached Ned, Ned was awake and ready to listen.

Nate explained to Grandpa that the "love letter" from the Creator was really the Bible. He described heaven as a wonderful place filled with people from every generation who all had something in common.

Nate shared that everyone in heaven was completely forgiven by God and spotless without any evil inside them. He quoted the Bible, saying that God had gone ahead to prepare a place for them, and that to be there, they had to believe in God.

When Grandpa asked who that was, Nate explained about Jesus, God's Son, who came to earth, lived a perfect life, and became the perfect sacrifice for humanity's sins.

Nate elaborated that this sacrifice was to pay the penalty for sin, which is death according to God's law. If someone broke that law, they had to pay the price.

He further explained that on judgment day, those not forgiven can’t enter God's presence and will be separated forever.

Grandpa asked if that’s why he couldn’t go with the angel. Nate clarified that the key was to believe Jesus paid for their sins and to accept His forgiveness as a gift.

Nate told his grandfather about Jesus dying on the cross, not for Himself, but for those who accept this free gift.

He also explained that although Jesus was buried in a tomb, He rose three days later in a new body and then ascended back to heaven after instructing His disciples.

Nate assured Grandpa that the first step to be ready was admitting he was a sinner, and then believing Jesus died to pay for those sins and asking Him for forgiveness.

Grandpa prayed with Nate, confessing his sins and asking Jesus to forgive him. Nate told him now his name was written in the book of life.

On the third day, the family noticed Grandpa waking up from his sleep. Ned joyfully told his son he had his letter and asked if Nate had his own.

Ned began telling his father what had just happened. Nate shared scripture verses about being saved by believing in the Lord Jesus Christ.

The story ends with a form asking if the person admits they are a sinner, believes Jesus died for their sins, and has asked forgiveness—highlighting the choice and step toward faith.

Title: Where's Rabbi Waxman?
Subject: Israel
Author: Chick
Responses:
Here is the story based on the comic strip:

Rabbi Waxman was sick and needed to be in bed, but Nathan was very upset. Nathan’s friend David said that the Messiah had already come, and they must trust Him for their salvation. Nathan struggled with this because, as a Jew, he believed that the Messiah had not yet come.

Rabbi Waxman tried to reassure Nathan, reminding him that Nathan was one of the Chosen people. However, Nathan replied that David said even the Chosen must believe in the Messiah. The Rabbi explained that their people were still waiting for the Messiah and that he had not come yet, but Nathan questioned whether that was really true.

Nathan shared that David showed him many Scriptures that indicated the Messiah had already come. Rabbi Waxman called it crazy talk and asked to see the paper. When the Rabbi looked at the Scriptures, he was shocked and realized he had seen them before. He worried that accepting these Scriptures would cause the people to disown him.

Nathan apologized as the Rabbi, Samuel Waxman, began coughing badly. The Rabbi told Nathan it was time for him to leave and insisted that Samuel go to bed immediately. At home, Samuel’s child said she didn’t like her father’s color, and his wife told the child to make chicken soup while she called Dr. Levi.

Dr. Levi examined Samuel and found fluid on his lungs. He ordered someone to call 911 because the situation was very serious. An ambulance rushed Rabbi Waxman to the hospital, where doctors urgently worked to save him. Despite their efforts, they still had a flat line on the monitor and lost him.

The community mourned Samuel Waxman and said the Kaddish, the prayer for the dead. Many felt that if anyone deserved heaven, Rabbi Waxman did.

In the afterlife, Samuel faced judgment. The record showed that his name was not in the Book of Life and that he died in his sins. He protested, reminding God that he was one of the Chosen and asked about his good deeds. God replied that all their righteousnesses were like filthy rags and that Samuel was without excuse because he was deceived.

Jesus Christ appeared and said that Nathan was sent to show Samuel Scriptures that spoke about Him. Samuel had rejected them. Jesus invited Samuel to look again at the prophecies describing the Messiah, including His birth, life, suffering, death, resurrection, and glory. Jesus was the only one who could fulfill all these prophecies.

Samuel asked if there was any hope for him, but Jesus said it was too late because anyone not found in the Book of Life is cast into the lake of fire. Jesus reminded Samuel that He is the only way to heaven.

The story then explained that the Messiah came to earth, shed His blood to take away the sin of the world, arose from the dead, and was seen by over 500 witnesses.

Meanwhile, Nathan accepted Jesus as the promised Messiah, believing that He died for his sins and asking Jesus to be his Savior.

Forty years later, Nathan died and found his name in the Book of Life. He was welcomed as a good and faithful servant into the joy of the Lord. The story concluded by explaining that Jesus was not just a Jewish carpenter but the Creator of the Universe, who fulfilled Jewish law perfectly and is the Savior of all mankind. He wants to save everyone who puts their faith in Him right now.

Title: Where's Your Name?
Subject: Hell
Author: Chick
Responses:
The story begins with the arrival of millions of angels in hell, pulling out the damned souls from their hiding places. The damned refer to all those who died in their sins, with their bodies long turned to dust. Although their bodies are gone, their souls remain alive and continue to suffer. The Bible describes hell as a place where these lost souls instantly enter upon death and where eternal burning, pain, and emotion persist.

Before hell was created, a lot happened in heaven. Among the angels created by God, one was named Lucifer, who was the most beautiful and wisest of them all. Lucifer held the highest position of power and honor in heaven and protected God's throne. However, Lucifer became prideful and turned against God, thinking he was equal and should rule heaven. He deceived a third of the angels to rebel alongside him. God, the Son (the most powerful being in the universe who created all things including Lucifer), threw Lucifer and the rebellious angels out of heaven. These fallen angels became known as devils, and Lucifer became Satan, the most deadly enemy.

The story then shifts to humanity's involvement. God created the first man, Adam, breathing life into him. Adam was made to live forever and was warned not to eat from a certain tree in the Garden of Eden. God gave Adam a wife, Eve, and everything initially was perfect. However, Satan deceived Adam and Eve into sinning, which caused mankind’s ruin. Following this, people were born spiritually dead and separated from God.

Cain, Adam and Eve’s firstborn son, was the first known person to die and have his soul cast into hell after he murdered his brother Abel. However, only God knows the exact details because He sees everything.

God saw how wicked the people on earth had become and decided to destroy all mankind with a great flood. Only Noah and his family were righteous and saved in an ark. Despite surviving the flood, humanity quickly forgot God and returned to sinning, building cities and nations, continuing their rebellion.

In response, God, in His love, made a way for sinners to be saved from hell and join Him in heaven. He sent His only begotten Son, Jesus Christ, to be born as a baby, to live, and to die as a sacrifice for humanity’s sins. Jesus loved humanity so much that He shed His blood to pay for their sins. However, many rejected Him despite His warnings that He is the only way to God.

Jesus died a brutal death, but three days later, He rose from the dead. Before ascending to heaven, He promised to return with His angels to judge the world and defeat evil.

God offers forgiveness and eternal life for free. Those who believe in Jesus and accept Him as their Savior are spiritually reborn and saved from hell. Their sins are washed away, and their names are written in the book of life. Once saved, their bodies become temples of God, who promises never to forsake them.

In the near future, Jesus will return at the battle of Armageddon, defeat the armies attacking Jerusalem, and reign as the supreme ruler for a thousand years. He will judge all souls, removing the damned from hell during the Great White Throne judgment. Those whose names do not appear in the book of life will be cast into the lake of fire, a place of eternal punishment prepared for the devil and his angels.

The story warns that rejecting God's love and Jesus' sacrifice leads to eternal damnation. However, by believing in Jesus and accepting Him, people can avoid this fate and gain everlasting life. The story ends by encouraging readers to make a personal decision to accept Jesus as their Savior and assures them of God's blessing.

Title: Who Cares?
Subject: Islam
Author: Chick
Responses:
On a day marked by chaos and shock, Omar and his mother watched a live broadcast showing the Twin Towers. Suddenly, one tower was hit by a plane, and then a second plane struck the other tower. Omar's mother anxiously called out, urging Omar to see the devastating scene. She asked, "Omar, who would do this?" and with a heavy heart, Omar explained, "Terrorists, mama..." His mother worried further, questioning what would happen if the terrorists were Muslims and who would protect them. Omar reassured her as they both watched the second tower collapse, recognizing that life would never be the same.

In the days following, the military heightened their alert as it became clear that Muslim extremists were responsible for the attack. The community around Omar grew furious, demanding revenge. Omar’s mother pleaded with him not to go to work, fearing for his safety, but Omar insisted he had to work because their family was out of money. Despite her pleas, Omar promised to stay home for now while every news report worsened the mood.

At Omar’s workplace, he was met with hostility. A child pointed him out to his mother, who declared that she would never shop at Omar's store again. Customers scolded Omar, blaming him and his people for the tragedy. One man shouted that his cousin had died in the towers because of people like Omar. Fear and anger fueled threats and insults against Omar, who tried to plead for mercy. Realizing he needed supplies, Omar sought out a nearby shop in hopes of buying batteries, but the rising tension in the neighborhood was tense.

Suddenly, Omar was attacked by a group of men, but a bystander intervened, helping him up and urging him to get to emergency care. Though Omar protested that he had no money, the man assured him he would pay for the care. At the medical center, a doctor noted that Omar’s bleeding had stopped, thanking the man who brought him in. Omar was shocked when the man revealed he was a Christian. Omar asked why he’d helped him since he wasn't Muslim.

The man simply said, "Because I'm a Christian and you needed help," explaining that Jesus teaches to love your enemies. Omar confessed that he wouldn't have helped the man if their roles were reversed, labeling him an infidel. The man replied, "I'm doing this because of something Jesus taught me." He then told Omar about a parable Jesus shared—the story of a certain man who was beaten and robbed, left to die by the side of the road.

The man explained that a priest and a Levite, both religious men, passed by without offering help, but a hated Samaritan stopped to aid the wounded man, showing him kindness despite their differences. This Samaritan cared for the man, bandaging his wounds and paying for his care at an inn.

Omar listened as the man asked who the true neighbor was in the story. Omar answered that it was the one who showed mercy. The man encouraged Omar to go and do likewise, telling him he had a message from the prophet Jesus.

Omar was skeptical, calling the man an infidel and doubting how he could have a message from the prophet Jesus. The man explained that Jesus is more than just a prophet and invited Omar to hear what Jesus said about Himself. Omar agreed to listen.

Jesus had told a blind man that he had seen Him, and that He was the one speaking to him. The man believed and worshiped Jesus as the Son of God. The Christian man shared that Jesus loved the world and gave His only Son so that whoever believes in Him would have everlasting life. He explained that Jesus died, was buried, and rose again three days later. 

Omar was stunned, admitting he'd never heard that Allah loved him. The man assured him that God indeed loves him and sent His Son to die for his sins.

The Christian shared that while Mohammed died and rose not from the dead, Jesus rose, proving He is God. He explained that Mohammed died in sin because he denied Jesus is God, but Jesus conquered death for all who believe.

God promised that if Omar confesses Jesus as Lord and believes, he would be saved, forgiven, and have eternal life with Christ. The man warned that Mohammed and Allah offer nothing but empty dreams, whereas Jesus offers true forgiveness and will come again to reign.

Omar realized that Allah did not truly love him or care for him, but Jesus, God’s Son, did. He understood he must choose Jesus as his Lord and Savior. The Christian man encouraged Omar to pray and ask Jesus to be his Lord.

Omar prayed, accepting Jesus’ message, and was saved through faith in Him. The story ends with Omar finding peace and new life through choosing Jesus.

Title: Who is Allah?
Subject: Islam
Author: Carter
Responses:
A father and son observed a group of people praying at a mosque. The son asked what they were doing, and the father explained that they were praying to their moon god. Curious and confused, the son questioned the concept of a moon god. The father accused him of being an infidel for questioning and warned that the holy Qur'an commands punishment for such words.

The father expressed fear and anger, saying only a fool would speak against his religion and that people should be trembling because Islam is the second largest and fastest-growing religion in America, threatening Christianity. He proclaimed that soon a Muslim flag would fly over the White House, signaling the end of Christianity in America, and that Britain was already being brought to its knees by Islam.

Then, a man spoke to the father, acknowledging he was a Christian and telling him that Islam's teachings distorted the Bible. He argued that Jesus was indeed crucified and is the Son of God, as the Bible states, despite Islamic teachings to the contrary. The man explained that before Islam, Arabs worshipped the moon god Allah among many idols, and Muhammad created his religion by declaring himself Allah's prophet.

He recounted how an archaeological discovery in Palestine uncovered idols of the moon god, affirming Allah as a pre-Islamic pagan deity. He presented a photo of the idol, Allah, seated on a throne with a crescent moon on his chest — a symbol seen extensively in Islam. According to the man, Muhammad used this pagan god to gain power.

The man then explained that there is a true God who loves everyone, including Muslims, and that God sent His Son, Jesus Christ, to save humanity. He emphasized that Jesus is the only begotten Son of God, who created the universe, and that everyone is alive because of Him, though many don't know Him. The Bible's words were cited to show Jesus made all things and that He would judge all people.

When the father expressed despair over his situation, the man assured him of God's mercy, explaining Jesus' sacrifice on the cross, which washed away sins and opened the gates to heaven. The man spoke of Jesus' resurrection and promise to return. He invited the father to accept Jesus as his Savior, repent, and be saved.

Moved by these words, the father admitted he was deceived, accepted Jesus into his heart, and felt changed and free, now embraced by God's love. The man assured him of Jesus' eternal presence and support, welcoming him as a brother in faith.

Despite the father's new faith, he resolved to tell his people about the moon god and the true Christ who saves, aware his decision might cost his life but trusting it would be worth it for eternal life with God.

The story ends by referring readers to further resources for learning about the differences between Islam and Christianity.

Title: Who is He?
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
The story begins with a group of people questioning who Jesus really is. Some say He is Jesus, while others claim He was a revolutionary black man or a Muslim. Some even say Jesus was the Christmas baby or Buddha’s cousin, while others disagree or are confused, making the group debate who Jesus truly was. They discuss misconceptions like whether He was cut off at a party or if He ever lived at all. This confusion drives everyone nuts, wondering who Jesus really is.

It is then revealed that Jesus is the most important person anyone will ever meet, and what one does with Him determines whether they will go to heaven or hell. The story illustrates the miracles Jesus performed that proved His divine nature, such as giving sight to the blind, healing lepers, casting out devils, and even raising Lazarus from the dead after four days. These acts demonstrate that only God could perform such wonders.

Jesus is shown fulfilling numerous Old Testament prophecies which further confirm His identity as the Son of God, the one who has always reigned in heaven and created everything in the universe. Jesus humbled Himself by being born in a humble stable, despite His divine glory and the splendor He left behind in heaven.

The reason for needing a Savior is explained: everyone sins and thus deserves eternal judgment. Jesus, knowing this, chose to go through immense suffering willingly, being arrested unjustly, tried, and sentenced to crucifixion—the cruelest form of torture. His death paid the penalty for humanity’s sins. Despite brutal suffering, Jesus survived and ultimately died as a sacrifice for all people’s guilt and shame.

After three days, Jesus rose from the dead, appearing to over 500 witnesses, commanding His followers to spread the gospel so that all may have the chance to be saved. Those who love and believe in Jesus are promised eternal life and a place in heaven.

The story concludes by affirming Jesus’ true identity—as the King of kings, Lord of lords, and the Savior of all. It warns that Jesus will come again soon to judge all people. Everyone must decide whether to accept or reject Him, for judgment is inevitable. Heaven or hell is the ultimate choice, and salvation comes through confessing faith in Jesus Christ, who alone offers eternal life.

Title: Who Loves You?
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Carter
Responses:
This story begins with the question: who gave you life? The Bible answers that Jesus made all things, including you. According to John 1:3, without Him, nothing was made that exists.

Then, it asks who created the world for you to live on. The Bible says Jesus created everything—visible and invisible, earthly and heavenly things, powers, and dominions—as stated in Colossians 1:16.

Next, we learn that Jesus knows everything you've said or thought in your heart. Psalms 139:4 tells us that nothing we say is hidden from Him.

The story continues by revealing that Jesus understands how lonely and scared you may be. Hebrews 4:13 explains that nothing is hidden from His sight; everything is open and exposed to Him.

Further, Jesus knows all about your sins—murder, cheating, unbelief, stealing, and more. Matthew 9:4 emphasizes that He knows even the evil thoughts in your heart.

Jesus wants you to be next to Him in Heaven. 1 Thessalonians 4:16-17 describes how He will return with a shout and the dead in Christ will rise to meet Him.

He also desires to keep you from going to Hell. 2 Peter 3:9 says the Lord is not willing that anyone should perish but that all should come to repentance—meaning being truly sorry for sin and turning away from it.

The story reveals that Jesus loved you so much He left His throne in Heaven, as John 3:16 states. He gave His only Son so that believers won't perish but have eternal life.

Jesus loved you so much that He shed His precious blood to wash away your sins and died for you. Colossians 1:14 teaches that redemption comes through His blood.

Not stopping there, Jesus rose from the dead and ascended back to Heaven, as recorded in Acts 1:9.

He loves you enough to build you a magnificent mansion in Heaven to live in. John 14:2-3 assures believers of this promise.

Jesus wants you to tell Him how very sorry you are for your sins and to turn away from them. Luke 5:32 explains His mission to call sinners to repentance.

He also desires to come into your heart if you ask Him. Romans 10:9 promises salvation if you confess and believe in your heart.

If you accept Jesus, then He loves you so much that He wants to share His riches, power, and glory with you. 1 John 3:2 speaks of believers as children of God who will be like Him when He appears.

Jesus would put angels by your side to protect you. Hebrews 1:14 describes angels as ministering spirits sent to help those who will inherit salvation.

He wants you to be with Him when He returns to Earth as King of Kings and Lord of Lords. Revelation 19:11, 14, 16 offers a vision of His return dressed in righteousness, followed by armies of believers.

Jesus loves you so much that He wants you to rule with Him throughout eternity. Revelation 5:10 speaks of believers reigning as kings and priests with God.

This is a beautiful love story. Who else could ever love you like that? Only God Almighty!

And that is who Jesus really is—the Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end, the Almighty, who is, was, and is to come, as described in Revelation 1:8.

This story reveals the profound love God has for you through Jesus Christ, offering redemption, protection, eternal life, and reigning glory with Him forever.

Title: Who Murdered Clarice?
Subject: Abortion
Author: Chick
Responses:
On a cold, foggy Friday morning at 6:30 AM, two people entered a side door. The crime they were about to commit was carefully planned, and the killers were waiting. A butcher carried out a gruesome deed, as murder was his business. Poor Clarice met a terrible death and was dismembered, with all evidence disappearing. There was no funeral or gravesite; Clarice, beautiful and innocent, was simply gone.

The crime was shrugged off and forgotten because no one cared. Unknown to those involved, someone was watching—eyes like flames that alone could hear Clarice’s silent screams. Those responsible would one day stand before Him, charged with Murder One. Clarice’s brutal death would be avenged, for as the Bible says, “Vengeance is mine: I will repay, saith the Lord.” Years later, Oswald Gilmore, M.D., ended his bloody career, dying a very wealthy man. It was now time to review the murder of little Clarice.

When questioned, Gilmore asked what the big deal was over one “lousy abortion." But he was charged with murder, along with other conspirators in this crime. Suddenly, the judge was revealed as the Lord Jesus Christ Himself, who would judge every soul on the planet.
