He created the universe, knows every thought, and has witnessed everything done during our lifetime. Nothing escapes Him.

Before Jesus came to earth as a man, He was the One who gave the Ten Commandments to Moses on Mt. Sinai. Jesus was the Great Lawgiver. He can be our most loving friend or our most frightening enemy. The Bible warns, “Fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him (Jesus) who is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.”

Dr. Gilmore pleaded his case, claiming he performed the abortion at the mother's request and that it was perfectly legal, thus working within the law. But the Bible condemns murderers and those involved in such deeds to the lake of fire and brimstone. Gilmore was accused of selling baby ears for profit and was damned to hell.

All involved—the parents, relatives, doctors, nurses, senators, congressmen, lobbyists, and even Supreme Court justices and presidents—were called to give an account. The Lord said He heard every excuse and rejected all excuses, stating, “All nations before him are as nothing...vain.”

God had told the prophet Jeremiah, “Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee...I sanctified thee...I ordained thee to be a prophet unto the nations.” Jesus loved the little children because He created them as real, living persons, not just “little globs of tissue.” But Satan hates children and uses various techniques to destroy them.

In Egypt, Pharaoh ordered all Jewish baby boys to be drowned in the river. Throughout history, Satan murdered babies, sacrificing them to false gods like Molech and Kali. Of all babies ever born, only one did Satan desperately try to kill—the baby named Jesus, who was foretold by the prophets. Wise men from the East followed a star to worship this newborn King, but King Herod, fearing loss of his throne, ordered the massacre of all children two years and under in Bethlehem, known as the “slaughter of the innocents.”

Warned by a dream, Jesus’s family escaped to Egypt, sparing Him from Satan's murder. When Adam and Eve sinned, mankind was cursed, but Jesus made salvation possible through His death on the cross. He shed holy blood—the only way sin can be washed away—and rose three days later.

Abortion today is rampant, with 45 million children murdered yearly worldwide. This wickedness devastates not only the child but also the mother, causing deep sorrow and guilt. Yet, there is forgiveness if one repents and invites Jesus into their heart.

Jesus will soon return, furious over this wickedness. His judgment is coming, but those who trust Him will receive blessing instead of wrath. And in heaven, beautiful people like Clarice await those who repent and believe.

Title: Who's It Gonna Be?
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Carter
Responses:
One rainy evening, Eddie sat inside his car, making engine sounds with the ignition. Outside the movie theater, people dashed through the rain, clutching umbrellas. Suddenly, Eddie slammed his sneaker down on the gas pedal, screeching as he sped away through the crowded street.

Inside the theater lobby, a woman mourned loudly over a coffin, questioning why God would let such tragedy happen. Another voice responded, agreeing with her point and adding, "If I were God, you know what I’d do?" Jimmy, wearing a construction vest labeled "A.J. Demolition," declared he’d gather every bad person on earth and demolish them all at once.

The scene shifted to towering city skyscrapers, where a cloud of smoke billowed ominously. A voice calmly interrupted Eddie, "It’s already been done." The story then remembered the biblical account of God destroying the entire wicked world except for Noah and the eight people who remained alive with him on the ark. But evil quickly returned, raising a question: if you were God, would you destroy the world every time it became too wicked?

Jimmy explained that even if God spared just one family, evil could still flourish. He proposed rounding up only the very worst people to wipe them out as a lesson to everyone else. He even demonstrated this idea with a small helicopter equipped with an axe but quickly failed. Eddie smiled, noting that God was far ahead of human plans.

God wiped out an entire valley in a single day, as told in the Bible’s story of Sodom and Gomorrah. Only Lot and three of his family members were spared—but even they sinned, creating two warring nations. This showed that taking people out of bad places doesn’t remove the wickedness from their hearts.

Eddie realized he would never end the world’s problems no matter how many bad people he eliminated because evil existed regardless of the number of wrongdoers. He then wondered what the smallest number of people to be destroyed would be to solve the big problems. The answer was just one.

That one was God’s Son, who chose to die instead of humanity. The Bible verse John 3:16 was quoted, emphasizing God’s love for the world and the gift of eternal life through belief in His Son.

Jimmy learned the big problem was not out in the world—it was within each person's heart. The Bible confirms that the heart is deceitful and wicked beyond understanding. Only God truly knows what is inside our hearts and will judge each person accordingly.

God’s judgment is real and coming. Though all sinners deserve to die, death isn’t the end. It brings torment until their lives are judged by Jesus, as described in biblical passages. After judgment, the dead will be raised and judged by their deeds. Those whose names are recorded in the "book of life" will spend eternity with God. Those whose names are not will face eternal separation and punishment.

People have the freedom to choose God or reject Him. Jesus’ death on the cross paid for all sin. He rose from the dead and ascended to heaven, opening the way for anyone who admits they are a sinner and places their trust in Him.

Jesus promises to forgive sins, make believers new creations, and give them the Holy Spirit as a guide. This Holy Spirit helps in prayer and living a life pleasing to God. Jesus will present believers to God the Father as His own children, fulfilling a promise of eternal love and care.

The story concludes with a sobering reminder: everyone will die and face judgment. Someone has to pay for sins—either Jesus or the person themselves. The question is posed: who will you choose? Jesus or you?

A prayer is provided for those ready to confess their sin, believe in Jesus, and ask Him to forgive. There is also a space to remember this life-changing decision.

This story teaches about faith in God’s plan, the reality of sin and judgment, and the hope of salvation through Jesus Christ.

Title: Who's Missing?
Subject: End Time Prophecy
Author: Chick
Responses:
Here's the written story based on the comic strip:

---

A man sits joyfully, receiving another present from a woman who calls him "glorious one," praising him as marvelous and needed. Suddenly, chaos erupts with a loud yell as people are thrown from an office chair, signaling a violent event.

Later, a person in a protective suit investigates a room and confirms that sarin gas was used, with no survivors found. A news report announces the assassination of Dr. Ngaba, head of the U.N. delegation for peacekeeping forces, causing negotiations to collapse and many military leaders fearing Armageddon.

In a home, a man named Bob is told he has a call from Damien, an ex-priest. Damien explains he is at his sister Helen's house, who is a wreck and terrified, believing that an all-out war is imminent. She can't escape the terrifying news, and Damien asks Bob to come speak with her.

Bob agrees and reassures that he and Helen will be right over. When they arrive, Helen is frantic and convinced that the end of the world is near, scared by news commentators and experts. Bob tries to calm her, urging her to listen to what Jesus said about the end of the world—the beginning of sorrows, not the final end.

Bob explains that Jesus spoke of wars, earthquakes, famines, and plagues as a sign of upcoming troubles, but that the world has no idea what’s truly coming. He quotes scripture describing great tribulation unlike anything ever before or to come, warning that before God's judgment hits, the whole system will descend into chaos. Those living through it will wish they had never been born.

Helen asks what this terrible time will be like, and Bob describes horrors including murder, plagues, witchcraft, cannibalism, and complete control by Satan. They are doomed unless something happens. Bob promises that a remnant will escape this nightmare because God has planned a way out. To do so, one must first believe the gospel.

He explains the gospel: Jesus died for humanity’s sins, was crucified, shed His blood to wash away sins, rose from the dead, and returned to heaven. For almost 2,000 years, this message has been spread. Jesus instructed His disciples to preach this gospel to every creature before the end would come.

Bob tells Helen about two signs that must still happen: The great falling away and the man of sin being revealed. He describes how pastors and evangelists once preached the Word of God but were undermined by Satan’s influence in Bible colleges and seminaries, which caused many to lose faith and moral understanding. Judgment is coming, but many avoid it.

Helen asks about the man of sin, and Bob explains that Satan created a counterfeit church with a counterfeit leader, called the man of sin. The pope is often mistakenly called the Holy Father, but this title is blasphemy against God.

Bob then discusses the event called the rapture, when God will take His church to heaven, but not a moment before the last person is saved. At that moment, the trumpet of God will sound, the dead in Christ will rise first, and then believers who are alive will be caught up in the clouds to meet the Lord in the air, never to be separated from Him again.

Helen marvels, saying this means she wouldn’t suffer the horrible tribulation, but Bob tells her to sit down, knowing there is more to explain.

Many will miss this moment and be left behind because they did not believe in Jesus, despite doing good works. Jesus said that on Judgment Day, many will deny knowing Him because they were not truly His followers.

Bob says the precious Catholics are lost and Jesus wants them out of that system, like Helen’s brother Damien. She rejects this idea angrily, defending her faith in the Mother Church and rejecting the Bible.

Damien is replaced by others who support the gospel. Pastor Malcolm invites Bob to the rapture preaching service. They discuss how, with all the war and fear, Jesus said to lift up heads because redemption is near. If the rapture happens tonight, those faithful will be gone in a flash.

After this, heaven and earth will be shaken, and believers will be rewarded, joining the marriage supper of the Lamb. While Satan tries to destroy the earth, Jesus will return with tremendous power, casting Satan into the bottomless pit to rule the world with Jesus reigning.

The story ends by urging the reader not to be left behind when Jesus comes again, quoting scripture promising salvation to all who believe.

---

That is the narrative revealed in the comic strip turning dramatic events, biblical prophecy, and gospel teaching into a story.

Title: Who's The Real Hater?
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
A fierce nation arose in the Middle East, intent on conquest. They threatened neighboring countries with a stark ultimatum: submit or die. This ruthless power destroyed kingdoms and captured tens of thousands of people, brutally torturing and killing the rest. To demonstrate their oppressive devotion, they chopped off the feet, hands, and heads of captives, worshiping a god linked to ancient deities of the moon, Venus, and the sun.

Despite their cruelty, God had compassion on them. Many of God's people despised these Assyrians, as the story reveals. When God called His prophet Jonah to pronounce judgment on the great city of Nineveh (near modern Mosul, Iraq), Jonah fled in the opposite direction, refusing to go. He hated the Assyrians and wished for their destruction, calling them animals.

However, Jonah understood the truth about God’s graciousness, mercy, and readiness to forgive. He lamented that it would be better for him to die than for these “terrorists” to repent and be forgiven. Jonah even hoped that if he disappeared, God would have to judge the Assyrians without him intervening.

Like many haters, Jonah justified his own spite and chose to withhold preaching God’s word to Nineveh, thereby showing his hatred by not warning them of God’s coming judgment. Yet, God had other plans and eventually turned Jonah around—though that is another story.

Today, Bible-believing Christians are often labeled “haters” for the opposite reason: they warn others about God’s judgment and the lake of fire, which unbelievers hate to hear about. Unbelievers think these warnings stem from hatred, but actually, God is patient and does not want anyone to perish.

Christians love people so much that they do not want anyone to face Jesus at the Great White Throne judgment and be cast into the lake of fire. They desire that no one’s deeds be judged harshly but that everyone be with God forever in the new heaven and earth.

Therefore, Christians warn people to be saved and avoid eternal punishment. The purpose of sharing the gospel and passing out tracts is to shock unbelievers into recognizing their need for a Savior. This leads sinners to turn from sin to Jesus Christ in simple faith, believing He died and rose again for their salvation.

If Christians hated the lost, like Jonah, they would refuse to share the gospel or lie, pretending the lost are saved and comfortable in their false security. But these warnings come out of love, not hate.

On the cross, Jesus shed His blood to wash away sins. He died and three days later rose from the dead. For those who believe in Him, God's free gift of everlasting life is available, as described in John 3:16.

If you want this gift of love and salvation, you must accept it through simple faith and follow the instructions given in the gospel.

Title: Why Is Mary Crying?
Subject: Catholicism
Author: Chick
Responses:
Poor Mary is heartbroken, and her pain comes from the very ones who are supposed to love her. Despite being honored and loved worldwide by the faithful, they have failed to do what she asked.

Mary was a beacon of faith, exemplifying devotion and obedience. When the angel told her, "Fear not, Mary: for thou hast found favour with God. And, behold, thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son, and shalt call his name JESUS" (Luke 1:30-31), she was shocked because she was a virgin. Her life was in danger; she could be accused of adultery and stoned to death under Jewish law. Still, Mary was willing to obey God at any cost, saying, "Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word" (Luke 1:38).

After Jesus was born, Mary followed custom and brought her offering to the temple, showing her obedience to God's Word, admitting her need for a Savior. God then revealed to Mary, through a man named Simeon, a prophecy that her child would be the cause of great suffering and division: "Yea, a sword shall pierce through thy own soul also, that the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed" (Luke 2:34-35).

Mary witnessed her son crucified. Jesus, the Lamb of God, shed His blood to save the world from sin. This was the Son of God, yet Mary's tears didn’t end there. She was about to experience heartbreak she never expected.

Mary felt pain because people began worshipping statues of her, bowing down to images she never authorized. This breaks God's commandment: "Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image... thou shalt not bow down thyself to them..." (Exodus 20:4-5). 

She was also saddened when men called her "The Mother of God," a title she found undeserved. She reminded people that Christ existed before her and that He was divine while she was human, saying, "The Word of God says, speaking of Jesus... 'without him was not anything made that was made'" (John 1:3).

Mary wept when people taught she was sinless. While Jesus was without sin, the Scriptures say, "All have sinned, and come short of the glory of God" (Romans 3:23). Mary urged people to look to Jesus, not her, quoting, "He did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth" (1 Peter 2:22).

Her tears were for the deceived multitudes who saw her as a mediator. She declared, "There are not two mediators! Only one!" quoting the scripture that says, "one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus" (1 Timothy 2:5).

From there, the story cautions readers to consider carefully if they have been deceived by false teachings about Mary. If she cannot intercede for prayers, answer prayers, or reign as the Queen of Heaven as some claim, then are millions praying to a being they misunderstand? The story stresses that God does not deceive people.

The narrative shifts to the history behind this confusion, explaining Satan’s plan. After Noah’s flood, survivors built Babylon. Satan found a "virgin" woman named Semiramis, using her to spawn a cult. She married Nimrod, became the Queen of Babylon, and was worshipped as a goddess under many names (the Madonna, Baalti, Mother of Mankind). They set up confessions and celibacy, with Nimrod as Moloch, to maintain control.

Semiramis gave birth to a child called Tammuz, linked to sun worship, and monuments to the goddess and child appeared worldwide. These pagan beliefs spread: China had Shing Moo; India had Devaki and Krishna; Babylon had Semiramis and Tammuz; Egypt had Isis and Horus; Greece had Aphrodite; Rome had Venus and Jupiter; Israel had Ashtoreth and Baal.

Roman Catholicism adopted this worship around 300 AD, transferring pagan goddess worship to Mary. The comic claims this was a strategy to control people with religious fear, making Mary the only mediator to appease an "angry Jesus."

It concludes by saying this worship unites many religions—Christianities, Islam, New Age—and Satan tries to deceive people worldwide through these false portrayals of Mary. But time is running out as Jesus is coming soon.

The comic closes with a call to Christian believers, quoting Acts, Revelation, and urging people to come out of false worship and trust only in Jesus Christ for salvation. It encourages readers to learn the true doctrines of Catholicism and seek God’s Word.

Title: Why No Revival?
Subject: For Christians
Author: Chick
Responses:
Certainly! Here's the written story adapted from the comic strip:

---

Dear ones in Christ,

Many pastors are unable or unwilling to say the things that appear in this book. Many things will make you angry and upset (I hope so), but I pray it will lead to repentance and revival. I direct this book to myself as well but believe it applies to all of us.

---

In the past, Christians openly declared their faith in Jesus Christ. A man asked another if he was a follower of Jesus, and he confidently replied, "Yes! He is my Lord and my Savior!" But today, being very religious is often questioned or mocked. One man nervously explains that he only goes to church to keep his wife happy and asks for forgiveness.

---

The family altar, once a place for prayer and spiritual focus, is now cluttered with distractions like TV guides and inappropriate magazines. This scattering of attention symbolizes why revival is lacking. Meanwhile, self-righteous believers take pride in not having sinned for over 20 years and look down on others, forgetting the warning from Matthew 16:11 to beware of the leaven of the Pharisees.

---

Modern saints wrestle with everyday temptations. One prays fervently for money to buy a new color TV and lottery ticket but fails to grasp the spiritual urgency as 120 souls slip into eternity every minute. Meanwhile, Elisabeth Elliot’s husband was killed by hostile Indians, but God opened the way for her to live and minister to them. She works tirelessly to bring God’s Word to the lost, demonstrating true love and dedication.

---

Neighbors suffer from neglect and prejudice. A hungry child asks his mother to seek help from church-going neighbors, but they're refused because they don’t attend church. The mother sadly admits that Christians have forgotten to love their neighbors as they should.

---

A family mealtime scene shows prayer being interrupted by a child wanting to feed the dog despite the father praying. Outside, a young girl from Mexico works under harsh conditions to spread the Gospel despite persecution and malnutrition; tonight, she’s trained as a missionary.

---

Within the church community, pastors earn modestly, preaching only a few hours a week. Congregants complain about money and the pastor’s family conditions, expressing hatred for the church and refusing to support their leaders. They simultaneously demand more help and critique their ministers.

---

On Sunday mornings, many Christians attend church half-heartedly, enduring dry sermons and avoiding fellowship. One preacher even recycles sermons from the previous year, confident that no one will notice.

---

Prayer meetings and church events often focus on social gatherings like refreshments and choir practices, rather than deep spiritual revival. Meanwhile, some worship music has shifted toward modern styles that attract youth but risk losing reverence.

---

Hypocrisy and judgment abound among believers. Some accuse others of being phonies, dismissing calls for holiness. The scriptural call to live holy lives is often ignored.

---

For those unsaved, the comic paints a bleak picture of eternal separation and punishment, warning that without accepting Christ as Lord, their future is lost.

---

Many pastors preach messages that tickle ears rather than challenge sins. Some label Satan weak and dismiss spiritual warfare, ignoring the prevalence of evil described in the Bible.

---

The teaching of "positive confession" or claiming health and wealth as guaranteed by faith is criticized for misrepresenting Paul’s message and the full counsel of Scripture.

---

Some modern churches reject the King James Bible, calling it outdated and full of errors, yet it has been a steadfast Word for generations.

---

Judgment begins at the house of God, signaling warning signs appearing everywhere spiritually.

---

Compromise has diluted the Gospel and made pastors hesitant to preach against sin and error, leading to predicted widespread falling away and persecution.

---

Scripture calls out lukewarm Christians and urges them to repent and be zealous for the Lord to avoid coming judgment.

---

Broken Christians are implored to ask for God's cleansing, forgiveness, and love, and to repent from hypocrisy, unbelief, and hatred within the community of believers.

---

Revival bursts forth among believers who experience genuine conversions, miracles, and joy in Christ, leading to salvation for many souls.

---

The call to humbly seek God, pray, and repent is emphasized with the promise of forgiveness and healing for the land.

---

The mission is clear: preach the Gospel to every creature, warning of impending judgment and God’s longing for all to be saved. Yet the world suffers in ignorance, and many reject the church and God’s message.

---

This story challenges believers to examine their faithfulness, repent, and join the movement of revival, lest the warnings upon God’s house come true.

---

This written version captures the main themes and messages presented in the comic strip.

Title: Why Should I?
Subject: Your Soul
Author: Chick
Responses:
A man confronts another, telling him that he is a victim. The other man denies this, saying he's just fine. The first man insists that the second has been lied to, claiming the second is a victim of brainwashing. The second man refuses this labeling and even questions the first, asking if he came from monkeys. 

The first man then asks if the other believes in evolution; the second man rejects it and tells the first man he should too. Calling him strange, the second man wonders why the first is so focused on "Jesus stuff." The first man explains he's concerned about the second man's soul catching on fire. The second man replies skeptically, not even understanding what a soul is or if he is supposed to have one.

The first man explains that everyone has a soul, which looks just like the person, is born with them, and continues living after death. While the body will rot in the grave, the soul will live forever and never die. He elaborates that the soul can think, speak, hear, see, get thirsty, and remember everything. The second man doubts this, but the first remains confident.

When asked about the soul catching on fire, the first man explains that if it catches fire it will burn but not burn up, and he hopes the second man will avoid this fate. The second man admits he never even knew he had a soul. The first man says everyone has, but no one thinks about it because of brainwashing by a powerful being who wants souls for himself—the Devil.

The first man warns that unless Jesus blocks the Devil, the Devil will drag souls down to hell. The second man finds this scary but listens intently. The first man says Jesus left heaven to save souls, which shocks and surprises the second man, who points out Jesus might be just another religious figure. The first man responds that Jesus created the universe and made a way to keep souls from ending up in hell's lake of fire.

The second man argues that everyone is God's child, but the first man explains that because of Adam's sin, his descendants are sinners and spiritually children of the Devil. He quotes biblical scripture to back this up. The second man asks what to do, lamenting the idea that he's a sinner doomed to hell.

The first man tells him to ask Jesus to forgive his sins and save his soul. Jesus was born without sin, lived a perfect life, and allowed Himself to be crucified to die for sins, shedding His blood to wash sins away. Jesus held back His angels and accepted crucifixion despite the hatred of the people He created.

The first man says salvation is a gift, and the key is trusting Jesus alone to save the soul. The second man wonders if asking Jesus will save him, and the first affirms that it will, saying it's a free gift that can be accepted anytime. The second man asks about the rapture, the next event when Jesus will return to meet the saved, both dead and living.

The story continues with descriptions of the rapture, the dead rising, and the saved being taken to heaven. Then, the world enters a time called the Great Tribulation, with the Antichrist demanding worship and the mark of the beast, without which people will starve. Those who receive Jesus during this time face martyrdom, a price for salvation, while the saved must believe in Jesus, keep God's commandments, refuse the mark, and face beheading if necessary.

The second man prays, asking Jesus to forgive his sins and save his soul, thanking Him for the sacrifice. The first man explains the second man's soul is now spiritually alive, born again, and he's a child of God. He tells him not to worry anymore because he made the right decision.

The first man describes how the God who saved him is doing something special now, building a mansion for him in heaven. The mansion is just one of Jesus's many surprises. He tells the second man that at death, his body becomes a temple of God and his soul holds the power that raised Jesus from the dead.

He will fly beyond the universe into heaven, where the Lord Jesus will greet him. The story contrasts this with a description of hell, where screams, fire, and unbearable pain await those who reject Jesus. The second man is warned that the gift of eternal life through Jesus is ready, and the tribulation is coming soon.

When the trumpet sounds, all who are saved will be taken to meet Jesus, and now the second man knows the terrible price for not believing Jesus. The story ends urging confession and belief in Jesus Christ as the only way to be saved, stressing that each person's soul will end up in either heaven or hell, and the choice is theirs.

Title: Word Became Flesh, The
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Carter
Responses:
Around 700 B.C., a Jewish prophet named Isaiah made a prophecy stating that the Lord Himself would give a sign: a virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and His name shall be called Immanuel, meaning "God with us." This prophecy is found in Isaiah 7:14 and is interpreted in Matthew 1:23 as referring to God being with us.

Seven hundred years later, the angel Gabriel was sent from God to a city in Galilee named Nazareth. Gabriel was sent "to a virgin espoused (engaged) to a man named Joseph of the house of David, and the virgin's name was Mary," as recorded in Luke 1:26-27.

The angel reassured Mary not to fear, saying, "Thou hast found favor with God," and explained that she would conceive in her womb and bring forth a son named Jesus (Luke 1:30-31). He told her that her son would be great, called the Son of the Highest, and would be given the throne of his father David. He would reign forever over the house of Jacob, and his kingdom would never end (Luke 1:32-33).

Mary asked the angel how this could be since she knew no man. The angel explained that the Holy Ghost would come upon her, and the power of the Highest would overshadow her, making the child born of her holy. This Holy One would be called the Son of God (Luke 1:34-35).

The Bible reveals that there are three who bear record in heaven: the Father, the Word, and the Holy Ghost; these three are one (1 John 5:7). The Word mentioned here is Jesus. John 1:1-3 says, "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God," and that all things were made through Him.

Isaiah had described this Holy One 700 years before His birth, saying, "For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given; and the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace" (Isaiah 9:6).

Around 730 B.C., another prophet named Micah was told about this Holy One's birth and the place of His birth. He prophesied that though Bethlehem Ephratah was a small place among the thousands of Judah, "out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel; whose goings forth have been from old, from everlasting" (Micah 5:2). Jesus Himself later said, "I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the ending" (Revelation 1:8).

Joseph, engaged to Mary, was upset to find Mary with child, which was not his. The angel appeared to Joseph in a dream, telling him, "Fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost" (Matthew 1:20). The Bible also confirms that Joseph "knew" Mary not until she had brought her firstborn son, Jesus (Matthew 1:25).

A decree from Caesar Augustus required all the world to be taxed. Joseph and Mary traveled from Nazareth to Bethlehem for this purpose. While there, Mary gave birth to her firstborn son, wrapped him in swaddling clothes, and laid him in a manger, because there was no room in the inn (Luke 2:1-7).

Shepherds in nearby fields were visited at night by angels who brought them good news of great joy: "For unto you is born this day in the city of David a Saviour, which is Christ the Lord" (Luke 2:10-11).

The Bible says, "He was in the world, and the world was made by Him, and the world knew Him not" (John 1:10). It also states, "And the Word was made flesh and dwelt among us" (John 1:14). Jesus grew strong in spirit and wisdom, and the grace of God was upon Him (Luke 2:40). At twelve years old, He was found in the temple in Jerusalem, sitting among teachers, asking and answering questions. All who heard Him were amazed as He increased in wisdom and favor with God and man (Luke 2:41-52).

John the Baptist began preaching, urging people to prepare the way of the Lord and repent for the Kingdom of God was near. He called people to bring forth fruits worthy of repentance, warning them of the coming wrath (Luke 3:4-8). He introduced Jesus as "The Lamb of God which taketh away the sin of the world" (John 1:29). Jesus was then baptized.

After His baptism, Jesus was led by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil. He fasted for forty days and nights and was afterward hungry. During this time, He was tempted by Satan and lived among wild beasts while angels ministered to Him (Matthew 4:1-2; Mark 1:13).

Following John's imprisonment, Jesus began His public ministry in Galilee, preaching the gospel of the Kingdom of God. He urged people to repent and believe the gospel (Mark 1:14-15). Jesus gathered His disciples, some of whom had been possessed by devils (John 6:70).

He taught the multitudes, saying, "Ye are the light of the world. Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works and glorify your Father which is in heaven" (Matthew 5:14, 16).

Jesus exposed the hypocrisy of the religious leaders, calling them "serpents" and a "generation of vipers," condemning their outward appearance of righteousness while being full of iniquity (Matthew 23:28-33). He warned people to fear God rather than man, because God can destroy both soul and body in hell (Matthew 10:28).

Jesus explained His mission: "For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost" (Luke 19:10). The Bible also states that all have sinned and fall short of God's glory (Romans 3:10, 23).

Many multitudes followed Jesus, and He healed them all (Matthew 12:15b). He performed miracles such as giving sight to the blind, cleansing lepers, raising the dead, and preaching the gospel to the poor (Matthew 11:5). Notably, He raised Lazarus from the dead after four days in the grave, commanding, "Lazarus, come forth!" (John 11:43).

Jesus taught His followers, encouraging them to believe in God and Himself and promised that in His Father's house were many mansions. He said He would prepare a place for them and come again to receive them (John 14:1-3).

When asked about the signs of the end of the world, Jesus spoke of wars, rumors of wars, famines, pestilences, earthquakes, iniquity, and false prophets performing wonders to deceive many (Matthew 24).

He warned that many would fear and look after worldly things causing their hearts to fail. He spoke of His coming in power and great glory (Luke 21:26; Matthew 24:22; Luke 21:27).

One disciple, Judas, betrayed Jesus with a kiss. Jesus was then arrested, falsely accused, tortured, and sentenced to crucifixion (John 18:12). Despite this, God showed His love by sending Christ to die for sinners. Jesus declared, "It is finished!" before He died (John 19:30).

After His death, Jesus' body was placed in a tomb. Three women found the tomb empty, and angels announced, "He is risen!" (Mark 16:6). Jesus later appeared to His disciples, rebuking their unbelief and instructing them to preach the gospel to all creation (Mark 16:14-15).

As Jesus ascended into heaven, two angels told His disciples that He would return in the same manner as they had seen Him go. Jesus promised, "Surely I come quickly" (Acts 1:11; Revelation 22:20).

Jesus can come at any moment, "Behold, He cometh with clouds; and every eye shall see Him" (Revelation 1:7). Every knee shall bow, and every tongue confess Jesus Christ as Lord, to the glory of God the Father (Philippians 2:10-11).

Title: You Have a Date!
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Chick
Responses:
A woman proudly stands before a large mansion, declaring, "It's all mine!" Confident in her wealth, she quotes Luke 12:19, saying to her soul that she has accumulated much and will now enjoy life with ease, eating, drinking, and being merry. But that very night, conviction strikes her as she gasps, "I can't breathe!" and screams, "Nooo!" The figure of Death appears, holding a scythe. She falls to the ground as the words of Luke 12:20 resonate, telling her that her soul will be required of her.

At her funeral, people mourn and praise her: "Our baby's gone," "Everybody loved her," and "She was a good wife." Yet, she internally protests, "Not me!" Isaiah 64:6 reminds that all are unclean and righteousness is like filthy rags; all fade like leaves, and iniquities take them away.

Suddenly, she hears a voice: "Marvel not at this; for the hour is coming in which all in graves shall hear His voice." Startled, she asks, "Did someone call me?" and is commanded to "ARISE!" She wakes, shocked, realizing she is dead — "Wait—I'm dead! It's all over!" The scripture John 5:29 speaks of those who have done good rising to life, and those who have done evil rising to damnation.

Frightened, she questions, "Judgment? Why? This is crazy... I don't want to go. I'm scared!" An angel insists, "You must come... You have a date!" She asks if others will be there, to which the angel replies, "Oh yes, quite a number." They fly through stars, the angel pointing to her destination. She insists, "This can't be happening! I'm too nice for this."

In the heavenly court, she pleads, "Listen to me... I shouldn't even be here! It's all a big misunderstanding." The angel responds, "Everything has been recorded." The judge calls, "NEXT!" Romans 3:10 says there is none righteous, not even one.

Before the throne of God, the dead, great and small, stand as books are opened — including the book of life. The dead are judged according to their deeds. A voice orders, "Review her life!" "Yes, Lord!" comes the answer as a screen shows: "THIS WAS YOUR LIFE!"

Images reveal her as a baby, and she wonders if everything will be reviewed. The scripture from Mark 4:22 affirms nothing hidden will remain so. Further scenes reveal her as a teenager, called "bi*" for bisexual. Her peers say, "How do you know if you're bi* if you don't try?" She pleads, "Stop! Don't show what we did next!" Romans 1:29 lists wickedness, including fornication.

More reveals follow: threats of marriage to a man named Todd, ignoring her mother’s pleas. Images list sins like theft, lies, pornography, gossip, witchcraft, drugs, pride, hypocrisy, cruelty, backbiting, and more, matched with dates, reciting Matthew 10:26 about nothing hidden remaining concealed.

She recalls attending church, saying, "Wait! Look! — That's me in church. See, I wasn't so bad." The preacher speaks John 3:16 about believing in the Son for eternal life. She replies sarcastically, "Who cares?" and worries that her professor would "flunk me" if she showed faith. Matthew 12:37 is quoted about justification by words.

The story shifts as she listens to Jesus' words from John 14:6, "I am the way, the truth, and the life." She struggles, calling this intolerant and hateful, claiming there are many ways to heaven and that she must have been insane.

She confesses despair, "What can I say? I'm lost! Without hope—Without Christ! I'm guilty—guilty!" Galatians 6:7 warns God is not mocked, for one reaps what they sow.

The judge orders, "Open the book of life!" The angel sighs, "Her name does not appear, Lord!" The sentence is delivered: "Depart from me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire prepared for the devil and his angels," as per Matthew 25:41. She is cast into eternal punishment while the righteous enter eternal life (Matthew 25:46).

The final passage reminds that anyone not found in the book of life is cast into the lake of fire (Revelation 20:15).

A closing message offers hope: "THIS CAN BE YOUR LIFE!" It reveals God's promise is patient, desiring repentance so none perish (2 Peter 3:9).

The woman finally asks, "Of course I believe the Bible, and I’m convinced I’m going to hell. But what must I do to be saved?" The answer is clear: "Repent! Surrender your life to Christ, believe He died for your sins and receive Him as your Saviour!" Quoting Jesus: "Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God." (John 3:3)

She prays, "Lord, I know I’m a sinner. I repent and trust in Lord Jesus Christ as my personal Saviour!"

With newfound faith, she lives according to Isaiah 1:18: though her sins are scarlet, they shall be made white as snow. She is remembered not only as a great wife and mother but also a fine Christian (Philippians 1:21).

As Death returns one night, she takes Jesus' hand, saying, "Take my hand, Lord Jesus. I’m coming home!" The sword of Death strikes, but she is welcomed into heaven with, "Well done, thou good and faithful servant... enter into the joy of thy lord." (Matthew 25:21) Finally, 1 Corinthians 2:9 reminds us that the joys prepared for those who love God are beyond human comprehension.

Title: Your Best Life
Subject: Islam
Author: Chick
Responses:
Once there was a man who felt wealthy but empty inside. He enjoyed his wealth with servants attending him, but inwardly, he was restless. He believed in the saying, “There is that maketh himself rich, yet hath nothing…” (Proverbs 13:7).

One day, death unexpectedly came to him, reminding him of the truth: “Boast not thyself of to-morrow; for thou knowest not what a day may bring forth” (Proverbs 27:1). This moment forced him to see all things come to the same end, “all things come alike to all… to the righteous, and to the wicked...” (Ecclesiastes 9:2).

At his funeral, many mourned and said he was a good man. But Scripture reminded, “But we are all as an unclean thing, and all our righteousnesses are as filthy rags…” (Isaiah 64:6). 

Then, the man was called from the grave by God’s command: “ARISE!” (Hosea 13:14). Awakening in a new realm, he reflected on his life, hoping his good deeds would outbalance his failings in the scales of Allah and that he could cross over the bridge to Muhammad. However, an angel warned, “It will not be what you expect.”

The man protested, “Surely Allah will accept me! I have fasted and prayed, given to charity, and gone to Mecca!” but the angel replied, “Everything has been recorded!” (Psalm 14:3).

A grand judgment took place. The dead, great and small, stood before God. Books were opened—including the book of life—and each person was judged according to their works (Revelation 20:12).

The man was told, “Review his life!” and God showed him scenes from his journey on earth, beginning as a baby, through his teenage years, adulthood, and all the secret moments unseen by others but remembered by God (Proverbs 5:21; Ecclesiastes 11:9; 12:14).

Although he had done some good, it was clear none of it met God’s perfect righteousness: “But we are all as an unclean thing…” (Isaiah 64:6). The man begged to explain, pointing to his attendance at the mosque and his friend who had introduced him to Jesus. But God said, “That is not what I required” (Matthew 25:41),

The man admitted his friend was his only Christian friend. He asked if humans could make themselves perfect. The answer was no; only God could make a person perfect. Even after performing pilgrimage rites and believing his sins were forgiven, God asked whether he still sinned. He confessed he did (Ezekiel 18:4, 20).

The man then realized that no deed or ritual could save him. He needed someone to die in his place, and that only God could save him by such a sacrifice. He learned about Jesus, who took the punishment for sin by dying on the cross, was buried, and rose again, defeating death because He is God Almighty (John 3:18a).

The man listened as his friend explained Scripture, urging him to confess Jesus as Lord and believe God raised Him from the dead to be saved (Romans 10:9). Jesus declared, “I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me” (John 14:6).

Despite the evidence, the man’s pride led him to reject Jesus, claiming, “I will take the way of Islam!” But his decision meant his name did not appear in the book of life, and eternal separation from God awaited him: “Depart from me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire...” (Matthew 25:41).

Filled with regret, the man lamented, “I should have believed in Jesus!” (John 3:18b).

Yet, the story offered hope. This could be one’s best life if the heart turned to Christ. The Lord is patient, desiring all to come to repentance (2 Peter 3:9).

A call was made: “REPENT! Let your heart turn to Christ. Trust that He died for your sins. Receive Him as your only Savior” (John 3:36).

One man responded, “Jesus, I know I’m a sinner. I believe You died to take my punishment. I trust You only as my Savior.” Together, they reasoned with Scripture, “Though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow” (Isaiah 1:18).

That man’s life changed. He asked, “Dear Lord, what is your will for me now?” He learned to live for Jesus out of love, not just to gain heaven (Philippians 1:21).

When death came for him, he joyfully took Jesus’ hand and went to be with the Lord, hearing, “Well done, thou good and faithful servant… enter thou into the joy of thy lord” (Psalm 116:15; Matthew 25:21).

And so, if you choose to believe in Jesus and follow Him today, this truly can be your best life.

Title: Your Big Moment
Subject: Basic Gospel
Author: Carter
Responses:
A woman, enjoying her wealth and luxury, proudly declares, "It's all mine!" She raises a glass in celebration, with a fast car and mansion behind her. The scripture Luke 12:19 says, “And I will say to my soul, Soul, thou hast much goods laid up for many years; take thine ease, eat, drink, and be merry.”

Suddenly, she gasps, struggling to breathe as Death appears and says, "Nooo!" Luke 12:20 warns, "But God said... this night thy soul shall be required of thee." Ecclesiastes 12:14 adds that God brings every work into judgment.

A funeral scene shows mourners lamenting the loss of their beloved. They say she was a good wife and loved by many. But Isaiah 64:6 reminds that "all our righteousness are as filthy rags," and iniquities take us away like the wind.

The dead woman hears a voice calling, "Marvel not at this: for the hour is coming, in the which all that are in the graves shall hear his voice." She wonders, "Did someone call me?" then is commanded, “ARISE!” John 5:29 speaks of the resurrection of life and damnation.

Fear grips her as an angel confronts her, saying she must face judgment. She protests, "Judgment? Why? I’m scared!" The angel insists, it’s her big moment, and she wonders if others will be there. The angel replies, "Oh yes, quite a number."

Flying through space, the angel points to her destination. She protests, "This can’t be happening! I'm too nice for this." She pleads, "Listen to me... I shouldn’t even be here! It’s all a big mistake." The angel states, "Everything has been recorded." Romans 3:10 says, "There is none righteous, no, not one."

Before a throne sits a judge. Books are opened and the dead are judged according to their works, as Revelation 20:12 describes. A command arrives: "Review her life!" The angel replies, "Yes, Lord!" A screen shows her life flashing before her eyes, confirming that everything will be reviewed (Mark 4:22).

Memories reveal her youth and struggles: she was bisexual, surrounded by unrighteousness, fornication, and wickedness according to Romans 1:29. She was rebellious, marrying Todd despite warnings of adultery (Mark 10:12). Gossip, lies, pornography, and other sins crowd her life (Matthew 10:26).

She recalls moments in church dismissing God’s word, thinking her professor would scorn biblical teachings. She heard Jesus say, "I am the way, the truth, and the life" (John 14:6) but rejected it as intolerant. Now, she is lost without hope, feeling guilty (Galatians 6:7).

The judge orders the book of life opened, but her name does not appear. Matthew 25:41 and 25:46 pronounce her cursed to everlasting fire prepared for the devil and his angels, while the righteous enter eternal life. Revelation 20:15 describes her being cast into the lake of fire.

The story ends with a warning: "THIS CAN BE YOUR LIFE!" citing 2 Peter 3:9 about God’s longsuffering and desire for repentance.

Then a hopeful turn: a woman asks, "What must I do to be saved?" The response is "Repent! Surrender your life to Christ, believe He died for your sins and receive Him as your Savior!" (John 3:3). She prays, "Lord, I know I’m a sinner. I repent and trust in Jesus as my Savior!" Isaiah 1:18 encourages, "though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow."

She asks, “Dear Lord, what is Your will for me now?” and is shown living a transformed life, where "to live is Christ, and to die is gain" (Philippians 1:21). Her loved ones see a great change: "She’s not only a great wife and mother, but also a fine Christian!"

Finally, the woman, now ready, thinks, "Take my hand, Lord Jesus, I’m coming home!" Death follows behind no longer a menace. Matthew 25:21 promises, "Well done, thou good and faithful servant... enter thou into the joy of thy Lord." 1 Corinthians 2:9 assures, "Eye hath not seen... the things which God hath prepared for them that love him."

Her story is one of warning, judgment, and ultimately, salvation through faith.

Title: Your Life
Subject: Basic Gospel
Responses:
Once there was a man who lived a comfortable and prosperous life. He felt secure in the goods he had acquired and said to his soul, "Soul, thou hast much goods laid up for many years; take thine ease, eat, drink, and be merry." However, one night, his soul was required of him suddenly, and he was reminded that life only comes once and is followed by judgment.

At his funeral, loved ones mourned, saying, "He was a good man!" But scripture reminds us that all people are unclean and sinful, and righteousness on its own is like filthy rags. Everyone fades and is taken away by their sins.

Then, the man found himself awakening in the grave, called to arise. The hour had come for all who were in their graves to hear the voice of Christ and come forth. Angels approached him, saying, "Come, you have an appointment!" He was confused and refused to believe what was happening, denying judgment, heaven, and hell.

The angels showed him his destination in the cosmos, but he still refused to accept it, insisting he'd lived a good life and was no different than others. Everything had been recorded, and he was next for judgment.

Before God, the dead stood as the "books" were opened, one being the Book of Life. The man was to have his life reviewed. This review included moments from his childhood, teenage years, and adulthood. The man realized that every idle word would be accounted for, and hidden sins and wrongful deeds, from envy and deceit to lust and false accusations, would all be revealed.

He remembered going to church and thought he wasn't so bad, but the truth was clear: without faith and confession in Jesus Christ, no one is saved. Jesus says He is the way, the truth, and the life; no one comes to the Father but by Him. But the man stubbornly insisted he didn’t need Christ and would make it his own way, thus condemning himself.

The book of life was opened, and it was found that his name was missing. He was condemned to everlasting fire prepared for the devil and his angels. The man was cast into the lake of fire, the place for those not found in the Book of Life.

The story warns that this can be anyone's life unless they repent and believe. The Lord is patient, not wanting any to perish but all to come to repentance.

If a person believes the Bible and knows they are lost and going to hell, they must repent, surrender their life to Christ, acknowledge His sacrifice, and receive Him as Savior. Jesus promised that those who come to Him will be forgiven, made pure as snow.

Having accepted Christ, a person can live asking, "Lord, what is your will for me now?" and find joy in serving Him. Then, when they come to die, they can say, "Take my hand Lord Jesus, I’m coming home!" and enter into the joy of the Lord.

Indeed, precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His faithful saints.
